result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the camera MediaStream outlives the view. `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:281) is dead code because demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 wraps the pane in <KeepAlive> sized (App.vue:107, :max="6") so extract is never evicted. Confirmed live: after navigating from #/extract to #/palettes the pane leaves the DOM but `stream.getTracks()[0].readyState` is still "live", and returning to #/extract restores a still-open viewfinder. The structural root — the shell owns the caching policy while a leaf SFC owns a device resource, with no contract between them — is the same defect that makes the quantize Worker's terminate (useImageQuantize.ts:148) and the debounce clear (useExtractSession.ts:194) dead too; and it exists at all only because the SFC re-implemented a camera capability that already exists, with a correct disposer, unused, in useImageQuantize.ts:115 (L-2).
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for balance: the public-surface half of the premise does NOT hold. The extract subtree consumes value.js only through published bare subpaths (@mkbabb/value.js/{color,css,quantize}); there is not a single @src/… or ../../src/… reach in demo/workbenches/extract/**; quantize-worker.ts:6-7 imports quantizePixels and its types through @mkbabb/value.js/quantize in lines a real consumer could write verbatim; and `npx tsc --traceResolution` confirms those specifiers resolve through this repo's own package.json#exports by package self-reference — the same mechanism a downstream package uses. verbatimModuleSyntax is clean throughout the subtree. The rot is in the resolution machinery around that surface (L-9, L-10), in the surface's own shape (L-8), and in the unenforced demo boundaries (L-5) — not in how this component reaches the library.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue (+ its composables, controls, drop zone, worker, and the quantize library it consumes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — claude-opus-5[1m] (1M-context variant). Declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-2 — the camera MediaStream leaks when unmount races the permission prompt: `cameraStream = await getUserMedia(...)` assigns AFTER the await, so `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` sees `null` and the tracks are never stopped. Proven live: workbench unmounted, then permission resolved → `{ tracks: [{ id: "S1", stopped: false }] }`. The camera hardware stays powered on a page the user has navigated away from, with no UI anywhere to turn it off; only closing the tab clears it. (C-1 — the instrument rendering image A while reporting image B's palette — is the equal-severity correctness blocker.)
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative results checked and recorded in the report so the next seat need not re-walk them: verbatimModuleSyntax clean across all six files; no ValueUnit wrapping in the tree; no defineModel (sliders are one-way :model-value + @update:model-value); no oklch→HSV roundtrip so stableHue is not applicable; glass-ui useBreakpoint does remove its matchMedia listener (dist/dom.js:46-49); worker terminated on unmount (useImageQuantize.ts:148-151); debounce timer cleared on unmount (useExtractSession.ts:194-196); chromaWeight=0 boundary correctly distinguished from undefined (useImageQuantize.ts:102-103) and the `v && $emit` guard tests the array not the value so [0] passes; k domain 1..16 sits inside the library's [1,64] integer guard; empty-palette and length-1 position divide-by-zero both guarded; REPORT.json /#/extract shows overflowX 0, main 1, pageErrors [] in all four Safari matrices.)

defects.defect: The instrument lies: the preview and the extracted palette + '% of the image' readout can describe two different images. `onFile` writes `lastFile` synchronously but writes `previewDataUrl` after an un-sequenced `await readAsDataUrl(file)` (FileReader completion is size-ordered, not call-ordered), then calls `runQuantize()` which re-reads `lastFile.value` at await-resume time. No request token reconciles the two paths.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:164-168. Live repro output: {"fileSizes":{"A":11537022,"B":107},"previewIsA_bigRed":true,"previewDataUrlLength":15382718,"dominantReadout":["oklch(45.201371817442% 0.313214388634 264.05202261637deg)"],"verdict":"DESYNC: preview=A(red), palette=B(blue)"} — hue 264.05deg is image B (blue) while the rendered img carries A's 15.4MB data URL (red).
defects.mechanism: unguarded async continuation acting on state that moved — no request identity attached to the await
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — dispatch two `drop` events in the SAME tick on the drop zone: A = 2400x1800 all-red noise PNG (11.5 MB), B = 8x8 solid #0000ff PNG (107 B). After 4s the preview shows A and the dominance readout reports B's blue.
defects.proposedCure: Transposition, not patch: give the session a monotonic requestId; capture it at entry and gate BOTH the preview write and the quantize dispatch on `id === current`. Better — drop the FileReader entirely and use `URL.createObjectURL(file)`, which is synchronous, so the preview write lands in the same tick as `lastFile` and the desync window closes by construction (also kills the 15.4 MB base64 retention in C-7).

defects.defect: Camera MediaStream leaks when the component unmounts while the permission prompt is open. `cameraStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...)` assigns after the await; `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` can only stop an already-assigned stream, so the promise resolves into a dead component's closure and the tracks are never stopped. No AbortController, no unmounted flag, no post-await guard.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-263 (assignment at :242, teardown at :281). Live repro output: {"workbenchUnmounted":true,"tracks":[{"id":"S1","stopped":false}],"verdict":"LEAKED — camera track never stopped"}
defects.mechanism: unguarded async continuation acting on a disposed scope — resource acquired after its owner's teardown ran
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — stub `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` to return a deferred promise whose stream's track records stop() (the stub controls only TIMING; the component path is untouched). Click the title="Open camera" DockControl, then `location.hash='#/picker'` to unmount the workbench, then resolve the deferred. track.stopped === false.
defects.proposedCure: Extract `useCameraStream()` — a composable that owns the resource lifetime: an AbortController + a `disposed` flag, a post-await guard (`if (disposed) { stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()); return; }`), and its own `onScopeDispose`. Two consumers already want it: this workbench and the zero-caller `quantizeFromCamera` in useImageQuantize.ts:115-146, which is a third independent implementation of the same lifecycle.

defects.defect: A second camera open orphans the first stream. The camera DockControl is never disabled while the camera is live: ExtractWorkbench.vue:70 computes `:disabled="isProcessing || cameraActive"` but ExtractControls forwards `disabled` ONLY to the Reset button. A second click re-enters startCamera and overwrites `cameraStream`, stranding the first stream's tracks forever.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:49-55 (camera control, no :disabled) vs :84 (reset, has it); ExtractWorkbench.vue:70. Live repro output: {"cameraButtonStateAfterOpen":[{"disabled":false,"ariaDisabled":null}],"tracks":[{"id":"S1","stopped":false},{"id":"S2","stopped":false}],"videoCount":1} — two live streams, one <video>, zero stops.
defects.mechanism: non-idempotent resource acquisition; a mutable single-slot handle overwritten without releasing the prior occupant
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — stub getUserMedia to resolve immediately with a stop()-recording track. Click title="Open camera", wait 300ms, click it again. Both tracks report stopped:false.
defects.proposedCure: The same `useCameraStream()` as C-2 — a resource composable is idempotent on start() by construction (it releases or reuses the prior handle). The disabled-prop fan-out in ExtractControls is a symptom; the cure is that the workbench should not be able to acquire twice at all.

defects.defect: The camera viewfinder has no close affordance. Its only control is the 'Capture frame' shutter — no cancel, no X, no Escape handler, no backdrop dismiss. A user who opens the camera by accident must either take a photo they do not want or leave the route, and leaving the route mid-permission is C-2.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:34-59 (the whole camera block: one DockControl, title="Capture frame"). Live enumeration of every button inside the <video> container: {"viewfinderControls":[["Capture frame"]],"videoCount":1}
defects.mechanism: a modal-ish surface shipped without its dismissal half; the sibling ImageEyedropper has the pattern and the camera did not receive it
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — open the camera; enumerate buttons inside the viewfinder container. Only 'Capture frame' exists. The drop zone behind stays click-live, so clicking it opens the eyedropper rather than dismissing the camera.
defects.proposedCure: Add a `title="Close camera"` DockControl beside the shutter bound to `stopCamera`, plus a keydown.escape — mirroring ImageEyedropper.vue:227-235, which already ships exactly this for its own overlay. The affordance exists one directory over; reuse it rather than reinventing.

defects.defect: A malformed image produces an unhandled promise rejection (a page console error), NO error shown to the user, a broken in the drop zone, and a wedged workbench. `runQuantize()` discards the promise from `quantizeFromFile` (no await, no catch); `createImageBitmap` rejects before `isProcessing`/`error` are ever touched, so no state changes at all. `previewDataUrl` is still set, which flips `:disable-click` true, so clicking the zone mounts ImageEyedropper over a zero-dimension image — where `onMounted(() => loadAndFit())` also discards its promise and fires a SECOND unhandled rejection behind a blank overlay.
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:153-157 (discarded promise); useImageQuantize.ts:105-108 + :86-87 (throw precedes the isProcessing/error writes); ImageEyedropper.vue:237-240 + useImageSampler.ts:74. Live repro output: {"unhandledRejections":["The source image could not be decoded."],"hasPreviewImg":true,"imgNaturalW":0,"imgSrcPrefix":"data:image/png;base64,AQIDBAUGBwg=","errorLineText":[],"mainText":"... · UNDEVELOPED PLATE — FEED IT AN IMAGE · ..."}. Browser console: [ERROR] The source image could not be decoded.
defects.mechanism: fire-and-forget async whose rejection path has no owner; error state set downstream of the throw site
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — drop a File named 'broken.png' with type 'image/png' whose bytes are Uint8Array([1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]) (a real class: truncated download, renamed file, HEIC). Console error fires; the error line stays empty; the zone shows a broken image and flips to sample mode.
defects.proposedCure: Make decode failure first-class in the Result idiom the codebase already runs on (src/quantize.ts:22, serializeCssColor at useExtractSession.ts:55): `quantizeFromFile` returns `Result<..., QuantizeIssue>` with a new `quantize_image_undecodable` variant flowing into the existing quantizeError channel, and gate the previewDataUrl write on a successful decode so the zone never enters sample mode over a corpse.

defects.defect: The eyedropper — the workbench's headline sampling capability — is unreachable by keyboard, and focus never enters the overlay when it opens. `:disable-click="!!previewDataUrl"` drives ImageDropZone's `:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"` AND gates its keydown handler off, while the workbench's only activation binding is a `click` listener. The element keeps role="button" and the label 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors' while being inert to Enter/Space and out of the tab order.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:23-25 (the trigger) + ImageDropZone.vue:19,22. Live repro output: {"zoneTabindex":"-1","zoneRole":"button","zoneLabel":"Image preview area, tap to sample colors","overlayBefore":"closed","afterKeyboardEnterSpace":"closed","afterMouseClick":"OPEN","focusWhenOverlayOpen":"DIV|Image preview area, tap to sample colors"} — WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
defects.mechanism: one element overloaded with two mutually-exclusive roles (drop target + sample action), gated by a boolean that silently strips keyboard operability
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — drop a valid 2x1 PNG, then dispatch Enter and Space keydown/keyup on the zone (overlay stays closed), then a click (overlay opens). document.activeElement remains the tabindex=-1 div behind the overlay.
defects.proposedCure: Stop overloading the element. The zone is a drop target; sampling is an action. Give the preview state its own real DockControl ('Sample colours from image'), keep the zone at tabindex="0" for replace-by-keyboard, and let ImageEyedropper move focus on mount and restore it on close (it already owns Escape at ImageEyedropper.vue:227).

defects.defect: The component allocates 45.8 MB and transfers 22.9 MB to the worker in order to read 10,500 of 6,000,000 pixels — 99.825% waste — and does the readback on the main thread. `imageFileToPixels` decodes at native resolution, rasterises to a full-size OffscreenCanvas and calls getImageData (main-thread), then `pixels.buffer.slice(0)` copies the whole thing AGAIN before transferring. Meanwhile src/quantize.ts sub-samples with targetPixels=10_000. The preview adds a 15.4 MB retained base64 string for an 11.5 MB file.
defects.evidence: useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 and :93; src/quantize.ts:41,52. Measured (exact imageFileToPixels body replayed on a 3000x2000 JPEG): {"decode_createImageBitmap_ms":8.6,"getImageData_mainthread_ms":13.8,"bufferSlice_copy_ms":1.8,"total_mainthread_ms":24.3,"bytesAllocated_MB":45.8,"bytesTransferredToWorker_MB":22.9,"pixelsInImage":6000000,"pixelsQuantizerActuallyReads":10500,"wastedFraction":0.99825}. Plus previewDataUrlLength 15382718 from the C-1 run.
defects.mechanism: work done at full fidelity upstream of a sampler that discards 99.8% of it; the worker boundary is defeated by a main-thread readback
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — in-page, replay imageFileToPixels verbatim on a 3000x2000 JPEG File and time each phase. Scale to a 12 MP phone photo (4032x3024): 48.7 MB ImageData + 48.7 MB slice = ~97 MB transient, on mobile Safari.
defects.proposedCure: `createImageBitmap(file, { resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality: 'low' })` sized to sqrt(targetPixels) — the decoder does the downscale off-thread; the canvas becomes 200x150, getImageData becomes 120 KB, and the slice(0) disappears entirely (transfer imageData.data.buffer directly, since the ImageData is discarded on the next line). For the preview, URL.createObjectURL is O(1) and drops 15.4 MB.

defects.defect: The dominance readout can name a colour that is not the card's first swatch, contradicting the component's own stated invariant ('the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen'). src/quantize.ts sorts by population with a STABLE sort (ties keep insertion order); useExtractSession's `dominant` uses a different rule — strict `>` on population PLUS a chroma tiebreak. The two orderings disagree on every population tie.
defects.evidence: Invariant asserted at ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117. Conflicting orderings: src/quantize.ts:128 vs useExtractSession.ts:121-142. Library derivation (npx tsx on src/quantize.ts, 2x1 image of #ff0000 + #0000ff): index 0 = [0.628, 0.2577, 29.234] pop=1 (RED, first swatch); index 1 = [0.452, 0.3132, 264.052] pop=1 (BLUE). Live readout for that same image: "oklch(45.201371817442% 0.313214388634 264.05202261637deg)" — hue 264deg, the BLUE one.
defects.mechanism: two independent orderings over the same data, only one of which the card renders; a documented invariant enforced nowhere
defects.reproduction: npx tsx: quantizePixels(new Uint8ClampedArray([255,0,0,255, 0,0,255,255]), 2, 1, {k:5, chromaWeight:0.5}) returns red at index 0. Then drop that same 2x1 PNG on http://localhost:9000/#/extract: the readout names the blue cluster while colors[0] (and thus the first swatch) is red.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the 22-line `dominant` loop. quantizePixels already guarantees max-population-first, so `dominant = presented.value[0] ?? null` is the whole function, is BY CONSTRUCTION the first swatch, and restores the stated invariant. If a chroma tiebreak is genuinely wanted it belongs in src/quantize.ts's sort, where the card's ordering also sees it — one ordering, one truth.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: no test in the repository ever feeds this component an image. There is no unit test for ExtractWorkbench.vue, useExtractSession.ts, or useImageQuantize.ts, and every e2e oracle that names Extract visits only the never-fed empty state or counts headings/cards. The developed path — worker, palette, dominance readout, camera, eyedropper mount, every error path — is entirely untested, which is why C-1, C-5 and C-8 shipped.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "setInputFiles\|DataTransfer\|input\[type=.file" e2e/ test/` → NO OUTPUT. Coverage that exists: test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts (3 its, a different file, no image); e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:125 (empty plate only); o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1080 (track contrast); o7/o10d/o11 (heading+card census); walk.spec.ts:74 (heading visible).
defects.mechanism: gates that assert the resting frame of a component whose entire value is in its transitions
defects.reproduction: Mutation that keeps every existing gate green: replace the body of useExtractSession.onFile with `{ lastFile.value = file; }` (delete the preview read and the quantize dispatch), and delete startCamera/stopCamera/captureFrame and the entire ImageEyedropper mount at ExtractWorkbench.vue:172-180. Full vitest + playwright suites still pass.
defects.proposedCure: One component test that drives a synthetic File through useExtractSession with an injected workerFactory — the seam is ALREADY BUILT and documented at useImageQuantize.ts:35-41 ('tests + a Safari-worker fallback can swap a fake/pooled factory') and has zero callers. The affordance was designed for exactly this and never used. Add the three boundary cases the probes above exercised: two-drops-in-a-tick (C-1), undecodable bytes (C-5), population tie (C-8).

defects.defect: Async results are announced to nobody. There is no aria-live region anywhere in the extract surface; the error line has no role="alert"; and the one announcing element (PaletteCardSkeleton, role="status" aria-label="Loading palette") is unreachable in practice because Transition mode="out-in" requires the shadow plate's leave transition to finish before it may enter, and the worker returns first. A screen-reader user drops an image and receives no feedback of any kind.
defects.evidence: Live probe of <main> on /#/extract: {"live":[]} — zero [aria-live], [role=status], [role=alert]. Error line ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85 (no role); result branch :108-157 (no live region). Measured on a 6 MP drop: {"skeletonAppearedAtMs":"NEVER","cardAppearedAtMs":250}. The 15-line comment at ExtractWorkbench.vue:87-101 describes a state that does not render.
defects.mechanism: announcement carried by a transient branch that a transition mode makes unreachable; the outcome itself carries no announcement at all
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — (a) query main for [aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert] on load: empty. (b) drop a 3000x2000 JPEG and poll at 25ms for [data-slot="palette-card-skeleton"]: never appears, while the developed card appears at 250ms.
defects.proposedCure: One polite live region on the result column that speaks the OUTCOME ('5 colours extracted, dominant oklch(...) at 50%'), and role="alert" on the error line. The skeleton's role="status" is the wrong carrier — it announces the wait, not the answer, and it is racing a transition it cannot win.

defects.defect: This component contributes the entire nameless-button count of its route in all four Safari matrices (3 of 3), plus two 12px-wide slider thumbs against WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum. The three DockControls (Upload / Open camera / Reset) carry only `title`, which is the last-resort accname fallback and is not surfaced on touch at all.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:98,105,110,112 — /#/extract: 3, in every matrix (the highest in the repo; every other route scores 0 or 1). Attributed live: {"namelessCount":3,"nameless":[{"title":"Upload image",...},{"title":"Open camera",...},{"title":"Reset",...}]} = ExtractControls.vue:40,49,83. Tap targets live + REPORT.json: {"thumbs":[{"label":"Number of colors","w":12,"h":24},{"label":"Chroma weight","w":12,"h":24}]}. glass-ui dist/dock.js:1121 — DockControl exposes no label prop and forwards no aria-label.
defects.mechanism: icon-only controls relying on `title` for their accessible name; thumb geometry below the target-size floor on the route's primary controls
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — enumerate visible button/[role=button] with no aria-label/aria-labelledby/textContent: exactly the three ExtractControls DockControls. Measure [role=slider] bounding rects: both 12x24.
defects.proposedCure: Per owner edict 4 the fix belongs in glass-ui, not here: DockControl should take a `label` prop and emit aria-label (keeping `title` for the mouse tooltip) — one producer change clears 18 nameless buttons across 7 routes. The thumb width belongs to the demo/ui/slider root (edict 5: root-level, never a per-instance override in this workbench).

defects.defect: Dead dual paths (owner edict 2). (a) `layout: "split"` is unreachable — one call site, which passes "column" — yet it is branched on in four template expressions and is the sole consumer of a live matchMedia listener registered on every mount. (b) `quantizeFromCanvas` and `quantizeFromCamera` (37 lines, including a THIRD independent getUserMedia lifecycle) have zero callers. (c) kSliderGradient's "var(--muted)" fallback never renders — it is always overridden by the later `backgroundColor: trackInk`. The composable docblock still claims 'both shells now consume this session'; the second shell is gone.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "ExtractWorkbench" demo/` → only ExtractPane.vue:11,25 (and it passes layout="column" at ExtractPane.vue:13). Dead branches: ExtractWorkbench.vue:4-8, 13, 17-21, 148; dead listener :226. Dead APIs: useImageQuantize.ts:110-146. Dead fallback: useExtractSession.ts:103 vs ExtractControls.vue:22. Stale claim: useExtractSession.ts:5.
defects.mechanism: a collapsed twin-shell refactor (T20) that deleted the second consumer but kept every branch, prop, listener and API that existed to serve it
defects.reproduction: grep enumeration above — the "split" branch, isWide, useBreakpoint, quantizeFromCanvas, quantizeFromCamera and the "var(--muted)" string are provably unreachable at HEAD.
defects.proposedCure: Delete "split", isWide, the useBreakpoint call, quantizeFromCanvas, quantizeFromCamera and the dead fallback; correct the stale docblock. ~60 lines of a 294-line component serve paths that cannot execute. Note the deletion is not merely hygiene: quantizeFromCamera is the camera lifecycle C-2/C-3 needed — it was written, abandoned, and then re-implemented badly in the component.

defects.defect: In-flight quantizes are neither cancelled nor tokenised. useImageQuantize stores a single pendingResolve/pendingReject pair; a second runQuantize before the first reply overwrites both, so the earlier promise NEVER settles, and the first worker reply then resolves the SECOND caller with the FIRST palette and sets isProcessing=false while run #2 is still in the worker (early skeleton drop + stale render). The worker is also never re-created after onerror, so one worker crash bricks every subsequent extraction for the session.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:89-98 (single-slot pending pair), :57-68 (onmessage resolves whatever is currently in the slot), :69-75 (onerror sets error but leaves the dead worker installed), :54-56 (getWorker only constructs when `worker` is null).
defects.mechanism: single-slot continuation storage for a multi-request channel; no request identity on the postMessage payload
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis by code path. Forcing the overlap needs a quantize exceeding the 300ms debounce (useExtractSession.ts:159-162); the desktop probe measured the full cycle at 250ms, so I could not force it live. The dropped-promise and dead-worker mechanisms are unconditional and visible in the source.
defects.proposedCure: Attach a per-request id to the postMessage payload and echo it from quantize-worker.ts:20; discard replies whose id is not current. This is the same token that cures C-1, applied one layer down — which is the point: one identity discipline, two layers. Re-create the worker on onerror rather than leaving a corpse installed.

defects.defect: `isProcessing` is false during the image-decode window: quantizeFromFile awaits imageFileToPixels BEFORE runQuantize sets isProcessing=true, so nothing renders during the decode — and if the decode throws, nothing ever renders (C-5).
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:105-108 (the await) vs :86-87 (where error/isProcessing are actually written). Measured blind window on a 6 MP file: total_mainthread_ms 24.3 (createImageBitmap 8.6 + getImageData 13.8 + slice 1.8), multiples of that on mobile Safari for a 12 MP capture.
defects.mechanism: loading state raised downstream of the first expensive await instead of at the operation boundary
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — replay imageFileToPixels on a 3000x2000 JPEG and time it (24.3ms here); during that entire window the component is in its resting state with no indication that work has begun.
defects.proposedCure: Raise isProcessing at the TOP of quantizeFromFile inside a try/finally, so the loading state brackets the whole operation rather than only its worker tail. (Cure C-10 alongside it — a loading flag nobody can perceive is only half the fix.)

defects.defect: Camera failures are filed as quantize errors. The component reaches through the session object to write a writable computed whose setter targets the worker's error ref, so a camera fault occupies the quantizer's error channel and the next successful quantize silently erases it. A raw DOMException is template-interpolated, so the user reads 'Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: Permission denied'. There is no dismiss.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 (`session.quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\``); the writable computed at useExtractSession.ts:66-73; the erasure at useImageQuantize.ts:86 (`error.value = null`).
defects.mechanism: two unrelated failure domains sharing one channel; a component mutating composable-owned state directly instead of through an action — the encapsulation the session exists to provide, bypassed at the one place it matters
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — deny camera permission: the quantize error line shows the stringified DOMException. Then drop any valid image: the camera message vanishes without the user having acknowledged it.
defects.proposedCure: A separate `cameraError` ref rendered on its own line, written through a `session.setCameraError()` action rather than by reaching into a computed; map the three real getUserMedia rejection names (NotAllowedError / NotFoundError / NotReadableError) to human sentences.

defects.defect: `@click="() => {}"` binds an explicit no-op to PaletteCard's click emit, while the card's root unconditionally carries cursor-pointer and the cartoon-surface press choreography. The result card advertises hover, press-squash and a pointer cursor while doing nothing — a lying affordance.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:152; the unconditional affordance at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:19 ('group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer') with `v-bind="press.handlers"` at :23.
defects.mechanism: an interactive affordance hard-coded into a component root rather than derived from whether the consumer actually handles the interaction
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — extract a palette and hover/press the result card: it responds with the full press choreography and shows cursor:pointer; clicking does nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Root-level per edict 5: PaletteCard should derive cursor-pointer and press.handlers from whether a click listener is attached, or take an explicit `interactive` prop — never a per-instance override in this workbench. Then the no-op binding here simply disappears.

defects.defect: Two adjacent template refs use two different idioms: `ref<InstanceType<typeof ImageDropZone> | null>(null)` on one line and `useTemplateRef<HTMLVideoElement>("videoRef")` on the next. useTemplateRef is the Vue 3.5 form the repo standardises on (owner edict 7) and is used correctly one line below and in ImageDropZone.vue:78.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:222 vs :223; the correct idiom also at demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:78.
defects.mechanism: incomplete idiom migration leaving both forms live in one file
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — direct source read; both lines are visible together.
defects.proposedCure: `const dropZoneRef = useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof ImageDropZone>>("dropZoneRef")` and drop the `ref` import if it becomes unused.

defects.defect: `await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)` is used as a DOM-settle wait. Three faults: a raw ungated rAF in a repo carrying a documented PRM-RAF epidemic; never cancelled, so on unmount it resolves into a dead closure (compounding C-2); and rAF is SUSPENDED in background tabs, so backgrounding during the permission prompt means `videoRef.value.srcObject = cameraStream` never runs — leaving the camera live behind a permanently black viewfinder that C-4 gives no way to close.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:249 (`await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)`) followed by the conditional assignment at :250.
defects.mechanism: a rendering-cadence primitive used as a framework-lifecycle primitive; suspended by the platform under exactly the condition that makes the leak worst
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the background-tab arm (rAF suspension is specified platform behaviour). The uncancelled-on-unmount arm is unconditional and visible in the source.
defects.proposedCure: `await nextTick()` — the guaranteed, cancel-safe DOM-flush primitive, which is what the line actually wants. Under the C-2 cure the continuation is additionally gated on the disposed flag.

defects.defect: captureFrame trusts three nullable results: `canvas.getContext("2d")!` (null under memory pressure or a context-count limit — exactly the mobile-Safari condition C-7 manufactures) and `canvas.toBlob((b) => resolve(b!))`, where a null blob makes `new File([null], ...)` stringify to the 4 bytes "null", which then takes the C-5 path: unhandled rejection, no error, wedged workbench. There is also no re-entrancy guard on the shutter.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:272 (`canvas.getContext("2d")!.drawImage(...)`) and :274-277 (`canvas.toBlob((b) => resolve(b!))` then `new File([blob], ...)`).
defects.mechanism: non-null assertions used as guards on platform APIs that are specified to return null
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. Reaching the null-context branch requires exhausting the canvas-context budget, which I did not force on this machine.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow both with real checks and route a null result into the same Result error channel proposed in C-5, so a failed capture becomes a visible message rather than a corrupt File; add an in-flight guard on the shutter.

defects.defect: Reset does not reset, and a loaded image can never be removed. onReset restores k=5 and chromaWeight=0.5 and re-quantizes; it never clears previewDataUrl, lastFile, or the palette. The control is a RotateCcw icon named 'Reset', which reads as 'clear'. Combined with C-6's disable-click, there is no path anywhere in the workbench back to the empty state — the ShadowPalette / 'undeveloped plate' surface is reachable exactly once per mount, on first paint.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:180-184 (onReset touches only colorCount, chromaWeight and re-runs the quantize); the control at demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:83-90 (title="Reset", RotateCcw).
defects.mechanism: a control whose name promises a state transition its implementation does not perform; no dispose path for the session's principal resource
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract — load any image, then click Reset: the image, the preview and the palette all remain; only the two sliders return to 5 / 0.5. No other control clears them.
defects.proposedCure: onReset clears the whole session (image, palette, k, kC — and revokes the object URL under the C-1 cure) and the control is renamed 'Clear image'. If a params-only reset is also wanted, it is a second, separately-named control — not one button silently meaning half of what it says.

defects.defect: `extractedPalette` calls `new Date().toISOString()` for both createdAt and updatedAt inside the computed body, with paletteName as a dependency. Renaming the palette therefore re-mints its creation date, and every recompute hands PaletteCard a fresh object identity.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:95-96 (the two Date calls) with the paletteName.value dependency at :92.
defects.mechanism: impure value construction inside a computed — the derived value is a function of wall-clock time, not only of its inputs
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis; the drift is invisible in the current UI because the extracted card does not display its createdAt. It becomes real the moment onSave (:186-188) or any consumer reads it.
defects.proposedCure: Stamp createdAt once when the palette is produced (in the quantize completion path) and keep the computed pure over its inputs; updatedAt likewise moves to the mutation site.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — model id claude-opus-5[1m]; seat declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — every interactive WatercolorDot in the component is inert (glass-ui 7.0.0 renders a prop-closed, inheritAttrs:false, aria-hidden, pointer-events:none <span>; the component still passes the 6.x tag/slot/aria-label/@click/:disabled API), so the Mix workbench's colors mode — the default mode — has NO add path at all: measured ghostTag SPAN, ghostAriaHidden true, ghostPointerEvents none, plusPresent false, focusablesInWell 0, and [data-mix-source] count 0 before and after a forced real click and after clicking every "From palettes" swatch.
result.negativeProof: Sound where I could not fault it, with positive evidence: (1) the Colors/Palettes SegmentedTabs are canon-sanctioned — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.2 names "Mix Colors/Palettes source-mode tabs" as a surviving P092 site, and the component consumes SegmentedTabs variant="pill" with no descendant corrections; (2) contrast passes — canvas-resolved sRGB ratios 5.08:1 ("Selected" on the well), 6.29:1 ("From palettes" on the plate), 5.71:1 (count micro-label), all >= 4.5 (an earlier oklab-naive 3.19 reading of mine was wrong and is discarded in the report); (3) no horizontal overflow at 1440/720/390/320 (scrollWidth-clientWidth = 0), matching REPORT.json overflowX 0 on all four /#/mix rows; (4) zero console errors and zero page errors on /#/mix in all four audit matrices (REPORT.json consoleErrors [] / pageErrors []); (5) reduced motion honoured by the global guard — measured animation-duration 0.00001s under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; (6) RTL mirrors correctly at the container level (dir=rtl: well x224 w462, ghost moves to x624.5); (7) verbatimModuleSyntax respected — both type-only imports at :10,:11 are `import type`; (8) no god module (283 L, one job); (9) palette identity correctly keys on slug (K-PALID) and aria-pressed is present and truthful on the palettes-mode seats.

defects.defect: Every interactive WatercolorDot in the component is inert; colors mode cannot accept a single color. The component passes a glass-ui 6.x API (tag="button"/"div", default slot <Plus>, aria-label, @click, :disabled, :title) to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which is prop-closed ({color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} only), inheritAttrs:false, and renders a hard-coded <span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">. All four call sites are silently discarded.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (no `tag`, no slot) + dist/watercolor-dot.js (`inheritAttrs: !1`, render `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", ... style:[...,{pointerEvents:"none"}]})`). MixSourceSelector.vue:148, :150, :164-176, :211-221. Live WebKit measurement (isolated, http://localhost:9000/#/mix, seeded 2-palette library), identical on light/1440, dark/1440, light/390: {"ghostTag":"SPAN","ghostAriaHidden":"true","ghostAriaLabel":null,"ghostPointerEvents":"none","ghostCursor":"pointer","plusPresent":false,"svgClasses":["watercolor-filter-host"],"hitTest":"DIV.swatch-row ...","focusablesInWell":0}; "clickAdd":{"before":0,"after":0}; "fromPalettes":{"firstSwatch":{"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"pe":"none"},"chipsAfterClick":0}; "tabOrder":["BUTTON :: Colors","BUTTON :: Palettes","BUTTON :: From palettes2","BUTTON :: Color space","BUTTON :: Hue method"]
defects.mechanism: Producer major-version adoption (glass-ui 7.0.0, W44) migrated the package but not the call sites; inheritAttrs:false swallows the dropped props and Vue emits no warning. Family-wide: `grep -rn 'tag="button"' demo` = 4 live sites (this file x2, GenerateControls.vue:203, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:98, SwatchHoverMenu.vue:17,32); `tag="div"` = 14 more.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/probe-mix.mjs — navigate /#/mix, seed localStorage["color-palettes"], reload, force-click .add-slot-ghost and every .w-8 palette swatch; [data-mix-source] stays at 0 in all three matrices. Manually: open http://localhost:9000/#/mix and try to add any color — there is no path.
defects.proposedCure: The dot is a FACE, never a SEAT — that is exactly what glass-ui 7 encodes by shipping it aria-hidden with pointer-events:none. Transpose the whole family: every operable dot becomes a real <button>/<div> seat that CONTAINS a <WatercolorDot> face, with the accessible name, disabled state, handler, focus ring and the Plus glyph on the seat. If the idiom recurs across the 6 sites, it is a producer ask (a WatercolorSwatchButton in glass-ui), never a demo wrapper.

defects.defect: The component applies a register law to its chips and violates it 60 lines later on its cards, and condemns guard-then-alpha de-emphasis in one comment while shipping it in the next block. The file argues against itself twice, in writing.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:134-145 excises `ring-2 ring-primary/50` and declares "rings on WatercolorDots ride the dot's own silhouette ... or do not exist — the dead utility is excised, never re-minted geometric"; :256-261 mints `ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background`. :186-189 kills a /50 alpha because "the token IS the de-emphasis rung; attenuating it further is the guard-then-alpha class"; :260 ships `opacity-75` (measured computed opacity 0.75 on the unselected seat).
defects.mechanism: Register laws were recorded as prose comments at the site that discovered them rather than encoded structurally, so a sibling block in the same file can violate them without any gate noticing.
defects.reproduction: Read MixSourceSelector.vue:134-145 vs :256-261 and :186-189 vs :260; live computed opacity of the unselected palettes-mode wrapper = 0.75 (probe-mix.mjs palettesMode.wrappers[].opacity).
defects.proposedCure: One selection register for the whole component, expressed on the entity the producer owns (PaletteCard's pressed seat per PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12), not an outer geometric ring; de-emphasis by rung token, never post-hoc alpha. Encode the law in the producer recipe so a sibling block cannot contradict it.

defects.defect: The colors-mode empty state — the state the app boots into — was never designed: a 462x108 CSS px well holding one inert 48px dot, no eyebrow, no message, no hint, no operable control. The sibling palettes-mode empty state in the same component ships a full EmptyState.
defects.evidence: Measured well/ink at four arms: 1440 -> 462x107.9 well, 48px ghost, ink share 4.36%; 720 -> 462x105.4, 4.73%; 390 -> 324x100.6 (44px ghost), 5.94%; 320 -> 254x100.6, 7.58%. Palettes-mode empty rendered text (Chromium, empty store): "· NOTHING TO MIX · / No saved palettes yet. / Save two or more palettes, then pour them together here." (MixSourceSelector.vue:239-244). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §1 and §5.3.
defects.mechanism: Two empty species were designed at different times by different waves; only the palettes one received the EmptyState treatment, and the colors one was left as a bare container because the (dead) ghost dot was assumed to be the invitation.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/mix with an empty color selection (default) and measure .dashed-well vs .add-slot-ghost; see docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png and safari-mobile-light/mix.png.
defects.proposedCure: One empty grammar for the component: the colors-mode empty speaks the same EmptyState invitation (eyebrow/message/hint + a real CTA seat) that palettes mode does, and the well collapses to the height its content actually needs instead of reserving a fixed void.

defects.defect: One palette entity, two visual grammars 40px apart in the same pane, and inside the hand-rolled one the same colors are encoded twice (full-bleed strip + a dot row repeating it). Two truncation policies for the same string.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:197-223 hand-rolls `rounded-card border border-border/30 overflow-hidden` + PaletteColorStrip + name + count + dot row (measured 462x124.9 desktop / 324x121.6 mobile; border resolves to oklab(.../0.3) and is invisible in dark — own capture mix-colors-dark-1440.png). :264-267 renders PaletteCard for the same object. Name truncation: `truncate` at :205 vs PaletteCard.vue's `line-clamp-2 sm:line-clamp-1`. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5.
defects.mechanism: A private card dialect was invented for the in-mode picker rather than composing the producer's PaletteCard, so the component now maintains two divergent presentations of one entity.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix.mjs then compare scratchpad/mix-colors-light-1440.png (colors mode, disclosure open) with scratchpad/mix-palettes-light-1440.png (palettes mode) — same two palettes, two grammars, and the strip/dot-row duplication visible in both light and dark captures.
defects.proposedCure: One palette-entity presentation in this component: the from-palettes picker composes PaletteCard in a compact composition whose swatches are real seats; delete the private dialect and the duplicate dot row (the strip already encodes the colors).

defects.defect: A native <button> wraps PaletteCard, producing a button inside a button, a role="article" inside a button, and a second click owner inside the first — and inverting PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12, which requires the card root to be noninteractive and its ONE named <button aria-pressed> to be a CHILD.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 (`<button type="button" :aria-pressed ...><PaletteCard .../></button>`); PaletteCard.vue:5-26 renders `<div role="article" ... cursor-pointer @click="$emit('click')">` containing `<Button aria-label="Palette menu">`. Measured: {"wrappers":[{"aria":"Select palette Sunset Drift","pressed":"false","nestedInteractive":["BUTTON:Palette menu"]}, ...]}. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.12 verbatim: "The Card/article root is a noninteractive container ... Its one native named <button type=\"button\" aria-pressed> child spans specimen/identity and alone owns activation, visible selection and focus."
defects.mechanism: Selection was bolted on from the outside because PaletteCard exposes no pressed-seat API to this consumer; wrapping was the cheapest way to get aria-pressed, at the cost of the content model and the canon's seat law.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix.mjs (palettesMode section) — nestedInteractive lists BUTTON:"Palette menu" inside every button[aria-pressed] wrapper. Or inspect the /#/mix Palettes tab DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Move the seat inside: PaletteCard exposes the §5.12 pressed seat (a named <button type="button" aria-pressed> spanning specimen/identity) and MixSourceSelector binds it. The wrapper button, the outer ring and the card root's own @click all disappear together.

defects.defect: Selection ring paints the wrong ground and shares one cascade channel with the focus ring: ring-offset-2 + ring-offset-background stamps --background (never the plate the card sits on), and focus-visible:ring-2 outranks the selection ring on the same --tw-ring-* properties, so a focused selected card loses its selection colour.
defects.evidence: Measured on the selected seat: box-shadow "... rgb(251,250,248) 0 0 0 2px, oklch(0.470927 0.093396 169.83403) 0 0 0 4px" (light); --tw-ring-offset-color: "hsl(24 9% 4%)" (dark), "light-dark(hsl(40 30% 98%), hsl(24 9% 4%))" (mobile). Class string (:256-261): 'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40' + 'ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background'. Both Tailwind v4 utilities write --tw-ring-width/--tw-ring-color/--tw-ring-shadow; .focus-visible\:ring-2:focus-visible has specificity 0,2,0 vs .ring-2 at 0,1,0. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier" and "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency." Light capture also shows the ring occluding the card's cartoon-surface cast that its unselected sibling keeps.
defects.mechanism: Selection is drawn at the wrong level (an outer wrapper with utility rings) instead of on the producer's own selected register, so it inherits --background as its offset ground and collides with the focus utility on one custom-property channel.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the focus collision — HYPOTHESIS. WebKit/macOS omits buttons from Tab order by default (60 Tab presses never reached the seat) and the Chromium arm did not receive the seeded library; the offset-ground and cast-occlusion halves ARE measured (probe-mix.mjs palettesMode.afterSelect + scratchpad/mix-palettes-light-1440.png).
defects.proposedCure: Selection moves onto the producer's pressed seat (with D-5) and uses a register that is not the focus channel — a producer-owned selected face/border rung — leaving focus-visible as the sole owner of --tw-ring-*. The ring-offset against --background dies with the wrapper.

defects.defect: The disclosure per-instance-overrides its own producer recipe: it re-declares overflow:hidden, replaces the house spring with a generic 0.2s ease-out under a FOURTH animation family name, and hand-rolls the chevron rotation off a local ref instead of the producer's data-state — two sources of truth for "open".
defects.evidence: Producer recipe node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/disclosure.css: `.disclosure-content{overflow:hidden;animation-duration:var(--spring-smooth-duration);animation-timing-function:var(--spring-smooth)}`, `.disclosure-content[data-state="open"]{animation-name:disclosure-open}`, `.disclosure-group-trigger[data-state="open"]>.disclosure-icon{rotate:180deg}`, plus its own PRM and forced-colors blocks. Consumer MixSourceSelector.vue:195 `overflow-hidden data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down data-[state=closed]:animate-collapsible-up`; :190-193 hand-rolled ChevronDown + `:class="paletteDropdownOpen && 'rotate-180'"`. Measured on the open content: {"cls":"disclosure-content overflow-hidden data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down ...","animationName":"collapsible-down","animationDuration":"0.2s","animationTiming":"ease-out","--disclosure-content-size":"265.875px"}. demo/styles/animations.css:60: "three named families; a fourth name is a defect (gate (a), R.W4 §Hard gate)" — the sanctioned families being vj-enter/vj-morph/vj-celebrate, one of which this same file uses at :121.
defects.mechanism: A shadcn-era collapsible idiom was carried onto a glass-ui primitive that already owns the whole register, so consumer utilities now beat producer declarations on animation-name, duration and timing, and the open state is duplicated in a local ref.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix4.mjs — click the "From palettes" trigger and read getComputedStyle('.disclosure-content'): animationName collapsible-down, duration 0.2s, timing ease-out, while the element also carries the producer's .disclosure-content class.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the three utilities and the hand-rolled chevron; consume the producer disclosure whole (its spring, its overflow, its .disclosure-icon and its data-state-driven rotation, its PRM and forced-colors blocks). If a different curve is wanted it is a producer token, not a consumer override.

defects.defect: Two type registers for one job in one component: the section label "Selected" renders Fraunces 600 (a display family at semibold for a control label) while its sibling section label "From palettes" renders the glass-ui .section-label primitive in Fira Code 400 uppercase.
defects.evidence: Measured: "Selected" — family Fraunces, 16.4px (14px mobile), weight 600, transform none, tracking normal, hand-rolled `text-small font-display font-semibold text-muted-foreground` (MixSourceSelector.vue:119). "From palettes" — family "Fira Code", 14.384px, weight 400, transform uppercase, tracking 1.4384px, via glass-ui `.section-label` (:183; recipe at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css `.section-label{@apply text-mono-caption;color:var(--muted-foreground)}`). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4: control or label -> text-small -> "Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold".
defects.mechanism: The first label was styled inline at the site before the .section-label primitive was consumed by the second; nothing forced the two to converge.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix2.mjs — rhythm.selectedLabel vs rhythm.fromPalettesLabel computed styles on http://localhost:9000/#/mix.
defects.proposedCure: Both section labels consume the one .section-label primitive; the type-role matrix decides the register once, at the root, for every section label in the workbench family.

defects.defect: The disclosure trigger is a 29.6px-tall tap target (26.3px on mobile) because the consumer's py-1 is its whole vertical measure; glass-ui's own trigger recipe carries a 44px min-block-size that is bypassed.
defects.evidence: Measured: {"cls":"disclosure-trigger flex items-center gap-2 w-full cursor-pointer group py-1","rect":{"w":462,"h":29.6},"minBlockSize":"0px","padding":"4px 0px"}; mobile 324x26.3. Producer: `.disclosure-group-trigger{min-block-size:2.75rem}` (disclosure.css). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-12. The audit's smallTapTargets sweep does not flag it (its threshold clears 24px), so REPORT.json's 8 mix rows miss this one.
defects.mechanism: The consumer supplied its own layout classes to the producer trigger instead of consuming the producer's sized trigger composition, so the 44px floor never applied.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix4.mjs — report.trigger rect/minBlockSize/padding on http://localhost:9000/#/mix.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the producer's sized trigger composition (or its 2.75rem floor token) so operable geometry is owned at the root and the optics ride the rung — never a py-1 at the site.

defects.defect: The disclosure trigger's accessible name is "From palettes2" — the label and the palette count are adjacent text nodes with no separator or aria-label; the count is also a bare unlabelled number.
defects.evidence: Measured accName: "From palettes2" (probe-mix4.mjs report.trigger.accName). Source: MixSourceSelector.vue:183 (label span) + :184 (count span). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5.
defects.mechanism: Two sibling spans inside a button concatenate into one accessible name with no text separator.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix4.mjs, or read the accessible name of the "From palettes" button on /#/mix.
defects.proposedCure: Give the trigger an explicit accessible name that states the relation (e.g. label plus a counted noun), and let the visible count be a labelled data mark rather than a naked integer.

defects.defect: The one motion the component designs is architecturally prevented: TransitionGroup keys embed the array index, so removing one chip invalidates every surviving chip's key — the row plays three leaves and two enters instead of one leave plus a move, and the shared .vj-enter-move neighbour reflow can never fire.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:79-89 keys on `${sc.css}::${i}`. Exact algorithm replay (node -e): initial [0,1,2] -> after removing index 0 [3,4] -> re-add [0,1,2] -> duplicates [0,5]. demo/styles/utils.css:168-178 exists precisely so "neighbours reflow on the family move class" (.vj-enter-move); with index-bearing keys no element survives to be moved. The watch at :90-98 then prunes the map, guaranteeing keys are never reused.
defects.mechanism: SelectedColor ({css, source}) carries no identity, so the site manufactured one from position — which is exactly the quantity a removal changes.
defects.reproduction: NONE in the running app (the populated state is unreachable per D-1). Algorithm replayed exactly: node -e '<swatchKeys replay>' — output pasted in the report §D-11.
defects.proposedCure: Mint identity at the source: useMixingState.addColor stamps a stable id on each SelectedColor; the key becomes sc.id and the key map, the counter and the pruning watcher (~20 lines) are deleted outright.

defects.defect: One vertical interval is nudged out of the tokenised rhythm: the root is gap-3 (12px) everywhere, but the tabs wrapper adds pb-1, making that single seam 16px.
defects.evidence: Measured children of the gap-3 root: tabs [245.2 -> 288.2], well [300.2 -> 408.1], disclosure [420.1 -> 449.7]; computed gap 12px; MixSourceSelector.vue:104 `flex items-center justify-center pb-1`. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.3 (one owner per interval).
defects.mechanism: A per-instance padding nudge stacked on a systematic gap token, so two mechanisms own one seam.
defects.reproduction: node probe-mix2.mjs — rhythm.kids rects and rootGap on http://localhost:9000/#/mix.
defects.proposedCure: One spacing owner per interval: delete pb-1 and let the section rhythm token carry the seam (or name a distinct tabs->content token if the interval genuinely differs).

defects.defect: `:css-color="''"` passes an empty string to an optional prop, defeating the designed nullish fallback in PaletteCard.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:266 `:css-color="''"`; PaletteCard.vue:186 `cssColor?: string | undefined`; PaletteCard.vue:226 `props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? props.cssColor ?? EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH` — '' is not nullish, so a zero-colour palette renders an empty CSS colour instead of EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH.
defects.mechanism: A placeholder value was supplied to satisfy an API the consumer has no value for, masking the fallback the producer designed.
defects.reproduction: Read MixSourceSelector.vue:266 against PaletteCard.vue:186,226. Render repro requires a zero-colour palette.
defects.proposedCure: Omit the prop. Optional props are omitted, never stubbed with a sentinel value.

defects.defect: The chip remove badge is positioned with physical insets (-top-1 -right-1) in a layout that mirrors under RTL, so it does not follow its chip's logical corner.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:153 `absolute -top-1 -right-1`. RTL measured (dir=rtl): well x224 w462, ghost x624.5 — the row's leading edge moves to the right, i.e. the layout mirrors while a physical `right` inset does not.
defects.mechanism: Physical inset utilities in a component whose flex row is direction-aware.
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Chips are unreachable (D-1), so the mirrored badge cannot be photographed; the container mirroring is measured (probe-mix2.mjs report.rtl).
defects.proposedCure: Logical insets (inset-inline-end / inset-block-start) throughout, so the badge rides the chip's logical corner in both directions.

defects.defect: The chip remove control is hover-only, has no accessible name, and is a 16x16 CSS px target with no touch reveal path.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:152-158: `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, `w-4 h-4`, icon-only <X> with no aria-label and no text; only focus-visible:opacity-100 offers a non-hover reveal, which needs a keyboard. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-07 ("Hover-only/unlabeled controls ... every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state") and §5.7 (glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities).
defects.mechanism: A hover-reveal desktop idiom applied to a control that must also be reachable by touch and AT.
defects.reproduction: NONE in the running app — blocked by D-1; CONFIRMED in source at :152-158.
defects.proposedCure: A named, persistently discoverable remove seat with an invisible 44px hit area and a visible glyph at the rung — never a hover-gated 16px nameless badge.

defects.defect: Import discipline is internally inconsistent: three glass-ui subpath imports plus one routed through a demo/ui barrel that re-exports the package root, and TransitionGroup is imported explicitly while the parent uses <Transition> unimported.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:4,:7 (@mkbabb/glass-ui/tabs, /watercolor-dot) vs :5 (../../ui/collapsible, whose body is `export { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`); `grep -rln "ui/collapsible" demo` returns exactly this file. :2 imports TransitionGroup while MixPane.vue:111 uses <Transition> unimported. Note: demo/ui/* is a house-wide barrel layer (19 barrels, all re-exporting glass-ui), so this is consistency, not a boundary violation.
defects.mechanism: Two import idioms coexist in one file; the barrel path additionally pulls the package root rather than a subpath.
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/collapsible/index.ts; grep -rln "ui/collapsible" demo
defects.proposedCure: One import idiom per file — subpath imports for glass-ui throughout — and drop the redundant TransitionGroup import (Vue 3.5 resolves built-ins in templates).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declaration present, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — `object-contain` is defeated and the Extract route's declared protagonist (the source image) is silently centre-cropped: a 400x1200 portrait renders at 1374px inside a 320px clipping box (527px cropped top AND bottom, 23.3% visible), and in the same frame the extracted palette names purple, red and orange — three colours that appear nowhere in the visible preview. The component's own comment (ImageDropZone.vue:3) claims "the specimen never lies".
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the report is not read as uniform condemnation — four registers were tested and hold: (1) Motion is fully tokenized (vj-enter/vj-morph from demo/styles/animations.css:83-139 driven by --duration-*/--spring-*/--ease-*; no component-local duration literals) and the global prefers-reduced-motion guard (animations.css:184-193) genuinely neutralises it — measured live animation count 19 -> 6 between the desk-light and reduced-motion matrices (probe-D-geometry.json). (2) Zero horizontal overflow at every arm: overflowX = 0 at 1440, 720 (200% zoom), 390 mobile, 360 (400% zoom), LTR and RTL — 8/8 matrices (probe-D-geometry.json). (3) Zero page errors and zero component-attributable console errors on /#/extract across the 4 census matrices (visual/REPORT.md per-capture table) and my 8 (only line is the pre-existing dev VITE_API_URL notice). (4) The contrast remediation is real: --ink-muted resolves to oklch(0.4469 0.0039 34.6) light / oklch(0.8894 0.0038 41.9) dark and the O-18 track-ink cure did move the sliders off the recorded born-RED 1.88:1 / 1.85:1. verbatimModuleSyntax is clean (import type { SpaceId } at ExtractWorkbench.vue:189 is the only type-only import and is correctly marked); props use the Vue 3.5 reactive-destructure idiom and emits are typed.

defects.defect: `object-contain` is defeated: the uploaded source image overflows its `overflow-hidden` container and is silently centre-cropped, so the preview contradicts the extracted palette in the same frame.
defects.evidence: probe-D-type-crop.json (400x1200 portrait, 1440x900): {"imgBox":{"y":-326.3,"h":1374,"bottom":1047.7}, "zoneBox":{"y":200.7,"h":320,"bottom":520.7}, "objectFit":"contain", "croppedTopPx":527, "croppedBottomPx":527, "visibleFractionPct":23.3}. probe-D-final.json (2400px square): img h=458 in dropMaxH "320px". Frame: frames-crop/portrait-crop.png shows a 6-band image rendering as yellow+green only, with the palette below reading purple/red/green/yellow/orange. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:41 (`w-full h-full object-contain`) + ExtractWorkbench.vue:20 (`max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]`).
defects.mechanism: height:100% against an indefinite containing-block height resolves to auto, so the img takes its intrinsic aspect at the full 458px width; the max-height cap lives on the container, which then clips with justify-center splitting the overflow top/bottom.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-type-crop.mjs ; open frames-crop/portrait-crop.png
defects.proposedCure: REPLACE, not patch. The preview is a stage, not a capped flow child. Give the drop-zone root a definite block size (aspect-ratio, or an h-[clamp()] on the root rather than a max-h on a content-sized box) so object-contain has a real box to fit into, and let the specimen letterbox against the well ground. Cropping the protagonist to preserve a layout rhythm is the wrong trade for a colour-extraction instrument.

defects.defect: The `isProcessing` loading state never renders. During the entire compute window the UI shows the unchanged empty-state ghost and the caption "· undeveloped plate — feed it an image ·", instructing the user to do what they have already done.
defects.evidence: probe-D-final.json, MutationObserver + per-rAF occupant sampler, Chrome CPU throttled 20x, 2400x2400 source: OCCUPANT TRACE = [[0,"ghost"],[2894,"card"]] — two occupants in 2.9 seconds; SKELETON never appears. Corroborated unthrottled in both engines (probe-D-focus-transition.json: ghost through t≈210ms, then card; no SKEL sample in 60 samples over 2.1s). Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:102-107 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` + `v-if="session.isProcessing.value"`). The claim it breaks is ExtractWorkbench.vue:92-99: "isProcessing swaps ghost → KNOWN-IMMINENT skeleton IN PLACE (same bones — a material change, not a layout jump)".
defects.mechanism: `mode="out-in"` holds the entering branch until the leaving branch's transition resolves; by then isProcessing has flipped back to false, so the branch that wins is always the developed card. The out-in mode chosen to protect the skeleton is what makes it unreachable. The `role="status"` / aria-label="Loading palette" announcement is likewise never made.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-final.mjs — read the OCCUPANT TRACE line.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse ShadowPalette and PaletteCardSkeleton into ONE plate component with state: "empty" | "working" | "developed", and drop mode="out-in" so the working register can cross-fade in. The 'same bones' promise then holds structurally instead of by hand-copy across two files (which already differ: ShadowPalette strip uses gap-px + flex-1, PaletteCardSkeleton uses no gap + width:100/count%).

defects.defect: The NORMATIVE card-lock law is violated on both of its arms: a slider value change moves the containing Card by 128px, and the one Fraunces display-scale live number lacks tabular-nums, jittering the readout row by 21.88px per value change.
defects.evidence: demo/DESIGN.md '### The card-lock law (NORMATIVE — R.W3 Lane A / A6, U31)': "a value change may never move the card: dragging any component slider from min to max changes NO containing card rect (±0px)" + "a Fraunces-set number MUST declare tabular-nums". probe-D-cardlock.json: empty-k5 pane {"y":200.98,"h":578.27} ghost h=150 ; empty-k16 pane {"y":137.00,"h":706.27} ghost h=278 → Δh=+128.00px, Δy=−63.98px. img-k1 statRect.w=191.36 rightGroup.x=427.36 code.x=526.88 code.w=155.13 ; img-k5 statRect.w=169.48 rightGroup.x=405.48 code.x=505.00 code.w=177.00 → Δ=21.88px; fontFamily "Fraunces", fontSize "41.888px", fontVariantNumeric "normal", fontFeatureSettings "normal". Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:122 (no tabular-nums), vs ExtractControls.vue:15 and :78 which both declare it.
defects.mechanism: ShadowPalette's swatch row wraps at 6-per-row so each 6 colours of k adds a 64px band; and a proportional-figure Fraunces number inside a `flex items-baseline` row with `ml-auto` on the right group propagates its own width change into the eyebrow + readout position and into the readout's available width (so the colour string's truncation point moves with an unrelated statistic).
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-cardlock.mjs — compare the empty-k5/empty-k16 pane rects and the img-k1/img-k5 statRect widths.
defects.proposedCure: tabular-nums on the dominance stat (one class), and reserve the ghost's swatch band from a fixed row count rather than letting k reflow it — the instrument's SHAPE is the information, not its row count. At k>=7 the empty placeholder (214px) already exceeds the drop zone (180px).

defects.defect: Empty secondary content occupies 31–72% of the pane, 2–5x over the binding ≤15% ceiling.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.2: "Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears." Measured (ghost + gap-2 + caption) / pane block size, from probe-D-geometry.json + probe-D-cardlock.json: desktop k=5 → 179.58/578.27 = 31.1%; desktop k=16 → 307.58/706.27 = 43.6%; mobile 390 → 186.50/552 = 33.8%; 400% zoom (360px) → 242.30/338 = 71.7%. By area at desktop k=5: 462x150 = 69,300px² of a 512x578.27 = 296,074px² pane = 23.4%, i.e. 83% of the drop zone's own area.
defects.mechanism: The empty result is rendered as a full-material counterfeit of the answer (a k-sized card) instead of an invitation; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04 is the owning family ("Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE. Collapse absent support").
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-D-geometry.mjs — read the ghost/caption/pane rects across the desk-light, mobile-light, zoom-200 and zoom-400 matrices.
defects.proposedCure: REMOVE. The empty result collapses to a one-line invitation in the flow; the plate's shape is not information the user needs before an image exists.

defects.defect: The binding Extract mobile order is inverted: controls precede the result.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1, Extract row: "Mobile order | source, sampled result, controls"; §3.6 repeats "stage→inspector→action". Measured at mobile-light 390 (probe-D-geometry.json): dropZone y=182 → kRail y=378 (controls) → ghost y=469 (result). Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:64 places <ExtractControls> before the result <Transition> at line 102 in the same column, so the order is structural and identical on desktop.
defects.mechanism: The workbench composes one flat flex column with the dial cluster ahead of the output seat, so the pane leads with a control before it has shown anything to control.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-D-geometry.mjs — the mobile-light rects block.
defects.proposedCure: TRANSPOSE: result seat before the control cluster in the single column, matching the ratified composition; the controls become the trailing action region.

defects.defect: Material-tier inversion — the empty placeholder is the heaviest object in the pane, out-shadowing and out-opaquing the input protagonist.
defects.evidence: probe-D-geometry.json (desk-light computed styles): drop zone (the input protagonist) dropBg = oklab(0.470927 -0.080988 0.097088 / 0.05) with 2px dashed edge at α0.3 and NO shadow; ghost (empty output) ghostBg = oklab(0.913299 0.005463 0.013024) — α 1.0 — with a solid --card-edge hairline and a 3-layer shadow-cartoon-sm; pane Card α 0.664. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.8: "Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow." Frames: visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png and safari-mobile-light/extract.png show the grey-block reading.
defects.mechanism: The pane is translucent (α 0.664) and picks up the live aurora, so it reads warm pink; the ghost is opaque and shows only its own near-neutral token — a dead grey rectangle on a chromatic plate, in a chromatic-laboratory product. The same frame's right-hand pane renders TRUE EMPTY as a dashed, plate-tinted dot trio: two empty grammars side by side in one screenshot, and ShadowPalette.vue's own header concedes the rule ("TRUE EMPTY speaks the EmptyState dot trio — N-3 re-aimed").
defects.reproduction: Open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png ; colours from probe-D-geometry.json.
defects.proposedCure: TIGHTEN: the empty plate loses opacity and the cartoon shadow — it must sit BELOW the input in material tier, not above. Better still, adopt the app's own EmptyState dot-trio grammar so one route does not ship two empty species in one frame.

defects.defect: Type-role inversion: a derived support statistic is set at exactly the pane identity's rung, in the same family.
defects.evidence: probe-D-type-crop.json + live eval: pane identity H3 "Extract" fontSize 41.888px Fraunces; dominance stat "33% of the image" fontSize 41.888px Fraunces — identical. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.13: "route H1/major argument text-display; instrument identity --type-title"; §5.11: "A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading or live status"; §3.8 "do not compete … through equal size". Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:122 `class="font-display text-display"`.
defects.mechanism: text-display was applied to a support readout that has no claim on the display rung, so the pane has two protagonists at identical scale 480px apart.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-D-type-crop.mjs — read the `type` block.
defects.proposedCure: TIGHTEN: the stat drops one golden rung below the identity; identity keeps the display voice alone.

defects.defect: The dominant-colour readout displays 31% of itself at the reference desktop viewport; chroma and hue — the colour's identity — are entirely cut.
defects.evidence: probe-D-type-crop.json: readoutFull "oklch(56.686341050833% 0.147031011912 285.636092993966deg)", readoutShownPx 182, readoutNeededPx 585, readoutTruncated true → 182/585 = 31.1%. What survives is `oklch(56.68634105…` — twelve significant digits of lightness. Visible in frames-crop/portrait-crop.png and frames-final/final-populated.png. Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:137-141 (`truncate`), with the pre-excuse at lines 134-136.
defects.mechanism: Two compounding causes: the serializer emits 12-significant-digit precision for a DISPLAY string, and the 41.888px stat (D-7) consumes the line before the readout gets any width. A `title` attribute does not rescue it — invisible to touch, to keyboard, and in a screenshot.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-D-type-crop.mjs — read readoutShownPx / readoutNeededPx.
defects.proposedCure: TIGHTEN: display precision belongs to the display — round to the house readout precision — and give the value its own line. It is the answer, not a footnote to a percentage.

defects.defect: RTL is not honoured by either slider: the fill and thumb do not mirror, so the value label and its own gauge point in opposite directions.
defects.evidence: probe-D-geometry.json, thumb offset from its track's start edge — Number of colors: LTR 364.5−252 = 112.5, RTL 866.5−754 = 112.5; Chroma weight: LTR 433.4−360.5 = 72.9, RTL 921.8−849 = 72.9. Identical to the tenth of a pixel. Frame: frames/rtl-desk.png shows the "5" readout at the far right with the crimson fill growing from the far left. The container DOES mirror (rail inset flips side, label crosses the track), so the omission is isolated to the Slider primitive's direction handling.
defects.mechanism: `dir` is not threaded to the reka-ui Slider primitive, so min stays on the physical left while the surrounding flex row mirrors around it.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-D-geometry.mjs — compare the rtl-desk and desk-light `thumbs` arrays.
defects.proposedCure: ADD-AFFORDANCE: pass `dir` through to the Slider primitive at the demo/ui/slider root (root-level, not per-instance), so every slider in the app inherits the fix rather than this instrument alone.

defects.defect: Both slider thumbs are 12 CSS px wide — half the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 minimum — in all four census matrices and all eight of mine, and provide no visible handle affordance.
defects.evidence: visual/REPORT.json, every /#/extract row: {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Number of colors"} and {"w":12,"h":24,...,"Chroma weight"} desktop; {"w":12,"h":44,...} mobile. Reproduced independently in probe-D-geometry.json at 1440, 720 (200% zoom), 390 and 360 (400% zoom). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.7: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities."
defects.mechanism: All three quantities collapsed into one 12px bar; the thumb is exactly as tall as the 24px rail, so it fills the groove and reads as a colour break in the fill rather than a grabbable handle.
defects.reproduction: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json'));[print(r['matrix'],r['probe']['a11y']['smallTapTargets']) for r in d['results'] if 'extract' in r['route']]"
defects.proposedCure: ENLARGE the operable width to >=24px via an invisible seat while the visible glyph follows its own rung — exactly the separation §5.7 mandates.

defects.defect: The eyedropper is keyboard-unreachable by construction, while its own aria-label advertises the action to screen-reader users.
defects.evidence: probe-D-populated.json: "dropTabindex": {"tabindex":"-1", "label":"Image preview area, tap to sample colors", "cursor":"crosshair"}. TAB ORDER with an image loaded (extract pane only): span[Number of colors] → button[Upload image] → button[Open camera] → span[Chroma weight] → button[Reset] → button[Palette menu] — the preview never receives focus. Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:23 `:disable-click="!!session.previewDataUrl.value"` → ImageDropZone.vue:19 `:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"`; the keyboard handler at ImageDropZone.vue:22 is gated on `!disableClick`, so even forced focus would not open the sampler.

defects.defect: Camera failures are routed through the quantizer's error channel with a raw Error object interpolated into user-facing copy, with no dismiss; and the viewfinder renders a black box during the permission prompt with no state.

ExtractWorkbench.vue:240-247 sets `cameraActive.value = true` BEFORE awaiting getUserMedia, so an empty `bg-stage` rectangle renders during the permission prompt.

defects.proposedCure: Separate the camera register from the quantize register (error != error), map exceptions to house copy rather than interpolating `${err}`, give the error a dismiss, and add an explicit 'awaiting camera' state before the stream arrives.
