result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (the 1M-context Opus 5 seat), matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Not an inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — every demo-side import boundary in eslint.config.js is dead lint. The G-DEMO-1 / G-DEMO-3a / G-DEMO-3b rules are scoped to `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`, `demo/@/composables/**`; `demo/@` has not existed since W43/RF-15 (`ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory), and the banned specifier shape `@components/custom/**` was deleted with the aliases (vite.config.ts:66-71). `npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue` reports `no-restricted-imports = undefined`. Not the largest single cost — L-2 and L-3 cost more — but the one that made every other finding possible and will make them recur: nineteen alias barrels, a three-hop re-export chain, a 72-module cross-feature edge, and a `Ref<any>` shell handle all survive in a repo that believes it enforces its lattice.
result.negativeProof: Two sub-axes are genuinely SOUND with positive proof. (N-1) value.js is consumed exclusively through the published subpath export map: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/value.js" demo | sed …| sort | uniq -c` → 24 `/color`, 10 `/css`, 6 `/math`, 5 `/easing`, 4 `/quantize` — zero deep paths, zero bare-root imports (there is no "." export: `node -e "'.' in p.exports"` → false), and `grep -rn "@src/" demo` → no output. vite.config.ts:38-51 GENERATES the self-alias set from package.json#exports, so the alias set cannot drift from the published surface. Every library import this component makes is one a real npm consumer could write verbatim. (N-2) verbatimModuleSyntax is fully satisfied: grepping all 9 files of the cluster for non-`import type` lines containing a type specifier returns no output.

defects.defect: Every demo-side `no-restricted-imports` boundary rule is dead: the globs target the pre-W43 `demo/@/**` tree, which does not exist, and ban a specifier shape (`@components/custom/**`) that was deleted with the demo path aliases.
defects.evidence: eslint.config.js:230-300 (globs `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`, `demo/@/composables/**`); `ls -d demo/@` → `ls: demo/@: No such file or directory`; vite.config.ts:66-71 states "W43 (RF-15) killed the demo `@…` path aliases"; `npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue` → `no-restricted-imports for GradientVisualizer.vue = undefined`

Re-express the demo lattice as four layer tags — platform → session (color-session) → feature (palettes, workbenches/*, scenes/*, picker) → shell — with `shared` as a zero-dependency leaf, edges pointing down only and sibling feature→feature banned outright; add a lint assertion that the union of layer globs COVERS `demo/**`, so an unclassified or moved directory is itself the lint error. Only `inv-K-1` (files: ["src/**/*.ts"], banning src/→glass-ui) is live today and is correct.

defects.defect: Importing one zero-dependency `Symbol` (`LIBRARY_PORT_KEY`) from the palettes provider god-module drags 72 modules — the entire palettes + admin + api + auth graph — into the lazily code-split gradient route.

defects.defect: The value.js `/css` ↔ `/easing` seam is missing BOTH halves of its round-trip, and this component's tree owns both re-implementations — one of which is hand-mirrored byte-for-byte from a private glass-ui function with no test binding them.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "serializeTimingFunction\|serializeEasing\|timingFunctionToCss" src/` → no output (parseCssColor/serializeCssColor are symmetric; parseTimingFunction has no inverse). Missing half A — AST→callable — lives at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:106-117 (`timingFunctionValue(ast: CssTimingFunction): EasingFunction`, both types library-owned) plus linearStops() at :80-104 re-implementing the CSS Easing Functions L2 linear() position-fill because CssLinearStop (src/css/types.ts:28, `input: number[]`) and LinearEasingStop (src/easing.ts:14, both fields required) ship with no conversion. Missing half B — value→literal — at easing/easingCatalogue.ts:41-58, whose own comment reads "The literal mint law (byte-identity with the picker) … glass-ui `useEasingPicker.readout` mints cubic-bezier(…) by mapping each coordinate through +n.toFixed(3) … MUST be byte-identical"; the canonical serializer is unexported in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js:33-35.
defects.mechanism: a published capability seam with only one direction implemented — every consumer needing the other direction mints its own, so N consumers yield N implementations and "one home per concept" is broken by the library's shape, not by consumer carelessness
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "serializeTimingFunction|serializeEasing|timingFunctionToCss" src/` (empty) plus the three cited file:line blocks and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js:33-35. NONE for the future-desync consequence — that half is labelled a hypothesis; the duplication itself is fact.
defects.proposedCure: value.js `/css` gains `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` (the exact inverse of the parseTimingFunction it ships, the exact sibling of the parseCssColor/serializeCssColor pair); `/easing` gains `easingOf(ast: CssTimingFunction): Result<EasingFunction, EasingIssue>`. `linearStops` moves into `/css` as part of parseTimingFunction's own normalisation so CssLinearStop.input is already resolved at the API boundary. glass-ui's useEasingPicker.readout and the demo's bezierLiteral/stepsLiteral then both call one published function and byte identity becomes structural. Net deletion ~65 demo lines, ~10 glass-ui lines, one comment-enforced invariant.

defects.defect: The CSS-timing bridge in useGradientCSS.ts is unreachable at runtime — a parameter type was deliberately weakened so a test could reach an otherwise-impossible branch, and ~65 lines plus five library imports ship to the browser dead. It is also a false proof that the demo dogfoods `parseTimingFunction`.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:49 `type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue`; glass-ui dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts declares `readonly fn: EasingFn;` — REQUIRED. useGradientCSS.ts:120-122 weakens it to `Pick<GradientInterval,"css"> & Partial<Pick<GradientInterval,"fn">>`, then `:123` `if (interval.fn) return interval.fn;` always fires. Call-site census: production sites useGradientCSS.ts:190, GradientVisualizer.vue:78, easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52 all pass a full GradientInterval; only test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:49-50 passes an fn-less object. Dead: resolvedEasingCache (:69), easingValue (:71-77), linearStops (:80-104), timingFunctionValue (:106-117), the easingFnOf fallback body (:124-132), plus the imports of CubicBezier, easing, linearEasing, steppedEase, parseTimingFunction.
defects.mechanism: a type deliberately weakened at the boundary so a test can reach an unreachable branch — the test's convenience became production surface
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "easingFnOf" demo test` and cross-read the five call sites against glass-ui's `readonly fn: EasingFn;` declaration
defects.proposedCure: With L-3 landed, easingFnOf collapses to `interval.fn` and disappears; the CSS-literal→callable path becomes `easingOf(parseTimingFunction(css))` — a library function with library tests, in test/ where it belongs. Delete the module-level unbounded, never-cleared `resolvedEasingCache` Map with it.

defects.defect: Two sampling laws exist for one stated invariant, and they disagree by 107/255 on the red channel: the add-ghost/minted-stop colour (exact, component-local `colorAtPosition`) differs from the colour the rail actually paints (33 discrete stops the browser blends linearly).
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:2-4 claims the module "owns the ONE sampling law (`sampleCoalescedStops`)"; the second law is GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 `colorAtPosition(position)`, in `<script setup>` where it cannot be unit-tested or reused. Measured against the published dist/subpaths: `easing = steps(4, jump-end), stops = oklch(0.75 0.15 145) -> oklch(0.65 0.18 265); worst disagreement: {"pos":24.99,"d":107,"A":[107,198,112],"B":[0,197,160]}` — 42% of the red channel range.
defects.mechanism: the composable exposed only `model → samples[]`; the component needed `position → colour`, found no seam, and grew one. A stated invariant with no single callable to enforce it is a comment, not an invariant.
defects.reproduction: `node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/sampling.mjs`. In the app: set an interval to steps(4, jump-end) and hover the rail near 25% — the ghost previews rgb(107,198,112) while the rail under the cursor is rgb(0,197,160).
defects.proposedCure: Make `rampColorAt(model, position): AnyColor` the primitive and define `sampleCoalescedStops` as `positions.map(p => rampColorAt(model, p))` — one law, literally. L-17's native `in <space>` serialization then removes the discretisation and the divergence cannot exist.

defects.defect: `railRampCSS` recomputes on every `direction` and `type` change, values it provably never reads, because all three CSS computeds hang off one monolithic `modelState` object.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:102-109 builds a single `modelState` computed carrying all six fields; useGradientCSS.ts:325-327 derives three computeds from it. `serializeRailRamp` (useGradientCSS.ts:266-275) reads only stops and — via sampleCoalescedStops — intervals/interpolationSpace/hueMethod; it never reads type or direction (the rail is always `linear-gradient(90deg, …)`). The direction Slider is min 0 / max 360 / step 1 (GradientVisualizer.vue:232). Measured cost: `sampleCoalescedStops + serialize, 2-stop default model: 0.044 ms per call; per direction-slider tick the tree runs it TWICE (coalescedCSS + railRampCSS): 0.089 ms; sample count: 33, serialized bytes: 787`.
defects.mechanism: one god-shaped state object as the sole dependency surface; Vue does not deep-compare a computed returning a fresh object literal, so every consumer invalidates on every field
defects.reproduction: Read useGradientCSS.ts:266-275 (no type/direction access) against useGradientModel.ts:102-109 (both in the dependency); confirmed by construction. Cost measured by `node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/perf.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Split the state at its real invalidation seam: `rampState` (stops, intervals, interpolationSpace, hueMethod) and `geometry` (type, direction). railRampCSS depends on rampState alone; coalescedCSS composes both. The two serializers also stop computing the identical sample array twice.

defects.defect: The gradient serializers emit no `<color-interpolation-method>`, so the browser blends all 33 oklch sub-stops in sRGB; the entire coalescing apparatus exists to compensate for a serializer the library does not publish, on a platform that has supported the native form for years.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:219-224 (`rampGradient`) and :281-305 (`serializeCoalescedGradient`) emit `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` / `${type}-gradient(…)` with no `in <space>` clause. Measured live on the running app: `CSS.supports('background-image','linear-gradient(in oklch, red, blue)')` → true; `…'linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue, red, blue)'` → true; `…'conic-gradient(in oklab from 90deg, red, blue)'` → true. Computed styles: `.gradient-rail` → `{ subStops: 33, hasInterpMethod: false, bytes: 1478 }`; `[data-testid=gradient-render-tile]` → `{ subStops: 33, hasInterpMethod: false, bytes: 1471 }`.
defects.mechanism: the demo compensates in code for a missing library capability; ~1.5 KB of generated CSS per surface per keystroke to make an sRGB blend imperceptible
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: the three CSS.supports calls plus getComputedStyle(...).backgroundImage on .gradient-rail and [data-testid=gradient-render-tile].
defects.proposedCure: Move `serializeGradient` into value.js `/css`, emitting `linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue, <stops>)` natively and baking sub-stops ONLY where an interval carries a non-linear easing (easing genuinely cannot be expressed natively; space and hue-method can). Sub-stop density then only has to resolve the easing curve, not the colour space — a far weaker requirement — and L-5's divergence collapses with it. Pairs with lifting gradientParse.ts (301 L) into `/css` as `parseGradient`: `grep -rn "gradient" src/ -i` returns NOTHING today, and gradientParse.ts:12-16 names the library's flat-FunctionValue comma-grouping loss as the reason it had to hand-roll textual segmentation — a library defect documented in the demo instead of fixed in the library.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — `easingCatalogue.ts:174` re-declares value.js's easing taxonomy as a hardcoded `FAMILY_ORDER` allow-list and then FILTERS by it, silently dropping 6 of the library's 30 `bezierPresets` (the entire quart + quint families). Measured: the live strip renders 27 tiles; the library offers 33. Downstream, `tileIdFor` cannot name a quart/quint interval, so a first-class library curve reads as `custom` in the row head with no tile pressed. The gate is blind (`test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56` asserts only `length > 20`). Mechanism = the axis itself: the library publishes the presets as a bare Record without their taxonomy, so the consumer re-derived it by regex and closed it by hand — and it rotted.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the seat killed ten obvious CHALLENGE-L hypotheses with positive evidence, recorded in the report's "Negative proofs" section: (1) NO deep-import / false public-API proof — every library import in the subtree resolves through a real key in `package.json#exports` (`./easing`) or glass-ui's exports map (`./fading-scroll`, `./chip`, `./easing`, `./motion-core`), and `vite.config.ts:41-51` GENERATES the runtime alias set from the exports map so drift is structurally impossible; (2) `dist/` is FRESH — `find src -name "*.ts" -newer dist/subpaths/easing.js` returns empty; (3) NO dual value.js instance — glass-ui pulled a second 4.0.0 copy to `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js`, but `grep -rl "node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js" node_modules/.vite/deps/*.js` is empty and `_metadata.json`'s optimized set holds only `@mkbabb/glass-ui*`, so the anchored-regex aliases fold glass-ui's 13 bare value.js subpath imports onto the repo dist — one instance; (4) NO cycle — workbenches → color-session only, `grep -rn "workbenches" demo/color-session/ demo/shell/ demo/platform/ demo/shared/` finds one prose mention plus four lazy `defineAsyncComponent` shell imports; (5) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean at all 6 type-import sites; (6) Vue 3.5 idioms present (reactive props destructure :18, useTemplateRef :48); (7) Chip DOES emit `aria-pressed` (dist chip-DFZQr6rV.js) so L-5's missing wash is purely visual, state is announced; all 27 tiles carry accessible names; (8) the 1 nameless button on /#/gradient is the shell `dock-icon-button--compact`, not ours; (9) `overflowX: 0` on all four gradient captures — the strip's `bleeding` rows are correctly-clipped scroll-port content (scrollWidth 1482 / clientWidth 436); (10) `glyphPath` has exactly ONE home in the repo (`grep -rln "glyphPath|generateCurveSVGPath|1 - fn("` → 2 files, 1 definition), cost measured cold 1.73ms / warm 0.80ms for all 33 tiles.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue re-declares value.js's easing taxonomy as a hardcoded allow-list and FILTERS by it, silently dropping 6 of 30 library `bezierPresets` (all of quart + quint). The module's own docstring claims the catalogue "IS value.js bezierPresets … never a second mint" — it is a second mint, minus 6.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:174 `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` + :191 `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. Node run against dist/subpaths/easing.js: `ALL presets: 30` … `DROPPED quart ease-in-quart, ease-out-quart, ease-in-out-quart / DROPPED quint ease-in-quint, ease-out-quint, ease-in-out-quint` → `kept bezier tiles: 24 + 3 steps = 27`. Live page.evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `{ tileCount: 27, glassChipCount: 27, families: ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"] }`. Blind gate: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56 `expect(SPECIMEN_TILES.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)`.
defects.mechanism: library-knowledge re-declared in a consumer: value.js publishes `bezierPresets` as a bare Record<string, quad> with no taxonomy, so the demo derived families by regex (easingCatalogue.ts:168) and closed the set with a hand-written allow-list. New library families are now a silent no-op downstream.
defects.reproduction: `node -e 'import("/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/easing.js").then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m.bezierPresets).length))'` → 30; live `document.querySelectorAll("[data-specimen]").length` at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → 27. Downstream (derived from easingCatalogue.ts:219-223): set an interval's easing to `cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)` (= library `ease-in-quart`) and the row head reads `custom` with no tile pressed.
defects.proposedCure: GESTALT: value.js `/easing` publishes the structure it already has implicitly — `export const bezierPresetList: readonly { name: BezierPresetName; family: string; variant: string; points: readonly [number,number,number,number] }[]` — and the demo groups by the library's own `family` field in encounter order, never filtering. KISS/today: change `.filter()` to a sort (known families in FAMILY_ORDER order, unknown appended) so a new library family always appears, merely last. One line.

defects.defect: value.js's public `/css` surface parses timing functions but cannot serialize them, so the CSS-literal minting law is hand-implemented THREE times across two packages: glass-ui's `useEasingPicker.readout`, this component's `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral`, and a frozen third copy in `linearInterval()`.
defects.evidence: src/subpaths/css.ts:53 exports `parseTimingFunction`, :54 exports `serializeCssColor` — the color grammar is symmetric, the timing grammar is not. `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → serializeCssValue, serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeTimelineOptions; NO serializeTimingFunction anywhere. Copy 1: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts `readout: ComputedRef<string>` ("The complete re-parseable readout literal"). Copy 2: easingCatalogue.ts:48-56, whose comment at :41-45 declares it mirrors glass-ui byte-for-byte. Copy 3: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:56 `css: "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"` hardcoded. easingCatalogue.ts:44-45 names copy 3 as its own precedent "generalized to the whole catalogue". `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` are exported but consumed only inside their own file (grep: 4 hits, all in easingCatalogue.ts) — dead public surface on top of duplicated law.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric public surface: a grammar module that parses but does not serialize forces every consumer to hand-mint the inverse. N consumers → N copies of one law, each maintained by comment rather than by code.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "parseTimingFunction\|serializeCssColor" src/subpaths/css.ts` → :53 :54; `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → 4 hits, none for timing. Then `grep -rn "toFixed(3)" demo src --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` shows the demo's mirror at easingCatalogue.ts:49.
defects.proposedCure: value.js `/css` exports `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` — the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, with `parse ∘ serialize ≡ id` as a round-trip property test over the whole bezierPresets corpus + the steps space. glass-ui's `readout`, `bezierLiteral`, `stepsLiteral` and `linearInterval`'s frozen string all collapse into one call; the "byte-identity with the picker" law stops being a cross-package comment and becomes a fact of the grammar module. Same shape the library already got right for colors.

defects.defect: Reduced motion has four independent homes in the demo and a fifth — published, shared, single-listener — in the design system that nobody uses. This component is the sole `@vueuse/core` PRM site in the whole demo, and it duplicates a subscription already live in its own sibling seat.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:12 `import { useMediaQuery } from "@vueuse/core"` + :47. glass-ui publishes the concept: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/motion/core/useReducedMotion.d.ts — `readReducedMotion(): boolean` ("Read the current OS preference without subscribing (SSR-safe)") and `useReducedMotion(): Readonly<Ref<boolean>>` ("Share one reactive OS preference and one MediaQueryList listener"), re-exported at composables/motion/core/index.d.ts:6 → motion-core.d.ts → the published subpath `@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core`, which the demo ALREADY imports for useRAFLoop at useMixingAnimation.ts:42 and useInertiaGesture.ts:3. Census: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47 (vueuse) / useInertiaGesture.ts:36 + useMixingAnimation.ts:70 (glass `useBreakpoint` misused for a non-breakpoint query) / useOverture.ts:96 + useDockArrival.ts:26 (raw window.matchMedia) / glass useReducedMotion (zero demo consumers). Simultaneous duplication inside one row: `grep -o 'from "[^"]*"' node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui_easing.js` → `from "./useReducedMotion-vCXA_vyM-DVuAJw8b.js"`, i.e. the <EasingPicker> mounted by the sibling EasingAuthoringStage.vue:29 already runs glass's shared listener.
defects.mechanism: design-system ownership ignored: the producer publishes the primitive, the consumer re-mints it from a third-party utility. Per-instance subscription instead of the producer's shared one, so the listener count multiplies with L-4's per-row strip mounting.
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/motion/core/useReducedMotion.d.ts`; `grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion" demo --include="*.ts" --include="*.vue"` → the five demo sites, four mechanisms; `grep -rn "glass-ui/motion" demo/` → the demo already imports motion-core at two sites without taking useReducedMotion.
defects.proposedCure: One line in the strip: `import { useReducedMotion } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core"; const prefersReducedMotion = useReducedMotion();` — the @vueuse/core import dies. Fleet-wide the other four follow: `readReducedMotion()` for the two one-shot boot sites, `useReducedMotion()` for the two `useBreakpoint` misuses. No new demo module and no new shared/ dir — glass-ui already owns the concept, which is what edict 4 demands.

defects.defect: A 27-tile, 133-DOM-node selection strip is mounted for EVERY interval row inside `v-show`, although `openInterval` is a single ref so at most one row can ever be open. One strip is 23% of the entire page's element count; K intervals cost 133·K nodes, 27·K Chip instances and K MediaQueryList listeners for one visible surface.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 `const openInterval = ref<number | null>(0)` (single); :112 `v-for="row in specimenRows"`; :144 `v-show="openInterval === row.index"` (mounts); :152 the cheap ramp IS gated `v-if="openInterval === row.index && openIntervalRamp"`; :161 `<EasingSpecimenStrip>` is NOT gated. Live measurement at K=1: `{ stripNodeCount: 133, pageNodeCount: 579, stripShare: 23.0, tileCount: 27, glassChipCount: 27, stripCount: 1 }`. The component documents the consequence and works around it rather than removing it — EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:38-40 "scoped to THIS strip's own subtree (sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id)". Port geometry: `{ scrollWidth: 1482, clientWidth: 436 }` = 3.4x overflow, ~8 of 27 tiles reachable at desktop, ~5 of 27 at 390px mobile.
defects.mechanism: a singleton surface instantiated per collection item: the selection strip is stateless w.r.t. the row and only one row is ever open, so per-row instantiation is pure duplication. The subtree-scoped querySelector workaround exists solely to survive the duplication it should have prevented.
defects.reproduction: Live page.evaluate at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `document.querySelector('.specimen-strip').querySelectorAll('*').length` = 133 against `document.querySelectorAll('*').length` = 579 (23.0%), with `document.querySelectorAll('[data-specimen]').length` = 27 for a single interval. The K-multiplication follows from GradientEasingEditor.vue:112/144/161 (v-for + v-show, no v-if on the strip).
defects.proposedCure: Hoist ONE <EasingSpecimenStrip> out of the v-for, bound to `openInterval` — the disclosure body can only ever hold one row's content, so move it out of the loop entirely (or Teleport it into the open row). What dies: the `visible` prop (a strip that exists is visible), the "hidden twins" paragraph, the subtree-scoped querySelector, and 133·(K−1) nodes. What it enables: with one instance the strip can afford a wrapped grid instead of a 3.4x horizontal scroll that hides two thirds of the catalogue.

defects.defect: GLASS-OWNED (M3 / INBOX I-9 / D58). Chip's material CSS is not merely orphaned inside glass-ui 7.0.0 — it is UNREACHABLE through the published surface, because the exports map has no `./styles/*` wildcard. This component's tiles therefore render as circles with no pressed state.
defects.evidence: File ships at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css but `grep -rn 'glass-chip.css' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist` → NO MATCHES; dist/styles/glass.css lists 18 @imports (material, ladder, ladder-undershadow, grain-overlay, accent-tone, rim, surfaces, surfaces-pager, control-surfaces, glass-capsule, liquid-fill, surface-axis, material-roles, reveal, liquid-enter, deep, defined, squircle) — no glass-chip.css; dist/styles/index.css likewise. glass-ui exports map has `./styles`, `./styles.css`, `./styles/fonts`, `./styles/theme` and NO `./styles/*`, so a consumer cannot deep-import it even knowingly. Demo consumes both published surfaces correctly (demo/styles/foundation.css:56-57). THREE computed-style proofs from the live page: (a) `borderRadius: "9999px"` on an element carrying `glass-chip--cell`, where `.glass-chip--cell{border-radius:var(--radius-card)}` (--radius-card resolves to 1rem) should win → shape="cell" is inert; (b) selected vs unselected tile byte-identical — both `backgroundColor: "oklab(0.925644 0.0094459 0.0291917 / 0.83872)"`, `borderColor: "rgb(198, 180, 159)"`, `color: "rgb(91, 70, 51)"` — while `--accent-band` itself resolves fine, so `[data-mode="selectable"][data-state="on"]{background-color:var(--accent-band);…}` never lands; (c) `--chip-tint-floor` and `--chip-flood-t` both compute to the EMPTY STRING → the @property registration and flood recipe are absent. Visual: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/gradient.png (crops saved beside the report as strip-light.png / strip-dark.png) show eight round bevelled pucks with drop shadows, content pinched into the inscribed square ('in-out' running to the circle edge), and the pressed 'linear' tile identical in plate to its seven neighbours — selection carried ONLY by this seat's own --motion-accent glyph/label ink.
defects.mechanism: producer packaging defect: a component's material recipe exists in the tarball but is wired into no distribution surface and blocked from deep import by the exports map, so the component ships visually incomplete to every consumer.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'glass-chip.css' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist` → no matches; `grep -n '@import' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass.css`. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: getComputedStyle of any [data-specimen] tile → borderRadius 9999px, --chip-flood-t empty, and the data-state="on" tile's backgroundColor/borderColor/color byte-identical to a data-state="off" sibling.
defects.proposedCure: FOLD-BANK on glass (BJ born-RED), NO local patch. glass-ui adds `@import "./glass/glass-chip.css"` to dist/styles/glass.css (and the badge twin) and ships it. A demo-side `.specimen-tile{border-radius:var(--radius-card)}` plus a hand-rolled pressed wash would fork the design system's chip recipe into demo/ — exactly the masking fallback MT-F014 and edict 2 forbid — and would silently diverge the moment glass fixes the import. Our M3 mark already carries this; this seat adds the UNREACHABILITY fact (no ./styles/* export key) and the three computed-style proofs to the packet.

defects.defect: The seat overrides the producer Chip root's own geometry recipe per-instance (edict 5), and the override lands the tile at 43.8px — 0.2px under the design system's own `--touch-target: 2.75rem`, with `min-height: auto` and no block floor.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 `.specimen-tile { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:0.125rem; padding:0.3125rem 0.375rem 0.25rem; min-width:2.75rem }` replaces glass-ui's own cell recipe `cell: "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro"` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/chipVariants.d.ts) — the scoped rule's data-v specificity (0,2,0) beats the Tailwind utility (0,1,0). Live measurement: `{ id:"ease", tileRect:{w:44,h:43.8}, padding:"5px 6px 4px 6px", gap:"2px", minWidth:"44px", minHeight:"auto", glyphBox:{w:22,h:22}, labelBox:{h:10.8,fs:"9px",lh:"10.8px"}, touchTargetToken:"2.75rem" }`. Arithmetic: 22 + 2 + 10.8 + 5 + 4 = 43.8 exactly. With the producer's own py-2.5 (10px each): 22+2+10.8+20 = 54.8px. Compounded by L-5 — the `@media (pointer: coarse) { min-block-size: var(--touch-target) }` floor lives in the orphaned glass-chip.css, so mobile gets no bump either. The visual audit misses it: capture.mjs:98 filters `w < 24 || h < 24`, looser than the house token.
defects.mechanism: per-instance override of a design-system recipe: the consumer restyles the producer's root box model from outside instead of asking the producer for a size axis, and in trimming 11px of the producer's padding it silently crosses an a11y floor the design system itself defines.
defects.reproduction: Live page.evaluate at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient on `[data-specimen]` → height 43.8px, `min-height: auto`, `padding: 5px 6px 4px 6px`; `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--touch-target')` → `2.75rem` (44px).
defects.proposedCure: Stop overriding the producer root. Specimen scale is a SIZE axis on the cell recipe, which glass-ui already models (`ChipVariants` SIZE.sm): `<Chip mode="selectable" shape="cell" size="sm">`. If sm × cell does not yet compose to specimen scale, that composition is a glass-owned addendum on the same M3 packet — not a demo override. The seat keeps only what is genuinely its own: the --motion-accent ink on .tile-glyph path / .tile-label.

defects.defect: The strip resolves its scroll port by reaching into the producer's compiled DOM with a private class selector, `el.closest(".fading-scroll")`, and calls it "its documented DOM contract". FadingScroll exposes no port; the class is a literal in its compiled render function. The demo's OWN class sits on the same element, so the private selector buys nothing.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:58-60 `const port = el?.closest<HTMLElement>(".fading-scroll")` with the comment "(its documented DOM contract)". node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/fading-scroll/FadingScroll.vue.d.ts declares five props (axis, fadeStart, fadeEnd, ariaLabel, ariaLabelledby), one default slot, NO defineExpose and no exposed port ref. The class is a compiled literal: dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js `class: a(["fading-scroll", e.axis === "y" ? "fading-scroll--y" : "fading-scroll--x"])`. Live: `{ stripClass: "fading-scroll fading-scroll--x specimen-strip", portHasSpecimenStripClass: true }` — the demo's own `specimen-strip` class is on the identical element.
defects.mechanism: private-implementation-detail dependency: a consumer treats a producer's internal class name as API, coupling to something the producer never promised and can rename in a patch release.
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/fading-scroll/FadingScroll.vue.d.ts` (no exposed port); `node -e` slice of dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js showing the class literal; live page.evaluate → `tiles[0].closest('.fading-scroll').className` === "fading-scroll fading-scroll--x specimen-strip".
defects.proposedCure: Today, no glass change: take the root through Vue's own contract — `<FadingScroll ref="stripRef">` + `const stripRef = useTemplateRef<ComponentPublicInstance>("stripRef")`, scroll `stripRef.value.$el`. Zero producer-private knowledge, survives any class rename. If the reveal deserves to be first-class, bank a `defineExpose({ port })` / `scrollChildIntoView()` addendum on glass — the published `useFadingScroll(target)` composable already takes an explicit port, so the component simply has not surfaced the same handle. The single-axis discipline the comment defends is CORRECT (the scrollIntoView ancestor-walk it replaced was the O-19 root cause) — only the selector is wrong.

defects.defect: `easingCatalogue.ts` carries four concerns in one 230-line module, and the fourth makes a catalogue of easing curves import a gradient type — the curve catalogue knows what a gradient is.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts spans: :48-56 CSS literal minting, :66-74 SVG glyph painting, :98-203 tile/family construction, :207-230 gradient-interval identity (isStepsInterval/tileIdFor/specimenNameFor). The fourth forces :36 `import type { GradientInterval } from "../../composables/useGradientModel"`, though every predicate reads exactly one field, `interval.css`. Symptom of the same depth problem: useSpecimenRows.ts:13 climbs four levels, `../../../../color-session/useContrastSafeColor`.
defects.mechanism: unique-semantic-ownership smear: presentation-adjacent module accumulates minting + painting + cataloguing + model-identity, so a pure library-consumer module acquires a feature-model dependency it does not need.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "^import\|^export" demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts` shows the four concern blocks and the GradientInterval import at :36; `grep -rn "bezierLiteral\|stepsLiteral" demo/ test/` shows both are exported but consumed only inside their own file (dead public surface).
defects.proposedCure: Key the identity on the literal, not the model: `tileIdForCss(css: string): string | null` / `specimenNameForCss(css: string): string`. The GradientInterval import vanishes and the catalogue becomes a pure @mkbabb/value.js/easing consumer testable with string inputs. Greenfield lattice: easing/specimens.ts (catalogue + glyph painter, value.js/easing its ONLY import) · easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue + EasingAuthoringStage.vue (presentation) · ../composables/useGradientEasing.ts (interval↔specimen identity) · ../composables/useSpecimenRows.ts (row derivation, reach shortened to three levels). Minting dies entirely under L-2.

defects.defect: `isStepsInterval` accepts a two-truths state instead of forbidding it — a masking fallback in three tokens, inside a module whose own stated law is that the CSS literal is the single persisted truth.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:207-209 `return interval.mode === "steps" || interval.css.startsWith("steps(")`. The module's own comment at :43 declares `css` "the persisted TRUTH", and `stepsTile` (:139-153) sets `mode` and `css` from one source, so the two can never legitimately disagree. The `||` exists only to survive a state the mint law forbids.
defects.mechanism: masking fallback / dual truth: a defensive disjunction papers over a model inconsistency rather than making it impossible, so a genuine model bug would render as correct behaviour here and surface elsewhere.
defects.reproduction: Read easingCatalogue.ts:207-209 against its own stated law at :41-45 and the mint at :139-153 — `mode` is derived from the same literal it is being OR'd against.
defects.proposedCure: `return interval.css.startsWith("steps(")` — read the truth once. If `mode` can genuinely diverge from `css`, the model carries two truths for one fact, and THAT is the finding to fix in useGradientModel, not here.

defects.defect: Array-getter watch source allocates a fresh tuple per evaluation where Vue 3.5's idiomatic multi-source form is a getter array.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-51 `watch(() => [selectedId, visible] as const, () => { … }, { immediate: true })`. Idiomatic: `watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], …)`.
defects.mechanism: idiom drift, not a defect — the getter only re-runs when a tracked dep changes, so behaviour is identical.
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled as a legibility observation, no defect claimed.
defects.proposedCure: `watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], …)`. Cosmetic; fold into whichever wave touches L-4 (which deletes the `visible` source entirely).

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` is a hand-maintained second mirror of `package.json#exports` and has rotted: it declares three keys that do not exist and omits two that do and are used — while `vite.config.ts` GENERATES the same mirror from the exports map precisely so it cannot drift.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports = 7 keys {./color, ./value, ./css, ./easing, ./math, ./transform, ./quantize}. tsconfig.demo.json declares `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts (NO `.` key in exports; `ls dist/` → anchors-*.js, gh-pages, operations-*.js, result-*.js, subpaths — no index.d.ts), `/parsing` → ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts (does not exist), `/units` → ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts (does not exist), and OMITS `./css` and `./value` — `./css` is actively used at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:25 (`parseTimingFunction`). The file's own comment calls it "the CLOSED 8-key set" / "the 8 public keys". Contrast vite.config.ts:36-51, which builds anchored-regex aliases from `package.json#exports` with the stated rationale "GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map".
defects.mechanism: two mirrors of one fact, one generated and one hand-rolled; the hand-rolled one rotted and now typechecks only because TS bundler resolution self-references through package.json#exports for the two omitted subpaths — the paths block is simultaneously stale and redundant.
defects.reproduction: `ls dist/ dist/subpaths/` and `python3 -c "import json;print(list(json.load(open('package.json'))['exports']))"` against the paths block in tsconfig.demo.json.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the value.js entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths and let self-reference through `exports` resolve them (one source of truth, the same one vite reads). If an explicit map is wanted for build determinism, generate it the way vite generates its aliases. Either way: one mirror, not two.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID claude-opus-5[1m]. The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration and I observe myself to be that model; the declaration is not inherited or undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the panel headed "CSS" does not contain the component's CSS. The editor is bound to `simpleCSS` (raw stops, easing NOT baked), the render tile paints `coalescedCSS` (32 eased sub-stops), and Copy writes `coalescedCSS`. Measured live after selecting `in-out` on the sole interval: editor text = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` (2 stops), tile paint = 33 stops with the eased distribution (3.13% -> oklch(0.749813 0.150056 145.225), vs un-eased oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75)). The Easing section — 519px, 49.8% of the component's height — produces work the labelled output silently discards; a user who copies the visible text ships a linear ramp, and a user who presses Copy receives a 33-stop string they never saw.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Sound arms recorded in report §6 for balance: parse-failure state is well designed and atomic; verbatimModuleSyntax clean at :22/:25/:26/:28; reduced-motion honoured with rafPer1500ms=0 and no layout-forcing animated property; 200% zoom reflows with overflowX=0; dark mode structurally identical; tile correctly role="img" non-interactive; zero page/console errors and zero horizontal overflow on /#/gradient across all four Safari matrices.)

defects.defect: The panel headed "CSS" is not the component's CSS, and Copy emits a third, never-displayed string. Three surfaces claim to represent one gradient and are fed by two different serializers.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:259 `:model-value="simpleCSS"` (what the user READS); :224 `'--tile-render': coalescedCSS` (what the user SEES); :128 `writeClipboard(coalescedCSS.value)` (what the user GETS). useGradientCSS.ts:147-162 serializeGradient = raw stops, easing not baked; :281-305 serializeCoalescedGradient = 32 eased sub-stops. Live measured after clicking the `css -> in-out` tile: editorStopCount=2, tilePaintStopCount=33, easing literal `cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)`, tile sample @3.13% = oklch(0.749813 0.150056 145.225) vs un-eased oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75).
defects.mechanism: Two truths for one artifact — a second serializer kept as a silent parallel path with no surface labelling which is which.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900. The Easing accordion is open by default. Click the `css -> in-out` specimen tile. Read the contenteditable [role=textbox][aria-label="Gradient CSS"] textContent (2 stops, no easing) and getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-testid="gradient-render-tile"]')).backgroundImage (33 stops, eased). Press the pane Copy button: the clipboard receives the 33-stop string, not the visible text.
defects.proposedCure: One gradient, one serialization on screen. Bind the editor to the render truth. If the compact authored form is worth keeping, make it a named visible representation toggle inside the same well (producer SegmentedTabs, `Compact / Expanded`), and Copy copies exactly the bytes under the caret. Delete `simpleCSS` as an unlabelled parallel path — a second serializer no surface names is a dual path (owner edict 2).

defects.defect: At the canonical 390px mobile arm every one of the three primary settings truncates to three characters. The band is a fixed grid-cols-3 with no responsive step; the only responsive token in the band is on the element that did not need one.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:158 `class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3 min-w-0"`; the only breakpoint is :223 `w-20 sm:w-24` on the tile. Measured live at 390x844: gridTemplateColumns = "69.3281px 69.3359px 69.3359px"; SelectValue scrollWidth/clientWidth = 41/27 (Linear), 48/27 (OKLCh), 48/27 (Shorter) — all three truncated. Corroborated by the tranche's own WebKit capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/gradient.png which renders `Lin⌄ Ok⌄ Sh⌄`.
defects.mechanism: Desktop composition transplanted to mobile — a fixed N-across control grid with min-w-0 guarantees value truncation below a threshold width.
defects.reproduction: Resize to 390x844 and load http://localhost:9000/?m=1#/gradient. Read the three [aria-label="Gradient type"|"Interpolation space"|"Hue interpolation"] triggers: every value is clipped. Or simply open shots/safari-mobile-light/gradient.png.
defects.proposedCure: The band is a label/value list, not a 3-across. Below `sm` it stacks (or goes 2-up with Hue on its own row — Hue is a sub-option of Space and is meaningless in non-polar spaces); the render tile leaves the right rail and takes a full-width row below the band where its aspect can be owned. The trigger wraps; the value never does.

defects.defect: The render tile's aspect ratio is unowned — height is grid residue from `row-span-2` — so a gradient the dropdown captions "Center-outward circle" paints as an ellipse whose eccentricity changes with the viewport.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:223 `class="gradient-render-tile row-span-2 w-20 sm:w-24 ..."` — width authored, height emergent. Measured: 1440x900 -> 96.0 x 128.5 (aspect 0.747); 390x844 -> 80.0 x 121.9 (aspect 0.656). With type=radial the tile paint head is `radial-gradient(oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, ...` — no shape keyword, so CSS resolves `ellipse farthest-corner`. GRADIENT_TYPES at :55 captions radial "Center-outward circle". The source comment at :214-216 calls it "a square-ish surface"; 96:128.5 is 1:1.34. Screenshot: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/.playwright-mcp/radial-tile.png
defects.mechanism: Specimen geometry derived from foreign layout rather than designed — the surface that depicts shape has no owned shape.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient at 1440x900, set the Type select to Radial, screenshot the .grid.grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_auto] band: the 'circle' is a vertical ellipse. Repeat at 390x844: the eccentricity changes (0.747 -> 0.656).
defects.proposedCure: `aspect-ratio: 1` on the tile, and give it its own grid row instead of spanning two rows sized by other content. The type dropdown's promise and the paint then agree by construction.

defects.defect: Direction remains enabled, keyboard-focusable, labelled and live-reading while it controls nothing — the disabled state was never designed.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:55 states it: `direction: number; // degrees (for linear); ignored for radial`. useGradientCSS.ts:151-155 emits an angle only for linear/conic. Measured live with type=radial: thumb aria-disabled=null, data-disabled=false, tabindex="0", aria-valuenow="90", container opacity=1, visible readout "90°"; editor = `radial-gradient(oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` and tile paint = `radial-gradient(...` — neither carries an angle.
defects.mechanism: A permanent control with an undisclosed no-op branch; state coverage gap (disabled/absent never rendered).
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient, set Type = Radial, then drag or arrow the Direction slider. The readout counts 0-360 and nothing in the tile, the editor or the clipboard changes.
defects.proposedCure: Direction is a property of the type, not a permanent peer control. linear -> `Angle`; conic -> `From`; radial -> the row is absent and the grid closes. One control whose identity follows the model.

defects.defect: "Reset" does not reset — the per-interval easing survives it, so the gradient after Reset is not the default gradient.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:118-125 resetGradient() restores stops/type/direction/space/hue and clears the verdict but never touches `intervals`. useGradientModel.ts:89-100 re-seeds intervals only when `stops.value.length` changes; setStopsFromColors with 2 colours leaves length at 2, so the watcher never fires. Measured live: before Reset easingLiteral="cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)", tileStops=33; after Reset easingLiteral is still "cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)" and the tile still paints the eased distribution (3.13% -> oklch(0.749813 ...)).
defects.mechanism: Interval state kept in sync by a side-effect watcher on a derived quantity (stops.length) instead of being derived from the stop list.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient, click the `css -> in-out` easing tile, then click the Dock action-bar Reset (aria-label="Reset"). Read .readout-rail code — still cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) — and the tile's backgroundImage at 3.13% — still the eased value.
defects.proposedCure: resetGradient restores the whole model through one path; better, make `intervals` a derivation of the stop list rather than a parallel array a `watch` keeps honest.

defects.defect: In the shipped default state the render tile is a redundant second specimen — it paints the same 90deg left-to-right ramp the rail directly above it already paints.

defects.defect: `defineModel("selectedStopId")` is a public two-way component API with no consumer — a local ref wearing a prop/emit costume — and it dangles after Reset.

defects.reproduction: Read GradientPane.vue:25 — the only render site — and confirm no v-model:selected-stop-id binding exists. Then select a stop and press Reset: the ids are regenerated while selectedStopId retains the old one.
defects.proposedCure: Demote to a local `ref` until a real consumer exists, and clear it inside resetGradient (or key selection by stop position rather than by a minted id).

defects.defect: Silent no-op paths: `seedFromPalette` does nothing and says nothing in the route's shipped default state, and the parent optional-chains a method defineExpose statically guarantees.

(visible in all four Safari captures), so the Dock's 'Seed from palette' action is a silent no-op with no disabled state, no toast and no status. result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion and seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Explicitly declared for this seat, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — the strip is mis-SEATED, not mis-styled. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:50,58,210 ratifies Easing as a PEER ROUTE whose protagonist is a centered 19–22rem curve stage, with the "specimen strip" as its SUPPORT, and forbids "reducing it to a tiny nested widget"; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-09 disposes it ENLARGE. That route does not exist — demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-38 declares 14 paths and no /easing, and the shipped visual audit captures 15 routes, none of them /easing. So the 27-specimen gallery ships four containment levels deep inside /gradient (route -> plate -> interval row -> v-show panel -> strip), measured at clientWidth 436 vs scrollWidth 1482 (70.6% off-port desktop, 79.9% / 5-of-27-tiles at 390px), with no curve stage above it at all. Every other finding is downstream of that seat.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded as passing, with evidence, in the report's "What passes" section: verbatimModuleSyntax clean — `import type { SpecimenTile }` line 16 is the sole type-only import; Vue 3.5 idioms clean — useTemplateRef line 48, reactive props destructure lines 18-24, no defineModel; 215 lines, one job, catalogue extracted to a sibling — no god module; no legacy shims/dual paths/back-compat; no new shared dirs or wrapper components; reduced motion handled deliberately and measured correct (PRM {"prm":true} and the JS reveal resolves to behavior:"auto"); no animation deleted; and the deliberate refusal of scrollIntoView at lines 37-46, which names and prevents the O-19 pane-scroll-yank defect, is exemplary.)

defects.defect: The component occupies a seat the canon abolished: it is the "tiny nested widget" VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 forbids by name, because the /easing peer route it was designed to support was never cut.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-38 — 14 paths, no `/easing` and no `/about`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:50 (Easing = distinct member: "neutral curve/time stage | catalogue, specimen strip and code inspector"), :58 ("Easing is a peer route adjacent to Gradient rather than a nested P122 instrument"), :210 ("Catalogue and specimen strips support the curve rather than reducing it to a tiny nested widget"). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:53 PR-09 ENLARGE, "One 19–22rem protagonist". Measured live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `{scrollWidth: 1482, clientWidth: 436}` — the catalogue is 3.4x wider than its port. REPORT.md:119-178 captures 15 routes, none /easing.

Inside /gradient the interval row keeps only head glyph + literal + a link into /easing for that interval — not a second 27-item gallery. Closes PR-09 and dissolves D-09, D-10, D-13 and D-16 at the root.

defects.defect: The entire selected register rides a producer-private DOM attribute whose CSS does not exist; pressed and unpressed chips are byte-identical, and `shape="cell"` silently degrades to a disc that cannot geometrically contain its own content.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:204,208 style selection off `[data-state="on"]` (glass-ui Chip internals) although the component owns `selectedId` as a prop (line 20) and computes the state itself at line 104. probe-D-cascade-type.mjs enumerating every loaded stylesheet: `CHIP RULES: {"chipRules": [], "count": 0}` — zero rules match glass-chip/glass-chip--cell/glass-chip--interactive. `SURFACE: {on:{bg:"oklab(0.925644 0.0094459 0.0291917 / 0.83872)", border:"…/0px", shadow:"rgba(255,255,255,0.3) 0px 1px 0px 0px inset,…", filter:"none"}, off:{identical}, equal:true}`. `borderRadius: "9999px"` on a shape="cell" chip. Geometry: content rect 32x34.8 inside a 44x43.8 ellipse -> corner test (16/22)^2+(17.4/21.9)^2 = 1.160 > 1, i.e. the content corners fall outside the disc. Frames: frames/D-safari-desktop-light-2x.png, frames/D-forced-colors.png.
defects.mechanism: state expressed through a foreign component's undocumented internal attribute instead of state the consumer already owns; the producer's CSS is orphaned so the fallback is silent
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingspecimenstrip/probe-D-cascade-type.mjs` -> chipRules: [], SURFACE.equal: true, borderRadius 9999px.
defects.proposedCure: SPLIT. The missing `.glass-chip*` dist CSS is the glass BJ born-RED row already relayed as our mark M3 (INBOX.md:44 I-9, :68 O-6, :76 O-7 §F "still-banked, deliberately NOT patched") — FOLD-BANK it; a local radius or pressed wash would be exactly the MT-F014 masking fallback. The half that is OURS: stop styling off `[data-state]`; bind the component's own `selectedId` to a class it owns (`:class="{'is-pressed': tile.id === selectedId}"`) so the register is a fact of this component and survives any producer DOM change.

defects.defect: Hovering the pressed tile erases half its selected register (equal-specificity cascade, later rule wins), and because the rule is not gated on `(hover: hover)`, the very tap that selects a tile on touch triggers exactly that.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:208 `.specimen-tile[data-state="on"] .tile-label {color: var(--motion-accent,…)}` and :212 `.specimen-tile:hover .tile-label {color: var(--foreground)}` — both (0,3,0), the hover rule later. Reproduced with a real pointer: `HOVER-ON-SELECTED: {"beforeC":"oklch(0.438102 0.0748123 205)","afterC":"rgb(28, 25, 23)","afterW":"600","glyphStillAccent":"oklch(0.438102 0.0748123 205)"}`. At 390x844: `MOBILE390: {"hoverMedia": false, "anyHover": false, "pointerCoarse": true}` — coarse pointers latch :hover onto the last-tapped element.
defects.mechanism: an unguarded :hover rule ordered after the selected rule at equal specificity; no (hover: hover) capability gate
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient, expand the interval, hover the pressed `linear` tile — its label goes teal -> near-black while its glyph stays teal. At 390px, tap `ease` — its label never takes the accent.
defects.proposedCure: Hover is a pointer affordance and must never speak in the selection channel. Delete the `:hover` colour rule entirely and let hover be a surface/elevation delta (owned by the producer once glass's chip CSS lands). Any surviving hover ink belongs inside `@media (hover: hover)` and scoped `:not(.is-pressed)`.

defects.defect: Seven family divider rules in a composition whose binding retained-line count is `none`.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:143-146 `.strip-family + .strip-family { border-left: 1px solid var(--card-edge); padding-left: 0.875rem; }`. Measured: `divider: {borderLeft: "oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12) 1px", padLeft: "14px"}`; 8 families (css,sine,quad,cubic,expo,circ,back,steps) => 7 rules. OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binding inventory: "| Gradient | [] | none | none |" and "| Easing | [] | none | none |", followed by "Any additional line, automatic P122 divider, consumer-hidden producer line, terminal row rule, caster stroke or corner rule is a defect." PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 PR-05 and §5.4. Measured interval ratio: 28px inter-family trough vs 4px intra-family gap = 7:1.
defects.mechanism: a boundary expressed simultaneously by label, interval and rule

The missing tile boundary is the same border `shape="cell"` would have supplied — bank that half on glass (D-02), own the glyph/eyebrow arm locally.

defects.defect: A 27-item horizontal single-select rail implemented as 27 peer tab stops: no roving focus, no Home/End, an unfocusable scroll port, and AT semantics that misdescribe single-select as 27 unrelated toggles with the family IA hidden.
defects.evidence: Measured: `focusables: 27`; `tabIndexes: "0,0,0,…"` (27 zeros). No keydown handler exists in the file. `.specimen-strip` is `overflow-x: auto` with 1046px hidden and carries no tabindex. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:88 `role="group"` over 27 `aria-pressed` toggles; :96 `.family-eyebrow` is `aria-hidden="true"`; :112 the SVG portrait is `aria-hidden` with no textual description. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:129 §5.2 states the exact law: "horizontal Dock/rail roving focus | Right moves to the visual-right item; Left to visual-left | Home=first semantic item, End=last; activation is separate from movement".
defects.mechanism: a rail built as 27 peer buttons instead of as one composite widget
defects.reproduction: On /#/gradient with the interval open: `[...document.querySelector('.specimen-strip').querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile')].map(e=>e.tabIndex)` -> 27 zeros; focus a tile and press Home -> nothing happens.
defects.proposedCure: One composite: roving tabindex (a single tab stop), ArrowLeft/Right across the flat tile order, Home/End to first/last, activation separate from movement, and role="radiogroup"/role="radio"+aria-checked so the single-select truth is the announced truth. The eyebrow becomes a real aria-label on a per-family role="group" instead of aria-hidden decoration.

defects.defect: Both text species sit 18% below the design system's smallest existing rung, in the wrong family, and go bold — three simultaneous departures from a type matrix declared closed with exactly one exception that is not this one.

The Chip root already carries `text-micro`; the component overrides it downward. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 "Binding type matrix": "control or label, including dropdown options -> text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold … The type relation is exact across ALL18 … P019's 1/sqrt(phi) Picker pair is the sole paired-scale exception."

defects.proposedCure: Labels and eyebrows take `text-micro` (the existing floor rung), Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold, in both states. If 11px genuinely will not fit, that is D-01 speaking — the answer is the /easing stage, not a rung the system does not have.

defects.defect: The sparkline portraits are drawn without their unit box, so two of 27 specimens carry no information at all, the overshoot family has nothing to overshoot against, and the back-family tail collides with its own label at exactly 0px clearance.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:66-74 emits a bare polyline; EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:109-115 renders that single <path> into an empty viewBox="0 0 1 1" with no frame, baseline or axis. `steppedEase(1,"jump-start")` is the constant 1, so glyphPath emits `M 0 0 L … 0` — a straight horizontal rule at the top of an undrawn box (visible as such in frames/D-back-steps-families.png). Measured `getBBox()` for ease-in-out-back: `{x:0, y:-0.093, w:1, h:1.185}` — 9.3% above and 9.2% below the unit box, the family's entire identity, invisible without the box. Collision, measured live: `pathRect.bottom = 677.9`; label line box begins at `svgRect.bottom (675.9) + gap (2) = 677.9` — zero clearance. Contradicts the component's own stated thesis at :184 ("recognize-a-curve-by-its-shape").
defects.mechanism: a unit-box sparkline rendered without its unit box; a fixed 2px glyph->label gap that assumes the path stays inside the viewBox
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient, scroll the strip to its end, read the `start` and `end` tiles — bare rules. `document.querySelector('[data-specimen="ease-in-out-back"] .tile-glyph path').getBBox()` -> {y:-0.093, height:1.185}. Frame: frames/D-back-steps-families.png.
defects.proposedCure: The one painter draws its box — a hairline 0/1 ground rule at minimum, ideally the full unit rect — so a constant reads as a constant and an overshoot reads as an overshoot. Reserve the glyph slot for the real path bbox (1.185 units, not 1.0) so the tail can never reach the label.

defects.defect: 70.6% of the catalogue is hidden on desktop and 79.9% on mobile (5 of 27 tiles reachable at 390px) with no affordance announcing it — no scrollbar, no arrows, no count, no wrap, and no focusable port.

The only cue is FadingScroll's 16px mask (`maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(0,0,0,0) 0px, rgb(0,0,0) 16px, …)`). The port carries no tabindex (D-07), so keyboard access is Tab-walking and a wheel-only mouse reaches nothing past `sine`. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 PR-07 "Hover-only/unlabeled controls … ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE … every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state". Frame: frames/D-mobile-390.png.

defects.reproduction: `const s=document.querySelector('.specimen-strip'); [s.clientWidth, s.scrollWidth]` -> [436,1482] at 1440; [298,1482] at 390. Full script: probe-D-mobile-ring.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: D-01. On a real /easing stage the catalogue wraps into a grid and all 27 specimens are present at once — which is what a gallery is. Inside /gradient the interval row should not host a gallery at all.

defects.defect: The focus ring is clipped by the scroll port — 2px of block-end headroom for a 2px hard ring plus an 8px glow.
defects.evidence: Measured: `RINGGEO: {"port":{"top":622.27,"bottom":694.25}, "tile":{"top":648.45,"bottom":692.25}, "headroomBelow":2.00, "headroomAbove":26.19}`. `--focus-ring-shadow` = `0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg) 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px color-mix(… 15%, transparent)` — all painted outside the border box. Port computes `overflowY: "auto"` (overflow-x:auto forces the other axis out of visible) so it clips. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:132 `padding: 2px` with the comment "Headroom so pressed rings + overshoot portraits never clip" — 2px cannot contain 2px + 8px. Rendered proof at 3x: frames/D-focus-ring-clipped.png shows the crimson ring cut flat along the bottom and the disc shadows sliced by the same edge.
defects.mechanism: an outside-the-box focus indicator inside a scroll-clipping ancestor with 2px of reserve

defects.proposedCure: Reserve the ring's true extent (padding-block ~10px on .strip-row with negative-margin compensation on the port). Once D-04 lands, the family dividers — the only reason .strip-family stretches edge to edge — are gone and the row can simply breathe.

defects.defect: Contrast hierarchy is inverted — the pressed label is the LEAST legible label in the row — and the eyebrow carries a double de-emphasis that fails AA, of exactly the class the author already found and fixed for the glyph.
defects.evidence: Measured on the composited chip surface rgb(242,228,211): resting label rgb(91,70,51) = 7.10:1; pressed label oklch(0.438 0.075 205) = 6.02:1; pressed glyph same accent = 6.02:1; family eyebrow (--muted-foreground x opacity 0.75) = 3.24:1 against a 4.5:1 floor for 9px text — FAILS. Compensations for the pressed state are only font-weight 600 and stroke-width 1.25 -> 1.75px, both sub-perceptual at 9px/22px, while a merely FOCUSED neighbour gets a saturated crimson ring (frames/D-desktop-light-focus-ring.png) — a transient state louder than the persistent one. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:182-186 records the identical error being found and fixed for the glyph ("45% floated the sparkline under the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 graphics floor … 65% clears 3:1"); the reasoning reached one of three ink species.
defects.mechanism: de-emphasis multiplied on top of an already-de-emphasised token; selection expressed in an ink chosen for chromatic identity (the interval's ramp midpoint) rather than for emphasis
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingspecimenstrip/probe-D-states.mjs` — the `contrast` block prints {restLabel_on_chip: 7.1, selLabel_on_chip: 6.02, eyebrow_on_plate: 3.24}.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the `opacity` multiplier (it also breaks forced colors, D-06) and let --muted-foreground alone carry the eyebrow. Selection must lead in EMPHASIS, not only in hue — which is what the pressed surface (D-02) is for: accent stays the identity signal, surface supplies the emphasis.

defects.defect: A specimen grid with no grid — two tile module widths produce a ragged rhythm within a single family.
defects.evidence: Measured width histogram over all 27 tiles: `{"44": 18, "45.23": 9}`. Within the css family alone: linear 45.23, ease 44, in 44, out 44, in-out 45.23. Cause: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:169 `min-width: 2.75rem` plus the intrinsic width of a `white-space: nowrap` label (line 199), so 6-character labels push 1.23px wider than 2-character ones. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.8 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent."
defects.mechanism: intrinsic sizing in a set that must read as a module
defects.reproduction: `[...document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile')].map(e=>+e.getBoundingClientRect().width.toFixed(2))` -> two distinct values, 44 and 45.23.
defects.proposedCure: One fixed module (`inline-size`, not `min-width`) for every tile, with the label truncating or the label set abbreviated to a fixed measure.

defects.defect: Twenty-seven shadow-casting discs seated inside a row the host explicitly declares flat and shadowless.
defects.evidence: Measured boxShadow on every tile: `rgba(255,255,255,0.3) 0px 1px 0px 0px inset, rgba(255,25…` — the .glass-capsule register including its floating drop shadow, visible at 3x as a soft caster under each disc in frames/D-focus-ring-clipped.png (and sliced by the port edge). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:15 §2 "Instrument veil … no drop shadow"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 PR-05 "Dividers, caster shadows and corner marks repeat a boundary — REMOVE"; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:34 §3.8 "Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow." The host row declares itself flat at GradientEasingEditor.vue:108-110 ("Z2 in-plate specimen rows: flat on the plate, --card-edge hairline, no shadow") and then seats 27 casters inside it.
defects.mechanism: a producer capsule register carrying floating elevation onto in-chrome controls
defects.reproduction: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.specimen-tile')).boxShadow` on /#/gradient.
defects.proposedCure: FOLD-BANK ON GLASS. Same mechanism already relayed as MT-F026 (INBOX.md:76 O-7 §G: ".glass-capsule puts --glass-shadow-floating on in-chrome controls; measured: plate none, pills 0 8px 24px"). A local `box-shadow: none` would be a masking fallback; the correct fix is a producer tier separating capsule shape from capsule elevation.

defects.defect: The reveal motion is native browser smooth-scroll rather than the one producer-owned spring register, and the watcher forces a synchronous layout read on every tile press.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:71-76 `port.scrollBy({left: dx, behavior: prefersReducedMotion.value ? "auto" : "smooth"})`. Measured `getComputedStyle(strip).scrollBehavior` -> "auto", i.e. the smoothness is JS-supplied and untokenized. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:139 §6 "Spatial continuity uses ONE producer-owned glass-ui spring register." Separately, the watcher runs `{immediate: true}` (line 79) and inside nextTick performs two getBoundingClientRect() reads (lines 62-63) after the DOM write that changed the pressed state — a forced reflow on every press and every row reveal. CREDIT: reduced motion is handled correctly and deliberately (measured `PRM {"prm":true}`; the sibling stage carries the PRM carve-out at EasingAuthoringStage.vue:112-114).
defects.mechanism: motion delegated to the platform rather than to the design system; a read-after-write in the selection path
defects.reproduction: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.specimen-strip')).scrollBehavior` -> "auto" while the reveal still animates; read EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-80.
defects.proposedCure: Drive the reveal through the glass-ui spring register the rest of the app uses — or, once D-01 lands and the catalogue wraps instead of scrolling, delete the reveal entirely. A gallery you can see all of needs no scroll-into-view.

defects.defect: The strip saturates the visual harness's 12-slot bleeding budget on /#/gradient in all four matrices, blinding the detector to any genuine bleeding element elsewhere on that route.
defects.evidence: capture.mjs:107-111 collects elements whose getBoundingClientRect().right > documentElement.clientWidth + 1, `.slice(0, 12)`. REPORT.json /#/gradient bleeding arrays, all four matrices, 12/12 entries and every one this component: ['div.strip-row','div.strip-family','span.family-eyebrow','div.family-tiles','button.glass-chip.glass-capsule' x3,'svg' x2,'path' x2,'span.tile-label'] (desktop) and the mobile variant. Cause: the 1482px `width: max-content` row (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:129) laying out from x~272 to x~1754 inside a 1440px viewport. Not user-visible overflow — REPORT.json records `overflowX: 0` on the route.
defects.mechanism: a max-content layout box far exceeding the viewport, clipped by its port but not by layout
defects.reproduction: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json')); [print(r['matrix'], r['probe']['bleeding']) for r in d['results'] if r['route']=='/#/gradient']"`
defects.proposedCure: Dissolved by D-01/D-10 — a wrapped catalogue has no max-content row.

defects.defect: The `custom` state — one of only two states the interval model can be in — has no design: the strip renders identically to "nothing has ever been selected" while the row header simultaneously prints `custom`.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:219-223 `tileIdFor()` returns null for any bezier quad not byte-identical to a preset. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:52 then early-returns from the reveal, no tile receives :model-value="true" (line 104), and no tile carries [data-state="on"]. The head meanwhile prints `custom` via specimenNameFor (easingCatalogue.ts:228-230, rendered at GradientEasingEditor.vue:136). The strip's own doc comment (lines 30-32) asserts "an interval always has a curve" — true of the model, false of the rendering. Full state table in the report: custom UNHANDLED, hovered DESIGNED WRONG (D-03), pressed ZERO SURFACE DELTA (D-02), focused CLIPPED (D-11) and louder than selection (D-12), overflowing UNHANDLED (D-10), RTL BROKEN (D-05), forced-colors BROKEN (D-06); reduced-motion HANDLED; empty/loading/error correctly n/a (build-time constant catalogue); zoom 200% no change vs 1440.
defects.mechanism: an identity function that can return null feeding a view with no null arm
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient, expand the interval, press the sliders icon to disclose the authoring canvas, drag either control point to any non-preset position. Head reads `custom`; `document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile[data-state="on"]').length` -> 0. (Derived from the code path with certainty — the DOM consequence is structural, not probabilistic.)
defects.proposedCure: `custom` is a first-class specimen state and needs a rendered register. Either give the strip an explicit `custom` tile, or make the strip's no-tile-pressed state visibly and textually MEAN custom so it agrees with the head — the kf precedent quoted at easingCatalogue.ts:215-217 puts Custom in the sidebar, which the constitution's Easing composition also supplies as the code inspector.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue (+ easingCatalogue.ts, useSpecimenRows.ts)

(Cleared hazards, each verified, are recorded in the report's "Negative proofs" table: zero rAF in the component; prefers-reduced-motion honored at :74; the O-19 scrollIntoView cure holds — instrumented scrollBy/scrollTo/scrollIntoView across a full press cycle showed exactly ONE call, scrollBy on .fading-scroll, and .fading-scroll genuinely is the scroll port per dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js:34-45 and the live DOM chain; tap targets 44.0-45.2 x 43.8 px pass WCAG 2.5.8 and the strip contributes ZERO of the 6 smallTapTargets on /#/gradient; 27/27 chips have accessible names; overflowX 0 on all four Safari matrices so the 12 `bleeding` rows are in-port content, not page overflow; verbatimModuleSyntax clean; Vue 3.5 idiom clean; no defineModel/ValueUnit/stableHue/parseCssColor/WebGL surface; no god module, no legacy shim, no invented shared dir, no deleted animation.)

defects.defect: All three `back`-family specimen tiles crash the entire Gradient workbench on a single press. The catalogue mints overshoot curves whose eased progress leaves [0,1]; the gradient's color-mix contract rejects that, and the demo demotes the library's Result-err into an uncaught throw inside a computed on the render path, so the pane's error boundary swallows the whole bench (easing bench, gradient rail, CSS output, stop editor).
defects.evidence: Live pane body after the click: "This panel hit an unexpected error. / Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Measured fn ranges over t in [0,1] (65 samples, through the gradient's own easingFnOf): ease-in-back cubic-bezier(0.6,-0.28,0.735,0.045) fn(0.5)=-0.0636 min=-0.0969; ease-out-back cubic-bezier(0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275) fn(0.5)=1.0676 max=1.0868; ease-in-out-back cubic-bezier(0.68,-0.55,0.265,1.55) min=-0.0926 max=1.0927. No other tile leaves [0,1]. Direct invocation in-page: interpolateStopColors(c0,c1,fnIB(0.5),'oklch','shorter') -> "Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range"; serializeCoalescedGradient(model with that css) -> same. Sites: src/color/operations.ts:65 (returns err, correct); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:207 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 (the throw inside a computed); easingCatalogue.ts:176-190 (mints the back tiles unguarded). The strip's own CSS comment at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:172-179 explicitly renders headroom for these overshoot curves.
defects.mechanism: Domain contract violated across a module boundary, with a Result->throw demotion at the seam: the easing catalogue's codomain is R, the gradient sampler's domain is [0,1], nothing reconciles them, and the one mechanism that could report it politely (the Result) is discarded.
defects.reproduction: Fresh http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (default two-stop gradient, Easing row 1 open). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-out-expo"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(1, 0, 0, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-out-circ"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(0.075, 0.82, 0.165, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-back"] -> pane replaced by the error boundary. ease-in-out-back reproduces independently.
defects.proposedCure: Make the gradient's progress type TOTAL, once, at the ramp sampler — not in the catalogue and not as a try/catch. Introduce the [0,1] clamp at the single point where an eased t becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return, or a rampProgress(fn,t) helper beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit it; this is the correct CSS-gradient semantic (an interval cannot produce a color beyond its endpoints, so overshoot MEANS hold-at-endpoint), a domain law rather than a masking fallback, and the repo already speaks the idiom (test/value-domain-clamp.test.ts). Then delete both throw sites (useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, useGradientCSS.ts:207) — with a total domain they are unreachable, and an unreachable throw on a render path is a liability. Deleting the back family instead is strictly worse: it removes curves the producer's own picker still offers and contradicts the strip's overshoot-headroom design.

defects.defect: FAMILY_ORDER is written as an allow-list rather than a sort key, so six of value.js's thirty bezierPresets (ease-{in,out,in-out}-quart and -quint) are silently dropped from the strip. The glass EasingPicker still offers all thirty, so authoring one of the six labels a NAMED preset as `custom` with no tile pressed — breaking the module's own stated identity contract.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:174 (FAMILY_ORDER lacks quart/quint) and :191 (FAMILY_ORDER.filter(f => byFamily.has(f))). Measured live: families [css:5, sine:3, quad:3, cubic:4, expo:3, circ:3, back:3, steps:3], SPECIMEN_TILES.length 27, hasQuart false, hasQuint false. Picker menu measured at 30 options including all six (glass dist/easing.js:13 `H = Object.keys(P)` over the same bezierPresets). Unit: tileIdFor({css:'cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)'}) -> null; specimenNameFor -> 'custom'; same for ease-out-quint. Contract stated at easingCatalogue.ts:15-17.
defects.mechanism: Enumeration expressed as a closed allow-list standing in for an open set — an upstream addition silently shrinks downstream coverage with no failure anywhere.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> Easing row 1 -> 'Author a custom curve' -> Easing preset combobox -> ease-in-quart. Measured result: readout 'cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)', head spans ['1 → 2','','','','custom'], pressedTiles [].
defects.proposedCure: Turn FAMILY_ORDER into a rank, never a filter, so an unknown family sorts last but still renders: const rank = f => { const i = FAMILY_ORDER.indexOf(f); return i < 0 ? FAMILY_ORDER.length : i; }; return [...byFamily.keys()].sort((a,b) => rank(a)-rank(b) || a.localeCompare(b)).map(family => ({ family, tiles: byFamily.get(family)! })). familyLabelFor's regex is already general, so no other edit is needed and a future upstream preset can never vanish.

defects.defect: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css ORPHANED — nothing in the package imports it — so for this component the Chip shape="cell" recipe, the data-state="on" pressed wash, and the coarse-pointer 2.75rem touch floor all silently do not exist. The tiles render as full circles, the pressed tile is visually indistinguishable in fill/border from its 26 neighbours, and 11 of 27 labels spill outside the painted chip.
defects.evidence: grep -rn 'glass-chip.css' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ -> no output (nothing imports it), while grep -rl 'glass-chip--cell' finds the rules in dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css and the class emitted in dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js. dist/styles/index.css -> ./glass.css imports 18 ./glass/*.css files, glass-capsule.css among them, glass-chip.css NOT. Runtime: glassChipCssPresent (any live stylesheet containing 'glass-chip--cell') = false.
