defects.defect: value.js's css + easing modules load twice in the dev module graph — once inlined into the Vite optimized-dep chunk serving glass-ui, once served unbundled to the demo.
defects.evidence: node_modules/.vite/deps/css-CwYd9pBf.js.map `sources` = ['../../../dist/result-CZJK1CwL.js','../../../dist/anchors-C_wdoOYd.js','../../../dist/subpaths/css.js'] — the local checkout build, inlined. Meanwhile `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/.../demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts" | grep '^import'` shows `import { parseTimingFunction } from "/@fs/.../dist/subpaths/css.js?t=1785167569503"` — a second, unbundled instance. Both copies are the checkout (the vite alias was honoured by the optimizer).
defects.mechanism: Vite dep pre-bundling inlines the aliased self-package into the optimizer chunk while the demo's own modules import it unbundled — two module instances of one physical file.
defects.reproduction: With the dev server up: `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('node_modules/.vite/deps/css-CwYd9pBf.js.map','utf8')).sources"` then `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/$PWD/demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts" | grep '^import'`.
defects.proposedCure: No action required. Recorded honestly with its own refutation: `grep -n "^const .* = new Map\|^let " src/css/*.ts src/easing.ts` finds only frozen constant Sets and pure functions — no mutable module state — so two instances cannot desynchronise. Dev-only byte cost; documented so the next reader need not re-derive it.

defects.defect: A registry copy of value.js@4.0.0 sits in node_modules as a real directory (npm auto-installed from glass-ui's peerDependencies), shadowing the checkout for any specifier that escapes vite.config's generated alias set.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js is a real directory, not a symlink (`readlink` returns nothing), at version 4.0.0; value.js is absent from its own package.json dependencies. Only vite.config.ts:41-50's generated anchored-regex alias binds glass-ui's bare `@mkbabb/value.js/*` imports to the checkout. Measured divergence today: easing/color/math/quantize/value/transform SAME by sha1; css local=43973 bytes/6dfbff9f vs installed=43972/0cd5611e, and the diff is minifier identifier mangling only (`< r as ee / s as f` vs `> r as f / s as p`).
defects.mechanism: A package that cannot install itself, consumed through a self-alias, while a registry tarball of the same package is auto-installed as a transitive peer — two candidate resolution targets for one name.
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled a hypothesis. No behavioural divergence exists at c654824e; the two builds are semantically identical. The shadow becomes real only once src/ advances past published 4.0.0 while some specifier escapes the alias set.
defects.proposedCure: Pin the exposure rather than the symptom: keep the alias generated from package.json#exports (already correct), and add a CI assertion that no module in the served graph resolves under node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js. Longer term, glass-ui's peer on value.js plus this repo BEING value.js is the structural oddity — a workspace/link posture removes the second copy entirely.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), matching the explicit Opus 5 declaration at spawn. Seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the magnifier loupe paints NOTHING on first show and, on the touch path, never paints at all: `showLoupeAt` flips `loupeVisible` and calls `drawLoupe` in the same synchronous tick, so the `v-if` canvas does not exist yet and `drawLoupe` early-returns; `onHover` is then gated by `if (pinned.value) return`, so no later event can repaint it. Measured `opaquePx 0 / 12100` on two fixtures and two interaction paths. The magnifier is the entire reason this component exists rather than a click handler on the drop zone, and it is a transparent hole exactly on the phone path where a finger occludes the pixel.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but five plausible defects were probed and REFUTED, which bounds the blast radius: (NEG-1) the loupe's edge mapping is correct — HTML Standard drawImage clips the source rect and the destination rect *in the same proportion*, so at image pixel (0,0) the loupe centre still resolves to (0,0); measured centerRGBA [255,0,0,255] with opaquePx 2996/12100. (NEG-2) WatercolorDot's dist contains 0 `@keyframes`, so no internal animation can bubble and clear `swatchPulse` early. (NEG-3) the capture-phase unpin listener and the gesture's bubble-phase pointerdown are on the same element; at AT_TARGET they run in registration order, but the two write disjoint state so the outcome is order-independent. (NEG-4) the un-coalesced hover path costs 0.022 ms/move (200 moves in 4.5 ms) — real but NOT a defect; reported so the mega-tranche does not spend a wave on it. (NEG-5) the CORS-tainted-canvas hazard is unreachable: imageUrl is always a FileReader data: URL (useExtractSession.ts:29-36,166). Also swept clean: no defineModel, no ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no WebGL, no ungated rAF (the coast rides glass-ui useRAFLoop with pauseWhenHidden + an explicit PRM decision — the exemplary part of this component), and verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied at every import site.

defects.defect: The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show, and on the touch path never renders at all — the canvas is painted one tick before the v-if element that owns it exists.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt sets loupeVisible.value=true then calls drawLoupe synchronously) + :30 (early-return on !loupeCanvas) + ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (canvas is inside v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value") + ImageEyedropper.vue:165 (onHover opens with `if (pinned.value) return`). MEASURED live at http://localhost:9000 (dpr 2): hover1 @ image(8,8) -> loupe opaquePx 0/12100, centerRGBA [0,0,0,0]; hover2 @ SAME coords -> opaquePx 9604/12100, centerRGBA [0,255,0,255]. Touch path, two independent runs/fixtures: A_firstTapGreen.loupe = {opaquePx:0, total:12100, centerRGBA:[0,0,0,0]}; touchTapLoupe (512x512 grid fixture) = {opaquePx:0, total:12100}.
defects.mechanism: Event handler mutates reactive state and then acts on the DOM in the same synchronous tick, before Vue's render flush creates the element — compounded by a state gate (pinned) that makes the miss permanent instead of self-healing.
defects.reproduction: On a touch device (or with synthesised touch PointerEvents): open /#/extract, drop an image, click the preview to open the eyedropper, TAP once anywhere on the image. The loupe circle appears and is fully transparent (no magnification), and stays that way until you unpin. On desktop, hover once -> blank; hover a second time -> it fills.
defects.proposedCure: Make the paint a function of state, not a side effect of an event: delete the exported-but-unused drawLoupe call from showLoupeAt and drive the canvas from a single `watch([loupeVisible, loupeRelX, loupeRelY], ..., { flush: 'post' })` inside useLoupeCanvas. That removes the ordering hazard structurally rather than sprinkling nextTick, and collapses the composable's public surface.

defects.defect: `justUnpinned` is a cross-tick latch with exactly one exit, so a pan-while-pinned leaves it set and the NEXT clean tap is silently swallowed — no sample, no pin, no feedback.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (capture-phase pointerdown sets justUnpinned=true whenever pinned) + :151-155 (onTap is the ONLY clearer) + useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when !hasMoved). MEASURED, one scripted touch sequence, 16x16 fixture: A tap(8,8) -> readout `oklch(86.643961752344% 0.294827224543 142.495345041444deg)` (=#00ff00, pins); B press+drag 80px+release -> readout unchanged, pinned now false, flag stuck; C clean tap -> readout UNCHANGED (swallowed); D byte-identical tap at identical coords -> readout `oklch(59.987080562215% 0 none)` (=#808080). C and D are the same input with different outcomes.
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled boolean flag carried across two separate gestures through a capture-phase side channel, whose clear-path is reachable only on one of the three ways a gesture can end.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, tap to sample+pin, then press-drag to pan the image, release. Now tap once to sample a new pixel — nothing happens. Tap again — it works. Every first tap after a pan is dropped.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the flag and the capture-phase interceptor. Move `pinned` into useInertiaGesture, which already owns hasMoved/isPanning, and let it decide at pointerup between unpin / sample / pan-end from facts it already has. One state machine in one place instead of two halves talking through a boolean.

defects.defect: A malformed or non-image file produces two unhandled promise rejections and a dead, error-less eyedropper overlay that still advertises "tap to sample"; the <input type=file> path also lacks the MIME guard the drop path has.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:72-75 (`img.onerror = reject` — rejects with a raw Event, not an Error) + ImageEyedropper.vue:238,247 (loadAndFit() is a floating promise at both call sites, no catch) + ImageDropZone.vue:87-92 (onFileSelected has NO type check) vs :97 (onDrop DOES check `file?.type.startsWith("image/")`). MEASURED: assigning an application/pdf File to the hidden input yields {previewZoneAppeared:true, previewLabel:"Image preview area, tap to sample colors", overlayOpen:true, canvasBacking:[300,150], readout:"Tap to sample", errorSurfacedToUser:false} and unhandled rejections ["The source image could not be decoded.","error"]. Browser console log .playwright-mcp/console-2026-07-28T13-54-12-549Z.log: `[38906ms] The source image could not be decoded.` / `[38971ms] Event`. canvasBacking [300,150] is the browser DEFAULT — proof loadImage threw before useImageSampler.ts:88-89 ever sized the canvas.
defects.mechanism: Async work started from a lifecycle hook as a floating promise, with the failure branch rejecting a non-Error and no consumer-side error state — so the failure is invisible to both the user and the code.
defects.reproduction: On /#/extract click the drop zone, choose 'All Files' in the OS picker, select any non-image (a .pdf). The preview zone appears labelled 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'; click it; the eyedropper opens permanently empty saying 'Tap to sample' with no error anywhere, and two unhandled rejections hit the console.
defects.proposedCure: loadImage rejects with a real Error; the shell owns an `imageError` ref rendered in the same `text-destructive` register the sibling already uses (ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85); and ImageDropZone applies its existing MIME guard at BOTH entrances rather than only at the drop.

defects.defect: The eyedropper is 100% inoperable by keyboard and invisible to assistive technology: no dialog role, no focus move/trap/restore, no aria-live on the async readout, and the sampling surface is aria-hidden with no keyboard alternative.
defects.evidence: MEASURED on the live open overlay: overlay role=null, aria-modal=null, [aria-live] count inside overlay = 0, document.activeElement on open = BODY (focus never enters), focusables inside overlay (unpinned) = 1 (Close only), canvas tabIndex=-1 + aria-hidden="true", viewport div tabIndex=-1 role=null, buttons = [{title:"Close eyedropper", ariaLabel:null, text:""}] at 40x40 CSS px. Source: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (bare div `absolute inset-0 z-popover ... glass-floating`), :74 (aria-hidden canvas), :35-37 (readout span, no aria-live), :43-58 (Add/Apply are v-if="pinned", and pinned is set only from onTap i.e. only from a pointer). Entry is gated too: ImageDropZone.vue:21 sets tabindex -1 once a preview exists.
defects.mechanism: A modal surface hand-rolled from positioning utilities instead of adopting the design system's dialog primitive — the hand-roll is the direct cause of every missing semantic.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/extract, upload an image, open the eyedropper, then use only the keyboard. Tab moves into the controls the overlay is visually covering, never into it. There is no key that samples a pixel, and the Add/Apply buttons never render because pinned is pointer-only. WCAG 2.1.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A), 2.4.3 (A) all fail.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive (edict 4) so role/aria-modal/focus-trap/restoration come from the design system; add aria-live="polite" to the readout; and bind arrow keys to the same sampleAt the pointer uses so pinning has a keyboard path.

defects.defect: A ResizeObserver is wired directly to the initialiser, so any viewport size change unconditionally discards the user's zoom and pan.
defects.evidence: useInertiaGesture.ts:354-360 (`new ResizeObserver(() => fitToViewport())`) + :164-166 (fitToViewport unconditionally assigns `zoom.value = fit` and recentres pan). MEASURED with a 512x512 fixture, changing only a CSS height on a DOM ancestor (no component API called): beforeZoom {zoom:0.691406}, afterWheelZoom {zoom:1.39125}, afterResize {zoom:0.691406}, afterRestore {zoom:0.691406}. A 2.01x inspection zoom is destroyed and does not return when the resize is undone.
defects.mechanism: Conflation of 'fit' (a one-time initialisation) with 'reflow' (a size-change response), so a continuous observer keeps re-running an initialiser.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on any image, ctrl+wheel to zoom in, then resize the window (or on mobile Safari, scroll so the URL bar collapses). The zoom snaps back to fit and the pan recentres.
defects.proposedCure: Split the two: fitToViewport stays a one-time call from loadAndFit/onTransitionEnd (where ImageEyedropper.vue:203,207 already calls it), and the ResizeObserver runs a distinct `reflow()` that preserves the zoom ratio and the image-space centre point and only re-clamps the pan.

defects.defect: Off-image sampling leaves a stale readout and a parked loupe — the instrument reports a colour that is not under the pointer, with no 'nothing here' state.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:114-115 (sampleAt returns null out of bounds) + ImageEyedropper.vue:156-171 (both callers are `if (result) {...}` with NO else). MEASURED, 16x16 fixture where the image occupies viewport x in [174,334]: hover3 @ image(0,0) -> readout `oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)` (=#ff0000), loupe centerRGBA [255,0,0,255], opaquePx 2996; hover4 @ viewport(5,5) — 169 CSS px OUTSIDE the image — readout UNCHANGED, loupePresent true, centerRGBA STILL [255,0,0,255].
defects.mechanism: The one honest failure signal the sampler produces (null) is dropped on the floor by every caller, so the last successful sample masquerades as the current one.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on an image smaller than the viewport, hover over the image (readout shows a colour), then move the pointer into the empty letterboxed area beside the image. The readout and the loupe keep showing the old pixel.
defects.proposedCure: Have sampleAt return a discriminated result rather than `T | null` so a caller cannot silently ignore the miss, and give onHover/onTap an explicit miss branch: hide the loupe and return the readout to its 'Tap to sample' register.

defects.defect: The 'added to palette' confirmation pulse cannot restart inside its own 0.65 s window, so a rapid second Add gives the user no feedback at all.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:21-22 (`:class="[..., swatchPulse ? 'swatch-pulse' : 'w-7 h-7']"` with `@animationend="swatchPulse = false"`) + :215 (onAddToPalette sets swatchPulse.value = true) + :285-289 (`.swatch-pulse { width:1.75rem; height:1.75rem; animation: swatch-pop 0.65s var(--ease-spring) forwards }`). If swatchPulse is already true the class list does not change, so the CSS animation is never re-triggered — no reflow-forcing removal, no :key restart, no `animation:none` toggle anywhere in the file. Secondary: `.swatch-pulse` re-declares the same 1.75rem that `w-7 h-7` carries in the other branch, so the swatch size has two sources of truth.
defects.mechanism: A CSS animation restarted by toggling a boolean that is already set — the classic missing-restart, made structural by having the animation class also own the element's size so the two cannot be decoupled.
defects.reproduction: Pin a sample, then click 'Add to palette' twice within 650 ms. The first click pops the swatch; the second emits addToPalette but produces no visible confirmation.
defects.proposedCure: Keep `w-7 h-7` unconditionally, add/remove only `swatch-pulse`, and restart with an incrementing `:key` on the WatercolorDot. The keyframe itself stays put (edict 6 — animations are moved or tokenized, never deleted).

defects.defect: `loadImage` resurrects a disposed sampler: its post-await continuation re-allocates a full-resolution offscreen canvas and flips `imageLoaded` true on a component that has already unmounted.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:242-245 (onBeforeUnmount calls sampler.dispose()) + useImageSampler.ts:68-95 — everything after `await new Promise(...)` runs unconditionally: `offscreenCanvas = document.createElement("canvas")` (:80), `offscreenCtx.drawImage(img,0,0)` (:84), `imageLoaded.value = true` (:94). dispose() at :97-101 nulls the handles and sets imageLoaded=false, but there is no generation token and no abort, so the continuation undoes all three.
defects.mechanism: Un-cancelled async work whose completion path writes to state the teardown has already reclaimed — the same missing generation token that produces r1's D-12 re-entrancy race, seen from the teardown side.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on a large photo and press Escape (ImageEyedropper.vue:226-235 -> emit('close') -> v-if unmount at ExtractWorkbench.vue:174-177) before the decode finishes. A full-resolution canvas (~48 MB for a 12 MP image) is allocated after the component is gone. Not a lasting leak — the closure is unreachable so GC reclaims it — which is why this is MINOR.
defects.proposedCure: One generation counter in useImageSampler: increment on every loadImage and on dispose, and have the continuation bail if its generation is stale. That single token fixes both this and the overlapping-load race.

defects.defect: glass-ui `DockControl` exposes no accessible-name prop, so the eyedropper's three controls are named solely by a fall-through `title` attribute — and the consumer cannot fix it without a per-instance patch that edict 5 forbids.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts — the complete __VLS_Props surface is `shape | compact | active | type | disabled | as | asChild | class`; there is no label/ariaLabel/title prop. MEASURED on the live overlay: buttons = [{title:"Close eyedropper", ariaLabel:null, text:""}, {title:"Add to palette", ...}, {title:"Apply as current color", ...}]. Sibling dock components in dist/dock.js already do this correctly: `"aria-label": e.label ?? e.id`. Related: ImageEyedropper.vue:279-282 reaches into the control's slotted svg (`.eyedropper-action-btn:hover:not(:disabled) svg { color: var(--hover-color); transform: scale(1.2) }`) driven by an inline per-instance `--hover-color` at :10.
defects.mechanism: A design-system primitive missing a first-class affordance, which pushes consumers into per-instance overrides and title-only naming — an upstream gap, not a call-site bug.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static read of the shipped .d.ts plus a live DOM measurement of the rendered buttons; there is no failing interaction beyond the weak accessible name (title is the last-resort accname source and is invisible on touch).
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox under the standing relay edict: DockControl should take a `label` prop and stamp aria-label the way its dock siblings already do, and should own the 'icon tints to the active colour on hover' variant that ImageEyedropper currently fakes with a descendant selector. Fix upstream; delete the demo-side override.

defects.evidence: `git check-ignore -v docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/evidence-touch-tap-blank-loupe.png` -> `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/.gitignore:10:audit/components/**/*.png`. defects.defect: The test gate is vacuous: the sole test file exercises one pure formatting function, and seven named mutations that delete or invert the component's entire behaviour keep it 3/3 green. No e2e spec ever opens the eyedropper, and the visual audit never renders it.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "Eyedropper|useImageSampler|useInertiaGesture|useLoupeCanvas" test/ e2e/` -> exactly one file, test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts (31 lines, 3 tests, all calling only formatInColorSpace on a sampler built with `canvasRef: ref(null)` and an identity transform, :8-14). `grep -rn -i "eyedrop" e2e/` -> one prose comment at e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:16. Green-keeping mutations: viewportToImage -> {ix:0,iy:0}; sampleAt -> return null; delete the bounds check at useImageSampler.ts:114-115; delete useLoupeCanvas.ts; delete useInertiaGesture.ts; loadImage -> throw always; Math.floor -> Math.round in viewportToImage. Visual gate is equally empty: REPORT.json /#/extract records counts.canvas:1 (the atmosphere field) in all four Safari matrices — the eyedropper's two canvases are absent because the overlay only mounts after an upload plus a pointer click; the 3 namelessButtons and 6 smallTapTargets on that route are itemised in the JSON as belonging to other components (input 160x23, 'Switch to slug', 'Generate new slug', 'Cancel', two 12x24 slider label spans); and shots/zoom-200-desktop/ contains adminusers, blob, browse, gradient, picker — no extract.
defects.mechanism: Coverage aimed at the one pure function that was easy to isolate, while every stateful surface (coordinate mapping, bounds, load, gesture machine, loupe) sits behind DOM/pointer wiring no gate drives.
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts` passes 3/3. Apply any mutation in the table above and it still passes 3/3 — including deleting both composables that contain both BLOCKERs.
defects.proposedCure: The two composables are already injectable by construction (useImageSampler takes a canvasRef; useLoupeCanvas takes getOffscreenCanvas + viewportToImage). A happy-dom test feeding a known 2x2 ImageData and asserting sampleAt at four corners, one out-of-bounds, and one alpha-0 pixel would fail on every mutation listed and would have caught N-1. The tap/unpin machine becomes unit-testable the moment C-2's cure moves it into the gesture composable — the cure and the coverage are the same change.

defects.defect: Carried forward from r1 and NOT independently re-verified by this seat: alpha discarded (transparent pixels emitted as opaque black), the see-through specimen (displayed colour != sampled colour over alpha), and the double full-resolution canvas with a force-promoted compositor layer.
defects.evidence: challenge-C-implementation.r1.md D-3 (useImageSampler.ts:32-35,116-118 — data[3] is never read), D-7 (useImageSampler.ts:84,91 — drawImage onto a transparent canvas inside a translucent glass-floating overlay), D-8 (useImageSampler.ts:80-92 sizes BOTH canvases to natural dimensions + ImageEyedropper.vue:71 will-change-transform pins the visible one as its own layer; r1 measured 4000x3000 -> bytesVisibleCanvas 48000000, totalCanvasBytesMin 96000000). This seat independently confirmed the shared premise — the visible canvas backing always equals the image's natural size (measured [16,16] for the 16x16 fixture, [512,512] for the 512x512 fixture, and the browser-default [300,150] when the decode failed) — but did not construct the alpha or compositing measurements.
defects.mechanism: Same root as the premise this seat did verify: the sampler treats the visible canvas as a second full-resolution copy of the bitmap and reads only RGB from the offscreen one.
defects.reproduction: NONE by this seat — see challenge-C-implementation.r1.md for r1's reproductions. Listed here so the r2 hand-off loses nothing from r1.
defects.proposedCure: Per r1: read data[3] and refuse (or carry) alpha via the null path sampleAt already owns; paint an opaque ground (the bg-stage token the workbench already uses) under the specimen; cap the visible canvas at the viewport's device-pixel budget and keep native resolution only in the never-composited offscreen canvas; promote only while gestureActive, which is already tracked.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared for this seat, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-21 — the demo's TYPE resolution of the published value.js surface has drifted off `package.json#exports`: `tsconfig.demo.json:42,44,47` map `@mkbabb/value.js` → `dist/index.d.ts`, `/parsing`, `/units`, all three targets MISSING and none of the three a published `exports` key; and the two subpaths that ARE published but unmapped include `/css` — the exact specifier this component's composable imports at `useImageSampler.ts:13`. The runtime alias set is GENERATED from `package.json#exports` (vite.config.ts:33-49) and cannot drift; the type side was hand-maintained and did. Both prior audit passes certified "the published-surface discipline is what is sound"; this falsifies the type half of that certification. Cure is a deletion, and its sufficiency is already proved: `tsc --traceResolution` shows the UNMAPPED `@mkbabb/value.js/css` resolving correctly to `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` through Node self-reference, i.e. through `package.json#exports` itself.
result.negativeProof: Three axes were probed and are provably clean, so the DEFECTIVE verdict is scoped, not global. (1) IMPORT DIRECTION: every edge in the chain was traced to its home (11 edges, tabulated in the report §0). No feature→shell, feature→boot (demo/color-picker), or cross-feature edge exists; the one cross-tree edge (workbenches/extract → color-session) is explicitly permitted by docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:56-62 (`feature → color-session / own descendants / platform / shared / published packages`). (2) RUNTIME PUBLISHED-SURFACE HONESTY: `useImageSampler.ts:12-13` imports `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`; both are literal keys in `package.json#exports` (package.json:20-49), and the Vite alias set that resolves them is generated from that same map with anchored regexes (vite.config.ts:33-49), so a deep `src/` path could not silently work. `grep -rn "@src" demo/workbenches/extract` → zero hits. A real npm consumer could write both lines verbatim. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8): every type-only import carries `type` — ImageEyedropper.vue:99 (`type DisplayColorSpace`), useImageSampler.ts:11 (`type Ref`), :12 (`type SpaceId`), :19 (`type PickerColor`), useInertiaGesture.ts:1 (`type Ref`). Also clean: no object-URL leaks in this feature (`grep -rn "createObjectURL" demo` → only demo/palettes/export.ts:88,126, both revoked at :99,:114,:131); `willReadFrequently` correctly set (useImageSampler.ts:83); `@keyframes swatch-pop` is correctly a scoped component keyframe (edict 6, no violation); and inv-K-1 (`src/**` never imports glass-ui, eslint.config.js:204-217) is the one boundary lint still alive and is unaffected.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json `paths` has drifted off package.json#exports: three mappings point at files that do not exist, two published subpaths (including `/css`, used by this component) have no mapping at all, and the one bare specifier that IS mapped is not a published exports key. The runtime axis is generated and drift-proof; the type axis is hand-maintained and drifted. NEW — absent from both prior passes (grep -c tsconfig on the pre-existing 958 lines = 0).
defects.evidence: tsconfig.demo.json:42 `@mkbabb/value.js` → `./dist/index.d.ts`; :44 `/parsing`; :47 `/units`. Measured: `for f in dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts; do [ -e $f ] && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING; done` → MISSING / MISSING / MISSING. `ls dist/subpaths/` → color css easing math quantize transform value (7, .d.ts+.js each). package.json:20-49 exports keys = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize — no `.` root key (vite.config.ts:203-205 states so). `/css` and `/value` have NO tsconfig mapping; useImageSampler.ts:13 imports `@mkbabb/value.js/css`. Also md5 -q dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts → e0968b8d3b9a5ecabc7c8c1d01de9995 vs 4309648d15b521dc8281eab37ccc32a2 (hoisted glass-ui peer copy is a different file).

defects.proposedCure: DELETE the entire `@mkbabb/value.js*` paths block (tsconfig.demo.json:42-49). Node/TS self-reference resolves all seven subpaths through package.json#exports — the same single source the Vite alias is generated from — making the type axis drift-proof by construction rather than by vigilance. The traceResolution output above is the proof of sufficiency: an unmapped published subpath already resolves exactly right. Corollary benefit: dist/index.d.ts and /parsing and /units become unreachable, which is correct — they are not published.

defects.defect: Hex serialization has four independent demo homes because the published library surface has none. value.js parses hex but cannot write it, so every consumer that needs a hex string mints its own encoder. NEW — the prior passes' L-9 covers the byte→string→parser round-trip but not the hex-writer ownership gap (killing the round-trip does not kill formatHex; only a library toHex does).
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "export function.*[Hh]ex\|export const.*[Hh]ex" src/` → zero hits. test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts:19 proves both halves: parseCssColor accepts '#ff0000', and serializeCssColor of it emits 'rgb(255 0 0)', never hex. Four mints: `grep -rn "padStart(2" demo src --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` → useImageSampler.ts:33, picker-color.ts:215, MiniColorPicker.vue:103, palettes/export/bytes.ts:31.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric public surface — the library owns one direction of a bijection (parse) and declines the other (serialize), so the missing half is re-implemented once per consumer. Ownership vacuum, not duplication-by-carelessness.

defects.proposedCure: `/color` exports `toHex(color, { alpha?: boolean }): string` beside the existing `toRgba8`. All four demo mints die; picker-color.ts:213-217 (pickerColorToHex) and its pass-through wrapper color-model.ts:61-65 (colorToHexString) collapse with them.

defects.defect: docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md §2 declares a canonical numeric library-display spelling for the four non-CSS spaces; nothing implements it, two demo modules invented two divergent notations, and a test canonizes a third. NEW reference axis — the prior pass-2 L-17 establishes that the two demo notations disagree with EACH OTHER but never cites the spec, so it could not show that both are wrong.
defects.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md §2 hsv row: 'no CSS spelling; numeric library display `hsv(hdeg s% v% / α%)` only' → for #ff0000 the specified rendering is `hsv(0deg 100% 100%)`. Shipped: useImageSampler.ts:38-44 emits 'HSV 0 · 1 · 1'; ColorSpaceSelector.vue:154-165 emits 'hsv · 0 · 1 · 1'. Both drop the required %/deg units AND print physical 0–1 coordinates where the spec's display form is percentage — differently SCALED, not merely differently formatted. test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts:26 freezes the eyedropper's version: expect(...).toBe("HSV 0 · 1 · 1").
defects.mechanism: a notation defined by the library's own specification has no library implementation, so the concern falls to consumers; two consumers implement it independently and neither reads the spec. Same root as L-22 (library declines a job that is its own).

defects.proposedCure: `/css` gains `serializeLibraryColor(color)` beside `serializeCssColor`, emitting the ARCHITECTURE §2 spelling for hsv/kelvin/ictcp/jzazbz. Both demo implementations then reduce to `CSS_PICKER_SPACES.has(s) ? serializeCssColor : serializeLibraryColor` — and that two-line function belongs once, in color-session/, not twice. The test's expectation is corrected to the spec, not the other way round.

defects.defect: The loupe's resolution loss is fixed by arithmetic at every devicePixelRatio (backing store == CSS box by construction), and the DISPLAY canvas has the opposite defect: it is bilinearly smoothed while sampleAt returns the exact nearest source pixel, so seen ≠ sampled at every edge above 1× zoom. NEW half — the prior L-2/L-3 note the 110→106 resample and 'no DPR policy'; neither states that the ratio is DPR-invariant by construction, and neither examines the display canvas's filter.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 hard-codes `width="110" height="110"`; the CSS box is `${LOUPE_SIZE}px` = 110px (ImageEyedropper.vue:194-195, constants.ts:8). backing ÷ CSS box = 1.0 regardless of dpr → 1/2 device resolution at dpr 2, 1/3 at dpr 3, on the surface that deliberately sets imageSmoothingEnabled=false (useLoupeCanvas.ts:40). Display canvas measured live on localhost:9000 #/extract with a 64×64 synthetic upload: canvasBacking {w:64,h:64}, transform 'translate(0px, 59.1836px) scale(7.9375)'. `grep -rn "image-rendering\|pixelated" demo --include=*.css --include=*.vue` → no output. sampleAt (useImageSampler.ts:111-119) reads the offscreen canvas at native resolution.
defects.mechanism: one bitmap rendered twice under two filter policies, split across two composables with no shared filter or DPR contract; and a backing-store size expressed as a template literal instead of derived from the constant + dpr. glass-ui already owns the concern (useCanvas2D `dprPolicy`) and is bypassed — edict 4.

grep -n 'LOUPE_SIZE' demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/constants.ts demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue
grep -rn "image-rendering\|pixelated" demo --include="*.css" --include="*.vue"   # zero hits
# live: navigate localhost:9000/#/extract, upload any image, click preview, read
#   document.querySelector('canvas.eyedropper-canvas').style.transform → scale(7.9375) with backing 64x64
defects.proposedCure: Size the loupe backing store `LOUPE_SIZE * dpr` with ctx.scale(dpr,dpr) — or mount it through glass-ui's useCanvas2D, whose dprPolicy already owns this (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/glass/canvas2d/useCanvas2D.d.ts). Give the display surface `image-rendering: pixelated` above 1× so seen == sampled. Under the File-based decode cure the display canvas becomes an and only the image-rendering decision survives.

defects.defect: The demo import lattice the dead lint was meant to encode is already written down normatively in docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:56-62 and is enforced by nothing; and its 'promoted once' clause is exactly what DisplayColorSpace×4 breaks, via a seam choice — the component reaches past color-session's face (color-model.ts) into its substrate (picker-color.ts). NEW — grep -c ARCHITECTURE on the pre-existing report = 0; pass 1's L-10 reports the dead lint but never names the law or the face/substrate mechanism.
defects.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:56-62 gives the six-row lattice and states 'Cross-feature internal imports are forbidden by construction' and 'When two live consumers need another semantic object, it is promoted once'. Nothing constructs it: eslint.config.js:235-238 and :275-276 glob demo/@/**; `ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory; the three globs match 0,0,0 files. The surviving glob (demo/color-picker/**) bans '@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue', an alias tsconfig.demo.json:36 records as deleted. Mechanism: useImageSampler.ts:14-19 imports from color-session/picker-color (substrate) not color-session/color-model (the face — its header at :1-6 declares itself the shared surface, and it owns DisplayColorSpace at :29, CSS_NATIVE_SPACES at :58, toCSSColorString at :67, colorToHexString at :61). color-session has no index.ts, so 'the face' is a convention nothing can enforce.
defects.mechanism: a boundary law expressed only as prose plus lint aimed at a deleted tree; combined with a flat domain directory that publishes no public/private seam, so a consumer cannot tell the face from the substrate and picks the deeper one — putting the canonical type out of view and inviting the local mint.

defects.proposedCure: Delete the three dead lint objects (they read as coverage, which is worse than absent) and encode the ARCHITECTURE lattice as real no-restricted-imports zones over the physical tree: for each demo/workbenches/<f>/**, ban demo/workbenches/!(<f>)/**, demo/shell/**, demo/color-picker/**, demo/picker/**, demo/scenes/**; for demo/color-session/**, ban every feature tree. Six objects, mechanically derivable from the doc. Optionally add color-session/index.ts as the face so the substrate reach is nameable too.

(b) defensive scaffolding for a state the type-level contract makes unreachable — legacy under edict 2; the `imageUrl: string` prop is too wide for what the only producer emits.
