defects.proposedCure: Per the greenfield lattice in the report: (1) promote useInertiaGesture WHOLE to @mkbabb/glass-ui/gesture as usePanZoom — 379 of the feature's 1002 lines, zero demo coupling, and it arrives with useResizeObserver + useDragVelocity already in hand; (2) decode once at the session (useExtractSession owns the ImageBitmap; ImageEyedropper takes File/ImageBitmap, not a string URL; the visible canvas becomes an ); (3) useImageSampler returns {r,g,b} only — hex to /color, display formatting to color-session — dropping it 139 → ~60 lines and removing both value.js imports and the four-hop climb; (4) useLoupeCanvas takes its canvas as an argument (or mounts it via glass-ui useCanvas2D) so existence and reference share one owner; (5) delete the three local DisplayColorSpace mints and import the canonical one.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared by the spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-02 — the two-law modal collision: after the first sample, every subsequent sample costs two clicks, and the discarded first click deletes the only commit affordance. Measured cycle at 1512x806 WebKit DPR2 (evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json `pinCycle`): hover A -> readout=A, 1 button, loupe painted 9684px; click A -> pinned, 3 buttons ["Close eyedropper","Add to palette","Apply as current color"]; **click B -> readout STILL A, buttons back to 1, loupe canvas gone**; click B again -> readout finally B. Cause: the capture-phase pointerdown unpin at ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 sets a non-reactive `justUnpinned`, and onTap (lines 151-155) early-returns on it. The same law makes the magnifier loupe permanently blank on touch (0 of 12100 non-transparent px, evidence/E2), because pinning suppresses the only redraw path.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but four named suspects were cleared with positive evidence and are recorded in report section 7: (N-1) no object-URL leak is possible — `grep -rn "createObjectURL" demo/workbenches/` returns 0 hits; the image path is FileReader.readAsDataURL at useExtractSession.ts:29-36, and the only createObjectURL in demo/ is palettes/export.ts:88,126 each with a matching revoke at 99,114,131. (N-2) tainted-canvas/CORS getImageData is unreachable — every imageUrl this component can receive is a same-origin `data:` URL minted in-process, so useImageSampler.ts:116 cannot throw SecurityError. (N-3) interior pointer→pixel mapping is EXACT — against a specimen obeying r=4·x, g=4·y, hovering the geometric centre of image pixel (ix,iy) produced swatch colours (16,16)→rgb(64,64,0), (48,16)→rgb(192,64,0), (16,48)→rgb(64,192,0), (48,48)→rgb(192,192,0); four for four, zero error. (N-4) prefers-reduced-motion IS honoured — measured swatch-pop animation-duration 0.00001s under reducedMotion:"reduce"; the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 reaches the scoped keyframes, and useInertiaGesture.ts:131-142 owns its own PRM branch. (N-6) horizontal overflow is clean at both 100% and 200% (docOverflowX 0).

defects.defect: The magnifier loupe paints nothing on the first sample, and never at all on touch — the component's one specialised organ renders as a hollow ring over the un-magnified image.
defects.evidence: useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 sets loupeVisible=true then calls drawLoupe() synchronously, but the canvas is behind v-if at ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 so loupeCanvasRef.value is still null and drawLoupe returns at line 30. Measured `loupeEmpty {nonAlphaPx: 0, totalPx: 12100}` and `loupeCenter [0,0,0,0]` in three independent matrices: desktop-dark after one pointermove, forced-colors, and mobile-dark after tap (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json). Visually confirmed in evidence/E1-desktop-dark-loupe-hollow.png and evidence/E2-mobile-dark-tap-loupe-blank.png.
defects.mechanism: draw-before-mount: imperative draw issued in the same tick as the v-if that creates its own canvas
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1512x806 DPR2 or 390x844 DPR3, http://localhost:9000/#/extract, load an image, click the drop zone to open the eyedropper, dispatch one pointerdown+pointerup on the sampler region (no prior pointermove), then read the loupe canvas: `document.querySelector('.loupe canvas').getContext('2d').getImageData(0,0,110,110)` has 0 pixels with alpha>0. On touch it never recovers because pinned=true suppresses onHover (ImageEyedropper.vue:165).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the imperative show/draw pair. Render the loupe unconditionally with opacity/visibility driven by a reactive `sample` model — never v-if — so no draw can precede its own canvas, and let the canvas repaint in a post-DOM effect on that model. The loupe becomes a derived view, not a commanded one.

defects.defect: Every sample after the first costs two clicks; the discarded intermediate click silently deletes Add-to-palette and Apply while leaving the previous colour on screen as if current.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 registers a capture-phase pointerdown that unpins and sets a plain `let justUnpinned = true` (line 123); onTap at 151-155 then early-returns. Measured `pinCycle` in evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json: hoverA readout=lab(26.204...), 1 button, loupeNonAlpha 9684 → click1 pinned, 3 buttons → click2 at a different pixel: readout UNCHANGED lab(26.204...), buttons back to ["Close eyedropper"], loupeNonAlpha null → click3 finally reads lab(75.771...).
defects.mechanism: two-law modal collision (hover-samples vs pin-freezes) mediated by a non-reactive flag and a capture-phase listener
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, hover pixel A, click A (pins, 3 buttons appear), click pixel B — the readout still shows A and only the Close button remains; click B again to actually sample it. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/evidence/probe-B.mjs` reproduces the four-step table.
defects.proposedCure: Introduce one `sample: {ix,iy,rgb,css} | null` + `frozen: boolean` model. A tap always sets a new sample and freezes it; delete `justUnpinned` and the capture-phase listener entirely so no gesture can be consumed without producing a sample. D-01, D-02 and D-11 collapse into this one change.

defects.defect: No keyboard or numeric sampling path exists at all — the only key bound anywhere in the component is Escape.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:226-235 is the entire keyboard surface (Escape only), registered globally on window at line 239. Measured `keyboard.focusablesInOverlay: 1` of `totalFocusables: 22` (evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json); the single overlay focusable is the Close button. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.2 row 'image sampler coordinates' mandates Right/Left = source-image x, Down/Up = source-image y, 'named x/y controls own Home=min and End=max; reticle, loupe and numeric value remain one model'. §7 Extract: 'Eyedropper and sampler have keyboard/numeric alternatives.' §5: 'every spatial action has a keyboard/numeric equivalent.'
defects.mechanism: missing model surface — the sample is only addressable by pointer coordinates
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper and press Tab 12 times: every landing is outside the overlay (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json `tabWalk`, all 12 entries `inOverlay: false`). Arrow keys, Home and End produce no sample and no reticle movement.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the §5 domain-neutral axis composition already used by Picker/Generate/Gradient/Atmosphere/Blob: a named x and y Slider pair over the same sample model, Home=min End=max, sharing the reticle/loupe/readout. No new mechanism is required — the composition already ships.

defects.defect: In RTL the sampler canvas is rendered 444 px outside its own clipping stage; only ~8 of 64 image columns remain visible and every sample addresses a pixel that is not under the pointer.
defects.evidence: Measured at 1512x806 WebKit, dir=rtl (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json `rtl`): sampler region x=767.5 w=508, canvas x=1211.5 w=508 → canvas.x − viewport.x = +444.0, while the model panX is 0. The LTR delta is 0.0. Visually catastrophic in evidence/E3-rtl-canvas-444px-off.png — the specimen collapses to a sliver overhanging the Extract card's rounded edge. sampleAt (useImageSampler.ts:111-119) computes ix from the model pan, so it disagrees with the render by 444 px / 7.94 = 56 image columns.
defects.mechanism: direction-unaware geometry: a statically-positioned canvas with origin-top-left + translate() flips its layout origin to the inline-end edge under dir=rtl
defects.reproduction: Set document.documentElement.dir='rtl' before app boot, open the eyedropper, and compare getBoundingClientRect() of canvas.eyedropper-canvas against the touch-action:none sampler region. `node .../evidence/probe-A.mjs` matrix 5.
defects.proposedCure: The sampler stage is a scientific coordinate surface, not chrome (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1). Position the canvas absolutely at inset-inline-start:0; top:0 (or express the whole pan/zoom in one direction-neutral transform anchored to the stage origin) so the render and the model share one origin in both directions.

defects.defect: A modal in geometry, nothing in semantics: the overlay has no role, no accessible name, no aria-modal, moves no focus in, restores no focus out, leaves 21 of 22 document focusables tabbable behind it, and installs a global window keydown listener.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 is a bare `<div class="absolute inset-0 z-popover ...">`; measured overlayRole null, overlayAriaModal null, overlayAriaLabel null, overlayTabindex null (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json). `keyboard.totalFocusables: 22`, `focusablesInOverlay: 1`, no inert or aria-hidden ancestor anywhere. focusAfter open = 'DIV|Image preview area, tap to sample colors' (focus never entered); after Escape closes it, activeElement is BODY — the opener is not restored. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 'Dialog/Drawer/Popover open and close | producer initial-focus rule on open; exact connected opener on close'. Global listener at line 239.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled dialog where a producer primitive exists
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper and Tab: focus cycles through the k slider, chroma slider and file input behind the overlay and never enters it (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json `tabWalk`). Press Escape twice: `escape.afterEsc2.active` = 'BODY|'.
defects.proposedCure: Use the producer Dialog primitive instead of `absolute inset-0` + window.addEventListener. Role, accessible name, aria-modal, initial focus, focus restoration and background inerting all arrive with it, and the global keydown listener disappears.

defects.defect: The sampler stage overflows the viewport fold and cannot be scrolled to, because the overlay is sized to a content-flow parent rather than anchored to the visual viewport.
defects.evidence: At 1512x806: overlay y=186.4 h=685.6 → bottom 872.0 vs innerHeight 806; sampler-region bottom 870.9; canvas bottom 811.1 (evidence/probe-A-matrices.json). At documentElement zoom 2: overlay bottom 1743.9, canvas bottom 2381.9, vs innerHeight 806 — two-thirds of the specimen off-fold (evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json `zoom200`, evidence/E4-zoom200-stage-off-fold.png). The sampler carries `touch-action: none` (ImageEyedropper.vue:66), so touch cannot scroll it back.
defects.mechanism: content-sized overlay geometry — `absolute inset-0` on ExtractWorkbench's content-height root instead of viewport-anchored dialog geometry
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper at 1512x806 and try to hover image row y=63 of a 64px specimen: the required client y is 807.2, below innerHeight 806. Set document.documentElement.style.zoom='2' and measure canvas.getBoundingClientRect().bottom = 2381.9.
defects.proposedCure: Make the sampler a region of the bound `golden` Extract stage rather than a plate-wide overlay (see D-10); if a dialog is retained, give it viewport-anchored geometry with max-block-size clamped to the dock-adjusted dvh so the stage can never exceed the fold.

defects.defect: The readout is a lying readout: it truncates the sampled value with no title, no tooltip and no expansion path — in a file whose sibling forty lines away documents the exact opposite rule.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:35-37 carries `truncate select-all` and no title. Measured (evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json `readoutTruncation`): full value `lab(52.149527332% -9.447862249415 56.024088496729)` = 50 chars, scrollWidth 510, clientWidth 371, clippedPx 139, hasTitle false. At 200% zoom clippedPx 378. On mobile it renders as `lab(52.1495…` (evidence/E2). The direct in-repo counterexample is ExtractWorkbench.vue:136-140, same route, same author, with the comment 'truncate may trim trailing digits at narrow widths; the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)' and `:title="session.dominant.value.serialized"`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 also requires live numbers to 'reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis' — measured reflow: readout box 275px unpinned → 371px pinned, a 96px jump.
defects.mechanism: lying readout — truncation without a recovery path, plus unreserved width
defects.reproduction: Sample any pixel and read `document.querySelector('.z-popover span.text-mono-small')`: scrollWidth 510 vs clientWidth 371, hasAttribute('title') === false.
defects.proposedCure: Reserve the widest legal representation for the selected space, round to the meaningful precision of an 8-bit sample (12 decimals on a value derived from three bytes is noise), and carry `title` with the full serialization exactly as the sibling does.

defects.defect: The readout ink uses the static `text-muted-foreground` token that both sibling files on this route explicitly retired for failing the text floor, and it measures 4.07:1 against its own composited paper — below the 4.5:1 AA floor — over an unbounded live-photograph ground.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:35 uses raw `text-muted-foreground`. ImageDropZone.vue:104-111 and ExtractWorkbench.vue:285-292 each carry the E1-R1 / T.W8 remediation comment 'instead of the STATIC `text-muted-foreground` that failed the text floor over the live-ambient plate in light' and use `--ink-muted` via `.plate-ink`; the eyedropper never received it. Measured contrast by decoding the rendered readout crop (268x48 device px) and computing WCAG relative luminance: p1 ink (112,89,66) L=0.1098, p99 paper (219,198,209) L=0.6005 → ratio 4.07:1. The ground is `oklab(0.936408 0.005529 0.013284 / 0.808)` + `backdrop-filter: blur(11px) saturate(1.6)` composited over the user's own photograph, so the ratio is content-dependent and unbounded. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.'
defects.mechanism: token regression plus an unbounded live-image ground behind small text
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on any image, screenshot the readout span, decode and compute WCAG luminance contrast: 4.07:1. `getComputedStyle(span).color` = rgb(112,89,66); the span's class list contains `text-muted-foreground`, not `plate-ink`.
defects.proposedCure: Thread `--ink-muted` / `.plate-ink` exactly as the two siblings do, and give the chrome bar a real instrument-veil tier (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2) with named alpha/clarity levers instead of compositing small mono text directly over a blurred user photograph.

defects.defect: Consumer CSS reaches inside a producer control to restyle its glyph, with an unguarded :hover that latches on touch — the close X renders permanently tinted the sampled colour and 1.2x larger than its siblings.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:279-282 `.eyedropper-action-btn:hover:not(:disabled) svg { color: var(--hover-color, var(--foreground)); transform: scale(1.2) }`, driven by an inline `--hover-color` on the row at line 10. No `@media (hover: hover)` guard. Visually confirmed in evidence/E2-mobile-dark-tap-loupe-blank.png: the X glyph is olive-tinted and visibly larger than the + and ✓ beside it. glass-ui 7.0.0 already publishes the seams — `--dock-control-hover-bg`, `--dock-active-color`, `--glass-accent`, `--dock-control-glyph-size` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/**). Owner edict 5 forbids per-instance overrides of a root that should be styled at the root; edict 4 puts variants in glass-ui. `:not(:disabled)` also guards a state no control here can reach — a dead selector.
defects.mechanism: per-instance override reaching past the design-system boundary, plus unguarded hover on a touch surface
defects.reproduction: On a touch context (WebKit 390x844, hasTouch), open the eyedropper by tapping the drop zone: the pointer lands on the overlay's close control and the hover style latches for the session.
defects.proposedCure: Drive the accent through the producer seams (`--dock-active-color` / `--glass-accent`) on the DockControl root, delete the descendant `svg` selector and the dead `:not(:disabled)`, and gate any hover-only affordance behind `@media (hover: hover)`.

defects.defect: The eyedropper occludes 100% of the binding Extract composition — result plate, both sliders, dominance readout and reset all disappear — where the ratified topology puts the sampler at 61.8% with result/controls at 38.2%.
defects.evidence: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:42 binds Extract to P122 `golden`: 'source/sampler 61.8033989%; result controls 38.1966011%; absent result collapses context' and 'image well is specimen, not Card'. The shipped component is `absolute inset-0` over ExtractWorkbench's root (ImageEyedropper.vue:8, mounted at ExtractWorkbench.vue:173-180); measured overlay 510x685.6 covering the whole workbench box. Visible in evidence/E1: the k slider, chroma slider, dominance row and palette card are all gone while sampling. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 8 also allows one pane exactly one full-strength protagonist.
defects.mechanism: overlay-instead-of-region — a mode implemented as a plate-wide takeover
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on /#/extract and observe that no control of the Extract instrument remains visible or reachable; measured overlay rect equals the workbench rect.
defects.proposedCure: Implement the sampler as a mode of the bound `golden` stage region rather than a full-plate overlay. The result and controls stay visible at 38.2%, the glass tier stops floating over a duplicate of its own specimen (retiring the double-image seam), and the off-fold geometry of D-06 disappears with it.

defects.defect: The commit affordances are bound to a transient pin mode rather than to the existence of a sample; a stray pointerdown removes Add-to-palette and Apply while the sampled colour survives.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:43-58 gates both action controls behind `v-if="pinned"`. Measured button lists across the click cycle (evidence/probe-B-behaviour.json `pinCycle`): ['Close eyedropper','Add to palette','Apply as current color'] → ['Close eyedropper'] → back again, while the readout text is unchanged across the first two. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace. A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth.' PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07/PR-08.
defects.mechanism: two-law modal collision — actions coupled to a mode instead of to state
defects.reproduction: Sample a pixel (3 controls appear), then press once anywhere on the image: the controls vanish though `sampledColor` is still set and still displayed.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the action set to `sample !== null`, not to `frozen`. The commit region then stops appearing and disappearing, and the 96px readout reflow of D-07 goes with it.

defects.defect: The magnifier is sub-device-resolution and has no reticle: its backing store is 110x110 for a 110 CSS-px box, so nearest-neighbour texels are bilinearly upscaled by the compositor, and nothing marks which of the 11x11 cells was actually sampled.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 hardcodes `width="110" height="110"`; measured loupeBox 110x110 CSS px at devicePixelRatio 2 (desktop) and 3 (mobile) → the buffer supplies 0.5x / 0.33x of the device pixels the box occupies. useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets `imageSmoothingEnabled = false` to draw crisp texels, which the compositor then smooths away on every retina display. drawLoupe (lines 27-53) draws the magnified region and never strokes a centre cell; the loupe is also centred exactly on the pointer (loupeStyle, lines 191-196), so it occludes the very pixel being sampled and sits under the finger on touch.
defects.mechanism: DPR-unaware backing store plus a magnifier with no index mark
defects.reproduction: Hover twice so the loupe paints, then read `document.querySelector('.loupe canvas')` — width/height attributes 110 while getBoundingClientRect() is 110 CSS px at devicePixelRatio 2. No stroked cell appears at the loupe centre in any captured frame.
defects.proposedCure: Size the backing store to `LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio` and scale the context, stroke the sampled cell's outline so the loupe indexes its own answer, and offset the loupe from the pointer (or render it in the chrome bar beside the swatch) so it stops occluding the target.

defects.defect: The stage paints with `image-rendering: auto` at up to 10x magnification, so the colour the user sees under the cursor is a bilinear blend while the sample taken is a single integer texel — three surfaces over one bitmap using three resampling laws.
defects.evidence: Measured `getComputedStyle(canvas.eyedropper-canvas).imageRendering === 'auto'` with `transform: matrix(7.9375,0,0,7.9375,0,59.789)` — a 7.94x upscale, and useInertiaGesture allows maxZoom 10 (ImageEyedropper.vue:149). The loupe explicitly disables smoothing (useLoupeCanvas.ts:40); sampleAt takes one nearest texel (useImageSampler.ts:111-119). My N-3 proof shows the sampler arithmetic is exact, so the divergence is entirely display-side: on a 1-px checker the blend is precisely the average of the two texels.
defects.mechanism: three resampling laws over one bitmap
defects.reproduction: Load a 1-px red/blue checker, magnify, and compare the composited screen pixel under the cursor against the reported value — the screen shows the blend, the readout reports one texel. Confirmed independently by round 1 (evidence quoted in challenge-D-design.r1.md §D-1: composited rgb(127,0,128) against a reported #0000FF).
defects.proposedCure: One resampling law owned in one place: `image-rendering: pixelated` on the stage above 1x so a texel is a visible square and the loupe becomes a true magnification of the same law. Below 1x, sample the area-average over the source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers — i.e. sample what the pixel shows. Do not patch sampleAt; the arithmetic is correct.

defects.defect: A dead prop from an abrogated API: `tag="div"` is passed to WatercolorDot, which has no such prop in glass-ui 7.0.0, and the demo typecheck does not catch it.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:29 passes `tag="div"`. glass-ui 7.0.0 declares `props: { color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed }` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js) — no `tag` — because VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 / OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md P051 removed the public tag/interactive-host branch. The attribute is silently swallowed: measured `document.querySelectorAll('[tag]').length === 0`. Gate gap: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 with zero output. Owner edict 2 forbids legacy residue.
defects.mechanism: legacy residue against an abrogated producer API, plus a typecheck that does not see unknown component props
defects.reproduction: Read ImageEyedropper.vue:26-33; grep the glass-ui dist props list; run the demo typecheck and observe exit 0 with no diagnostic.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `tag="div"` attribute. Separately, close the gate gap so an unknown prop on a producer component is a hard typecheck failure — otherwise every future producer API removal leaves silent residue across the demo.

defects.defect: No loading, decode-error or out-of-bounds state exists, and the image-load rejection is unhandled — a decode failure leaves the overlay permanently blank with an unhandled promise rejection.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:72-75 rejects on `img.onerror`; loadAndFit (ImageEyedropper.vue:200-204) has no try/catch and is fired and forgotten from onMounted (line 238) and from the imageUrl watcher (line 247). Nothing in the template renders an `imageLoaded === false` state — the overlay opens as an empty glass panel. sampleAt returns null out of bounds (useImageSampler.ts:114-115) and the caller silently ignores it (lines 156-162), so an out-of-range gesture produces no feedback of any kind.
defects.mechanism: absent states — the happy path is the only path rendered
defects.reproduction: Supply an imageUrl that fails to decode: the promise rejects with no handler and the overlay stays blank indefinitely with no error, retry or dismissal cue beyond Escape.
defects.proposedCure: Model load as an explicit union (`idle | decoding | ready | failed`) rendered by the overlay, with the failure arm naming the fault and offering dismissal — the same discipline ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85 already applies to quantizeError.

defects.defect: Two sources of truth for two dimensions: the loupe diameter is both a constant and a literal, and the swatch size is stated once as a utility and again in CSS.
defects.evidence: constants.ts:8 `LOUPE_SIZE = 110` drives the CSS box (ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196) while line 85 hardcodes `width="110" height="110"` for the backing store — changing the constant silently desyncs the buffer from the box and distorts the magnification. ImageEyedropper.vue:21 swaps `w-7 h-7` out when the pulse class is applied, so lines 285-289 re-declare `width: 1.75rem; height: 1.75rem` to compensate; measured computed 28px x 28px.
defects.mechanism: duplicated constant
defects.reproduction: Change LOUPE_SIZE to 140 in constants.ts: the CSS box grows to 140px while the backing store stays 110px, and the magnifier silently rescales. Change the swatch utility from w-7 to w-8: the pulse animation still renders at 28px.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the canvas width/height from LOUPE_SIZE (times DPR, per D-12), and drive the pulse from a class that adds animation only, never one that replaces the sizing utilities.

defects.defect: All three overlay controls carry only a `title` attribute with `aria-label: null`, against the app's own convention and against the audit harness's own nameless-button rule.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:11, 46, 53 use `title` and no aria-label; measured controls `[{title:'Close eyedropper', aria:null},{title:'Add to palette', aria:null},{title:'Apply as current color', aria:null}]`. Every other button probed on the page carries aria-label and no title ('Save edit', 'Cancel edit', 'Select view', 'Toggle action bar', 'Menu'). The mega-tranche harness at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:102-105 counts a button nameless unless it has aria-label, aria-labelledby or text content — title is not consulted — so these three would score as nameless if the audit ever opened the component. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07: 'every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state'.
defects.mechanism: naming — title as the sole accessible-name source
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper and read the three buttons' aria-label attributes: all null. Apply the harness predicate at capture.mjs:102-105 to them: all three score nameless.
defects.proposedCure: Give each control an aria-label matching the app convention; keep title only as a supplementary pointer tooltip, never as the sole name.

defects.defect: `will-change: transform` is applied unconditionally and permanently to a full-resolution image canvas, promoting a layer sized to the source bitmap for the lifetime of the overlay.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:71 `class="origin-top-left will-change-transform eyedropper-canvas"`; measured `getComputedStyle(canvas).willChange === 'transform'` with the canvas backing store equal to the image's natural size (measured [64,64] for the test specimen; a phone photograph is 4000x3000). MDN and the CSS Will Change spec both direct that will-change be applied only for the duration of the change, not permanently.
defects.mechanism: unconditional layer promotion
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper and read the computed willChange on canvas.eyedropper-canvas: 'transform', present at rest with no gesture in flight. NOTE: the GPU-memory magnitude for a large photograph is a HYPOTHESIS — I measured the property and the backing-store sizing rule, not the allocation for a 12MP source.
defects.proposedCure: Apply will-change only while `gesture.gestureActive` is true — the component already tracks exactly that flag for the `.no-transition` class at line 72 — and drop it at rest.

defects.defect: The component has no rendered coverage anywhere in the mega-tranche visual audit, so none of the above is visible to the tranche's evidence base.
defects.evidence: `ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/zoom-200-desktop/` → adminusers.png blob.png browse.png gradient.png picker.png — no extract. The same five-route set holds for rtl-desktop, rtl-mobile, forced-colors-desktop, keyboard-focus-desktop and reduced-motion-desktop. The four Safari matrices do capture /#/extract (REPORT.md:122,137,152,167) but only in its empty state — the eyedropper is behind `v-if="eyedropperActive && session.previewDataUrl"` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:174), and no capture loads an image. STATES.json contains no #/extract row.
defects.mechanism: evidence gap — a state-gated component that no capture path ever reaches
defects.reproduction: grep '#/extract' docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/STATES.json → no match; list the non-Safari shot directories.
defects.proposedCure: Extend states.mjs with a fixture-image upload step for /#/extract so the eyedropper's open, hovered, pinned, RTL, 200%-zoom and forced-colors states enter the standing matrix. The probes in ./evidence/ are a working template.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (round 2) of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: Three of the twenty-seven shipped specimen tiles (the whole `back` family) destroy the Gradient pane on a single click, in the default two-stop state — and the crash emits ZERO page errors and ZERO console errors, so every automated console gate (including this formation's own visual audit) is structurally blind to it.
defects.evidence: probe14.mjs on a fresh page at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `BEFORE: {"heads":1,...}` then `ease-in-back -> clicked {"heads":0,"code":null,"easingSection":false,"paneText":102}` (pane body text 599 -> 102 chars); subsequent tiles report MISSING because the subtree is gone. probe15.mjs numeric proof: ease-in-back quad [0.6,-0.28,0.735,0.045] fn(0.5) = -0.0636, ease-out-back [0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275] fn(0.5) = 1.0676, both -> `Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range`; ease-in-out-back ramp min/max -0.0923 / 1.0927. probe15 full listener output after the fatal click: `MESSAGES: ["DEBUG [vite] connecting...","DEBUG [vite] connected.","ERROR Failed to load resource: ... 404"]` — no pageerror, no component console error. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (`fn(0.5)` fed to interpolateStopColors); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (`if (!mixed.ok) throw`); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:206-208 (same unclamped throw in the sampler). Corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json which records consoleErrors: [] / pageErrors: [] for /#/gradient in all four Safari matrices.
defects.mechanism: Domain contract stated in prose, enforced nowhere: `mixColors` models progress as a closed [0,1] interval while CSS easing output is unbounded by spec; the demo converts the library's Result rejection into a throw inside a computed that the template reads during render, so the whole GradientVisualizer subtree unmounts.
defects.reproduction: Fresh page -> http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> wait for settle -> click the tile `#easing-interval-0 [data-specimen="ease-in-back"]` (or ease-out-back, or ease-in-out-back). The Easing section and the rest of the pane vanish; document.querySelectorAll('.interval-head').length goes 1 -> 0. Script: scratchpad/probe14.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Not a Math.min at the crash site. Introduce ONE eased-progress boundary for the gradient tree — a single named `easedProgress(fn, t): number` that is the only place an easing OUTPUT becomes a mix PROGRESS, clamping to [0,1] there with the reason documented — and route useSpecimenRows, sampleCoalescedStops and GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition through it. This is fidelity, not a fudge: browsers clamp gradient colour interpolation identically. If the owner instead rules overshoot must be visible, the same boundary is where the extrapolation lives, and it is still one place.

defects.defect: `FAMILY_ORDER` silently deletes 6 of the library's 30 bezier presets from the specimen catalogue; those curves are unreachable from the selection strip AND, when chosen from the EasingPicker's own preset menu, are labelled `custom` — a false identity for a canonically named curve. The module header's claim of catalogue parity with the picker is false at HEAD.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:174 `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` and :191 `return FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. scratchpad/fam.mjs replaying the real PRESETS table (src/easing.ts:34-65): `families derived from presets: css, cubic, sine, quad, quart, quint, expo, circ, back, steps` / `DROPPED FAMILIES: quart, quint` / `tiles rendered: 27  bezier presets covered: 24 of 30`. Live DOM (Playwright MCP on /#/gradient): {"tileNodeCount":27,"hasQuart":false,"hasQuint":false}. probe2.mjs: `PRESET MENU OPTIONS: 30 [... "ease-in-quart","ease-out-quart","ease-in-out-quart","ease-in-quint","ease-out-quint","ease-in-out-quint" ...]`. probe3.mjs: `ease-out-quint => {"headName":"1 → 2custom","readout":"cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)","pressedTiles":[]}` and `ease-in-quart => {"headName":"1 → 2custom",...}`. False claim at easingCatalogue.ts:15-17.
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained allow-list used as a FILTER over a derived set: buildFamilies() derives ten families from the library, then discards any family the constant forgot, with no error and no test. Same mechanism class as C2-1 and C2-5 — an invariant that lives in a comment.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/fam.mjs (pure, no browser). Or live: /#/gradient -> open the row's tune stage -> open the `Easing preset` combobox -> select `ease-out-quint` -> the closed-row head reads `custom` and no tile is pressed, while the readout correctly shows cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). Script: scratchpad/probe3.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Delete FAMILY_ORDER as a filter; make it a sort RANK over the derived set so the catalogue is total by construction: `const rank = f => FAMILY_RANK.get(f) ?? FAMILY_RANK.size` then sort the derived keys — unknown families sort last, never vanish. The 'SPECIMEN_TILES covers every bezierPresets key' invariant then becomes structural and the unit test can assert it by enumeration instead of by `> 20`.

defects.defect: `useSpecimenRows` is one monolithic computed that couples the WCAG ink certification to the whole `modelState` object, so dragging the Gradient DIRECTION slider — which cannot change any curve, endpoint colour or ink — re-derives every row. At 20 stops it is 60.3% of all main-thread JS on the route, 44x the cost of the serialization the drag actually requires.
defects.evidence: CDP Profiler, 100us sampling, inclusive time, 60-move verified drag (direction 90 -> 270), scratchpad/probe13.mjs: 2 stops / 1 interval -> busy 504 ms, useSpecimenRows inclusive 67.3 ms (13.4%), certifyAccentInk 64.2 ms, useGradientCSS 11.3 ms. 20 stops / 19 intervals -> busy 1441 ms, useSpecimenRows inclusive 869.3 ms (60.3%), certifyAccentInk 810.5 ms, useGradientCSS 19.8 ms => 14.5 ms per direction tick (87% of a 16.7 ms frame). scratchpad/probe11.mjs at the live surface lightness (--ink-ambient-l = 0.79): msPerFullSpecimenRowsRecompute = 19.04 for 19 rows. scratchpad/bench.mjs, 2000 iterations each: glyphPath 0.0064 ms, interpolateStopColors 0.0062 ms, certifyAccentInk 1.6849 ms (99.2% of per-row cost). Code: useSpecimenRows.ts:42-73; useGradientModel.ts:102-109 (modelState returns a fresh object literal on any of type/direction/stops/intervals/space/hue); useContrastSafeColor.ts:356 (ambient dep) and :229-232 ('the AMBIENT is what moves per frame').
defects.mechanism: Over-broad dependency: the computed takes `modelState` wholesale but needs only interpolationSpace + hueMethod, and it recomputes cheap per-row identity (48-sample glyph paths, tile ids, labels) in the same body as the expensive ambient-dependent WCAG floor walk.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe13.mjs — paste a 20-stop gradient into the code editor, then pointer-drag [role="slider"][aria-label="Gradient direction"] 60 moves under CDP Profiler; read inclusive samples for `(anon) @ useSpecimenRows.ts:17` (8693 samples = 869.3 ms) vs total busy (1441 ms).
defects.proposedCure: Split the computed along its real seams rather than memoizing the symptom: (1) derive identity per row from (stops[i], stops[i+1], intervals[i]) so an untouched interval never rebuilds its glyph; (2) memoize the certified ink on (c0, c1, space, hue, ambient, dark); (3) stop passing modelState wholesale — take narrow getters `() => modelState.interpolationSpace` / `.hueMethod` so `type` and `direction` cease to be dependencies BY CONSTRUCTION, which is stronger than any cache.

defects.defect: Every interval eagerly mounts a full producer <EasingPicker> and a full 27-tile specimen strip, although at most one row's body can ever be shown and zero tune panels are disclosed.
defects.evidence: scratchpad/probe9.mjs on /#/gradient: 2 stops -> 511 pane elements / 1 easing-picker / 27 tiles / 6076 document nodes / 1241 JS listeners; 8 stops -> 1705 / 7 / 189 / 11468 / 2997; 20 stops -> 4093 / 19 / 513 / 21817 / 6389. scratchpad/probe8.mjs at 8 stops: openPanels = ["easing-interval-0:flex", 6x "none"], tunePanels = all "none" — i.e. 7 pickers mounted with no tune disclosed. ~199 elements per hidden row. Code: GradientEasingEditor.vue:143-147 (body is v-show) and :203-213 (authoring stage v-show=tuneOpen with an inner v-if gated on intervals[i], which is always true).
defects.mechanism: The docstring's state-continuity argument for v-show (GradientEasingEditor.vue:16-18) is sound for the OPEN row and false for the other N-1: their state is intervals[i], which lives in the model, not in the picker instance.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe9.mjs — paste 2-, 8- and 20-stop gradients into the code editor and count [data-testid="easing-picker"], [data-specimen] and document nodes after each.
defects.proposedCure: Render the disclosed body for the open row only (v-if="openInterval === row.index") and mount the authoring stage on FIRST disclosure (v-if="tuneOpen[row.index]"), keeping it alive thereafter. Closed rows keep their head — the specimen label, which is the entire closed-row design — at ~15 elements instead of ~199. Continuity is unaffected because the model already owns it.

defects.defect: Disclosure state is keyed by array index and never reconciled with the collection, producing two observable failures: a DEAD state (after the interval list shrinks below openInterval, no row is open at all, contradicting the component's own contract) and RESURRECTION (a stale tuneOpen key re-opens the authoring stage on a completely different interval when the list re-grows).
defects.evidence: scratchpad/probe8.mjs verbatim: after opening row 6 + its tune at 8 stops -> expandedHeads [false x6, true], tunePanels [... "easing-authoring-6:block"]. Shrunk to 3 stops -> rows 2, expandedHeads ["false","false"] (NO row open). Re-grown to 8 stops -> expandedHeads [false x6, "true"] and tunePanels [... "easing-authoring-6:block"] — state resurrected onto a different interval whose curve applyCSS had re-seeded to linear (gradientParse.ts:292-297). Code: GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 (openInterval seeded 0), :84-88 (tuneOpen only ever adds keys). Contract cited: GradientEasingEditor.vue:4-6 and e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:40-41 ('The bench mounts with row 0 open').
defects.mechanism: UI state keyed by positional index rather than by stable identity, with no clamp on shrink and no prune on removal; the object-spread in toggleTune guarantees monotonic key growth.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe8.mjs — at 8 stops click .interval-head[6] then its 'Author a custom curve' rail button; paste a 3-stop gradient (no row open, all aria-expanded false); paste an 8-stop gradient again (row 6 and its tune re-open). Realistic user path is the stop editor's Remove control, not a paste.
defects.proposedCure: Key both openInterval and tuneOpen by the stable left-anchor stop id (GradientStop.id already exists, useGradientModel.ts:34) instead of by index. A removed stop then takes its disclosure state with it: no clamp needed, no key can resurrect, and r1's C-4 positional re-hosting dissolves in the same move — one change, three defects.

defects.defect: The only unit gate covering this component asserts far less than its own title claims, so every mutation that actually shipped keeps it green; and the sole e2e that would catch the BLOCKER has no CI step at all.
defects.evidence: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:55-58 — `it("builds every easing specimen from valid Result values")` asserts only `expect(SPECIMEN_TILES.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)` plus a NaN check; actual length is 27. Verified green: `npx vitest run test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts` -> `✓ test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts (3 tests) 10ms`. CI: `ls .github/workflows/` -> ci.yml deploy-pages.yml release.yml; `grep -rn "playwright\|e2e" .github/workflows/` -> no matches. e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:117 and :189 both click [data-specimen='ease-out-back'], so o17 must be RED at HEAD and never runs.
defects.mechanism: An arithmetic proxy (`> 20`) standing in for a totality invariant (`every`), plus zero assertions over the portrait geometry and the per-specimen ink that are the component's entire thesis.
defects.reproduction: Green-keeping mutations, each verified against both gates by inspection: (1) delete "circ" and "expo" from FAMILY_ORDER (easingCatalogue.ts:174) -> 21 tiles > 20 passes; o17 touches only ease-out-back and step-end, both in kept families -> green. This is exactly the mutation that already shipped for quart/quint. (2) make glyphPath return a constant "M 0 0 L 1 1" -> NaN check passes, o17 never reads a `d` attribute -> green. (3) make useSpecimenRows' ink return null always -> no gate reads --motion-accent on a specimen row -> green.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the arithmetic with the invariants it was proxying, all three as UNIT tests so they run in the CI that exists today: (a) totality — the set of tile css literals equals the set of bezierPresets literals plus the steps literals; (b) round-trip identity — specimenNameFor(interval with tile.css) === tile.id for every tile, which kills the `custom` lie; (c) domain safety — serializeIntervalRamp must not throw for any catalogued curve, which fails on ease-in-back in milliseconds without a browser and would have stopped C2-1 shipping.

defects.defect: A failed clipboard copy is completely silent and a successful one is never announced: the seat passes no onCopyError and never reads the producer's "failure" status, and there is no aria-live region on the route.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:94-103 (`useClipboard({ resetMs: 1400 })`, no onCopyError; copiedRow at :96-98 maps anything not "success" to null) and :181 (the only success signal is the button's own accessible name flipping to 'Copied'). Producer implementation node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js sets status "failure" and invokes onCopyError on no-api / clipboard-api rejection.
defects.mechanism: Error path discarded at the consumer; the confirmation signal is a name change on the focused element, which AT does not reliably re-announce.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the failure branch specifically (it requires a denied clipboard permission or a non-secure context). The silent-discard code path itself is direct from source: the "failure" status has no reader anywhere in the component.
defects.proposedCure: This belongs to the design system, not the seat. glass-ui already owns the confirmation state machine; it should own the announcement — a role="status" node seated by the producer alongside the existing FeedbackMark — so all 88 demo components inherit one copy voice instead of 88 silent ticks.

defects.defect: The seat styles the producer component's private internals with :deep() and !important, reaching in through a data-testid (a test hook used as a style hook) — a per-instance override of a design-system component and a variant authored in demo/ rather than glass-ui.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:88-115 — `:deep([data-testid="easing-picker"]) { grid-template-columns: 1fr }`, `:deep(.glass-card) { background: var(--well-bg); box-shadow: none; backdrop-filter: none }`, `:deep(svg[role="img"]) { block-size: auto !important; aspect-ratio: calc(1 / var(--vb-ratio, 1.2)) !important }`. Violates standing edicts 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides). The file documents the debt at :14-27 and files it on the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet.
defects.mechanism: Consumer-side compensation for missing producer variants; the seat's own doc concedes the overrides 'retire at the adopt'.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — direct source read. Note r1 reports the svg[role="img"] selector is already dead against glass-ui 7.0.0 (the node is now role="group"), which would make the !important rules no-ops while still violating the edicts.
defects.proposedCure: Land the three laws as producer variants on <EasingPicker> (a `layout="single-column"` prop, a `surface="well"` variant reusing the existing surface vocabulary, and a viewBox-driven intrinsic aspect) so the seat consumes them by name and the entire :deep() block, including both !important declarations, is deleted rather than migrated.

defects.defect: Two uncancelled requestAnimationFrame callbacks are scheduled per authoring emission for one idempotent DOM read; nothing coalesces or cancels them.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-67 — `function onAuthored(v) { requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio); emit("authored", v); }` plus `watch(() => value.css, () => requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio), { flush: "post" })`. A bezier drag emits update:model-value per pointermove, and each emission both schedules an rAF directly and propagates to the parent (updateInterval -> new value.css) which schedules a second rAF for the identical read.
defects.mechanism: Unmanaged one-shot fan-out: no handle is retained, so a one-second drag queues ~120 querySelector + viewBox.baseVal reads and up to 120 writes to a reactive ref. Not the PRM-RAF loop epidemic — these are one-shots and the null guard at :50 makes post-unmount execution harmless.
defects.reproduction: NONE measured — this is a code-level defect confirmed by reading the two scheduling sites; the drag path was not instrumented per-frame.
defects.proposedCure: Retain one handle and cancel-then-schedule, and delete the onAuthored rAF entirely: the watch on value.css already covers every geometry change, since the file's own premise (:55-56) is that 'Every geometry change routes through an emission'.

defects.defect: `toggleTune` clones the entire record on every press and never prunes it — an unnecessary contrivance under Vue 3 deep reactivity, and the mechanical half of the C2-5 resurrection.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 — `const tuneOpen = ref<Record<number, boolean>>({})` with `tuneOpen.value = { ...tuneOpen.value, [index]: !tuneOpen.value[index] }`. `ref` on a plain object is already deeply reactive; `tuneOpen.value[index] = !tuneOpen.value[index]` suffices (edict 7 idiomatic Vue 3.5, edict 3 KISS).
defects.mechanism: Defensive immutability applied where the reactivity system does not need it, which also guarantees monotonic key growth.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — direct source read; the growth consequence is demonstrated by probe8.mjs (C2-5).
defects.proposedCure: Assign in place. Then re-key by stop id per C2-5, at which point the record prunes itself naturally as stops are removed.

defects.defect: Three of 27 shipped specimen tiles, and ordinary control-point dragging in the disclosed authoring stage, silently destroy the entire /gradient route (error boundary, bare "Try again", no message and no logged error). The catalogue is a mechanical enumeration of Object.keys(bezierPresets) with no domain filter, and the row's decorative ink is an unbounded fn(0.5) evaluation.
defects.evidence: src/color/operations.ts:90 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`; demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 `if (!mixed.ok) throw`; useGradientCSS.ts:199-207 `const easedT = easing(t) … if (!mixed.ok) throw`; easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 calls it inside a computed with fn(0.5); easingCatalogue.ts:178 enumerates every preset. Measured midpoints (independent node bezier solve): ease-in-back fn(0.5)=-0.063622, ease-out-back fn(0.5)=1.067553, ease-in-out-back fn(0.5)=0.606680. Fresh-page WebKit trials, before.rows=1 each: ease-out-back/pointer -> rows=0 tryAgain=true pageErrors=0 consoleErrors=0; ease-in-back/KEYBOARD (focus+Enter) -> rows=0 tryAgain=true; ease-in-out-back/pointer -> rows=0 tryAgain=true; steps/pointer (control) -> rows=1 tryAgain=false. Drag trial: handle moved 30px above the plot box -> {"rows":0,"tryAgain":true,"literal":null}, pageErrors:[]. Producer sr-only text read live: "Up and Down change y from -0.6 to 1.6". Screenshot DE-crash-ease-in-back.png shows both plates gone.
defects.mechanism: Domain/range mismatch at a composition seam: an unbounded easing RANGE is piped into a [0,1]-bounded colour-progress DOMAIN at two call sites, with the failure surfaced as a throw inside a Vue computed, swallowed by a route error boundary.
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (first Easing row is open by default) -> scroll the specimen strip to the "back" family -> press ease-in-back, ease-out-back or ease-in-out-back by click OR by Tab+Enter. Alternative: press the sliders glyph in the readout rail to disclose the authoring stage, then drag the upper control handle above the plot box.
defects.proposedCure: Declare the bounded progress domain ONCE at sampleCoalescedStops — already named "the ONE sampling law" (useGradientCSS.ts:3) — and map curve range into it there (clamp, or a named overshoot-to-endpoint reflection). useSpecimenRows consumes the same mapped value instead of raw fn(0.5). No try/catch at the seat; no quiet deletion of the back family from the catalogue.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 "Gradient cannot stand in for Easing". research/proportion-register.md:32 PR-09 "Gradient preview and embedded Easing selector are presently subordinate/tiny" verb ENLARGE owner W27. Measured: demo/color-picker/router/index.ts has no /easing (falls to :37 catch-all redirect "/"); the curve is DRAWN at 166.7px = 10.42rem, 45% below the 19rem floor, behind two disclosures; row card computed border-radius 16px = --radius-card; boundary count in one open row = 1 card + 1 ramp + 7 family hairlines + 1 rail well + 1 authoring well + 1 producer .glass-card.
defects.mechanism: A whole instrument compressed into the wrong housing: a 19-22rem P122 golden composition folded into a 462x39px accordion head inside another route's inspector column.

defects.proposedCure: Execute PR-09: lift the instrument to its own /easing route + InstrumentChassis with the curve/time stage as the 19-22rem centred protagonist and the catalogue as the 38.2% inspector. What remains in /gradient is one identity+selection line per interval (name, portrait, literal) linking out. defects.defect: "Law 3 — zero letterbox" is dead CSS: it targets svg[role="img"] but glass-ui 7.0.0 renders the plot as role="group". All three :deep declarations, the rAF sync, the onMounted call and the watch are inert; --vb-ratio is frozen at its seed; the canvas ships the exact 2.05:1 letterbox the law was written to kill.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:19-24 declares the law; :48-50 querySelector("svg[role='img']"); :104-115 the :deep(svg[role="img"]) block. If the rules applied: aspect calc(1/1.2)=0.833, block-size auto, inline-size min(100%,19rem)=304px, transition naming aspect-ratio — none true. defects.mechanism: A consumer re-deriving a producer's intrinsic ratio through a DOM-attribute read plus rAF, keyed on a role selector that drifted at the glass-ui 7 adoption; the failure is invisible because the ref seed (1.2) happens to equal the linear viewBox ratio.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient, press the sliders glyph in the readout rail, then read getComputedStyle on `.easing-authoring svg` — role is "group", inline-size 410px, block-size 200px, aspect-ratio "1 / 1", transition "all".
defects.proposedCure: Delete the whole --vb-ratio apparatus. The plot's aspect is a producer fact: put it on the EasingPicker root (producer-owned custom property, or intrinsic aspect-ratio on the svg) via the existing P7 packet. Until then size by inline-size alone and let the svg's own ratio govern.

defects.defect: The tiles request shape="cell" and render as circles, because glass-capsule (radius 9999px) is in the producer's BASE class string and cell does not override it — so the 9px labels overhang the disc by 6.56px. The seat then per-instance-overrides every geometric property of the recipe it just asked for.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js: base = "glass-chip glass-capsule accent-tone inline-flex …", cell = "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro". Measured tile: border-radius 9999px, 45.23 x 43.80. Overhang geometry: label width 33.23px; label band at |dy|=17.90 from centre; capsule silhouette there = 26.67px; OVERHANG = 6.56px (3.28px per side). Overrides measured: display inline-flex->flex, gap 6px->2px, padding 8/10px->5/6/4px, label 11px(text-micro)->9px. Visible on `linear`, `in-out`, `smooth` in every capture.
defects.mechanism: Producer boundary crossed at the seat: a root-level recipe consumed and then nullified property-by-property per instance, on top of a producer variant whose radius token is unreachable.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient and read getComputedStyle on any .specimen-tile: border-radius 9999px on a 45.23x43.80 box; compare the .tile-label rect (33.23px) against the capsule chord at the label's own vertical band (26.67px).
defects.proposedCure: glass-chip--cell must own its own corner radius rather than inheriting glass-capsule — relay to glass-ui on the standing BH/BI inbox. At the seat, delete the .specimen-tile geometry block entirely and consume the producer cell rhythm; if that scale is wrong for a specimen, request a producer size rung.

defects.defect: Two off-ladder type sizes (9px, hardcoded), and three different semantic roles — interval identity, specimen name, exported value — rendered byte-identically in size, family, colour and weight 40px apart.

defects.defect: RTL breaks twice: the interval identity renders `2 → 1` when the model says `1 → 2` (bidi reorder of a domain coordinate), and every family divider lands on the wrong edge because the rule uses physical border-left/padding-left — no rule at the css|sine boundary, a stray rule at the strip's outer left.
defects.evidence: (a) useSpecimenRows.ts:63 `label: `${i + 1} → ${i + 2}``; measured logical headLabelText="1 → 2", rendered "2 → 1" in rtl-desktop/gradient.png and my clip DE-rtl-easing.png. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2: "CSS direction keywords, physical axes, code, hex, slug, ID | preserve the declared physical/domain meaning … inside an LTR-isolated value". (b) EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:143-146 `border-left: 1px solid var(--card-edge); padding-left: 0.875rem`. Measured RTL rects, DOM order: css [962.5→1201.0] border-left 0px; sine [792.3→948.5] border-left 1px pad-left 14px; quad [622.1→778.3] 1px/14px; … steps [-277.1→-122.1] 1px/14px and leftmost with nothing beyond it. css renders to the RIGHT of sine, so sine's left rule separates it from quad, not from its predecessor.
defects.mechanism: Physical-property and bidi assumptions: an LTR writing direction baked into a separator rule and into a coordinate rendered as a bidi-sensitive string.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient, run `document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl")`, wait ~1s. Read the head's first span (renders 2 → 1) and getComputedStyle borderLeftWidth/borderRightWidth on each .strip-family (borderLeft 1px, borderRight 0px, on the inline-END side).
defects.proposedCure: border-inline-start / padding-inline-start for the family rule; give the interval ordinal the LTR isolation the constitution already prescribes for code/hex/slug values — or stop rendering an ordinal pair as a bidi-sensitive string at all.

defects.defect: A 27-item single-select gallery injects 27 tab stops (28 with its focusable port) into a 52-stop route while hiding 70.6% of itself on desktop and 79.9% on mobile — and the only affordance that made it navigable, the family filter, was deleted and replaced with an aria-hidden decorative eyebrow.

defects.defect: Two focus registers inside one component, and an unnamed focusable region in the middle of its tab run: the buttons take the house --focus-ring-shadow while the FadingScroll port (tabIndex 0, no role, no accessible name) takes the UA default outline.

defects.defect: The "one literal" export mints long-form beziers for the five CSS keyword easings, so the row names `linear` 40px above a rail that refuses to write `linear`.
