defects.defect: The disclosure teleports and pays its full mount cost anyway: both v-show panels have no transition while the chevron animates, and every interval's complete EasingPicker is mounted on first paint and stays mounted when the row collapses.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:144 and :204 are v-show with no transition; :138 the chevron carries `transition-transform`. Measured on first paint, no interaction: authoringStage mounted = 1, authoringVisible = 0. After collapsing the row: {openRows: 0, mountedPickers: 1, visibleStages: 0}. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 "Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register." The header comment defends the always-alive picker at :16-18, but EasingAuthoringStage is fully controlled (takes :value, emits) and holds no state.
defects.mechanism: Instrument compressed into the wrong housing: a disclosure invented to fit the accordion, which neither animates nor defers.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient without interacting and count document.querySelectorAll('.easing-authoring') = 1 with zero visible; toggle the accordion head and observe the panel appear/disappear with no transition while the chevron rotates.
defects.proposedCure: Either the disclosure is real — v-if plus one named motion family from demo/styles/animations.css — or it is not a disclosure and the editor is always visible, which is what D2-02's /easing chassis wants.

defects.defect: "One ink per specimen" is false by construction: fn(0.5) collides across every symmetric curve and returns a pure endpoint colour for the single-step curves, so the row's identity ink duplicates the endpoint dot 30px to its left.
defects.evidence: useSpecimenRows.ts:1-9 claims "one ink per specimen". Measured: linear, ease-in-out, ease-in-out-expo, smooth-step-3 and steps(4, jump-end) all yield oklch(0.438102 0.074812 205) — five of the 24 reachable specimens share one ink. step-start -> oklch(0.456744 0.18 265), hue 265 = stop 2 whose dot is oklch(0.65 0.18 265); step-end -> oklch(0.432757 0.136109 145), hue 145 = stop 1 whose dot is oklch(0.75 0.15 145).
defects.mechanism: A derivation that does not derive: a single sample of a curve is not an identity of that curve.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient and press linear, ease-in-out, smooth-step-3, steps, step-start, step-end in turn, reading getComputedStyle('.head-glyph path').stroke and the two .specimen-dot --dot-c values after each press.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the ink from something that actually distinguishes curves (e.g. the signed area between the curve and the diagonal), or drop the per-row ink and let the shared accent carry it — and in either case not from an unbounded evaluation (D2-01).

result.axis: design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law) — CHALLENGE-D, pass 2 (consolidated with pass 1)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the component's primary affordance does not exist. The "Add current color" control (the only add path in Colors mode, the default mode) renders as a `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events: none`, `tabIndex -1`, no `aria-label`, no `disabled`, no click listener and no `+` glyph. glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot is prop-closed and slot-closed (`inheritAttrs:false`, only class+style forwarded, root always `<span aria-hidden pointer-events:none>`), so `tag="button"`, `@click`, `:disabled`, `:aria-label`, `:title` and the `<Plus>` slot child are all silently discarded. Proven three ways on the running app: complete attribute list, `elementFromPoint` at the ghost centre returning the container div, and a synthetic bubbling click dispatched directly on the element leaving `[data-mix-source]` at 0. `focusablesInWell: []`. The same mechanism kills all 35 palette swatches in the live "From palettes" disclosure. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91` named this producer change AND this exact site ("...Generate, Mix and Gradient sites") as scheduled migration work; the producer shipped, the consumer never moved.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundness, for completeness: the SegmentedTabs component choice is canon-sanctioned at this site per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89; canvas-resolved contrast passes at 5.08/6.29/5.71:1; `overflowX = 0` at 1440/720/390/320 matching REPORT.json; zero console/page errors on /#/mix in all four Safari matrix rows; palette identity correctly keys on `slug` per K-PALID; the palettes-mode EmptyState is genuinely well-designed and is the standard the colors branch fails.)

defects.defect: Every interactive WatercolorDot in the component is inert decoration. Colors mode — the default mode — cannot accept a single color by pointer, keyboard or AT.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:148,150,164-176,211-221 pass a glass-ui 6.x API. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js: `inheritAttrs: !1`; `let n = h(), c = i(() => n.class), f = i(() => n.style)` (class+style ONLY); render is `o("span", { "aria-hidden": "true", …, style: u([f.value, { …, pointerEvents: "none", … }]) }, [ …svg…, ghost-stroke ])` with NO `<slot/>`. WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} — no `tag`. LIVE (Playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/mix): {"tagName":"SPAN","attrs":["data-v-292b9032=","data-v-a3e86846=","aria-hidden=true","class=add-slot-ghost …","data-testid=watercolor-swatch","data-variant=ghost","style=…pointer-events: none;…"],"pointerEvents":"none","tabIndex":-1,"hasSvgPlus":false,"childCount":2} — the attrs list is complete: no aria-label, no disabled, no title, no onclick. Hit test: {"elementFromPointAtGhostCenter":"DIV.swatch-row flex items-center gap-2.5 flex-wrap"}. Listener probe: {"beforeSources":0,"afterSources":0} after ghost.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click',{bubbles:true})). {"focusablesInWell":[]}. Visible in all four Safari captures: no `+` glyph in the ghost.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui 7.0.0 major adoption (W44) migrated the package but not the call sites; `inheritAttrs:false` swallows unknown attrs and Vue emits no warning, so a removed public API fails silently. Family: `grep -rn 'tag="button"' demo` → 4 live sites; `tag="div"` → 14 more.
defects.reproduction: npm run dev; open http://localhost:9000/#/mix; click the dashed circle in the "Selected" well — nothing happens; Tab through the pane — the well is skipped entirely. Programmatic: document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost').dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click',{bubbles:true})); document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-source]').length stays 0.
defects.proposedCure: The dot is a FACE, never a SEAT — which is exactly what glass-ui 7 encodes by making it an aria-hidden span, and exactly what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91 specifies ('Selection, activation, drag and keyboard focus belong to a named enclosing geometric button/seat'). Transpose: one shared `WatercolorSwatchButton` seat authored IN glass-ui (owner edict 4) that contains a `<WatercolorDot>` face plus the glyph as siblings, with name, :disabled, focus ring and press choreography on the seat. Gradient stops and Generate specimens consume the same seat. Discharges D-1, D-15(naming) and D-21.

defects.defect: The "From palettes" disclosure is unbounded and, at real library size, pushes COLOR SPACE / HUE METHOD / the Mix button — the instrument's primary commit action — entirely below the fold.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:195 — CollapsibleContent carries only `overflow-hidden` (for the height keyframe); no max-height, no scroll container, no virtualisation. Live capture .playwright-mcp/mix-expanded.png at 1440x900 with the real 5-palette store, disclosure open: the palette list runs past the pane bottom and the entire config+commit region is off-screen. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:34 (§3.8) 'One pane may have one full-strength visual protagonist. Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow.' The canon prescribes the shape at :214 — 'advanced grouped disclosure … and a scroll-confined inspector.'
defects.mechanism: Unbounded content region inside a scrolling pane; a supporting affordance for CHOOSING operands evicts the protagonist that CONSUMES them. Invisible to the prior audit pass because its 2-palette fixture produced only a 265.875px content height.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix with >=4 saved palettes in localStorage; click the 'From palettes' trigger; the Mix button leaves the viewport.
defects.proposedCure: max-block-size on the disclosure content at a rung tied to the pane's own rhythm, with overflow-y:auto inside it, so the commit region never moves. The mode control leaves the scroll box entirely — it is chassis, not content (the pane-scroll-fade currently washes it out when scrolled).

defects.defect: The zero-operand "Selected" rack is a bordered, tone-stepped, shadowed fixture at ~4.7% ink occupancy — filler at exactly the state the canon forbids filler — while the sibling Palettes branch ships a designed EmptyState forty lines away.
defects.evidence: LIVE measured: well {"w":462,"h":106.5,"area":49203}, dots {"dotCount":1,"dotArea":2304} → 4.68% occupancy; pass 1 independently measured 4.36% (1440), 4.73% (720), 5.94% (390), 7.58% (320). wellEdge {"border":"1.5px dashed oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12)","background":"oklab(0.913295 …)"} + box-shadow var(--shadow-cartoon-sm) per demo/styles/utils.css:90-107. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202 'No shadow palette filler appears when an operand is absent'; :48 'absent operands occupy no filler'; :28 'Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (<=15% of the stage) or disappears'. Contrast with MixSourceSelector.vue:231-244, a 22-line comment defending the refusal of ghost filler in the OTHER branch.
defects.mechanism: The colors-mode empty state was never designed — the fixture is authored for the populated case and left dressed at zero. Compounded by a dashed-inside-dashed register collision: the well's 12%-alpha neutral dashed edge 40px from the ghost's full-chroma dashed edge (measured ghostStroke.borderColor oklch(0.7 0.15 30)).
defects.reproduction: Clear localStorage; open http://localhost:9000/#/mix — boot state. Measure document.querySelector('.dashed-well').getBoundingClientRect().
defects.proposedCure: At zero operands the rack collapses to the invitation itself — the named add seat (D-1) plus one line of copy, content-hugging, no border, no tone step, no shadow — in the same EmptyState register the Palettes branch already uses. The well earns its boundary at >=1 operand, when there is a set to bound. One empty grammar per component, not two.

defects.defect: The palettes-mode tile wraps PaletteCard in an outer <button>, inverting the canon's card/seat law and shipping a <button> inside a <button>.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 wraps <PaletteCard> in <button type="button" :aria-pressed>. PaletteCard.vue:5-26 root is <div role="article" … cursor-pointer @click="$emit('click')"> and PaletteCard.vue:80-106 unconditionally renders <Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label="Palette menu"> (demo/ui/button → native <button>). Measured nesting: {"wrappers":[{"aria":"Select palette Sunset Drift","pressed":"false","nestedInteractive":["BUTTON:Palette menu"]}]}. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:77 (§5.12) is the exact inverse: 'The Card/article root is a noninteractive container: it owns no activation, focus or selection state … Its one native named <button type="button" aria-pressed> CHILD spans specimen/identity and alone owns activation, visible selection and focus.' VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 forbids the 'seven-mode omnibus' this tile imports wholesale.
defects.mechanism: Selection was bolted on by the consumer as a wrapper rather than bound to the card's own pressed seat. Second order: PaletteCard's cartoon-surface press choreography and the wrapper's opacity-75→100 transition-all run simultaneously — two hover registers, two press registers, one object (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 PR-06 names 'duplicated selected fills' and names Mix tabs).
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix → Palettes tab with >=1 saved palette; inspect the tile: button > div[role=article] > button[aria-label="Palette menu"].
defects.proposedCure: Mix does not wrap PaletteCard. It consumes the same card with PaletteCard's OWN pressed seat bound to mix selection — one seat, aria-pressed, inside, spanning specimen/identity only, per §5.12. If the omnibus affordances must not appear in Mix, that is a PaletteCard composition prop decided in the card, not a wrapper bolted on by a consumer.

defects.defect: The Colors/Palettes mode control has no accessible name and takes toggle semantics though it owns a panel. To AT, Colors mode is an empty region.
defects.evidence: LIVE: {"tabs":{"role":"group","ariaLabel":null,"html":"<div role=\"group\" class=\"segmented-tabs segmented-tabs--pill …\">"}}. SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts exposes `ariaLabel` ('Accessible name shared by the desktop strip and responsive Select') — not passed; and `semantics` ('When omitted, preserves the historical mapping: pill → toggle') plus per-option `controls` ('completing the APG tablist↔tabpanel linkage for consumers that own a panel'). MixSourceSelector.vue:114/230 v-if/v-else swaps the whole body — it owns a panel. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 (§4.1): 'Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.' Related: the 'Selected' label (:119) is a bare <span> with no aria-labelledby to the row it names, and every occupant of that row is an aria-hidden producer span (D-1).
defects.mechanism: Producer options left at defaults; the consumer configured the material (variant="pill") and nothing else. This OVERTURNS the prior pass's negative-proof claim that the tabs are clean — the component CHOICE is canon (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89 names 'Mix Colors/Palettes source-mode tabs' as a surviving P092 site), the CONFIGURATION is not.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix; document.querySelector('.segmented-tabs').getAttribute('aria-label') → null; .getAttribute('role') → 'group'.
defects.proposedCure: Pass ariaLabel, semantics="tabs" and per-option `controls` pointing at the panel ids; give the swatch row list semantics and tie 'Selected' to it with aria-labelledby. All producer-supplied — no local ARIA hand-rolling.

defects.defect: The 20-line "stable keys" apparatus mints index-derived keys, so the TransitionGroup move transition it exists to enable can never fire, and the convergence animation's source positions remount mid-flight.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:79-89 — `const mapKey = `${sc.css}::${i}`` puts the index inside the identity; :90-98 a watch prunes the map, guaranteeing keys are never reused. Replay: initial [0,1,2] → after rm0 [3,4] (every survivor got a NEW key) → re-add [0,1,2] → duplicates [0,5]. Removing 1 of 3 plays 3 leaves + 2 enters instead of 1 leave + a move; .vj-enter-move (demo/styles/animations.css:99) cannot fire. :125-126 documents that data-mix-source/-color let 'the convergence animation lift a pigment drop from each chip's real position (W3-6)'. Repro script: swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs in the report directory.
defects.mechanism: Identity was synthesised at the render layer from (value, position) instead of minted at the source. SelectedColor is {css, source} with no id. Owner edict 3 (KISS/no contrivance): a Map + counter + watcher deliver exactly `:key="i"` while APPEARING to deliver stability.
defects.reproduction: Blocked live by D-1 (the populated state is unreachable); the algorithm replay is exact and scripted at swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Mint identity at the source: useMixingState.addColor returns {id, css, source}. The key becomes sc.id and the Map, counter and watcher all delete (~20 lines). The same id is the prerequisite for D-19's reorder.

defects.defect: The disclosure overrides its producer recipe per instance with a fourth animation family name that animates `height` — forcing layout every frame on the component's largest, unbounded subtree.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/disclosure.css already owns .disclosure-content (overflow:hidden; animation-duration:var(--spring-smooth-duration); animation-timing-function:var(--spring-smooth); named disclosure-open/close; PRM + forced-colors arms) and .disclosure-group-trigger{min-block-size:2.75rem}. MixSourceSelector.vue:195 overrides with `overflow-hidden data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down data-[state=closed]:animate-collapsible-up`. Measured: {"animationName":"collapsible-down","animationDuration":"0.2s","animationTiming":"ease-out"} — the house spring replaced by generic ease-out. tw-animate-css/dist/tw-animate.css: `@keyframes collapsible-down { from { height: 0 } to { height: var(--reka-collapsible-content-height, auto) } }`. demo/styles/animations.css:60 states the law: 'three named families; a fourth name is a defect (gate (a), R.W4 §Hard gate)' — and vj-morph is documented in that same block as owning 'optional height morph via --vj-morph-collapse/-expanded'. `grep -rn "collapsible-down" demo/ src/` → exactly one hit, this line. Chevron at :190-193 duplicates .disclosure-icon and the producer's [data-state=open] rotation, driven off a LOCAL ref — two sources of truth for 'open'.
defects.mechanism: A vendor keyframe utility reached past the design system's own disclosure recipe; owner edict 5 (root-level styling) and edict 6 (tokenized motion) both breached at one call site.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix; open 'From palettes'; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.disclosure-content')).animationName → 'collapsible-down'.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the three override classes and the hand-rolled chevron rotation; consume the producer .disclosure-content recipe and its data-state icon rule. If a height morph is genuinely wanted, it is vj-morph with --vj-morph-collapse/-expanded — the house family that already owns it.

defects.defect: The operand-count guard is off by one against both the state machine and the canon, producing a terminal dead-end state at exactly one operand.
defects.evidence: Three authorities disagree: MixSourceSelector.vue:37,39 `MIN_COLORS = 1`, `canRemoveColor = selectedColors.length > MIN_COLORS` → floor 1. useMixingState.ts:51 `canMix = selectedColors.value.length >= 2` → floor 2. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202 'An ordered N-operand rack (2–12 colors, or two or more potentially unequal palettes)' → floor 2. At exactly one colour: the × is disabled, canMix is false, the Mix button is dead, and the add slot is inert (D-1) — the only exit is the dock overflow menu (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:220). The comment at :36 ('remove needs >= 1 remaining') states the intent precisely; the intent is one below the real invariant.
defects.mechanism: The count invariant is authored twice, in two files, with two different values — the selector re-derives a floor the state machine already owns.
defects.reproduction: Blocked live by D-1 (cannot add a colour). Source-provable: the guard blocks length→0 and permits length==1, where canMix is false.
defects.proposedCure: Delete MIN_COLORS/MAX_COLORS from the component. Expose canAdd/canRemove from useMixingState beside the canMix it already owns, at the canon's 2–12 bounds. One authority for the operand-count invariant.

defects.defect: The canon's "ordered N-operand rack" ships with no reorder affordance at all — no grab, no drag, no arrow reorder, no ordinal announcement.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202 'An ORDERED N-operand rack … Source mode, add/remove/REORDER, method, unequal-palette strategy, provenance and commit share the same control grammar.' VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:131 (§5.2) specifies the exact contract: 'horizontal explicit reorder: palette colors, OPERANDS, stops — after Space grabs, Right moves one visual position right; Left one visual position left … every move announces item and `position of total`; Space drops, Escape cancels.' MixSourceSelector.vue implements none of it. The rack IS ordered in the state machine (selectedColors is an array; mixColorSequence consumes it in order) and unordered in the interface.
defects.mechanism: Never built. This supersedes the prior pass's 'dragging | n/a | no reorder here' — reorder is not absent-by-design; the canon names operands explicitly, twice.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis-free absence, proven by grep over the component (no draggable, no keydown, no reorder handler) against two quoted canon clauses.
defects.proposedCure: Build reorder on D-11's stable operand id, using the §5.2 grab/move/drop/cancel contract, so pointer drag, arrow movement and any numeric entry resolve to the same ordinal. Same control grammar as add/remove, per :202.

defects.defect: Two peer section headings in two different type registers 60px apart, one of which is outside the closed type matrix entirely (Fraunces, semibold, at control size).
defects.evidence: Measured: `Selected` (:119) = Fraunces, 16.4px, weight 600, sentence case, hand-rolled `text-small font-display font-semibold`; `From palettes` (:183) = Fira Code, 14.38px, weight 400, UPPERCASE, tracking 1.44px, via glass-ui `.section-label`. Live confirmation: {"sectionLabels":["From palettes","Color space","Hue method"]} — 'Selected' is the one peer heading absent from that list. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:66-78 (§4) declares the role matrix 'closed across all eighteen compositions': control/label → text-small → Plus Jakarta Sans, NON-BOLD; section heading → text-heading → Plus Jakarta Sans; palette identity → --type-subheading. The palette name at :205 repeats the error (text-small font-display font-semibold where --type-subheading is required). The two counts use two families for one role: :184 sans text-micro, :206 fira-code text-micro; text-micro is not a matrix rung in either family.
defects.mechanism: Marks authored ad hoc per site instead of read off the closed matrix; the .section-label primitive exists and is consumed by three of the four peer labels.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix; getComputedStyle on the two labels returns the families/weights above; visible without measurement in safari-desktop-light/mix.png (serif title-case 'Selected' directly above uppercase letterspaced 'COLOR SPACE').
defects.proposedCure: Re-read every mark from §4: .section-label for Selected, --type-subheading for palette identity, Fira Code text-mono-small/mono-caption for both counts. No local type recipes in a workbench.

defects.defect: The component states a register law for rings and de-emphasis in its own comments and violates both, 60 and 70 lines later.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:134-145 excises `ring-2 ring-primary/50` and declares 'rings on WatercolorDots ride the dot's own silhouette … or do not exist — the dead utility is excised, never re-minted geometric'; :256-261 mints exactly that on the palettes seat (`ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background`). :186-189 kills a /50 post-hoc alpha because 'the token IS the de-emphasis rung; attenuating it further is the guard-then-alpha class'; :260 de-emphasises unselected cards with `opacity-75` (measured opacity: 0.75). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 (PR-06) names the family and the route: 'Three adjacent action species or duplicated selected fills → REMOVE … One action/selection owner across Generate and owner/Admin/Mix tabs.'
defects.mechanism: Two authors' laws in one file with no enforcement surface; comments are not gates.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix → Palettes tab; getComputedStyle on an unselected tile → opacity 0.75; on a selected tile → the ring box-shadow pair.
defects.proposedCure: One selection register for the whole component, expressed on the entity the producer owns (PaletteCard's pressed seat, per §5.12), never an outer ring; de-emphasis by token rung, never post-hoc alpha.

defects.defect: The selection ring offsets against --background rather than the plate the card sits on, and shares its Tailwind ring channel with focus-visible so a focused selected card loses its selection colour.
defects.evidence: Measured: light `box-shadow: … rgb(251,250,248) 0 0 0 2px, oklch(0.470927 0.093396 169.83403) 0 0 0 4px`; dark `--tw-ring-offset-color: hsl(24 9% 4%)` — i.e. --background, never the tier="resting" plate (MixPane.vue:61). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 (§4.1): 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast ON THE ACTUAL MATERIAL TIER; a token name is not evidence.' Selection is `ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2`, focus is `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40` — same --tw-ring-* channel, and .focus-visible\:ring-2:focus-visible (0,2,0) outranks .ring-2 (0,1,0). §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.mechanism: A per-instance utility ring assumes the page ground; Tailwind v4 collapses selection and focus into one custom-property channel so the later/more-specific rule wins outright rather than composing.
defects.reproduction: Offset ground: CONFIRMED by the pasted computed values. Focus/selection collision: HYPOTHESIS — keyboard focus could not be landed on the seat to photograph (WebKit/macOS omits buttons from Tab order by default; the Chromium arm lacked the seeded library). Mechanism is deterministic CSS; the render is unphotographed.
defects.proposedCure: Selection moves onto PaletteCard's own pressed seat (D-5) with a producer-owned selected register that does not consume the ring channel, leaving focus-visible sole owner of the ring. Any offset reads the actual host tier token, never --background.

defects.defect: The colors-mode empty state was never designed, while the palettes-mode empty state 40 lines away is fully designed and defended in a 22-line comment.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:239-244 ships EmptyState with eyebrow '· nothing to mix ·', message and hint, preceded by :231-238 arguing 'TRUE EMPTY speaks the EmptyState invitation ALONE … never ghost cards before the caption'. Colors mode (:116-178), the DEFAULT mode, ships a 462x108 well with one inert dot, no eyebrow, no message, no hint and nothing pressable. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 (§5.6): 'Add affordance when the surviving action/state is otherwise undiscoverable. Subtraction precedes explanation.'
defects.mechanism: Two empty grammars in one component; the branch the user meets first is the undesigned one.
defects.reproduction: Clear localStorage; open http://localhost:9000/#/mix — the default Colors tab shows a labelled void; click Palettes — a composed invitation.
defects.proposedCure: One empty grammar per component: the colors rack collapses to the same EmptyState register plus the named add seat, content-hugging.

defects.defect: The only per-chip remove control is hover-only, nameless and 16x16, and the only clear-all action lives in the dock's overflow menu.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:152-158: `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, `w-4 h-4`, icon-only <X>, no aria-label — this is the `1` in REPORT.md:99 `namelessButtons … safari-desktop-light /#/mix: 1`. On touch there is no hover; the only other reveal is focus-visible, which requires a keyboard. Clear-all: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:220 `{ key: "clear", icon: Trash2, title: "Clear", handler: () => paneRefs.mix.value?.clearSelection?.() }`. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 (PR-07): 'Hover-only/unlabeled controls and invisible drag state → ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE … every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state.' §5.7: 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities.'
defects.mechanism: Progressive disclosure by hover on a surface that is majority-touch; the compensating action was relocated off-component instead of the affordance being fixed.
defects.reproduction: Confirmed in source and in every mobile capture (no × visible). Render of the populated hover state blocked by D-1.
defects.proposedCure: The remove control becomes a persistently-visible named seat at the touch floor, on the same SwatchSeat as D-1's cure; clear-all returns to the rack as a named action beside it.

defects.defect: The disclosure trigger is a 29.6px tap target while the producer's own trigger recipe carries a 44px floor that goes unused.
defects.evidence: Measured 462 x 29.6 desktop, 324 x 26.3 mobile; min-block-size: 0px; padding: 4px 0px — MixSourceSelector.vue:182 `py-1` is the whole vertical measure. glass-ui _shared/disclosure.css: `.disclosure-group-trigger { min-block-size: 2.75rem; }`. result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: N-1 — the dead `layout="split"` arm has already killed a FOREIGN feature's public API. Commit 95993197 (2026-07-10) deleted ImagePaletteExtractor.vue, the only `layout="split"` consumer, and its own commit body records that it verified its own deletions were grep-zero but did not re-derive reachability of the surviving producer's conditional arms. ExtractWorkbench.vue:148 (`:layout="layout === 'split' && isWide ? 'aside' : 'default'"`) is the ONLY `layout` binding to PaletteCard anywhere in the demo, so with `split` unreachable it is a constant — making PaletteCard's entire `aside` implementation (PaletteCard.vue:20,35,36,39,40,192-193) dead public API on the `palettes/browser/card` barrel seam, kept nominally alive by a dead branch in a different feature. Confirmed live: `.rounded-l-card` = 0 and `.sm\:grid-cols-2` = 0 on /#/extract, /#/mix and /#/. This is dead code that MIGRATED across a feature boundary and became dead API — strictly worse than accumulation, because it is now surface a future consumer could reasonably build on. It is also the direct proof of why the unenforced boundary law (N-6) matters.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable — verdict is DEFECTIVE. One sub-area is genuinely SOUND and is stated in the report (§4): the component's consumption of the published library surface. Every value.js reach in demo/workbenches/extract/** goes through a real `package.json#exports` key — ExtractWorkbench.vue:189 (/color), useExtractSession.ts:14,15 (/quantize, /css), useImageQuantize.ts:9 (/quantize), quantize-worker.ts:6,7 (/quantize), useImageSampler.ts:12,13 (/color, /css). Zero `@src/*`, zero `../../src/*`, zero `dist/*` reaches in the subtree. A real consumer could write every one of those lines verbatim, so the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds here. The rot is in the resolution machinery AROUND the surface (tsconfig paths drift, the stale self-install), not the specifiers.

defects.defect: The camera MediaStream outlives the view: `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` never fires because the shell caches the pane under <KeepAlive>, which deactivates rather than unmounts. The quantize Worker terminate and the 300ms debounce clear bind to the same dead hook.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:281 onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera) · demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 `<KeepAlive :max="max">` · demo/color-picker/App.vue:107 `:max="6"` for exactly the 6 non-admin left panes · `grep -rn "onActivated|onDeactivated" demo/` => 2 hits, BOTH in demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue (onDeactivated appears ZERO times in the entire demo) · same dead hook at useImageQuantize.ts:148-151 (worker.terminate) and useExtractSession.ts:194-196 (clearTimeout)
defects.mechanism: Resource-lifetime ownership split across an uncontracted seam: the caching policy is owned by the shell (PaneSlot), the device-resource lifetime by a leaf SFC three layers down, with no contract between them. The leaf assumes mount/unmount semantics the shell does not provide.
defects.reproduction: Pass 1 confirmed this live with Playwright, substituting canvas.captureStream() for getUserMedia: open camera at #/extract -> tracks ["live"]; location.hash='#/palettes', wait 2000ms -> extractStillInDom false but tracksAfterViewSwitch ["live"]; back to #/extract -> viewfinderStillOpen true, tracks ["live"]. I re-verified the mechanism statically this pass (greps above). Attribution: found by pass 1 (challenge-L-library.pass1-2026-07-27.md L-1), re-verified here.
defects.proposedCure: Do not sprinkle onDeactivated at three sites. Introduce ONE lifecycle primitive expressing the shell's real contract — `demo/shell/usePaneLifecycle.ts` exporting `onPaneRelease(fn) { onDeactivated(fn); onBeforeUnmount(fn); }` — and make every resource-owning composable consume it. Then move the camera out of the SFC entirely into `demo/platform/media/useCameraCapture.ts` (a sibling of the existing auth/ storage/ transport/), which owns its own release.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 pure pass-through barrels of glass-ui, and this single three-file feature reaches the design system through both routes simultaneously.
defects.evidence: Every demo/ui/*/index.ts is a one-line re-export: `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, `export { Card, ... } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, 19 directories. Meanwhile ExtractWorkbench.vue:187-188 imports DockControl and useBreakpoint DIRECTLY from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock and /dom, while ExtractControls.vue:99 imports Slider from ../../ui/slider and ExtractPane.vue:24 imports Card from ../../ui/card. The hop also widens the specifier: demo/ui/* reaches the glass-ui ROOT barrel while glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes ./slider, ./card, ./badge, ./button, ./tooltip as narrow subpaths (73 export keys in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json).
defects.mechanism: An indirection layer with zero content — a legacy alias tier left over from the shadcn-vue era after every member was converted to a re-export. Violates edict 2 (no aliases/dual paths) and edict 3 (KISS, no wrapper components).

defects.proposedCure: Dissolve demo/ui/ and repoint consumers at glass-ui subpaths. The precedent is already in this repo: the SAME commit as N-1, 95993197 F3, dissolved `dark-mode-toggle/` with the words 'a 2-line re-export folder. DISSOLVED: the 4 consumers repoint DIRECTLY at @mkbabb/glass-ui/controls'. The rule was applied to one folder and not to the other nineteen. Preserve demo/ui/alert/index.ts's historical prose in demo/DESIGN.md, not as a folder.

defects.defect: 'The dominant color' has three implementations across two ownership layers; the library's published `dominantColor()` has zero production consumers and the demo re-derives an ordering the library already guarantees.
defects.evidence: src/quantize.ts:127 `output.sort((a, b) => b.population - a.population)` — the returned array IS dominance-ordered. src/quantize.ts:132-139 `dominantColor()` re-quantizes at a hardcoded `k: 5` and returns value[0]; `grep -rn dominantColor src/ demo/ test/ e2e/` shows ZERO production consumers (only test/v4-quantize.test.ts, test/v4-c1.test.ts, and a demo COMMENT at useExtractSession.ts:10 explaining why it is not used: 'the library's dominantColor() re-quantizes and is the wrong tool'). useExtractSession.ts:120-141 is a 22-line max-population rescan with a chroma tiebreak. MEASURED: 400 synthetic 24x24 images against the built dist/subpaths/quantize.js, k in [1,16], chromaWeight in [0,1.5] => 'trials=400  first-place ties=9  demoDominant !== value[0] : 4', sorted-descending invariant held 400/400.
defects.mechanism: The library publishes a dominance primitive of the wrong shape (hardcoded k, a second O(n*k*iters) pass) while leaving the ordering guarantee it DOES provide unstated in the return type (bare `readonly QuantizedColor[]`). The consumer therefore defensively re-derives the maximum by hand, and the only genuinely live behaviour in those 22 lines is a chroma tiebreak that fires on exact integer population ties.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/dom.mjs — runs the demo's dominance loop verbatim beside value[0] over 400 seeded random images. Output: trials=400 first-place ties=9 demoDominant !== value[0] : 4. This empirically CONFIRMS pass 1's assertion that the `population >` branch is unreachable and quantifies the tiebreak's actual effect at 1% of trials.
defects.proposedCure: The chroma tiebreak is a QUANTIZER semantic, not a presentation semantic. Move it into the comparator at src/quantize.ts:127 so value[0] is authoritative for every consumer; the demo's 22-line loop then collapses to `palette[0]`. Retire `dominantColor` from src/quantize.ts and src/subpaths/quantize.ts (a 4.0.0 -> 5.0.0 surface change; the test/v4-c1.test.ts:342 census row updates with it), or replace it with `dominantOf(palette: readonly QuantizedColor[])` which takes the palette rather than pixels. Express the sort in the type or assert it in test/v4-quantize.test.ts so no consumer ever re-scans again.

File existence: dist/index.d.ts MISSING, dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts MISSING, dist/subpaths/units.d.ts MISSING, dist/subpaths/css.d.ts EXISTS, dist/subpaths/value.d.ts EXISTS. `parsing` and `units` are the v3 names that v4 renamed to `css` and `value`; tsconfig.demo.json:5-7 still calls this 'the 8 public keys' in prose. defects.mechanism: vite.config.ts:39-52 GENERATES the runtime alias set from package.json#exports precisely so it 'can never drift'. tsconfig.demo.json then hand-maintains a second map for types, which drifted. The map is inert exactly where the component depends on it (/css, imported at useExtractSession.ts:15 and useImageSampler.ts:13) and non-empty exactly where nothing does. Related latent hazard: node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 is a real installed directory, not a symlink, contradicting vite.config.ts:24-26 ('A package does not install itself') — a second resolvable surface. I verified its exported SYMBOL SETS are identical to the repo's dist and quantize.js is byte-identical, so this half is a hypothesis, not a live break.
defects.reproduction: node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' '))" vs the paths keys in tsconfig.demo.json ; for f in dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts; do [ -f $f ] && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING; done => all MISSING ; npx tsc --traceResolution on a probe .ts placed inside the package with the demo's paths block.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the seven @mkbabb/value.js* entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths outright, keeping only the vue/@vue/* dedupe entries. Node/TS package self-reference through package.json#exports is already the resolution that fires, it is the SAME mechanism a real external consumer uses, and it cannot drift. Separately, remove node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js from the install tree (it is not in dependencies; it is a lockfile artifact) and assert its absence beside the existing test/dist/ hygiene checks.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) · demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-13 — `package.json:20 "sideEffects": false`, a LIBRARY publishing hint, eliminates the entire DEMO APPLICATION from the production build because demo and src share one package manifest. `vite build --mode gh-pages` emits 698 bytes of modulepreload polyfill and zero application JavaScript; MixSourceSelector.vue does not exist in the production bundle at all. Proven by a minimal two-arm A/B whose `sideEffects:false` arm emits a chunk with the SAME CONTENT HASH (`index-Dezn_h7o.js`) as the real gh-pages build. Its component-level twin is L-1 (independently re-derived and CONFIRMED): the component codes against a `WatercolorDot` `tag`/slot/attrs contract glass-ui 7.0.0 does not publish, so both colour-add controls are inert `<span aria-hidden pointer-events:none>` — and the repo's OWN e2e gate `e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts` is RED on exactly this today.

Rolldown concludes every module in the package is side-effect-free and eliminates the application entry (an inline `<script type="module">` that exports nothing and only calls `app.mount`). The gh-pages production build emits NO application JavaScript and NO application CSS. The subject component is absent from the production bundle entirely.

Real build: `npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir <scratchpad>/ghp --emptyOutDir` -> `assets/index-Dezn_h7o.js 0.69 kB`; emitted JS = {index-Dezn_h7o.js 698 B (modulepreload polyfill IIFE only), quantize-worker-xMwe415C.js 11774 B}; emitted CSS = {glass-fonts-DH5GtBvs.css 132943 B} — no app bundle. defects.mechanism: One package.json owns two artifacts with contradictory requirements — a tree-shakeable ES library and an application whose entry is pure side effect. A library publishing hint leaks onto the app build because the module boundary between library and demo does not exist at the package level.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/probe-L13-sideeffects.mjs <workdir>  (exits 0 and prints 'L-13 CONFIRMED'). Full-scale: npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir <tmp> --emptyOutDir; ls <tmp>/assets/*.js
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a flag edit: `demo/` becomes its own package in an npm workspace — demo/package.json with its own dependency set, no `sideEffects` field, an explicit `main.ts` entry, and `@mkbabb/value.js` as a real `file:..` dependency. That single move also makes the demo a GENUINE external consumer (the dogfood proof currently simulated by vite.config.ts's valueJsSelfAlias) and deletes the drifted tsconfig.demo.json `paths` block wholesale. `"sideEffects": ["demo/**"]` would also make the build pass and is exactly the masking patch edict 2 forbids.

defects.defect: The component consumes glass-ui's `WatercolorDot` through a `tag` prop, a default slot, and attribute fallthrough — none of which glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes. `tag`, `title`, `aria-label`, `:disabled`, `@click` and the `<Plus>` child are all silently discarded. Both colour-add paths of the Mix workbench's Colors mode (the default mode) are inert `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">` elements. CONFIRMED independently in pass 2, and the repo's own e2e gate is red on it.
defects.evidence: Published dist `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js`: `inheritAttrs: !1`, setup re-applies only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`, root is `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", style:[…,{pointerEvents:"none"}]})`, no renderSlot, props={color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}. Live DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: `.add-slot-ghost` -> tagName SPAN, attrs contain no aria-label/title/disabled/tag, hasSvgPlus=false, isFocusable=false, computed pointer-events="none". Hit-test: rect x=1276.4 y=295.5 w=49.5 h=49.5, elementFromPoint(centre) -> DIV.swatch-row (the PARENT); click at centre -> [data-mix-source] 0 -> 0; Mix button .disabled=true. Repo gate: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke` -> 1 failed, "expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed ... getByRole('button',{name:'Add current color to the mix'}) ... element(s) not found". Call sites: MixSourceSelector.vue:146-151, 164-176, 211-221.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui has no polymorphic element register on this primitive, though its own `Button` publishes `as?: string | Component` (visible in the strictTemplates probe output). `inheritAttrs:false` closes the fallthrough escape hatch; the demo invented a private `tag` prop no shipped version has; W44 adopted glass-ui 7.0.0 whole without migrating a call site; nothing in the toolchain objects (see L-15).
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/mix, then in the console: const d=document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost'); const r=d.getBoundingClientRect(); document.elementFromPoint(r.left+r.width/2, r.top+r.height/2)  -> returns DIV.swatch-row, not the control. Or: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line --workers=1
defects.proposedCure: Upstream (the real home, edict 4 + the standing glass-ui BH relay): WatercolorDot adopts the register glass-ui already speaks in Button — `as?: string | Component`, a default `<slot/>`, and aria-hidden/pointer-events confined to the decorative sub-layers, never the root when the root is interactive. Demo-side today with zero new abstractions: the dot is decoration INSIDE a real `<button>` — the file already does exactly that twice (the remove-X at 152-158 and the palettes-mode card wrapper at 246-268), so the defect is that one file uses two idioms for one job. Collapse to one.

defects.defect: The behavioural oracle that catches L-1 already exists, is already written, already fails — and is not gating. Pass 1 concluded the CI gates are blind; that is true of vue-tsc and eslint and FALSE of the e2e suite, which encodes this exact contract in two specs and is red today.

defects.defect: Importing the single Symbol `LIBRARY_PORT_KEY` from the provider god-module `demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts` drags 42 extra modules / 168,138 bytes — the entire admin console and admin API client, plus vue-router — into this leaf's static closure, across a lazy code-split boundary. The parent MixPane already injects the same key and already prop-drills other palette state, so the child's inject is a duplicate acquisition of one concept by two mechanisms.
defects.evidence: Measured closure (resolving .ts/.vue/index.ts as the bundler does): MixSourceSelector.vue full = 96 local modules / 387,167 B; with usePalettePorts.ts cut = 54 modules / 219,029 B; delta = 42 modules / 168,138 B. The 42 include demo/palettes/api/{admin-audit,admin-colors,admin-palettes,admin-users,versions}.ts and AdminUsersPanel.vue, AdminAuditPanel.vue, AdminNamesPanel.vue, AdminTagsPanel.vue, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue, AdminListItem.vue, PaginationBar.vue, PaletteSlugBar.vue. vue-router enters the external set only via this edge. Corroboration: a tsconfig whose `include` names exactly one file (MixSourceSelector.vue) builds a program in which 16 distinct .vue files report strictTemplates errors, all admin/browse. Sites: MixSourceSelector.vue:6,33-34 vs MixPane.vue:16,83-84; lazy boundary at demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:75.
defects.mechanism: The injection key — dependency-free data — is exported from the same module as the five-port wiring that statically imports 15 sibling composables. A consumer that wants the key cannot avoid the graph.

defects.proposedCure: Two moves. (1) Free: delete the inject (lines 6, 33-34); MixPane already holds the port, so pass `:saved-palettes`. MixSourceSelector becomes a pure presentational leaf — glass-ui + two sibling SFCs + two type imports, zero feature reach. (2) Structural so it cannot recur: move the five InjectionKey constants and port types into a dependency-free demo/palettes/ports.keys.ts; the provider imports them to provide(). demo/color-session/keys.ts already applies exactly this discipline to CSS_COLOR_KEY / EDIT_TARGET_KEY — the pattern is in-tree, palettes just never adopted it.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is 19 content-free shim barrels that re-export from glass-ui's ROOT export, and this file uses the shim idiom and the correct subpath idiom in the same three-line import block. Reaching Collapsible through the root barrel names a 30.3x larger module graph than the published `@mkbabb/glass-ui/collapsible` subpath that exists for it.
defects.evidence: demo/ui/collapsible/index.ts is one line: `export { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. MixSourceSelector.vue:4 `@mkbabb/glass-ui/tabs`, :5 `../../ui/collapsible`, :7 `@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot`. Static closure over glass-ui dist: root `.` = 66 modules / 224,193 B; `./collapsible` = 3 modules / 7,407 B; `./tabs` = 20/50,466; `./watercolor-dot` = 6/9,503. glass-ui package.json `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]` so the CSS side is explicitly not prunable. defects.mechanism: A half-retired migration/alias layer (edict 2) interposed between the demo and the design system (edict 4), reaching the root barrel instead of the subpath the producer publishes — the same tree-shake-honesty problem demo/palettes/browser/index.ts already writes down for its own sub-barrels (PI-6 / T.W1 F7).
defects.reproduction: Closure walk over node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist from glass-ui.js vs collapsible.js: 66 modules/224193 B vs 3 modules/7407 B. Delivered-bytes impact is a HYPOTHESIS: the production build emits no app JS at all (L-13) and the live network probe was unavailable (concurrent seat held the MCP browser).
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely and rewrite the 90 sites onto glass-ui subpaths. Pure deletion — no new directory, no wrapper (edict 3) — and it makes the violation unrepresentable: once demo/ui/ does not exist, an import can only name @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>.

Enabling it fires 7 errors in this file today — and the granular flags do not reduce the cost.

defects.mechanism: Vue models an unknown prop on a component as a legal fallthrough attribute and models nothing about inheritAttrs:false suppression or slot content handed to a slotless component. eslint has no such rule class. W44 adopted a producer MAJOR version behind gates provably incapable of detecting a deleted prop, a deleted slot, or a flipped inheritAttrs.

Type-checking narrows the hole; only L-1's architectural cure closes it — `tag` still slips through.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to pass-1 L-9: tsconfig.demo.json `paths` has drifted from package.json#exports, and the two value.js artifacts it straddles are NOT the same file. The demo is typechecked against the npm-published tarball for `/css` and `/value` while Vite serves the local checkout build — a live dual-resolution of the package's own public surface, on a surface this component transitively depends on.

Byte divergence: `wc -c dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` -> 12490 (checkout, what Vite serves) vs 10910 (tarball, what vue-tsc reads) — 1580 bytes apart, both claiming 4.0.0. defects.mechanism: The runtime alias set is GENERATED from package.json#exports (vite.config.ts valueJsSelfAlias) while the typecheck alias set is hand-written. Where the hand-written set forgets a key, TS falls through to node resolution and finds a transitively-installed, pinned, immutable copy of the package's own published surface.
