Under L-13's workspace cure this becomes unnecessary entirely: a real `file:..` dependency needs no `paths`.

defects.defect: The mix convergence choreography is a stringly-typed DOM protocol spanning five modules with no type, test or lint rule binding it: the selector writes `data-mix-source` / `data-mix-color` / `data-mix-colors` (a JSON.stringify'd slice) and the animation reads them back by querySelectorAll, with three e2e specs hard-coding the same magic strings.
defects.evidence: Writer: MixSourceSelector.vue:131-132 (`data-mix-source`, `:data-mix-color`), :252-255 (`:data-mix-source`, `:data-mix-colors` = JSON.stringify(palette.colors.slice(0,4).map(c=>c.css))). Reader: demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:126-129 `root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-mix-source]")`. Specs: e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:45, e2e/smoke/safari/mix-flow.spec.ts:35, e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:55.
defects.mechanism: An undeclared cross-module vocabulary. Rename an attribute in the writer and the animation silently stops lifting pigment; typecheck and lint stay green and only a full e2e run notices — the same suite shown to be red and ungated (P2-0).
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "data-mix-source|data-mix-color" demo/ e2e/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'  -> writer, reader and three specs, no shared declaration
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT replace the mechanism — reading real laid-out geometry off the DOM is correct for an animation that must lift pigment from where the chips actually are. Declare the vocabulary: one leaf module demo/workbenches/mix/mixStageAttrs.ts (no new directory, no wrapper) exporting the three attribute names and the data-mix-colors payload type, imported by the writer, the reader, the e2e specs, and the ambient HTMLAttributes augmentation L-15's cure requires. One file discharges both findings.

defects.defect: The demo un-Results the library at every call site and owns colour math the library should own: `mixColorSequence` (N-ary weighted mixing with finite/nonnegative/positive-sum weight validation) lives in demo/palettes/mix.ts while @mkbabb/value.js/color ships only binary mixColors, and a private `mixedOrThrow` adapter destroys the package's headline 'failure-explicit' Result contract.
defects.evidence: package.json:4 describes the package as 'Immutable, failure-explicit …'. src/color/operations.ts:83-120 mixColors is scrupulously Result-typed with seven distinct err({code}) returns. demo/palettes/mix.ts:31-36 `if (!result.ok) throw new Error(...)` plus a `as unknown as` double cast; demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:16-20 same shape for toRgba8. demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:79-101 startMix calls the throwing wrapper with no try. mixColorSequence at demo/palettes/mix.ts:37-64; its only consumers are MixConfigBar.vue:14, useMixingState.ts:21 and test/mix-v4.test.ts (the library's own suite reaching into the demo tree).
defects.mechanism: A library capability implemented one level too high, plus a per-feature throwing adapter — the same concept (Result -> exception) implemented once per caller instead of once anywhere.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural/ownership finding read from the sources named; no runtime failure demonstrated (a malformed saved palette would surface as an unhandled exception inside a click handler, but I did not construct one).
defects.proposedCure: Promote mixColorSequence into @mkbabb/value.js/color beside mixColors, Result-typed like its neighbour (Result<Color<S>, ColorIssue>), taking readonly AnyColor[][] so no Palette type crosses the boundary; the leftover-strategy palette logic stays in the demo where it belongs (a palette concept, not a colour concept). test/mix-v4.test.ts then tests src/ and stops importing demo/. Then either the library ships an explicit throwing register the demo may name honestly, or the demo propagates Result to a rendered failure state — what must not survive is a private `…OrThrow` per feature.

defects.defect: The TransitionGroup key allocator (20 lines of module-scope counter + Map + computed + GC watcher) is view-local surrogate identity doing the state machine's job, and it is keyed by array INDEX, so removing any non-last chip re-mints the key of every survivor and defeats the very FLIP behaviour the keys exist to enable.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98, mapKey = `${sc.css}::${i}`. By construction: [A,B,C] -> A::0=0, B::1=1, C::2=2; removeColor(0) (useMixingState.ts:59-61) -> [B,C] whose keys B::0 and C::1 are both absent and minted fresh as 3 and 4. TransitionGroup name="vj-enter" at line 120 therefore sees leaves+enters instead of moves. SelectedColor carries no id: useMixingState.ts:25-28 `{ css: string; source: string }`.
defects.mechanism: Identity is invented by the view, in a side table, after the fact; it belongs to the state machine that mints the value. (Currently unobservable because L-1 makes two chips unreachable — it becomes visible the instant L-1 is cured.)
defects.reproduction: Deterministic replay of lines 79-89 over [A,B,C] then remove index 0 -> survivor keys change from [1,2] to [3,4]. (Pass 1 recorded this as evidence/probe-C4-keychurn.mjs / swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs.)
defects.proposedCure: Give SelectedColor an `id` minted once in addColor (crypto.randomUUID()); the view keys on sc.id; lines 78-98 and the watcher delete entirely; duplicate colours become first-class; the removal choreography becomes correct by construction. Animations are moved, not deleted — vj-enter and the .add-slot-ghost scoped rule are untouched (edict 6).

result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof of soundness is claimed. What I checked and found CLEAN, with positive evidence, so the report is not read as blanket condemnation: (1) The value.js public surface is NOT violated by this component — it imports no @mkbabb/value.js specifier at all; the only value.js externals on its 96-module closure are `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`, both published subpaths, both reached by `import type` where type-only (useMixingState.ts:19). No `@src/*` and no deep `src/` path anywhere in the mix workbench; the T.W1 dogfood keystone holds at the SPECIFIER level (the RESOLUTION is split — L-17). (2) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean: both type-only imports (lines 10, 11) are `import type`; `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0. (3) The three named historical suspects are NOT on this component's chain — I computed the closure and searched it: demo/palettes/export.ts / usePaletteExport.ts / export/serializers -> absent; useLayerTransition -> absent; useMarkdownHighlighting and the useDark trio -> absent. The export dual path is real (usePaletteExport.ts:9 imports ./export while only demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts imports export/serializers) but belongs to another component's report and I do not claim it here. (4) This is not a god module: 283 lines, one concern, four props in / five emits out; its composable (useMixingState.ts, 138 lines) honours the documented ONE-CLOCK law and owns no timer. (5) The barrel reach `../../palettes/browser/card` is the sub-barrel the written seam law permits (it is merely unenforced — L-14). (6) The /#/mix visual-matrix rows carry no fingerprint of this component: REPORT.json safari-desktop-light /#/mix shows overflowX 0, pageErrors [], consoleErrors [], main 1; the 8 smallTapTargets are the login capsule (22x22) and the picker channel rails (12x24) and the 1 namelessButton is dock-level — and critically, none of the route's 30 buttons is the add slot or a palette swatch, because those are aria-hidden spans the scanner cannot see. The matrix's silence is corroboration of L-1, not absolution.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m] (1M-context variant); the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D2-01 — the undeveloped state is exactly the "giant shadow placeholder" VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:198 names and forbids, and it inverts OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:42's "absent result collapses context": measured live at 1440x900, the ShadowPalette ghost (153.0px) plus its caption (24.5px) = 177.5px against a 182.9px image stage = 97.0%, i.e. 82,165 px² of pure placeholder in a 463px column. The component's own defence (the ghost makes k legible) duplicates a 20px numeral that is already printed one row above.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundness, tested rather than assumed: the three-family motion register is honoured with no fourth name and a global prefers-reduced-motion guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184; the dark treatment is NOT inverted — PIL sampling of the mobile PNGs gives ghost-vs-plate ratios light 1.12/1.15 and dark 1.15/1.50, so --skeleton-ink is scheme-true and the dark arm is stronger; REPORT.json /#/extract shows overflowX 0, bleeding [], pageErrors [], consoleErrors [], main 1, imgNoAlt 0 in all four Safari matrices; useExtractSession derives dominance from the returned palette without re-quantizing and tears the debounce down on unmount; verbatimModuleSyntax and the Vue 3.5 reactive-props-destructure idiom are honoured.)

defects.defect: The undeveloped state renders a full-material shadow plate that is 97.0% the height of the image stage, inverting the binding 'absent result collapses context' row and the constitution's verbatim 'not a giant shadow placeholder'.
defects.evidence: Live Playwright measurement, http://localhost:9000/#/extract at 1440x900: dropZone {w:463.1,h:182.9}; ShadowPalette {w:462.9,h:153.0}; caption {w:462.1,h:24.5} → 177.5/182.9 = 97.0%, 82,165 px². Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:198, OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:42, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:34 (law 8). Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:158-167.
defects.mechanism: absence-is-depicted: the component treats 'no result yet' as a thing to render at full material weight instead of collapsing the region
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/extract at 1440x900, cold load, no interaction — this is the default frame. Re-measure with getBoundingClientRect on [data-slot=shadow-palette] and the drop zone.
defects.proposedCure: Delete ShadowPalette from this seat; the result region has zero height until a result exists (literally 'absent result collapses context'). The invitation already lives in the stage copy; live-k feedback moves onto the k rail, which is already a color-bearing track. ShadowPalette.vue then has no seat and dies with the row.

defects.defect: The eyedropper/sampler is pointer-only: the drop-zone root keeps role="button" and an aria-label instructing the user to tap it, while tabindex flips to -1 and its keydown handler is gated off the moment an image exists.
defects.evidence: Live: dropZone (developed) → tabIndex -1, role="button", aria-label "Image preview area, tap to sample colors", cursor crosshair. Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:23-25 (:disable-click="!!preview", @click opens eyedropper), ImageDropZone.vue:19 (:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"), :22 (@keydown gated on !disableClick). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:198 'Eyedropper and sampler have keyboard/numeric alternatives', :126 (image sampler axes), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70.
defects.mechanism: specimen-as-button: the operable affordance is welded onto the specimen element, so making the specimen a sample surface removes it from the keyboard entirely
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, drop any image, then Tab through the pane — the image well is never reached, and Enter/Space on it do nothing. Confirmed by measured tabIndex -1 plus the gated handler.
defects.proposedCure: Promote sampling to a named control in the action region (a DockControl toggle 'Sample colors' beside Upload/Camera) that switches the stage into sampling mode; the stage stays tabbable in every mode and the sampler exposes the two named numeric x/y axes VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:126 already specifies.

defects.defect: The dominance readout renders a derived value at the route-H1 type rung — byte-identical to the pane identity — uses an off-matrix rung for its unit phrase, and carries no tabular figures or reserved width.
defects.evidence: Live computed: "60% of the image" → font-size 41.888px Fraunces w400, font-variant-numeric normal; pane title "Extract" → font-size 41.888px Fraunces w400. Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:122-128. text-body resolves via glass-ui @utility (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css) but is not one of the seven roles in the closed matrix; grep -rln "text-body" demo/ → 3 files. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:68-78, :78 (tabular + reserve), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:76 (law 11).
defects.mechanism: type-role inversion: a statistic borrows the identity rung, flattening hierarchy, and a live number is set proportionally with no reserve so it reflows its row
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, drop an image, read getComputedStyle on the .font-display span and on the pane title — both 41.888px Fraunces. Change k and watch the ml-auto right group shift as the percentage changes glyph count.
defects.proposedCure: Render the line as the mandated pair — text-mono-small Fira value + text-small label — with tabular-nums and a three-glyph reserve. A headline statistic here needs a ratified paired-clamp exception (the way P019 was ratified for Picker), not a borrowed H1 rung.

defects.defect: The copyable specimen readout is an unrounded 56-character float with a non-canonical deg suffix, and it needs 565px in a ~202px slot at the shipped desktop column, so roughly 36% of the value is visible.
defects.evidence: Live: code textContent = "oklch(53.1574088865% 0.129031386517 261.300836681396deg)" (56 chars), scrollWidth 565px @ 16.4px Fira Code. Shipped column measured 463.1px; row = percentage 172.5 + gap 8 + 'dominant' ≈72 + gap 8 → ≈202px available. Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:137-141 (truncate + title + select-all); the component's own comment at :134-136 concedes truncation. Pass-1 D-8 measured 31% by direct reading.
defects.mechanism: precision leaked from the serialization boundary into the presentation layer, then papered over with CSS truncate and a tooltip
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract at 1440x900, drop an image, read the <code> element's textContent, scrollWidth and clientWidth. (Width arithmetic combines two measured constituents: scrollWidth at a 999px column and the 463px shipped column on the same page.)
defects.proposedCure: Round at the presentation boundary — the visible readout takes a fixed, reserved, widest-legal representation per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78 — and let the full-precision string ride the Copy action only.

defects.defect: The camera is a one-way door: the viewfinder offers only a Capture chip, there is no Cancel/Escape, and the disabled value the workbench computes for exactly this case is consumed by 1 of 6 controls.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:34-59 (viewfinder contains one DockControl, 'Capture frame'); exits only via captureFrame→onFile→stopCamera (:265-279), a file drop, or unmount (:281). :disabled="session.isProcessing.value || cameraActive" at :70 is consumed only by ExtractControls.vue:84 (Reset); Upload (:41), Camera (:50) and both sliders ignore it. Reset itself is :disabled="disabled || !hasImage" and only restores k/chroma defaults (useExtractSession.ts:180-184).
defects.mechanism: a mode was implemented as a boolean overlay rather than as a stage mode with an entry/exit pair, so its exit was never authored
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract on a device with a camera, press the Camera control, then attempt to dismiss the viewfinder without capturing — no control exists; Reset is disabled (no image) and would not help.
defects.proposedCure: Make the camera a mode of the stage: entering swaps the stage content and the action region gains Cancel + Capture, with Escape cancelling — the canon's select→tune→commit grammar applied to a mode rather than a value. One disabled prop, six consumers.

defects.defect: The camera capability is implemented twice: useImageQuantize already exports quantizeFromCamera (with the stop() handle) and quantizeFromCanvas, both dead, while the view hand-rolls getUserMedia, video, canvas, toBlob, File and teardown — and the shipping path PNG-encodes and base64-round-trips a canvas to reach a function that accepts a canvas.
defects.evidence: grep -rn "quantizeFromCamera" --include=*.ts --include=*.vue demo/ test/ e2e/ → only useImageQuantize.ts:4 (comment), :115 (definition), :159 (export). grep -rn "getUserMedia" demo/ → ExtractWorkbench.vue:242 and useImageQuantize.ts:116. Round trip: ExtractWorkbench.vue:274-277 (canvas.toBlob PNG → File) → useExtractSession.ts:166 (FileReader → data URL) → useImageQuantize.ts:19-25 (createImageBitmap → pixels).
defects.mechanism: dual path: a capability written in the composable layer was re-implemented imperatively in the view, leaving the well-formed copy dead and the ad-hoc copy shipping
defects.reproduction: Run the two greps above; both return the quoted output on branch tranche-u at HEAD c654824e.
defects.proposedCure: Delete startCamera/stopCamera/captureFrame from the view; the session owns a camera sub-state built on quantizeFromCamera, and quantizeFromCanvas consumes the captured frame directly (no PNG encode, no base64, no re-decode).

defects.defect: The camera viewfinder is object-cover clipped to max-h-200px while captureFrame captures the full uncropped video frame, so roughly 43% of the captured image was never shown before capture — and the palette is quantized over pixels the user never saw.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:44 (video class="w-full max-h-[200px] object-cover") against :269-272 (canvas.width = video.videoWidth, canvas.height = video.videoHeight, drawImage(video,0,0)); requested source is 640x480 ideal (:244-247). At the measured 463px column the preview box is 463x200 = 2.32:1 against a 1.33:1 source.
defects.mechanism: preview geometry and capture geometry are specified independently, so WYSIWYG breaks precisely where the product's whole value is 'the colors in this image'
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the rendered arm — no camera in the probe environment. The geometry is deterministic from the two source coordinates above.
defects.proposedCure: One geometry for both: object-contain on the viewfinder (what you see is what you get) or crop the capture to the displayed rect. Which wins is a product choice; disagreeing is not an option.

defects.defect: The failure register is color-only, unannounced, undismissable, prints raw exception text, and rides the wrong channel — camera permission errors are written into quantizeError and rendered in the result column.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:79-85 (a bare text-destructive div — no icon, no role=alert, no aria-live, no dismiss); :252 (`Camera access denied: ${err}` interpolates a DOMException); useExtractSession.ts:66-73 (quantizeError getter reads the worker error, setter writes it); useImageQuantize.ts:86 (error cleared only inside runQuantize). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 'failed … states are never color-only'.
defects.mechanism: one shared error string used as a global mailbox, with no status region contract behind it
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, press Camera, deny permission — a red line reading 'Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: …' appears in the result column and never clears unless a later quantize succeeds.
defects.proposedCure: One status region per instrument with three registers: pending (role=status), failure (role=alert + icon + human copy + Retry), idle (absent). Camera failures surface at the camera, not on the result plate.

defects.defect: The developed result is an operable ornament: PaletteCard's root is unconditionally cursor-pointer with role="article" and a click emit, and the workbench feeds it a no-op handler; it also opts into inline rename inside the card body.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:19 ('… bg-well cursor-pointer' in the static class list), :22 role="article", :26 @click="$emit('click')"; ExtractWorkbench.vue:154 @click="() => {}" and :151 editable-name. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 'not a clickable role=article' and 'The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu…'.
defects.mechanism: a library-entity component reused as a result specimen, with a dummy handler supplied to satisfy its emit
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, drop an image, hover the developed card — the pointer cursor claims the whole surface; clicking anywhere non-interactive does nothing.
defects.proposedCure: The extract result is a specimen, not a library entity — it should not be PaletteCard at all; naming belongs to the Save commit step. Producer-side, PaletteCard's cursor-pointer must be conditional on a real click consumer.

defects.defect: The mandated domain-neutral axis composition is not adopted: neither axis has a visible label or unit, both sliders take per-instance track overrides, a bespoke rail is painted behind a transparent producer track, and the thumbs measure 12-13px on the inline axis.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:14-35 (k axis: only visible text is the numeral; 'colors' exists solely in aria-label), :66 (label 'kC' with meaning in a title), :19-23 + :32 (absolute rail div + --slider-track-bg: transparent + inline boxShadow ring), :75 (--slider-track-bg: trackInk). REPORT.json /#/extract, all four matrices: {"w":12,"h":24,"label":"Number of colors"} and {"w":12,"h":24,"label":"Chroma weight"}; live re-measure role=slider thumbs 13x24. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 (label, unit, reserved live value, numeric entry; 'not new slider mechanics'), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72.
defects.mechanism: consumer-side reinvention of a producer primitive, with the semantic parts of the composition (label, unit, numeric entry) dropped
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract and read the two slider rows: visible text is '5' and 'kC'. Measure [role=slider] rects → 13x24. The REPORT.json rows reproduce it in Safari across all four matrices.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the one axis composition (label + unit + reserved tabular value + optional numeric entry) and push the color-bearing track into the producer Slider as a variant, so no consumer paints a rail behind a transparent track.

defects.defect: The workbench binds two different facts from one predicate (disable-click ≡ !!preview), making two authored ImageDropZone states unreachable and deleting click-to-replace entirely.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:22-23 (:preview and :disable-click from the same value) against ImageDropZone.vue:20 (aria-label ternary whose middle branch requires preview && !disableClick) and :61 ({{ disableClick ? 'sample' : 'replace' }} under v-if="preview"). The 'Replace image, click or drop a new image' label and the 'replace' chip are therefore unreachable. Live: developed drop zone reports tabindex -1, cursor crosshair, label 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'.
defects.mechanism: predicate collapse: two independent states (hasImage vs sampling-mode) driven from one boolean, so half the authored state space is unreachable
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, drop an image, hover the preview — the corner chip always reads 'sample'; there is no state in which it reads 'replace', and clicking the preview opens the eyedropper rather than the file picker.
defects.proposedCure: Two predicates for two facts: hasImage, and mode: 'idle' | 'sampling'. Sampling becomes an explicit named mode; with the mode off the stage is click-to-replace and says so.

defects.defect: All three of the workbench's primary actions (Upload, Camera, Reset) are named by a title tooltip only — no visible label and no aria-label — which is invisible to sighted users until hover and unavailable on touch.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json /#/extract: "namelessButtons": 3 in all four Safari matrices (Browse 0, Mix 1, Picker 1). Live tab-order probe: {tag:'button', label:'', title:'Upload image'}, {…'Open camera'}, {…'Reset'}. Source: ExtractControls.vue:41, 50, 84; a fourth in the camera state at ExtractWorkbench.vue:52. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 PR-07.
defects.mechanism: icon-only action bar with naming deferred to a hover-only fallback attribute
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract on a touch device (or the mobile Safari matrix) — the three action glyphs carry no visible or announced name; the audit harness counts 3 nameless buttons in every matrix.
defects.proposedCure: Give each action a visible label or at minimum an aria-label; PR-07's disposition is ADD-AFFORDANCE — every surviving action seat has a name and a state.

defects.defect: A failed re-quantize leaves the previous developed card fully rendered with its stale dominance percentage, under a red error line, because palette.value is never invalidated on error.
defects.evidence: useImageQuantize.ts:57-66 (on the error branch, error.value is set and isProcessing cleared; palette.value untouched); useExtractSession.ts:75-99 (extractedPalette derives from palette); ExtractWorkbench.vue:80 (v-if on error) and :109 (v-else-if on extractedPalette) are independent conditions.
defects.mechanism: result and failure modelled as two independent flags rather than one union, so 'stale + wrong + complaining' is representable
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Requires a worker failure I did not manufacture; the mechanism and the rendering consequence are entailed by the cited source coordinates.
defects.proposedCure: Model result and failure as one union: palette clears (or is explicitly marked stale, dimmed and labelled) the moment a run fails.

defects.defect: Pressing Camera a second time while the camera is live overwrites cameraStream without stopping the previous stream's tracks, leaking the first MediaStream and leaving the camera indicator lit after stopCamera runs.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-255 (cameraStream = await getUserMedia(...) with no guard and no teardown on re-entry) against :257-263 (stopCamera only knows the last assignment). The Camera button is never disabled while active because ExtractControls.vue consumes `disabled` only at :84.
defects.mechanism: mutable module-scope device handle assigned across an await with no re-entry guard
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Requires a real camera-permission grant, unavailable to the headless probe; the mechanism is unambiguous in source.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of D2-08's mode design — a mode cannot be entered while already active. Better: delete the hand-rolled camera entirely and use quantizeFromCamera's stop() handle (D2-16).

defects.defect: The empty placeholder wears a boundary line plus a three-layer cartoon caster, against the binding boundary inventory for Extract (boundaries [], reserve none, no retained dividing line).
defects.evidence: Live computed on [data-slot=shadow-palette]: border-color oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12); box-shadow oklab(...) -2px 2px 0 0, -3px 3px 0 0, -4px 4px 0 0. Source: ShadowPalette.vue:47 (border border-card-edge … shadow-cartoon-sm). Canon: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:76, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 (PR-05).
defects.mechanism: an empty surface given object-containment chrome it has no object to contain
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract cold and read getComputedStyle on [data-slot=shadow-palette] for border-color and box-shadow.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D2-01 — the surface goes away. If any ghost survives elsewhere it takes material and interval only: no edge, no caster.

defects.defect: The result seat runs vj-morph with mode="out-in" over three keys of unequal intrinsic height while setting none of the family's height geometry, so the max-height arm resolves to none and the height snaps in a two-phase collapse-then-grow.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:102 (<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">); grep -rn "vj-morph-" demo/workbenches/ → no output; only PaletteCard.vue:361-362 sets --vj-morph-collapse/-expanded repo-wide. Measured heights: ghost 153.0 + caption 24.5 (463px column) vs label row 66.7 + card 211.1 (999px column). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:141 'No full-slab remount hole'.
defects.mechanism: a morph family whose height arm is opt-in was used for the one swap whose defining delta is height
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract and drop an image — the plate region collapses and re-grows rather than morphing. Height constituents measured as quoted (the two readings are at different column widths; the direction is certain, the magnitude approximate).
defects.proposedCure: With D2-01 applied there are only two states and the absent one has zero height; a single vj-morph on the card with content-driven height removes the hole, and a re-quantize of an already developed plate should not re-enter the loading key at all.

defects.defect: The split layout branch has no consumer anywhere in the repo, keeping a dead grid arm, a dead breakpoint subscription and a dead PaletteCard 'aside' layout alive — and its 50/50 grid contradicts the binding golden composition anyway.
defects.evidence: grep -rn "ExtractWorkbench" demo/ → only ExtractPane.vue:11,25 (layout="column") and usePaneRouter.ts:72,85; grep -rn 'layout="split"' demo/ → no output. Dead: ExtractWorkbench.vue:4-9, :13, :18-20, :148, :226 (useBreakpoint/isWide). OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:42 requires golden 61.8033989% / 38.1966011%; the branch is sm:grid-cols-2 = 50/50.
defects.mechanism: a dual path retained for a consumer that no longer exists (owner edicts 2 and 3)
defects.reproduction: Run the two greps above on branch tranche-u at HEAD c654824e.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the split branch, isWide, useBreakpoint and the aside layout. If a two-column Extract returns, it adopts P122 with the ratified golden ratio rather than a local sm:grid-cols-2.

defects.defect: The .plate-ink rule — one declaration, color: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground)) — is copy-pasted into five separate scoped style blocks, each with its own justification comment.
defects.evidence: grep -rn "plate-ink {" demo/ --include=*.vue → ExtractWorkbench.vue:290, ExtractControls.vue:148, ImageDropZone.vue:109, demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:102, demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:84. Owner edicts 5 (root-level styling) and 3 (KISS).
defects.mechanism: a token expressed as a per-component scoped rule instead of once at the root
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above; five sites, identical body.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist it once into demo/styles/ as a single utility (or consume the certified ink token directly at the root) so the next certified-ink change has one landing site instead of five.

defects.defect: The eyedropper overlay behaves as a modal — absolute inset-0 over the entire workbench — while declaring no dialog semantics, trapping no focus, and restoring focus to nothing on close.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:173-180 (v-if sibling inside the workbench root; @close="eyedropperActive = false" and nothing more) with ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (absolute inset-0 z-popover, no role="dialog", no aria-modal). The opener cannot receive focus anyway (tabindex -1, D2-11). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:115.
defects.mechanism: an overlay authored as a visual layer rather than as a declared modality or a stage mode
defects.reproduction: NONE for the tab-order arm — HYPOTHESIS (the shared browser was taken by a concurrent session before I could Tab through it). The structural facts (v-if sibling, absolute inset-0, no inert, no role) are source-confirmed.
defects.proposedCure: If it is modal, declare modality and trap focus; if it is a mode of the stage — which it is — it occupies only the stage and leaves the controls live and uncovered.

defects.defect: Two adjacent lines use two different template-ref idioms, one of them the pre-3.5 form.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:222 const dropZoneRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof ImageDropZone> | null>(null); :223 const videoRef = useTemplateRef<HTMLVideoElement>("videoRef"). Owner edict 7.
defects.mechanism: idiom drift within a single file
defects.reproduction: Read demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:222-223.
defects.proposedCure: useTemplateRef for both.

defects.defect: The empty-state ghost runs twelve perpetually animating elements (5 segments + 2 meta blocks + 5 swatches at k=5) to depict a palette that does not exist.
defects.evidence: ShadowPalette.vue:58-79 (per-element animate-pulse with staggered inline animation-delay); live computed on .shadow-seg → animation-name: pulse, animation-duration: 2s. Pass-1 D-15 counted 34 perpetual animations on the idle empty page.
defects.mechanism: animation budget spent on a surface that should not exist
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract cold and read getComputedStyle('.shadow-seg').animationName, or count .animate-pulse under [data-slot=shadow-palette].
defects.proposedCure: Remove the host, not the register — owner edict 6 is satisfied because the motion family and its PRM guard are untouched; only the surface they decorate disappears (D2-01).

defects.defect: The /#/extract route appears in none of the five special state matrices, so the mega-tranche holds zero tracked evidence for this component under forced colors, reduced motion, RTL, 200% zoom or keyboard focus.
defects.evidence: ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/{forced-colors-desktop,reduced-motion-desktop,rtl-desktop,rtl-mobile,zoom-200-desktop,keyboard-focus-desktop} → each contains exactly adminusers.png, blob.png, browse.png, gradient.png, picker.png. states.mjs's ROUTES never included #/extract.
defects.mechanism: capture-matrix route list narrower than the component inventory it is used to certify
defects.reproduction: Run the ls above; extract.png is absent from all six directories.
defects.proposedCure: Add #/extract (and the remaining workbench routes) to states.mjs so these five states are certifiable rather than assumed.

defects.defect: NEGATIVE RESULT — the dark treatment of the ghost is not inverted or vanishing; the --skeleton-ink recipe is scheme-true and the dark arm is in fact stronger.

defects.defect: Once an image loads the eyedropper is unreachable by keyboard, while the element still announces as a button named 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'; the 'Replace image' label branch is dead code.
defects.evidence: ImageDropZone.vue:18-21 (:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"), ExtractWorkbench.vue:22-26. Measured r2: {"ariaLabel":"Image preview area, tap to sample colors","tabindex":"-1","focusableInMain":["Number of colors","Upload image","Open camera","Chroma weight","Reset","input"]} — the zone is absent from the focusable set.
defects.mechanism: one element overloaded with two mutually-exclusive roles (drop target vs sample action)
defects.reproduction: Load a valid PNG on /#/extract, enumerate focusable elements in <main> — the drop zone is gone; no other control opens the overlay. Focus also never enters the overlay and is never restored on close.
defects.proposedCure: Split the roles: a real focusable 'Sample colours from image' control for the preview state (the corner Fira tag is already the visual affordance — make it the button), zone stays tabindex=0 for replace-by-keyboard, and ImageEyedropper owns focus on mount + restore on close.

defects.defect: Nothing caches pixels: every k/kC change re-decodes the whole image and does a full main-thread pixel readback, then copies the buffer again before transferring it.
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:153-157, useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 and :93. Measured r2 for ONE ArrowRight on the k slider with a 3000x2000 image loaded: {"decodes":[{"ms":11.9,"w":3000,"h":2000}],"getImageData":[{"ms":13.4,"bytes":24000000}]} plus a second 24MB slice(0). src/quantize.ts:51 sub-samples to ~10,000 points regardless (stride 24 for this image).
defects.mechanism: expensive artefact re-derived per reactive tick instead of once per file
defects.reproduction: Load a 3000x2000 PNG on /#/extract, focus the 'Number of colors' slider, press ArrowRight once, instrument window.createImageBitmap and CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.getImageData.
defects.proposedCure: Decode once per file into a session-held {pixels,width,height} — or transfer the buffer to the worker once and re-run k-means on its retained copy; and use createImageBitmap(file, {resizeWidth, resizeHeight}) sized to sqrt(targetPixels) so the readback is ~120KB, not 24MB.

defects.defect: The dominance readout can name a colour that is not the card's first swatch, contradicting the component's own stated invariant.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117 asserts 'the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen'; src/quantize.ts:128 sorts by population (stable, ties keep insertion order) while useExtractSession.ts:121-142 adds a chroma tiebreak. r2 npx tsx derivation: quantizePixels order [0] C=0.2577 H=29.23 (red), [1] C=0.3132 H=264.05 (blue); dominant picks C=0.3132 H=264.05; AGREE? false.
defects.mechanism: two orderings for one claimed identity
defects.reproduction: npx tsx: quantizePixels(px([[255,0,0],[0,0,255]]), 2, 1, {k:5, chromaWeight:0.5}) then apply useExtractSession's dominant loop verbatim — index 0 and the loop's winner differ on any population tie.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the 22-line dominant loop: dominant = presented.value[0] ?? null. quantizePixels already guarantees max-population-first, which restores the invariant by construction. If a chroma tiebreak is genuinely wanted it belongs in src/quantize.ts's sort, where the card's ordering also sees it.

Reproduced r2: 4s after a successful decode of a 3000x2000 PNG — decodes [{ms:23.2,w:3000,h:2000}], unhandled [], errors [] — the result column DOM is PaletteCardSkeleton (5 bones + 5 swatch blocks, colText '5 kC 0.5'). Warm-server control (probe 4): the identical load completes in 502ms (post at t=437ms carrying 24,000,000 bytes; worker-message result n=5 at t=502ms).

defects.defect: Single-slot pendingResolve/pendingReject: overlapping quantizes orphan the earlier promise permanently, clear isProcessing while the later request is still running, and mis-route worker errors; a crashed worker is never replaced.
defects.evidence: useImageQuantize.ts:51-52 (one slot pair), :89-98 (overwritten per call), :57-75 (cleared on the FIRST reply), :69-75 (dead worker left installed). Generator: ExtractWorkbench.vue:70 passes :disabled but ExtractControls.vue consumes it at exactly one site (:84, Reset) — the k slider (:24-34), kC slider (:68-77), Upload (:40-44) and Camera (:49-55) all ignore it, so the user can queue requests during processing.

defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the visible symptom; the orphaned promise and the retained dead worker are unconditional in source.

defects.reproduction: NONE required — direct ordering in source, corroborated by the measured decode timings.
defects.proposedCure: Raise isProcessing at the top of quantizeFromFile inside try/finally — or, with C-22's cure, derive it from the in-flight record which is created before the decode.

defects.defect: Camera faults are filed into the quantizer's error ref and are never cleared by a successful camera start; every failure mode is labelled 'denied'.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 writes session.quantizeError.value, whose setter writes workerError (useExtractSession.ts:66-73); startCamera (:239-255) never resets it, and only useImageQuantize.ts:86 clears it. `${err}` renders [object Object] for a non-Error throw.

defects.reproduction: Deny camera once (error line appears), then grant on retry — the stale 'Camera access denied: ...' line persists under the live viewfinder until an unrelated extraction clears it.
defects.proposedCure: A separate cameraError ref with its own line and a session.setCameraError() action; map NotAllowedError / NotFoundError / NotReadableError / insecure-context to distinct human sentences.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — `easingCatalogue.ts:174,191` closes value.js's preset taxonomy with a hardcoded `FAMILY_ORDER.filter()`, silently dropping the entire `quart` and `quint` families (6 of 30 `bezierPresets`). Reproduced end-to-end in the live app: the producer's own `<EasingPicker>` menu offers all 30, and selecting `ease-out-quart` through it yields head text `"1 → 2custom"`, readout `cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)`, `pressedTile: "NONE PRESSED"` — a first-class library curve, chosen through the design system's own control, renders as unnamed. Two surfaces in one open row disagree about whether a named curve has a name. The module's docstring asserting "the tile catalogue IS value.js bezierPresets … never a second mint" is false on both clauses.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable — verdict is DEFECTIVE. For the record, 13 hypotheses were killed with positive evidence and are recorded in the report's "Negative proofs" section. The most load-bearing: (a) the published-surface question is CLEAN at the specifier level — `grep -rn 'from "@src|../../../src/|value.js/dist' demo` returns no output, and all 5 distinct value.js specifiers the demo writes (`/color` 25, `/css` 10, `/math` 6, `/easing` 5, `/quantize` 4) are real `package.json#exports` keys, with `vite.config.ts:41-51` generating the runtime alias set from that map so runtime drift is structurally impossible; (b) the literal-minting duplication is currently byte-identical — a 33-case probe against the real `useEasingPicker` gives 30/30 bezier + 3/3 steps agreement and equal preset-name sets, so L-2 is latent rather than live; (c) no dependency cycle — workbenches → color-session with no reverse edge; (d) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean across all four easing files; (e) `glyphPath` has exactly one home in the repo; (f) `aria-pressed` is emitted by glass's Chip, so L-5's missing pressed wash is purely visual; (g) 0 page errors and 0 route console errors on `/#/gradient` across all four Safari matrices, `overflowX: 0`; (h) the six `smallTapTargets` on `/#/gradient` are slug-bar controls and stop handles, not the specimen tiles.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue closes value.js's preset taxonomy with a hardcoded allow-list, silently dropping 6 of 30 `bezierPresets` (the whole `quart` + `quint` families). A named library curve then renders as `custom` with no tile pressed.
defects.evidence: `demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:174` `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` + `:191` `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. Live: strip renders 27 `[data-specimen]` ids, picker offers 30 options. `AFTER selecting ease-out-quart: {"headText":"1 → 2custom","readout":"cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)","pressedTile":"NONE PRESSED"}`. Gate blind: `test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56` asserts only `SPECIMEN_TILES.length > 20`.
defects.mechanism: The library publishes presets as a bare `Record<string, quad>` and does not publish their taxonomy, so the consumer re-derived the taxonomy by regex (`:168`) and then closed it with a hand-written allow-list. A projection of library data masquerading as a mirror; adding a preset family upstream is a silent no-op downstream.
defects.reproduction: Dev server at localhost:9000. `node scratchpad/quart.mjs` → 27 tile ids, no quart/quint. `node scratchpad/quart2.mjs` → open `/#/gradient`, click `button[aria-controls="easing-authoring-0"]`, click "Pick a curve", read 30 options, click option `ease-out-quart` → head reads `custom`, no tile pressed.
defects.proposedCure: Gestalt: value.js `/easing` publishes `bezierPresetList: readonly BezierPreset[]` with `{name, family, variant, points}` — taxonomy as DATA, not a consumer regex. KISS today: make `FAMILY_ORDER` a rank rather than a gate — `[...byFamily.keys()].sort((a,b) => rank(a)-rank(b))` with unknown families ranked last, so a new library family always appears.

defects.defect: MT-F030 / OM-4 radius incoherence: five distinct radius registers (0 / 4 / 6 / 16 / 9999 px) inside one 462x197 card; three of the five are not role-bearing house tokens, and nothing derives from anything.
defects.evidence: Live computed (`scratchpad/radii.mjs`, `/#/gradient`): `rowCard 16px`, `intervalHead 0px`, `fadingScrollPort 0px`, `rampStrip 6px`, `readoutRail 6px`, `railBtn 4px`, `specimenTile 9999px`, `specimenDot 9999px`, `pickerGlassCard 16px`. Sources: `GradientEasingEditor.vue:153` + `:176` use `rounded-md` (6px) — not one of DESIGN.md:192-197's four role tokens; `:242` hand-rolls `border-radius: 9999px` against DESIGN.md:201's explicit prohibition; `:274` uses `--radius-input`, which measures `0.25rem` (4px) while `demo/DESIGN.md:195` documents "8 px" (glass chain: `--radius-input: var(--radius)` → `--radius: 0.25rem` in `dist/styles/components.css`, a Tailwind stock var; demo overrides neither).
defects.mechanism: The house canon lists four radius ROLE tokens but states no DERIVATION law, so nested surfaces pick values off the raw Tailwind scale by eye instead of deriving them from their parent. Compounded by L-5: the tiles' 9999px is glass's `.glass-capsule` winning because `.glass-chip--cell`'s 16px never loads — so the most conspicuous register in OM-4 is glass-owned, and a local fix would be MT-F014.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/radii.mjs` (headless chromium against localhost:9000/#/gradient) prints the token table and every computed radius. Witness image: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png`; dark confirmation `audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/gradient.png`.
defects.proposedCure: Add the missing derivation clause to DESIGN.md §Radii and apply it: (1) a nested surface's radius is its parent's HALVED, floored at `--radius-xs` — 16 → 8 → 4; a surface never picks from the Tailwind scale. (2) The pill register belongs to POINTS (dots, markers, lamps, dock controls — meaning is position); a CELL (glyph + label) takes the derived rect register. Applied: ramp + readout rail 6→8, rail buttons 4, `.specimen-dot` → `var(--radius-pill)`, tile → 8 via glass's cell recipe (banked on M3, NOT patched locally). Separately correct DESIGN.md:195's `--radius-input` value to its actual 4px, or raise the token to the documented 8px in `demo/styles/`.

defects.defect: glass-ui 7.0.0's Chip material CSS is orphaned in the published dist and unreachable through its exports map, so this component's 27 selectable cell-chips render as incomplete glass: pill circles instead of cells, and selected chips byte-identical to unselected.
defects.evidence: Live stylesheet scan: `chipRules: 0` — ZERO selectors containing `.glass-chip` in ANY loaded stylesheet, against `capsuleRules: 10`. The element carries five such classes: `glass-chip glass-capsule … glass-chip--interactive … glass-chip--cell …`. `grep -c "glass-chip" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` → 0. `dist/styles/glass.css` lists 18 `@import`s, none is `glass-chip.css`. No `./styles/*` wildcard in glass-ui's exports map, so it cannot be deep-imported knowingly. Consequences measured: `specimenTile: "9999px box 45x44"` where `.glass-chip--cell { border-radius: var(--radius-card) }` (=1rem, token resolving) should win; `tileBg` and `tileOnBg` both `oklab(0.925644 0.0094459 0.0291917 / 0.83872)` — byte-identical, so `[data-state="on"] { background-color: var(--accent-band) }` never paints; the `@media (pointer: coarse)` 2.75rem touch floor is likewise absent. Blast radius N=1: `grep -rln "glass-ui/chip" demo | wc -l` → 1; `grep -rn 'shape="cell"' demo` → only `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:102`.
defects.mechanism: A producer packaging defect: the recipe file ships but is aggregated by no entry point and exposed by no export key. `.glass-capsule` (which IS aggregated) supplies the pill radius, so the `shape="cell"` prop is inert and selection affordance falls back entirely onto this seat's own scoped `--motion-accent` glyph/label ink.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/radii.mjs` — walks every `document.styleSheets` entry counting `.glass-chip*` selectors and reads the selected/unselected chip backgrounds. Visual: OM-4 (light) and `shots/safari-desktop-dark/gradient.png` — round bevelled pucks, pressed tile visually identical to its neighbours.
defects.proposedCure: FOLD-BANK on glass (BJ born-RED, mark M3 / INBOX I-9 / D58 / O-7 §F). NO local patch: a demo-side `.specimen-tile { border-radius: var(--radius-card) }` plus a hand-rolled pressed wash forks the design system's chip recipe into `demo/` — exactly the masking fallback MT-F014 and edict 2 forbid — and diverges the moment glass fixes the import. Add to the M3 packet: the zero-selectors-loaded proof, the `./styles/*` unreachability, and the N=1 blast radius.

defects.defect: value.js `/css` parses timing functions but cannot serialize them, so the `cubic-bezier(…)`/`steps(…)` literal law is hand-minted in three places; the byte-identity that `tileIdFor`'s string equality depends on is guarded by ONE assertion on ONE of 30 presets.
defects.evidence: `src/subpaths/css.ts:53-54` exports `parseTimingFunction` and `serializeCssColor`; `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → 4 hits, none for timing functions. Three inverses: glass-ui's public `useEasingPicker.readout`; `easingCatalogue.ts:48-56` (`bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral`, comment `:41-45` says it mirrors glass "byte-for-byte"); `useGradientCSS.ts:52-61` frozen `css: "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"`. Sync probe: `bezier: 30 compared, 0 mismatched`, `steps compared: 3`, `producer-only: [] demo-only: []`. Guard: `e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:189-192` asserts one preset (`ease-out-back`); zero assertions in vitest. `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` are exported but consumed only inside their own file.
defects.mechanism: An asymmetric grammar module: the colour arm has `parse`/`serialize`, the timing arm has only `parse`. Every consumer that needs the inverse writes its own, and the resulting cross-package invariant is maintained by a code comment instead of by the grammar. The catalogue's own comment names `linearInterval()` as the 'precedent … generalized' — it generalized the duplicate rather than retiring it.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/equiv.mjs` — instantiates the real `useEasingPicker` in an `effectScope`, walks all 30 `bezierPresets` plus the 3 steps tiles, and diffs the producer's `readout` against the demo's `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral`. Currently 0 mismatches: the defect is latent, so no live failure exists to reproduce; the coverage gap (1/30) is the measured fact.
defects.proposedCure: Gestalt: value.js `/css` exports `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string`, with `parseTimingFunction ∘ serializeTimingFunction ≡ id` as a round-trip property test over the whole preset corpus + the steps space; glass's `readout`, `bezierLiteral`, `stepsLiteral` and `linearInterval`'s frozen string collapse into one call. KISS today: `useEasingPicker` is a public export — mint the catalogue through it once at module scope and delete the hand-assembly.

defects.defect: `prefers-reduced-motion` is re-minted from `@vueuse/core` although glass-ui — the declared design system — publishes `useReducedMotion()` with an explicitly shared single MediaQueryList listener. Five demo sites, three idioms, zero consumers of the owner.
defects.evidence: `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:12,47` `useMediaQuery("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")`. glass-ui publishes it at `dist/composables/motion/core/useReducedMotion.d.ts` → `motion-core.d.ts` → export key `./motion-core`: "Share one reactive OS preference and one MediaQueryList listener." Census (`grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'`, 11 files): `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47` vueuse; `useInertiaGesture.ts:37` + `useMixingAnimation.ts:69` misuse glass's `useBreakpoint` for a non-breakpoint query; `useOverture.ts:96` + `useDockArrival.ts:26` raw `window.matchMedia().matches`. The demo already imports `useRAFLoop` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core` at two of those exact sites.
defects.mechanism: Ownership inversion (edict 4): the design system owns and publishes the concept; each consumer re-mints it. In one open specimen row the duplication is simultaneous — `<EasingPicker>` runs glass's shared subscription while the sibling strip runs its own — and multiplies by interval count via L-4.
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/motion/core/useReducedMotion.d.ts` then `grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'`. Behavioural symptom is listener count, not a user-visible break.
defects.proposedCure: One line: `import { useReducedMotion } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core"; const prefersReducedMotion = useReducedMotion();` — the `@vueuse/core` import dies. Fleet-wide: `readReducedMotion()` for the two one-shot boot sites, `useReducedMotion()` for the two `useBreakpoint` misuses. No new demo module, no new `shared/` dir.

defects.defect: A 27-tile / 133-node strip is mounted per interval row inside `v-show`, though `openInterval` is a single ref and only one row can ever be open — one selection surface is 26% of the whole route's element count, multiplied by interval count.
defects.evidence: `GradientEasingEditor.vue:61` `openInterval = ref<number|null>(0)` (single); `:112` `v-for="row in specimenRows"`; `:144` `v-show` (mounts); `:152` the CHEAP ramp is gated with `v-if`; `:161` the expensive strip is not. Measured: `{stripNodes:133, stripChips:27, stripSvgs:27, docNodes:511, portScrollWidth:1482, portClientWidth:436}` → 133/511 = 26.0%, and the port is 3.4x overscrolled (≈8 of 27 tiles reachable at desktop, ≈5 of 27 at 390px). The strip's own comment `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:38-40` documents the consequence — "sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id" — and works around it.
defects.mechanism: A one-of-N surface was made a child of each of the N rows rather than a single surface bound to the open row. The `visible` prop, the subtree-scoped `querySelector`, and the hidden-twins scoping paragraph are all workarounds for that placement, not requirements of it.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/cost.mjs` against localhost:9000/#/gradient counts nodes under `.specimen-strip` and in the document. At K intervals the arithmetic is 133·K nodes, 27·K Chip instances, K MediaQueryList listeners; the default 2-stop gradient gives K=1.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist ONE `<EasingSpecimenStrip>` out of the `v-for`, bound to `openInterval`. The disclosure body can only ever hold one row's content, so move it out of the loop entirely. This deletes the `visible` prop (a strip that exists is visible), the hidden-twins scoping, the subtree `querySelector`, and 133·(K−1) nodes — and, with one instance, permits a wrapped grid instead of a 3.4x horizontal scroll.

defects.defect: The seat restyles the producer's Chip root element from outside, replacing glass's own cell geometry and landing the tile 0.2px under the design system's own `--touch-target`.
defects.evidence: `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170` `.specimen-tile { gap: 0.125rem; padding: 0.3125rem 0.375rem 0.25rem; min-width: 2.75rem }` — scoped specificity (0,2,0 with `data-v-*`) beats glass's Tailwind utility (0,1,0). glass's own recipe: `chipVariants` `cell: "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro"`. Measured tile box `45x44` (r1 measured 44 x 43.8 with padding `5px 6px 4px 6px`, gap `2px`, `min-height: auto`), against `--touch-target: 2.75rem` = 44px. Under the producer's `py-2.5` the tile would be ≈54.8px. Not flagged by the audit because `capture.mjs` filters at `w<24||h<24`.
defects.mechanism: Edict-5 violation: per-instance override at a consumed component's root instead of a variant/size axis on the design system's recipe. The seat cut 11px of the producer's padding and set an inline floor with no block floor.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/radii.mjs` reports `specimenTile: "9999px box 45x44"`. Compare `chipVariants` cell string in `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js:12`.
defects.proposedCure: Stop overriding the producer root. Specimen scale is a SIZE axis on the cell recipe, which glass already models: `<Chip mode="selectable" shape="cell" size="sm">`. If `sm × cell` does not compose to specimen scale, that composition is a glass-owned addendum on the same M3 packet. The seat keeps only what is genuinely its own — the `--motion-accent` ink on `.tile-glyph path` / `.tile-label`.

defects.defect: The reveal-scroll reaches into the producer's private DOM by class name (`.closest(".fading-scroll")`), and the comment justifying it asserts a "documented DOM contract" that glass-ui's published type surface does not carry.
defects.evidence: `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:58-60`. `dist/components/fading-scroll/FadingScroll.vue.d.ts` declares five props (`axis, fadeStart, fadeEnd, ariaLabel, ariaLabelledby`), one default slot, no `defineExpose`, no exposed port ref, and never names the class. `.fading-scroll` / `--x` / `--y` are string literals inside the compiled render function `dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js`. Measured: the element matched by the demo's own `.specimen-strip` IS the port (`portScrollable: true`, `scrollWidth 1482 > clientWidth 436`), so the class-name probe buys nothing.
defects.mechanism: The producer exposes no handle to its scroll port, so the consumer couples to a compiled implementation detail; the comment then launders that coupling as a contract.
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/fading-scroll/FadingScroll.vue.d.ts` (no expose, no class) and `grep -o 'fading-scroll[a-zA-Z_-]*' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js`. No runtime break today — the coupling is latent until glass renames.
defects.proposedCure: Take the root through Vue's own contract: `<FadingScroll ref="stripRef">` + `useTemplateRef<ComponentPublicInstance>("stripRef")` → `stripRef.value?.$el`. Zero producer-private knowledge, survives any rename. If the reveal deserves to be first-class, bank a `defineExpose({ port })` / `scrollChildIntoInlineView()` addendum on glass — `useFadingScroll(target)` is already published and already takes an explicit port element. Preserve the single-axis discipline verbatim: the `scrollIntoView` ancestor-walk it replaced was the O-19 root cause.

defects.defect: `easingCatalogue.ts` holds four unrelated concerns, and the fourth makes a curve catalogue depend on the gradient model — a leaf-feature type imported into what should be a pure library consumer.
defects.evidence: Spans: `:48-56` literal minting, `:66-74` SVG glyph painting, `:98-203` tile/family construction, `:207-230` gradient-interval identity. The fourth forces `easingCatalogue.ts:36` `import type { GradientInterval } from "../../composables/useGradientModel"`, yet every predicate reads exactly one field (`interval.css`). Symptom at the sibling: `useSpecimenRows.ts:13` climbs four levels — `../../../../color-session/useContrastSafeColor`.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated in both directions: presentation-adjacent identity logic lives in the catalogue, and derivation logic lives at presentation depth. The catalogue cannot be tested or reused without knowing what a gradient is.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural finding, not a runtime failure. Read `easingCatalogue.ts:36, 207-230`.
defects.proposedCure: Key identity on the literal, not the model: `tileIdForCss(css: string)` / `specimenNameForCss(css: string)`. The `GradientInterval` import vanishes and the catalogue becomes a pure `@mkbabb/value.js/easing` consumer testable with string inputs. Lattice: `easing/specimens.ts` (catalogue + painter, value.js/easing its only import), `composables/useGradientEasing.ts` (interval ↔ specimen identity), the two SFCs presentation-only.

defects.defect: `isStepsInterval` accepts a state its own module forbids — a masking dual-truth in three tokens.
defects.evidence: `easingCatalogue.ts:207-209` `return interval.mode === "steps" || interval.css.startsWith("steps(")`. The module's stated law is that `css` is "the persisted TRUTH" (`:43`) and that `mode` is minted FROM it (`stepsTile`, `:139-153`, sets both from one source).
defects.mechanism: A masking fallback (edict 2): the `||` papers over a `mode`/`css` disagreement instead of forbidding it, so a model bug would present as correct behaviour here.
defects.reproduction: NONE — no input currently produces the divergent state, because `stepsTile` sets both fields from one source. Hypothesis-shaped by construction; the code path is unreachable-or-masking, which is the finding.
defects.proposedCure: `return interval.css.startsWith("steps(")`. If `mode` can genuinely diverge from `css`, the model carries two truths for one fact — and that is the finding to fix in `useGradientModel`, not here.

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` hand-mirrors `package.json#exports` and has drifted — 3 phantom entries, 2 real exports omitted — and the block is inert besides, because TS self-reference already resolves every subpath through the exports map.
defects.evidence: Measured set diff: `exports: ./color ./css ./easing ./math ./quantize ./transform ./value` vs `tsconfig: . ./color ./easing ./math ./parsing ./quantize ./transform ./units` → `ts-only: . ./parsing ./units`; `exp-only: ./css ./value` (and `./css` is used at 10 demo sites incl. `useGradientCSS.ts:25`). `dist/index.d.ts`, `dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts`, `dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` do not exist. `tsconfig.demo.json:38-41` calls it "a CLOSED 8-key set"; the map has 7 keys and no `.`. Resolver trace: `@mkbabb/value.js/css` → `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` with NO paths entry (Package ID `…@4.0.0`); `@mkbabb/value.js/parsing` → UNRESOLVED despite having one.
defects.mechanism: Two mirrors of one fact where `vite.config.ts:36-51` deliberately GENERATES its mirror to prevent exactly this. The hand-written one drifted and, because TS self-reference resolution already handles all seven subpaths, contributes nothing but drift surface.
defects.reproduction: `node -e '…compare package.json#exports to tsconfig.demo.json paths…'` prints the four sets. `node -e '…ts.resolveModuleName with traceResolution from demo/…/easingCatalogue.ts…'` prints the resolution table above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the value.js entries from `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` and let self-reference through `exports` do the work — one mirror, and the surviving one is generated. If an explicit map is wanted for build determinism, generate it the way vite generates its aliases.

defects.defect: The repository installs a registry copy of ITSELF into `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js` because keyframes.js declares `@mkbabb/value.js` as an exact-version `dependency` rather than a peer — a guaranteed two-build tree the moment this repo cuts 4.0.1.
defects.evidence: `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js` → `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js` with `@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 → @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0 → @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 deduped`. `keyframes.js` `dependencies: {"@mkbabb/value.js":"4.0.0"}` (exact, a dependency); glass-ui `peerDependencies: {"@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0"}` (correct). `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/` is a real directory with its own `dist/`, not a symlink (`realpathSync` stays inside `node_modules`); currently byte-identical (`diff dist/subpaths/easing.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/easing.d.ts` → identical).
defects.mechanism: Wrong dependency direction/kind in a producer: a library that composes value.js pins it exactly as a hard dependency, so npm materialises a second copy in every downstream tree — including value.js's own. INBOX O-7 §B proposes a 4.0.1 for the shipping parser P0, which would pin that copy at the stale version permanently.
defects.reproduction: `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js`; `node -e 'console.log(require("./node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js/package.json").dependencies)'`. No live divergence today (trees identical, and r1 proved the copy is out of the Vite graph) — the failure is conditional on a 4.0.1 cut.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to keyframes.js: move `@mkbabb/value.js` to `peerDependencies` at `^4.0.0`, as glass-ui already has it. One producer line; removes a whole class of two-instance failure from every downstream tree. Ride it on the same packet as the O-7 §B 4.0.1-vehicle decision.

defects.defect: The reveal watch allocates a fresh tuple per evaluation instead of using the idiomatic multi-source array form.
defects.evidence: `EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-51` `watch(() => [selectedId, visible] as const, () => {…}, { immediate: true })`.
defects.mechanism: Legibility only — the getter re-runs only when a tracked dep changes, so behaviour is correct. Vue 3.5's form for two independent sources is an array of getters.
defects.reproduction: NONE — no defect claimed; labelled a legibility observation.
defects.proposedCure: `watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], …, { immediate: true })`.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 2 / r2) of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue and the easing corpus
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context). Declared for this seat, not inherited.

defects.defect: All three `back`-family specimen tiles tear down the entire Gradient workbench on one click: their easing callables leave [0,1], the library returns err(color_progress_out_of_range) as a Result, and the demo seam demotes it to an uncaught throw inside a computed on the render path.
defects.evidence: Live probe at HEAD 80fc5c40 (probe-C2-radius-census.mjs §E): click ease-in-back / ease-out-back / ease-in-out-back → stripAlive:false, boundary "This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range Try again"; ease-out-circ immediately before is clean. Domain measured through each tile's own shipped payload (probe-C2-catalogue-domain.mjs): ease-in-back lo=-0.0969, ease-out-back hi=1.0868, ease-in-out-back lo=-0.0926 hi=1.0927; no other tile leaves [0,1]. Chain: src/color/operations.ts:65 (correct Result) → demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 throw → useGradientCSS.ts:207 throw → easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 inside a computed → easingCatalogue.ts:176-190 mints a tile for every preset with no domain check.
defects.mechanism: Domain contract violated across a module boundary, with a Result→throw demotion at the seam: the catalogue's codomain is R, the gradient sampler's domain is [0,1], and nothing reconciles them.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, easing row 1 open, click [data-specimen="ease-in-back"]. 3/3 tiles reproduce; `node probe-C2-radius-census.mjs` prints the boundary text.
defects.proposedCure: Make the ramp-progress domain total ONCE, where an eased t becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return or a rampProgress(fn,t) helper beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit it — an overshooting timing function on a two-endpoint interval MEANS hold-at-endpoint, so this is a domain law, not a masking fallback — then delete both demo throw sites, which become unreachable. Do NOT delete the back family: the producer picker still offers those curves and the strip's overshoot headroom is designed for them.

defects.defect: MT-F030 radius incoherence: five distinct radius registers (4 / 6 / 16 / 9999 px) inside one 197px easing card, and the house radius scale is silently clobbered by a glass-ui cascade-layer token collision that downshifts --radius-input from 10px to 4px.
defects.evidence: Measured census (probe-C2-radius-census.mjs §A): interval card rounded-card = 16px (462x197); ramp strip rounded-md = 6px; readout rail rounded-md = 6px; .rail-btn var(--radius-input) = 4px (24x24); .specimen-dot 9999px; specimen tile 9999px (45.2x43.8 ellipse); disclosed .glass-card 16px; picker control surfaces 9999px. Resolved :root tokens: --radius 0.25rem, --radius-lg 0.5rem while node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/radius.css declares `@theme { --radius: 0.625rem; --radius-lg: var(--radius) }` and dist/styles/components.css carries a bare `:root { --radius: 0.25rem; --radius-lg: 0.5rem; --radius-sm: 0.25rem }`; index.css:1 `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` and its tail `@import "./components.css" layer(components)` — components outranks theme, so the stock Tailwind scale wins. Declaration sites: GradientEasingEditor.vue:114,153,176,242,274. Live icon-button comparison on /#/gradient: dock-icon-button r=9999px 40x40, rail-btn r=4px 24x24 — glass's own icon idiom is `.glass-chip--icon{border-radius:var(--radius-pill)}` and --radius-control:9999px. Witness images: audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png and easing-card-3x-r2.png.
defects.mechanism: Design-system register consumed without a declared consumer-side ladder, compounded by a producer cascade-layer token collision: a compiled Tailwind bundle re-emits generic defaults into a higher layer than the semantic @theme scale it was built to replace.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingspecimenstrip/probe-C2-radius-census.mjs` against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (easing row 1 open) prints the census and the resolved token table.
defects.proposedCure: Split the disposition. (a) The layer collision is GLASS-OWNED — FOLD-BANK a new BH mark beside M3: components.css must not re-emit --radius* into the components layer (emit the theme defaults into `theme`, or drop the stock keys). Never re-declare --radius in demo/styles/ — that is a consumer patching a producer cascade, the MT-F014 masking fallback. (b) OURS: declare three named rungs for the corpus — --radius-card for the interval card, ONE in-card rung (--radius-md) shared by ramp, readout rail AND tile, --radius-pill for genuinely round things (the 10px dots) and for ghost icon controls so they match the dock — and retire the five ad-hoc call sites including the raw 9999px literal at GradientEasingEditor.vue:242 (GradientStopEditor.vue:318 already writes var(--radius-pill), so the corpus contradicts itself two files apart).

defects.defect: The glass Chip cell recipe and its pressed wash never paint: dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css is orphaned, so shape="cell" renders a 9999px ellipse with a pressed state byte-identical to the resting state, no coarse-pointer floor, and 11 of 27 labels breaking outside the painted chip.

defects.defect: FAMILY_ORDER is used as an allow-list rather than a sort key, so six of the thirty library bezier presets (quart x3, quint x3) are silently dropped from the catalogue; authoring one of them from the producer picker yields a byte-correct literal that the head then labels `custom` and the strip shows unpressed.

The module docblock at easingCatalogue.ts:15-17 asserts the opposite contract ('the tile catalogue IS value.js bezierPresets … never a second mint').
defects.mechanism: Enumeration expressed as an allow-list rather than a rank — a closed set standing in for an open one, so upstream growth silently shrinks the product with nothing failing.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../probe-C2-catalogue-domain.mjs` prints count 27 / hasQuart false / hasQuint false and the quart identity collapse. UI path: /#/gradient → easing row → 'Author a custom curve' → Easing preset → ease-in-quart → head reads `custom`, no tile pressed.
defects.proposedCure: Make FAMILY_ORDER a rank, never a filter: `const rank = (f) => { const i = FAMILY_ORDER.indexOf(f); return i < 0 ? FAMILY_ORDER.length : i; }` then sort all byFamily keys by rank then locale. familyLabelFor's /^ease-(in-out|in|out)-(.+)$/ is already general, so a new upstream preset can never vanish again with no edit.

defects.defect: For any steps interval whose live parameters departed the tile defaults, tileIdFor falls back to the generic `steps` tile — so a tile whose literal is steps(4, jump-end) renders PRESSED while the readout three pixels below says steps(7, jump-end), and because the press handler only emits on `on`, pressing that lit tile does nothing: there is no path back to the default staircase through the selection surface.

Module confirmation: tileIdFor({mode:"steps", css:"steps(7, jump-both)"}) → "steps" while SPECIMEN_TILES.find(id==="steps").css === "steps(4, jump-end)". Code: easingCatalogue.ts:219-223 (many-to-one fallback), EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:33-35 (`if (on) emit("select", tile)`), the component's own law at :7-8 ('pressed tile IS the interval's curve').

defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../probe-C2-steps-inert.mjs` against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Manual: press the `steps` tile, open 'Author a custom curve', arrow the Step count slider up, then press the still-lit `steps` tile — nothing happens.
defects.proposedCure: Make selection idempotent instead of one-way: `function onTileToggle(tile) { emit("select", tile) }` with the Chip's :model-value still controlled, so pressing a lit tile re-asserts its literal. That is exactly the radio semantics this 27-way single-select already wants (C-08), turns the family tile into a reset-to-family-default (the kf law's actual intent), and costs one boolean.

defects.defect: A 27-way single-select is shipped as 27 independent aria-pressed toggle buttons with no radio semantics, no roving tabindex and no arrow keys, sitting behind a focusable div with no role and no accessible name because the FadingScroll ariaLabel prop is never passed.

defects.defect: The keep-in-view watch source returns a fresh array literal on every evaluation, so Vue's hasChanged gate is always true and the change detection the getter is written to express is defeated.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-80 — `watch(() => [selectedId, visible] as const, …, { immediate: true })`. A new array is never Object.is-equal to its predecessor. Harmless today because the callback is idempotent and guards on `!visible || selectedId === null`.
defects.mechanism: Identity-compared reactive source allocated fresh per evaluation.
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-level; the over-fire has no observable effect while the callback stays side-effect free.
defects.proposedCure: Use the idiomatic multi-source form `watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], …)`, which compares element-wise and costs nothing.

defects.defect: Pass 1's intermittent keep-in-view failure did NOT reproduce in this pass — 3/3 selection-arm trials and the reveal arm all scrolled correctly; the flush:"pre" + nextTick race remains a code-level hazard only.
defects.evidence: probe-C2-catalogue-domain.mjs §3, three fresh-reload trials pressing step-end (~1044px off-port): [{before:0, after:1044, visible:true, readout:"steps(1, jump-end)"} x3] and §4 REVEAL ARM {scrollLeft:1044, visible:true}. Pass 1 (challenge-C-implementation.pass-1-2026-07-27.md, C-07) recorded one trial where scrollLeft stayed 0. The code reading stands: the watch is flush:"pre" and schedules its measurement with nextTick (:54), so the measurement can race the parent's patch and a pre-layout read computes dx = 0 and silently skips at :71.
defects.mechanism: Scheduler race between a pre-flush watcher's nextTick measurement and the parent's DOM patch — HYPOTHESIS, unreproduced.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a correction of a prior finding; the failure could not be reproduced in 3 trials.
defects.proposedCure: Cheap hardening regardless: `{ flush: "post" }` on the watch and delete the nextTick wrapper (one option added, one line removed), so the measurement always reads settled geometry rather than racing the scheduler.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries / ownership / dependency direction / public surface) under demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue

result.strongestDefect: R2-1 — the eased-ramp concept has no owner: value.js ships three `ease-*-back` presets whose eased output leaves [0,1] (src/easing.ts:62-64) and a `mixColors` that rejects progress outside [0,1]; the adapter between the two published capabilities belongs to nobody, so the demo implements it THREE times (useGradientCSS.ts:175, GradientVisualizer.vue:64, easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52) and all three violate the contract. The demo then catalogues the crashing presets as clickable tiles (easingCatalogue.ts:13,174). (4) Feature-internal data flow is correct: `useGradientModel()` is called exactly once (GradientVisualizer.vue:49); child editors receive state by props and emit upward. (5) Animations edict not engaged — <style scoped> :266-278 declares a paint stack only; no keyframes moved or deleted. defects.mechanism: Missing home for the easing->mix progress adapter between two correct-in-isolation published capabilities. No owner means N consumers mint N copies, and every copy inherits the same contract violation.

defects.proposedCure: Transposition, not a patch at the throw site. New `src/gradient/ramp.ts` published as `@mkbabb/value.js/gradient`: `sampleRamp(stops, spans, opts): Result<RampSample[], RampError>` and `rampColorAt(stops, spans, position, opts): Result<AnyColor, RampError>`, framework-free. `sampleRamp` owns and NAMES the one decision the demo has nowhere to put — what an eased t outside [0,1] means for a colour mix: `overshoot: "clamp"` (default, matching how browsers rasterise an overshooting native gradient) or `"extend"` (unclamped mix in the working space). All three demo copies then delete and become calls; the divergence in R2-7 becomes structurally impossible; and one fix serves every future consumer.

defects.defect: The two surviving sampling laws diverge by up to 24.3/255 sRGB units even on a SMOOTH easing, so the add-ghost misreports the rail beneath the cursor under any steep curve — not only stepped ones.
defects.evidence: Measured (<scratchpad>/divergence.mts, ease-in-expo = cubic-bezier(0.95,0.05,0.795,0.035), sweep 0->100% at 0.25%): WORST {"pos":97.75,"d":24.31,"comp":"oklch(66.088% 0.1767 251.94deg)","rail":"rgb(18.7 148.5 248.8)"} where d is Euclidean sRGB distance on the 0-255 scale. Cause: sampleCoalescedStops is discrete (COALESCE_RESOLUTION = 32, useGradientCSS.ts:42) and the browser lerps linearly between sub-stops in sRGB, while colorAtPosition (GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88) is continuous in oklch. GradientVisualizer.vue:59-63 documents colorAtPosition as feeding 'the stop editor's add ghost AND the color a bar-click mints'.
defects.mechanism: Two expressions of one law (model->samples[] vs position->colour) with no shared primitive, so their discretisation choices differ silently.
defects.reproduction: `node_modules/.bin/vite-node <scratchpad>/divergence.mts`. In the app: set an interval to a steep easing (ease-in-expo) and hover the rail near 98%.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by R2-1: make rampColorAt the primitive and define sampleRamp as positions.map(p => rampColorAt(..., p)). One law, literally — the divergence cannot exist.
