result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (round 2) on demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context seat). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: R2-N5 / C-1 — typing any empty-argument CSS function (oklch(), rgb(), hsl(), lab(), color(), color-mix(), light-dark(), device-cmyk(), hwb(), lch(), oklab(), rgba(), hsla(), and calc() through the POSITION/ANGLE path) into the Gradient CSS editor destroys the entire gradient pane and every unsaved stop, position, easing curve and setting. The component consumes partial parsers (parseCssColor/parseCssScalar) at a total-oracle contract and its declared model-or-reject boundary (applyCSS) is not total, so the TypeError escapes the debounced keystroke handler into the pane error boundary. Confirmed live from a clean load; the rejection surface the whole design exists to feed never fires (`"verdict": null`). The shipped default editor content is two oklch(...) calls — deleting the numbers inside either one is the gesture.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative proofs recorded inside the report for four specific hypotheses that did NOT hold: (1) colorAtPosition's `No gradient interval contains` throw is unreachable — brute-forced 11^4 four-stop position states x 201 hover positions, no throw; (2) the drag path is sub-frame — p50 8.3ms / p95 9.4ms / max 32.8ms over 60 steps, and the redundant double `update:position` dispatch is batched by Vue (12 pointermoves -> 12 style mutations), so it is redundancy not perf; (3) the handles' 24px hit inflation genuinely works — elementFromPoint at centre+11px returns HANDLE, +13px returns the rail, computed ::before is 24x24 with pointer-events auto, so WCAG 2.5.8 is MET and the visual REPORT's two 20x20 rows are measurement artifacts; (4) the direction slider's 0px/opacity-0 thumb is glass-ui 7's intended `standard` variant and is fully keyboard-operable (aria-valuenow 90->135), not a defect.)

defects.defect: C-1's crash class is wider than the colour slot: parseCssScalar — the oracle for STOP POSITIONS (gradientParse.ts:111-118) and the DIRECTION preamble (gradientParse.ts:96-108) — also throws, on `calc()`. So `linear-gradient(90deg, red calc(), blue)` and `linear-gradient(calc(), red, blue)` destroy the pane from tokens that are not colours at all. A try/catch around isColorToken would leave two live doors open.

Try again"}. Screenshot evidence/challenge-C-r2-pane-destroyed-oklch.png. Chain: GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 -> useGradientModel.ts:158-168 -> gradientParse.ts:191 -> :92-94/:111-118/:96-108.
defects.mechanism: partial function consumed at a total-function contract; no Result boundary at the one place the type already promises totality

Pane is replaced by a 'Try again' card and the whole gradient is lost. defects.proposedCure: Two moves, in order. (1) Upstream — make parseCssColor/parseCssScalar TOTAL (Result, never throw); that is the V·π mini-tranche's whole purpose and kills the class everywhere. (2) Locally and independently — make `applyCSS` actually total: its declared type GradientParseResult already promises model-or-reject, so map any thrown library fault to `{ ok:false, reason }` at that ONE boundary and let the existing parseVerdict surface do the job it was built for. Do NOT sprinkle try/catch at the three oracle call sites — that is a patch and it misses the position/angle doors.

defects.defect: A CANCELLED pointer gesture commits the add. `onBarPointerUp` is bound to both @pointerup and @pointercancel and is the handler that emits `add`. pointercancel means the platform abandoned the gesture (second touch, system gesture, OS interrupt) — committing on it is the inverse of the contract. Same conflation on the handle (@pointercancel -> onHandlePointerUp) runs the re-tap-to-deselect branch on a cancelled press.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:207-208 (@pointerup + @pointercancel both -> onBarPointerUp) and :101-110 (the emit('add')); handle at :267-268. Live probe output: `A) handles at rest: 2` / `B) handles after pointerdown → POINTERCANCEL on the bar: 3` / `B) labels: ["Gradient stop at 0%","Gradient stop at 40%","Gradient stop at 100%"]`
defects.mechanism: one handler serving two events with opposite semantics; the tidy-looking reuse ('both end the gesture') erases the only distinction that matters
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-pointercancel.mjs` — touch-enabled context, dispatch pointerdown at 40% of the rail then pointercancel at the same point, no pointerup. Handle count goes 2 -> 3.

defects.defect: CORRECTION retiring round-1's C-8 (MAJOR). The Copy CSS control is NOT nameless and is NOT 'the route's one nameless button'. defects.defect: Every successful parse re-mints every stop id, so `:key="stop.id"` destroys and rebuilds all handle DOM nodes each debounced parse (every 500ms while typing), and `selectedStopId` becomes an id that no longer exists — the selection and its remove chip vanish with no signal. Two independent uid() minters share one `stop-N-<base36 ms>` namespace (useGradientModel.ts:66-69 and gradientParse.ts:31-34), a duplicated 4-line function across two modules.
defects.evidence: `B) handle node identity after an arrow-key nudge: ["T0","T1","T2"]` (stable) vs `C) handle node identity after ONE successful parse: ["NEW","NEW","NEW"]`; `C) stop ids before: ["stop-1-ms4sdf9g","stop-3-ms4sdiq0","stop-2-ms4sdf9g"]` -> `after: ["stop-1-ms4sdlez","stop-2-ms4sdlez","stop-3-ms4sdlez"]`; `C) remove-chip after parse (selection survived?): 0` (was 1). Sources: gradientParse.ts:252-257, GradientStopEditor.vue:231, :67-69, :263.
defects.mechanism: identity minted at parse time instead of reconciled, so a textually-identical model is a wholly new model to Vue's keyed diff
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-identity-churn.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: applyCSS reconciles instead of replacing: a parsed stop whose (cssColor, position) matches an existing stop keeps that stop's id. The rail then keeps its DOM, the selection survives, transitions do not restart, and the collision hazard collapses because one minter serves one namespace.

defects.defect: Unconditional coalescing: sampleCoalescedStops always emits ~32 sub-stops at IEEE-noise precision even when every interval's easing is the IDENTITY cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1) — the seeded default, and the state the parser re-seeds after every successful parse. For identity easing the browser's own interpolation is identical, so all 32 sub-stops are redundant. 2115 bytes where 74 suffice (28.6x), recomputed for the rail AND the tile AND every clipboard copy, with 12 significant decimals per channel.
defects.evidence: At rest, on load, no user edits: `EDITOR SHOWS (len 74): linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` vs `CLIPBOARD GOT (len 2115): linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% 0.15 145deg) 0.00%, oklch(74.687500147402% 0.150937499558 148.749998231174deg) 3.13%, …`. Sources: useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 (sampler), :53-62 (identity seed), gradientParse.ts:295-298 (re-seed).
defects.mechanism: a sampling law applied unconditionally, blind to the case where the sampled function is the identity
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-clipboard-divergence.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: (a) When every interval is the identity easing, serialize the raw stops — no coalescing (this also cures round-trip fidelity of the default state). (b) Round channels once, in the gradient consumer of colorToCss, to a display-honest 4-6 significant figures instead of presenting floating-point noise as authored CSS.

defects.defect: The 'owned paint stack' material contract is copy-pasted into two components: .gradient-rail and .gradient-render-tile carry the identical six-declaration recipe (background layer over --alpha-checker / background-origin / -clip / -repeat / -size / box-shadow). The visualizer's own comment concedes it ('the rail's material contract, same shape'). A contract asserted twice in two files is not a contract — the next edit to one is a silent divergence. Per owner edicts 4 and 5 this is a glass-ui primitive, not two scoped blocks in demo components.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326 vs GradientVisualizer.vue:271-278 (identical declarations); the concession is at GradientVisualizer.vue:267-270.
defects.mechanism: a design-system primitive expressed as duplicated per-component scoped CSS
defects.reproduction: NONE — static read; diff the two scoped blocks.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox (standing formation invariant) and land an alpha-honest surface primitive in glass-ui that paints an arbitrary layer over the checker ground; both call sites consume the one primitive.

defects.defect: Two silent-drop / misleading-reason cases that violate the parser module's own stated doctrine ('Silent-drop is forbidden (P2-17) -> explicit reject', gradientParse.ts:175-176). Out-of-range stop positions are silently clamped rather than rejected, and spec-valid CSS Color 4 `<color-interpolation-method>` syntax is rejected with a reason that blames a keyword for being a bad colour.
defects.evidence: `linear-gradient(90deg, red -50%, blue 300%) → OK dir=90 stops=red@0,blue@100` (clamp at gradientParse.ts:281-283); `linear-gradient(in oklch, red, blue) → reject: unparseable color "in"`. The model HAS an interpolationSpace; it is simply not wired to the gradient's own `in <space>` syntax.
defects.mechanism: a normalization step (clamp) placed after the validation boundary, and a token vocabulary narrower than the syntax the component itself emits colours in
defects.reproduction: `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-model-probe.ts` (section R6)
defects.proposedCure: Reject out-of-range positions with the named token instead of clamping (the doctrine the module already states), and wire `in <space>` to the existing interpolationSpace so the round-trip covers the syntax the app's own colour space selector implies.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration and the served tier matches it; the seat is declared, not inherited. No undeclared-seat defect.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the panel headed `CSS` is not the gradient's CSS. `GradientVisualizer.vue:259` feeds the code editor `simpleCSS` (raw stops, easing NOT baked in) while `:224` paints the tile and `:128` writes the clipboard from `coalescedCSS` (32 eased sub-stops). Measured live: selecting the `in-out` easing specimen moves the tile's 3.13% sample from `oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75)` to `oklch(0.749813 0.150056 145.225)` while the editor text stays byte-identical at `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` (editorStops 2 vs tileStops 33). The Easing region is the component's largest (49.8% of its height) and everything authored there is silently discarded by the only string a user can read or select-and-paste.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negative results (positive evidence, §8 of the report): (a) `/#/gradient` is mechanically clean in all four Safari matrices — `overflowX 0`, `main 1`, `pageErr 0`, `consoleErr 0`, `hasDarkClass` true in both dark matrices (REPORT.md:125,140,155,170); (b) 200% zoom passes — at 720px CSS width the three Select value boxes measure 108px with 43–50px of ink, `clipped 0`, and shots/zoom-200-desktop/gradient.png shows an intact composition; (c) the tile does honestly repaint per type — three live probes returned three genuinely different strings (`linear-gradient(90deg,…)`, `radial-gradient(oklch(…) 0%…)`, `conic-gradient(from 90deg,…)`), so `coalescedCSS` reaches the paint; the defect is the frame and the label, not a stale binding; (d) all three Selects carry explicit `aria-label`s (`Gradient type` / `Interpolation space` / `Hue interpolation`) — the route's single nameless button is the Copy control and only that; (e) the component authors zero motion, animates no layout-forcing property, and its 49 baseline subtree transitions are all producer-owned and tokenized; (f) `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean — every type-only import uses `import type`; (g) the one sampling law (`colorAtPosition`, :64-88) genuinely feeds the add-ghost, the minted stop colour and the tile from the same easing resolver.

defects.defect: The panel headed `CSS` is not the gradient's CSS: two serializers feed three surfaces, so everything authored in the Easing region (the component's largest, 49.8% of its height) is discarded by the only string the user can read and paste, while Copy emits a 33-stop string the user has never seen.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:259 (`:model-value="simpleCSS"`), :224 (`'--tile-render': coalescedCSS`), :128 (`writeClipboard(coalescedCSS.value)`). Live Chromium 1440x900, pasted: BEFORE easingLiterals ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"] tileStops 33 tileBgHead "…oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 3.13%…" editorText "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)" editorStops 2 → AFTER-EASE easingLiterals ["cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)"] tileBgHead "…oklch(0.749813 0.150056 145.225) 3.13%…" editorText BYTE-IDENTICAL editorStops 2.
defects.mechanism: F1 — two serializers, one gradient. `serializeGradient` (raw, un-eased) and `serializeCoalescedGradient` (32 eased sub-stops, COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32) in useGradientCSS.ts; they agree only while every interval is `linear`, and no surface labels which one it shows.
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; read tile computed background-image and the code editor text; click the `in-out` easing specimen tile; re-read both. Tile sample at 3.13% changes, editor text does not.
defects.proposedCure: One gradient, one serialization on screen. The editor shows the render truth and Copy copies exactly the bytes under the caret. If the compact authored form is worth keeping it becomes a named, visible representation toggle in the same well (producer `SegmentedTabs`, `Compact ⇄ Expanded`). Delete `simpleCSS` as an unlabelled parallel path — a second serializer no surface names is a dual path (owner edict 2).

defects.defect: At both named narrow evidence arms the three primary semantic selectors of the instrument clip mid-word to unreadable; at 320px the value box is four CSS pixels wide.

A fixed 3-up with no responsive step shares its row with a fixed-width fixture; the only responsive token in the band is on the tile, the one element that did not need one. :159-161 records that the per-select *subtitle* rows were excised for truncating — the cure was applied to the symptom's neighbour while the value itself still truncates.

defects.defect: The render tile has no proportion of its own — its block size is a residue of neighbouring label line-boxes — so the Type option's own promise of a "Center-outward circle" renders as an ellipse whose eccentricity changes with the viewport.

PROPORTION-AUDIT §1: every element earns its scale from its job relative to the local protagonist.

defects.defect: The Direction slider stays live, focusable and identically labelled for `radial`, where it controls nothing, and silently changes meaning to "start angle" for `conic` — one label, three semantics, one of them null, with no disabled affordance and no announcement.

Live with type=radial: `sliderDisabled { ariaDisabled: null, dataDisabled: null, tabIndex: 0, pointerEvents: "auto", opacity: "1" }`, tileBg `radial-gradient(oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0% …` with no angle. Also measured `aria-valuetext: null`, `aria-valuenow: "90"` — the unit is never announced.
defects.mechanism: F7 — states that were never drawn. A type-agnostic axis over a type-dependent CSS grammar.

defects.proposedCure: The control is type-conditional, not type-agnostic: `linear` → "Angle"; `conic` → "Start angle"; `radial` → replaced by the parameters radial actually has (shape, extent). A single Direction slider across all three types is the wrong model, not a slider that needs a disabled skin. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: disabled states are never color-only — here the state is not expressed at all.

defects.defect: Three consumer-authored `<hr>` dividers where the tranche's binding register says every non-Admin composition retains zero, each one immediately followed by an `<h3>` that already declares the boundary.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 restates it; §5 card-law 4: "Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative." PR-14 rules the identical About pathology 7→0.
defects.mechanism: F4 — consumer-authored boundaries; the boundary is stated twice, once by material/heading and once by line.
defects.reproduction: `document.querySelectorAll('main hr').length` on /#/gradient → 3.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three; section rhythm plus the heading own the grouping. If a boundary is ever genuinely needed it is `InstrumentChassis`'s typed boundary set (`{stage-inspector, inspector-action}`), not a consumer `<hr>` — and glass-ui 7.0.0 ships `./separator` if a line is ever ruled legitimate.

defects.defect: The three section headings are rendered in Fraunces `text-subheading` — the palette-identity jurisdiction — instead of Plus Jakarta `text-heading`, and are simultaneously the largest non-title type in the pane and painted in the de-emphasis colour.

PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.13 restates it.

defects.defect: The four control labels (TYPE / SPACE / HUE / DIRECTION) are rendered in Fira Code — the closed matrix's value/code/provenance family — uppercased and letterspaced, which also inflates them in the one band with no width to spare.

Sites :163, :180, :197, :229. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: "control or label, including dropdown options → `text-small` → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold."

defects.defect: The Copy CSS control is simultaneously (a) the route's only nameless button in every Safari matrix, (b) a Dock control species planted in a pane body, and (c) the second seat for a command the Dock action set already owns.
defects.evidence: (a) Using the audit's own predicate verbatim (audit/visual/capture.mjs:102-105 — aria-label || aria-labelledby || textContent; `title` not counted), five engine/viewport runs (chromium-1440, chromium-320, chromium-prm-1440, webkit-1440, webkit-390) each return exactly one nameless visible button: `{cls: "dock-icon-button glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover dock-icon-button--compact", title: "Copy CSS", inPane: true}` = GradientVisualizer.vue:254-256. That is REPORT.md:100,107,111,113 `namelessButtons: 1` on /#/gradient in all four matrices including both mobile ones, where the Dock contributes zero. (b) :13 `import { DockControl } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"`. (c) usePaneRouter.ts:209 registers `{key:"copy", icon: Copy, title:"Copy CSS", handler: () => paneRefs.gradient.value?.copyCSS?.()}`, reached via this file's own `defineExpose` at :131.

defects.defect: Copy has no confirmation and no failure state: a rejected clipboard permission, an insecure context or a NotAllowedError produces an unhandled rejection and a UI indistinguishable from success.

defects.mechanism: F6 — one command with no durable result.
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis by code read — I did not deny clipboard permission in a live run). The absent error path is visible at :127-129.
defects.proposedCure: The action region owns one durable result region for the whole instrument; `copyCSS` returns a result the region renders. Not a toast and not a tooltip — PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.6, "Subtraction precedes explanation."

defects.defect: Protagonist inversion: the support fixture carries a byte-identical shadow to the declared protagonist, out-masses it 3.21x on the block axis, and occupies 66.8% of its area.

defects.defect: Five design-system boundary breaches in one 279-line file: select, slider, divider, label/field couple and numeric entry are all hand-rolled or taken from demo/ui while glass-ui 7.0.0 ships a producer primitive for each — and the one glass-ui import the file does make is the Dock's control species, planted in a pane body.

GradientVisualizer.vue:9 `from "../../../ui/select"`; :10 `from "../../../ui/slider"`; :148,:240,:251 raw `<hr class="border-border">`; `<span class="section-label">` + control hand-rolled 4x; no numeric entry for Direction; :13 `import { DockControl } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"` rendering live as `dock-icon-button glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover dock-icon-button--compact`. defects.defect: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the component's surfaces gain transitions rather than losing them: transitioning elements in the visualizer subtree rise 49 → 250 and the render tile acquires a 0.1s colour transition, where the global guard declares 0.01ms !important.
defects.evidence: Measured chromium 1440 without PRM: tile `transitionProperty "all"`, `duration "0s"`, 49 transitioning elements in the subtree. With `reducedMotion: "reduce"` (matchMedia matches true): tile `transitionProperty "opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow"`, `duration "0.1s"`, 250 transitioning elements. demo/styles/animations.css:184-191 declares `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*, *::before, *::after` for that exact query — the rendered value is 10,000x larger. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state." This also CORRECTS pass 1's negative result, which inferred PRM compliance from STATES.json `rafPer1500ms: 0` (a RAF measurement, not a CSS one).
defects.mechanism: F7 — states that were never drawn. The winning declaration is unidentified: my CSSOM walk returned `hits: []` and no source file in demo/ or glass-ui declares that property list under a reduce query. THE MECHANISM IS A LABELLED HYPOTHESIS; the measurement is not.
defects.reproduction: Launch a Playwright context with `reducedMotion: "reduce"` at /#/gradient; count elements in the visualizer subtree with transitionDuration !== "0s", and read the render tile's computed transitionProperty/transitionDuration. 250 and "0.1s".
defects.proposedCure: Cure at the global root (owner edict 5), not per-instance: establish why the universal guard is being outranked and replace the blunt `*` !important with a layered, deliberate reduced-motion register. The component authors no motion of its own and has no local remedy.

defects.defect: Forced-colors is entirely unhandled in this file — for a component whose whole information payload is `background-image` — and the tranche's forced-colors capture is void, so the state is unproven rather than passing.

defects.defect: `seedFromPalette` is a named Dock action with a hard-coded selection model and three silent no-op paths: it always takes savedPalettes[0], never asks which, and does nothing at all when there is no port, no palette, or fewer than two colours.

Advertised at usePaneRouter.ts:210 as `{key:"seed", icon: Pipette, title:"Seed from palette", description:"Seed gradient stops from a saved palette."}`. defects.proposedCure: The command either has a subject or is not offered: absent a qualifying palette the action is disabled with a stated reason; when it fires it names which palette seeded. Palette choice belongs to the user, not to index 0.

defects.defect: The render tile's accessible name is a single constant string across every state it exists to communicate, so its entire non-visual content is identical for 3 gradient types x 361 angles.

defects.defect: In RTL the Direction label/value pair mirrors while the physically-anchored slider track correctly does not, so the word DIRECTION captions the track's maximum end and the live value captions its minimum end.

Source :228 `flex items-center justify-between` (logical) over a physical track. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2: "numeric/scientific sign never mirrors" — the track is right; the annotation is not.

defects.reproduction: Open shots/rtl-mobile/gradient.png (or set dir=rtl at /#/gradient, 390px) and compare the label/value positions against the fill's origin.
defects.proposedCure: Bind label, unit and value to the track's own start/end through the producer axis composition (E-4), which resolves the logical/physical conflict once instead of per-consumer.

defects.defect: At the component's default and reset state the render tile is a pixel-duplicate of the rail above it, so 28.4% of the mobile control width buys redundancy — and it earns its area only when type is not linear or direction is not 90/270.
defects.evidence: Measured tile background-image at default: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.746875 …` — while useGradientCSS.ts:258-262 states the rail "ALWAYS paints this — at every type/direction". resetGradient (:118-125) restores exactly that state. Tile + gap = 92px of a 324px content box at 390. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2 / PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-04: redundant/absent support collapses.
defects.mechanism: F2 — the right-rail render tile. The file's own comments admit the split (:214-218 "the honest surface"; useGradientCSS.ts:258-262 "normalized to 90° for editing").
defects.reproduction: At /#/gradient default state, read the rail's and the tile's computed background-image → the same 32-substop 90deg ramp.
defects.proposedCure: THE GESTALT TRANSPOSITION: one gradient, one specimen, one serialization. The meniscus rail becomes the render (type + direction applied) with stop handles riding an explicit normalized axis track beneath it; failing that, the render becomes a full-inline-width specimen band at the top of the Interpolation section where it can own an aspect-ratio and costs the controls nothing. Either way the right-rail fixture dies and D-2, D-3, D-11, D-13, D-14, E-1, E-2, E-3, E-4 and E-7 close together.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-18 — three of the twenty-seven tiles this component offers as one-click choices (`ease-in-back`, `ease-out-back`, `ease-in-out-back`) destroy the entire `/#/gradient` route into the app error boundary. Two steps from a cold load, no console error, 100% reproducible, and invisible to the shipped 60-capture harness because nothing in it presses a control. The design designed the overshoot PORTRAIT (docblock lines 172-176 name the back family by name and reason about drawing past the box) and never asked what happens when someone SELECTS it — a state half-designed and made fatal to press.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded as genuinely passing, all re-verified this pass: reduced motion is handled deliberately and correctly via `useMediaQuery` → `behavior:"auto"`; no motion property forces layout (only `scale` and scroll position); the docblock's own WCAG 1.4.11 claim that 65% ink clears 3:1 in both schemes is TRUE — measured 4.92:1 light / 3.39:1 dark; the refusal of `scrollIntoView` (lines 37-46) is exemplary and names the O-19 defect it prevents; `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean; Vue 3.5 idioms clean; no god module, no legacy shim, no wrapper component, no new shared/ dir; zero curve maths re-derived — every portrait samples the library callable through one painter and the minted literals are byte-mirrored against the picker's law.)

defects.defect: Selecting any of the three `back`-family specimen tiles destroys the whole /#/gradient route into the app ErrorBoundary. The catalogue is built by blind enumeration of `Object.keys(bezierPresets)` with no domain filter; the back presets' output escapes [0,1]; the row's ink derivation and the ramp sampler both feed that value into a colour mixer whose `progress` domain is closed, and the demo converts the library's honest `Result` into a `throw` inside a render-time `computed`.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-tile-crash-sweep.mjs (WebKit, fresh context per tile): before={rails:1,strips:1,tiles:27,rows:1,selected:["linear"]} → afterBackClick={rails:0,strips:0,tiles:0,rows:0}. 10-tile sweep: ease-out/ease-in-out-sine/steps/step-start/smooth-step-3/ease-in-expo/ease-out-circ survive; ease-in-back, ease-out-back, ease-in-out-back ALL → tryAgain:true, caught:[]. Frame frames/D2-CRASH-after-selecting-ease-out-back.png. Chain: easingCatalogue.ts:178 `for (const name of Object.keys(bezierPresets))` → src/easing.ts:62-64 the three back quads → measured fn(0.5): ease-in-back -0.063622, ease-out-back +1.067553, ease-in-out-back 0.606680 with range [-0.0927,1.0927] → useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 `interpolateStopColors(c0,c1,fn(0.5),…)` → useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 `if (!mixed.ok) throw new Error(...)` → src/color/operations.ts:90 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({code:"color_progress_out_of_range"})`. Independently corroborated by the CHALLENGE-C seat, challenge-C-implementation.md:74-76 (captured boundary string "Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range").
defects.mechanism: unguarded enumeration of a producer catalogue into a consumer with a closed numeric domain; a Result→throw conversion inside a render-time computed
defects.reproduction: Cold-load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (interval 1→2 opens by default, GradientEasingEditor.vue:61). Click [data-specimen="ease-out-back"]. The entire route is replaced by a bare "Try again" button. Repeat for ease-in-back and ease-in-out-back.
defects.proposedCure: Curate, do not enumerate. Make the curve-space→colour-space boundary ONE named projection: `SpecimenTile` declares its range, and the single site where an easing output becomes a mixer `progress` performs the declared domain projection — not a scattered Math.min and never a try/catch around the computed (that would be the MT-F014 masking fallback). Alternative honest cure: the back family is declared out-of-catalogue for colour intervals and the three tiles do not exist.

defects.defect: The radius register the owner marked (MT-F030 / OM-4): six boxes in one instrument carry five different radii, and rendered curvature (r ÷ min dimension) runs INVERSELY to box size — the two smallest boxes are full semicircles (0.500) and the largest is 0.082. Equal absolute radius is not equal curvature (ramp and rail both 6px read 0.300 vs 0.188). EasingSpecimenStrip.vue itself declares ZERO border-radius in 215 lines, so it has no radius governance at all. Critically, the pending glass fix does NOT cure this.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-radius-material-matrix.mjs radiusRegister at 1440px: chip tile 45.2×43.8 @9999px (0.500) · specimen dot 10×10 @9999px (0.500) · ramp 436×20 @6px (0.300) · readout rail 436×32 @6px (0.188) · rail button 24×24 @4px (0.167) · row plate 462×196 @16px (0.082). Declarations: `grep -rn "radius|rounded" demo/workbenches/gradient/` → EasingSpecimenStrip.vue 0 hits; GradientEasingEditor.vue:114 rounded-card(16px), :153 rounded-md(6px), :176 rounded-md(6px), :242 9999px hand-rolled, :274 var(--radius-input)=4px; EasingAuthoringStage.vue 0 hits. Tokens measured: --radius-card 1rem, --radius-md 6px, --radius-input 0.25rem(=4px), --radius-pill 9999px. demo/DESIGN.md §Radii says `rounded-pill/rounded-full — chips` (so the disc is 'correct' by the doc) and states --radius-input = 8px, which is DRIFT — live is 4px. Post-fix arithmetic: glass's orphaned `.glass-chip--cell{border-radius:var(--radius-card)}` gives 16/44 = 0.364, still the most-rounded box in the row and now the SAME absolute radius as the 462px plate.
defects.mechanism: no derivation law between nested radius registers; role tokens applied without size conditioning, so curvature is an accident of box aspect
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient, expand interval 1→2, run probe-D2-radius-material-matrix.mjs; read the radiusRegister block. Compare against docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png.
defects.proposedCure: Two halves. OURS: a radius DERIVATION law in the register (the gap DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:73 already names) — corner curvature holds constant or grows with box size, never inverts; nested registers derive from their parent. GLASS (ask, relayed with M3): `.glass-chip--cell` must derive its radius from the chip's own box or expose `--chip-cell-radius`; a fixed --radius-card rung cannot serve both a 44px tile and a 462px plate.

defects.defect: The seat per-instance-overrides four of the producer's five Chip cell-recipe declarations and never passes the `size` prop that already exists — an edict-5 violation (style at the root, never per-instance) whose direct consequence is the touch-target failure D-21.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js chipVariants: shape.cell = "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro"; size.md = "gap-1.5 px-3.5 py-1.5 text-small". Call site EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:98-102 passes mode+shape only, NO size (defaults md). Overrides: line 168 `padding: 0.3125rem 0.375rem 0.25rem` (5/6/4px vs producer 8/10px); line 167 `gap: 0.125rem` (2px vs 6px); line 195 `font-size: 0.5625rem` (9px vs the producer's text-micro, measured 11px on the chip root); line 169 `min-width: 2.75rem` added.
defects.mechanism: a needed size variant implemented as consumer CSS instead of consumed from (or asked of) the producer's size axis
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'padding\|gap\|font-size\|min-width' demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue lines 163-200; getComputedStyle on `.specimen-tile` → fontSize 11px (producer text-micro) while `.tile-label` → 9px.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all four overrides and pass `size="sm"`. If `sm` is still too large for a specimen grid, that is an ASK on glass for a specimen rung on the existing size axis — relayed through the same M3 channel — not a local shrink.

defects.defect: On coarse pointers the tiles miss the 44px target floor by 0.2px, and the producer rule that would have met it lives in the orphaned stylesheet — so the glass Chip residual has an accessibility consequence, not merely a cosmetic one.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-port-census.mjs at 390×844 isMobile/hasTouch: `mobile: { tileBox:{w:45.23,h:43.80}, coarsePointer:true, touchFloorMet:false }`. The unlanded rule, dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css: `@media (pointer: coarse){ .glass-chip--interactive{ min-inline-size: var(--touch-target,2.75rem); min-block-size: var(--touch-target,2.75rem) } }`; measured --touch-target = 2.75rem = 44px. Invisible to the shipped harness: capture.mjs:98 filters `m.w < 24 || m.h < 24`, and REPORT.json's six /#/gradient smallTapTargets are the three 22×22 dock slug controls, two 20×20 stop seats and one 160×23 input — none is this component.
defects.mechanism: an orphaned producer stylesheet drops the coarse-pointer minimum; the seat's local padding shrink (D-20) put the box within 0.2px of the line
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2-port-census.mjs (mobile matrix) → touchFloorMet:false, h=43.80.
defects.proposedCure: FOLD-BANK on glass with M3 — and upgrade the M3 row from 'visual residual' to 'visual + a11y residual' with this measurement attached. Do NOT add a local min-height: that is the masking fallback. The ours-half is D-20 (stop shrinking the producer recipe).

defects.defect: The family eyebrow carries the entire information architecture of the strip and fails four ways at once: 9px (18% below the smallest rung the system defines), 2.77:1 light / 2.94:1 dark contrast (WCAG 1.4.3 fail in both schemes), aria-hidden with no accessible substitute, and off-port 75–88% of the time with no sticky behaviour.
defects.evidence: Measured font-size 9px (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:149) vs glass's smallest rung --type-micro: 0.6875rem = 11px (dist/styles/typography/scale.css). probe-D2-rendered-contrast.mjs (DPR-3 screenshot decode, extreme-luminance pixel pair): eyebrow 2.77:1 light, 2.94:1 dark — caused by `opacity: 0.75` (line 153) multiplying an already-de-emphasised --muted-foreground. aria-hidden="true" at line 96. probe-D2-port-census.mjs: desktop 1440 portW 436 / contentW 1482 = 3.40× → 2 of 8 families fully visible, 8/27 tiles; mobile 390 portW 298 = 4.97× → 1 of 8 families, 5/27 tiles; zoom-200 unchanged (436/1482). frames/D2-scroll-end-back-steps.png shows leftmost visible tiles with no eyebrow at all; shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png shows an eyebrow sliced mid-word to "ad" (from "quad").
defects.mechanism: the sole grouping carrier implemented as a decorative, doubly-attenuated, off-ladder, non-sticky label
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2-rendered-contrast.mjs → eyebrow ratios; node probe-D2-port-census.mjs → famsFullyVisible 2/8 desktop, 1/8 mobile; scroll the strip to any non-zero offset and read which family the visible tiles belong to.
defects.proposedCure: The eyebrow becomes a real `aria-label` on a per-family `role="group"`, takes `text-micro` with the opacity multiplier deleted (de-emphasis by ink token, never by opacity — which also breaks forced colors), and sticks to the port's inline start while its family is in view. If the strip survives pass-1 D-01 at all.

defects.defect: The strip is instantiated once per interval inside the accordion's v-for, so a module-level constant catalogue is duplicated into display:none twins of a surface that can never be seen — 134 elements, 42.5% of the route's entire main subtree, per hidden row.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-dom-mass.mjs at one interval: routeElements(main *) 315, stripElements 134, easingCardElements 194, svgPaths in strip 27 (49 points each). defects.defect: Dock-scoped primitives in a plate with no dock, and `compact` opts out of the one out-of-dock guarantee glass-ui actually ships. Three `<DockControl compact>` + `DockSeparator` render inside `.mix-plate`, which has no `.glass-dock` ancestor. glass-ui's touch-floor rule is written `.dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *))` — non-compact, outside a dock → 44px floor; in-dock is covered by the dock's own coarse block. Compact + outside a dock is the single uncovered quadrant and is exactly what this component instantiates: 20px glyph + 2×4px padding = 28×28px. Secondarily the three buttons carry `title=` and no `aria-label`, using a register the demo itself declares retired.

This is the SAME MECHANISM as round 1's BLOCKER (`tag="button"` on a `WatercolorDot` with no `tag` prop): the glass-ui 7.0.0 whole-adoption at W44/D58 moved the dependency version but never the consumer prop surface, and nothing in the toolchain can see a renamed producer prop. That makes it a family, not an incident — the cure is structural (`inheritAttrs: false` on glass-ui primitives, or a demo lint rule seeded from the producer `.d.ts`), not two prop edits.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. But the sound half is recorded as evidence in §10 of the report, because it constrains the cure: (1) the value.js import at MixConfigBar.vue:12 (`type HueInterpolationMethod` from `@mkbabb/value.js/color`) is one a real consumer could write verbatim — measured `import.meta.resolve` → OK, `dist/subpaths/color.js`, backed by `src/subpaths/color.ts:7`; (2) ZERO deep-`src/` reaches anywhere in demo/ (the 4 grep hits are prose comments naming other repos); (3) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — all 4 type-only imports are `import type`; (4) idiomatic Vue 3.5 — reactive props destructure with default at :25-45, typed defineEmits, lazy computeds, no defineModel stale-read hazard; (5) zero styling contraband — no `<style scoped>`, no `:deep()`, no numeric z-literals, `.section-label`/`.text-micro` both glass-ui-owned; (6) the component contributes NONE of /#/mix's a11y defects — the route's 8 small tap targets are dock slug buttons (22×22) and picker channel rails (12×24), its 1 nameless button is `send-btn` measured OUTSIDE `<main>`, while this component's own controls measure 227×36 and 462×40, all accessibly named; (7) /#/mix is clean on every hard signal in all 4 Safari matrices (REPORT.md:123,138,153,168 — overflowX 0, main 1, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0). The through-line: every automated instrument this repo owns is green, and two of its most load-bearing statements about the world (the Button register, the published-surface path map) are false.

defects.proposedCure: Three moves, structural over patch. (1) Audit the WHOLE consumer surface against the published 7.0.0 .d.ts set — every `<GlassComponent prop=…>` in demo/ where prop ∉ Props is dead; mechanisable from the declaration files. (2) Migrate at the root, all 51 sites, no adapter/shim (edict 2): here `<Button emphasis="primary">`; fleet-wide outline→emphasis="secondary", ghost→emphasis="quiet", destructive→tone="danger". `primary-audacious` is not a 7.0.0 value — RELAY to the glass-ui BH inbox (standing fond): if "audacious" is a real design rung it is a producer emphasis/tone member; if not it dies. (3) Close the mechanism: `inheritAttrs: false` + an explicit attrs allowlist on glass-ui primitives (relay), or a demo eslint rule seeded from the producer .d.ts making an undeclared prop on a @mkbabb/glass-ui component an error. Without (3) the next glass-ui major repeats this silently.

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` has drifted 5 keys from `package.json#exports`: 3 PHANTOM keys (`@mkbabb/value.js` bare root, `/parsing`, `/units`) that typecheck green but are runtime-fatal, and 2 REAL exports absent from the map (`/css`, `/value`) — `/css` being a direct dependency of this component. The T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone's guardrail is therefore a false proof of the public API. This CORRECTS round 1's own negative proof, which claimed the demo 'cannot drift from the published map'.
defects.evidence: MEASURED via real node exports resolution in this checkout: `node --input-type=module -e "…import.meta.resolve…"` → FAIL @mkbabb/value.js -> ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; OK @mkbabb/value.js/color -> file:///Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/color.js; OK @mkbabb/value.js/css -> …/dist/subpaths/css.js; FAIL @mkbabb/value.js/parsing -> ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; FAIL @mkbabb/value.js/units -> ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. package.json#exports = 7 keys {./color ./css ./easing ./math ./quantize ./transform ./value}. tsconfig.demo.json#paths = 8 keys {. /color /easing /math /parsing /quantize /transform /units}. tsconfig.demo.json's own comment claims 'the CLOSED 8-key set' and 'Mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map' — but vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES its 7 aliases from Object.entries(VALUE_JS_PKG.exports) while the tsconfig is hand-written. Demo actually imports 5 subpaths: `grep -rhoE '"@mkbabb/value\.js(/[a-z]+)?"' demo | sort | uniq -c` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize. /css is used at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:28 — a direct dep of MixConfigBar — with NO paths entry, proving the map is not the resolution authority it claims. Round 1 report §11 (challenge-L-library-round-1.md:494-502) asserts the opposite.
defects.mechanism: Two resolution authorities for one boundary: vite generates its alias set from package.json#exports (cannot drift); tsconfig hand-mirrors it (has drifted). A demo import a real consumer could not write typechecks green and dies only at bundle time.
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e "const specs=['@mkbabb/value.js','@mkbabb/value.js/color','@mkbabb/value.js/css','@mkbabb/value.js/parsing','@mkbabb/value.js/units']; for (const s of specs){ try { console.log('OK  ', s, await import.meta.resolve(s)) } catch(e){ console.log('FAIL', s, e.code) } }" — run from the repo root. Then diff against `grep -oE '"@mkbabb/value\.js[^"]*"' tsconfig.demo.json | sort` and `python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.load(open('package.json'))['exports']))"`. Currently LATENT: no demo file imports a phantom key today, so nothing is red — the guardrail is simply not load-bearing.
defects.proposedCure: KISS, and the move that makes the demo a genuine external consumer: DELETE the value.js `paths` block from tsconfig.demo.json entirely. `moduleResolution: bundler` honours `exports`, and node already resolves the self-package through the node_modules self-link (proved above). One authority — package.json#exports — for typecheck, vite, vitest and any real consumer alike. If a paths entry must survive for editor ergonomics, GENERATE tsconfig.paths.json from exports in a prebuild step exactly as vite.config.ts's valueJsSelfAlias does, so drift is structurally impossible rather than comment-asserted.

defects.defect: THREE independent hand-rolled N-color chain samplers exist in demo/, with three divergent off-by-one/joint conventions and two different error channels, because the library ships only the BINARY `mixColors` primitive. Round 1's L-2 named one of the three.
defects.evidence: (1) demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:68-85 — perSegment = max(2, ceil(k/segments)+1); `for (let j = i===0 ? 0 : 1; j < perSegment; j++)`; returns null on failure. (2) demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:180-214 (sampleCoalescedStops) — stepsPerInterval = max(2, round(COALESCE_RESOLUTION/(n-1))); `for (let j = 0; j <= (i < stops.length-2 ? stepsPerInterval-1 : stepsPerInterval); j++)` — a ternary on the loop BOUND; throws on failure. (3) demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:100-107 (pigmentRamp) — Array.from({length: RAMP_STOPS}, (_, i) => mixColors(from,to,i/(RAMP_STOPS-1),…)); throws. Two of the three live inside this component's own feature tree (demo/workbenches/mix/). Library surface: `grep -rn 'export function mixColors' src/` → src/color/operations.ts:83 only, and it is 2-color.
defects.mechanism: The library's public granularity sits one level below what every consumer actually writes. The demo is the dogfood; three copies of one loop is the specification for the missing operation.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'mixColors' demo | grep -v node_modules — enumerates 6 call sites across 5 modules; read the three loops named above and compare their joint/bound conventions and error channels side by side. No runtime failure is required: the defect is structural duplication with divergent semantics.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition into the library. Add to src/color/operations.ts, exported through src/subpaths/color.ts: `export function sampleColorRamp(colors: readonly AnyColor[], options: { space: SpaceId; hue: HueInterpolationMethod; count: number }): Result<AnyColor[], ColorIssue>` — one inclusive-chain contract, one joint-dedupe rule, one `count` that means count (kills L2-7), one Result error channel. Site (1) collapses to serialization, (2) becomes easing+position decoration over it, (3) becomes an sRGB projection over it. The operation moves under test/ where it can be property-tested. Composes with round 1's L-2 cure (promote `mixColorSequence` alongside).

defects.defect: `PickerSpace` is a bare rename of the library's `SpaceId` (17 members) with no narrowing, but the component's dropdown renders only the 9 rows of INTERPOLATION_SPACES. The prop `colorSpace: PickerSpace` therefore promises 8 states the component emits no SelectItem for, and that 17-wide type flows onward through useMixingState, MixAnimationCanvas, MixResultDisplay and mixStage.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:35 `export type PickerSpace = SpaceId;` — a pure alias (edict 2: no aliases). dist/subpaths/color.d.ts:103 `SpaceId = "rgb"|"hsl"|"hsv"|"hwb"|"lab"|"lch"|"oklab"|"oklch"|"xyz"|"kelvin"|"srgb-linear"|"display-p3"|"a98-rgb"|"prophoto-rgb"|"rec2020"|"ictcp"|"jzazbz"` — 17 members. demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26-36 INTERPOLATION_SPACES — 9 rows (oklch, oklab, lab, lch, hsl, hsv, hwb, rgb, xyz). Admitted-but-unrenderable, exactly 8: kelvin, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, ictcp, jzazbz. MixConfigBar.vue:33 types the prop PickerSpace; useMixingState.ts:44 `ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")`.
defects.mechanism: The type models the library's full space catalog while the UI models a curated interpolation subset; nothing links the two, so a state the type permits has no rendering.
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS for the runtime symptom. No live path sets an unlisted space (useMixingState.ts:44 seeds "oklab"; only MixConfigBar writes it), so a blank SelectValue trigger is unproven. The TYPE-MODELING defect is CONFIRMED by the measured 17-vs-9 membership count.
defects.proposedCure: Make the type the vocabulary's shadow, not the library union's rename: `export type InterpolationSpace = (typeof INTERPOLATION_SPACES)[number]["value"]` in color-space-meta.ts, typed on the prop, the emit, and useMixingState's ref. The 8 unrenderable states become unrepresentable. Retire `PickerSpace` in favour of the library's own `SpaceId` wherever the full 17 genuinely apply (the picker's space catalog) — a demo type that exists only to have a demo name is an edict-2 alias.

defects.defect: `HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS` is typed as a plain `HueInterpolationMeta[]` over a LIBRARY-OWNED union (`HueInterpolationMethod` from @mkbabb/value.js/color). There is no compile-time link in either direction, so value.js can ship a fifth hue arc and the demo compiles green while BOTH the Mix and Gradient hue dropdowns silently omit it.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:38 `export const HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS: HueInterpolationMeta[] = [ {value:"shorter"…}, {value:"longer"…}, {value:"increasing"…}, {value:"decreasing"…} ]` — 4 hand-listed rows. color-space-meta.ts:6 imports `type HueInterpolationMethod` from "@mkbabb/value.js/color" (dist/subpaths/color.d.ts re-exports it from ../color/index) — the demo does not own the union. Consumed at MixConfigBar.vue:18,69,129 and GradientVisualizer.vue:19-20,203. Contrast the correctly-policed shape 46 lines away in the same component: MixConfigBar.vue:85 `strategyLabels: Record<LeftoverStrategy,string>` IS exhaustive by construction.
defects.mechanism: Ownership direction was not considered when the vocabulary was authored. A library-owned union needs type→vocabulary exhaustiveness (Record); a demo-owned union needs vocabulary→type derivation (as const). Applying the plain-array shape to both leaves both unpoliced — the same seam L2-4 shows from the type side, and round 1's L-7 shows for the demo-owned case.
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS, contingent on an upstream library change. Demonstrable statically: adding a 5th member to `HueInterpolationMethod` in src/color/ and rebuilding produces zero demo diagnostics (`vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exit 0) while the dropdown still renders 4 rows. The structural absence of the link is CONFIRMED by reading color-space-meta.ts:38 against dist/subpaths/color.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Match the exhaustiveness mechanism to the ownership direction. LIBRARY-owned union → `const HUE_INTERPOLATION_META: Record<HueInterpolationMethod, {label: string; description: string}> = {…}` + `Object.entries` at the render site: a new library member then fails the build until the demo names it. DEMO-owned union (LeftoverStrategy, round 1 L-7) → `as const` array in the type's home + `type LeftoverStrategy = (typeof LEFTOVER_STRATEGIES)[number]["value"]`. Same treatment for INTERPOLATION_SPACES, whose members are SpaceIds — see L2-4.

defects.defect: Three `<label class="section-label">` captions carry no `for` attribute and wrap no control — they are dangling `<label>` elements that label nothing, wearing form semantics for a decorative caption. The accessible name is carried separately by `aria-label` on each SelectTrigger, so the element choice buys no association and risks a doubled announcement. The diverged twin renders the identical caption as `<span>`.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:98, :121, :145 use `<label class="section-label">`; `grep -n "for=" demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue` → no matches. MEASURED live at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: labels = [{"text":"Color space","hasFor":false,"wrapsControl":false,"ctrl":null},{"text":"Hue method","hasFor":false,"wrapsControl":false,"ctrl":null}] — `label.control === null` for both (the third is behind v-if="showLeftoverStrategy", absent in colors mode). Names live at MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147 as aria-label on the trigger. Twin: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue:180 and :195 use `<span class="section-label">` for the same caption. `.section-label` itself is correctly glass-ui-owned — node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css `@layer components { .section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground) } }`.
defects.mechanism: Two copies of one control (round 1 L-3) diverged in DOM semantics as well as feature set; neither copy has a rule for what element a caption is.
defects.reproduction: node playwright script: goto http://localhost:9000/#/mix, wait 2000ms, evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll("main label")].map(l => ({text: l.textContent.trim(), hasFor: l.hasAttribute("for"), wrapsControl: !!l.querySelector("input,select,textarea,button"), ctrl: l.control ? l.control.tagName : null}))` → both entries have ctrl: null.
defects.proposedCure: Fold into round 1 L-3's shared-component extraction (demo/color-session/InterpolationSelects.vue) and pick ONE answer applied at both former copies: either `<span class="section-label" :id>` + `aria-labelledby` on the SelectTrigger, retiring the now-duplicated `aria-label`; or plain `<span>` keeping the existing `aria-label`. Do not keep `<label>` without `for` — it is the wrong element for a caption that labels nothing.

defects.defect: `RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT = 16`, documented as 'the F6 sample count (≈16)' and 'the k samples distribute across the chain', never produces 16 stops — the arithmetic yields 17, 17, 19, 17, 21, 19, 22 for 2..8 operands. The vitest oracle re-derives the identical formula to build its expectation, so it is tautological on the count axis and can never catch drift.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:35-36 ("k — the F6 sample count (≈16)") and :50 ("the k samples distribute across the chain"); the loop at :68-85. MEASURED from the exact source arithmetic: `node -e "const k=16; for(let n=2;n<=8;n++){const segments=n-1; const perSegment=Math.max(2,Math.ceil(k/segments)+1); let stops=0; for(let i=0;i<segments;i++) for(let j=(i===0?0:1);j<perSegment;j++) stops++; console.log('operands='+n,'perSegment='+perSegment,'TOTAL stops='+stops);}"` → operands=2 →17, 3→17, 4→19, 5→17, 6→21, 7→19, 8→22. Oracle: test/preview-chips.test.ts:60 `const perSegment = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT / 1) + 1);` and :68 `Math.max(2, Math.ceil(RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT / 2) + 1); expect(stops).toHaveLength(perSegment * 2 - 1);` — the same expression as the code under test.
defects.mechanism: A constant named for a count that the algorithm treats as a per-segment seed, plus an oracle that computes its expectation the same way the implementation does — so the sampler ≡ library VALUE leg is real and good, while the COUNT leg proves nothing.
defects.reproduction: Run the node one-liner above (pure arithmetic transcribed from sample.ts:68-85, no runtime needed). Then read test/preview-chips.test.ts:60,68 to confirm the expectation is the same expression.
defects.proposedCure: Dies with L2-3: once `sampleColorRamp(colors, {space, hue, count})` lives in the library, `count` is a contract other consumers size buffers against and must mean count (distribute k samples across the whole chain, joints deduped, return exactly k). The oracle then asserts a literal expected length against the contract instead of re-deriving the implementation's formula.
