result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue (r2 pass; r1 preserved alongside)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-2 — the Mix verb is unreachable in the shipped app: the only add-color affordance renders as a non-interactive `aria-hidden` `<span>` (glass-ui 7 `WatercolorDot` has no `tag`/`as`/`asChild` prop and no default slot), so `selectedColors` can never reach 2 from a cold load, so `canMix` is false forever, so MixConfigBar's Button is permanently disabled AND `operandColors` is permanently `[]` — every T-17 preview chip is absent. Measured: `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]')` → null; `getByRole("button", {name:"Add current color to the mix"}).count()` → 0; two forced clicks on `.add-slot-ghost` → `{"mixDisabled":true,"dots":1}`; both Select menus open with `{"options":9,"chips":0}` / `{"options":4,"chips":0}`. The feature 60% of this file exists to host has never rendered for a user, and the single green O-14 leg is the one that asserts the chips are ABSENT.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but the following absences were checked and are real (recorded so they are evidence, not silence): (1) No hazard-class code in the file — all 173 lines read: zero `requestAnimationFrame` (no PRM-RAF exposure), zero `addEventListener`, zero observers, zero timers, zero lifecycle hooks, zero async/fetch/WebGL/canvas — nothing to leak or clean up. (2) No `defineModel` — explicit `defineProps` (:32) + `defineEmits` (:76), so the WritableComputedRef stale-read hazard cannot arise; the reactive props destructure at :25-45 is idiomatic Vue 3.5. (3) No `ValueUnit` construction, no `stableHue`, no direct `parseCssColor`, no reka slider. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — all four type-only imports (:12-15) use `import type`. (5) Degenerate operands do not crash or emit garbage: driven live through the offered spaces with `oklch(none none none)`, "", "   ", `currentColor`, `color-mix(...)`, `oklch(0.5 0.2 NaN)` → all null, no throw; `transparent`, `rgb(0 0 0 / 0)`, `#000`, `oklch(0 0 0)`, `oklch(0.5 0.2 400)`, `color(display-p3 1 1 1)` → 17 well-formed stops, no NaN/Infinity/undefined; achromatic pairs give 17 distinct stops in hsv/hwb/oklch, so the `Math.atan2(0,0)=0` hue-collapse hazard does not degenerate the ramps. (6) Stop count bounded: 2 operands → 17 stops, 9 operands → 17 stops. (7) "Costs nothing at rest" is TRUE — computeds are lazy and SelectContent unmounts closed; measured 0.72 ms (2 ops) / 1.03 ms (9 ops) per full 9-space map, sub-frame, only while a menu is open — perf is NOT a defect here. (8) REPORT.json all four matrices on /#/mix: consoleErrors [], pageErrors [], overflowX 0, main 1. (9) This component contributes ZERO to the /#/mix small-tap-target count — its controls measure 227x36, 462x40, option rows 221x49.5; all 8 reported rows belong to the picker sliders and the palette-name input. (10) The two PreviewRamp guards (`v-if` null-check + `stops.length >= 2`) leave no hole — the sampler cannot return a 1-element array.

defects.defect: `variant="primary-audacious"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7.0.0's Button. The pane's ONE verb renders at glass-ui's DEFAULT `data-emphasis="secondary"` (the `glass-wash glass-capsule` recipe) — exactly the wash tier the file's own comment at :158-161 forbids — and the dead prop leaks into the DOM as an invalid HTML attribute. The HARD demo typecheck is green because no `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates` exists anywhere, so unknown component attributes are never checked.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:162-170. glass-ui 7.0.0 ButtonProps = {emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class}, no `variant` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts); runtime default `emphasis: { default: "secondary" }` at dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:11. `grep -rl "primary-audacious" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches. LIVE DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: attrs = [data-slot="button", data-emphasis="secondary", data-tone="neutral", data-size="md", type="button", disabled="", class="button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display", variant="primary-audacious"], bg=oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686 / 0.52), opacity=0.5. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → EXIT=0. `grep -n vueCompilerOptions tsconfig*.json vite.config.ts package.json` → no output. Demo-wide: 51 Button `variant=` call sites vs 2 uses of the 7.0.0 `emphasis` API.
defects.mechanism: retired glass-ui-7 prop name still passed at a demo call site; Vue attribute fallthrough renders it silently inert; vue-tsc with strictTemplates off reports nothing
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-two.mjs — navigate http://localhost:9000/#/mix, dump attributes of the `button[data-slot="button"]` whose textContent is "Mix". `variant="primary-audacious"` is present as a raw attribute and `data-emphasis` reads "secondary".
defects.proposedCure: Speak glass-ui 7's two orthogonal axes at the call site — `<Button emphasis="primary" tone="…">` — and delete `variant` here and at GenerateControls.vue:158 (the only other site). If "audacious" is a register the system lacks, it is a glass-ui `emphasis`/`tone` value authored in glass-ui (owner edict 4), never a demo-side string. Structurally: turn on `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates`, which converts this whole family from invisible to compile-RED.

defects.defect: The Mix verb is UNREACHABLE. The only add-color affordance (MixSourceSelector's `<WatercolorDot tag="button" aria-label=… @click=…>`) renders as a non-interactive `<span aria-hidden="true">` because glass-ui 7's WatercolorDot declares no `tag`/`as`/`asChild`, no default slot, hardcodes aria-hidden and does not forward attrs/listeners. Consequence entirely on MixConfigBar's surface: `canMix` is false forever, so its Button is permanently disabled; `operandColors` is `[]` forever, so every preview chip is permanently absent. The T-17 feature has never rendered for a user.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:164-175; glass-ui 7 WatercolorDot props = {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} (dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts); `grep -o 'inheritAttrs:[!a-z0-9]*|aria-hidden[^,]*' dist/watercolor-dot.js` → aria-hidden":"true" x3 + inheritAttrs. LIVE: `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]')` → null; rendered element = `<span data-v-… aria-hidden="true" class="add-slot-ghost … watercolor-swatch" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" data-variant="ghost">`; `getByRole("button",{name:"Add current color to the mix"}).count()` → 0; two forced clicks + 750ms → {"mixDisabled":true,"dots":1}. Menus open: Color space {"options":9,"chips":0}, Hue method {"options":4,"chips":0}. Gate: useMixingState.ts:50-53 `selectedColors.value.length >= 2`.
defects.mechanism: same family as C-1 — a retired glass-ui-7 prop (`tag`) passed at a demo call site; fallthrough makes it inert, and here the inertness removes the element's interactivity, accessible name and click handler
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-three.mjs — navigate http://localhost:9000/#/mix, query `.add-slot-ghost`, click it twice with force, re-read the Mix button's `disabled` and the dot count; then open both Selects and count `[data-stops]`.
defects.proposedCure: Stop passing props the design system does not declare. Give the add-slot a real interactive host — a `<button>` wrapping the dot — or add a commandable `asChild`/`Primitive` affordance to glass-ui's WatercolorDot (owner edict 4: authored in glass-ui, not shimmed in demo/). Then `strictTemplates: true` so this class cannot recur silently.

defects.defect: With three or more operands the preview chip does not contain the color Mix produces. The chip samples an N−1-segment piecewise interpolation chain (sample.ts:52-86) while the button computes a weighted running accumulation (mixColorSequence, palettes/mix.ts:39). The two coincide only for 2 operands. Under the component's own quoted law ('a chip that approximates the library output is FORBIDDEN … a lying preview is worse than none') the ≥3-operand chip is exactly the forbidden object — byte-honest to mixColors, wrong referent for the operation.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:38-44 declares the chips' referent as 'the CURRENT mix operands'. Measured in-page against the shipped modules, operands [oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), rebeccapurple, rgb(20 120 200)], space oklch, arc shorter: {"rampLen":17, "mixedCss":"oklch(54.069139698567% 0.193255046847 307.570128060664deg)", "nearestStop":"oklch(48.520384700172% 0.187721999536 319.979741366417deg)", "nearestIndex":6, "nearestDistance":0.0656, "exactMember":false}. Two-operand control: {"rampLen":17, "exactMemberIndex":8} — the result IS stop 8 exactly.
defects.mechanism: the preview samples a different operator than the verb executes; the honest-absence guard cannot fire because the ramp is non-null, merely wrong-referent
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-four.mjs — imports demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts and demo/palettes/mix.ts through Vite's /@fs, samples the 3-operand ramp, computes mixColorSequence over the same operands, and searches the 17 stops for the result.
defects.proposedCure: Either sample the ACTUAL operator — walk mixColorSequence over prefix weights so the chip's last stop IS the mix result — or restrict the chip to the 2-operand case where chain and operator agree and show honest absence above that. The choice belongs in sample.ts (one sampler, both consumers), not in the view.

defects.defect: In the app's shipped default color space (`oklab`, rectangular) the Hue-method Select is inert and its four preview chips are byte-identical — a four-row quartet asserting a distinction that does not exist. Four of the nine offered spaces (oklab, lab, rgb, xyz) are rectangular; the app boots into one of them.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:66-74 samples the quartet in the CURRENT space; useMixingState.ts:44 `const colorSpace = ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")`. Measured in-page, distinct ramps across the 4 arcs for operands [oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), rebeccapurple]: {"oklch":2,"oklab":1,"lab":1,"lch":2,"hsl":2,"hsv":2,"hwb":2,"rgb":1,"xyz":1}. The four oklab rows at stop 4 are the identical string `oklch(57.506794900057% 0.22159155218 0.258910679707deg)`. Screenshots shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png and shots/safari-mobile-dark/mix.png show the boot state COLOR SPACE: OKLab / HUE METHOD: Shorter.
defects.mechanism: a control rendered as live when the component holds every fact needed to know it is inert; the interpolation-space vocabulary carries label+description but not the cylindrical/rectangular fact
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-six.mjs — for each of the 9 offered spaces, sample all 4 arcs and count distinct serialized ramps.
defects.proposedCure: Add `cylindrical: true` to the five hue-bearing rows of INTERPOLATION_SPACES (color-space-meta.ts — the neutral home already exists, no new module), then bind `:disabled="!isCylindrical(colorSpace)"` on the Hue-method Select (glass-ui SelectProps.disabled exists) and skip hueRamps in that branch. One fact, authored once, consumed by the two surfaces (Mix, Gradient) that already share the module.

defects.defect: The preview chip paints a CONTINUOUS multi-stop gradient, contradicting both its own docstring ('discrete-stop linear gradient', PreviewRamp.vue:6-7) and the module's sampling law ('never CSS gradient interpolation, because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would', sample.ts:5-11). With 17 stops across a 41.9px chip, the library owns 17 pixel-columns and the browser's gradient engine paints the other ~25 and all of the transitions.
defects.evidence: PreviewRamp.vue:24-26 `linear-gradient(90deg, ${stops.join(", ")})` — no positions, no `in <space>`. Measured computed value: {"hasPositions":false,"stopCount":17,"computedHead":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), oklch(0.608767 0.263144 5.64831), oklch(0.597534 0.256287 1.49662), …"}. Chip width `inline-size: 2.618rem` = 41.9px (PreviewRamp.vue:43). Modelled worst-band deviation (sRGB chord between adjacent stops vs the library's own value at that parameter, Euclidean 0-255): oklch·longer 23.5/255 at band 7; oklch·shorter 1.1/255; hsv·longer 0.5/255. The e2e leg (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:374-387) asserts only that the LISTED stops appear in the paint — structurally blind to everything between them.
defects.mechanism: the paint mechanism silently reintroduces the very interpolation engine the sampling law was written to exclude; the truth oracle checks stop membership, never the interpolant
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-four.mjs (gradient form) and node scratchpad/probe-five.mjs (band error) — build the real 17-stop gradient, read its computed value, then for each band compare the sRGB midpoint of the two neighbouring stops against the library's value at that parameter.
defects.proposedCure: Emit the discrete gradient the docstring already promises — doubled positions `s_i (i/n)% ((i+1)/n)%` — so every painted pixel is a library sample and nothing is interpolated by the engine. That also makes the chip's honesty verifiable by construction rather than by a stop-list substring check.

defects.defect: The T-17 chips have no live verification and no unit coverage, and beneath the C-2 deadlock the byte-identity assertion could not pass anyway: the spec's `parseOklchTriples` regex requires three bare numeric groups but `serializeStop` emits a `%` on L and a `deg` on H, so it matches ZERO stamped stops while matching the browser-canonicalised paint — `expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)` would evaluate `expect(17).toBe(0)`.
defects.evidence: o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168 regex `/oklch\(([\d.]+)[ ,]+([\d.]+)[ ,]+([\d.]+)(?:\s*\/\s*[\d.%]+)?\)/g`. Live output of the shipped serializeStop: `oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)` (from "red"), `oklch(60% 0.2 30deg)`, `oklch(0% 0 none)`, `oklch(100% 0 none / 6.25%)`. Live computed paint: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), …)` — matches. Both chip-rendering legs (:346, :404) start with the C-2 dead locator. `grep -rn "MixConfigBar" . --exclude-dir=node_modules -l` → only MixPane.vue + a doc comment; nothing mounts it. test/preview-chips.test.ts exercises sample.ts in isolation only.
defects.mechanism: vacuous gate — the only green leg asserts ABSENCE, the two legs that would exercise a rendered chip are unreachable, and their central assertion has never matched the format it claims to parse
defects.reproduction: VACUOUS-GATE MUTATION, named exactly: delete both `<PreviewRamp …/>` elements (MixConfigBar.vue:111 and :133). `npm test` stays fully green (nothing imports the component); the one green e2e leg ('honest absence … the rows carry NO chip') stays green because the chips become unconditionally absent; the two red legs stay red. The entire T-17 feature can be deleted from this file without turning a single gate a different colour.
defects.proposedCure: (1) fix the add-slot host so the flow is drivable (C-2); (2) delete parseOklchTriples and compare `data-stops.split("|")` against the painted stops through ONE shared normalizer owned by sample.ts — the module already owns stampStops, so the referent exists; (3) add a @vue/test-utils mount asserting the one thing only this file owns: Space row i carries the ramp for space i with the current arc, and Hue row j the ramp for arc j with the current space.

defects.defect: Three `<label>` elements that label nothing: no `for`, no labelable descendant, `HTMLLabelElement.control === null`, and clicking the visible label neither focuses nor opens the Select. MixConfigBar is the ONLY site in demo/ that uses `<label>` for the `.section-label` recipe — every one of the seven peer sites uses `<span>`/`<div>` — so this is a lone divergence that promises label semantics and delivers none. The accessible name survives only via a hand-duplicated `aria-label` on each trigger.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:98, :121, :145. LIVE: [{"text":"Color space","htmlFor":"","controlTag":null,"controlId":null},{"text":"Hue method","htmlFor":"","controlTag":null,"controlId":null}]. Label click result: {"active":"BODY ","listboxOpen":false}. Divergence: `grep -rn "section-label" demo/` → GradientVisualizer.vue:163,180,197,229 <span>; MixSourceSelector.vue:183 <span>; GenerateControls.vue:221,255 <span>; SearchFilterBar.vue:20,32,48,63 <div>; TagEditPopover.vue:8 <div>; AdminTagsPanel.vue:87 <div>; MixConfigBar.vue:98,121,145 <label> ← only site. glass-ui 7 ships the primitive and demo/ui/label/index.ts already re-exports it with `LabelProps { for?: string; … }`.
defects.mechanism: semantic element used as a style hook; the name is authored twice (visible text + aria-label) instead of once through the design system's Label primitive — the standard start of name/label drift
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-configbar.mjs — enumerate `label.section-label`, read `.htmlFor` and `.control`, then click the 'Color space' label and re-read document.activeElement and the presence of [role=listbox].
defects.proposedCure: `<Label for="mix-space">Color space</Label>` + `id="mix-space"` on the trigger (×3) and drop the duplicated aria-labels. One name, authored once, in the design system's own primitive (owner edict 4).

defects.defect: Legacy comma-with-alpha CSS colors throw in the demo's parser, and the two consumers of that parse handle it asymmetrically: sample.ts catches and returns null, so MixConfigBar's chip vanishes under a guard documented as 'honest absence — the preview has nothing true to say', while useMixingState.startMix does the identical parse UNGUARDED. The pane can therefore say 'nothing to preview' and 'ready to mix' at the same time, when the truth is 'pressing this throws'.
defects.evidence: Live calls to the shipped parseColorIn: "rgba(255,0,0,1)" → THROW PickerColorError: Invalid CSS color; "rgba(255,0,0,0.5)" → THROW; "hsla(0,100%,50%,1)" → THROW; while "rgb(255,0,0)", "rgb(255 0 0 / 100%)", "#ff0000ff", "red" all parse. Throw origin demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:159. Guarded consumer sample.ts:60-66 (returns null) vs unguarded consumer useMixingState.ts:88-90 → mix.ts:35 throws. Guard semantics documented at sample.ts:50-51 and MixConfigBar.vue:40-42.
defects.mechanism: one predicate ('can this operand be read?') evaluated in two places with two different failure policies; the absence guard conflates 'nothing to say' with 'cannot read this'
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-four.mjs — call parseColorIn on the legacy comma-with-alpha forms and observe the throw. HYPOTHESIS on end-to-end reachability: I did not find a stored PaletteColor.css in rgba()/hsla() form this session; the parse failure itself is measured fact, the user-reachable path is unproven.
defects.proposedCure: The parser gap belongs to the parser seat. This component's half: the absence guard must distinguish 'nothing to say' from 'cannot read this', and whatever answer the chip gives the Mix button must give the same one — one predicate, both surfaces.

defects.defect: `serializeStop`'s `.replace(/ \/ 1\)$/, ")")` is dead code — the serializer never emits the string it removes. It omits alpha entirely at α=1 and emits a PERCENTAGE otherwise, so ` / 1)` is not in its output language. A legacy no-op sitting in the module that owns the T-17 truth law.
defects.evidence: sample.ts:38-41. Live outputs of colorToCss(…, "oklch"): `oklch(0.6 0.2 30 / 1)` → `oklch(60% 0.2 30deg)`; `#ff0000ff` → `oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)`; achromatic α<1 → `oklch(100% 0 none / 6.25%)`; α=0 → `oklch(0% 0 none / 0%)`. serializeStop's output is byte-identical to colorToCss's in every case.
defects.mechanism: legacy transformation retained after the serializer's output format changed; the docstring describes a property the serializer already provides, not one this line provides (owner edict 2 — no legacy, no dual paths)
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-four.mjs — for each of rgb/hex/oklch inputs with and without alpha, print colorToCss(...) and serializeStop(...) side by side; they are equal for every input.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `.replace`; the docstring's promise is already the serializer's contract.

defects.defect: `class="h-9"` on all three SelectTriggers de-tokenizes the height glass-ui already ships as `size="sm"`, severing these controls from `--control-h-sm`; tailwind-merge drops the token class in favour of the literal. Same idiom on the Button (`class="h-10 …"`) while `ButtonProps.size` exists.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:100, :123, :147, :165. glass-ui ships both `.h-\(--control-h-sm\){height:var(--control-h-sm)}` and `.h-\(--control-h-md\){height:var(--control-h-md)}` in dist/styles/components.css, plus `.h-9{height:calc(var(--spacing) * 9)}` = 2.25rem = 36px. Measured live trigger height = 36px = exactly --control-h-sm. Measured trigger box 227×36.
defects.mechanism: per-instance pixel costume overriding a named design-system register (owner edict 5 — style at the root component level, never per-instance)
defects.reproduction: Read the computed height of `[role=combobox][aria-label="Color space"]` on http://localhost:9000/#/mix → 36px; compare to the shipped `--control-h-sm` token. A retune of --control-h-sm moves every control in the app except these three.
defects.proposedCure: `<SelectTrigger size="sm">` ×3, drop `h-9`; express the Button's register through size/emphasis/tone (which also closes C-1).

defects.defect: The component reaches past the design system into reka-ui for `AcceptableValue` — a union wider than glass-ui's actual emit — and then launders it with three unchecked `as` casts. glass-ui 7 narrowed the contract to `SelectionValue = string | number` precisely so consumers need not touch reka; reka is a devDependency.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:15 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";` and handlers at :99, :122, :146 of the form `(v: AcceptableValue) => emit('update:colorSpace', v as PickerSpace)`. glass-ui 7: SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue] } (dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts) with `type SelectionValue = string | number` (dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts). reka's AcceptableValue includes Record<string, any> | null.
defects.mechanism: masking cast — an unchecked narrowing from a union containing null, advertising values the design system will never send (owner edict 2: no masking fallbacks)
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; read MixConfigBar.vue:15/:99/:122/:146 against dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts and dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Annotate `(v: string | number)` — the literal SelectionValue — and narrow honestly with a membership check against INTERPOLATION_SPACES / HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS (both already imported, both already the source of the rendered rows) instead of `as`. Deleting the reka-ui import from the demo tree is the architectural half; it also closes C-16.

defects.defect: The decorative `<Blend>` icon carries no `aria-hidden`, so it is exposed inside the button as a nameless `img` node. The sibling component gets this right, so it is an inconsistency inside one feature rather than a house style.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:168 `<Blend class="w-4 h-4" />` — @lucide/vue (^1.16.0, package.json:87) does not add aria-hidden. Contrast MixSourceSelector.vue:174 `<Plus class="w-5 h-5 …" aria-hidden="true" />`. Note: this is a spurious child node, not a nameless control — the button's own accessible name ("Mix") is intact, and this is NOT the /#/mix `namelessButtons: 1` row in REPORT.json (that count is desktop-only and absent on mobile, where this button also renders).
defects.mechanism: decorative graphic left in the accessibility tree
defects.reproduction: NONE beyond the AX tree read — inspect the accessible tree of the Mix button on http://localhost:9000/#/mix; the icon appears as an unnamed img child.
defects.proposedCure: `<Blend class="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />`.

defects.defect: The leftover-strategy vocabulary is duplicated inside the view as a hand-written array plus a label Record. The Record is exhaustiveness-checked by TypeScript; the ARRAY is not — adding a fourth strategy to the union compiles clean and the new strategy silently never appears in the menu.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:83-89 (`const STRATEGIES: LeftoverStrategy[] = ["discard","repeat","distribute"]` + `strategyLabels: Record<LeftoverStrategy,string>`); the type is owned by demo/palettes/mix.ts:19. The file states the opposite principle for the other vocabulary at :16-18 ('the interpolation vocabulary lives in its neutral home … no more cross-feature reach').
defects.mechanism: vocabulary left behind in the view when its sibling vocabulary was homed; a non-exhaustive array is a silent-omission hazard on every future union extension
defects.reproduction: NONE — static. Add a fourth member to `LeftoverStrategy` in demo/palettes/mix.ts:19: `strategyLabels` goes RED (exhaustive Record), `STRATEGIES` stays green and the new row never renders.
defects.proposedCure: Put `{ value, label }` metadata beside the type in demo/palettes/mix.ts, the same shape color-space-meta.ts uses, and import it. Zero new modules — the neutral home already exists.

defects.defect: The pane's only verb is natively `disabled` on every cold load with no reason, no tab reach and no hint: a native disabled button is removed from the tab order, so a keyboard or screen-reader user cannot reach it to discover it exists or why it is unavailable. Given C-2 that state is permanent. Separately the mix result is asynchronous from the user's point of view and lands with no aria-live anywhere in the chain.
defects.evidence: Measured live: {"disabled":true,"ariaDisabled":null,"opacity":"0.5","describedby":null}. canMix gate at useMixingState.ts:50-53. Narration window opened at useMixingState.ts:100; result rendered by MixPane.vue:111-119 with no role=status / aria-live in the chain.
defects.mechanism: unavailability expressed by removal rather than by explanation; async completion never announced
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-two.mjs — read the Mix button's disabled/aria-disabled/aria-describedby/tabIndex on a cold load of http://localhost:9000/#/mix.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the button focusable and use `aria-disabled` + a short `aria-describedby` hint on the disabled state; give the result plate `role="status"`. The aria-live belongs on the result surface, recorded here so the mix seat does not drop it between components.

defects.defect: MixPane passes `:operand-colors` as a freshly-mapped array on every render, so both computeds invalidate on renders where nothing changed by value. Measured cost is sub-frame, so this is recorded as INFO, not a perf defect: the 'costs nothing at rest' claim in the file's own comment is TRUE and verified.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:103 `:operand-colors="mode === 'colors' ? selectedColors.map((sc) => sc.css) : []"`. defects.defect: CORRECTED · MAJOR (r1 filed MINOR with the wrong mechanism) — the `<TransitionGroup name="vj-enter">` fires zero transition classes, ever. Fixing the key alone resurrects nothing.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:60 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`), :63 `key="well"` / :76 `key="content"`, :92-96 TransitionGroup with no `appear`. All 24 are vj-morph on plate/content divs plus vj-enter on MixSourceSelector's chip divs (whose group lives across updates, so its transitions do work). The shared recipe at demo/styles/utils.css:174-179 advertises MixResultDisplay as one of three consumers — it is inert for this one.
defects.mechanism: declared animation on a subtree that is always freshly mounted; TransitionGroup's no-initial-transition rule makes the whole `vj-enter` name and the shared `.swatch-row` recipe dead code for this consumer
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/wbmix-probe9.mjs — arm a MutationObserver on class attributes, set a 3-colour palette result with animationPhase='mixing', force paints, flip to 'done', force paints; filter the log for elements with data-testid='watercolor-swatch' → empty array.
defects.proposedCure: Decide what the row's arrival IS. If the dots should stagger as the plate inks: add `appear` to the TransitionGroup and key on colour identity (not the index, which also couples a dot's silhouette seed at :104 to its slot rather than to what it is). If the plate's `vj-morph` is meant to be the only motion — one surface, new content, the family law the docstring cites at :17 — then delete `name="vj-enter"` and the `swatch-row` class and correct the utility's comment to two consumers. defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MAJOR — clipboard failure is completely silent and never resets. `:32` collapses a four-state machine to `status === "success"`, and the shipped useClipboard arms its reset timer only on the success branch.

(a.value="success", l=setTimeout(…"idle"…, i.resetMs ?? 1500), n) : (a.value="failure", i.onCopyError?.(n.reason), n)` — no timer on failure, and `onCopyError` is never supplied here. Reproduced by replacing navigator.clipboard.writeText with a NotAllowedError rejection (the shape of the non-secure-context / denied path the repo hits over LAN http, vite.config.ts `server.host: true`): `[console.warning] [useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected: NotAllowedError: denied` then `{"before":{"title":"Copy color"},"after":{"title":"Copy color","plateText":"RESULT","liveRegions":0,"role":0}}`.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MAJOR — the copy confirmation goes stale across a re-mix and affirms the wrong value.

Nothing in this component calls it, and nothing watches `result`, so a re-mix during the 1500 ms window leaves the check mark asserting the previous colour.
defects.mechanism: confirmation state not invalidated when the value it confirms is replaced
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis by construction from the source and the shipped dist; not separately driven (the 1500 ms window plus headless rAF throttling makes a timing repro unreliable, and D-10'/D-16 consumed the probe budget).
defects.proposedCure: `watch(() => result, invalidate)` — the library already exposes exactly the affordance this needs; use it rather than adding a local timer.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MAJOR — two divergent copy implementations for one user-visible action, with the dock routed to the one that gives no feedback (edict #2, no dual paths).

defects.mechanism: the same behaviour implemented twice at two altitudes, with the text-building expression copy-pasted between files
defects.reproduction: NONE — established by reading the three call sites; not driven in the browser.
defects.proposedCure: One implementation. The plate owns the result and owns the confirmation, so `copyResult` on MixPane should delegate to the plate (an exposed method on the child, or hoist the single `useClipboard` scope to MixPane and pass `status` down) — never a second `writeClipboard` path. defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MAJOR — an empty palette result renders a plate captioned 'Result' with live Copy and Save over nothing.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MINOR — the `MixResult` type permits states the plate renders as blank, and that looseness is what forces four masking `??` fallbacks.

defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/wbmix-probe6.mjs case E — set mixResult to {type:'color'} with no css on the live pane → blank plate, three live buttons.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED · MAJOR (test truth) — the gate is vacuous, and the vacuous mutation is behaviourally identical to what ships.
defects.evidence: No test mounts the component: `grep -rln "MixResultDisplay\|mix-result" test demo e2e` → only demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue, MixResultDisplay.vue, demo/styles/utils.css. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → clean, exit 0 (Vue models unknown component attributes as fallthrough attrs, so 'forwarded into a black hole' has no diagnostic). Run at HEAD: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` → `1 failed`, `Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByRole('main', …).getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' }) / element(s) not found` at `> 42 | await expect(addSlot).toBeVisible();` — so the `[data-mix-target]` assertion at e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:52 (and e2e/smoke/safari/mix-flow.spec.ts:40) has never been evaluated.

defects.reproduction: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line (output pasted above). And the source-selector break must be fixed so the mix specs stop masking every downstream assertion behind one early failure.

result.axis: DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue, round 2
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]`, as explicitly declared in the spawning system prompt. The seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the page's ONE verb is styled by a prop that does not exist. `variant="primary-audacious"` is not a member of glass-ui 7's Button API (props are `emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class`); the string appears nowhere in the package; Vue deposits it as an inert DOM attribute and the button resolves to the runtime default `data-emphasis="secondary"` — the quiet glass capsule that the source comment on MixConfigBar.vue:161 explicitly says it was chosen to avoid. Measured live and visible in all four Safari captures: the primary action is the weakest-reading element in its own group.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable (verdict is DEFECTIVE), but the following were specifically hunted and hold, each with a measured witness: RTL is clean (dir=rtl → grid `direction: rtl`, Mix button x 754→224, trigger x 989→459, label `text-align: start`); focus survives forced colors (trigger computes `outline: solid 2px rgba(5,0,73,0.8)` under forcedColors:active with focus applied — this discharges the concrete risk round 1 flagged as unknown); reduced motion is producer-handled (`.button` carries `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { transition: none }`, component adds no motion); no truncation at 320/390/720/1440 (`scrollWidth == clientWidth` for the longest value "Decreasing"); no horizontal overflow (REPORT.md `/#/mix` overflowX 0, all four matrices); no route errors (REPORT.json `/#/mix` consoleErrors/pageErrors/failedRequests all empty); `demo/ui/select` and `demo/ui/button` are pure re-exports of glass-ui (no local fork — edict 4's letter honoured); verbatimModuleSyntax clean (4/4 type-only imports are `import type`, lines 12-15); idiomatic Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure; no god module, no legacy shims; the honest-absence law is genuinely implemented (sample.ts:58 returns null below 2 operands, no canned swatch); and — correcting the record — the REPORT rows `smallTapTargets: 8` and `namelessButtons: 1` on `/#/mix` are NOT this component (probe payload: picker channel spans 12x24, slug controls 22x22, and one unrelated `button.send-btn`).

defects.mechanism: retired/nonexistent producer API handed to glass-ui 7.0.0; Vue fallthrough turns a wrong prop into a decorative DOM attribute rather than an error, so neither the eye nor vue-tsc objects. Family: 106 `variant=` sites vs 2 `emphasis=` sites across demo/ (round-1 census).

defects.proposedCure: Delete `variant` (here and at GenerateControls.vue:158) and pass `emphasis="primary"` plus a named `tone`. Delete the whole `class="h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display"` costume. If an "audacious" register is genuinely wanted it is a glass-ui `emphasis` member filed as a producer ask (edict 4), not a consumer attribute. Close the family with a sweep that fails the build on any `variant=` reaching a glass-ui root.

defects.defect: BLOCKER — `Hue method` is inert in the shipped default state, and the "four-arc quartet" is never four in ANY reachable state. ESCALATES round 1 D-4, which proved only the acylindrical case by construction.
defects.evidence: src/color/anchors.ts:360-366 `HUE_INDEX = { hsl:0, hsv:0, hwb:0, lch:2, oklch:2 }`; src/color/operations.ts:101-111 reads `options.hue` only inside `if (i === hueIndex)`. Default space is oklab (useMixingState.ts:44). Runnable proof, red→green, 8 samples, all 9 offered spaces: oklab/lab/rgb/xyz → distinct ramps 1/4 (all four methods byte-identical); oklch/lch/hsl/hsv/hwb → distinct ramps 2/4 (increasing≡shorter, decreasing≡longer). Comment at MixConfigBar.vue:127-128 claims "the four-arc quartet".
defects.mechanism: the bar models the dependency that does not matter (mode→leftover strategy, gated at :144) and refuses the one that does (space→hue relevance); an over-enumerated, partly synonymous vocabulary is presented as flat and orthogonal at equal geometry, material and weight to the control that actually decides the mix.
defects.reproduction: node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/color.js').then(({rgb,convertColor,mixColors})=>{ /* unwrap Results; for each space build 8-sample ramps under all 4 hue methods; count distinct */ })" — output pasted in the report. Zero UI steps needed.
defects.proposedCure: Gate the row on `HUE_INDEX[colorSpace] !== undefined` (one boolean from the library, no new vocabulary) so a space without a hue channel has no hue row at all — the same honest-absence restraint already used for the operand ramps. Then reduce the surviving vocabulary to the two real arcs; `increasing`/`decreasing` are library-level synonyms of `shorter`/`longer` for a two-operand mix and should not be separate UI rows. Preview chips then always show two genuinely different ramps, which is the only reason to show chips.

defects.defect: MAJOR — the three 36px Select triggers breach the producer's coarse-pointer contract and fall below its 44px touch floor. CORRECTS round 1 D-10, whose cited evidence (REPORT smallTapTargets) was the wrong elements.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147 `class="h-9"` while SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts exposes `size?: "sm"|"default"`. glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css: `--control-h-sm: max(calc(2.25rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))`; tokens/light-dark.css: `@media (pointer: coarse) { :root { --ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5); --control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); } }`. Measured under iPhone 13 emulation: resolved --ui-scale "1.5", --control-floor "2.75rem"; triggers render height 36px, min-block-size auto — contract is max(54px,44px)=54px. Mix button gap measured 8px vs producer calc(0.375rem*1.5)=9px. REPORT.json /#/mix smallTapTargets are picker channel spans (12x24) and slug controls (22x22) — zero MixConfigBar elements.
defects.mechanism: per-instance hard-coded geometry over a producer token that had already solved viewport/pointer scaling and the accessibility floor (owner edict 5); the harness threshold never tested the coarse-pointer arm, so nothing caught it.
defects.reproduction: Playwright context with devices['iPhone 13'] → http://localhost:9000/#/mix → getBoundingClientRect() on the three [aria-label] combobox triggers = {w:158,h:36}; getComputedStyle(documentElement).getPropertyValue('--control-h-sm') = 'max(calc(2.25rem * 1.5), 2.75rem)'.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `h-9` from all three triggers and `h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display` from the Button. Use `size="sm"` on the triggers if a smaller register is genuinely wanted; nothing at all on the Button. Geometry belongs to the producer's scale, which already encodes the touch floor.

defects.defect: MAJOR — the bar's information exists only mid-gesture: the ramp is placed in the one slot that cannot reach the trigger, and the menu that reveals it occludes the verb and hides 2 of 9 options below its own fold.

defects.defect: MAJOR — the component fuses the tune region and the commit region into one node, making the canon's Mix mobile sequence 'operand rack, result, controls' structurally unreachable.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 Mix row, mobile-order column: "operand rack, result, controls"; outer housing "its own InstrumentChassis composition". Measured DOM order inside `.pane-scroll-fade`: [pane-header-title, pane-header-desc-wrap, MixSourceSelector root, MixConfigBar root] with the result plate (MixPane.vue:111-119) rendering AFTER — i.e. rack → controls+commit → result. §5: "Commit uses one glass-ui action set." MixConfigBar.vue:93-171 is a single `flex flex-col gap-3` that terminates in the Button.
defects.mechanism: regional conflation: a chassis action region and an inspector tuning group share one DOM node, so the action cannot be relocated without dragging two Selects with it; on mobile the answer therefore renders below the button that produced it.
defects.reproduction: Playwright at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: [...document.querySelectorAll('.pane-scroll-fade > div > *')].map(e => e.tagName + '.' + e.className) → the config bar precedes the result plate; canon requires the reverse.
defects.proposedCure: Split by job: MixConfigBar keeps the tuning group only; the Mix verb moves to the chassis action region alongside the result's Save/Copy, where §5's single action set already lives. One transposition makes emphasis (D-1), loading/precondition state (D-5) and canonical order (this) expressible instead of impossible — three patches collapse into one move.

defects.defect: MAJOR — third breach of the closed type matrix (`text-micro` is below and outside it), and one visible label already disagrees with its own control's accessible name. EXTENDS round 1 D-5/D-8.

One string, one source. `.section-label`'s mono-caption voice on a control label is a systemic canon conflict (7 components, 17 sites) and belongs to the canon owner, not to this file alone.

defects.defect: MINOR — under forced colors the primary action and its secondary siblings collapse to the same object, and disabled rides entirely on an opacity forced-colors does not normalise.

Select trigger: background rgba(255,255,255,0), border-top `1px rgba(5,0,73,0.8)`, box-shadow none, opacity 1. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."
defects.mechanism: emphasis expressed only through glass material (fill, specular inset, capsule shadow) leaves no forced-colors residue; and the entire disabled signal is `opacity: 0.5`, a property forced-colors does not override — so in a high-contrast profile the page's one verb is a faded 1px outline identical in weight to a settings dropdown, carrying no semantic mark.

defects.proposedCure: Give the commit a forced-colors-durable mark that is not material: the producer's `emphasis="primary"` + `tone` path (D-1) plus a state expressed through `aria-disabled` and text (D-5), so disabled and primary both survive when backgrounds and shadows are stripped.

defects.defect: MINOR — a state change of the action region was given no motion at all, while a decorative sibling got a full tokenized transition; the verb teleports ~72px on a source-mode toggle. REFINES round 1 D-7 with the component-local number.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:144 bare `v-if="showLeftoverStrategy"` with no <Transition>. Measured bar-root height across the mode switch: 1440x900 → 113.58px (colors) vs 187.16px (palettes), Δ +73.58px; iPhone 13 → 130.25px vs 200.50px, Δ +70.25px. Sibling result plate is wrapped in `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (MixPane.vue:111). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "A scene swap preserves the specimen and changes the surrounding instrument."
defects.mechanism: one pane, two motion grammars — a tokenized morph for a decorative result plate, a hard cut for the control that displaces the commit button under the user's finger. Not a prefers-reduced-motion violation: there is nothing to reduce, and the producer already handles the button's own transitions.
defects.reproduction: Playwright at /#/mix: measure `.grid.grid-cols-2`.parentElement height, click the Palettes tab, re-measure → +73.58px at 1440, +70.25px at iPhone 13.
defects.proposedCure: The three method controls are one region whose track count is content-derived, so the strategy row joins the existing rhythm rather than breaking it, and the region — not the page — absorbs the mode change. Once the verb moves to the action region (D-7) its y-coordinate stops being a function of a tab it does not own.

defects.defect: MINOR — glass-ui's SelectItem #description slot ships layout but no typography, so five consumers re-mint the identical class string eight times.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier this seat was spawned with (explicit, not inherited)
result.strongestDefect: D-18 — the component's two-line `<style scoped>` block (`MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154`) silently overrides the producer `vj-morph` motion family on the same element by attribute specificity. Measured while `.vj-morph-enter-active` is applied: `transition-property: opacity` (not `opacity, transform, max-height`), timing `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` = `--ease-standard` instead of `--ease-decelerate`/`--spring-snappy`. Consequence, rAF-sampled every frame: the plate goes 102.7px → 218.7px with NO intermediate frame — a +116.0px (2.13x) single-frame snap. This also invalidates the prior run's cure for its own D-3 (setting `--vj-morph-collapse/-expanded` cannot work on an element whose transition-property is `opacity`).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but the following survived a hostile second pass and is affirmatively sound, each measured rather than assumed: (1) reduced-motion — the global guard at `animations.css:183-191` neutralises every transition and `useMixingState.ts:13-15`'s immediate-settle path is honoured; measured across a full reduced-motion WebKit context. (2) 200% zoom — rem-based sizing throughout; measured plate 216.7px at a 720px-equivalent viewport, no clipping, zero horizontal overflow. (3) Specimen faces are correctly ornamental — `aria-hidden`, non-interactive, and covered TWICE by `demo/styles/foundation.css`'s colour-surface roster (`.swatch-row > *` and `.watercolor-swatch`) in both `@media (forced-colors: active)` and `@media print`, so the dots keep faithful colour in HCM and in print. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — `import type { MixResult }` (line 7) is the only type import and is correctly marked. (5) Idiomatic Vue 3.5 — reactive props destructure with a default (lines 20-23), no `defineModel` async round-trip and therefore no stale-read hazard, so no `shallowRef` is warranted. (6) The one-clock law holds — the component owns no timer; the only timing is `useClipboard`'s producer-owned `resetMs`. (7) Motion family NAMING is disciplined — `vj-morph` + `vj-enter`, no fourth name, satisfying the `animations.css:59` hard gate (only the scoped override defeats the declarations). (8) No god module — 159 lines, one job. (9) The seed-continuity idea is genuinely good design thinking and is worth repairing rather than deleting.

defects.defect: The scoped `transition` shorthand defeats the producer `vj-morph` motion family on the same element by attribute specificity, so the plate's arrival is a 116.0px single-frame snap with no transform and no height morph. Supersedes and corrects the prior run's D-3 diagnosis AND its cure.
defects.evidence:
chD-probe4.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, live CSSOM + computed style read while the plate carries `vj-morph-enter-active`:
  classes            : mix-plate … bg-well mix-plate--ghost vj-morph-enter-active vj-morph-enter-to
  transitionProperty : opacity
  transitionDuration : 0.2s
  transitionTiming   : cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)   ← --ease-standard
  transform          : none
  maxHeight          : none
The two competing rules read out of the CSSOM:
  .vj-morph-enter-active      { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-decelerate), transform var(--spring-snappy-duration) var(--spring-snappy), max-height var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-decelerate); }
  .mix-plate[data-v-0f138735] { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard); }
Specificity (0,2,0) > (0,1,0); the shorthand resets transition-property to `opacity`.
Source: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154.
Consequence, chD-probe5.mjs rAF sample every frame for 2500ms across a 12-colour swap, compressed to state changes: [{"t":44,"h":102.7,"op":0.55,"dots":1,"btns":0},{"t":265,"h":218.7,"op":1,"dots":12,"btns":3}] — minHeight 102.7, maxHeight 218.7, no intermediate height. Single-colour arm real flow: desktop 118.7→158.7 (+40.0), mobile 112.3→158.6 (+46.3).
defects.mechanism: Scoped-CSS specificity override of a producer motion family. `animations.css:59-62` states the family law verbatim: "The family owns the CURVE + TOKEN pairing; a consuming site may parameterise only GEOMETRY through the `--vj-*` custom properties." This component parameterises the CURVE and the PROPERTY SET via a scoped `transition` shorthand — the two things the law forbids — and wins by attribute specificity. No gate in the tranche can see it.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chD-probe4.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/mix; or in DevTools arm a mix and read getComputedStyle($('.mix-plate')).transitionProperty during the enter frame.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `<style scoped>` whole. The ghost dimming belongs on the specimen tier (the `variant="ghost"` dot already expresses it), not on the container. Combined with making the ghost render the result's own shape and count, the container never resizes, `mode="out-in"` becomes unnecessary and there is no height to morph — the family is restored rather than patched.

defects.defect: The gradient strip depicts an interpolation the user did not choose — it never receives `colorSpace`/`hueMethod` — while the same pane already ships the correct, library-sampled, space-aware ramp primitive forty lines away.
defects.evidence:
chD-probe3.mjs, WebKit, identical stops, midpoint pixel sampled from the painted render:
  linear-gradient(to right, …)          → rgb(135,117,169)

defects.defect: A non-modal overlay claims a `window`-level Escape key it does not own the modality for.

defects.defect: Three of the 27 specimen tiles this component renders (the whole `back` family) destroy the entire Gradient pane on click. The demo converts value.js's Result error back into a thrown Error inside a Vue `computed`, which has no error channel, so it escapes to the app ErrorBoundary. The structural cause is a missing seam owner: no package owns 'an eased t may leave [0,1]; a colour ramp clamps'.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (`const easedT = easing(t); … if (!mixed.ok) throw new Error("Gradient color mix failed: " + mixed.error.code)`) against src/color/operations.ts:65 (`if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`). Duplicated verbatim at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37. Measured ranges over dist/subpaths/easing.js: ease-in-back [-0.0969, 1.0000] · ease-out-back [0.0000, 1.0869] · ease-in-out-back [-0.0927, 1.0927]. Live capture — BEFORE {"rows":1,"tiles":27,"stage":1} / AFTER {"rows":0,"tiles":0,"stage":0,"bodyText":"… This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range  Try again"}.
defects.mechanism: Result→throw conversion at a render boundary + a domain seam (overshooting eased progress vs mixColors' [0,1] contract) that has no owner in any of the three packages; the catalogue that offers curves and the sampler that consumes them are two homes for one invariant.
defects.reproduction: Headless Chromium → http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → wait for settle → click the `ease-out-back` specimen tile in the open easing row (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). The pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary. Script: scratchpad/L-crash.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Give the seam a single owner: new `demo/workbenches/gradient/model/rampDomain.ts` exporting `clampProgress(t: number): number`, and route EVERY eased-t → colour call through it (sampleCoalescedStops, interpolateStopColors). Clamping is not a fallback — it is what CSS itself does when interpolating a gradient, so overshoot curves then render exactly as `linear-gradient` renders them, while overshoot survives where it is meaningful (glyph portraits, picker canvas). Simultaneously delete the duplicated Result→throw conversion and thread an explicit `{ok:false, reason}` verdict the way `applyCSS` already does (useGradientModel.ts:158-168). Codify the repo invariant: `src/` returns Result; `demo/` may throw only from an event handler, never from a computed, a watch callback, or module top-level.

defects.mechanism: Consumer styles the producer by internal DOM selector (ARIA role, class name, and `data-testid` — a test contract used as a styling contract) instead of through published props; the coupling died silently across a glass-ui major with no gate catching it. Compounded by the demo scraping from the DOM a value (`viewBox`) the producer already publishes as a ComputedRef on `useEasingPicker`.

Consumer-side: EasingAuthoringStage.vue loses its entire script body (rootEl / vbRatio / syncVbRatio / rAF / watch — 21 dead lines) and its entire `<style scoped>` block; 116 lines collapse to a props adapter. defects.defect: The O-17 easing-composition oracle — the one gate written to certify exactly what N-1 and N-2 break — reds on the same dead `svg[role='img']` selector in its `discloseAuthoring` helper, so all three of its tests die before reaching the tile clicks. The line that would reproduce N-1 in one action is never executed. The only unit coverage is a NaN-in-glyph proxy that asserts nothing about consumability.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:52-54 — `const svg = row.locator("#easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img']"); await expect(svg).toBeVisible();` — matches 0 elements (specHit: 0, N-2). defects.mechanism: A gate red for reason A masks a BLOCKER for reason B; and the invariant that mattered (a tile must be consumable by the sampler that renders the row it selects) was proxied by a glyph-shape check instead of asserted directly.
defects.reproduction: Run the command above; observe all three tests fail inside `openEasingBench`/`discloseAuthoring`, before any `[data-specimen]` click. Deterministic supporting proof is the in-page `specHit: 0` measurement plus the glass-ui grep, neither of which depends on the harness.

(b) Move the missing invariant DOWN to a unit test where it is three lines: for every tile in SPECIMEN_TILES, `sampleCoalescedStops` over a two-stop model must not throw. defects.defect: Four sites in the demo convert value.js Result errors back into thrown Errors, two of them reachable from a Vue `computed` and one at module evaluation. Collectively they undo the library's central design decision — that failure is a value the consumer routes, not an exception that unwinds an unknown amount of UI.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:206-208 (mixColors, reachable from computed) · useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (mixColors, reachable from computed, byte-identical message string) · useGradientCSS.ts:76 and :128 (CubicBezier / parseTimingFunction, via easingFnOf) · easingCatalogue.ts:103 (CubicBezier, thrown at MODULE EVALUATION — easingCatalogue.ts:198 builds eagerly, and the module is a static import of GradientEasingEditor.vue → GradientVisualizer.vue → the async GradientPane chunk).
defects.mechanism: Result→throw conversion at the wrong altitude. In a Vue computed there is no unwinding target short of the app error boundary, so every one of these is a pane-killer waiting for the right input; the module-level one is a whole-bundle brick waiting for a library data change.
defects.reproduction: N-1 is the realised case for the first two. For the module-level one: NONE — this is a hypothesis, labelled as such (it requires a future malformed `bezierPresets` entry).
defects.proposedCure: One module owns the conversion policy for the gradient feature and its output is a diagnostic VALUE, not an exception: `composables/rampDomain.ts` exporting `clampProgress` plus `sampleCoalescedStops(m): Result<CoalescedSample[], RampIssue>`. The serializers thread the verdict the way `applyCSS` already does, and the component renders a degraded strip with a visible reason instead of vanishing. Build the catalogue lazily behind a memo and skip-with-diagnostic rather than throw. Codify and lint the invariant: `src/` returns Result; `demo/` may throw only from an event handler.

defects.defect: Correction/sharpening of r3's L-6. The `tsconfig.demo.json` `paths` entries do not merely duplicate the exports map — they BYPASS it. Five published subpaths resolve through `paths` and never consult `package.json#exports`, so the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone is a false proof for them: a subpath could be deleted from `exports`, breaking every real consumer, and `npm run typecheck` would stay green.
defects.evidence: `npx tsc --noEmit --traceResolution -p tsconfig.demo.json` — adjacent imports in demo/color-session/picker-color.ts: `@mkbabb/value.js/color` → "'paths' option is specified … matched pattern … Trying substitution './dist/subpaths/color.d.ts'" (exports map NOT consulted); `@mkbabb/value.js/css` → "Found 'package.json' … Entering conditional exports … Using 'exports' subpath './css'" (exports map IS the gate). Programmatic diff: exports = /color /css /easing /math /quantize /transform /value; tspaths = (bare) /color /easing /math /parsing /quantize /transform /units; MISSING FROM paths: /css /value; NOT IN EXPORTS: bare root, /parsing, /units. `ls dist/index.d.ts` → No such file or directory. None of the three dead specifiers is imported anywhere in demo/.
defects.mechanism: Two resolution mechanisms for one package, with `paths` taking precedence over the exports map — a hand-rolled twin of the thing vite.config.ts:37-50 correctly GENERATES from package.json#exports so it cannot drift.
defects.reproduction: Run the traceResolution command above and read the two adjacent resolution blocks; then `ls dist/index.d.ts`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all eight `@mkbabb/value.js*` entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths. TypeScript's self-name resolution already routes them through this package's own `exports` (proven for /css), so removal makes the exports map gate typecheck and runtime identically from one source of truth — exactly the invariant the vite alias generator already achieves. This is not tidying; it restores the gate.

defects.defect: The row's curve NAME — the single datum the component exists to state — measures 3.86:1 (light) and 3.73:1 (dark) against its rendered ground, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for 16.4px/400 text, at every arm and both schemes. The same ink 40px lower (the CSS literal) measures 5.06/5.82 because it sits on an opaque bg-well. The file's own comment at :167-175 diagnoses this exact mechanism ('composited ~2.7:1 (fails AA); a bg-well well floors it') and applies the cure to one of the three runs that share the ink. Because the head's ground is the live translucent pane over a user-driven atmosphere, the ratio is uncertifiable by construction, not merely wrong today.
defects.evidence: Pixel-sampled from the rendered composite (screenshot IS the composite, so no compositing model is needed), WebKit 1440x900 @dsf2, both schemes. Ink resolves to L=0.1098 = rgb(112,89,66) = resolved --muted-foreground, confirming the sample is the true ink. Measured: rail literal (welled, GradientEasingEditor.vue:177) 5.06 light / 5.82 dark PASS; head curve name (unwelled, :136) 3.86 light / 3.73 dark FAIL; family eyebrow (9px, opacity .75) 2.47 light / 2.79 dark FAIL. Independent re-run at 1440x1400 with the row collapsed, sampling a ground patch 20px right of the text: 3.90/3.89 light, 3.75/3.75 dark. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 — 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.' Also PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73. Frames + probe scripts at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingeditor/frames-r3/.
defects.mechanism: a design token name substituted for a rendered fact: an ink specified against --card is drawn against a translucent glass pane over a user-driven atmosphere, so the ratio is neither fixed nor certifiable; the cure (an opaque well) was applied to the value run and withheld from the identity run
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 dsf2 (light, then dark). Screenshot. Crop the head's name span rect (see frames-r3/probe-contrast-targets.json) and any 40x27 patch of plate 20px to its right. Compute WCAG relative luminance: ink = 0.5th percentile (light) / 99.5th (dark), ground = luminance mode. Yields 3.86-3.90 light, 3.73-3.75 dark. Reproduced twice with different geometry.
defects.proposedCure: Do not add a third well. The defect is that one row carries three text runs across two material tiers with one ink. Put the row's identity on one tier and let the tier own certification: either the whole row head sits on the same opaque rung the rail already uses (one surface per row — which also dissolves D3-04 and D3-06), or the identity run takes an ink minted against the live pane through useSafeAccentFn('resting'), the machinery this component's own useSpecimenRows.ts:40 already uses for the decorative glyph but not for the text.

defects.defect: Focusing a COLLAPSED interval row changes zero pixels — measured live in the shipped app at N=4, not in a fixture. The row's overflow-hidden (:114) clips a box-shadow-only focus ring (:228-231, outline:none) whose head is flush with the clip rect on all four sides. Even the OPEN row keeps only one ring edge of four: a 4px band, 244 px². With N stops there are N-1 rows and at most one is open, so N-2 rows are permanently in the zero-indicator state.
defects.evidence: Live at 1512x900 @dsf2, N=4: collapsedFocus = {isFocused:true, matchesFocusVisible:true, outline:'none 3px rgb(28,25,23)', boxShadow:'color(srgb 0.665 0 0.2615 / 0.3) 0 0 0 2px, ... 0 0 8px 0', rowOverflow:'hidden', insets:{t:1,b:1,l:1,r:1}, rowH:41.2, headH:39.2}. PIL/numpy diff of frames-r3/D3-02-focus-collapsed-BEFORE.png vs D3-02-focus-collapsed-AFTER-zero-delta.png: 'px with maxdelta>2: 0 / >4: 0 / >8: 0; bbox(>8): None'. Same diff on the open row: 'px with maxdelta>8: 244; bbox(>8): x 25->944, y 104->107' — a 4px band along the bottom edge only. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84; WCAG 2.4.7/2.4.11. Component comment :220-221 asserts it uses the house ring 'never a bespoke outline'.
defects.mechanism: a box-shadow-only focus indicator (outline explicitly suppressed) on an element whose border box coincides with an ancestor's overflow clip rect on every side — the ring is minted and then 100% clipped
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75% (5 stops, 4 rows, row 0 open). Blur, screenshot a clip around the head of row index 2 (collapsed). Focus that head via .focus(), wait 400ms, screenshot the same clip. Diff the two PNGs: zero pixels differ above a 2/255 threshold. Repeat on row 0 (open): 244 px differ, in a 4px band on the bottom edge only. Script: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: The clip has no job — nothing in the row overflows (.head-glyph's declared overshoot stays inside the 39px head band) and border-radius alone rounds the panel corners. Delete overflow-hidden; better, delete the per-row card box entirely (see D3-05/D3-06), at which point no clip rect exists. If a clip must survive, express focus as outline, which no ancestor overflow clips and which forced-colors preserves and recolors. Seating glass-ui's Collapsible (r1 D-05) gets both for free.

defects.defect: The component's stated §8 law 'one ink per specimen' is falsified in the visible frame: four intervals carrying the IDENTICAL curve and the IDENTICAL literal render four different --motion-accent hues. The glyph is the only differentiated mark in the row (r1 D-08), and it is differentiated by the interval's stop colours, not by its curve — so the list's only colour signal asserts that four identical easings differ.
defects.evidence: Measured at N=4, all four intervals holding the default linear (identical interval.css 'cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)', identical row.name 'linear', identical glyph path): row0 oklch(43.469% 0.0994 159.34), row1 oklch(43.733% 0.0757 189.28), row2 oklch(44.027% 0.0805 220.60), row3 oklch(44.705% 0.1288 250.66); distinctInks: 4. Source: useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 — ink = interpolateStopColors(s0.cssColor, s1.cssColor, fn(0.5), ...), i.e. two of three inputs are the STOP colours. Witnesses: frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png and D3-n4-mobile-390-four-intervals.png. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 (§5.5) — a small mark is 'data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus/selection register or removed'. Round 2's D2-15 proved the collision direction (five curves -> one ink); this is the injection direction and the one a user sees.
defects.mechanism: an identity ink derived from an expression dominated by variables other than the identity it claims to encode; fn(0.5) is neither injective nor well-defined with respect to the specimen
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. Read row.style.getPropertyValue('--motion-accent') on each of the four .interval-head parents, or simply look at frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png: four rows all reading 'linear', four differently-coloured glyphs.
defects.proposedCure: Either derive the ink from something that actually distinguishes curves — the signed area between the curve and the diagonal separates ease-in from ease-out, which fn(0.5) cannot — or delete the per-row ink and let the shared accent carry the glyph. It must not be a stop colour dressed as a curve identity. This also removes the unbounded fn(0.5) evaluation that round 2's D2-01 BLOCKER runs through.

defects.defect: Proximity inversion: sibling interval rows sit 8px apart while the parts INSIDE one row sit 10px apart. Elements in one group are further from each other than from elements of another group, so at N>1 the rows read as one continuous striped block. The per-row card border — a boundary this composition's binding table gives a count of zero — is currently the only thing compensating for the inverted spacing scale.
defects.evidence: Measured live at N=4: interRowGaps [8, 8, 8] (GradientEasingEditor.vue:107, 'flex flex-col gap-2'); panelGap 10px (:146, gap-2.5); headPad '8px 12px 8px 12px'; panelChildren ramp 436x20 @y592.13, strip 436x71.42 @y622.13, rail 436x32 @y703.55; intraGaps [10, 10]. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 (§5.3) — 'Header->headline uses title gap; headline->next semantic section uses section gap' (two named, different quantities). OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 gives Gradient boundaries [] / dividing line none. Witness: frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png. Probe: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs, probe-rhythm.json.
defects.mechanism: one spacing rung used for two opposite semantic distances (between-group and within-group), with a forbidden boundary line added to compensate for the resulting ambiguity
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. For each pair of adjacent .interval-head parents compute next.getBoundingClientRect().y - prev.getBoundingClientRect().bottom -> 8.00. Read getComputedStyle on the open row's [id^='easing-interval-'] panel -> rowGap '10px'. Script: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Fix the rhythm and the boundary dies with it: inter-row gap must exceed intra-row gap by at least one rung, letting spacing plus material carry grouping — exactly the disposition the binding table already records for Gradient ('grouping job: meniscus, stop seats and code/action interval carry grouping'). Then strip the per-row card box, which also dissolves D3-02's clip and D3-05's radius question.

defects.defect: OWNER MARK OM-4 / MT-F030, carried and sharpened: the radius incoherence is intra-element and state-dependent, not merely cross-element. One class, one token (--radius-card 16px), two boxes 8px apart in the same list — the collapsed row renders curvature 0.391 and the open row 0.081, a 4.83x swing that fires on click with no transition. Both readings the owner named ('too rounded in some areas, not rounded enough in others') are present in the SAME declaration.
defects.evidence: Measured live at N=4: open row 462 x 196.36 @ border-radius 16px -> r/min-dimension 0.081; closed row 462 x 40.94 @ border-radius 16px -> 0.391; ratio 4.83x. Declaration: GradientEasingEditor.vue:114 'rounded-card border border-card-edge overflow-hidden'. Owner mark: ROOT-FINDINGS.md:1421, witness audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png. The existing registry rows (DEFECT-LEDGER.md:29659, :31873) are a cross-element census at N=1 (five registers 0/4/6/16/9999px) and contain no state-dependent measurement. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 (§5.8) — 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent... measured rects... token presence alone cannot close a row.' Canon gap already named at DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:73 and design-canon-census.md:316 (C-4).
defects.mechanism: a size-blind absolute radius rung applied to a box whose height varies 4.8x by disclosure state, so rendered curvature is an accident of state rather than a register
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. getComputedStyle(row).borderRadius is '16px' for every .interval-head parent; getBoundingClientRect().height is 196.36 for the open row and 40.94 for each collapsed row. Divide. Script: frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs (register block) and probe-rhythm.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: The radius derivation law the canon gap already demands must be stated in terms of CURVATURE, not absolute radius — corner curvature holds constant or grows with box size, never inverts — and a box whose height is state-dependent may not carry a size-blind radius rung. Structurally the cure is the same one D3-04 and D3-06 reach: the interval rows should not be boxes at all. Deleting the per-row card removes four of the instrument's six radius registers.

defects.defect: OWNER MARK OM-13 / MT-F037, carried and mechanised: the bg-well rung is applied against a TRANSLUCENT pane, so its declared 'opaque tone-step of the plate' inverts sign between schemes (+0.117 L in light, the well ADVANCES; -0.038 L in dark, it RECEDES) and changes hue family (pink plate -> cream well, ~60 deg apart). That is why the owner's light-mode crop reads as a foreign raised slab rather than a recessed field. Separately, the producer census shows glass-ui 7.0.0 Input has ZERO slots, so the cure is a marked glass-forward ask, not a consume.
defects.evidence: Pixel-sampled from the rendered composite, 1440x900 @dsf2. Light: plate behind the head rgb(240,184,202) L=0.5703; readout well rgb(224,215,206) L=0.6878; delta +0.1174. Dark: plate rgb(119,74,85) L=0.0947; well rgb(76,65,57) L=0.0567; delta -0.0380. Magnitudes differ 3.1x. The row's own background measures rgba(0,0,0,0), i.e. the surrounding 'plate' is glass over atmosphere, not --card. Token recipe: demo/DESIGN.md:98 — '--well-bg: color-mix(in oklab, var(--card) 92%, var(--foreground) 8%)', declared as 'an opaque tone-step of the plate'. Site: GradientEasingEditor.vue:176. Producer census: @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 exports ./forms -> ./components/input; InputProps has disabled/invalid/readonly/size; compiled dist/Input-9BlLluik.js renders classes ['input','input','input','field-control glass-defined'] and 'slots: false'. Zero demo files consume field-control. Owner mark ROOT-FINDINGS.md:1564, witness owner-marked/OM-13-easing-readout-not-glass-input.png. Same shape recurs at MixResultDisplay.vue:31 and App.vue:362 (DEFECT-LEDGER.md:31542).
defects.mechanism: a material rung defined relative to an opaque token (--card) applied on a translucent host, so the step's sign and hue are set by the ambient atmosphere rather than by the token — the same class of defect as D3-01
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 dsf2 in light, then dark. Screenshot. Sample a 12x12 patch of the head band background and the central 15% of .readout-rail; convert to WCAG relative luminance. Light: 0.5703 -> 0.6878 (+0.1174). Dark: 0.0947 -> 0.0567 (-0.0380). Producer half: node -e on node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/Input-9BlLluik.js -> /renderSlot/.test(src) === false.
defects.proposedCure: Two halves. OURS: stop applying an opaque --card-derived rung on a translucent pane — the well tier must be defined relative to the surface it is actually drawn on, or the row must supply an opaque host first (which one-surface-per-row, D3-04, gives for free). GLASS (marked ask, relayed on the standing BH/BI inbox with M3): Input must accept a trailing adornment slot, or glass must ship a read-only value/code field with an action rail. Three consumer sites share the shape. A local restyle here would be precisely the masking fallback the standing edict forbids.

defects.defect: At 320px — an arm the canon names explicitly — the SHORTEST literal the catalogue can produce truncates by 26.6%. Composed with round 1's D-04 (the widest cubic-bezier overflows the 360px box by 27.7px at 1512px), there is no viewport width at which the component's stated 'one-literal law' holds for all 27 specimens. The only recovery is :title, a native tooltip unavailable on every device that is actually 320px wide.
defects.evidence: Measured, WebKit, four arms, default linear interval: 1440 desktop code clientW 360 / scrollW 360, not truncated, strip hidden 70.6%; 720 (= 1440 at 200% browser zoom) 360/360, not truncated, 70.6%; 390 mobile 222/222, not truncated, 79.9%; 320 (canon arm) clientW 152 / scrollW 207, TRUNCATED 26.6%, strip hidden 84.6%. 'cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)' is 24 chars, the shortest literal the catalogue emits. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78 names the 1440/390/320/400%-zoom arms and requires live values to 'reserve their widest legal representation'. WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA) also binds at 320px; a CSS literal is text, not content requiring 2D layout. Site: GradientEasingEditor.vue:177. Witness: frames-r3/D3-07-reflow-320.png; probe frames-r3/probe-arms.mjs, probe-arms.json.
defects.mechanism: reservation allocated to the wrong element: two 24px ghost icons win a width fight against the payload the row exists to export, with no wrap or scroll fallback at any width
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient in a 320x640 WebKit context. Read the .readout-rail code element: clientWidth 152, scrollWidth 207 -> truncated. Repeat at 1440, 720 and 390 for the comparison row. Script: frames-r3/probe-arms.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: The literal is the protagonist of the rail; the two icons are support. Reserve the literal's widest legal width and let the rail wrap its actions beneath it at narrow widths. Since the rail is being rebuilt for D3-06 anyway, the producer field should own wrapping or scrolling of its own value. title is not a design.

defects.defect: Deleting a gradient stop while a later interval row is open leaves the Easing section with ZERO open rows — an undesigned dead state. openInterval dangles past the last row, v-show matches nothing, and the section's entire working surface (ramp, specimen strip, literal, copy, authoring stage) evaporates silently in response to an action taken on a different instrument.
defects.evidence: Live repro, 1440x900 @dsf2. Before: rows 4, expanded [false,false,false,true], openCount 1, visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)'], visibleRamps 1, visibleStrips 1, sectionH 344.5. After deleting the 50% stop: rows 3, expanded [false,false,false], openCount 0, visibleLiterals [], visibleRamps 0, visibleStrips 0, sectionH 139.6, pageErrors [], consoleErrors []. Source: GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 seeds ref(0) and nothing restores it; useGradientModel.ts:88-98 truncates intervals from the END ('intervals.value.length = needed'); GradientEasingEditor.vue:144 v-show='openInterval === row.index'. serializeIntervalRamp (useGradientCSS.ts:236-238) returns null for the out-of-range index rather than throwing, which is why this presents as silence. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 (§5) — 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace.' Witness: frames-r3/D3-08-dead-state-zero-open-rows.png; probe frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs, probe-removal.json.
defects.mechanism: UI disclosure state keyed on array position while the model truncates that array from the end, so a structural edit can strand the state outside the row set with no restoration path
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75% (5 stops, 4 rows). Click the LAST row's head (openInterval = 3). Focus the stop handle labelled 'Gradient stop at 50%', press Delete. Result: 3 rows, all collapsed, openCount 0, section height 344.5 -> 139.6px, no error of any kind. Script: frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: The accordion's open state must name an INTERVAL, not a slot. Give intervals stable ids the way stops already have them (useGradientModel.ts:117, id: uid()) and key openInterval / tuneOpen / copiedIndex / the update-interval emit on the id. Deleting stop k then removes exactly one interval and leaves every other row's identity, open state and disclosure intact. A glass-ui Collapsible keyed by id (r1 D-05) gets this for free.

defects.defect: Authored curves migrate to a different interval on insert: the curve follows the array slot, not the interval. Authoring ease-in-out across the whole gradient and then inserting one midpoint leaves ease-in-out governing 0-25% while the remaining 75% silently reverts to linear. No notification, no undo affordance, no mark on the affected row. Round 1 filed this as an explicitly labelled HYPOTHESIS; it reproduces.
defects.evidence: Live repro, WebKit 1512x900. afterAuthor: heads ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out'], visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)']. afterInsertMid (one click at 25% of .gradient-rail): heads ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out', '2 -> 3 linear'], visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)']. Source: useGradientModel.ts:116-119 addStop inserts position-sorted while :88-98 appends new intervals at the END; GradientEasingEditor.vue keys openInterval (:61), tuneOpen (:84), copiedIndex (:95) and the update-interval emit contract (:49) on array position. The component's own header comment at :52-53 claims 'identity derived from the interval, the truth' — true of useSpecimenRows, false of every stateful ref and of the model beneath it. Probe: scratchpad probe-state.mjs (same recipe as frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs).
defects.mechanism: array position used as entity identity across a structural mutation that renumbers the array, so authored data silently reassigns itself to a different entity
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (2 stops, 1 interval spanning 0-100%). Press the 'in-out' specimen tile in the css family: head reads '1 -> 2 ease-in-out', literal cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1). Click .gradient-rail at 25%.
