Result: two rows, ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out', '2 -> 3 linear'] — the authored curve now governs 0-25% and 75% of the gradient has reverted to linear.
defects.proposedCure: Same root as D3-08: stable interval ids, and this component keys on the id. It is a model change, but the design assertion is this component's — 'a row is an interval, not a slot' — and it is currently untrue.

defects.defect: Reservation is inverted within one row: the head holds 51.3% of its width as empty slack for a 6-character word, 30px above a catalogue that hides 70.6-84.6% of itself at every arm. Reservation is allocated by CSS accident (flex-1 on the identity span) rather than by role.
defects.evidence: Measured, 1440 arm, open row: headW 460.00; nameSpan width 296.53 (flex-1 min-w-0, GradientEasingEditor.vue:136); name text width 60.55 (Range.getBoundingClientRect on 'linear'); slack 235.98 = 51.3% of the head. Strip in the same row: clientW 436, scrollW 1482, hidden 70.6%. The worst-case name is bounded: specimenNameFor (easingCatalogue.ts:228-229) returns the tile id or 'custom', 6-16 characters. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 (§5.7) — 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities.' Witness: frames-r3/D3-n4-mobile-390-four-intervals.png; probe frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.
defects.mechanism: layout reservation derived from a flex growth rule rather than from the datum's legal width, so slack accumulates on the shortest run and starves the longest
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. On the open row's head, read the last span's getBoundingClientRect().width (296.53) and a Range over its contents (60.55). Difference 235.98 against a 460px head. Script: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Size the identity run to its own legal width and give the recovered ~236px to the catalogue, which is the element actually starved. This is subsumed by the /easing chassis cure (round 2 D2-02) but is independently correct in the current housing.

defects.defect: The disclosure buys nothing and costs +117% of the route's DOM per three added intervals. Every authoring stage is fully mounted before the user has pressed anything and stays mounted when its row collapses, so the disclosure reduces neither cost nor attention — it only buries the editor two levels deep.
defects.evidence: Measured on /#/gradient, same page, before/after adding three stops: specimen rows 1 -> 4; specimen tiles rendered 27 -> 108; EasingPicker plot SVGs mounted 1 -> 4; .fading-scroll ports 1 -> 4; document elements (whole route) 511 -> 1109 (+598, +117%); visible focusables 55 -> 67. At N=3 with nothing disclosed: stagesVisible [false,false,false], stagesMounted (svg) 6. Sites: GradientEasingEditor.vue:161 (strip inside v-for), :204-213 (stage v-show), header comment :16-18 defends always-alive pickers on state-continuity grounds although EasingAuthoringStage is fully controlled. Probes: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs, probe-tune (scratchpad), probe-n4.json.
defects.mechanism: a global module constant (the 27-tile catalogue) and a heavyweight editor instantiated once per row instead of once per editor, with v-show rather than v-if, so the composition pays full mount cost for hidden duplicates
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, record document.querySelectorAll('*').length (511) and .specimen-tile count (27). Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. Re-record: 1109 and 108. Query [id^='easing-authoring-'] svg with nothing disclosed: non-zero. Script: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: One catalogue for the editor, positioned by the open row — the classic single-inspector arrangement — rather than one catalogue per row. And either the disclosure is real (v-if plus one named motion family from demo/styles/animations.css) or it is not a disclosure and the editor is always visible, which is what the /easing chassis of round 2's D2-02 wants.

defects.defect: Authoring disclosure is per-row sticky with no indicator, and leaves stale aria-expanded='true' on display:none controls. The Easing section is silently in two different modes depending on which row you opened, and the only open-state cue is a colour change in the row's data-derived ink — so 'authoring is open' is a different hue on every row.
defects.evidence: Measured live, 3 intervals: tune disclosed on row 0 -> tuneExpanded ['true','false','false'], stagesVisible [true,false,false]. Switch to row 1 -> tuneExpanded ['true','false','false'] (row 0's HIDDEN button still advertises expanded), tuneVisible [false,true,false], stagesVisible [false,false,false]. Switch back to row 0 -> tuneExpanded ['true','false','false'], stagesVisible [true,false,false]. Source: GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 (tuneOpen is a Record<number, boolean> keyed by array position, so it also inherits D3-09's migration bug), :190 (.rail-btn--on), :289-291 (colour-only on-state). Probe: scratchpad probe-tune.mjs.
defects.mechanism: per-row modal state with no cross-row indicator, plus an ARIA state assertion left true on a control removed from the accessibility tree
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, add two stops. Press the sliders glyph on row 0 (tune discloses). Click row 1's head. Read aria-expanded on all buttons labelled 'Author a custom curve': row 0's is still 'true' while its offsetParent is null. Click row 0's head again: the editor reappears with no cue that it would.
defects.proposedCure: Disclosure state belongs to the interval identity (D3-08/D3-09's ids), and the on-state needs a non-colour channel — the pressed register the producer Button/Toggle already owns — so the state is learnable across rows. This disappears entirely if the hand-rolled disclosure is replaced by glass-ui Collapsible/ExpandableContainer (r1 D-05).

defects.defect: Disabled, busy and error are not states this component has. There is no disabled binding, no pending/loading treatment and no error rendering anywhere in the 296 lines or the four children; the awaited clipboard write has neither a pending state nor an error branch. A state that was never designed is a design defect.
defects.evidence: Enumerated live on the running route: elements matching '.interval-head[disabled], .rail-btn[disabled]' = 0; elements with [aria-busy] = 0; [aria-live]/[role=status]/[role=alert] inside this component = 0. Source cross-check: GradientEasingEditor.vue:100-103 awaits copy() with copiedRow gated only on copyStatus === 'success' (:96-98), so copyStatus === 'error' renders nothing. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 — 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.' Probe: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs (hasDisabled / ariaBusy / liveRegions block).
defects.mechanism: the state space was enumerated as {collapsed, open} only; failure, pending and disabled were never modelled, so the surface silently reports success for every outcome
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient and evaluate document.querySelectorAll('[aria-busy]').length -> 0, and '.interval-head[disabled], .rail-btn[disabled]' -> 0. Grep the SFC for 'disabled', 'error', 'pending' -> no rendering path. Script: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: A stable accessible name plus outcome in a polite status region owned by the instrument (the same region the CSS section's copy already needs), and a real disabled treatment for the case where an interval cannot be authored. Consuming glass-ui Button/Input — both of which already carry disabled and invalid axes — supplies most of this at the root instead of per-instance.

defects.defect: Unguarded :hover washes on surfaces reachable by coarse pointers, where the house has established the guard idiom in one file. On real iOS Safari a :hover rule with no @media (hover: hover) guard persists after tap until the user taps elsewhere, leaving the row visually 'hovered' with no meaning.
defects.evidence: Sites: GradientEasingEditor.vue:225-227 (.interval-head:hover) and :281-284 (.rail-btn:hover), neither guarded. Census: 'grep -rn "@media (hover" demo/ | wc -l' -> 1 (demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue — the house DOES have the idiom). Workbench files with :hover and no guard: ImageEyedropper.vue, GradientEasingEditor.vue, EasingSpecimenStrip.vue. Attempted reproduction on a coarse-pointer arm (hasTouch: true; matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)') -> true, '(hover: hover)' -> false): hoverBefore 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', hoverAfterTap 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' — headless WebKit does not emulate iOS Safari's hover-persists-after-tap behaviour.
defects.mechanism: a pointer-capability-dependent style declared unconditionally, with no arm in the audit matrix able to decide it
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled HYPOTHESIS. Headless WebKit at hasTouch:true did not reproduce sticky hover (computed background unchanged after touchscreen.tap). Deciding it requires a real iOS Safari arm, which is absent from the mega-tranche visual matrix — the same class of coverage gap round 1 recorded for forced-colors.
defects.proposedCure: Wrap both washes in @media (hover: hover), matching the one existing house precedent — or, better, delete them along with the hand-rolled controls when the row consumes glass-ui Collapsible + Button, whose hover treatments are the producer's problem. Separately: add a real coarse-pointer arm to the visual matrix so this class of finding can be decided rather than hypothesised.

result.strongestDefect: D3-01 — the row's curve NAME, the one datum the component exists to state, renders at 3.86:1 (light) and 3.73:1 (dark), below WCAG AA at every arm and both schemes, at the app's own default seed. The same ink, in the same file, forty pixels lower, was already found to fail, already explained in a nine-line comment (":167-175 — composited ~2.7:1 (fails AA); a bg-well well floors it"), and already cured with an opaque well. The cure was applied to the value and withheld from the identity. Because the identity's ground is the live translucent pane over a user-driven atmosphere rather than an opaque surface, its contrast is not merely wrong today — it is uncertifiable by construction, which is exactly what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 forbids when it says "a token name is not evidence." D3-02 is the more severe failure in kind (a focus indicator painting literally zero pixels is a total loss, not a degraded one) and is now proved in the running application at N=4 rather than in a fixture.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded so the next seat does not re-spend the budget, the axes I attacked at N>1 and could NOT break: (1) route destruction on stop add/remove — 3 adds plus a keyboard delete, N 1->4->3, pageErrors [], consoleErrors [] (excluding the app's own dev-config warning), tryAgain false throughout; round 2's D2-01 is specific to the back-family/authoring path, not to N. (2) Document horizontal overflow at N=4 — false on all four arms including 320px; the 1482px strip stays contained. (3) Tab-stop explosion at N=4 — visible focusables 55 -> 67 (+12), not 55 -> 136, because collapsed panels are display:none and their 81 extra tiles are correctly out of the tab order; round 2's 28-of-52 figure is an N=1 fact and does not multiply. (4) Accessible names at N=4 — per-row unique head labels, both rail buttons labelled, ramp role="img" with a label, decorative marks aria-hidden; the route's one nameless button is not in this subtree. (5) Target sizes across 1440/720/390/320 — rail buttons 24x24 and tiles 45.2x43.8 at every arm; neither shrinks on mobile. (6) verbatimModuleSyntax — every type-only import at :27-40 is `import type`. (7) Vue 3.5 idiom — reactive props destructure used correctly at :42-46, no defineModel round-trip in this file. (8) Motion tokenisation — --duration-fast / --ease-standard declared rather than literal at :222-231 and :269-291. (9) No god module (296 lines, three children plus one composable and one catalogue, each with one job). (10) No legacy shims, aliases, dual paths or masking fallbacks in any of the five files. (11) Reduced motion honoured via the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D3-01 — the colour instrument is built on the wrong material tier. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:15` reserves `glass-floating` for Structural glass (dock/header/plate) and mandates the Instrument-veil tier for "controls genuinely over live color" — "denser neutral veil with named alpha/clarity levers; no drop shadow". The overlay measures `background-color: oklab(…/0.808)` (19.2% transparent), `backdrop-filter: blur(11px) saturate(1.6)`, plus a drop shadow: three breaches in one declaration. Consequence, measured from the rendered PNG: the ImageDropZone preview `` bleeds through the chrome bar and the letterbox bands as a 60%-oversaturated phantom duplicate of the very image being sampled ((244,187,181) and (195,236,181) sampled from the chrome bar are the fixture's own red and green quadrants), and the readout's ground becomes arbitrary user photography — measured 3.95:1 against the red half, below the 4.5:1 AA floor. A `saturate(1.6)` veil inside the one instrument in the product whose entire product is colour truth is a category error, and the source comment at `ImageEyedropper.vue:4-7` records it as a deliberate T.W3-1 decision.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these suspects were tested and cleared, so the register is not padded: (1) Coarse-pointer tap targets are SOUND — measured 44×44 for all three DockControls on iPhone 13 (`{"pointerCoarse":true,"btns":[{"Close eyedropper",44,44},{"Add to palette",44,44},{"Apply as current color",44,44}]}`), despite `--dock-control-size` being undefined outside the dock. (2) prefers-reduced-motion for MOTION is honoured — under `reducedMotion: "reduce"` the canvas `transitionProperty` drops `transform` entirely (`"opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow 0.1s"`), `swatch-pop` measures 0.00001s, and `useInertiaGesture:131-142` owns an explicit PRM branch on top of glass-ui `useRAFLoop{pauseWhenHidden}`. No animation was deleted; the scoped keyframe stays scoped. (3) `--z-controls` is NOT a dangling token — my hypothesis was withdrawn after finding `--z-controls: 20` shipped in `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css` and the idiom documented at `demo/DESIGN.md:302`. (4) The WatercolorDot's AT semantics are CORRECT per DECISIONS.md B-25 — glass-ui 7 renders `<span aria-hidden="true" pointer-events:none>` with `forced-color-adjust: none` (measured `swatchForcedAdjust:"none"`, `swatchBg: rgb(255,0,0)`), so the specimen survives forced colors while the text carries the value. (5) Module hygiene is SOUND — 299 lines across three focused composables with real dependency injection (not a god module), `verbatimModuleSyntax` respected, `useTemplateRef` + reactive props destructure used idiomatically, no back-compat shims, no new `shared/` dir. (6) `docOverflowX: 0` at 100% and 200% zoom; zero page errors in every matrix. (7) Object-URL leak and tainted-canvas CORS — innocent, re-confirmed: the only `createObjectURL` calls in `demo/` are `palettes/export.ts:88,126`, each revoked, and the image path is a same-origin `data:` URL from FileReader.

defects.defect: The eyedropper is built on the Structural-glass tier (`glass-floating`) where VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:15 mandates the Instrument-veil tier for 'controls genuinely over live color'. Measured overlay: alpha 0.808, backdrop-filter blur(11px) saturate(1.6), plus a drop shadow — three breaches of one canon row. The underlying preview image bleeds through the chrome bar and the letterbox bands as a 60%-oversaturated phantom duplicate of the specimen, and the readout's ground becomes user photography at a measured 3.95:1 (below AA 4.5:1). The same surface is simultaneously chrome bar and specimen well, breaching 'One surface has one tier' (VC:19), which also requires the specimen well to be opaque.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (`glass-floating`), source comment lines 4-7 recording the choice. Live computed style: `OVERLAY: {"zIndex":"130","bg":"oklab(0.936403 0.00557132 0.0133027 / 0.808)","backdrop":"blur(11px) saturate(1.6)","shadow":"oklab(…/0.3) 0px 1px 0px 0px inset, …","border":"1px solid oklab(…/0.05)","radius":"12px"}`. Pixel scan of shots/D-02-desktop-pinned.png at device y=442 (behind the readout): cssx=400→(244,187,181), cssx=470..650→(195,236,181) — the fixture's own red and green quadrants. WCAG: rgb(112,89,66) on (244,187,181) = 3.95:1 FAIL; on (195,236,181) = 5.00:1; on the card surface (244,229,224) = 5.36:1. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:15 and :19 and :82.
defects.mechanism: wrong material tier — chrome vocabulary applied to an instrument surface, so the ground behind text and the ground around the specimen are both supplied by arbitrary user content
defects.reproduction: Start the dev server; navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/extract; upload docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/shots/D-00-fixture-quad64.png; click the preview to open the eyedropper. Read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[class*="z-popover"]'))` → backgroundColor alpha 0.808, backdropFilter 'blur(11px) saturate(1.6)'. Screenshot and sample the chrome-bar strip: it carries the uploaded image's colours. Driver: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe-CHD-p2.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the overlay to the two tiers the canon already names: an OPAQUE Specimen well for the stage (killing the bleed, the phantom duplicate and the unbounded readout ground in one move) and a single dense, neutral Instrument-veil strip with named alpha/clarity levers and no drop shadow for the controls. Not a per-instance alpha bump — a tier change at the root, so the rule is legible from the class name.

defects.defect: The confirmation animation for the component's only two commit actions fires exactly once per session and never resets. `@animationend="swatchPulse = false"` is bound to `<WatercolorDot>`, but glass-ui 7.0.0 declares `inheritAttrs: false` and forwards only `class` and `style` from `useAttrs`, so the listener is never attached to any element. `swatchPulse` latches true forever: every Add-to-palette and Apply after the first is completely silent, and the `.swatch-pulse` rule permanently overrides the `w-7 h-7` utility.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:18-23 (`@animationend`), :285-289 (`.swatch-pulse{width:1.75rem;height:1.75rem;animation:swatch-pop 0.65s … forwards}`). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js:82 `inheritAttrs: !1` with `setup(e){ let t=e, n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style) …` — only class and style consumed. Measured transcript: `A| ADD#1 => "swatchClass":"shrink-0 transition-transform swatch-pulse watercolor-swatch"` / `A| 1.65s after ADD#1 => …swatch-pulse…` / `A| ADD#2 => …swatch-pulse…` (animation is 0.65s, so 1.65s later it is long over and the class is still on).
defects.mechanism: event listener silently dropped by a producer component's `inheritAttrs:false`; the success state is encoded as a transient CSS class whose removal depends on that dropped event
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover twice and click to pin, then click the 'Add to palette' button. Wait 1.5s and read `document.querySelector('[class*="z-popover"] [data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]').className` — still contains `swatch-pulse`. Click Add again: no animation, no feedback of any kind. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Stop encoding a commit result as a one-shot animation whose reset depends on an event the design system does not forward. Derive the swatch's state from the data — a durable 'in palette' mark computed from the palette store — so the confirmation is a rendered fact that survives, replays and needs no teardown. If a pulse is still wanted it belongs on a plain element the consumer owns, not on a producer face with `inheritAttrs:false`.

defects.defect: A pinned sample keeps reporting its old value and old magnification after the transform moves. `drawLoupe` is called only from `showLoupeAt`, which is called only from `onTap`/`onHover`; there is no watcher on panX/panY/zoom. Wheel and trackpad zoom never emit `pointerdown`, so they never trip the unpin handler — the image slides under a stationary reticle while the readout and the loupe content stay frozen. The state the component presents as a commitment (it grows two commit buttons) is the state in which it is least truthful.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:160,170 (only call sites of showLoupeAt); ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60; ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (unpin is `pointerdown`-only). Measured: `A| TAP GREEN again => {"readout":"lab(87.818534365028% -79.27106","pinned":true,"loupeInk":9683,"transform":"translate(65px, 0px) scale(5.90625)"}` then `A| WHEEL ctrl-zoom while pinned => {"readout":"lab(87.818534365028% -79.27106","pinned":true,"loupeInk":9683,"transform":"translate(53.66px, -10.0088px) scale(6.26063)"}`. Source texel under the unmoved reticle centre: floor((381-65)/5.90625)=53 before, floor((381-53.66)/6.26063)=52 after. Reported value unchanged.
defects.mechanism: pinned state is a mode flag rather than a derived value; nothing recomputes the sample when the viewport transform it depends on changes
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover then click to pin a pixel. Without releasing the pin, ctrl+scroll (trackpad pinch-zoom) over the stage. The reticle stays put, the readout is unchanged, the loupe canvas is byte-identical, but the transform has changed — so the reticle now sits over a different source texel than the one being reported. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the `pinned`/`justUnpinned` mode flags with one `sample: {ix, iy} | null` owned by the sampler, and derive the readout, the swatch, the loupe position and the loupe content from it via a `watchEffect` on `(sample, panX, panY, zoom)`. The stale-pin case then cannot be expressed.

defects.defect: Pinned and unpinned are pixel-identical under forced colors. The only differentiators are `border-color: var(--primary)` and a `box-shadow` ring; forced colors overrides the border colour to the system value and suppresses box-shadow entirely, so the committed state and the live-tracking state become indistinguishable.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:262-276 (`.loupe` / `.loupe-pinned` differ only in border-color and box-shadow). Measured under `forcedColors: 'active'`, both states in one run: `FORCED-COLORS unpinned loupe: {"pinnedClass":false,"borderColor":"rgb(0, 0, 0)","borderWidth":"2px","boxShadow":"none","outline":"none rgb(0, 0, 0)"}` and `FORCED-COLORS pinned loupe: {"pinnedClass":true,"borderColor":"rgb(0, 0, 0)","borderWidth":"2px","boxShadow":"none","outline":"none rgb(0, 0, 0)"}` — identical in every property. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only' and :84 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.mechanism: state encoded only in colour and shadow, both of which the forced-colors palette erases
defects.reproduction: Launch Chromium with `forcedColors: 'active'`, open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover twice, read the `.loupe` computed style, then click to pin and read it again. The two objects are equal. Driver: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe-CHD-p2.mjs section C plus the CHD-p3 forced-colors run described in §3.4 of the report.
defects.proposedCure: Give the pinned state a geometric register the forced-colors palette cannot erase — draw the reticle and its committed variant inside the loupe's own canvas as a contrast-safe double stroke (light-over-dark) rather than as a CSS border-colour swap on a brand hue. That single move also fixes D3-05 and supplies the reticle the canon requires.

defects.defect: The loupe's own boundary has no contrast law and is measured far below the 3:1 floor for a non-text UI boundary. The unpinned ring is a 50%-alpha near-black; the pinned ring is `var(--primary)`, a brand hue. Both are drawn over arbitrary user photography, so neither can be guaranteed at any ratio — and a brand-hue state marker vanishes entirely when the user samples a pixel of that hue.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:265 (`border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-color) 50%, transparent)`) and :274 (`border-color: var(--primary)`). Measured computed value: `"loupeBorder":"2px solid color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.5)"`. WCAG ratios: pinned olive-green ring vs the red field it sits on in shots/D-02-desktop-pinned.png = 1.52:1; unpinned ring vs a blue field = 1.73:1. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 — 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.'
defects.mechanism: a single-stroke boundary in a fixed colour drawn over content the design cannot constrain
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01) over the four-quadrant fixture; hover the blue quadrant — the unpinned ring is effectively invisible. Pin on the red quadrant and compare shots/D-02-desktop-pinned.png: the olive ring computes to 1.52:1 against the field.
defects.proposedCure: Draw every boundary that sits over live content as a two-tone stroke (an inner light stroke and an outer dark stroke, or a dashed alternation) so contrast is guaranteed against any ground by construction. Same treatment for the reticle. Never mark state over user content with a single brand-hue stroke.

defects.defect: `LOUPE_SIZE = 110` is a hard CSS-px constant inside a container-scaled stage, so the magnifier does not scale with the instrument. At 200% browser zoom the stage measures 508x238 and the 110px loupe occupies 46.2% of its height — a flat coloured ball that occludes the region it claims to magnify.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/constants.ts:8 (`export const LOUPE_SIZE = 110`); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196 (loupeStyle hard-codes width/height from it). Measured at 720x450 @2x (= 1440x900 at 200% zoom): `C| zoom200+PRM+forced-colors viewport box: {"x":106,"y":236.984375,"w":508,"h":238}` → 110/238 = 46.2%. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/shots/D-04-zoom200-forced-colors.png. Canon: docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.8 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent.'
defects.mechanism: fixed-px ornament inside a container-scaled stage — no relation is expressed at all
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper at a 720x450 viewport (equivalent to 200% zoom on 1440x900), hover and pin. The loupe circle is nearly half the stage height. See shots/D-04-zoom200-forced-colors.png.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the loupe diameter from the stage's own measured box (a clamped fraction of `min(stageW, stageH)`), the same way the fit-zoom is derived, so the magnifier holds a constant proportional relation to the specimen at every viewport and zoom level.

defects.defect: The stage has exactly one layout — a full-width top bar over a full-bleed image — and no response to a short-wide container. At 200% browser zoom the image renders 238x238 inside a 508x238 stage, leaving 53% of the instrument's own well empty.
defects.evidence: Measured stage `{"w":508,"h":238}` with transform `translate(135px, 0px) scale(3.71875)` → image 238x238; 1 − (238·238)/(508·238) = 0.531. demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useInertiaGesture.ts:152-167 (`fitToViewport` only centres; nothing re-flows the chrome). Frame: shots/D-04-zoom200-forced-colors.png. Canon: docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-10 ('form acreage exceeds preview') and §5.3.
defects.mechanism: single-layout stage; the chrome bar always consumes the full width regardless of the stage's aspect
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper at 720x450 (200% zoom on a 1440x900 window). Measure the viewport box and the canvas transform: the specimen fills 47% of the stage. See shots/D-04-zoom200-forced-colors.png.
defects.proposedCure: Let the chrome respond to the stage's aspect — a vertical control rail beside the specimen when the stage is short and wide, the current top bar when it is tall. One breakpoint on the measured container, not on the viewport, so the same rule holds at 200% zoom and in the split-column layout.

defects.defect: The unpin flag survives a pan and swallows the next clean tap. `justUnpinned` is set on every `pointerdown` while pinned but consumed only inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap` (`didMove` is true), so the flag stays set and eats the following genuine sample. The readout still updates from hover, so the user gets partial feedback implying success while the commit affordances never appear.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :151-156 (consumed only in onTap), :178-184 (set on every pointerdown while pinned); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when `!didMove`). Measured: `A| DRAG-pan while pinned => {"pinned":false,"actionBtns":1,…}` then `A| TAP GREEN (.75,.35) after pan => {"pinned":false,"actionBtns":1,…}` (swallowed) then `A| TAP GREEN again => {"pinned":true,"actionBtns":3,…}`.
defects.mechanism: a latch consumed on only one of its two exit paths — the drag path leaves it armed
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01). Hover, click to pin. Then press, drag ~40px to pan, release. Now move to a different quadrant and click once: the readout changes but no pin occurs and the Add/Apply buttons do not appear. Click again in the same place: it pins. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the flag with the mode. Under the `sample: {ix,iy} | null` model of D3-03, a pointerdown clears `sample` and a tap sets it; there is no cross-gesture latch to leave armed, and no capture-phase DOM listener reaching around the gesture composable to implement it.

defects.defect: The eyedropper cannot be opened by keyboard, by construction. Its only opener is `ImageDropZone`, which sets `:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"` and gates its Enter/Space handler on `!disableClick` — and `disableClick` is exactly the condition (a preview exists) under which the eyedropper becomes openable. So the control leaves the tab order and loses its key handler at precisely the moment it acquires the sampling capability, while still announcing 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:19 (`:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"`), :20 (aria-label 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'), :22 (`@keydown.enter.space.prevent="!disableClick && openFilePicker()"`); demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:22 (`:disable-click="!!session.previewDataUrl.value"`) and :25 (`@click="session.previewDataUrl.value && (eyedropperActive = true)"`). Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:198 'Eyedropper and sampler have keyboard/numeric alternatives' and :126 (the image-sampler axis row requiring named x/y controls with Home/End plus a reticle).
defects.mechanism: the same boolean both enables the capability and removes the control's keyboard surface
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/extract, upload an image, then Tab through the page: the preview region is never focused (tabindex -1) and Enter/Space on it do nothing. There is no other opener in the DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Make the sampling entry a real named control rather than a click handler on a role=button div whose tabindex is conditioned away. Then give the overlay the coordinate model the canon already specifies (named x/y numeric fields with Home/End bound to the same `sample` value as the reticle and the readout), which opens the capability keyboard-to-keyboard instead of bolting a shortcut onto a pointer-only instrument.

defects.defect: Wheel and trackpad zoom sit outside the `gestureActive` gate, so `.no-transition` is never applied on that path and every wheel tick animates the canvas transform over 200 ms. A continuous trackpad scroll therefore chases a moving target, and the pixel under the cursor is in flight while `sampleAt` reads the committed transform.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useInertiaGesture.ts:175 and :271 (gestureActive set only from pointerdown/pointerup) and :299-321 (`onWheel` sets neither); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:72 (`:class="gesture.gestureActive.value ? 'no-transition' : ''"`) and :254-256 (`transition: transform var(--duration-fast)`). Measured `canvasTransition: "transform 0.2s"` in the default matrix.
defects.mechanism: the gesture gate is keyed to pointer events, but one continuous input path is a wheel event
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01) and ctrl+scroll continuously over the stage while watching the canvas: the transform lags each tick by 200 ms rather than tracking the input.
defects.proposedCure: Move the gate from 'a pointer is down' to 'the transform is being driven', set by every input path including wheel with a short trailing release. One predicate, all inputs.

defects.defect: `DockSeparator` renders as a 1x0 px element — a dock-scoped glass-ui primitive used outside any dock, whose height comes from a dock row context that does not exist here. Dead chrome in the DOM; and canon says a divider does not belong on this surface even if it did render.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:15 (`<DockSeparator />`), :95 (imported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`). Measured live: `"sepPresent":true,"sepTag":"DIV","sepClass":"dock-separator","sepRect":{"x":267,"y":221.6875,"width":1,"height":0}`. Canon: docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-05 (dividers REMOVE) and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 (boundaries `[]`).
defects.mechanism: a design-system primitive lifted out of the scope that supplies its geometry
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01) and evaluate `document.querySelector('[class*="z-popover"] .dock-separator').getBoundingClientRect()` → `{width: 1, height: 0}`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete it. Spacing plus the material change already express the boundary between the close action and the specimen readout, which is exactly PR-05's test for retaining a divider.

defects.defect: `--hover-color` applies the sampled colour to the icon of every control in the bar, including Close — an action with no relationship to the sampled colour — and the value is arbitrary user photography with no legibility floor, so hovering Close after sampling a near-white pixel makes the glyph vanish.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:10 (`:style="{ '--hover-color': sampledColor ?? '' }"` on the whole bar), :279-282 (`.eyedropper-action-btn:hover:not(:disabled) svg { color: var(--hover-color, var(--foreground)); transform: scale(1.2) }`), applied to the Close control at :11-13. The rule also reaches inside a producer `DockControl` to restyle its glyph.
defects.mechanism: a semantic tint scoped to a class rather than to the actions the tint actually means, with an unbounded value
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), sample the white quadrant of the fixture, then hover the Close button: the `×` glyph takes the sampled near-white colour on the near-white panel.
defects.proposedCure: Scope the sampled-colour tint to the two commit actions it actually describes, and pass it through a legibility clamp against the veil it sits on rather than straight from the pixel. Better still: drop the tint — the swatch beside the readout already carries the colour, and PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.5 says a mark is data, status or a labelled action, not decoration.

defects.defect: The loupe is centred exactly on the pointer, so on touch it sits entirely under the fingertip — the one situation a magnifier exists to solve. It is also clipped to a crescent by the parent's `overflow-hidden` whenever the sample is near a stage edge, with no offset or flip rule.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196 (`left: loupeRelX - LOUPE_SIZE/2`, `top: loupeRelY - LOUPE_SIZE/2`) inside the `overflow-hidden` viewport at :64. Measured on iPhone 13: `"loupe":{"x":217,"y":378,"w":110,"h":110}` for a tap whose coordinate is the circle's exact centre. Frame: shots/D-03-mobile-first-tap-blank-loupe-ghost-image.png.
defects.mechanism: fixed centre-on-pointer placement with no occlusion or edge model
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on a touch device (or WebKit with `devices['iPhone 13']`) and tap the stage: the loupe centre equals the tap point. Tap near the left or top edge: the circle is clipped to a crescent by the viewport's overflow-hidden.
defects.proposedCure: Offset the loupe from the sample point by a touch-safe distance with an automatic flip when the offset would leave the stage, the standard magnifier placement rule — and let it hang outside the stage bounds rather than being clipped, since it is chrome, not specimen.

defects.defect: `style="--vj-enter-y: 0px"` is written as a raw inline style attribute for a token the codebase already expresses as a named CSS recipe in two other places.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:8. The established idiom: demo/styles/utils.css:174 (`.swatch-row { --vj-enter-y: 0px; --vj-enter-scale: 0 }`) and demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:297. Token consumed at demo/styles/animations.css:96.
defects.mechanism: per-instance token override where a named class recipe already exists
defects.reproduction: NONE — static source comparison; no runtime symptom.
defects.proposedCure: Express the opacity-only enter as a named modifier class alongside the existing `.swatch-row` recipe in demo/styles/utils.css, so the enter family's variants are enumerable in one place instead of being pinned inline at each call site.

defects.defect: `useLoupeCanvas` exports `drawLoupe` and no consumer calls it — dead public surface, and it is precisely the hook the missing transform-watcher of D3-03 would use.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:71 (returned in the public object); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue references only `loupeVisible`, `loupeRelX`, `loupeRelY`, `showLoupeAt`, `hideLoupe` (lines 80-85, 160, 170, 181, 230). No `loupe.drawLoupe` call exists anywhere in demo/.
defects.mechanism: an imperative primitive exposed for a redraw path that was never wired
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; `grep -rn 'drawLoupe' demo` returns only the definition, the internal call in showLoupeAt, and the export.
defects.proposedCure: Fold it away entirely: under D3-03's derived-sample model the loupe redraws from a `watchEffect`, so the composable's surface shrinks to state plus `showLoupeAt`/`hideLoupe` and there is no imperative draw to leak.

defects.defect: HYPOTHESIS (not reproduced): two full-resolution canvases plus a base64 data URL are retained per image, and `dispose()` nulls the references without zeroing `canvas.width`. On a 12 MP photograph that is roughly 96 MB of canvas backing store on a path that must run on iOS Safari, which caps total canvas memory.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:80-92 (offscreen canvas AND the visible canvas both sized to naturalWidth/naturalHeight and both drawn), :97-101 (`dispose()` sets the refs to null only); demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:29-36 (`readAsDataURL` retains the base64 string). Measured on the 64x64 fixture the footprint is trivial — `[{w:300,h:150},{w:64,h:64},{w:110,h:110}]` ≈ 0.24 MB — so the concern is unverified at scale.
defects.mechanism: unbounded source-resolution buffers, duplicated once for sampling and once for display
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. Would require loading a >=12 MP image on iOS Safari and observing the canvas-memory ceiling; not attempted this round.
defects.proposedCure: Keep exactly one full-resolution buffer for sampling and cap the DISPLAY buffer at a device-pixel-sized bitmap, since the display canvas is a duplicate of a bitmap the sampler already owns. Zero `canvas.width` on dispose so the backing store is released rather than waiting on GC.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + adjudication of r1/r2)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), the tier declared at spawn. Seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the magnifier loupe paints ZERO pixels on the touch path, permanently. `showLoupeAt` sets `loupeVisible.value = true` and then calls `drawLoupe` in the same tick, but the loupe canvas lives behind that `v-if`, so `loupeCanvasRef.value` is still null and the draw is dropped (useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60, guard at :30). On touch there is no hover to redraw, and `onHover` opens with `if (pinned.value) return` (ImageEyedropper.vue:165), so the pin lasts forever with an empty circle. Measured `loupeOpaquePx: 0 / 12100` on Chromium-touch DPR 2 AND on WebKit-touch DPR 3 (first WebKit confirmation across all three seats), still 0 at +800 ms; the identical code path with a preceding hover yields 9683. The magnifier is the whole reason this is a component rather than a click handler, and it is absent on the platform its `touch-action: none` / pinch-zoom / "Tap to sample" affordances were built for.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field carries the bounded claims and refutations instead (§IV of the report), which matter for blast radius: (1) r2's C-5 "ResizeObserver refit destroys zoom" was NOT reproduced by my instrument — I zoomed to scale(0.2226) and resized the browser viewport 1280x900 -> 1100x800 and the transform was unchanged — but the same capture shows why: the observed box did not change (`viewportRect [508,378] -> [508,378]`), so the observer never fired. My instrument was wrong, not r2's finding; r2's C-5 STANDS and is code-evident (useInertiaGesture.ts:357 wires a ResizeObserver to an unconditional initialiser at :164-166). Recorded so no later seat reads my silence as disagreement. (2) The uncoalesced per-pointermove sample pipeline is REAL in shape — measured strictly 1:1, 61 mouse.move -> 61 getImageData + 60 loupe drawImage — but r2 measured its cost at 22 microseconds per move (~0.26% of a 120 Hz frame). I did not measure a contradicting number and I explicitly DO NOT raise it to a defect; both seats now agree from different directions, so the mega-tranche should not spend a wave on it. (3) The load-race / post-dispose-resurrection defect (r1 D-12, r2 N-3) is a HYPOTHESIS: the code is unambiguous (useImageSampler.ts:68-95 runs its whole tail unconditionally after the await; dispose() at :97-101 has no generation token) but three timed swap attempts (0/15/40 ms, big->small) all stayed consistent and did not invert. (4) Swept and clean: no `defineModel` anywhere (stale-read hazard N/A), no `ValueUnit` wrapping on the sampling path, no oklch->HSV roundtrip, no WebGL, and the inertia coast rides glass-ui `useRAFLoop` with `pauseWhenHidden: true` plus an explicit PRM decision in `startInertia` — it is NOT part of the PRM-RAF epidemic and is the best-engineered part of the component. `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied at every import site; edicts 1 (no god modules), 2 (no legacy), 7 (Vue 3.5 idioms) satisfied; tap targets measure 44x44.

defects.defect: The magnifier loupe renders nothing on every touch device, permanently: `showLoupeAt` paints before Vue mounts the `v-if` canvas, and `onHover`'s `if (pinned.value) return` guarantees no redraw ever follows a tap.
defects.evidence: WebKit mobile DPR 3, single tap: {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 80.804928170435 69.890964768624)","loupeVisible":true,"loupeOpaquePx":0,"backing":110,"dpr":3,"buttons":3}. Chromium mobile DPR 2: loupeOpaquePx 0 at tap, still 0 at +800ms, still 0 after tap#3. Same code path with a preceding hover (desktop): loupeOpaquePx 9683. Code: useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (paint in the same tick as the visibility flip), guard at useLoupeCanvas.ts:30, v-if at ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86, hover gate at ImageEyedropper.vue:165. Visual: scratchpad/ccED/wk-touch-loupe.png shows a bare outlined circle with unmagnified image through it.
defects.mechanism: Event handler mutates reactive state then acts on the DOM synchronously, before the render flush — the effect is a side effect of the event rather than a derivation of the state.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/extract on any touch device (or Playwright hasTouch context), upload an image, tap the preview to open the eyedropper, tap the image once. The loupe circle is empty and never fills. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe3.mjs` section 1 (WebKit) reproduces it.
defects.proposedCure: Stop conditionally mounting the loupe canvas. Keep it permanently in the DOM and drive only its visibility (opacity/hidden) from `loupeVisible`, so `drawLoupe` always holds a live 2D context and the paint stops being ordered against Vue's scheduler at all. Equivalently (r2's formulation): make the paint a post-flush `watch([loupeVisible, loupeRelX, loupeRelY], …, { flush: 'post' })` inside `useLoupeCanvas`, which also deletes `drawLoupe`'s exported-but-unused surface. A `nextTick` inside `showLoupeAt` is the wrong patch — it makes a synchronous pointer handler async and re-opens the race under rapid taps.

defects.defect: `justUnpinned` is a one-exit latch armed on pointerdown but cleared only inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap`, so the flag survives and swallows the next genuine tap whole.
defects.evidence: Touch (CDP-dispatched multi-event drag): tap#1 red quadrant -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":3,"pinned":true}; after drag -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":1,"pinned":false}; tap#2 on the YELLOW quadrant -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":1,"pinned":false} (NO change at all); tap#3 same spot -> {"readout":"lab(97.607007864501% -","buttons":3,"pinned":true}. Desktop: pin click buttons=3 -> after drag buttons=1 -> click post-drag buttons=1, loupePinned=false -> next click buttons=3. Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (capture interceptor sets the flag), :151-155 (only clearer), useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (`if (!didMove)` gate).
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled boolean latched across two independent gestures, living outside the state machine (`useInertiaGesture`) that already owns `hasMoved`/`isPanning`.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, tap to pin, drag to pan, then tap somewhere else. On touch nothing happens at all (no readout change, no pin, no loupe); on desktop the pin silently fails. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe5.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the flag and the capture-phase interceptor. Move the pinned state into `useInertiaGesture`, which already knows at pointerup whether the gesture was a tap, a pan-end, or a pinch-end, and let it dispatch between unpin / sample / pan-end from facts it already holds. This retires the duplicate listener (C-11) at the same time.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to the standing record (r2 filed this as a bounded 650 ms window, MINOR; r2's NEG-2 refuted the hazard by testing the wrong mechanism). `swatchPulse` latches TRUE forever: `WatercolorDot` compiles with `inheritAttrs: false` and hand-merges only `class` via `useAttrs`, so the consumer's `@animationend="swatchPulse = false"` is never bound to any element. After the first press of the overlay's life, every subsequent Add-to-palette / Apply press is silent forever.
defects.evidence: $ grep -o "inheritAttrs[^,}]*" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js -> `inheritAttrs: !1`; $ grep -o "onAnimationend|\$attrs|mergeProps|useAttrs" ... | sort | uniq -c -> `1 useAttrs` (no attr forwarding). Class sampled over 2s after ONE press: before add `w-7 h-7 watercolor-swatch`; t~80ms/300ms/700ms/1200ms/2000ms all `swatch-pulse watercolor-swatch` (animation is 0.65s); second add after full settle, +200ms: still `swatch-pulse`. Document-level capture listener, two presses 150ms apart: events = ["animationstart:swatch-pop-5659b98f:SPAN.swatch-pulse|watercolor-swatch","animationend:swatch-pop-5659b98f:SPAN.swatch-pulse|watercolor-swatch"] — ONE animationstart for two presses, and the animationend fires but the component never hears it. Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:18-23, :212-224.
defects.mechanism: Depending on attribute fall-through from a design-system component that explicitly opts out of it — the effect is bound to a listener that does not exist.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, sample, press '+' (Add to palette) twice with any gap. Only the first press animates; the class never reverts. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe7.mjs` and `probe6.mjs`. NOTE for future seats: Vue scoped styles rename keyframes, so a matcher on `e.animationName === "swatch-pop"` returns a false zero — the real name is `swatch-pop-5659b98f`.
defects.proposedCure: Stop relying on fall-through: keep `w-7 h-7` always, add/remove only `swatch-pulse`, and force the restart with `:key="pulseSeq"` on the dot incremented per action (this also cures the within-window restart half r2 identified). Separately, relay the fall-through gap to the glass-ui BH inbox under the standing relay edict — a design-system dot that silently swallows every native listener a consumer attaches will bite more than this call site. Fold into the same letter as r2's N-5 (`DockControl` has no `label`/`ariaLabel` prop).

defects.defect: NEW (neither r1 nor r2 carries it). A viewport change across a layout breakpoint destroys the entire extract session — the overlay, the sample, the zoom AND the uploaded image itself — because `eyedropperActive` and `useExtractSession` live as local setup state inside an async-loaded pane the shell is free to unmount.
defects.evidence: Chromium, 2400x1800 upload, pinned sample: before resize {"overlayPresent":true,"canvasPresent":true,"viewportRect":[508,378],"transform":"translate(2px, 0px) scale(0.21)","previewStillLoaded":true,"readout":"lab(53.216681509299% …)"}; after 1100x800 unchanged; after 1000x640 {"overlayPresent":false,"canvasPresent":false,"viewportRect":null,"transform":null,"previewStillLoaded":false,"readout":null}; after 600x640 same. `previewStillLoaded` is `img[alt="Uploaded image"]` (ImageDropZone.vue:37-43) i.e. `session.previewDataUrl` — the uploaded image is gone, not merely the overlay. Code: ExtractWorkbench.vue:220,224 (session + eyedropperActive in setup scope), usePaneRouter.ts:72 (async pane).
defects.mechanism: Session-lifetime state stored at a component altitude the layout can destroy — the same family as C-1/C-2: state placed where the framework, not the domain, decides its lifetime.
defects.reproduction: /#/extract at 1280x900: upload, open the eyedropper, sample, then resize the window to 1000x640 (or rotate a phone / let mobile Safari's URL bar collapse across a breakpoint). Overlay, sample, zoom and the uploaded image are all gone; the user must re-upload. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe9.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Lift `previewDataUrl` + `eyedropperActive` (and the rest of `useExtractSession`) to the pane-router/store altitude the repo already has — `usePaletteStore` is the in-repo precedent — so a layout switch re-renders the view without destroying the session. This is an altitude fix, not a guard; adding a `keep-alive` or a remount guard would paper over the same misplacement.

defects.defect: A malformed or undecodable image produces an unhandled promise rejection and two page errors, and leaves a dead overlay with no error state, no aria-live, no retry and no self-close; every subsequent click silently returns null.
defects.evidence: Uploading 320 garbage bytes named `bad.png`: overlay {"open":true,"readout":"Tap to sample","canvasW":300,"canvasRect":{"w":300,"h":150},"loupeVisible":false}; after click on dead canvas {"readout":"Tap to sample","buttons":1}; unhandled rejections ["InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.","error event on src=data:image/png;base64,Tk9ULUEtUE5HLUFULU"]; page errors ['pageerror: The source image could not be decoded.','pageerror: Event']. The second rejection is `img.onerror = reject` at useImageSampler.ts:74 floating out of `loadAndFit()` (ImageEyedropper.vue:238,247). `canvasW: 300 / 300x150` is the browser's DEFAULT canvas geometry, proving useImageSampler.ts:86-92 never ran; imgWidth/imgHeight stay 0 so fitToViewport bails at useInertiaGesture.ts:157; sampleAt returns null at :112.
defects.mechanism: An async failure with no result type and no consumer — `loadImage` rejects into a floating promise at both call sites, so the failure has nowhere to be rendered.
defects.reproduction: /#/extract, choose 'All Files' in the picker and select any non-image (or a truncated PNG), click the preview. The overlay opens onto a dead 300x150 canvas reading 'Tap to sample' forever. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe.mjs` section C.
defects.proposedCure: `loadImage` returns the repo's own result shape (`{ ok, value } | { ok:false, error }` — see useExtractSession.ts:22-27 and `serializeCssColor`) instead of throwing into the void; the shell owns an `imageError` ref rendered in the destructive register the workbench already has (ExtractWorkbench.vue:79-85) with `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`; and `ImageDropZone.onFileSelected` applies the same MIME guard `onDrop` already applies (ImageDropZone.vue:97) — one guard, both entrances.

defects.defect: The overlay claims modality it does not implement: no dialog role, no accessible name, no aria-modal, no focus move on open, no restore on close, no focus trap, no keyboard sampling path, and no live region on the async result.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live open overlay: {"role":null,"ariaModal":null,"ariaLabel":null,"ariaLive":"none","dialogCount":0,"vpTabIndex":null,"vpRole":null,"focusablesInOverlay":1,"active":"DIV.group"} (desktop — focus stays on the drop zone BEHIND the overlay) / "active":"BODY" (mobile). Tab trail from the open overlay: ["INPUT inOverlay=false","BODY inOverlay=false","SPAN{Number of colors} inOverlay=false","BUTTON[Upload image] inOverlay=false","BUTTON[Open camera] inOverlay=false","SPAN{Chroma weight} inOverlay=false"] — six presses, focus never enters, and it walks controls the overlay physically covers (visible bleeding through the glass in scratchpad/ccED/overlay-dark.png). Canvas is aria-hidden (ImageEyedropper.vue:74); the Add/Apply controls are `v-if="pinned"` and `pinned` is set only from `onTap`, i.e. only from a pointer. Entry point is equally closed: with a preview loaded ImageDropZone sets tabindex=-1 and disables its keydown handler (ImageDropZone.vue:19,22) while the eyedropper opens from the native @click (ExtractWorkbench.vue:25).
defects.mechanism: A modal hand-rolled out of `absolute inset-0 z-popover glass-floating` (ImageEyedropper.vue:8) instead of the design system's dialog primitive — the hand-roll IS the cause of the missing semantics.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper and press Tab six times; focus never enters the overlay. Or try to sample with a keyboard: there is no path, and no path to open it either. WCAG 2.1.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A), 2.4.3 (A) fail.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive (edict 4) rather than hand-rolling the overlay: role/aria-modal/labelledby, focus moved to the close control on enter and restored on exit, and a real trap come with it. Bind arrow keys + Enter to the same `sampleAt` the pointer uses so pinning is reachable from a keyboard, give the readout `aria-live="polite"`, and give the three DockControls real accessible names (which needs the `label` prop relayed under r2's N-5 — an `aria-label` at the call site is exactly the per-instance patch edict 5 forbids).

defects.defect: Two full-native-resolution bitmaps of the same photo are held simultaneously (offscreen sampling canvas + visible display canvas), with `will-change: transform` promoting a layer of that size for the whole overlay lifetime, on top of the retained base64 data URL.
defects.evidence: 2400x1800 upload measured: {"canvasW":2400,"canvasH":1800,"bitmapMB":16.5,"inline":"translate(2px, 0px) scale(0.21)","dropzoneImgNatural":"2400x1800"} — 16.5 MB RGBA per canvas x2 in this component (33 MB), rendered at scale 0.21, plus the drop zone's decoded as a third copy and the base64 string retained in useExtractSession.ts:43,166. Code: useImageSampler.ts:80-92 (both canvases sized to native and drawn), ImageEyedropper.vue:71 (`will-change-transform`).
defects.mechanism: Duplicated bitmap state — a canvas used purely to DISPLAY an image that is already decoded as an , plus an unconditional compositor-layer hint.
defects.reproduction: Upload a 2400x1800 image and read `canvas.width/height` on `canvas.eyedropper-canvas` and the offscreen; scale to a stock 12 MP phone photo (4032x3024) and the pair is ~98 MB. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe2.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: There is no need for a second bitmap: make the visible layer the `` element itself under the same transform (zero extra decode — the drop zone already holds it), leaving exactly one `willReadFrequently` offscreen canvas for sampling. Apply `will-change` only while `gestureActive` is true, not for the overlay's lifetime.

defects.defect: Alpha is discarded at the point of formatting: a fully transparent pixel is reported to the user, and emitted to the palette / applied as the current colour, as opaque black.
defects.evidence: Fixture `alpha.png` (left half opaque #ff0000, right half alpha=0): opaque-red half -> readout `lab(54.290541404672% 80.804928170435 69.890964768624)`; TRANSPARENT half -> readout `lab(0% 0 0)` i.e. #000000. Code: useImageSampler.ts:117 `formatHex(data[0] ?? 0, data[1] ?? 0, data[2] ?? 0)` — `data[3]` is never read.
defects.mechanism: A lossy projection (RGBA -> RGB hex) chosen as the component's internal colour currency, so the alpha channel has no representation anywhere downstream.
defects.reproduction: Upload a PNG with a transparent region, open the eyedropper, hover/tap the transparent area — it reads as pure black. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe9.mjs` section ALPHA.
defects.proposedCure: Carry the sampled colour as RGBA through `sampleAt`/`formatInColorSpace` and serialize with alpha (`#rrggbbaa` / `rgb(... / a)`), or refuse the sample with the same honest-null path that out-of-bounds already uses. Independently corroborates r1's D-3.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to r2's Part IV attribution: it names the route's three nameless buttons from `REPORT.json`'s `smallTapTargets` array, which cannot be the source because every row there HAS a label. The true baseline three are ExtractControls' Upload image / Open camera / Reset, and the eyedropper's own unmeasured contribution is +1 nameless button unpinned, +3 pinned.
defects.evidence: Running capture.mjs's own filter (lines 102-105 — counts aria-label || aria-labelledby || textContent, IGNORES title) against the live route: closed -> {"count":3,"inOverlay":0,"titles":["Upload image","Open camera","Reset"]}; open -> {"count":4,"inOverlay":1,"titles":["Upload image","Open camera","Reset","Close eyedropper"]}. All three overlay controls measured title-only: [{"tag":"BUTTON","w":44,"h":44,"title":"Close eyedropper","ariaLabel":null,"text":""}, {…"Add to palette"…}, {…"Apply as current color"…}].
defects.mechanism: Accessible names carried solely by a fall-through `title` attribute — the last-resort source in the accname computation, invisible to touch screen readers — because `DockControl` exposes no label prop.
defects.reproduction: `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe4.mjs` (WebKit) runs capture.mjs's exact predicate closed and open.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to glass-ui: `DockControl` should take a `label` and stamp `aria-label`, as the sibling dock components already do. Separately, add an eyedropper state to the visual audit's `states.mjs` (upload a fixture, tap once) so the overlay enters the matrix at all — today no matrix ever uploads, so this component contributes zero rows and its clean record is empty.

defects.defect: NEW (r2 carries only a 'wheel momentum double-counted' hypothesis). A plain wheel over a fitted image unconditionally cancels the page default, pans nothing because clampPan re-centres it to a no-op, and still arms an inertia coast that burns ~70 frames each doing a forced layout.
defects.evidence: ONE wheel tick over a fully fitted image, 1000 ms window: getBoundingClientRect calls: 75, rAF requests: 253, canvas transform unchanged at `translate(0px, 57.8203px) scale(7.9375)`. The route's ambient baseline is `rafPer1500ms: 270` (~180/s) per STATES.json, so ~70 frames are the coast. Code: useInertiaGesture.ts:300 (unconditional preventDefault on a passive:false listener, :333), :311-320 (velocity seeded and startInertia called unconditionally), :80-89 (clampPan re-centres when content fits), :75 and :126 (getBoundingClientRect per call, per frame).
defects.mechanism: An effect armed from an input event without first asking whether the effect is possible — the gesture is inert, expensive, and event-swallowing at the same time.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on an image that fits the viewport and scroll the wheel once over it. Nothing moves, the page default is cancelled, and a coast loop spins. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe3.mjs` section 2.
defects.proposedCure: Gate on effect: compute the clamped delta first; if it is zero, neither preventDefault nor arm inertia. Cache the viewport rect — the ResizeObserver at :354-360 already exists to invalidate it — instead of measuring inside a per-frame loop.

defects.defect: The loupe's canvas backing store ignores devicePixelRatio, in a component whose whole purpose is per-pixel fidelity and which explicitly disables image smoothing to get crisp nearest-neighbour blocks.
defects.evidence: {"dpr":2,"loupeBackingW":110,"loupeCssW":110} (Chromium mobile) and {"dpr":3,"backing":110,"cssW":110} (WebKit mobile). Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 (`width="110" height="110"` with `class="w-full h-full"`), constants.ts:8 (`LOUPE_SIZE = 110`), useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 (`imageSmoothingEnabled = false`).
defects.mechanism: A raster surface sized in CSS pixels rather than device pixels — the nearest-neighbour discipline is thrown away by the compositor at the last step.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on any DPR>1 display and hover; every crisp 10-CSS-px block is resampled 2x/3x. Measured in probe.mjs (matrix A) and probe3.mjs (matrix C).
defects.proposedCure: Size the backing store `LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio`, `ctx.scale(dpr, dpr)`, keep the CSS box at `LOUPE_SIZE`, and re-size on a `matchMedia('(resolution: …)')` change.

defects.defect: The colour readout prints 12 decimal places for CSS-native spaces (while library-only spaces round to 4), then truncates with no `title` and no recovery — the exact anti-pattern the sibling readout in the same workbench documents having cured.
defects.evidence: {"readout":"lab(41.909687279726% -4.519858059834 -17.827996111849)","readoutLen":54,"readoutClipped":true}; `readout has title attr: false`; a second sample `lab(2.226639248986% 0.207418620522 -0.760925297353)` also clipped. Rendered result on a phone (scratchpad/ccED/wk-touch-loupe.png): `lab(54.2905…`. Code: useImageSampler.ts:39-41 rounds library spaces to 4 dp; :63-65 hands CSS spaces to `serializePickerColor` unrounded; ImageEyedropper.vue:35-37 has `truncate select-all` but no `:title`. Contrast with ExtractWorkbench.vue:134-141, whose comment reads 'the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)'.
defects.mechanism: Two formatting policies inside one function, and half of a two-part display idiom copied from a sibling.
defects.reproduction: Sample any pixel with the display space set to a CSS-native space; the readout is unreadable and unrecoverable at any realistic bar width.
defects.proposedCure: One rounding policy for both branches (`formatLibraryColor`'s 4 dp is the house standard) plus the `:title` the sibling already proves. This is the component's contribution to the owner-marked OM-14 value-formatting-decimals defect.

defects.defect: The shell hand-rolls a capture-phase `pointerdown` listener that duplicates the gesture composable's own binding, inside a `watch` with no removal on unmount and no unbind when the ref changes.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 — `watch(viewportRef, (el) => { if (!el) return; el.addEventListener('pointerdown', …, { capture: true }); })`: no removeEventListener, no oldEl unbind, no `{ immediate: true }`. Ten lines above, useInertiaGesture.ts:327-350 and :362-368 do exactly this correctly with bind/unbind and teardown.
defects.mechanism: The shell reaching around the abstraction it owns to mutate state that abstraction is already sequencing — which is what makes C-2 structurally possible.
defects.reproduction: Static: the listener added at ImageEyedropper.vue:178 has no matching removal anywhere in the file. A second viewport element would receive a second listener while the first keeps its own.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by C-2's cure — delete the listener entirely and let the tap handler in `useInertiaGesture` own the unpin decision.

defects.defect: Vacuous test gate: one 31-line test file exercising exactly one exported function, no e2e, and the single error-branch test asserts a state the product can never reach while the error path that DOES fire in production has no test at all.
defects.evidence: $ npx vitest run test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts -> `✓ test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts (3 tests) 7ms`. All three call only `formatInColorSpace`, on a sampler built with `canvasRef: ref(null)` and an identity transform (test:8-14). $ grep -rn "eyedropper|Eyedropper" e2e/ test/ -> one prose comment (e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:16) plus the import line. Untested: sampleAt, viewportToImage, loadImage, dispose, getOffscreenCanvas, all of useLoupeCanvas, all 379 lines of useInertiaGesture, and the SFC. Test:27-30 asserts `formatInColorSpace('not-a-color')` throws, but the product only ever passes a locally generated #rrggbb (useImageSampler.ts:117), so the throw at :59-61 is dead code on the shipped path — and it sits on the HOVER path, so were it reachable it would raise once per pointermove.

defects.proposedCure: Give useGradientCSS — which already declares itself 'the ONE sampling law' — the seam, as one adapter both consumers route through: `const sampleEased = (fn, t) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, fn(t)))`. If overshoot colour extrapolation is genuinely wanted it is a library decision (mixColors growing an explicit extrapolation option), not a demo guard. Either way a catalogue must not offer a tile that cannot be rendered.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; declared, not inherited. No defect on this axis.
result.strongestDefect: P3-1 — the forged `Palette` entity is a bidirectional knowledge CYCLE, not a one-way display hack. `useExtractSession.ts:91` mints `id: "__extracted__"`; `demo/palettes/utils.ts:20` hardcodes that literal in `TEMP_ID_PREFIXES = ["gen-","__extracted__","mix-"]` and `getPaletteKind()` parses it back; `PaletteCard.vue:225` feeds the result to `PaletteCardMenu.vue`, which branches on it at NINE `v-if` sites (`:16,28,49,64,74,84,134,144,153`). So the menu the extract workbench's card renders is selected by a string literal the extract workbench writes and a foreign feature parses — untyped in both directions, invisible to vue-tsc at every hop. The decisive test of a misplaced boundary: adding a fourth workbench that renders a PaletteCard requires editing `demo/palettes/utils.ts`, a foreign feature's source file, or the card silently renders the "saved" menu (Publish/Rename/Delete) on a thing that was never saved. That has already happened three times. Passes 1 and 2 both found the forgery; NEITHER found the return edge that makes it a cycle.
result.negativeProof: The published-library surface — the axis's headline question — is CLEAN and provably so. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/value.js" demo/workbenches/extract/` returns exactly 9 imports across 3 specifiers (`/color`, `/css`, `/quantize`), all three real keys in `package.json#exports`. `grep -rn "@src\|from \"src/" demo/workbenches/extract/` returns NONE — zero deep reaches, zero `dist/*` reaches. Symbol-by-symbol against the declared surface: `SpaceId` → `src/subpaths/color.ts:11`; `serializeCssColor`+`parseCssColor` → `src/subpaths/css.ts`; `QuantizedColor`/`QuantizeOptions`/`quantizePixels` → `src/subpaths/quantize.ts:1-2`. `vite.config.ts:38-49` GENERATES the demo self-alias set from `package.json#exports`, so an unpublished subpath cannot resolve in the demo either — the dogfood cannot drift from the contract. A real external consumer of `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` could write all nine lines verbatim; there is no false proof of the public API here. Three further negatives proved rather than assumed: (1) verbatimModuleSyntax — every type-only import in the 12-file subtree is `import type` or an inline `type` specifier, zero violations; (2) the `../../palettes/browser/card` reach complies with G-DEMO-3b's letter (`browser/index.ts:23-30` re-exports the `./card` sub-barrel, `:11-13` blesses sub-barrel reaches) independently of that rule being dead; (3) I went looking for a tree-shaking cost in the `demo/ui/` root-barrel hop and did NOT find one — `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json` declares `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]`, so the bundler may elide unused root re-exports; that finding is coherence-only and is stated as such rather than inflated into a perf claim. I also WITHDREW a finding I had drafted cold (a glass-ui `DockControl` accessible-name defect) after pass 2's live measurement showed all eight other DockControls in the app already carry `aria-label` and `ExtractControls.vue:41,50,85` is the sole divergence — pushing a title→aria-label fallback into the design system would have installed a masking fallback to accommodate one file.

Host: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 `<KeepAlive :max="max">`. `grep -n ':max=' demo/color-picker/App.vue` → `88:"9"  107:"6"  133:"4"`; App.vue:96-99 states :max=6 equals "the 6 distinct non-admin LEFT panes (color-picker · browse · extract · atmosphere · generate · gradient)". `grep -rn "onDeactivated" demo/` → 0 hits (2 onActivated, both HeroBlob.vue:27,246). defects.proposedCure: Do not patch the SFC with onDeactivated. Hoist acquisition into `demo/platform/media/useCameraCapture.ts` that owns the stream inside an effectScope and releases on onScopeDispose + onDeactivated, and add `demo/shell/usePaneLifecycle.ts` exposing `onPaneRelease = onDeactivated + onBeforeUnmount` so pane lifetime is a shell concept components can name. The dead `useImageQuantize.quantizeFromCamera` is the ancestor of this module — it already returns the correct `stop()` handle.

defects.defect: NEW (neither prior pass reached it): the forged Palette entity is a bidirectional knowledge cycle — the palettes feature parses the extract workbench's private sentinel back out and branches nine ways on it.
defects.evidence: Outbound: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:88-100 mints `{ id: "__extracted__", slug: "extracted", isLocal: true, ... }`. Return: demo/palettes/utils.ts:18-30 `const TEMP_ID_PREFIXES = ["gen-", "__extracted__", "mix-"]` + `getPaletteKind()` matching by `id.startsWith`. Consumption: PaletteCard.vue:225 `getPaletteKind(props.palette)` → :85 `:palette-kind="kind"` → PaletteCardMenu.vue nine v-if branches at :16,28,49,64,74,84,134,144,153. `grep -rn "__extracted__" demo/` → 3 sites: mint, parse, type-doc (types.ts:17). Coverage check: `grep -c TEMP_ID_PREFIXES` and `getPaletteKind` → 0 in BOTH pass-1 and pass-2 reports.
defects.mechanism: There is no type for 'a candidate palette not yet persisted'. Its absence forces the workbench to impersonate a persisted entity, which forces the palettes feature to un-impersonate it by string sniffing. Two halves of one missing type, split across two features and joined by an untyped literal.
defects.reproduction: Static and total: `grep -rn "__extracted__" demo/` enumerates all three edges; `grep -n paletteKind demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue` enumerates the nine consuming branches. The boundary test: adding a fourth workbench that renders a PaletteCard requires editing demo/palettes/utils.ts:20 — a foreign feature's file — or the card silently renders the 'saved' menu (Publish/Rename/Delete) on an unsaved object.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a patch. Introduce `demo/palettes/draft.ts` — `PaletteDraft { name: string; colors: readonly PaletteColor[] }` — as a first-class sibling of `Palette`. Make the card's contract `Palette | PaletteDraft` and derive `PaletteKind` from the UNION TAG, not `id.startsWith`. `TEMP_ID_PREFIXES` is deleted, the return edge disappears, and the palettes feature stops knowing that workbenches exist. This single 2-field type also retires the forged-entity finding (pass1 L-13), the K-PALID defeat (P3-2), the store bypass's missing port verb, and the stubbed `@click` on PaletteCard.

defects.defect: NEW: the forged entity defeats the K-PALID id-honesty type predicate by construction — the invariant installed specifically to stop client-minted keys masquerading as store keys cannot distinguish the forgery.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:47-55 — `const savedPalettes = computed(() => getStore().value.palettes.filter((p): p is Palette & { id: string } => p.isLocal && p.id != null))`, with the comment 'K-PALID: ... The type predicate encodes the store invariant — every stored local palette is minted an `id` (`createPalette`/`addPublishedPalette`)'. The forgery satisfies both conjuncts: useExtractSession.ts:97 `isLocal: true`, :91 `id: "__extracted__"`. demo/palettes/types.ts:15-27 has already been WIDENED to grandfather the forgeries in ('client-minted (`crypto.randomUUID()` or a `gen-`/`mix-`/`__extracted__` temp prefix)'). `grep -c K-PALID` → 0 in both prior passes.
defects.mechanism: An invariant enforced by a type predicate over structural fields, while three features mint those fields outside the two functions the invariant names. The type doc was then amended to describe the defeat as the design.
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled a hypothesis-grade structural finding, not a live bug. The forged object never enters `getStore().value.palettes` today (onSave at useExtractSession.ts:185 calls createPalette, which mints fresh). It becomes live the moment any workbench pushes its display object into the store.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of P3-1's cure: with `PaletteDraft` as a distinct type, no workbench ever constructs a `Palette`, `id` minting returns to `createPalette`/`addPublishedPalette` exclusively, and the K-PALID predicate becomes honest again. Delete the `gen-`/`mix-`/`__extracted__` prose from types.ts:17.

defects.defect: NEW: the camera writes its error into the quantizer's error channel through a writable computed over another composable's private ref, where the next unrelated image drop silently erases it.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:251-254 `catch (err) { session.quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\`; ... }`. demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:66-73 — `quantizeError` is `computed<string|null>({ get: () => workerError.value ?? ..., set: (value) => { workerError.value = value; } })`. demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:86 `error.value = null;` at the top of every runQuantize. `grep -c quantizeError` → 0 in both prior passes.
defects.mechanism: One mutable error slot shared by three semantically distinct producers (worker failure, serialization failure, device-permission denial), with a write path exposed from outside the composable that owns it. The `set:` half of the computed is the whole defect in one construct.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/extract → press the camera control → DENY camera permission → the destructive line at ExtractWorkbench.vue:100-105 reads 'Camera access denied: …'. Now drop any image → the message vanishes on runQuantize's first statement (useImageQuantize.ts:86) with no user action acknowledging it. (Live probe attempted; both browser drivers held by concurrent seats — errors pasted in report §4. Carried on the three cited lines, which are unambiguous.)
defects.proposedCure: `useCameraCapture` owns its own `error` ref alongside the stream; the SFC renders whichever of the two error registers is set. Delete the `set:` half of the `quantizeError` computed entirely — a writable computed over another composable's private state is not a channel, it is a hole.

defects.defect: Dual path: camera capture is implemented twice, and the complete, more-correct copy is dead code. Carried from pass 1, re-verified.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "quantizeFromCamera|quantizeFromCanvas|useImageQuantize" demo src test e2e` → only the definitions at useImageQuantize.ts:110,115 and their returns at :158,:159. ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-279 reimplements it inline (getUserMedia :242, createElement('canvas') :269, drawImage :272) WITHOUT that discipline. 41 of useImageQuantize.ts's 161 lines unreachable.
defects.mechanism: Second implementation of one concept, alive in two homes, where the dead one is the one that solved the lifecycle problem the live one has (B-1).
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "quantizeFromCamera" demo src test e2e` — definition and return only, no callers.
defects.proposedCure: Delete quantizeFromCamera and quantizeFromCanvas from useImageQuantize; promote their content into `demo/platform/media/useCameraCapture.ts` (B-1's cure) as the ONE camera implementation, returning `{ active, start, stop, captureFrame(): Promise<File> }`. useImageQuantize keeps quantizeFromFile only.

defects.defect: The workbench reaches around its own published port to write directly into another feature's store. Carried from pass 1, re-verified.

defects.defect: The entire demo module-boundary lint regime is dead; nothing has ever guarded this component's imports, and a feature seam asserts in prose that it is enforced. Carried from pass 1, re-verified.
defects.evidence: `npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue | jq .rules["no-restricted-imports"]` → `null`. Same for useExtractSession.ts and palettes/browser/card/index.ts.
