defects.defect: The WatercolorDot contract this component calls does not exist in @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0. `tag`, the default slot, `@click`, `aria-label`, `:disabled` and `title` are all discarded; the component hard-renders `<span aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" style="pointer-events:none">`. Both add paths in the Mix workbench's colors mode are therefore inert, canMix (>=2) is unreachable, and the feature is functionally dead.

Live probe7.mjs output: `ADDSLOT_children: { tag: 'SPAN', ariaHidden: 'true', pe: 'none', children: ['svg.watercolor-filter-host','SPAN.watercolor-ghost-stroke'], tabIndex: -1 }` / `chips after 5 clicks on add-slot: 0` / `chips after 4 clicks on dropdown swatch: 0` / `focusable watercolor swatches: 0 total swatches: 4`. Vue fallthrough attrs make the orphaned calls type-legal, so nothing failed.
defects.reproduction: Dev server live at http://localhost:9000. Seed two local palettes into localStorage["color-palettes"] via Playwright addInitScript, goto /#/mix, wait 3.5s, then issue 5 real mouse clicks at the centre of `.add-slot-ghost` and 4 at a dropdown `.watercolor-swatch`. `document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-source]').length` stays 0. Script: scratchpad/probe7.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Do not re-add `tag` — a polymorphic :is prop is the contrivance that caused this. glass-ui keeps WatercolorDot strictly decorative (aria-hidden + pointer-events:none is the right call) and adds a first-class `WatercolorSwatchButton` to @mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot: a real <button type="button"> composing the dot, forwarding aria-label/disabled/@click, owning focus-ring geometry on the dot's own seeded silhouette, accepting a slot for an overlay glyph. All 6 dead tag="button" sites migrate; 18 decorative tag="div" sites drop the dead prop. Relay to the glass-ui BH/BI inbox — the fix cannot land in this repo.

defects.defect: The disclosure's motion contract is overridden per-instance and the design system's spring loses. glass-ui's `.disclosure-content` already ships animation-duration/timing tokens and overflow:hidden; MixSourceSelector.vue:195 layers `overflow-hidden data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down data-[state=closed]:animate-collapsible-up` on top and wins the cascade.
defects.evidence: glass-ui.css verbatim: `.disclosure-content{…animation-duration:var(--spring-smooth-duration);animation-timing-function:var(--spring-smooth);overflow:hidden}`. Live computed style (scratchpad/probe10.mjs): {"DELIVERED_duration":"0.2s","DELIVERED_timing":"ease-out","DELIVERED_name":"collapsible-down","GLASS_TOKEN_duration":"calc(0.35s * 1)","GLASS_TOKEN_settle":"0.35s","GLASS_TOKEN_timing_stops":48}. A 48-stop linear() spring at 350ms is replaced by ease-out at 200ms — a 43% duration cut.
defects.mechanism: Motion has two owners and the wrong one wins. `animate-collapsible-down` is a tw-animate-css utility (demo/styles/foundation.css:2), a radix-era package whose keyframes resolve height through var(--radix-…, var(--bits-…, var(--reka-collapsible-content-height, auto))) — the demo's motion is specified by a fourth package keyed on a fifth package's variable namespace, reaching glass-ui's value only via the third fallback. Violates edicts 4 (glass-ui is the design system), 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance override) and 6 (motion tokenized).
defects.reproduction: Seed palettes, goto /#/mix, click 'From palettes', read getComputedStyle on [id^="glass-disclosure-content"] → animationDuration '0.2s', animationTimingFunction 'ease-out', while document.documentElement's --spring-smooth-duration is 'calc(0.35s * 1)'. Script: scratchpad/probe10.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three utility classes from line 195. <CollapsibleContent> then inherits .disclosure-content and animates on --spring-smooth like every other glass surface, with zero demo-side motion code. A genuinely different motion is a glass-ui variant, not a call-site class list. Once no demo file names animate-*, audit tw-animate-css out of foundation.css — a radix-era dependency outliving radix is the legacy edict 2 forbids. No animation is deleted, only returned to its tokenized owner (edict 6 satisfied).

defects.defect: Eight of the demo application's runtime packages — including `vue` itself — are declared devDependencies only. package.json `dependencies` holds exactly two entries, both of them the library's needs.
defects.evidence: Resolving every bare specifier imported under demo/ against the manifest: runtime-imported-but-devDependency = @lucide/vue ^1.16.0, @vueuse/core ^14.3.0, @vueuse/integrations ^14.3.0, highlight.js ^11.11.1, katex ^0.16.47, reka-ui ^2.9, vue ^3.5.34, vue-router ^5.1.0 (plus vitest, legitimately dev). `dependencies` = {"@mkbabb/glass-ui","@mkbabb/keyframes.js"}. MixSourceSelector.vue:2 imports vue, :3 imports @lucide/vue (47 demo files do), and its ../../ui/collapsible edge reaches reka-ui — 3 of its 5 runtime package edges undeclared.
defects.mechanism: One manifest owns two artifacts with contradictory requirements — a second, independent instance of the mechanism P2's L-13 found in the sideEffects field. The two-entry dependencies block is CORRECT for the published colour library (it must not force Vue on consumers) and incorrect for the application, because one manifest cannot be correct for both.
defects.reproduction: node script over `grep -rhoE 'from "[^.\"][^\"]*\"' demo --include=*.vue --include=*.ts`, mapping each bare specifier to its package root and intersecting with Object.keys(package.json.devDependencies) minus dependencies. Output pasted in the report. Consequence is latent until any `npm ci --omit=dev` in a demo deploy path, which yields a tree in which the app cannot boot.
defects.proposedCure: Same cure as P2's L-13, now with two independent justifications: split into an npm workspace so demo/ has its own package.json declaring vue, vue-router, reka-ui, @vueuse/*, @lucide/vue, highlight.js, katex, @mkbabb/glass-ui, and @mkbabb/value.js by file:.. . Each artifact then declares only what it needs, making L-13 and L-20 both unrepresentable. Do not land the split without re-homing the 8 dependencies or the demo package is born broken.

defects.id: L-21 (NEW in P3 — refutes a recorded negative)
defects.defect: The 'stable keys for TransitionGroup' apparatus is duplicated verbatim in two homes, and both copies are provably wrong. Passes 1 and 2 both recorded the negative 'No duplicate implementation of this component's concept'.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98 vs demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useSwatchActions.ts:42-59 — same comment header `// --- Stable keys for TransitionGroup ---`, same module-scope counter, same `${…}::${i}` map key, same mint-on-miss computed, same prune watch. `grep -rn "swatchKeyCounter" demo` returns these two sites and no others. Executed transcription (scratchpad/keytrace.mjs): `keys [a,b,c]: [0,1,2]` → `keys after remove(0): [3,4]` → survivors re-keyed, so TransitionGroup unmounts and remounts instead of moving.
defects.mechanism: Identity was derived in the view from positional data the view does not own; the workaround was then copied rather than homed. A list item's identity is a property of the model.

Live UI reproduction is blocked by L-1.

The same transposition applies to whichever store owns savedColorStrings. Both copies of the apparatus then delete — the shared thing was a workaround, so the right move is to delete it twice rather than extract it once (edict 3). Strike the 'no duplicate implementation' bullet from the P1 negative list so it stops carrying false assurance.

defects.defect: The selection cardinality rule has no owner: MIN_COLORS/MAX_COLORS live in the view, the state machine that mutates enforces nothing, and the second of the view's own two add paths does not consult the guard at all.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:38-42 declares MIN_COLORS=1, MAX_COLORS=12, canRemoveColor, canAddColor. useMixingState.ts:55-61 — addColor/removeColor apply no bound whatsoever. MixSourceSelector.vue:172 `:disabled="!canAddColor || undefined"` on the add slot; MixSourceSelector.vue:211-221 (the palette-dropdown swatch, the other add path in the same file) has no :disabled and no guard — `:220 @click="emit('addColor', color.css, palette.name)"`.
defects.mechanism: Policy was written where it was rendered rather than where it is enforced, so a second call site could be added without it — and was. Compounded by L-1: pass 1's L-2 census records MixSourceSelector:164 as the only site that also loses a :disabled guard to the phantom API, so the one path that does consult the bound is the one whose guard the glass-ui cut silently dropped.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent. Confirmed by code read at the three cited line ranges; live reproduction is blocked because L-1 makes every add path inert. It surfaces the instant L-1 is cured, in the same wave.
defects.proposedCure: Move MIN_COLORS/MAX_COLORS into useMixingState; have addColor/removeColor refuse out-of-range mutations; export canAddColor/canRemoveColor from the machine. The view then renders a decision it does not make, both add paths are governed by construction, and a third add path cannot reintroduce the hole. Fold into one six-line edit of useMixingState.ts together with L-5/L-21's id minting — both are the same transposition (state belongs to the state machine).

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-barrel pure-alias layer over glass-ui; demo/ui/collapsible has exactly one consumer in the repo (this file) and re-exports from the glass-ui ROOT barrel although @mkbabb/glass-ui/collapsible exists. Three design-system import idioms appear in one 9-line import block.

All 19 demo/ui/* barrels are pure re-exports (18 are 1 line, alert is 2). `grep -rn 'ui/collapsible' demo` → one hit, MixSourceSelector.vue:5. glass-ui root statically imports 43 chunks vs 1 for ./collapsible. For this file it is one line, after which all three glass-ui imports read identically. Note for the record: pass 2's 30.3× static-closure figure and this −12.0% delivered figure measure different things (what the bundler walks vs what survives shaking); quoting 30.3× as a payload figure would overstate it.

defects.defect: The mix workbench reaches into the browse view's card cluster; PaletteCard is a 10-prop/13-emit god component, so a display-only consumer must smuggle it into a native <button>, producing invalid nested interactive content.

PaletteCard.vue:183-213 = 10 props, 13 emits. MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 wraps it in a hand-rolled <button>; :266 passes `:css-color="''"` to an already-optional prop. defects.mechanism: One component carries two concepts — the presentation of a palette and the action surface of a palette — so a consumer needing only the first must import the second. The HTML button content model forbids interactive descendants.
defects.reproduction: Seed palettes, goto /#/mix, click the 'Palettes' tab, then enumerate document.querySelectorAll('button') and count interactive descendants of each. Two outer buttons each contain a 'Palette menu' button. Script: scratchpad/probe8.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Split at the card boundary in the card's own home: PaletteCardView (pure presentation, zero emits), PaletteCard (the browse action surface composing it, owning the 13 emits and the menu), and a selectable form for the mix/generate/extract consumers — the button wrap then becomes legal because the view has no interactive descendants. Then re-home the presentational half to demo/palettes/card/, with browser/ importing it like everyone else, killing the cross-boundary edge without inventing a shared/ dir (edict 3).

Since canMix requires >= 2 selected colours and no add path works, the Mix workbench's colors mode is entirely inoperable. Recorded negatives (hypotheses that measurement killed, per the report's P3 negative-proof section): (1) variant="pill" on SegmentedTabs is NOT a second phantom — SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts:20 declares `export type SegmentedTabsVariant = "pill" | "underline"` and :55 `variant?: SegmentedTabsVariant`; WatercolorDot is the only phantom surface in this file. result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D3-01 — the dominance readout names a colour that is not the card's first swatch, so the label has no referent anywhere in the UI. The component deleted its dominant marker on the written grounds that the marker was redundant with swatch 0 (`ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117`: "The duplicate dominant dot died — the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen"). Measured: dominant = oklch(73.89…) (green), swatch 0 = oklch(54.49…) (crimson). Pass 1 read the same comment and recorded its claim as fact (pass1 D-16), so this defect survived two prior adversarial passes.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but three negatives were established and are recorded so the cure wave does not chase them: (1) Reduced motion is correctly handled — the global guard at animations.css:184-192 neutralises `animate-pulse` and both `vj-` families app-wide; no local override exists. (2) No layout jump is reproducible on the result morph — 31 samples across a six-step keyboard k-drag and full settle measured a flat 325px (probe4-log.txt P3); this corroborates pass1 D-2 (the skeleton never appears, so there is no swap to jump) rather than refuting pass2 D2-14. (3) The route never throws — REPORT.json `/#/extract` shows pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, horizontalOverflow 0 in all four Safari matrices. Every defect here and in the two prior passes is a design defect on a green route, which is why no gate this repo runs can see any of them.

defects.defect: BLOCKER (NEW) — The dominance readout points at nothing. The design deleted its dominant marker on the stated grounds that the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen; it is not. `extractedPalette` (useExtractSession.ts:85-89) preserves quantizer return order while `dominant` (useExtractSession.ts:121-142) is an independent max-population scan with a deliberate chroma tiebreak (:120). When populations tie, the tiebreak walks the dominant off index 0 and the card is never told. No ring, no ordinal, no reordering — the label names one of five identical circles with no way to find it. Pass 1 accepted the comment as fact (pass1 D-16 line 468: 'the dominance readout names swatch #1 in text'); that clause should be struck.
defects.evidence: probe/probe5-log.txt, 1440x900 light, 200x200 PNG of four equal 50px bands #c81e5a/#1e5ac8/#5ac81e/#e8e0d0. `=== dominant serialized === oklch(73.892055422424% 0.217857767251 137.844885067367deg)` (L=73.89 -> the GREEN). `"swatchSeats": [{"bg":"oklch(0.544872 0.202432 7.683829)","x":238}` (crimson, index 0), `{"bg":"oklch(0.738921 0.217858 137.844879)","x":302}` (green, index 1 = the dominant), blue, cream]. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117 and :137-141; demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:85-89 vs :120-142. Screenshot: probe/P2-fold-1440x900.png, and probe/P7-crop-rails.png where at k=5 swatch 0 is blue and the dominant is still green.
defects.mechanism: Invariant asserted in a comment, bound by no structure — two independent orderings (quantizer return order for the card, max-population+chroma-tiebreak for the label) are documented as identical and never reconciled.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract. Upload a PNG of four equal-height solid bands (equal populations force the chroma tiebreak). Compare `document.querySelector('code.fira-code').title` with the first swatch's computed backgroundColor. They differ deterministically on the first attempt. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe/wbex-probe5.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Sort `extractedPalette` by population descending in useExtractSession.ts:85-89. Index 0 then IS the dominant by construction, the comment becomes true, and the card's population-proportional strip gains a second meaning for free — left-to-right becomes a ranking, which is what a viewer already assumes a proportional strip means. One sort closes three defects (this, the unbound label, and the strip's currently-arbitrary order). The alternative — restore a marker on the dominant seat — is acceptable; asserting the binding in prose and rendering nothing is the only option worse than either.

defects.defect: BLOCKER (severity upgrade of pass1 D-1) — The preview crop is not a fidelity nuisance: it makes the preview and the palette disagree about what is in the picture. `object-contain` is declared (ImageDropZone.vue:41) inside an `overflow-hidden` container clamped to `max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:20), but the img's `h-full` resolves against the content box, computing to 458px inside a 320px box — 69px destroyed top and bottom. The quantizer reads the full file via createImageBitmap (useImageQuantize.ts:19-25). Result: a colour present in the palette is absent from the picture shown. Two further consequences neither prior pass records: ImageEyedropper receives the UNCROPPED previewDataUrl (ExtractWorkbench.vue:175), so the session presents two different specimens; and equal source areas render 39.7%/100%/100%/39.7% under a readout that says every band is 25% of the image.
defects.evidence: probe/probe6-log.txt: `"imgRect":{"y":131.7,"h":458,"bottom":589.7}`, `"containerRect":{"y":200.7,"h":320,"bottom":520.7}`, `"containerOverflow":"hidden"`, `"imgObjectFit":"contain"`, `"imgHeightDecl":"458px"`, `"croppedTopPx":69`, `"croppedBottomPx":69`, `"croppedFraction":0.301`. Visual proof: probe/P7-crop-rails.png — the source carries an 8px solid black rail at its top edge and another at its bottom; NEITHER appears anywhere in the preview, yet the card renders a black strip cell and a black swatch at k=5. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:8,41 and demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:20,175.
defects.mechanism: `h-full` on a child of a max-height-clamped flex column: percentage height resolves against the indefinite content box, the img exceeds the clamp, and `overflow-hidden` center-crops it — defeating the declared `object-contain`. Same family as D3-01: a fidelity law stated in prose (ImageDropZone.vue:3-5, 'the specimen never lies') with no binding structure.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract at 1440x900. Upload a 200x200 PNG of four equal bands with an 8px black rail at row 0-8 and row 192-200. The preview shows no black; the k=5 palette contains black. Measure: img.getBoundingClientRect().height (458) vs its container's (320). Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe/wbex-probe6.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Pass 1's `max-height:100%` / `min-h-0` stopgap closes the mechanism but leaves the design unowned and will regenerate at the next viewport change. Transposition: the specimen seat becomes a stage with a DECLARED ASPECT RATIO, letterboxing inside it — the same law ShadowPalette already applies to the result plate. Critically, whichever geometry wins must be the geometry the quantizer AND the sampler see, or the disagreement survives the fix.

defects.defect: MAJOR (independent re-confirmation of pass1 D-7 / pass2 D2-03) — Type-rung collision: the derived dominance statistic is set at byte-identical size and family to the pane's own identity heading, 493px below it in the same 462px column. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.13 assigns text-display to 'route H1/major argument' and value/provenance to text-mono-small/mono-caption; §5.11 adds 'A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading or live status.' defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-8 / pass2 D2-04, with a NEW mobile number) — The headline value renders 30% of itself on desktop and 17% on mobile, because it is an unrounded 58-character float dump. The component's own comment (ExtractWorkbench.vue:134-136) rules this acceptable because 'the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)' — but `title` is a hover tooltip that does not exist on touch, which is precisely the 17% case.
defects.evidence: probe/probe5-log.txt desktop 1440x900: `"clientW":178, "scrollW":585, "visibleFrac":0.30`, full string `oklch(73.892055422424% 0.217857767251 137.844885067367deg)` (58 chars). probe/probe4-log.txt mobile 390x844: `"codeClientW":87, "codeScrollW":500, "visibleFraction":0.17`. Rendered text: `oklch(73.8920554…` — function name and lightness only; chroma and hue entirely gone. Screenshot: probe/P4-mobile390-populated.png. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:137-141.
defects.mechanism: No presentation-boundary rounding: twelve significant decimals on chroma and hue is a serialization artifact, not a designed readout. The truncate/title/select-all apparatus exists only to excuse the over-precision.

Then delete the truncate/title/select-all triad it exists to excuse. This is not this component's private problem.

defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass2 D2-08/D2-09 + NEW live proof) — The camera is a modal state implemented additively: no exit, an inert `disabled` contract, and a leaked live MediaStream. The viewfinder contains exactly ONE control (capture); Escape does nothing; stopCamera has only two callers (onFile :236, onBeforeUnmount :281). `:disabled="isProcessing || cameraActive"` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:70) is honoured by 1 of 5 controls — only Reset (ExtractControls.vue:84). Because 'Open camera' stays live, re-pressing it overwrites cameraStream (:242) without stopping the previous stream, orphaning a live MediaStream that only page unload reclaims (OS camera indicator stays lit).
defects.evidence: probe/probe-log.txt: `"viewfinderButtons":[{"title":"Capture frame","aria":null,"text":""}]` — one control. `=== C3. Escape pressed; video still present: true`. With camera live: `{"t":"Upload image","disabled":false},{"t":"Open camera","disabled":false},{"t":"Reset","disabled":true}` and `"sliders":[{"label":"Number of colors","dataDisabled":false},{"label":"Chroma weight","dataDisabled":false}]`. NEW live proof: `=== C1b. k slider live while camera up === {"ariaValue":"6","shadowSegs":6}` — I drove k 5→6 with the viewfinder open. Leak: `=== C2 === {"streamCount":2,"trackStates":["live","live"]}`. Screenshot: probe/C-camera-active.png.
defects.mechanism: A mode modelled as an additive boolean rather than as a stage mode with its own chassis; the disabled contract is asserted at the parent and dropped by four of five consumers.
defects.reproduction: Stub navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with a canvas captureStream, load /#/extract, click 'Open camera'. Press Escape (nothing). Press 'Open camera' again: window.__streams.length === 2, both tracks 'live'. Script: probe/wbex-probe.mjs section C.
defects.proposedCure: The viewfinder becomes a MODE of the stage, not a floating block: entering it swaps the stage content and the action region gains the pair the mode requires — Cancel and Capture — with Escape bound. Guard startCamera with `if (cameraActive) return`. The `disabled` prop must either reach every control in the cluster or be deleted: a contract honoured by 1 of 5 consumers is worse than no contract.

defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-11 / pass2 D2-11, NEW proof shape) — The eyedropper, the workbench's headline sampling capability, is pointer-only and invisible. ExtractWorkbench.vue:23-25 sets `:disable-click` true whenever a preview exists, which makes ImageDropZone set `tabindex="-1"` (:19) and guard its own keydown handler off (:22), then binds a `@click` listener only — and role="button" does not synthesize click from Enter the way a native <button> does. The only sighted cue is `cursor: crosshair` plus a corner tag that is opacity-0 until group-hover/group-focus-visible (ImageDropZone.vue:58) — and group-focus-visible can never fire because the group was just removed from the tab order.
defects.evidence: probe/probe6-log.txt: `"dzTabindex":"-1"`, `"dzAriaLabel":"Image preview area, tap to sample colors"`. NEW: `=== P7b. tabbable set on the populated route ===` enumerates all 15 tabbables — the preview is absent entirely. NEW: `=== P7c. Enter on the focused preview === {"eyedropperOpen":false,"activeEl":"DIV/Image preview area, tap to sample colors"}` — focused programmatically, Enter does nothing. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5 and PR-07.
defects.mechanism: An overloaded surface: one rectangle whose meaning changes with hidden state, whose keyboard path is disabled by the same flag that assigns it its new meaning.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, upload an image, Tab through the page — the preview never receives focus. Focus it programmatically and press Enter — the eyedropper does not open. Script: probe/wbex-probe6.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Sampling is an action; give it an action's seat. Either keep the preview focusable with its own keydown.enter.space opening the eyedropper (the handler already exists three lines away, merely guarded off), or add a named 'Sample colors' control to the controls row where Upload, Camera and Reset already live. Retire the overloaded-surface idiom.

defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-19 / pass2 D2-21 and pass2 D2-16) — Two dead alternate paths. (a) The `split` layout has no caller: `grep -rn "<ExtractWorkbench" demo/` returns exactly one hit, ExtractPane.vue:11, which passes layout="column". The grid branch (:5-6), sm:min-h (:13), the split max-height arm (:19), the PaletteCard 'aside' layout (:148) and the useBreakpoint matchMedia listener whose only consumer is that dead ternary (:226) are all unreachable; the prop doc still describes a dialog that no longer exists (:206). (b) The camera capability exists twice: useImageQuantize.ts:115-146 ships a complete quantizeFromCamera with correct stream lifecycle (stop() at :140-143) and zero consumers, while ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-279 hand-rolls the same thing with a gratuitous canvas.toBlob -> PNG Blob -> File -> createImageBitmap -> OffscreenCanvas round trip. The dead twin is the one with the correct lifecycle; the live one is D3-C3.
defects.evidence: `$ grep -rn "<ExtractWorkbench" demo/` -> `demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:11` (only hit); ExtractPane.vue:13 `layout="column"`. `$ grep -rn "quantizeFromCamera\|quantizeFromCanvas" demo/ test/ e2e/ | grep -v useImageQuantize.ts` -> no output. Owner edict 2 (no dual paths), edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance).
defects.mechanism: Dead alternate paths retained after a collapse (the T20 pane/dialog merge), so the reviewed surface is larger than the live surface — which is how D3-C3's stream leak survived: the correct implementation was sitting unused next to the defective one.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, proven by the two greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `split` prop arm, `isWide`, and the useBreakpoint import. For the camera: delete quantizeFromCamera/quantizeFromCanvas OR make the workbench consume quantizeFromCamera and delete its hand-rolled twin. One of the two camera implementations must die this wave.

defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-26 / pass2 D2-06) — Camera failure renders a raw DOMException into the quantizer's error channel, unannounced and mis-routed. ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 does `quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\``. Three defects in one line: (1) undesigned copy — `${err}` stringifies the exception, and the word 'denied' is asserted even when the cause is NotFoundError (no camera) or NotReadableError (device busy), so the message lies about two of the three common failures; (2) wrong channel — it writes the quantizer's ref, whose line is captioned in source as being for palette-serialization failures, so the next successful quantize silently erases it (useImageQuantize.ts:86); (3) never announced — role null, aria-live null on a message that appears asynchronously after a permission dialog.
defects.evidence: probe/probe-log.txt: `=== D. camera denied === "text":"Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent or the platform in the current context.", "color":"rgb(219, 36, 36)", "role":null, "ariaLive":null`. Screenshot: probe/D-camera-denied.png. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85, :251-254.
defects.mechanism: Error channel misuse — a device-permission failure routed through a data-serialization error ref, with template-literal exception stringification standing in for written copy.
defects.reproduction: Stub navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia to reject with a NotAllowedError DOMException, load /#/extract, click 'Open camera'. Script: probe/wbex-probe.mjs section D.
defects.proposedCure: A named camera-error state on the workbench (not the session), mapping the three DOMException.name cases to three written sentences, rendered in a role="status"/aria-live seat, cleared by the next camera attempt.

defects.defect: MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-13) — 'Reset' does not reset, and there is no path back to the empty state. defects.defect: MINOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-20 / pass2 D2-18) — `.plate-ink` is copy-pasted into five components because no root utility exists. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improperly implemented)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the Mix workbench's default (colors) mode is inert on main since f2c8f565 (2026-07-17): BOTH `addColor` emitters render as `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none" tabindex="-1">` with NO click listener bound, because glass-ui 7.0.0 removed WatercolorDot's `tag` prop, removed its `<slot/>`, and set `inheritAttrs:false` — so `tag="button"`, `@click`, `aria-label`, `:disabled`, `:title` and the `<Plus>` child are all silently discarded. Proven by a FORCED click that changed nothing (`FORCE-ERR null` + `SOURCES-AFTER-FORCE-CLICK 0`), by the e2e suite's own locator resolving to 0, and by the shipped Safari capture's `+`-less ghost slot. `selectedColors` can never leave `[]`, `canMix` (>=2) is unsatisfiable, the Mix button is permanently disabled. NEW this round: the gate that would catch it no longer even names it — it now dies earlier at the dock's `Select view` combobox never reaching "stable", so wiring Playwright into CI without first curing the dock substitutes one silence for another.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the hazard sweep produced firm negatives that must not be re-litigated: (1) PRM-RAF — zero rAF in the file; the dot's wobble is off by default (`animate:!1` in the shipped props) and when on rides glass-ui's single `useRAFLoop` with `pauseWhenHidden:!0, respectReducedMotion:!0`. (2) `defineModel` staleness — no `defineModel`; `mode` is a one-way prop + explicit `update:mode` emit. (3) oklch/HSV hue drift and `ValueUnit` nesting — no conversion and no ValueUnit construction anywhere; `sc.css` is a string end-to-end. (4) reka-ui pointer-capture — no slider. (5) WebGL — no drawing context; WatercolorDot is the suite's deliberate CSS/SVG counterexample. (6) Leaks — no listener/observer/timer; the one `watch` is setup-scoped; `swatchKeyMap` is pruned each tick (bounded). (7) `parseCssColor` crash class — DROVE the boundary (zero-colour palette through the full mix flow) and it did NOT throw: zero pageerror, so C-11's `:css-color=""` is a contract violation, NOT a live crash. (8) Reactivity fires correctly (props destructure -> `__props.x` getters; the machine replaces arrays rather than mutating). (9) Edicts 1, 6, 7, 8 pass. (10) The state machine `useMixingState` is genuinely sound — ONE-CLOCK law honoured, real re-entry guard at :83, pure math downstream.

Live probe (evidence/r3/probe-r3a-addslot.mjs vs http://localhost:9000/#/mix): addSlot = {tagName:"SPAN", ariaHidden:"true", ariaLabel:null, hasTagAttr:null, disabledAttr:null, innerHTMLHasSvgPlus:false, pointerEvents:"none", tabIndex:-1}; CLICK-ERR TimeoutError 3000ms; FORCE-ERR null; SOURCES-AFTER-FORCE-CLICK 0; ROLE-BUTTON-ADD-CURRENT-COUNT 0. Screenshot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png shows the ghost slot with no + glyph.
defects.mechanism: Glass-5 component API retained past a major version bump. glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot` removed `tag?: "div"|"button"`, removed `<slot/>`, replaced the `<component :is>` root with a hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`, and set `inheritAttrs:false` (verified in the shipped dist `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` and in the upstream cut `git -C ../glass-ui show 490cc46e -- src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue`). value.js's adoption commit f2c8f565 enumerated a long migration list and skipped this file.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/r3/probe-r3a-addslot.mjs (dev server on :9000). Or by hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/mix and try to add any colour — no affordance responds to mouse, touch, Tab or AT.
defects.proposedCure: Seat/face separation, not a patch: the Glass 7 dot is a FACE (aria-hidden, pointer-events:none by design), never a SEAT. Render a real `<button type="button" :disabled="!canAddColor" aria-label="Add current color to the mix" @click="addCurrentColor">` that CONTAINS the decorative dot plus the `<Plus>` glyph. Apply the identical transposition at all six interactive `tag="button"` sites in demo/ and all three slot-children sites, sweeping `tag=` to zero demo-wide in one commit. If the pairing recurs, it belongs in glass-ui as a `WatercolorDotButton` — never a new demo/shared/ wrapper (edicts 3, 4).

defects.defect: The only gate that tests this component is not run by CI at all, and at this HEAD it no longer even fails for the right reason — it dies earlier at the dock, so the blocker stays invisible behind a misattributed timeout.

defects.mechanism: Vacuous-gate at suite level. Vue types undeclared attributes as $attrs fallthrough, so a major-version prop/slot removal is type-invisible by construction; the behavioural suite that WOULD see it is dark in CI; and a separate dock-stability defect now short-circuits it before the assertion. `grep -rln "mount(" test/` returns nothing — the repo has no component-mount test anywhere, so the whole glass-ui consumer boundary is ungated in the lane CI actually runs. Mutations that keep every running gate green: delete the swatchKeys block and use :key="i"; set MAX_COLORS=1; delete the whole From-palettes Collapsible; drop aria-pressed from the palettes button; invert canRemoveColor.
defects.reproduction: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line  (pasted output above); and time npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit
defects.proposedCure: Sequenced: (1) cure the dock stability defect first or the mix gate cannot speak; (2) wire the five Playwright projects into ci.yml as hard steps — playwright.config.ts already provisions the webServer pair; (3) add the repo's FIRST component-mount Vitest test: mount MixSourceSelector with a stubbed LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, assert getByRole('button', {name: /Add current color/}) exists and that clicking it emits addColor. That single unit test runs in the lane CI already has and would have failed on f2c8f565.

defects.defect: A palette deleted from the library remains an invisible, un-deselectable operand of the mix — canMix still counts it and mixColors still consumes it.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:230-268 renders selection exclusively from `savedPalettes` while the selection lives in useMixingState.selectedPalettes (useMixingState.ts:43); nothing reconciles them. Independently re-measured this round with a different probe (evidence/r3/probe-r3e-c15-verify.mjs): SELECTED-SOURCES 2 / MIX-DISABLED false; after deleting one selected palette from the store -> CARDS-AFTER-DELETE 2, MIX-SOURCES-AFTER-DELETE 1, MIX-DISABLED-AFTER-DELETE false, and pressing Mix produced a RESULT with ERRS []. canMix requires length>=2 while only ONE selected card is visible — arithmetic proof the deleted palette is still an operand.
defects.mechanism: The selector holds a private copy of library rows instead of deriving them. removePalette can only be emitted from a card rendered from savedPalettes, so once a palette leaves the library its selection entry becomes unreachable while remaining live in the reducer.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/r3/probe-r3e-c15-verify.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Key selection by slug and DERIVE the operands: `const selectedSlugs = ref(new Set<string>())` plus `const selectedPalettes = computed(() => savedPalettes.value.filter(p => selectedSlugs.value.has(p.slug)))`. Deletion then removes the operand by construction — no watcher, no reconciliation, no possible skew, and a stale Set entry is inert and self-heals. This also retires addPalette's hand-rolled dedupe (useMixingState.ts:66) and fixes C-19 in the same stroke.

defects.defect: The 20-line "stable keys for TransitionGroup" mechanism re-keys every survivor on removal, which kills the `.vj-enter-move` FLIP the TransitionGroup exists for and force-remounts every following WatercolorDot.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98 — `const mapKey = `${sc.css}::${i}`` puts the INDEX inside the identity. Replayed verbatim (including useMixingState.removeColor's filter and the :90-98 pruner): `start red,blue,green => keys 0,1,2 / rm[1] red,green => keys 0,3 / rm[0] green => keys 4 / set4 a,b,c,d => keys 5,6,7,8 / rm[0] b,c,d => keys 9,10,11`. `.vj-enter-move` is defined at demo/styles/animations.css:99 and applies only to elements that persist across the patch.
defects.mechanism: Render-time side table holding identity that belongs to the datum. Positional identity means any non-tail removal renumbers every survivor, so nothing persists, so FLIP never runs and each survivor unmounts/remounts — discarding and re-minting its useId()-namespaced SVG <filter>, the exact per-swatch cost the Glass 7 dot's own docblock exists to avoid. Strictly worse than the two characters `:key="i"`, which at least patches survivors in place.
defects.reproduction: node -e with the :81-98 algorithm (output pasted above); also docs/.../wb-mix-sourceselector/swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Delete :78-98 entirely (the Map, the counter, the computed, the watcher, and the now-unused ref/watch imports). Mint identity where the datum is born: add `id: string` to SelectedColor and set `crypto.randomUUID()` in useMixingState.addColor, then `:key="sc.id"`. Identity belongs to the datum, never to a render-time side table.

defects.defect: Palettes mode wraps <PaletteCard> in a native <button>, nesting interactive content (a nested <button aria-label="Palette menu"> and a role="article") inside a button — invalid HTML, and a direct contradiction of PaletteCard's own written contract.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 wraps the card. PaletteCard.vue:1-4 states: "button semantics on the card are omitted because inner interactive controls must be reachable — using article + click is the correct pattern for a card container that also houses nested interactive elements." Live (evidence/r3/probe-r3b): INTERACTIVE-IN-BUTTON ["DIV|article|Palette: Sunrise","BUTTON||Palette menu","DIV|article|Palette: Deep Sea","BUTTON||Palette menu"]. HTML spec: <button>'s content model forbids interactive content descendants; ARIA 1.2 gives role=button presentational children, so descendant exposure is engine-dependent.
defects.mechanism: Consumer re-implements a producer's state and re-imposes the exact semantics the producer deliberately declined. PaletteCard already emits `click` (PaletteCard.vue:26) precisely so consumers take the interaction WITHOUT wrapping it.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/r3/probe-r3b-dropdown-and-nesting.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Drop the wrapper button. Bind `<PaletteCard @click="togglePalette(palette)" :selected="isSelected">` and move aria-pressed / aria-label / the selection ring into PaletteCard as a first-class `selected` prop — which is also the correct home for the ring (edicts 4, 5) and what the palette browser will want. NOTE for the cure wave: do NOT sell this on a double-fire; see C-COR.

defects.defect: The chip remove control is 16x16 px, has no accessible name, is hit-testable while fully invisible, and defaults to type="submit".

defects.defect: MAX_COLORS/MIN_COLORS are enforced only on discarded template attributes; one add path has no cap at all, and the reducer has neither bound.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:36-40 defines the bounds; :172 applies MAX only via `:disabled` on the ghost dot — an attribute Glass 7 discards (measured disabledAttr: null). The second add path :220 emits addColor with no check. useMixingState.ts:55-57 addColor has no cap; :42 boots at ref([]) while MIN_COLORS=1 declares 0 illegal.
defects.mechanism: Invariant expressed in the view rather than in the reducer. A guard in a template is a suggestion; a guard in the reducer is a law. The floor also traps the last chip — with exactly one colour the user can neither mix (needs >=2) nor clear it here; the only escape is demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:220.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent behind C-1; source-established at all three sites.
defects.proposedCure: Move both bounds into useMixingState (addColor returns early past the cap; drop MIN_COLORS — 0 is the honest floor since canMix>=2 already speaks the real constraint) and let the view read canAddColor/canRemoveColor off the machine.

defects.defect: NEW r3 — a zero-colour palette is a legal, selectable, ring-lit, canMix-satisfying, mixable operand that contributes nothing.

defects.defect: `:css-color="''"` defeats PaletteCard's EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH sentinel and threads an empty string into a colour resolver.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:266 passes :css-color="''". PaletteCard.vue:223-226: `const EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH = "#888"; const firstColor = computed(() => props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? props.cssColor ?? EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH)`. `''` is not nullish, so ?? keeps it; firstColor becomes '' for a zero-colour palette and flows into safeCss -> certifyAccentInk('') (demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:353-359).
defects.mechanism: An empty-string sentinel passed where `undefined` is the declared absence (`cssColor?: string | undefined`), silently disabling a downstream fallback.
defects.reproduction: PROBED AND IT DID NOT THROW — evidence/r3/probe-r3c drove a zero-colour palette through the full mix flow: zero pageerror, only the dev-config VITE_API_URL console notice. Report this as a CONTRACT VIOLATION, not as a live parseCssColor crash.
defects.proposedCure: Omit the prop entirely; it is optional. Also switch MixSourceSelector.vue:33 to `inject(LIBRARY_PORT_KEY)!` to match MixPane.vue:16 — the `pm?.savedPalettes.value ?? []` optional chain is a masking fallback (edict 2) that degrades to "you have no palettes" where the parent asserts presence.

defects.defect: Every teardown in the extract subtree is registered on `onBeforeUnmount`, but every pane in this app is rendered inside `<KeepAlive>` (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120, routed by demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:85). A view change DEACTIVATES the subtree — the DOM leaves the document but the component is not unmounted — so `onBeforeUnmount` never fires and NO teardown in this component ever runs on a view switch. Three independent resources leak as a result: the camera MediaStream, the quantize Worker, and the eyedropper's window keydown listener. This OVERTURNS the pass-2 negative result which recorded these same three hooks as 'Clean' on the basis of source presence.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 `<KeepAlive :max="max">` · demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:85 `if (name === "extract") return ExtractPane;` · ExtractWorkbench.vue:281 `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` · useImageQuantize.ts:148-151 · useExtractSession.ts:194-196 · ImageEyedropper.vue:242-245. MEASURED (probe-r3/WBX-probe7.mjs): `after open : {"fileInputs":1,"videos":1,"videoHasSrcObject":[true],"streams":1,"states":[["live"]]}` → `at #/mix : {"fileInputs":0,"videos":0,"streams":1,"states":[["live"]]}` → `at #/gradient: {..."states":[["live"]]}` → `6s later : {..."states":[["live"]]}`. MEASURED (WBX-probe8.mjs): `boot {made:0,terminated:0,kd:3,files:1}` → `eyedrop open {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:1}` → `at #/mix {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:0}` → `at #/gradient {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:0}`. The repo already documents this hazard for a sibling: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:232-233 'The picker pane is KeepAlive-cached; navigating away parks the blob'.
defects.mechanism: lifecycle-hook mismatch with the host contract — teardown registered for an unmount the component never receives
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract → click 'Open camera' → grant permission (let it fully resolve; videoHasSrcObject === true) → click any other view (Mix, Gradient). Camera hardware stays live indefinitely; only a full page reload releases it. Three steps, no timing dependency. Re-run: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-r3/WBX-probe7.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the app's own <KeepAlive> contract instead of assuming an unmount. Hoist the camera into a `useCameraCapture()` composable that owns the stream in a shallowRef with an idempotent start() (which also kills C-3, the double-open), a stop() wired to BOTH `onDeactivated` (view change) and `onScopeDispose` (genuine unmount), and an `active` flag the button's disabled binds to directly. Same treatment for the worker in useImageQuantize. The eyedropper's Escape handler moves off `window` onto the overlay element so there is nothing to leak. NOTE: this invalidates pass-2's proposed gestalt cure for C-2 — a request token 'invalidated by scope disposal' never invalidates, because the scope is not disposed on a view change.

defects.defect: The camera-leak BLOCKER is unconditional, not a timing race. Both variants are real, but they describe a second door. The front door needs no race: let getUserMedia fully resolve, then simply switch views.

defects.defect: The eyedropper adds a window-level keydown listener on mount and removes it on onBeforeUnmount; parked open by <KeepAlive>, the add runs and the remove never does. Compounding: the overlay has no modal semantics at all — no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no focus move on open, no focus trap, no focus restore on close, no inert on the covered content — so the leaked global Escape handler is also the ONLY keyboard dismissal the overlay has.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:237-245 (onMounted addEventListener / onBeforeUnmount removeEventListener) · ImageEyedropper.vue:8 is a bare `<div class="absolute inset-0 z-popover …">`. `grep -rn 'role="dialog"\|aria-modal\|useFocusTrap' demo/workbenches/extract/` → no output. MEASURED (WBX-probe8.mjs): window keydown listener count 3 → 4 on eyedropper open, and stays 4 at #/mix and at #/gradient.
defects.mechanism: lifecycle-hook mismatch with the host contract (C-29 family) + global listener where an element-scoped one belongs
defects.reproduction: /#/extract → upload an image → click the preview to open the eyedropper → switch to Gradient → press Escape. A hidden, parked component's close handler runs.
defects.proposedCure: Move the Escape handler onto the overlay element itself (it leaves the document with its subtree, so it cannot leak) and give the overlay real dialog semantics — role="dialog" + aria-modal + focus trap + focus restore — or stop shaping it like a modal.

defects.defect: The quantize Web Worker is never terminated. useImageQuantize's only disposal is onBeforeUnmount, which under <KeepAlive> never fires on a view change.
defects.evidence: useImageQuantize.ts:148-151 `onBeforeUnmount(() => { worker?.terminate(); worker = null; })`. MEASURED (WBX-probe8.mjs, Worker.prototype.terminate instrumented at page boot): `made: 1, terminated: 0` after leaving /#/extract for /#/mix and then /#/gradient (files: 1 → 0 proves the subtree left the document).
defects.mechanism: lifecycle-hook mismatch with the host contract (C-29 family)
defects.reproduction: /#/extract → upload any image (worker constructed) → navigate to /#/mix → /#/gradient. `Worker.prototype.terminate` is never called. Re-run: `node .../probe-r3/WBX-probe8.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: onScopeDispose + onDeactivated inside useImageQuantize (see C-29). Also required for pass-2's C-22 cure to terminate, since that cure assumes a worker-recreation path on a disposal that currently never happens.

defects.defect: `isProcessing` excludes the only phase that blocks the main thread. It is set inside runQuantize, AFTER `await imageFileToPixels(file)` — so createImageBitmap + drawImage + a 48MB getImageData, plus a second 48MB copy at `pixels.buffer.slice(0)`, all run on the main thread with the processing flag FALSE. The result: a half-second UI freeze during which the component's only accessible progress signal is provably absent. The module docstring advertising 'All run quantization off main thread with Transferable ArrayBuffer' is measurably false for the dominant cost.
defects.evidence: useImageQuantize.ts:87 (flag set) vs :106 (the await it sits behind) · :18-26 imageFileToPixels · :93 `const buffer = pixels.buffer.slice(0)` · docstring :1-6. MEASURED (WBX-probe5.mjs, 4000x3000 PNG, 6,824,131 bytes): `wall ms (upload -> readout): 1077` · `longTasks: [517,63]  maxLongTask: 517  totalLongMs: 580` · `anySkeleton (isProcessing ever rendered): false` · the 60ms sampling interval stops firing from t=181ms to t=700ms — a 519ms hole that is the long task itself. Corroborated by WBX-probe2.mjs (`skeletons: 0` at 150/400/900/2000/4000/7000ms) and all four WBX-probe4.mjs snapshots.
defects.mechanism: the async boundary is drawn in the wrong place — the worker offload offloads only the cheap part (k-means on <=10k sampled pixels) while two 48MB main-thread operations sit outside the state flag
defects.reproduction: /#/extract → upload a 4000x3000 image. Main thread blocks 517ms; PaletteCardSkeleton (its role="status" aria-label="Loading palette" being the only accessible progress signal) never renders. Re-run: `node .../probe-r3/WBX-probe5.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: createImageBitmap, OffscreenCanvas and getImageData are all available inside a worker. Post the File itself to quantize-worker.ts (File/Blob is structured-cloneable and cheap) and decode there. Main-thread pixel work drops to zero, the slice(0) copy disappears, decode failures arrive through the typed error channel that already exists, and isProcessing can honestly be set on the first synchronous line. One transposition folds C-5, C-7, C-14 and C-25.

defects.defect: The corrupt-image failure is not merely silent — it is stale attribution. Run AFTER a successful extraction (the realistic sequence; r1 and r2 both reproduced only from a fresh pane), the workbench displays a broken next to a k-rail gradient and a dominance readout that are byte-identical to the PREVIOUS image's, with no error line and an unhandled rejection. The preview is committed before anything decodes, and the fire-and-forget quantize call has no .catch.
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:164-168 (previewDataUrl written before decode) · :153-157 (runQuantize discards the promise, no .catch) · useImageQuantize.ts:105-108 → :18-26 (createImageBitmap unguarded). MEASURED (WBX-probe4.mjs, one session): `after-good : railBg="linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.543346 0.174006 29.6967) 0%, …" code="oklch(54.334570875357% …29.696692379622deg)" destructiveLines=[] imgNaturalW=64` then `after-corrupt: railBg="…oklch(0.543346 0.174006 29.6967)…" (IDENTICAL) code="oklch(54.334570875357% …)" (IDENTICAL) destructiveLines=[] imgNaturalW=0 unhandled=["InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded."]` · `PAGEERRORS: ["InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded."]`. Screenshot: probe-r3/WBX-corrupt.png. Contradicts the component's own comments: ExtractWorkbench.vue:79 'error ≠ empty: an explicit destructive line' and ImageDropZone.vue:3 'the specimen never lies'.
defects.mechanism: unguarded async with no error boundary; state committed ahead of validation, so a failure leaves a half-updated view that attributes old results to a new input
defects.reproduction: /#/extract → upload a valid image (palette develops) → upload a file with mimeType image/png whose bytes are not a PNG. Re-run: `node .../probe-r3/WBX-probe4.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: Decode first, commit second: one Result-returning intake pipeline where a decode failure sets quantizeError and leaves previewDataUrl and palette untouched. Falls out for free from the C-14 cure (decode in the worker, failure returns {type:'error', error:'image_decode_failed'} through the channel that already exists).

defects.defect: The dominance-vs-first-swatch disagreement that pass-2 derived is TIE-ONLY, and r3's live extraction is the non-tie case where the invariant holds. This scopes pass-2's finding rather than contradicting it — and makes its cure cheaper to justify.

result.strongestDefect: C-29 / C-2 — the camera hardware is never released. Every teardown in the extract subtree is registered on `onBeforeUnmount`, but every pane is rendered inside `<KeepAlive>` (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120, routed by usePaneRouter.ts:85), so a view change deactivates rather than unmounts and NO teardown ever runs. Open the camera on /#/extract, let it fully resolve, click any other view: measured `states:[["live"]]` at #/mix, at #/gradient, and 6s later, with `videos:0` and `fileInputs:0` proving the subtree left the document. The OS camera indicator stays lit with zero UI anywhere in the application that says the camera is on or can stop it; only a full page reload releases the hardware. Three steps, no timing dependency, measured twice by two different methods (WBX-probe6/7). This both re-scopes the r1/r2 blocker from "a race" to "unconditional" and overturns the r2 negative result that recorded the worker/listener/debounce teardowns as "Clean" on the basis of source presence — source-presence of a teardown hook is not evidence that teardown runs; only the host's lifecycle contract is. It also invalidates r2's proposed gestalt cure for C-2 (a request token "invalidated by scope disposal" never invalidates, because the scope is not disposed on a view change).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative is claimed for the component overall. What r3 DID prove clean, recorded so no seat re-walks it: (1) The k-slider debounce works — 8 ArrowRight presses at 35ms intervals produced `postsImmediatelyAfter8Presses: 0` and `postsAfterSettle: [13]`, exactly one worker message carrying the final k (useExtractSession.ts:159-162 behaves as designed). (2) The develop cycle is not wedged on the fast path — WBX-probe2 sampled at 150/400/900/2000/4000/7000ms: `shadowPalette 1 → 0` and `dominanceRow false → true` by t=400ms, stable through t=7000ms; the `<Transition mode="out-in">` at ExtractWorkbench.vue:102 completes, so pass-2's C-22 wedge is a slow-worker phenomenon and not a transition-mode bug. (3) The corrupt-file state is recoverable — WBX-probe4 `after-recover` shows a new gradient and a new readout; nothing latches. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` (edict 8) is clean across all six files — ExtractWorkbench.vue:189, useExtractSession.ts:14,18, useImageQuantize.ts:9,10, quantize-worker.ts:7, ExtractPane.vue:28, ImageEyedropper.vue:99 all use `import type`. (5) Route-level visual health is clean but uninformative — REPORT.json /#/extract, all four Safari matrices: overflowX 0, pageErrors [], consoleErrors [], main 1, imgNoAlt 0 — clean only because no capture ever hands the component a file. (6) None of the three named repo hazards apply: no ValueUnit wrapping, no defineModel, no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no ungated rAF loop (the single rAF at ExtractWorkbench.vue:249 is a one-shot await — its defect is the wrong primitive, carried finding C-18, not the PRM-RAF epidemic). CONVERSELY, the r2 negative result "Worker termination / debounce cleanup / eyedropper listener + sampler dispose — Clean" is WITHDRAWN by measurement (see C-29/C-30/C-31).

result.strongestDefect: D-1 + D-24 as a coupled pair: `/#/mix` boots into Colors mode, and Colors mode has no operable control at all — both add paths are `WatercolorDot`s carrying `tag="button"`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0 does not have (`inheritAttrs:false`, hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`, no slot), so `@click`/`aria-label`/`:disabled`/`:title`/`<Plus>` are all silently discarded. And the two e2e specs that gate this exact flow assert `getByRole("button", {name: "Add current color to the mix"})`, which resolves to **0** nodes on the shipped route — so the behavioural gate that should have caught the regression at the glass-ui 7 adoption is itself red.

The narrow negative proofs that do hold, each with positive evidence: (1) wrap/overflow is genuinely correct — at n=12 the well grows 107.9→180.3 px, two rows of 7+6, `overflowX 0`, `scrollHeight−clientHeight = 0`; this is the one populated behaviour that is right and no prior pass could verify it.
