defects.defect: Colors mode — the route's default mode — has no reachable add affordance. Both operand-entry paths are `WatercolorDot`s carrying `tag="button"`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0 removed. The producer is `inheritAttrs:false`, reads only `class`/`style` from `useAttrs()`, renders a hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`, and has no slot — so `@click`, `aria-label`, `:disabled`, `:title` and the `<Plus>` glyph are all silently discarded.
defects.evidence: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` render fn (`inheritAttrs: !1`; `let n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style)`; `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", … style:u([f.value,{…,pointerEvents:"none",…}])})`). Call sites `demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:164–176` and `:211–221`. Live WebKit probe: `ghost = {tagName:"SPAN", attrs:[data-v-292b9032, data-v-a3e86846, aria-hidden="true", class=…, data-testid, data-variant, style], pointerEvents:"none", tabIndex:-1, isFocusable:false, svgClasses:["watercolor-filter-host"]}` — complete attribute list, no aria-label/disabled/title/onclick, and the `<Plus>` svg is absent. `ADD-SLOT FORCE-CLICK: chips before = 0 after = 0`. `FOCUSABLES IN SOURCE SELECTOR SUBTREE: ["BUTTON|name=Colors","BUTTON|name=Palettes"]`.
defects.mechanism: producer-contract drift — a major-version adoption (glass-ui 7.0.0, W44) migrated the package but not the call sites; `inheritAttrs:false` swallows the dropped props with no Vue warning. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91` abrogated the `tag="button"` interactive host by name and listed Mix among the sites to migrate.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe.mjs` against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000; or open /#/mix and attempt to add a colour — nothing is clickable or focusable.
defects.proposedCure: Do not restore `tag`. Transpose onto the seat/face split the canon already specifies: one `SwatchSeat` composition IN GLASS-UI — a named `<button>` seat owning accessible name, `disabled`, focus and press, containing the `WatercolorDot` as an `aria-hidden` face plus the glyph as a sibling. Same seat serves Gradient stops and Generate specimens (VC:91). Discharges D-21, D-25, D-26, D-27, D-28 and the naming half of D-15 as a consequence.

defects.defect: The behavioural gate for D-1 is red and its central assertion is unsatisfiable. `e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:39–43` and `e2e/smoke/safari/mix-flow.spec.ts:28–34` both open with `main.getByRole("button", {name: "Add current color to the mix"})`, which resolves to zero nodes on the shipped route.
defects.evidence: Probe: `getByRole('button',{name:"Add current color to the mix"}).count() = 0`; `any node with that accessible text: 0`; `total buttons in main: 3`. Spec run: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` → `1 failed  [smoke] › e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:28:1 › mix flow: convergence lands at the result plate within budget` (observed failure is earlier, a Dock `option` instability at `e2e/smoke/fixtures/dock.ts:78`, `element is not stable`).
defects.mechanism: Two independent gates are blind for the same reason. The visual sweep counts `namelessButtons` (REPORT.md:99, `/#/mix: 1`) and structurally cannot see non-buttons; the behavioural sweep that names the affordance directly is failing upstream of the assertion. Nothing asserts that a route's default mode exposes at least one operable control.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe6.mjs` (count 0) and `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke` (1 failed). The two claims are stated separately: the pasted run does not itself prove the add-slot assertion fails, because it dies earlier.
defects.proposedCure: Restore the gate before the fix. The right gate is not 'the add button is visible' but a census: every route's default mode exposes ≥1 operable, named control. The current `namelessButtons` sweep cannot express that; the visual harness can. Fix the Dock `option` instability separately so the spec reaches its own assertions.

defects.defect: `TransitionGroup` keys are minted from `` `${sc.css}::${i}` `` — index inside identity. Removing one operand re-keys every survivor, so a single deletion tears down and re-creates the entire rack.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:78–98`. Live DOM, 3 operands, `removeColor(0)`, sampled at +120 ms: `before marks = ["m0","m1","m2"]`, `after = {count:5, marks:["m0","m1","m2","«NEW NODE»","«NEW NODE»"], leaving:3, entering:2}`. Frame `./frames/WBMSS-remove-churn.png` shows both survivors mid-scale — entering, not moving. `demo/styles/utils.css:174–177` sets `--vj-enter-scale: 0` and `position:absolute` on leaving children, so three out-of-flow corpses stack over two re-inflating survivors.
defects.mechanism: Identity synthesised from position. The 20-line Map + counter + watcher delivers exactly `:key="i"` behaviour while appearing to deliver stability; `.vj-enter-move` (animations.css:99) can never fire because no element survives with its key. Also breaks the `data-mix-source`/`data-mix-color` convergence lift documented at `:125–126`, which needs each chip's real position.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe4.mjs` — seeds 3 operands through the live `addColor`, calls `removeColor(0)`, samples the DOM at +120 ms. Prior passes labelled this 'reproduction blocked by D-1'; pass 3 unblocks it by driving the component's own functions through the Vue app instance.
defects.proposedCure: Mint identity at the source: `useMixingState.addColor` returns `{id, css, source}`; key on `sc.id`. The Map, the counter and the watcher (≈20 lines) all delete, `.vj-enter-move` starts working, and the same `id` is the prerequisite for the missing reorder (D-19).

defects.defect: The colors-mode empty state was never designed. At n=0 the well is a fully-dressed 462×107.9 px fixture (dashed border + `--well-bg` tone step + `--shadow-cartoon-sm`) holding one 48×48 inert ghost — 4.62 % ink — where the sibling Palettes mode ships a complete `EmptyState` with eyebrow, message and hint.
defects.evidence: Measured: well 462.0×107.9 / ghost 48×48 ⇒ 4.62 % (desktop), 324.0×100.6 / 44×44 ⇒ 5.94 % (390), 254.0×100.6 ⇒ 7.58 % (320), 700.0×215.9 / 96×96 ⇒ 6.10 % (actual 200 % zoom). Source selector = 162.9 px of a 684.7 px inspector card = 23.8 %. Canon: `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:28` (§3 law 2) 'Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears'; `:202` (§7 Mix) 'No shadow palette filler appears when an operand is absent'; `:48` 'absent operands occupy no filler'.
defects.mechanism: Two opposite empty doctrines in one component. `MixSourceSelector.vue:231–238` carries a 22-line comment defending the refusal of ghost filler in the Palettes branch — 'TRUE EMPTY speaks the EmptyState invitation ALONE … never ghost cards before the caption' — and forty lines earlier the default mode ships exactly the forbidden thing.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix and measure `.dashed-well` against `.add-slot-ghost`; `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe2.mjs` runs all six arms. Frames `./frames/WBMSS-desktop-1440.png`, `WBMSS-dark-1440.png`, `WBMSS-mobile-390.png`.
defects.proposedCure: At zero operands the rack collapses to the invitation itself — the named add seat plus one line of copy, content-hugging, no border, no tone step, no shadow. The well earns its boundary at ≥1 operand, when there is a set to bound. Use the Palettes-mode `EmptyState` register verbatim; the component already owns it.

defects.defect: `MAX_COLORS = 12` is silently unenforced AND unannounced. `canAddColor` goes false at the cap, `:disabled` is bound — and dropped by the producer — so the ghost still renders at slot 13, advertising capacity that does not exist, while the operand counter that would have said '12 / 12' was deleted at W5-7.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:40` (`canAddColor`), `:172` (`:disabled="!canAddColor || undefined"`), `:117–118` (the counter's deletion comment). Live at n=12: well 462.0×180.3, 12 chips, and the ghost still present in `./frames/WBMSS-n12.png`. Canon: `PROPORTION-AUDIT.md` PR-08 — 'Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient → ADD-AFFORDANCE'.
defects.mechanism: A boundary state expressed only through a dropped HTML attribute. With no counter, no message and no visual change, the cap is invisible in every direction — the user learns it by clicking nothing.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs` seeds 12 operands through the live `addColor`; the `.add-slot-ghost` node is still in the DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Move the count invariant into `useMixingState` beside the `canMix` it already owns (`canAdd`/`canRemove`), and render the boundary as durable state on the seat — the seat disappears or announces 'maximum 12 operands', not an inert dimmed ornament.

defects.defect: The remove badge is bounding-box anchored (`-top-1 -right-1`) on a per-seed randomised silhouette, and is a fixed `bg-destructive` red over arbitrary user colour — so both its position relative to the mark and its contrast against the mark are unbounded.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:153`. The blob edge is a seeded `border-radius` from glass-ui `randomRadii` over range `[20,80]` (`watercolor-dot.js`), so the mark's actual edge varies per seed while the badge anchors to the wrapper rect. Measured badge `bg: rgb(219,36,36)`. Frame `./frames/WBMSS-hover3-crop.png`: on the crimson operand the badge is a near-null delta against its own ground. The same file, at `:134–145`, states the register law it breaks: 'rings on WatercolorDots ride the dot's own silhouette … or do not exist — the dead utility is excised, never re-minted geometric.'
defects.mechanism: A hard geometric mark stamped onto an organic randomised silhouette, with a fixed colour on a user-data ground. In a chromatic laboratory, any control whose colour is fixed and whose ground is the specimen has no contrast floor by construction.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs`, hover the first chip; badge geometry and `bg` are printed. Frame `./frames/WBMSS-hover3-crop.png`.
defects.proposedCure: The remove control belongs on the seat rect (D-1's `SwatchSeat`), not on the face — a named control at a real target size, anchored to geometry the design owns, in a neutral register that composes with any specimen colour.

defects.defect: The sole mark in the n=0 well fails non-text contrast at the application's own default colour: ghost stroke vs well = 2.88 : 1, below the 3:1 floor. Because the stroke colour is `--watercolor-color` = the live picker colour, the ratio is unbounded below — pick a colour near the well tone and the only affordance in a 462×108 px fixture disappears.
defects.evidence: Canvas-resolved measurement on the live page: `{strokeColor: "lab(92 88.800003 20)", wellBg: "oklab(0.913299 0.005463 0.013024)", ratio: 2.88}`. WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor is 3:1. Canon: `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82` (§4.1) — 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.'
defects.mechanism: State/boundary contrast bound to user data rather than to the material tier. This narrows the standing negative proof: passes 1–2 measured three TEXT ratios (5.08/6.29/5.71) and declared contrast sound; no pass had measured the surface's only non-text mark.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs` — the `GHOST STROKE vs WELL` line. Dark-mode corollary in `./frames/WBMSS-dark-1440.png`: the stroke keeps full chroma while the well darkens, making the inert ornament the highest-chroma mark in the column.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of D-1's cure: once the affordance is a real seat with its own material, its boundary reads against `--well-bg` on a tokenised rung, and the specimen colour stays inside the face where it is data rather than chrome.

defects.defect: The operand floor is authored twice with two values — `MIN_COLORS = 1` / `canRemoveColor = length > 1` in the selector vs `canMix = length >= 2` in the state machine (and `VC:202` says '2–12 colors'). At exactly one operand the user is in a rendered terminal state: unmixable, unremovable, and (with D-1) unable to add.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:37,39` vs `demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:51`. Live at n=1: `removeButtons[0] = {w:16, h:16, opacity:"0.3", name:"«NONE»", disabled:true}` — `disabled:opacity-30` beats the hover-gated `opacity-0`, so a dimmed unnamed X is permanently visible with no explanation. Frame `./frames/WBMSS-n1-crop.png`. Only exit is the Dock overflow menu (`demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:220`).
defects.mechanism: A count invariant authored in two files with two values. The selector blocks the harmless state (0) and permits the useless one (1).
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs` with n=1 seeded. Pass 2 derived this from source; pass 3 renders it.
defects.proposedCure: The invariant belongs once, in `useMixingState`, exposed as `canAdd`/`canRemove` beside the `canMix` it already owns. Floor 0 (empty is the invitation), not 1.

defects.defect: Palettes mode wraps the Browse/Library entity `PaletteCard` — which itself contains a real `<Button aria-label="Palette menu">`, a vote control, an inline-rename target and its own root `@click` — inside a native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>`. Interactive content inside a button: invalid content model, flattened AT tree, unreachable inner controls.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:246–268` × `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:26` (`role="article" … @click="$emit('click')"`), `:78` (`PaletteCardMeta` vote), `:93–101` (`<Button … aria-label="Palette menu">`). PaletteCard's own authorship note at `:1–4` refuses this exact wrapper: 'button semantics on the card are omitted because inner interactive controls must be reachable — using article + click is the correct pattern'. Canon: `PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:77` (§5.12) — the seat is a `<button>` CHILD spanning specimen/identity, deliberately excluding the menu.
defects.mechanism: A category error: a library entity card is used as a mix operand, importing its whole verb surface (menu, vote, rename, drag handle, featured badge, cartoon press choreography) into a context where none of those verbs apply, then suppressed with an outer button. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102` uses 'seven-mode omnibus' pejoratively, in the sentence forbidding it.
defects.reproduction: Source-derived plus pass-2 live measurement (`wrappers: [{aria:"Select palette Sunset Drift", pressed:"false", nestedInteractive:["BUTTON:Palette menu"]}]`). Pass 3 could NOT re-render this — the dev server logs `value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED … targeting the cross-origin production API` and `pm.savedPalettes` is a read-only computed, so the library could not be seeded.
defects.proposedCure: An operand chip, not a library card: identity + colour strip + ordinal + remove, and nothing else. If PaletteCard is reused, add a `compact` register beside its existing `layout` prop and move the pressed seat INSIDE, spanning specimen/identity per §5.12. The Browse/Library card stays in Browse and Library.

defects.defect: Two type registers for one job, 12 px apart, inside one component. `Selected` (`:119`) is `text-small font-display font-semibold` — Fraunces, weight 600, 16.4 px, sentence case; its peer section heading `From palettes` (`:183`) and the adjacent `COLOR SPACE` / `HUE METHOD` use `.section-label` — Fira Code, 400, 14.38 px, uppercase, 1.44 px tracking.
defects.evidence: Computed on the live page: `selectedLabel = {cls:"text-small font-display font-semibold text-muted-foreground", font:"Fraunces…serif", size:"16.4px", weight:"600", tt:"none", ls:"normal"}` vs `colorSpaceLabel = {cls:"section-label", font:"Fira Code…monospace", size:"14.384px", weight:"400", tt:"uppercase", ls:"1.4384px"}`. Canon: `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:66–78` (§4) declares the role matrix CLOSED across all eighteen compositions; 'control or label, including dropdown options → text-small → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'.
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled label class bypassing the `.section-label` primitive its own sibling consumes. The palette name at `:205` repeats it (`text-small font-display font-semibold` where the matrix assigns palette identity `--type-subheading`).
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe.mjs` — the `selectedLabel` / `colorSpaceLabel` block. Visible in every frame: a serif bold word 12 px above a mono uppercase word, captioning sections of the same column.
defects.proposedCure: One label register, chosen once in the shared recipe: `.section-label` for both `Selected` and `From palettes`; `--type-subheading` for palette identity; Fira for both counts.

defects.defect: The remove control is hover-only, nameless and 16×16 — three separate floors breached by one 6-line element.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:152–158` (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, `w-4 h-4`, no `aria-label`, icon-only `<X>`). Measured at every n: `{w:16, h:16, opacity:"0"→"1" on hover, name:"«NONE»"}`. `FOCUSABLES IN WELL @n=3: ["BUTTON|tabindex=0|name=«NONE»" ×3]` — at 12 operands the AT transcript is twelve consecutive 'button's. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 floor is 24×24. Canon: `PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51` (PR-07) hover-only/unlabeled controls; §5.7 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities'.
defects.mechanism: Visual glyph, operable target and reveal condition collapsed into one 16 px box. On touch there is no hover, so the only in-component removal path does not exist on mobile; the only full-clear lives three levels away in the Dock overflow menu (`usePaneRouter.ts:220`).
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs` — `removeButtons` array and `FOCUSABLES IN WELL`. Frames `./frames/WBMSS-hover3-crop.png`, `WBMSS-n1-crop.png`.
defects.proposedCure: The remove control moves onto D-1's named seat: persistent (not hover-gated), named, and at a real target size via invisible seat geometry so the visible glyph can stay small — the exact separation §5.7 prescribes.

defects.defect: The 'ordered N-operand rack' has no ordinal display and no reorder affordance, while `mixColorSequence` consumes the operands in order.
defects.evidence: `useMixingState.ts:89` folds `selectedColors` in order. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202` — 'An ORDERED N-operand rack … Source mode, add/remove/REORDER, method, unequal-palette strategy, provenance and commit share the same control grammar'; `:131` (§5.2) — 'horizontal explicit reorder: palette colors, OPERANDS, stops — after Space grabs, Right moves one visual position right … every move announces item and position of total'. The component implements none of it. Live at n=12: twelve anonymous blobs, no ordinal, no handle, no key binding.
defects.mechanism: The rack is ordered in the state machine and unordered in the interface. D-11's key churn is the reason it cannot be added today — there is no stable identity to reorder.
defects.reproduction: Source + canon; rendered absence confirmed at n=12 (`./frames/WBMSS-n12.png`).
defects.proposedCure: Follows D-11's cure: once operands carry a minted `id`, add the §5.2 grab/move/drop keyboard contract plus an ordinal on each seat. Pointer drag, arrow movement and numeric entry must resolve to the same ordinal.

defects.defect: Operand provenance is unrenderable. `SelectedColor.source` ('picker' or a palette name) exists in the model and is spent entirely on `:title` on the `WatercolorDot`, which glass-ui 7 drops.
defects.evidence: `MixSourceSelector.vue:150` (`:title="`${sc.css} (${sc.source})`"`) vs `useMixingState.ts:25–28`. Measured on every rendered chip: `dots: [{title: null, aria: "true", …} ×12]`. Canon: `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202` requires provenance in the Mix control grammar.
defects.mechanism: Family with D-1 — the attribute is dropped by `inheritAttrs:false`. The data exists; the only channel chosen for it does not survive the producer.
defects.reproduction: `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe3.mjs` — the `dots` array at n=1/3/12.
defects.proposedCure: Provenance belongs in the seat's accessible name and, if it is worth showing, in visible chip metadata — not in a `title` tooltip on an `aria-hidden` face. Discharged by D-1's cure.

defects.defect: `.add-slot-ghost` is a scoped twin — the identical four-line recipe is declared in two components, while its sibling in the very same well (`.dashed-well`) is correctly a single shared recipe in `demo/styles/utils.css`.
defects.evidence: `demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:277` and `demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:286`. CSSOM on the live page: `"add-slot-ghost": [".add-slot-ghost[data-v-0ce6f2b0]", ".add-slot-ghost[data-v-a3e86846]"]` — both ship. `demo/styles/utils.css:186` states the rule: 'never a scoped twin (the S.W7-7 lesson)'.
defects.mechanism: A shared affordance recipe duplicated per component instead of hoisted. Compounding: with `WatercolorDot` slot-less, BOTH copies are inert — they centre a child that no longer renders.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "add-slot-ghost" demo/`; CSSOM scan in `node …/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe4.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Both copies delete when D-1's `SwatchSeat` lands in glass-ui and owns the glyph centring. No demo-side hoist is needed — the recipe belongs to the producer composition, not to `demo/styles/`.

defects.defect: `/mix` appears in ZERO of the six state matrices in the visual-audit corpus, so every state row for this component other than the four base captures is probe-derived rather than corpus-backed.
defects.evidence: `ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/{forced-colors,keyboard-focus,reduced-motion,rtl,rtl-mobile,zoom-200}-desktop/` → each contains exactly `adminusers.png · blob.png · browse.png · gradient.png · picker.png`. The base matrices (`safari-desktop-{light,dark}`, `safari-mobile-{light,dark}`) do carry `mix.png`.
defects.mechanism: State-matrix coverage was cut to five routes; the Mix workbench is not among them. This is the corpus-side twin of D-24: the surface with the blocker is the surface least observed.
defects.reproduction: The `ls` above.
defects.proposedCure: Extend the state matrices to the full route inventory, or at minimum to every route whose default mode owns an operable control. Pass 3's `WBMSS-probe2.mjs` is a working template for the six arms.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, round 3 (independent, additive to rounds 1 and 2)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context seat). Matches the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with; declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: `el.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` is called unguarded on the handle's pointerdown — the pane's only drag path. The call is specified to throw (NotFoundError / InvalidStateError); the throw lands in Vue's callWithErrorHandling and the app ErrorBoundary unmounts the whole pane, destroying every stop, position, easing curve and setting. `lostpointercapture` has no handler anywhere in the subtree.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue:132-133. Isolation run `probes/challenge-C-r3-stuck-drag.mjs`: S0 {"handles":["Gradient stop at 0%","Gradient stop at 100%"],"rail":true,"tile":true} → S1 {"handles":[],"rail":false,"tile":false,"mainText":"This panel hit an unexpected error. | Failed to execute 'setPointerCapture' on 'Element': No active pointer with the given id is found. | Try again"}. `grep -n "lostpointercapture" demo/workbenches/gradient/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: A DOM call whose specification includes a throw sits unguarded on the interaction path, inside an architecture where the model is instantiated INSIDE the component the ErrorBoundary unmounts (GradientVisualizer.vue:32) — so any throw anywhere is a total data-loss event. Same mechanism family as round 1's C-1 (partial parser at a total contract).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r3-stuck-drag.mjs — CONFIRMED via synthetic pointerdown (the path assistive tech / automation / injected events take). The everyday-human-mouse trigger is a HYPOTHESIS: a real mouse always has an active pointer. The unguarded throwing call, the crash and the blast radius are confirmed and pasted.
defects.proposedCure: Two moves, neither a try/catch (edict 2 forbids the masking fallback): (1) bind `lostpointercapture` to a RELEASE handler that clears draggingId/handleGesture and commits nothing — the same event split R2-N1 needs for pointercancel — and delete the rail's duplicate pointermove fallback so the handle solely owns the gesture; (2) hoist `useGradientModel()` to a route-scoped store provided ABOVE the ErrorBoundary so the model outlives its view. Move (2) simultaneously dissolves C-1, C-4's throwing computed and this finding.

defects.defect: Blurring the CSS editor inside the 500 ms debounce window destroys the user's in-progress text and then paints a permanent, FALSE invalid state: the pane marks its own canonical, valid serialization `aria-invalid="true"` with a verdict naming a token that is nowhere on screen. The verdict is sticky — a real model edit does not clear it. Directly contradicts the contract the file states in its own comments ("WIP is never destroyed").
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:34-40 (the stated contract), :55-57 (500 ms trailing debounce), :68-73 (`onBlur` consults `hasError`, i.e. the PREVIOUS parse's verdict). Run `probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs`: after blur → editorText reverts to "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)"; 1.2 s later → {"borderDestructive":true,"ariaInvalid":"true","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""}. Stickiness, `probes/challenge-C-r3-sticky-verdict-and-cost.mjs`: after 8 ArrowRight the model really changed (handles "Gradient stop at 8%", editor text updated) and {"invalid":"true","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""} survives.
defects.mechanism: A verdict and the text it judged are two refs on two independent clocks (focus-driven render vs a trailing timer), with no ordering relation and no shared identity, so they can describe different strings. WCAG 3.3.1 + 4.1.2.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs (P1) and .../challenge-C-r3-sticky-verdict-and-cost.mjs (A0/A1). CONFIRMED, pasted, twice.
defects.proposedCure: Make the authoring transaction ONE value. `onBlur` flushes the pending parse before deciding what to render (`demo/shared/utils.ts:36-42` already ships `.cancel()`; `.flush()` is the same three lines), and the verdict is stored WITH the source text it judged — `{ source, reason } | null` — so a verdict whose `source` is no longer what the editor holds is unrenderable by construction and `aria-invalid` cannot outlive the text that earned it.

defects.defect: Pressing Enter in the CSS editor silently welds the tokens on either side of the break: the text handed to the parser is read with `textContent`, which does not represent block breaks, so `red` ⏎ `0%` reaches the parser as `red0%` and the user is told a token they never typed is unparseable — on a surface explicitly built for multiple lines.
defects.evidence:
GradientCodeEditor.vue:59-62 (`editorRef.value?.textContent`), :93 (`min-h-[5rem] max-h-[12rem] overflow-y-auto whitespace-pre-wrap`). Run `probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs` (P2): {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, red0%, blue 100%)","editorHTML":"linear-gradient(90deg, red
0%, blue 100%)
","verdict":"unparseable color \"red0%\""}. Cure measured in the same probe (P4): textContent "…red0%…" vs innerText "…red\n0%…".
defects.mechanism: Reading a rich contenteditable's text with the DOM-text accessor instead of the RENDERED-text accessor. `tokenizeTopLevel` (gradientParse.ts:70-89) splits on whitespace, and the whitespace it needed was discarded one layer up.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs — CONFIRMED, pasted. A real multi-line PASTE is correct (measured: under white-space:pre-wrap the browser inserts literal \n), which is why no spec sees it — `typeIntoEditor` never presses Enter.
defects.proposedCure: `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` on the editor so the browser cannot insert block elements into a code surface at all; failing that, read `innerText` rather than `textContent` (measured to preserve the break exactly). One attribute or one identifier — no shim, no new module.

defects.defect: The stop-ordering invariant breaks on the KEYBOARD path, not just on drag, and the resulting array order desynchronises DOM/tab order from visual order: after a keyboard-only nudge, Tab visits the handles right → left → right.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:173-179 (`onHandleKeydown` emits the same `update:position` the drag does) → GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96 → useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (`updateStop` writes a raw position, no re-sort; `addStop` at :118 DOES sort and `gradientParse.ts:284-290` REJECTS non-monotonic input — three owners, three policies). Run `probes/challenge-C-r3-focus-order.mjs`: S1 rows=[{0,"Gradient stop at 70%",x:531},{1,"Gradient stop at 50%",x:444},{2,"Gradient stop at 100%",x:665}], domOrder=[0,1,2], visualOrder=[1,0,2]; S2 sequential focus order ["…70%","…50%","…100%"].
defects.mechanism: Ordering is treated as a habit of one of three call sites instead of a property of the type; the view renders `v-for` in array order, so an unsorted array is directly a scrambled focus order. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order + 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/challenge-C-r3-focus-order.mjs — CONFIRMED, pasted; screenshot evidence/challenge-C-r3-crossed-focus-order.png. Gesture: click the rail at 50% to add a stop, focus the first handle, press Shift+ArrowRight x7.
defects.proposedCure: One writer — `setStopPosition(id, pos)` returns the re-sorted model (and re-keys intervals, per C-5) — with `stops` readonly to the view. Ordering becomes unrepresentable-if-violated rather than re-established by whichever call site remembers.

result.strongestDefect: For the component overall, round 1's C-1 stands (an `oklch()` typed in the CSS box destroys the whole pane and every unsaved stop/position/easing curve). My round's contribution is that R3-3 reaches the identical total loss through a second, un-typed door — an unguarded `setPointerCapture` on the only drag path, measured live: two handles + rail + tile → zero, with `main` reading "This panel hit an unexpected error. | Failed to execute 'setPointerCapture' on 'Element': No active pointer with the given id is found." Two independent doors onto the same catastrophe make the shared cure non-negotiable: the model must outlive its view (hoist `useGradientModel()` above the ErrorBoundary). Of the findings FIRST filed by this round, the strongest is R3-1: type into the CSS box and click away, and the component destroys the user's text and then permanently marks its own valid canonical output `aria-invalid="true"` with a verdict naming a token that is not on screen — in direct contradiction of the contract the file states in its own comments, and surviving every subsequent legitimate edit.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the bounding evidence rather than an exoneration. Things I hunted and found CLEAN, each with positive evidence: (1) RTL is sound — the rail's ramp is a physical `linear-gradient(90deg,…)`, the handles use physical `left` (GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57) and `getPosition` measures from `rect.left` (:75-81), so all three are physical and cannot disagree; STATES.json rtl-desktop shows dir=rtl, overflowX 0, and shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png confirms. (2) `colorAtPosition`'s final throw (GradientVisualizer.vue:87) is unreachable by argument, not just by round 2's 11^4 brute force: with list[0].position < p < last.position, the least index j with s_j.position >= p satisfies s_{j-1}.position < p <= s_j.position, so pair j-1 always covers p for ANY array ordering. (3) Hover-ghost cost is bounded — 60 synthetic hover moves produced {"synthMoves":60,"styleWrites":120} with no stall. (4) `copyCSS` cannot produce an unhandled rejection: `writeClipboard` returns a discriminated result rather than rejecting, so round 1's C-2 is a silent-failure defect, not a rejection defect. (5) The `LIBRARY_PORT_KEY` injection IS provided — REPORT.json records "consoleWarnings":[] for /#/gradient on all four Safari matrices and my six live sessions produced none. (6) The three Selects render their label only; the `#description` slot does not leak into the trigger (zoom-200 and rtl shots). (7) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — GradientVisualizer.vue:22,25,26,28 are all `import type`. (8) No rAF loop, no WebGL, no ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch→HSV round-trip anywhere in this subtree (re-checked by grep at HEAD f36f780c). Round 1 was preserved byte-for-byte at challenge-C-implementation.pass-1-2026-07-27.md before the named path was rewritten; round 2 remains at challenge-C-implementation-r2.md.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue and its easing corpus
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier this seat was spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L3-1 — the persisted gradient MODEL is typed by a design-system widget's v-model payload (`export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;`, useGradientModel.ts:49). This is the corpus's inverted edge: a domain type that is parsed from CSS, serialized to CSS, persisted in app state and asserted on by the LIBRARY's own test tree is owned by @mkbabb/glass-ui. Every downstream contrivance follows from it — fabricated `steps: 4, term: "jump-end"` on every bezier tile (easingCatalogue.ts:124-125), fabricated `points: [0,0,1,1]` on every steps tile explicitly commented "Neutral transient cache — steps mode never reads points" (:150-151), and a live non-serializable callable `fn` inside persisted state. (The corpus's single most severe user-visible defect remains the FAMILY_ORDER whitelist — r2's L-1 — which this pass independently REPRODUCED live: selecting `ease-in-quart` in the producer's own preset menu makes the row read "custom" with no tile pressed.)
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four hypotheses were killed with positive evidence and are recorded as negatives: (1) PUBLIC-SURFACE CLEAN — `grep -rn "@src/" demo` returns nothing outside .md reference pages, and every `@mkbabb/value.js/*` (5 distinct) and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/*` (18 distinct) specifier written anywhere in demo/ is a real key in the respective package.json `exports` map; `./chip`, `./fading-scroll`, `./easing` all published. A real npm consumer could write every import in this corpus verbatim — the demo's proof of the public API is honest. (2) The historical "three parallel useDark stores" defect is CURED — all 6 sites import `useGlobalDark` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark`; `grep -rn "useDark(" demo` → no hits. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax fully respected across the corpus (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:16, easingCatalogue.ts:27/31/36, useSpecimenRows.ts:12/17, EasingAuthoringStage.vue:30 all `import type`). (4) The `bleeding` rows for /#/gradient in audit/visual/REPORT.json — 12 entries, all this component's subtree — are BENIGN, not overflow: capture.mjs:107-111 records any element whose right edge passes the viewport, and the strip is a scroll port (measured scrollWidth 1482 / clientWidth 436, overflow-x auto); all four Safari matrices report overflowX 0, pageErrors [], consoleErrors []. The strip is also NOT a god module: 215 lines, one concern.

defects.defect: The persisted gradient interval model is typed as the glass-ui EasingPicker's v-model payload — dependency direction inverted (model → design-system view contract).
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:12,49 — `import type { EasingPickerValue } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing"; export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;`. Consequences visible in-corpus: easingCatalogue.ts:124-125 gives every BEZIER tile `steps: 4, term: "jump-end"`; easingCatalogue.ts:150-151 gives every STEPS tile `points: [0, 0, 1, 1]` with the comment "Neutral transient cache — steps mode never reads points"; useGradientCSS.ts:53-62 fills all six fields to seed one linear interval; the model persists a live callable `fn`, which useGradientCSS.ts:119-123 must then treat as "only a live cache".
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency + wrong owner: a presentation payload type owns a domain model that is parsed, serialized, persisted and gated by the library's own test suite.
defects.reproduction: Read-path reproduction: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:20-24 constructs a GradientModelState literal whose `intervals` element is a glass-ui type; a change to EasingPickerValue in glass 8 therefore reds the value.js publish gate. No runtime repro needed — the type edge is the defect.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose: `export type GradientInterval = { readonly css: string }` (css is already the declared persisted truth and already round-trips via @mkbabb/value.js/css parseTimingFunction + easingFnOf's memo). Authoring params + fn become view state of the open row, derived by ONE 6-line adapter module (easing/pickerAdapter.ts: toPickerValue/fromPickerValue) that is the only place EasingPickerValue is named. Model becomes JSON-serializable; catalogue stops minting five fields to press one tile.

defects.defect: The LIBRARY's test tree imports demo feature internals — four edges from test/ into demo/workbenches/gradient/**, against the declared law that test/ mirrors src/.
defects.evidence: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:6-11 imports `../demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS`, `../demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation`, `../demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel`, `../demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue`. vitest.config.ts:19-22 states "the test tree mirrors the src shape"; vitest.config.ts:23-25 already includes `demo/test/**/*.ts`, and demo/test/{export,glass,palettes} exist.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home ⇒ wrong direction: the library's publish gate now depends on demo feature module paths four levels deep.
defects.reproduction: `git mv demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts <anywhere>` → `npm test` fails on an unresolved import inside test/ with src/ untouched. (Every structural cure this audit proposes — L3-1, r2 L-1, r2 L-8 — performs exactly that move.)
defects.proposedCure: Move the file to demo/test/gradient/v4-consume.test.ts — zero config change, the include glob already covers it, and the four relative paths shorten. If the library wants a 'Value 4 capability' gate it must be phrased against src/ alone.

defects.defect: A single-select group is hand-built from 27 independent Chip toggles while glass-ui publishes ToggleGroup/ToggleGroupItem — the exact component type.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/toggle-group/index.d.ts exports `ToggleGroup`, `ToggleGroupItem`, `ToggleGroupValue`, published at exports["./toggle-group"]. EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:88-117 instead renders N `Chip mode="selectable"` in a bare `role="group"`, and re-implements single-select by dropping an event: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:33-35 `function onTileToggle(tile, on) { if (on) emit("select", tile); }`. Measured: 27 <button> tiles per strip, none with tabindex=-1 → 27 tab stops per strip; 54 after one added stop.
defects.mechanism: Design-system reuse edict violated (edict 4: reuse existing component-type names); a composite widget's semantics (roving tabindex, single-value model) are re-derived from primitives and come out weaker.
defects.reproduction: `document.querySelectorAll('#easing-interval-0 .specimen-tile').length` === 27, all `<button>` with no tabindex attribute (probe-L3-dom-mass.mjs). Tab traversal therefore visits 27 stops to cross one strip.
defects.proposedCure: `<ToggleGroup type="single" v-model="selectedId">` + `<ToggleGroupItem :value="tile.id">` carrying the glyph/label as content. Deletes onTileToggle and the hand-rigged role=group; 'an interval always has a curve' becomes the component contract instead of a dropped event.

defects.defect: The strip's row-derivation composable reaches the BOOT layer through a bang-asserted inject, and that injection has two incompatible disciplines live in the tree.
defects.evidence: Chain: easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:13,40 → demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:345-348 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!;` → provided only by demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:54,82. Two disciplines for one key: `inject(K)!` at useContrastSafeColor.ts:347 and scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownColors.ts:25, vs `inject(K, null)` at picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:128 and picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:95.

defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis at runtime (no standalone mount harness for the gradient workbench exists, which is itself the point): with no provider, inject returns undefined and useContrastSafeColor.ts:356 dereferences `ambient.value` → TypeError. The dual discipline is confirmed by the four citations.
defects.proposedCure: One accessor at the key's home: demo/color-session/keys.ts already publishes INK_AMBIENT_KEY, so publish `useInkAmbient()` beside it with the documented fallback the `inject(K, null)` sites already prove is meaningful. useSpecimenRows then depends on color-session, not on whether useAtmosphereBoot ran.

defects.defect: "Unwrap a value.js Result or throw" exists in three independent copies because value.js publishes no unwrap.
defects.evidence: demo/.../easing/easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 and demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 are the same four-line helper `function easingValue(result: ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>, source: string)` differing only in the error prose; glass-ui carries a third at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js `function U(e,t){if(!t.ok) throw Error(`${e}: ${t.error.code}`); return t.value}`. src/subpaths/easing.ts exports Result-returning constructors and no unwrap.
defects.mechanism: Missing library seam ⇒ copies; identical in shape to the missing serializer (r2 L-2). Note both demo copies are typed by ONE producer function's return type, so they do not even generalize across CubicBezier/steppedEase/linearEasing except by structural accident.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural duplication, proven by the three citations).
defects.proposedCure: value.js publishes it once beside Result: `export function expect<T, E extends { code: string }>(r: Result<T, E>, ctx: string): T`. Three copies delete; the diagnostic message format becomes uniform.

defects.defect: One concept exported under two names across the package boundary (value.js `JumpPosition` vs glass-ui `JumpTerm`), paid for with a no-op cast in the demo.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:136 `const position = term as JumpPosition;`. The unions are provably identical: src/easing.ts:13 `export type JumpPosition = "jump-start" | "jump-end" | "jump-none" | "jump-both"`; src/easing.ts:68 `export const jumpTerms = [...] as const`; glass useEasingPicker.d.ts `import { jumpTerms } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"; export type JumpTerm = (typeof jumpTerms)[number];`. The demo imports one name from each package (easingCatalogue.ts:27-35).
defects.mechanism: Unique-semantic-ownership violation at the type level: glass re-mints value.js's own union, from value.js's own const, under a second name.
defects.reproduction: NONE (type-level; the cast compiles either way, which is why it is a masking cast rather than a real one).
defects.proposedCure: glass re-exports rather than re-mints (`export type { JumpPosition } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"`); the demo imports one name and deletes the cast. Same M3/P7 glass packet as L3-7.

defects.defect: glass-ui's easing default constants exist but are not on the published surface, so the demo hardcodes them in three places.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/constants.d.ts declares DEFAULT_BEZIER_PRESET, DEFAULT_STEP_COUNT = 4, DEFAULT_STEP_TERM = "jump-end", CUSTOM_PRESET; components/easing/index.d.ts (the whole of exports["./easing"]) re-exports only EasingPicker, EasingConfigurator, useEasingPicker and five types. defects.reproduction: NONE (surface gap, proven by the .d.ts citations).
defects.proposedCure: `export * from "./constants"` on the easing barrel — they are `declare const` literals, zero runtime cost — and the demo imports DEFAULT_STEP_COUNT / DEFAULT_STEP_TERM.

defects.defect: The strip's event payload is a catalogue object carrying a factory closure, so the parent's contract is typed by the catalogue's internals.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:88-91 `payload: () => EasingPickerValue;`; EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:26-28 `defineEmits<{ select: [tile: SpecimenTile] }>()`; GradientEasingEditor.vue:73-76 `emit("update-interval", index, tile.payload())`, forcing GradientEasingEditor.vue:34 to import `type SpecimenTile` for no other reason.

defects.defect: CORROBORATION of r2 L-1, now reproduced end-to-end in the live app: an ordering constant doubles as a whitelist and silently drops 6 of value.js's 30 bezierPresets, so a NAMED library preset selected through the producer's own menu reads as "custom" with no tile pressed.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:174 `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` used as a filter at :191 `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. Offline replay of the module's own familyLabelFor over the published presets: 30 presets → families built css,cubic,sine,quad,quart,quint,expo,circ,back → DROPPED quart,quint → 24 bezier + 3 steps = 27, matching the live DOM count exactly (27 .specimen-tile). glass builds its menu unfiltered: dist/easing.js `H = Object.keys(P)` where P = bezierPresets.
defects.mechanism: Two catalogues of one concept, one derived from the library and one hand-ordered; the hand-ordered one silently narrows the set, so adding a preset family to value.js is a no-op in the demo with no error.
defects.reproduction: node probe-L3-preset-drop.mjs (chromium, http://localhost:9000/#/gradient): INIT {"head":"1 → 2 linear","pressed":["linear"]}; the picker's preset menu lists 30 options including ease-in-quart; AFTER selecting ease-in-quart → {"head":"1 → 2 custom","literal":"cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)","pressed":[]}.
defects.proposedCure: Order must be a sort key, never a filter. Better: value.js publishes the taxonomy it already encodes in the preset names (`presetFamily(name)`), the demo sorts by it and renders every preset; unknown families sort last.

defects.mechanism: Two serializers for one model. `serializeGradient` (useGradientCSS.ts:147-162) emits only type/direction/raw stops; every keystroke in that panel triggers a full re-parse that re-seeds all intervals to the linear preset. The destructive act happens in the one surface that cannot display what it destroys.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click the `ease-in-out` easing specimen → click into the CSS panel → press End → type a single space → wait 1.4 s → read the interval literal and the tile background. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/ (pass-3 dataloss run, transcript pasted in report §6 F-1).
defects.proposedCure: The code well is a representation of the model, not a second model. Serialize every field the model holds — `linear-gradient(<angle> in <space> <hue> hue, …)` — and parse the same production, so the panel round-trips itself and Copy writes the bytes under the caret. If a compact authored form survives it becomes a named, visible representation toggle, and replacing the model becomes an explicit `Replace` command that states it discards per-interval easing.

defects.defect: The panel headed `CSS` omits three of the six model fields (intervals, interpolationSpace, hueMethod)
defects.evidence: Change Space OKLCh→HSL: editorIdentical: true (byte-identical text), tileIdentical: false (`oklch(…)` stops → `rgb(…)` stops). `GradientModelState` (useGradientModel.ts:50-60) has six fields; `serializeGradient` (useGradientCSS.ts:147-162) emits three; `serializeCoalescedGradient` (:281-305) bakes space/hue into 33 literal stops; `grep -n "interpolationSpace|hueMethod|shorter" gradientParse.ts` → only a comment.
defects.mechanism: Neither serializer can express the CSS `in <space> <hue> hue` production and the parser has no notion of it, so the instrument whose largest heading is `Interpolation` cannot read, write or round-trip the syntax that expresses interpolation.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → open the `Interpolation space` select → choose HSL → diff the CSS panel text and the tile's computed background-image. Transcript in report §6 F-2.
defects.proposedCure: Emit and parse the native interpolation clause; one string carrying all six fields becomes the single on-screen serialization and the clipboard payload.

defects.defect: The Direction axis's operable element is a 0×20 px, opacity:0 box carrying a second, unbranded focus indicator
defects.evidence: Measured: thumb role=slider w 0 h 20, width "0px", opacity "0", outline "rgb(0, 95, 204) auto 1px"; track 354×20 carrying the branded ring "color(srgb 0.665504 0.000101413 0.261748 / 0.3) 0px 0px 0px 2px"; document.elementFromPoint(thumb centre) → SPAN.slider-track, thumbIsTopmostAtItsOwnCentre: false; aria-valuetext null; root data-variant "standard". glass-ui CSS: `.slider-thumb{width:0;opacity:0}` with both the visible thumb and `:focus-visible{outline:none}` gated on `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum]`; SliderVariant = "standard" | "spectrum".
defects.mechanism: GradientVisualizer.vue:232 renders the bare `<Slider>` with no `variant`, so it inherits the producer's invisible zero-width thumb and the un-suppressed UA outline. WCAG 2.5.8 (24×24) and 2.4.7/2.4.11 both fail; §5's axis composition owes label, unit, reserved value, numeric entry and focus/target behaviour — this callsite satisfies one of five.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → focus `main [role=slider]` → read getBoundingClientRect, computed width/opacity/outline on the thumb and box-shadow on `.slider-track`, plus elementFromPoint at the thumb centre. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-reset-focus.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the §5 domain-neutral axis composition instead of the bare primitive: the variant that carries the focus register, the unit in aria-valuetext, the reserved live-value slot and the numeric entry. Producer relay to glass-ui BH: `outline:none` on `:focus-visible` belongs to `.slider-thumb`, not to the `spectrum` gate.

defects.defect: Control labels fail WCAG AA contrast in BOTH schemes on the actual composited material
defects.evidence: Rendered-pixel measurement (PNG decode of screenshot clips): `.section-label` 14.384px/400 → ink rgb(101,84,66) on ground rgb(244,182,213) = 4.31:1 (light); ink rgb(195,185,172) on rgb(122,76,98) = 3.57:1 (dark). AA 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1. Section h3 20.352px/600 → 4.03 light / 3.53 dark (passes AA-large 3:1 only because it violates the type matrix).
defects.mechanism: Two jurisdictions: `.section-label` is a shared recipe (demo/styles/utils.css:13, 9 files under demo/ reference it) so the cure is at the recipe root; but the h3 colour is authored right here — GradientVisualizer.vue:149,241,253 each write `text-muted-foreground`, painting the largest non-title type in the pane in the de-emphasis role.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient at 1440×900 in both colorScheme light and dark → screenshot-clip each label/heading rect → decode PNG → ground = modal pixel, ink = pixel furthest in relative luminance → WCAG ratio. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-composition.mjs §F, challenge-D-pass3-states.mjs §6.
defects.proposedCure: Root-level: fix `.section-label`'s ink at the typography recipe (never a per-instance override). Locally: drop `text-muted-foreground` from the three headings and take `text-heading` + Plus Jakarta at full-strength ink — de-emphasis comes from size and interval, not from muting a heading below its legal contrast.

defects.defect: Reduced motion is inverted product-wide — the component gains 202 transitioning elements when the user asks for less motion
defects.evidence: Measured on the visualizer subtree (250 elements): no-preference → 48 with non-zero transition-duration (0.12/0.2/0.44 s tokens); reduce → 250, durations seen ONLY 0.1s and 0.15s; tile transition-property becomes "opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow" at 0.1s. CDP CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode names the winner: `:not([data-allow-motion]) { transition-duration:.1s !important; transition-property: opacity,color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow !important }` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css:1.
defects.mechanism: The producer's reduce block is semantically inverted: elements that opted IN to motion (`[data-allow-motion]`) are frozen at 0.01ms, while every element that never asked for motion is GIVEN a 100 ms five-property transition. `:not(…)` (0,1,0) beats the app's own `* {transition-duration:.01ms !important}` guard (0,0,0) at demo/styles/animations.css:184-191. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 requires reduced motion to resolve directly to final geometry.
defects.reproduction: Launch chromium context with reducedMotion:'reduce', load /#/gradient, count elements in the visualizer subtree whose computed transitionDuration !== '0s' and read the tile's matched rules over CDP. Transcript in report §3.
defects.proposedCure: Producer fix at glass-ui (relay to the BH inbox): the reduce block must zero motion for everything and exempt only opted-in surfaces, not the reverse. Then delete the now-dead app guard rather than layering a third rule. No consumer-side patch (edict 5).

defects.defect: Dock Reset restores every field it names and silently keeps the one it forgot — the easing
defects.evidence: Live before/after with a dirty model: before {easing "cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)", dir 360, stops [5%,100%]} → after Reset {easing "cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)", dir 90, stops [0%,100%]}. GradientVisualizer.vue:118-125 `resetGradient()` touches stops/type/direction/interpolationSpace/hueMethod/parseVerdict and never `intervals`.
defects.mechanism: Direction and stop positions demonstrably reverted, proving the handler ran, so the surviving easing is an omission not a no-op. The post-Reset state is the worst combination: every visible surface shows a default gradient while the tile still paints an eased ramp.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → click `ease-in-out` → focus the Direction thumb, press End → focus a stop seat, press ArrowRight ×5 → click the Dock `Reset` seat → re-read the interval literal, aria-valuenow and stop labels. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-reset-focus.mjs (pass-2 filed this as an unreachable hypothesis; now CONFIRMED).
defects.proposedCure: Reset restores the whole model or it is not called Reset. Derive the default from one frozen model literal so a field cannot be forgotten by construction.

defects.defect: The route gives the instrument 36.4% and an empty companion the identical 36.4%, where the canon binds 61.8/38.2
defects.evidence: Measured at 1440×900: main x16 w1408; gradient pane x199 w512 (36.4% of main); Palettes companion x729 w512 (36.4%, rendering "No saved palettes yet."); 183 px dead gutter each side (26% of main unused); the empty companion is 50.0% of the 1024 px of pane area. OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §3 binds Gradient to P122 golden 61.8033989%/38.1966011% with a 'stop/easing/code inspector'; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2: empty secondary content 'never receives half the viewport'.
defects.mechanism: The companion is the shell's, but the reason no golden split can exist INSIDE the gradient pane is this file: it emits one `flex flex-col gap-5` column of ten siblings with no stage, inspector or action regions, so there is nothing for a chassis to proportion — and the canon's 38.2% inspector is precisely the stop/easing/code trio this component stacks vertically inside the stage.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient at 1440×900 → measure main and both `[class*=pane-scroll-fade]` rects → compute shares. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-composition.mjs §A.
defects.proposedCure: Emit the three named regions from the visualizer and let InstrumentChassis own the golden ratio; remove the Palettes companion from /#/gradient exactly as OPTICAL-BENCH §4 already removed it from the five Admin routes.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/*` is a pure alias layer over glass-ui, and it is load-bearing enough to have manufactured five false audit findings
defects.evidence: All 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts are one-line re-exports: `export { Select, SelectTrigger, … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`, `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`, `export { Separator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`. GradientVisualizer.vue reaches the same package by two paths in one file: `../../../ui/select` and `../../../ui/slider` (:9,:10) alongside `@mkbabb/glass-ui` and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` (:12,:13). demo/ui/alert/index.ts documents the layer's shadcn history in a comment.
defects.mechanism: Owner edict 2 forbids aliases and dual paths. Measurable harm on the record: pass 2 of this same audit read `from "../../../ui/select"` as a local shadcn re-implementation and filed a five-fold design-system breach (E-4) plus three derived cures (E-2/E-3/D-8) against a component already consuming the design system.
defects.reproduction: `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do echo "--- $f"; cat "$f"; done` — pasted in report §4.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the barrels; import the producer directly at every callsite. Repo-wide subtraction owned by demo/ui, not a gradient row.

defects.defect: The parse verdict names the wrong grammar production
defects.evidence: input `linear-gradient(in oklch shorter hue, red, blue)` (valid CSS Images 4) → verdict `unparseable color "in"`.
defects.mechanism: `in` is the interpolation keyword, not a colour. The error tells the user their colour is broken when what the parser lacks is a production, sending them to edit the wrong token.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → click the CSS panel → type `linear-gradient(in oklch shorter hue, red, blue)` → read `[data-testid=gradient-parse-verdict]`.
defects.proposedCure: Teach the parser the interpolation clause (closes F-2 with it); until then the verdict names the production it could not match, not a fabricated colour token.

defects.defect: The rejected state is loud but programmatically unassociated, and the specimen contradicts it
defects.evidence: verdict "unparseable color \"nonsense\"" role=status color rgb(219,36,36) 16.4px; editor aria-invalid "true", borderColor rgb(219,36,36), **aria-describedby: null**; tile still painting "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.746875 …".
defects.mechanism: A screen-reader user gets 'invalid' with no reason, and the screen simultaneously asserts 'this CSS cannot be parsed' and 'here is your gradient' with nothing marking which is true.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → click the CSS panel → type `linear-gradient(90deg, nonsense, )` → wait 1.2 s → read the verdict, the editor's aria-invalid/aria-describedby and the tile's computed background-image.
defects.proposedCure: Associate the verdict via aria-describedby, and give the rejected state a specimen treatment (stale-marked or held) so the two surfaces cannot assert opposite truths silently.

defects.defect: The minimum-stop refusal is silent — Delete does nothing, says nothing, shows nothing
defects.evidence: Measured: 2 stops + focused seat + Delete → 2 stops (no change, no message); click rail → 3 stops; 3 stops + Delete → 2 stops (works). GradientStopEditor.vue:158-161 `removeStop` guards on `removable`.
defects.mechanism: Correct policy with no expression: the seat is not disabled, the remove chip does not change, nothing is announced. Same family as D-17's three silent no-op paths in `seedFromPalette`.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → focus `button[aria-label^="Gradient stop"]` → press Delete → count seats; click the rail centre; repeat. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-reset-focus.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: A command that cannot act is disabled with a stated reason; the two-stop floor is a visible property of the rail, not an invisible early return.

defects.defect: One 20 px interval does the work of both title gap and section gap, so every heading floats equidistant between its rule and its content
defects.evidence: rowGap "20px"; the nine inter-child gaps of the body column measured 20/20/20/20/20/20/20/20/20 px; children at y 200.7(rail) 260.7(hr) 281.7(h3) 332.2(controls) 480.8(hr) 501.8(h3) 552.3(easing) 769.3(hr) 790.3(h3) 840.8(code).
defects.mechanism: PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.3 requires two intervals ('Header→headline uses title gap; headline→next semantic section uses section gap'). With one token, Gestalt proximity does no grouping and the three `<hr>` become structurally load-bearing — which is why they were added despite the canon setting the divider count to zero.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient at 1440 → read computed rowGap of the `flex flex-col gap-5` body and the top/bottom of each child. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-composition.mjs §C.
defects.proposedCure: Section gap > title gap on the existing φ ladder; once the heading is tied to its content all three `<hr>` delete without loss, closing F-12 and D-6 together.

defects.defect: The section named `Interpolation` contains two geometry controls and excludes the interpolation dimension with the most authoring surface
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:149 heads a region containing Type, Space, Hue, Direction. useGradientCSS.ts:148-155 puts Type and Direction in the function name and the leading angle (geometry); Space and Hue appear in no serialization at all (F-2); easing lives under a separate heading two sections down.
defects.mechanism: The taxonomy is wrong in both directions: the heading is wrong for the two controls it does emit and right for the two it never emits.
defects.reproduction: Read GradientVisualizer.vue:149-234 against useGradientCSS.ts:147-162 and gradientParse.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Group by what the parameters do: Geometry (type, angle/start-angle, plus the shape and extent controls `radial` actually needs) and Interpolation (space, hue, easing). Easing joins its own family instead of forming a third slab.

defects.defect: The composition degrades monotonically with content — the protagonist is scale-invariant while every support grows
defects.evidence: At 12 stops: body height 720.1 → 1321.8 px; easing section 686.6 px = 51.9% of the component; code well scrollHeight 477 vs clientHeight 190 (the CSS output no longer fits its own box); rail unchanged at 40 px = 3.0% (was 5.6% at two stops). Negative result in the same run: 0 overlapping seats at ~41 px pitch.
defects.mechanism: PR-09 'Gradient/Easing protagonist subordinated → ENLARGE' worsens with use rather than holding, because the rail has a fixed 40 px block while the easing inspector grows one row per interval.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → click the rail at ten evenly spaced positions → measure body height, easing section height, code-well scroll/client heights and seat rects. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-states.mjs §4.
defects.proposedCure: The rail must scale with the instrument (one 19–22rem protagonist per §7/PR-09) and the interval inspector must be a bounded, scrollable region rather than an unbounded stack.

defects.defect: Three integration channels in one 279-line component, one of them dead
defects.evidence: defineExpose({resetGradient, copyCSS, seedFromPalette}) at :131 (consumed via GradientPane.vue:11-14 → usePaneRouter); inject(LIBRARY_PORT_KEY) at :30 with no default and silent optionality; defineModel<string|null>("selectedStopId") at :51 with NO consumer — GradientPane.vue:25 mounts `<GradientVisualizer ref="visualizerRef" />` with no binding.
defects.mechanism: Three mechanisms for one job with three different failure modes; the public two-way contract has zero callers. Edicts 2 and 3.
defects.reproduction: grep the repo for `selected-stop-id` / `selectedStopId` outside the component and its child.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead defineModel; keep one integration channel (the exposed command surface) and give the palette port an explicit contract instead of an untyped silent inject.

defects.defect: The easing catalogue is clipped past the viewport's right edge in all four Safari matrices
defects.evidence: REPORT.json /#/gradient `bleeding` (predicate `getBoundingClientRect().right > documentElement.clientWidth + 1`, capture.mjs:107-111) lists 12 elements — strip-row, strip-family, family-eyebrow, family-tiles, 3× glass-chip.glass-capsule, tile-label, svg, path — in all four matrices INCLUDING desktop 1440, while overflowX is 0.
defects.mechanism: Content extends beyond the window and is clipped rather than scrolled to. It is GradientEasingEditor's strip, but it is this file's composition decision to nest a horizontal catalogue in a 462 px column (§7 Easing: catalogue strips must support the curve, not become a tiny nested widget).
defects.reproduction: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json')); …" filtered to route '/#/gradient' → read the `bleeding` array.
defects.proposedCure: Filed here, owned by the easing-editor seat: the catalogue belongs in a bounded region that fits the column measure, with its own reachable overflow, not a strip that runs off the window.

defects.defect: `seedFromPalette` ignores the palette contract's non-interchangeable owner states
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:112 `pm.savedPalettes.value[0]?.colors.map(c => c.css)` — the first row of an undifferentiated list. PALETTE-CONTRACT.md and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7: 'Device Drafts, unpublished Server Workspaces, Published lineages, and Trash are explicit, non-interchangeable owner states.'
defects.mechanism: A named Dock command whose subject is 'whatever is at index 0' — possibly a trashed palette — has no subject at all. Sharpens D-17 with the contract citation.
defects.reproduction: Read GradientVisualizer.vue:110-116 against docs/tranches/V/PALETTE-CONTRACT.md and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 'Palette library and Browse'.
defects.proposedCure: The command takes a chosen palette or it is not offered; absent a qualifying palette it is disabled with a stated reason, and success names which palette seeded.

defects.defect: The tile is the one surface with no transition and the most violent change
defects.evidence: Computed at rest: transition-property "all", transition-duration "0s". Switching linear → radial → conic replaces the entire painted field in one frame while surrounding controls ease at 0.12–0.44 s.
defects.mechanism: A gap in the motion register rather than an authored animation; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 'Colour/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve.'
defects.reproduction: Load /#/gradient → read getComputedStyle on [data-testid=gradient-render-tile] → change Type and observe the un-eased swap.
defects.proposedCure: Tokenize one short effect curve for the specimen swap. Nothing may be deleted here (edict 6) — the cure is to add the missing tokenized transition, and it dies anyway if the tile collapses into the rail (D-14's transposition).

defects.defect: Prior pass's five-fold design-system breach is WITHDRAWN — false premise
defects.evidence: Pass 2 §4 asserted GradientVisualizer imports Select and Slider from a local shadcn re-implementation in demo/ui/. In fact `cat demo/ui/select/index.ts` → `export { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectItem, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` and `cat demo/ui/slider/index.ts` → `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`. The producer's `#description` slot is declared in glass-ui/dist/components/select/SelectItem.vue.d.ts and renders three descriptions live.
defects.mechanism: An import-path inference substituted for reading the module. The genuine breaches that survive are the raw `<hr>` (while demo/ui/separator exists), the hand-rolled label/field couple (while Label exists), the missing numeric entry, and DockControl planted in a pane body.
defects.reproduction: for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do echo "--- $f"; cat "$f"; done
defects.proposedCure: Ledger action: withdraw E-4 and the cures derived from it (E-2/E-3/D-8 'adopt ./select, ./slider'); replace with F-8 (delete the alias layer) and F-3 (adopt the composition, not the bare primitive). Methodological note for the next seat: differential probing — change one thing in the live app and diff two surfaces — produced three of this pass's strongest rows; path-reading produced a false one.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (component: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m], the 1M-context tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: All three `back` family tiles destroy the entire Gradient workbench on a single click. The strip paints, labels, and renders bespoke overshoot headroom for curves whose codomain leaves [0,1]; a demo seam demotes the library's Result into an uncaught throw inside a render-path computed, so the error boundary eats the pane.
defects.mechanism: Domain contract violated across a module boundary, with a Result->throw demotion at the seam; the throw is raised inside a computed on the render path.
defects.reproduction: Start dev server on :9000. Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait for the Easing card, click [data-specimen='ease-in-back'] (or ease-out-back / ease-in-out-back). The whole pane is replaced by the error boundary. Control: [data-specimen='ease-out-circ'] presses clean. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingspecimenstrip/probe-C3-back-family-crash.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Total the progress domain ONCE at the ramp seam rather than patching call sites: clamp eased t to [0,1] where it becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return, or a rampProgress(fn,t) beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit totality; then DELETE both throw sites, which become unreachable. A CSS gradient interval physically cannot produce a color outside its endpoints, so an overshooting timing function MEANS hold-at-endpoint. Deleting the back family instead is strictly worse: the producer picker still offers those curves and it contradicts the strip's own overshoot design.

defects.defect: The catalogue silently drops 6 of value.js's 30 named presets. FAMILY_ORDER is used as a filter, not an order, so the quart and quint families are built and then discarded; tileIdFor() returns null for all six, so authoring one through the producer's own preset menu leaves the gallery blank of selection and labels a first-class library preset `custom`. The module docstring promises 'never a second mint'; FAMILY_ORDER is the second mint.
defects.evidence:
easingCatalogue.ts:174 (FAMILY_ORDER literal) and :191 (`FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`).
Module probe: bezierPresets count: 30 / SPECIMEN_TILES count: 27 / DROPPED (6): ease-in-quart, ease-out-quart, ease-in-out-quart, ease-in-quint, ease-out-quint, ease-in-out-quint; each `tileIdFor => null`.
Producer menu enumerates Object.keys(bezierPresets) (dist/easing.js: `Object.keys(P)`) — measured OPTIONS(30).
Live: AFTER ease-in-quart: {"pressed":[],"readout":"cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)","headName":"custom"} — witness evidence/C1-quart-no-tile-pressed.png
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained mirror of data the library already orders, used as a gate instead of a hint.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click the tune button (aria-label='Author a custom curve') -> open the 'Easing preset' combobox -> select 'ease-in-quart'. The strip shows no pressed tile and the row head reads 'custom'. Scripts: probe-C3-catalogue-drop.ts (vite-node), probe-C3-quart-live-repro.mjs
defects.proposedCure: FAMILY_ORDER must be a hint, never a gate: `const order = [...new Set([...FAMILY_HINT, ...byFamily.keys()])]` so an unlisted family appends instead of vanishing. src/easing.ts:34-63 already authors PRESETS in family order, so `byFamily.keys()` alone suffices — the cheapest correct cure is deleting FAMILY_ORDER. Enforce with the exact-equality catalogue test in C-12, not with prose.

defects.defect: The lit `steps` tile misreports its identity and is inert. tileIdFor falls back to the generic `steps` tile for ANY steps interval, but that tile's literal is fixed at steps(4, jump-end); meanwhile onTileToggle drops `on === false`, which is exactly what reka's Toggle emits for an already-pressed tile. So the tile renders pressed while the readout three pixels below it disagrees, and the one control that names steps(4, jump-end) refuses to emit it.
defects.mechanism: A many-to-one (surjective) identity function feeding a one-way toggle that assumes injectivity.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click [data-specimen='steps'] -> open the authoring stage -> focus the 'Step count' slider and press ArrowRight 3x (n=7) -> click [data-specimen='steps'] again. Readout stays steps(7, jump-end); the tile stays lit; nothing emits.
defects.proposedCure: Make selection idempotent instead of one-way: `function onTileToggle(tile) { emit("select", tile) }` with the Chip's model-value still controlled. Pressing a lit tile then re-asserts its literal, which makes the family tile a reset-to-family-default — the radio semantics this control already wants (C-08) — and costs one boolean.

defects.defect: glass-ui@7.0.0 ships dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css but NO file imports it, so every .glass-chip rule is orphaned. This component's 27 Chip tiles therefore render with no cell radius, no pressed wash, no pressed edge, no press flood, and no coarse-pointer touch floor. It is also the causal root of the 'too rounded' half of owner mark MT-F030/OM-4: the orphaned sheet contains `.glass-chip--cell { border-radius: var(--radius-card) }`, so the full circles are manufactured by the missing @import, not by our authorship.
defects.evidence:
$ grep -rn "glass-chip.css" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/  -> (no output)

defects.defect: glass-ui 7.0.0 RETIRED the polymorphic `tag` API by name and documents `as` as its successor — so r1 L-1 is a consumer stranded on a deliberately retired API, not merely an unknown prop. Worse, the demo has the two props exactly backwards across primitives: `variant` is real on WatercolorDot ("solid"|"ghost") and absent on Button (which uses emphasis×tone), yet the demo passes `variant` to Button (51/55 sites, r2 L2-1) and `tag` to WatercolorDot (26 `tag=` sites fleet-wide).
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/primitive.d.ts:11 `as?: AsTag | Component;` and :19 `/** Forward ordinary host attributes without reviving a retired polymorphic API. */ export declare function fixedHostAttrs(...)`. Button.vue.d.ts:4-19 — props are emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class, NO `variant`. WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:23-30 — props are color|variant|animate|cycleDuration|range|seed, NO `tag`. Installed version confirmed 7.0.0. defects.mechanism: A major-version prop-surface migration that landed the version but not the consumer surface, absorbed silently by Vue's fallthrough-attribute rule. The taxonomy is stale in BOTH directions at once (a prop dropped on one primitive, a prop that never existed on another, and the same prop correct on a third — SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts:6), so spot-fixing by reading call sites cannot be reliable.
defects.reproduction: head -20 node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts (no `variant`); sed -n '23,30p' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (no `tag`); head -20 node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/primitive.d.ts (the retirement comment). Round 2's live-DOM probe already showed the CTA rendering data-emphasis="secondary" with `variant="primary-audacious"` landing as a raw fallthrough attribute.
defects.proposedCure: Mechanise round 2's cure move 1: generate an eslint allowlist from glass-ui's shipped .vue.d.ts prop interfaces — every `<C p=...>` where p ∉ Props(C) is an error. Then migrate at the root (edict 2, no shims): `tag="button"` → `as="button"` (the producer's own documented successor), `variant="outline"` → `emphasis="secondary"`, `ghost` → `emphasis="quiet"`, `destructive` → `tone="danger"`. `primary-audacious` has no 7.0.0 home — relay to the glass-ui BH inbox. Close the mechanism with `inheritAttrs:false` on glass-ui primitives.

defects.defect: `.section-label` is shipped by glass-ui as a bare CSS class with no component atom, so sixteen demo call sites each invent their own host element — FOUR spellings across 7 files (`<label>` ×3, `<span>` ×7, `<div>` ×6). This component is the only site that chose `<label>`, and its three labels carry no `for` and wrap no control, forcing the accessible name to be re-typed as `aria-label` on each trigger — where it HAS ALREADY DRIFTED.

MixConfigBar.vue:98,121,145 `<label class="section-label">` with `grep -n 'for=' MixConfigBar.vue` → no matches. THE DRIFT: MixConfigBar.vue:145 `<label class="section-label">Size mismatch</label>` vs :147 `<SelectTrigger aria-label="Size mismatch strategy">`. Census: GradientVisualizer.vue:163,180,197,229 `<span>`; MixSourceSelector.vue:183 `<span>`; GenerateControls.vue:221,255 `<span>`; SearchFilterBar.vue:20,32,48,63 `<div>`; TagEditPopover.vue:8 `<div>`; AdminTagsPanel.vue:87 `<div>`.

With no component owning the element choice and the for/id wiring, every consumer invents both, and the accessible name must be duplicated as a string — duplication that drifts. Round 2 (L2-6) found two spellings and marked the class ownership 'sound'; the class IS owned, the ATOM is not, and that is the structural defect.

defects.proposedCure: glass-ui owns it (edict 4) — relay to the BH/BI inbox. Ship `FieldLabel` (or `Label variant="section"`) owning the element, the for/id wiring and the class: `<FieldLabel for="mix-leftover">Size mismatch</FieldLabel>` + `<Select id="mix-leftover">` so the accessible name is DERIVED and never re-typed. glass-ui's PrimitiveProps already ships `as` for the rare `<div>` caption, so one atom covers all three current spellings without a shim. Sixteen sites converge; the drift becomes structurally impossible. Note demo/ui/label already re-exports glass-ui's Label and has ZERO consumers (see L3-8).
