(b) o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168 parses with `/oklch\(([\d.]+)[ ,]+([\d.]+)[ ,]+([\d.]+)(?:\s*\/\s*[\d.%]+)?\)/g` but sample.ts:39-41 `serializeStop` emits `%` on L and `deg` on H. Measured by temporary vitest probe: `first stop: oklch(62% 0.27 9.8deg)` · `stamp head: oklch(62% 0.27 9.8deg)|oklch(60.876698725014% 0.263143499961 5.648311780535deg)|…` · `REGEX MATCHES ON STAMP: 0 of 17 stops` · `REGEX MATCHES ON CANONICALIZED PAINT: 2`. So `expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)` at spec line 377 evaluates `expect(17).toBe(0)` per chip. (c) `grep -rn "MixConfigBar"` over *.ts/*.vue yields exactly two live code hits, both in MixPane.vue (:6, :97); everything else is prose in docs/. test/preview-chips.test.ts exercises sample.ts in isolation — never the space×hue cross-product at :57-74, never the v-if guards, never the emit casts. The single passing T-17 leg (:334 "honest absence: with <2 operands the rows carry NO chip") asserts `count === 0`, which under C-2 is unfalsifiable.
defects.mechanism: Vacuous gating on three compounding levels: the oracle's precondition is unreachable (C-2), its core assertion is unsatisfiable against the serialization it claims to parse (a regex written against a different format than the one shipped), and the only test that passes does so because the feature is dead. The unit suite tests the sampler function, never the component that composes it.
defects.reproduction: Vacuous-gate mutations that keep every gate its current colour: M1 — change MixConfigBar.vue:71 to `sampleInterpolationRamp(operandColors, colorSpace, "shorter")` (ignore m.value); M2 — delete both `<PreviewRamp/>` elements (:111, :133); M3 — delete `variant="primary-audacious"` (:163); M4 — `INTERPOLATION_SPACES.slice(0,1)` at :107; M5 — swap the @update:model-value handlers at :99 and :122. For (b): write test/zz-ser.test.ts importing `sampleInterpolationRamp` + `stampStops`, apply the spec's exact regex to `stampStops(stops)` → 0 matches of 17 stops; apply it to a canonicalized paint string `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), …)` → matches. Run `npx vitest run test/zz-ser.test.ts`.
defects.proposedCure: (1) Fix the add-slot host (C-2) so the flow is drivable at all. (2) Delete `parseOklchTriples` from the spec entirely and compare `data-stops.split("|")` to the painted stops through ONE normalizer owned by sample.ts — the module already owns `stampStops`, so the single shared referent exists and the spec should never re-implement parsing. (3) Add one @vue/test-utils mount asserting the only thing this file uniquely owns: Space row i carries the ramp for space i at the current arc, and Hue row j the ramp for arc j at the current space. (4) Architecturally, add a producer-API conformance oracle — assert every demo <Button> resolves an intended data-emphasis and that no demo component passes an attribute name absent from the corresponding *.vue.d.ts prop union; that single gate catches C-1 and C-2 together, which no amount of extra unit tests would.

defects.defect: Three `<label>` elements that label nothing: no `for`, no labelable descendant, `HTMLLabelElement.control === null`. Clicking the visible caption neither focuses nor opens the Select. The accessible name survives only because `aria-label` is hand-duplicated on each trigger — one string authored twice — and the duplication has already drifted.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:98, :121, :145. Measured live: `"labels": [{"text":"Color space","htmlFor":null,"control":null,"inMixPane":true},{"text":"Hue method","htmlFor":null,"control":null,"inMixPane":true}]`; in palettes mode the third appears with the same defect (`['Color space','Hue method','Size mismatch']`). Drift already present: visible "Size mismatch" (:145) vs accessible `aria-label="Size mismatch strategy"` (:147) — WCAG 2.5.3 holds only because the visible text happens to be a prefix. Lone divergence, not a house pattern: every other `.section-label` in demo/ uses a non-semantic host (GradientVisualizer.vue:163,180,197,229 <span>; MixSourceSelector.vue:183 <span>; GenerateControls.vue:221,255 <span>; SearchFilterBar.vue:20,32,48,63 <div>; TagEditPopover.vue:8 <div>; AdminTagsPanel.vue:87 <div>) — MixConfigBar.vue:98,121,145 is the only <label> site. glass-ui 7.0.0 ships the primitive and demo/ui/label/index.ts already re-exports it with `LabelProps { for?: string }`.
defects.mechanism: A semantic element used as a styling hook. `<label>` was chosen for the `.section-label` recipe without wiring the association the element exists to express, so the a11y name had to be re-authored as an aria-label on the control — two sources for one truth, which is how name/label drift begins.
defects.reproduction: node+playwright to http://localhost:9000/#/mix, wait 3s, then `[...document.querySelectorAll('label.section-label')].map(l => ({text: l.textContent.trim(), htmlFor: l.htmlFor || null, control: l.control ? l.control.tagName : null}))` → both entries report htmlFor null and control null. Click the visible "Color space" text → document.activeElement stays BODY and no [role=listbox] opens.
defects.proposedCure: One name, one source: `<Label for="mix-space">Color space</Label>` using the glass-ui primitive demo/ui/label already re-exports, plus `id="mix-space"` on the SelectTrigger (accepted as fallthrough), and delete all three duplicated `aria-label`s. This also removes the existing "Size mismatch" / "Size mismatch strategy" divergence by construction rather than by vigilance.

defects.defect: Per-instance sizing overrides where the design system ships a root-level register: `class="h-9"` on all three SelectTriggers and `class="h-10 …"` on the Button, severing these four controls from the token every other control in the app follows. A future retune of `--control-h-sm` moves everything except them.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:100, :123, :147 (`<SelectTrigger … class="h-9">`) and :165 (`class="h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display"`). glass-ui 7.0.0 `dist/components/select/SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts` declares `/** Trigger height register. */ size?: "sm" | "default";` and `dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts` declares `ButtonSize = Extract<Size, "xs"|"sm"|"md"|"lg">`. Measured live trigger height: 36px = h-9 = exactly `--control-h-sm`. This exact cure was adjudicated two tranches ago and is still unlanded: docs/tranches/S/audit/lanes/dropdown-select-consistency.md:167 — "CONSUME FIX — swap `class=\"h-9\"` → `size=\"sm\"` (11 sites)".
defects.mechanism: Same family as C-1: the producer's vocabulary exists and the consumer hand-paints over it. Owner edict 5 (style at the glass/shadcn root component level, never per-instance overrides).
defects.reproduction: node+playwright to http://localhost:9000/#/mix; `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role="combobox"]')].map(t => ({name: t.getAttribute('aria-label'), h: Math.round(t.getBoundingClientRect().height)}))` → Color space and Hue method both 227x36. Compare against `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/select/SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts` which declares the `size` register.
defects.proposedCure: `<SelectTrigger size="sm">` ×3 with `h-9` deleted; express the Button's register through `size`/`emphasis`/`tone` rather than `h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display` — which also closes C-1. This is the already-ruled S-tranche consume fix; land it rather than re-deriving it a third time.

defects.defect: The component reaches past the design system into reka-ui for a type strictly wider than glass-ui's actual emit contract, then launders it with three unchecked `as` casts. It advertises values the producer can never send and narrows from a union containing null with no check.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:15 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";` consumed at :99, :122, :146 as `(v: AcceptableValue) => emit('update:colorSpace', v as PickerSpace)`. glass-ui 7.0.0's real contract: `dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts` → `SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue]; "update:open": [value: boolean] }` and `dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts` → `export type SelectionValue = string | number;`. reka's AcceptableValue additionally admits `Record<string, any> | null`. SHARPENING: the producer type is NOT re-exported — `dist/components/select/index.d.ts` exports the eight component prop/emit types and not `SelectionValue` — which is precisely the §4 producer ask behind register entry L-D7 (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/excavation/CONTRIVANCE-REGISTER.md:101, 4 sites: GradientVisualizer.vue:28, MixConfigBar.vue:15, GenerateControls.vue:33, AuroraPane.vue:25).
defects.mechanism: Consumer names the headless library the design system wraps (owner edict 4 violation), and does so with a wider type than reality, so the `as` cast masks cases that cannot occur — a no-op cast standing in for the honest 9-member string-literal narrowing (owner edict 2, masking fallback).
defects.reproduction: Static: `grep -n 'AcceptableValue' demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue` → :15, :99, :122, :146. `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts` → emits SelectionValue. `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts` → `string | number`. `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/select/index.d.ts` → SelectionValue absent from the barrel.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: annotate `(v: string | number)` and narrow honestly with a membership check against INTERPOLATION_SPACES / HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS — both already imported at :18 and both already the source of the rendered rows, so the check costs nothing and also closes C-16's type hole. Producer-side (the real cure, one line): re-export `SelectionValue` from glass-ui's select barrel so no demo surface ever needs to name reka-ui; relay per the standing glass-ui BH/BI edict.

defects.defect: The `#description` lane now carries the only surviving copy of the interpolation-space vocabulary (W5-7 deleted the permanent visible subtitles on the premise that the dropdown rows tell the story), and that lane is orphaned in the accessibility tree: the description text is not part of the option's accessible name and is not bound by aria-describedby to anything.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:95-96 records the deletion: "W5-7: the permanent subtitles died — the dropdown's own #description rows already tell the story once, on demand." Measured live on the first Color-space option: `{"textContent":"OKLCh Perceptual, hue-preserving","ariaLabel":null,"aria-describedby":null}` while the computed accessible name is exactly "OKLCh" (`getByRole('option',{name:'OKLCh',exact:true})` resolves to 1). The description spans are NOT aria-hidden (measured `aria-hidden: null` on both the wrapper `.flex.items-center.gap-2` and the `.text-micro.text-muted-foreground` span), so they are loose text inside the option node — neither name nor description. The slot is the producer's: glass-ui 7.0.0 `dist/components/select/SelectItem.vue.d.ts` declares `description?: (props: {}) => any`.
defects.mechanism: A producer slot named `description` that generates no id and no aria-describedby on its option, made load-bearing by a consumer-side deletion of the redundant visible copy. Most screen readers will read the option's contents anyway, so this is a degradation of the designed relationship rather than a total loss — hence INFO.
defects.reproduction: node+playwright to http://localhost:9000/#/mix, wait 3s, click the "Color space" combobox, wait 600ms, then read the first `[role="option"]`: `{textContent, ariaLabel: o.getAttribute('aria-label'), describedby: o.getAttribute('aria-describedby')}` → describedby null; and `[...o.querySelectorAll('span')].map(s=>({cls:s.className, ariaHidden:s.getAttribute('aria-hidden'), text:s.textContent.trim()}))` → the two description spans report aria-hidden null. Separately `page.getByRole('option',{name:'OKLCh',exact:true}).count()` → 1, proving the description is outside the accessible name.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side, relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing E13/BH-BI edict: a slot named `description` should mint an id on its rendered node and set `aria-describedby` on the owning option, so the lane is programmatically the description it is named for. No demo-side change; adding a demo-side aria-describedby would be a per-instance workaround against edict 5 and would duplicate the string a third time.

result.axis: design (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue, run 3
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier this seat was spawned with. Explicit declaration, not inherited.

defects.defect: The result is delivered off-screen. On iPhone 14, 0.00 px of the 215.81 px result plate is inside the scroll viewport at the moment the convergence completes. On desktop the bottom 28.5 px is clipped, which by the plate's own box model is the action row — Copy/Save/Reset are sliced in half. Nothing scrolls, focuses, or announces on settle.
defects.evidence: probe-results-webkit.json → settledAsDelivered.scroller: mobile-light/mobile-dark {plateVisiblePx: 0.00, plateFullyVisible: false, plate.h 215.81}; desktop-light/dark {plateVisiblePx: 190.22 of 218.69}. Arithmetic: plate top 686.78 + h 218.69 = bottom 905.47 vs scroller bottom 877 → 28.47 px clipped; action row spans 862.78→890.78, fold at 877 → 14.2 px of a 28 px control row below the fold. Frames: shots/mobile-light-settled-as-delivered.png (no plate) vs shots/mobile-light-settled.png (after manual scrollIntoView); shots/desktop-light-settled-as-delivered.png (three half-glyphs at the pane edge). Scroller is scrollable: scrollHeight 817 vs clientHeight 772.
defects.mechanism: Missing reveal contract. MixPane.vue:62 houses the pane in an inner `overflow-y-auto` Card; the plate is appended as the last child of that column. useMixingState.ts:104-106 `settleMix()` flips a phase and returns — no reveal, no focus move, no announcement. Both prior runs injected state via `__vueParentComponent.setupState` and took element captures, which structurally cannot observe the fold.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/probe.mjs — seeds two 12-colour palettes into localStorage `color-palettes`, clicks the Palettes tab, selects two palettes, clicks Mix, screenshots at settle BEFORE any scroll assist. Read settledAsDelivered.scroller.plateVisiblePx.
defects.proposedCure: The mix is a deliberate command producing a new artifact, so VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 row 7 governs the seam (reveal → focus → one durable announcement), not §6's scene-swap row. The plate owns a completion contract on the transition's @after-enter: scrollIntoView({block:"nearest"}), then one polite status naming the artifact ("12-colour result · OKLab · shorter") — which is the same provenance line run 2's D-21 already requires, so it earns its row twice. Lengthening the pane or shrinking the plate only moves the fold and is not a cure.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to run 2, load-bearing: run 2 concluded the component is "unreachable in the shipped product and none of its design can be validated in-app" and moved to setupState injection on that basis. Only the COLORS branch is dead. The palettes branch is fully live and drivable end-to-end.
defects.evidence: Measured on /#/mix: `document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-label^="Add color"]').length === 0` and no add-slot button in a full enumeration of the route's 31 visible buttons (colors path dead — MixSourceSelector.vue:164-176 and :211-221 are `WatercolorDot tag="button"` against a v7 component with no `tag` prop). But: `button[aria-label^="Select palette"]` count = 3 (MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 is a native <button type="button" aria-pressed>); after two clicks the wide Mix button enables; plate@180ms = {cls: "mix-plate … mix-plate--ghost vj-morph-enter-active vj-morph-enter-to", op: "0.55"}; plate@6s = {cls: "mix-plate … bg-well", op: "1", text: "RESULT"}.
defects.mechanism: P051 removed WatercolorDot's interactive-host branch in the glass-ui 7 major; MixSourceSelector's colors-mode affordances depended on it, the palettes-mode seats did not. Run 2 generalised the colors-mode failure to the whole component and switched to injection — and injection is exactly what hides D-25/D-26/D-27, because an injected result never travels the flow that fails.
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage `color-palettes` with two palettes, load http://localhost:9000/#/mix, click the Palettes tab, click two `button[aria-label^="Select palette"]`, click the 462 px-wide Mix button. The full flow is in probe.mjs::selectTwoPalettes + run().
defects.proposedCure: Validate this component through the palettes path in-app, not by injection. Every future π/DELTA frame for MixResultDisplay must come from a driven flow inside the real scroll container; audit/visual/states.mjs should drive Mix to `done` and capture ghost + settled in both schemes and both form factors (run 1 D-16's gate repair, now unblocked).

defects.defect: The convergence anchor `[data-mix-target]` does not exist in the DOM. The component's own docblock claims it plants "the anchor the canvas convergence lands on"; the drops actually converge on a hard-coded geometric guess, visibly nowhere near the plate.
defects.evidence: Measured mid-mix during the ghost phase: `### GHOST target present: { target: false, targetTag: undefined, targetRect: null }`. Rendered node: `<span aria-hidden="true" class="shrink-0 w-10 h-10 watercolor-swatch" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" data-variant="ghost">` — no data-mix-target. shots/desktop-light-ghost.png shows the pigment drops strewn across the SOURCE cards at y≈490-660 while the dashed ghost well sits alone at y≈1093.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui 7.0.0 WatercolorDot is `inheritAttrs: !1` and forwards only attrs.class and attrs.style (dist/watercolor-dot.js: `let n = h(), c = i(() => n.class), f = i(() => n.style)`). data-mix-target (MixResultDisplay.vue:69), tag="div" (l.67) and :title (l.103) are all discarded. mixStage.ts:121-123 then silently substitutes `{x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28}` — a masking fallback, owner edict 2.
defects.reproduction: node docs/…/probe.mjs (any arm); or in DevTools during the mixing phase: document.querySelector('[data-mix-target]') === null. Visual: shots/desktop-light-ghost.png.
defects.proposedCure: The anchor is the PLATE's geometry, not the face's — which is what P051 already rules (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2, OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS §5.3: the dot owns only its noninteractive organic face; named/operable sites use an enclosing geometric seat). One plate-owned element carries data-mix-target and the well geometry with the face inside it, in BOTH the ghost and settled branches, so ghost and landed dot measure the same box. collectStage must then return null loudly rather than guessing. Note the ordering constraint: the seat must be measured AFTER D-25's reveal, or the convergence will aim correctly at an element still below the fold.

defects.defect: In forced colors the result plate has no boundary at all — background forced to Canvas, border 0, shadow none — so the container ceases to exist and the label, dots and action glyphs float directly on the pane.
defects.evidence: Chromium forcedColors:"active" (probe-results-chromium.json → settled.plate): {bg: "rgb(255, 255, 255)", border: "0px solid", boxShadow: "none", radius: "12px"} — identical to the pane behind it. shots/forced-colors-settled.png shows no plate boundary. Same capture also renders run 2's D-20: the 430×16 gradient strip is not painted at all, and nothing is lost — the proof it carries no information the swatch row does not.
defects.mechanism: MixResultDisplay.vue:55 gives the plate `bg-well` and nothing else. A background alone does not survive WHCM's system-colour substitution; a real border does. The sibling in-plate fixture .dashed-well (demo/styles/utils.css:90-107) carries 1.5px dashed var(--card-edge) + var(--shadow-cartoon-sm) and would survive; the palette source Cards above keep their edge.
defects.reproduction: ENGINE=chromium ONLY=forced-colors node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/probe.mjs; read settled.plate.bg/.border/.boxShadow and open shots/forced-colors-settled.png.
defects.proposedCure: One token-anchored in-plate-fixture recipe shared with .dashed-well — its solid sibling — carrying --radius-card, --card-edge and --shadow-cartoon-sm. Same move retires run 2's D-23 (rounded-xl 12px vs --radius-card 1rem) and the two-different-wells incoherence, at the root rather than per instance (owner edict 5).

defects.defect: PROMOTION (run 1 D-9 / run 2, source-read → reproduced): a failed copy is completely silent — the UI after a rejected clipboard write is byte-identical to idle.
defects.evidence: clipboard-denied arm with navigator.clipboard.writeText returning a rejected promise: copy = {title: "Copy color", innerHtml: "<svg … lucide-copy …>", ariaPressed: null, plateHasLive: false}. Success arm on the same harness: {title: "Copied!", innerHtml: "<svg … lucide-check …>"}. Same title, same glyph, no live region.
defects.mechanism: useClipboard's status union is "idle"|"pending"|"success"|"failure" (dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:3); MixResultDisplay.vue:32 maps exactly one: `const copied = computed(() => status.value === "success")`. `failure` and `pending` are discarded, as is the onCopyError hook. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: failed/pending states are never colour-only — here failure is not even colour, it is absence.
defects.reproduction: ONLY=clipboard-denied node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/probe.mjs; compare copy.title/innerHtml against the desktop-light arm.
defects.proposedCure: Consume all four arms on the producer primitive rather than in a local boolean. glass-ui Button already models this axis — `loading` ("marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles") and `tone` — so replacing the borrowed dock seats with Button iconOnly closes P-3 and P-5 in one move.

defects.defect: PROMOTION (run 1 D-5 / run 2, corroborated → comparative): dock furniture used outside the dock loses its geometry contract. The plate's three seats are 28×28 on a coarse pointer while the same page's real dock control is 46.8×46.8, and glass-ui 7's own out-of-dock touch-target guard is not firing. The DockSeparator computes to height 0px.
defects.evidence: iPhone 14 (pointer: coarse = true): plate Copy/Save/Reset = 28×28, --dock-control-size "(unset)", min-width "0px", min-height "auto"; the real dock's control on the same page = 46.8×46.8, --dock-control-size "max(calc(2.5rem * 1.17), 2.75rem)". Desktop: 28×28 vs 40×40. Producer contract (DockControl.vue.d.ts header): "the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp)". glass-ui ships `.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)) { min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem) }` and it is NOT applying despite --dock-touch-target resolving to 2.75rem on the element. Separator, both viewports: {w:1, h:0, cssH:"0px", margin:"0px 6px", sepH:"(unset)", role:"separator", data-orientation:"horizontal", aria-orientation:"vertical"}.
defects.mechanism: Both recipes read custom properties declared ON `.glass-dock`. Outside that ancestor `--dock-control-size` and `--dock-separator-height` are unset; `height: var(--dock-separator-height)` becomes invalid at computed-value time → `auto` → 0px on an empty block, leaving only the 12px margin (the unexplained gap in shots/desktop-dark-settled.png). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 / PR-12: glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities — here they collapsed into one 28px box.
defects.reproduction: node docs/…/probe.mjs; read settled.buttons[].{w,h,dockControlSize} on the mobile arms, and the separator block in the plate outerHTML dump. Frames: shots/mobile-light-settled.png, shots/desktop-dark-settled.png.
defects.proposedCure: The plate's actions are not dock controls. glass-ui Button is the primitive for the job — iconOnly ("square geometry for an accessibly named icon command"), size, tone, loading — and it owns its own hit cell with no --dock-* scope dependency. Delete DockSeparator outright: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5's Mix row fixes boundaries [], reserve none, retained dividing line none, grouping job "rack, result and action regions remain distinct through geometry", and closes with "Any additional line … is a defect".

defects.defect: PROMOTION (run 2 P-1, injected-empty → ordinary-reachable): the one-colour result arm renders a 430×16 flat grey slab as its "gradient preview", restating the single 40px specimen 12px above it.
defects.evidence: one-color-palette arm: dots = 1; strip inline style = `background: linear-gradient(to right, oklab(0.72 0 0))` — a single stop; plate h = 170.69. shots/one-color-palette-settled.png: an orange palette mixed with a blue one yields a grey dot above a flat grey bar. Area ratio: strip 6,880 px² vs specimen 1,600 px².
defects.mechanism: MixResultDisplay.vue:109-116 builds the strip from result.colors alone with no arity guard. Reachable without injection: MixPane.onSave (MixPane.vue:41-43) mints a one-colour "Mixed Color" palette from this very component, so two of them mix to a one-colour result on an ordinary second visit. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.5: a mark is data, status, labelled action, drag affordance, focus register, or REMOVED. With no provenance line the user also cannot distinguish the achromatic OKLab midpoint from a bug.
defects.reproduction: ONLY=one-color-palette node docs/…/probe.mjs (seeds two one-colour palettes, exactly the shape MixPane.onSave writes); read settled.gradientStrip.inlineStyle.
defects.proposedCure: REMOVE the strip. It is a second rendering of the same ordered list at every arity — invisible in forced colors with nothing lost (D-27), a flat slab at N=1, and duplicative at N=12. If an adjacency/blend reading is genuinely wanted it is a different instrument, and the pane already ships the honest one: MixConfigBar.vue:23,111,133 consumes sampleInterpolationRamp + <PreviewRamp>, which are space- and hue-method-aware (run 2's D-19).

defects.defect: CORROBORATION + WIDENING (run 1 D-6 / run 2): the "Result" identity label is a fourth, undeclared type species that fights its own base utility, and its uppercase tracking is 4× tighter than the house caps rung.
defects.evidence: Measured, all arms: RESULT = Fraunces / italic / 700 / 14.384px / letter-spacing 0.3596px (0.025em); .section-label 4px away = Fira Code / normal / 400 / 14.384px / 1.4384px (0.1em); MixSourceSelector's "Selected" = Fraunces / 600 / text-small. New this run: glass-ui's `text-caption` utility itself sets `font-style: italic` and `font-weight: 400` (dist/styles/typography/semantic.css), so the four-utility stack at MixResultDisplay.vue:58 overrides two of its own base's four declarations and leaves italic standing; and --type-tracking-caps is 0.1em, making the uppercase label's 0.025em four times too tight.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance override of a root recipe (owner edict 5) where the pane's established label primitive .section-label exists and is used twice by its own sibling. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 / PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.13 close the matrix: control-or-label → text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold; Fraunces owns display/identity/palette-identity only. This label is Fraunces, bold, italic, one rung below text-small (14.384px vs 16.4px at 1440).
defects.reproduction: node docs/…/probe.mjs; compare settled.labels.result against settled.labels.config in any arm.
defects.proposedCure: Consume .section-label and delete the four-utility stack. Same move gives the plate's identity line the same voice as the config labels it sits beneath, which is the only reason the current label reads as a fourth species.

defects.defect: CORROBORATION (run 2 D-18) in a second driven flow: the component's scoped `transition` shorthand defeats the vj-morph family on the same element, so the plate's arrival is a single-frame height snap with no transform and no height morph.
defects.evidence: Measured on the plate in all 9 arms, including while it carries `vj-morph-enter-active vj-morph-enter-to`: transitionProperty "opacity", transitionDuration "0.2s" — not the family's "opacity, transform, max-height". Heights: ghost 102.69 → settled 218.69 = +116.00 px (+113%) with no intermediate; single-colour arm 102.69 → 170.69 = +68.00.
defects.mechanism: MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154 `.mix-plate { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard); }` compiles to `.mix-plate[data-v-0f138735]` = specificity (0,2,0), beating `.vj-morph-enter-active` (0,1,0); the shorthand then resets transition-property to `opacity` alone. animations.css:59-62 states the family law verbatim: "The family owns the CURVE + TOKEN pairing; a consuming site may parameterise only GEOMETRY through the --vj-* custom properties." This site parameterises the curve and the property set. Recorded here only as independent confirmation — run 2 owns the finding and its cure.
defects.reproduction: node docs/…/probe.mjs; read settled.plate.transition and ghost.plate.transition (both "opacity 0.2s"), and ghost.plate.h vs settledAsDelivered.plate.h.
defects.proposedCure: Run 2's cure stands: delete <style scoped> whole; the ghost dimming belongs on the specimen, not the container, and the family already owns the plate's arrival. Run 3 adds no new cure here.

defects.defect: COVERAGE HONESTY: two states this seat could not decide. 200% zoom is NOT COVERED (the component could not be reached at that arm), and keyboard focus is UNPROVEN (WebKit alone cannot decide it).
defects.evidence: zoom200 arm: nPal = 0 — the palette rack did not render at 720×450@2×, so no plate and no frame exists. Focus: after 45 Tab presses in WebKit, focus.inPlate = false, landing on a 105×32 dock button; audit/visual/states.mjs:8-9 names this exact trap ("macOS ships Full Keyboard Access OFF, so run ENGINE=chromium before believing any focus gap").
defects.mechanism: Harness limitation, recorded rather than reported as a pass. Run 2 reports a 200% PASS from an injected plate — that measures the plate's own rem-scaling, not the driven flow, and this run neither confirms nor contradicts it.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a stated coverage gap, not a defect claim.
defects.proposedCure: Re-drive the zoom arm at a real 400% in-app browser zoom (PROPORTION-AUDIT §2's named arm, which is the canon's anyway, not a substituted narrow viewport), and re-run the focus row under ENGINE=chromium keying focus identity by DOM path. No focus claim — positive or negative — may be made until then.

result.strongestDefect: D-25 — The result is delivered off-screen. On iPhone 14, 0.00 px of the 215.81 px result plate is inside the scroll viewport at the instant the convergence completes; on desktop 28.5 px is clipped, slicing the Copy/Save/Reset row in half (14.2 px of a 28 px row below the fold). The user issues the pane's one verb, watches a 1.2 s narration, and the viewport does not change. It is a missing reveal contract, not an overflow bug — the scroller has 45 px of scroll available and nothing scrolls it. Neither prior run could see this because both injected state via `__vueParentComponent.setupState` and took element captures, which never travel the flow that fails; correcting run 2's "unreachable in-app" premise (C-3) is what made it observable. Compounding it, the narration that leads there aims at a hard-coded guess, because `[data-mix-target]` is silently dropped by glass-ui 7's `inheritAttrs:false` WatercolorDot (D-26).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof is claimed for the component as a whole. What survived a hostile third pass, measured through the driven flow rather than by inspection, is recorded in §8 of the report: (1) reduced motion is genuinely clean — at t=170 ms under reducedMotion:"reduce" the plate is already at its settled height 218.69, so the completion event fires immediately and the phase machine is never stranded mid-mix, exactly as useMixingAnimation.ts:70-76 documents; (2) nothing bleeds — docOverflowX === 0 on all 8 reachable arms including RTL and both mobile schemes, at plate widths 462 and 324; (3) the one-clock law holds — the component owns no timer, its only timing being useClipboard's producer-owned resetMs: 1500; (4) motion family naming is disciplined and `.swatch-row` (demo/styles/utils.css:167-179) is correctly consumed rather than re-minted, the utility naming this component as one of its three sanctioned consumers; (5) Vue 3.5 idiom and verbatimModuleSyntax are clean — reactive props destructure with default (l.20-23), computed over destructured props stays reactive, no defineModel round-trip and so no stale-read hazard, `import type { MixResult }` (l.7) correctly marked; (6) the AT hygiene that exists is correct — the gradient strip is double-hidden (aria-hidden + role="presentation") and aria-pressed is correctly ABSENT on three controls that are commands rather than toggles (ariaPressed: null measured ×3); (7) the seed-continuity idea is good design worth fixing rather than deleting — D-26's cure keeps it and makes it true for the first time.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue (pin 71aa0a65… VERIFIED by shasum; no source edits landed)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; matches the explicit spawn declaration, seat is declared not inherited
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the `disabled` prop is bound to 1 of 5 interactive controls (only Reset, line 84); Upload, Camera and both Sliders ignore it. Measured consequence: 3 clicks on the Camera control acquire 3 MediaStreams and stop ZERO (gum:3, stops:0, all tracks readyState "live", one <video>) — the device camera keeps capturing, unreferenced and unstoppable, until page unload.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field carries the hazards I DISPROVED so the next seat does not re-run them. (1) defineModel stale-read: ABSENT — the component uses explicit defineProps/defineEmits with :model-value="[k]" and the parent writes a plain ref synchronously (useExtractSession.ts:171); no async round-trip exists. (2) The `absolute inset-0` rail does NOT block slider hit-testing: rail box {x:252,y:495,w:434,h:24} is byte-identical to the .glass-slider root box, and the slider is later in DOM order with position:relative, so it wins hit-testing — zero dead zone. (3) WCAG 2.5.8 AA is NOT failed by the 12px thumbs: I ran the spacing-exception test (24px-diameter circle on each undersized target vs every other target's bounding box) on the mobile capture and got zero intersections ("viol": []); nearest neighbours are the 44x44 DockControls at >=68px. (4) k label does not clip at k=16: labelW 20, labelScrollW 20, clipped false. (5) Keyboard fully operable: focus lands, ArrowRight x11 drives aria-valuenow 5 -> 16, tabindex="0" on both thumbs. (6) No ungated rAF loop in this tree (the single `await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)` at ExtractWorkbench.vue:249 is a one-shot await). (7) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all six imports at :96-101 are genuine value imports. (8) No WebGL, no ValueUnit construction, no oklch->HSV round-trip in this tree. (9) The three buttons DO get accessible names via the HTML-AAM `title` last-resort — Playwright ARIA snapshot resolves "Upload image"/"Open camera"/"Reset" — so the audit's namelessButtons:3 is strict-probe accounting (capture.mjs:104), not an AT blackout.

defects.defect: The `disabled` prop is honoured on exactly one of five interactive controls (Reset, line 84). Upload (:40), Camera (:49), the k Slider (:24) and the kC Slider (:68) silently discard it, even though glass-ui 7.0.0 declares `disabled?: boolean` on both DockControl and Slider. The parent explicitly passes `:disabled="session.isProcessing.value || cameraActive"` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:70). The consequence is a live-camera resource/privacy leak.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:84 is the sole read of `disabled`. API exists and was unused: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts:9 `disabled?: boolean;`. Measured with a real MediaStream (canvas.captureStream, track.stop instrumented) against localhost:9000: [{"t":"before","camDisabled":false,"gum":0,"stops":0,"videos":0,"live":[]},{"t":"after-1st-click","camDisabled":false,"gum":1,"stops":0,"videos":1,"live":["live"]},{"t":"after-2nd-click","camDisabled":false,"gum":2,"stops":0,"videos":1,"live":["live","live"]},{"t":"after-3rd-click","camDisabled":false,"gum":3,"stops":0,"videos":1,"live":["live","live","live"]}] — uploadDisabled false and both sliders aria-disabled null at every step.
defects.mechanism: prop-contract non-propagation: a declared `disabled` contract bound at one leaf instead of at the boundary, combined with a single-slot mutable `let cameraStream: MediaStream | null` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:228) that startCamera (:239-255) overwrites unconditionally, so stopCamera (:257) and onBeforeUnmount (:281) can only ever stop the LAST stream.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — headless WebKit, http://localhost:9000/#/extract, navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia stubbed to a real canvas.captureStream(5) with track.stop() counted; click the button with title="Open camera" three times, 600ms apart. Yields gum:3 / stops:0 / three tracks readyState "live". Second, worse path measured in probe2 (non-MediaStream fake so `srcObject=` throws after getUserMedia resolves): gum:1, stops:0, videos:0 — a live camera track with the viewfinder CLOSED; any post-acquisition failure reproduces this on real hardware.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the contract at the boundary, not the leaves: forward `:disabled="disabled"` to Upload, Camera and both Sliders (Reset keeps its extra clause per C-3), or give the controls row fieldset-disabled semantics so the prop can never be partially honoured again. Independently make acquisition a state transition rather than an accumulation: startCamera() calls stopCamera() at its head and stops the stream in its own catch, so `cameraStream` can never be orphaned. NOTE: privacy defect — recommend an out-of-band owner unpin for this ~4-line diff rather than holding it behind Glass 8.

defects.defect: An undecodable image uploaded through the control's own Upload button produces an unhandled promise rejection and a real page error with ZERO user-facing feedback, and leaves three UI surfaces contradicting each other.
defects.evidence: Repro output: {"unhandled":["Cannot decode the data in the argument to createImageBitmap"],"errorLineVisible":false,"errorText":null,"resetDisabled":false,"skeletonEls":["shadow-palette skeleton-ink-register …"],"ghost":true,"caption":1} and pageErrors: ["PAGEERR InvalidStateError: Cannot decode the data in the argument to createImageBitmap"]. A .txt file reproduces identically and additionally plants . The mega-tranche visual REPORT.json records pageErrors:0 for /#/extract because it never uploaded a file — this class is invisible to that audit.
defects.mechanism: unguarded async: useExtractSession.ts:167 calls runQuantize() fire-and-forget with no .catch; runQuantize (:153-157) discards the promise; useImageQuantize.ts:106 awaits imageFileToPixels(file), which throws inside createImageBitmap BEFORE runQuantize (:80-99) ever sets isProcessing/error — so quantizeError (useExtractSession.ts:66) stays null and the v-if destructive line at ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85 never renders. previewDataUrl is set before the decode is known good (useExtractSession.ts:166).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe6.mjs — headless WebKit at http://localhost:9000/#/extract; setInputFiles({name:"corrupt.png", mimeType:"image/png", buffer: Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x89,0x50,0x4e,0x47,0x0d,0x0a,0x1a,0x0a]), Buffer.alloc(40,0)])}). This truncated-but-correctly-typed PNG passes BOTH accept="image/*" (ImageDropZone.vue:30) and the drop-path guard file?.type.startsWith("image/") (ImageDropZone.vue:97), so no filter rejects it.
defects.proposedCure: Make the decode a typed outcome rather than an exception — quantizeFromFile returns the Result shape the session already speaks (presentedPalette is already {ok:true}|{ok:false,error}), so a decode failure lands in workerError and the existing destructive line renders for free. Set previewDataUrl only AFTER a successful decode; that one reordering also removes the broken and the lying hasImage.

defects.defect: The Reset control's enablement gate `disabled || !hasImage` (line 84) is wrong in both directions: dead exactly when the user needs it, and live when there is nothing to reset.
defects.evidence: False-negative measured: {"focused":true,"before":"5","k":"16","labelText":"16","resetDisabled":true} — eleven ArrowRight presses move k from 5 to 16 with no image loaded, the ShadowPalette ghost re-segments to 16, and the only control that restores k=5/kC=0.5 is disabled. The live-k-without-an-image behaviour is CERTIFIED, not accidental: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:147-158 drives the k slider with no image and asserts 5→6→5 segments; ExtractWorkbench.vue:92-95 documents it. False-positive measured in C-2's run: an undecodable file sets previewDataUrl → hasImage true → resetDisabled:false.
defects.mechanism: wrong predicate: onReset (useExtractSession.ts:180-184) resets k and chromaWeight and only CONDITIONALLY re-quantizes (`if (lastFile.value)`), so its precondition is parameter-dirtiness, not image-presence. The gate asks a different question than the action answers.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe3.mjs section C — navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/extract with no image, focus the slider named "Number of colors", press ArrowRight 11 times, then read the disabled state of the button with title="Reset". Returns k=16 with resetDisabled:true.
defects.proposedCure: Gate on dirtiness of exactly what Reset resets: expose `canReset` from useExtractSession (k !== 5 || chromaWeight !== 0.5) so the default constants live in ONE place instead of being duplicated across useExtractSession.ts:44,45,181,182 and the consumer. The `hasImage` prop then has no consumer and is deleted — the contract shrinks rather than gaining a second clause.

defects.defect: A dead `.touch-gate-target` rule in the component's own <style scoped> block matches no element and never can; it is the fossil of the touch-gate inflation mechanism that would have widened the component's measured 12.0 CSS px drag handle. A sibling file still documents ExtractControls as a consumer of that mechanism — a false cross-file claim.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:139-142 declares `.touch-gate-target { border-radius: var(--radius-pill); }`; grep shows the class is applied to no element in this template (only hits repo-wide are the picker's ComponentSliders.vue:58, SpectrumCanvas.vue:11, usePointerDebug.ts:121 — plus the rule itself). Being <style scoped> it compiles to `.touch-gate-target[data-v-…]` and can never match. ComponentSliders.vue:244 still reads "the ExtractControls … touch-gate-target uses" — false. Measured hit geometry (mobile, pointer:coarse, elementFromPoint sweep from thumb centre): {"boxW":12,"boxH":44,"hitW":12,"neighborAtMinus12":"SPAN.slider-range","neighborAtPlus12":"SPAN.slider-track"}; thumbCS {"w":"12px","h":"44px","before":"\"\""} — the ::before does not widen it. REPORT.json /#/extract lists both thumbs on all four matrices (desktop 12x24, mobile 12x44) = 2 of the 6 small tap targets per capture. The sibling picker sliders DO get a 44px coarse extension (ComponentSliders.vue:336+, @media (pointer: coarse) .channel-slider::before).
defects.mechanism: dead legacy shim — CSS for a mechanism that was never wired in this component, left behind when the touch-gate idiom was homed in the picker tree; the missing inflation leaves a 12px-wide drag handle on coarse pointers where a mis-grab lands on .slider-range/.slider-track and JUMPS the value instead of starting a drag.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe2.mjs section A — headless WebKit, 390x844 isMobile/hasTouch, http://localhost:9000/#/extract; sweep document.elementFromPoint horizontally from the thumb centre. HONEST CAVEAT, also measured: WCAG 2.5.8 AA is NOT failed — the 24px-circle spacing-exception test against every other target's bounding box returns "viol": [] (nearest neighbours are 44x44 DockControls at >=68px). File as ergonomics + dead code, never as an AA violation.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead rule and the false claim at ComponentSliders.vue:244. The 12px width is glass-ui's `.slider-thumb` geometry, so the real cure is a coarse-pointer width/hit rung in glass-ui's slider — NOT a fourth copy of the touch-gate idiom in a consumer (edicts #3/#4). Relay to the glass-ui BJ inbox; this is the one finding whose fix is genuinely gated on Glass 8.

defects.defect: Two <label> elements with no `for` and no wrapped control (lines 15 and 66) label nothing; the visible label text "kC" is absent from the accessible name "Chroma weight", and the k row markes up the live VALUE as a <label>.
defects.evidence: Measured live: "labels": [{"text":"5","htmlFor":null,"id":"","title":null},{"text":"kC","htmlFor":null,"id":"","title":"Chroma weight"}]. Playwright ARIA snapshot of the component shows them as bare text nodes, unassociated: `- text: "5"` / `- slider "Number of colors"` / `- text: kC` / `- slider "Chroma weight"` / `- text: "0.5"`.
defects.mechanism: semantic misuse — a <label> element used as a visual readout/abbreviation, producing an orphan form-association and a Label-in-Name mismatch.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe1.mjs + probe4.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/extract; read every <label> inside the extract controls root and take locator.ariaSnapshot(). WCAG 2.5.3 consequence: a voice-control user saying "click kC" cannot reach the slider, because the accessible name is "Chroma weight" and does not contain the visible text.
defects.proposedCure: They are not labels — they are a readout and an abbreviation. Make the k readout and the 0.5 readout (:78) `<span aria-hidden="true">` (the slider already announces aria-valuenow, measured "5"), and fold the abbreviation into the name so the visible text is contained in it: aria-label="kC — chroma weight". One tag change and one string; no new element, no wrapper.

defects.defect: All three DockControls rely on `title` as their sole accessible name, giving no tooltip at all on touch; /#/extract is the single largest contributor to the application's nameless-button census.
defects.evidence: Measured: [{"title":"Upload image","ariaLabel":null,"text":"","w":40,"h":40},{"title":"Open camera","ariaLabel":null,"text":""},{"title":"Reset","ariaLabel":null,"text":"","disabled":true}]. REPORT.md: /#/extract is the ONLY route with namelessButtons=3 in all four matrices and the only route above 1 on mobile; summing the census (desktop-light 9 + desktop-dark 9 + mobile-light 4 + mobile-dark 4 = 26 instances) extract contributes 12 of 26 = 46%, all three from this file. House inconsistency: the shell dock names properly (Dock.vue:143,144,154 aria-label; SlugEditLayer.vue:94,106,114) while the workbenches use title. The three Lucide <svg>s are also exposed as unnamed `img` nodes inside the buttons (ARIA snapshot `- img` x3); the sibling ImageDropZone.vue:60 correctly sets aria-hidden="true".
defects.mechanism: last-resort naming — HTML-AAM resolves `title` as the terminal fallback, so AT is served, but `title` renders no tooltip on touch and the repo's own probe definition (capture.mjs:104 accepts only aria-label/aria-labelledby/textContent) counts these as nameless.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe4.mjs — locator.ariaSnapshot() on the extract controls root at http://localhost:9000/#/extract returns `button "Upload image"`, `button "Open camera"`, `button "Reset" [disabled]`, each containing an unnamed `img`. So AT IS served; the residual defect is sighted-touch discoverability plus the exposed icon nodes.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label + title on each control (title kept for the desktop tooltip, aria-label as the authoritative name) and aria-hidden="true" on the three Lucide icons — adopting the shell dock's existing convention rather than inventing a third one.

defects.defect: The header comment's claim that the rail's inset hairline gives "a certified identity edge independent of its gradient content in every state" is false in the undeveloped state: the ring is painted in the same colour as the fill.
defects.evidence: Lines 6-11 make the claim; line 22 sets `backgroundColor: trackInk` and `boxShadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px ${trackInk}` — the same token twice. Measured live pre-image: "bgColor": "oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)", "boxShadow": "oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023) 0px 0px 0px 1.5px inset", "bgImage": "none". Identical colour = 1.0:1 ring-to-fill = zero visible edge.
defects.mechanism: a documented invariant contradicted by its own implementation — one token used for two layers that are supposed to separate from each other.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe1.mjs — getComputedStyle on [data-o18="extract-k-rail"] at http://localhost:9000/#/extract with no image loaded; compare backgroundColor to the boxShadow colour.
defects.proposedCure: Either narrow the comment to the developed state, or make the ring an actual edge: the ring's job is separation from the PLATE, so the ring should carry the certified ink and the fill should carry the de-emphasis rung — two tokens for two layers.

defects.defect: The `gradient` prop's empty-state value is entirely inert — a dead binding the producer mistypes and the consumer silently discards.
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:103 returns the string "var(--muted)" — a COLOUR — from a computed named kSliderGradient, for a prop declared `gradient: string` (ExtractControls.vue:107). Line 22 feeds it to the `background` shorthand and then overwrites the colour channel with `backgroundColor: trackInk` on the very next object key. Measured pre-image: "bgImage": "none".
defects.mechanism: shorthand/longhand collision in a style-binding object literal, masking a producer-side contract violation: the shorthand's colour channel is unconditionally clobbered by the following longhand, so the wrong-typed value can never be observed.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe1.mjs — getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-o18="extract-k-rail"]')).backgroundImage at http://localhost:9000/#/extract with no image returns "none", proving the gradient prop contributed nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Type the contract honestly — `gradient: string | null`, null when undeveloped — and use the explicit `backgroundImage` longhand instead of the `background` shorthand, so the two layers stop fighting over one property and the null case becomes a real branch instead of a swallowed one.

defects.defect: Three byte-identical per-instance `--btn-hover-color` style pins on siblings inside one flex row (owner edict #5: root-level styling, never per-instance overrides) — and the pin carries the RAW picked colour, bypassing the certification contract the same file establishes for the track.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:42, :51, :86 all carry `:style="{ '--btn-hover-color': cssColor }"` on three siblings inside the row opened at :39. `--btn-hover-color` is an inherited custom property, so one binding on the row container yields an identical cascade. Meanwhile lines 113-125 establish at length that the track material must be contract ink certified at GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR (=3, ink.ts:16), and trackInk (:123) implements it — but the three hover pins use the uncertified `cssColor`.
defects.mechanism: per-instance override of an inherited custom property, triplicated; plus a certification bypass on the sibling controls of the very element being certified.
defects.reproduction: Static: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:42,51,86 vs :39 and :123-125. Per-frame patch-count cost during a live colour drag is UNMEASURED and labelled a hypothesis in the report (C-11.3).
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the custom property to the row container and certify it in one place: `:style="{ '--btn-hover-color': trackInk }"` once at line 39. Three bindings collapse to one and the hover ink joins the contract instead of evading it.

defects.defect: Zero unit tests reference this component; the two e2e specs that touch its rendered tree would stay green under six distinct mutations, including the exact mutation that is C-1.
defects.evidence: grep -rn "ExtractControls" test/ e2e/ returns only two prose mentions in unrelated files. Coverage is limited to e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:152-158 (getByRole slider "Number of colors", keyboard, ghost segment count) and e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1106-1134 (colour samples of [data-o18="extract-kc"] .slider-track and [data-o18="extract-k-rail"]).
defects.mechanism: vacuous gate — the specs assert paint and one slider's segment count, never the component's prop contract, so the contract can be deleted without turning anything red.
defects.reproduction: Mutations that keep BOTH specs green: (a) delete `:disabled` from line 84 entirely — nothing asserts Reset's disabled state, which is precisely why C-1 shipped; (b) delete the @click handlers emitting 'upload' and 'camera' — no spec activates either button; (c) delete the whole .touch-gate-target block — already dead; (d) replace the kC @update:model-value handler with a no-op — o18 measures the track's colour, o9 drives only the k slider; (e) change :max="16" to :max="99" — no bound is asserted; (f) drop boxShadow from line 22 — o18 samples backgroundColor, not the ring. Only removing aria-label="Number of colors" or renaming either data-o18 hook breaks anything.
defects.proposedCure: One @vue/test-utils spec asserting the CONTRACT rather than the paint: that `disabled` reaches every control (C-1), that Reset's gate follows dirtiness not hasImage (C-3), and that each button exposes an aria-label (C-6). Three assertions kill six of the mutations above, and test/ is not covered by the BJ W4 pin so it can land immediately.

defects.defect: Three labelled HYPOTHESES with no reproduction: (1) the two `v[0]!` non-null assertions at lines 33 and 76 mask a `number[] | undefined` contract behind a truthiness guard that an empty array passes; (2) trackInk reaches parseCssColor via certifyAccentInk, and parseOklch handles !parsed.ok but not a THROW — the repo's live R1 crash class; (3) trackInk recomputes and five inline-style bindings patch per rAF-coalesced colour-drag frame.
defects.evidence: (1) ExtractControls.vue:33 `(v: number[] | undefined) => v && $emit('update:k', v[0]!)` and :76 likewise — `[]` is truthy, so v[0]! would emit undefined into colorCount.value and quantizeFromFile(file, undefined). (2) ExtractControls.vue:123 → useContrastSafeColor.ts:353 safeCss → ink.ts:130 certifyAccentInk → ink.ts:39 parseOklch → parseCssColor; the !ok branch is handled, a throw is not. (3) cssColor is the rAF-coalesced live pick; resolveLiveTintCached (useContrastSafeColor.ts:240) caches the getComputedStyle+canvas probe by (surface, darkClass, epoch) so that part is amortised, but certifyAccentInk's gamut/floor walk is not.
defects.mechanism: (1) type-assertion masking of an optional contract; (2) an unguarded throw path through a known-crashy parser; (3) unmeasured per-frame recompute.
defects.reproduction: NONE for all three. (1) I could not make the live reka-ui slider emit []. (2) cssColor here is app-serialized, so I could not drive a malformed string into parseCssColor from this component. (3) UNMEASURED — I chose not to spend a browser trace on it because C-9's hoist reduces the patch count 3→1 regardless of the measurement.

defects.defect: The `disabled` prop names a whole-component contract and governs exactly one of five controls; the parent's intent ("camera is running, stand down") is ignored by the camera button, and startCamera then overwrites cameraStream without stopping the prior stream.
