Upload (:40-46) and Camera (:49-55) carry no `:disabled`. Parent passes `:disabled="session.isProcessing.value || cameraActive"` at ExtractWorkbench.vue:70. ExtractWorkbench.startCamera :239-255 assigns `cameraStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({...})` with no prior stopCamera().
defects.mechanism: F4 — a prop name that overstates its scope; the API contract and the implementation disagree, and the disagreement lets a second getUserMedia land while the first stream is still live.
defects.reproduction: Read ExtractControls.vue:84 (sole reference) against ExtractWorkbench.vue:70 (the parent's intent) and :239-255 (the unguarded reassignment). Carried from r1; re-verified by grep at this HEAD.
defects.proposedCure: Either honour `disabled` across the whole cluster (Upload/Camera/both Sliders) or rename it to what it actually governs (`resetDisabled`). Independently, startCamera must call stopCamera() before requesting a new stream.

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json` `paths` has desynchronised from `package.json#exports`: three declared entries resolve to nothing, two live subpaths are absent — including `/css`, the one this component's trackInk transitively depends on — and the comment asserts a key count that is wrong.
defects.evidence: package.json exports = 7 keys, no root: ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize. tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 declares 8, comment at :40 calls it "a CLOSED 8-key set". `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → all three "No such file or directory". `import.meta.resolve`: FAIL @mkbabb/value.js → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; FAIL /parsing → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; FAIL /units → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. `/css` and `/value` resolve fine but have no paths entry; ink.ts:11-13 imports `@mkbabb/value.js/css`.
defects.mechanism: F4 — two configs describing one truth, one generated and one hand-maintained. vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES its alias set from the exports map explicitly so it "can never drift"; the tsconfig hand-maintains the same truth and has drifted. Not a live break (r1 traced self-exports resolution catching /css) — a config block that no longer proves anything, i.e. a false proof of the public API surface.
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e "for (const s of ['@mkbabb/value.js','@mkbabb/value.js/css','@mkbabb/value.js/value','@mkbabb/value.js/parsing','@mkbabb/value.js/units','@mkbabb/value.js/color']) { try { console.log('OK  ', s, '->', import.meta.resolve(s)); } catch (e) { console.log('FAIL', s, '->', e.code); } }" — pasted output in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the seven value.js `paths` entries — self-`exports` resolution already works and is the honest mechanism — or generate them from package.json#exports the way vite.config.ts already does. One source of truth.

defects.defect: The dogfood alias silently substitutes the working tree into glass-ui's and keyframes' own value.js dependency, and the comment justifying it is factually false at HEAD.
defects.evidence: vite.config.ts:25 says "A package does not install itself, so these exact aliases point the seven public specifiers at this checkout's freshly-built published surface." It does install itself transitively: package-lock.json:1291 glass-ui peer `@mkbabb/value.js: ^4.0.0`, :1330 keyframes.js hard pin `4.0.0`, :1336-1338 `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js` resolved from the registry tarball. `node -e "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/package.json').version"` → 4.0.0. `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/` → glass-ui keyframes.js value.js.
defects.mechanism: F4 — a comment that no longer describes reality. The Vite aliases are repo-wide anchored regexes on the bare specifiers, so glass-ui's and keyframes' own internal value.js imports are rewritten to this checkout's dist/ too. The demo runs glass-ui 7.0.0 against an unreleased value.js.
defects.reproduction: grep -n "@mkbabb/value.js" package-lock.json | head -8 and node -e "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/package.json').version" → 4.0.0 is installed, contradicting the comment.
defects.proposedCure: Defensible as a dogfood choice — but document it truthfully. Rewrite vite.config.ts:25 to state that the alias deliberately overrides the transitively-installed 4.0.0 for glass-ui and keyframes too, or scope the alias to demo-authored modules only so producer packages resolve their own pinned dependency.

defects.defect: Both slider thumbs render 12 x 24 CSS px against WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) 24 x 24 minimum — producer arithmetic, surfaced through this component.
defects.evidence: Live WebKit /#/extract: [{"label":"Number of colors","w":12,"h":24,"cssWidth":"12px","thumbSizeToken":"1rem","pass2_5_8":false},{"label":"Chroma weight","w":12,"h":24,"cssWidth":"12px","thumbSizeToken":"1rem","pass2_5_8":false}]. Producer: `[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb{width:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem) * .75); …}`. REPORT.json smallTapTargets for safari-desktop-light /#/extract contains exactly {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Number of colors"} and {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Chroma weight"}, in all four matrices.
defects.mechanism: F2 — producer default is wrong and the consumer cannot fix it without a per-instance override of a root-level design decision (edict 5), repeated at every slider in the repo.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/chalL-wbextract-probe2.mjs → the SC 2.5.8 check block; cross-check REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets for /#/extract.
defects.proposedCure: Glass 8: default `--slider-thumb-size: 2rem` so `size * .75` = 24px, satisfying SC 2.5.8 with no consumer override anywhere.

defects.defect: Dead scoped CSS shipped in the subject file: `.touch-gate-target` is compiled with this component's scope id and matches zero elements on the live route.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:139-142 declares `.touch-gate-target { border-radius: var(--radius-pill); }`; the class appears nowhere in the component's template. Live: {"rootScopeAttrs":["data-v-bfbc09b0","data-v-ce26fe94"],"touchGateTargetsInDoc":0,"touchGateTargetsInExtract":0,"touchGateRuleSelectors":[".touch-gate-target",".touch-gate-target:has(.slider-track)",".touch-gate-target.touch-gate-active",".touch-gate-target[data-v-bfbc09b0]"]}. The idiom's real home is ComponentSliders.vue:243-262, whose block is deliberately UNSCOPED and whose doc-block explains why.
defects.mechanism: F1 — a fragment copied across a component boundary where the mechanism does not travel. Same failure shape as L-11, expressed in CSS rather than tokens: the scoped compile makes it structurally unable to match.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/chalL-wbextract-probe.mjs → the `.touch-gate-target reachability` block enumerates live rules and match counts; `.touch-gate-target[data-v-bfbc09b0]` is present in the stylesheet with 0 matches.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 139-142. If the extract sliders genuinely need the touch gate, adopt the ComponentSliders mechanism whole (unscoped block + the class on the wrapper), not the styling fragment alone.

defects.defect: Per-instance icon sizing duplicates the producer's root-level token: `class="w-5 h-5 transition-colors"` on all three glyphs re-states glass-ui's own default and silently opts them out of `--dock-icon-glyph` retuning.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:45, :54, :89 each `class="w-5 h-5 transition-colors"`. Producer: `.dock-icon-button > svg { width: var(--dock-icon-glyph, 1.25rem); height: var(--dock-icon-glyph, 1.25rem); }` (dist/components/dock/styles/controls/icon-button.css) — 1.25rem = 20px = exactly w-5/h-5. Tailwind utilities land in @layer utilities and win over @layer components, so the demo's duplicate is what paints. `.dock-icon-button` already declares `transition: … color var(--dock-motion-fast) …` and the glyph inherits it through currentColor, so `transition-colors` is redundant too. `grep -rn 'class="w-5 h-5' demo --include='*.vue' | wc -l` → 13 sites.
defects.mechanism: F2 — producer seam bypassed. Edict 5 violation: styling at the instance rather than the root, hard-coding a value the design system already owns as a retunable token.
defects.reproduction: Read ExtractControls.vue:45/54/89 against the quoted icon-button.css rule; both compute 20px, so the override is pure duplication. Cascade-layer ordering (utilities > components) makes the demo copy authoritative.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the classes. If a workbench wants larger glyphs than the dock, set `--dock-icon-glyph` once at the control-bar root — one declaration governing the cluster instead of three per-instance overrides.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context arm) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1/D-3/D-5 share ONE mechanism: the T-44a "certified track ink" cure paints the ENTIRE slider track — range and remainder alike — in one opaque certified colour, and neutralises the producer track underneath it (ExtractControls.vue:32 `--slider-track-bg: transparent`; :75 `--slider-track-bg: trackInk`). Consequences, all measured: (a) `.slider-range` computes `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)` / `background-image: none` at every arm, so BOTH sliders read "100% full" at every value — k=5-of-16 renders as a solid full-width bar; (b) 15,948 px² of 100%-alpha chroma-0.218 seed tint on two support controls versus a 2px dashed C=0.0039 stroke on the declared protagonist stage — a 56× chroma inversion of the pane's hierarchy, and in dark the same clamp yields L=95.8% C=0.021 (ΔL 41.3pp, −90.3% chroma), making the track the brightest object on the page; (c) the "persistent certified identity ring" is byte-identical to the fill it sits on in the undeveloped state (ringSameAsFill: True, all four arms); (d) nothing forced-colors-durable survives — under `forced-colors: active` both tracks compute `rgb(255,255,255)` with `box-shadow: none`, so each slider renders as a lone 12×24 outlined rectangle floating in blank space with no track, extent or min/max. The certifier (`ink.ts:129-141`) is a one-sided stroke/text instrument with no luminance ceiling and no chroma preservation; it was applied as a FILL. Gestalt cure: certified ink inks the axis BOUNDARY and the RANGE, never the field; the producer keeps the track — which also deletes the absolutely-positioned rail-under-a-transparent-slider contrivance entirely.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negatives I did establish, recorded in report §6: hit region matches paint exactly — rail, `glass-slider` root and `.slider-track` all report {x 252, y 494.6, w 434, h 24}; the `w-5` k-label reservation holds at the widest legal value k=16 (scrollW 20 == clientW 20, overflows: false, 16.4px Fira); no horizontal overflow at 1440/390/320 (scrollWidth == clientWidth in every block); `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — every import is a value import; Vue 3.5 idiom clean — reactive props destructure correct, no template refs so `useTemplateRef` N/A, no `defineModel` so no `shallowRef` need; motion is token-backed (`--default-transition-duration` → 0.2s, dropping to 0.1s under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) and animates colour only, no layout-forcing property — no motion finding; disabled survives forced-colors as a distinct GrayText `rgb(96,0,0)`; `demo/ui/slider/index.ts` is a one-line re-export of glass-ui `Slider`, no hand-rolled clone.)

defects.defect: Both slider tracks disappear entirely under `forced-colors: active` — each axis renders as a lone 12×24 outlined rectangle in blank space, with no track, no extent, no min/max and no indication it is a control.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/D-probe2-states.txt block `forced-colors-active-1440-light`: rail `bg rgb(255, 255, 255)`, `box-shadow none`, `background-image none`; kcTrack 230.5×24 `bg rgb(255, 255, 255)`, `background-image none`; thumbs 12×24 border 2px rgb(0,0,0), background rgba(255,255,255,0). Rendered proof: evidence/D-forced-colors-1440-light.png. Cause sites: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:32 and :75.
defects.mechanism: Certified ink used as the track FIELD via an inline `background-color` + inline `box-shadow`, after the producer track was neutralised. forced-colors overrides `background-color` to Canvas and removes `box-shadow` outright (`forced-color-adjust: auto`), so nothing durable remains. Canon requires forced-colors survival for state in VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 and §4.2 (twice).
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/D-probe2.mjs` (first block) against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000/#/extract; or Chromium with forced-colors emulation on that route.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural: certified ink inks the axis BOUNDARY (a real border) and the RANGE; the producer's neutral well stays the track field. Producer seam β3 — glass-ui `Slider` ships a `@media (forced-colors: active)` track rule (CanvasText border, Canvas field). Blocked wave W·EC-β.

defects.defect: The kC (chroma-weight) axis collapses to a 22.5 px track at the canon's own named 320 px arm — the 12 px thumb is 53.3 % of its own track and one step is 0.70 CSS px of pointer travel. The control is inoperable, not merely cramped.
defects.evidence: evidence/D-probe1-rects.txt and D-probe2-states.txt: kC `.slider-track` width 230.5 px @1440, 92.5 px @390, **22.5 px @320**; thumb 12 px at every arm; usable travel 10.5 px for 15 steps = 0.70 px/step. Same row, k axis = 226 px @320 → 10.0× disparity within one cluster. Rendered proof: evidence/D-narrow-320-light.png. Cause: ExtractControls.vue:65 (`flex-1 min-w-0`, no minimum operable length, no wrap rule) against 5 fixed siblings (3×40 px buttons + 2 separators + 20 px label + 20 px readout).
defects.mechanism: The k axis was granted its own full-width row (ExtractControls.vue:14); the kC axis shares a 6-child fixed-width row at every viewport with no `min-inline-size` floor and no wrap breakpoint, so it absorbs 100 % of the width deficit.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe2.mjs` block `narrow320`; or load http://localhost:9000/#/extract at a 320 px viewport.
defects.proposedCure: Give the kC axis its own row below a named breakpoint, mirroring k — or a hard `min-inline-size` floor with the row wrapping. No axis under ~120 px operable track, ever. Blocked wave W·EC-α item 2.

defects.defect: Neither slider expresses its value: the range indicator paints nothing and the remainder is painted the same colour, so both sliders read "100 % full" at every value in 100 % of sessions.
defects.evidence: evidence/D-probe1-rects.txt desktop-light: `.slider-range` x 252 w 115.7 `bg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` `background-image none` (correctly SIZED — 115.7/434 = 26.7 % = (5−1)/(16−1) — and paints nothing); kC `.slider-range` x 360.5 w 76.8 same. Both `.slider-track` report `oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)`. Rendered proof: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png (k=5-of-16 as a solid full-width crimson bar) and shots/safari-mobile-dark/extract.png (same, near-white).
defects.mechanism: glass-ui's `.slider-range` (`glass-liquid-fill`) has no independent background token, so the consumer's only way to ink the track was to paint the WHOLE track — which erased the range/remainder distinction. The only surviving value cues are a 12 px thumb and a numeric readout.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract at any viewport/scheme; or `node evidence/D-probe1.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Producer seam β1 — `Slider` exposes `--slider-range-bg` independent of `--slider-track-bg`, defaulting non-transparent. Consumer then inks range + outline only. Blocked waves W·EC-β (β1) + W·EC-α (item 1).

defects.defect: The k readout is a lying readout — it displays the REQUESTED cluster count, not the delivered one, so it disagrees with the palette card's own badge in the same viewport.
defects.evidence: evidence/D-developed-k16-1440-light.png: the k label reads `16` while the palette card badge ~90 px away reads `10` and 10 swatches render. evidence/D-probe2-states.txt `k16.bgImg` carries only 10 gradient stops, so the component's own graphic already disagrees with its own number. Sites: ExtractControls.vue:16 renders `{{ k }}` unconditionally; useExtractSession.ts `colorCount` is the request. The governing principle is stated by the codebase itself at ExtractWorkbench.vue:135-136 — "never a lying readout".
defects.mechanism: The component's single numeric output is bound to its input request rather than to `presentedPalette.value.length`; the quantizer returns fewer clusters than k whenever the source has fewer distinct colours.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract → upload any image with fewer distinct clusters than k → raise k above the cluster count. Automated in `node evidence/D-probe2.mjs` block `developed-1440-light`.
defects.proposedCure: Render the DELIVERED count once developed (or `10 / 16`); the requested k stays the slider's own value. Never a bare number that contradicts the card badge in the same frame. W·EC-α item 3.

defects.defect: Certified ink applied as a field inverts the pane's visual hierarchy in both schemes: two support controls carry 15,948 px² of opaque near-gamut-edge seed tint while the declared protagonist stage carries a dashed hairline.
defects.evidence: Measured @1440: drop-zone stage (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 Extract — "The image is the stage") 462×180 = 83,160 px², no fill, 2 px dashed `--ink-muted` stroke at chroma 0.003862; k rail 434×24 = 10,416 px² at 100 % α chroma 0.218024; kC track 230.5×24 = 5,532 px² same → 56.5× chroma ratio. Dark: `oklch(0.958322 0.021053 9.834023)`, L = 95.8 %, ΔL 41.3 pp and −90.3 % chroma versus light. Rendered proof: shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png, shots/safari-mobile-dark/extract.png, evidence/D-developed-1440-dark.png (the kC bar out-lumes the `Extract` H1). Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 (seed tint forbidden outside ambient field / active accent / WatercolorDot-specimen / pastel Palettes lanes) and §3.8 (one full-strength protagonist).
defects.mechanism: `certifyAccentInk` (demo/color-session/ink.ts:129-141) is a one-sided stroke/text certifier with no luminance ceiling and no chroma-preservation constraint; it maximises rather than satisfies. Applied as a large opaque FILL it produces a maximum-chroma slab in light and a maximum-luminance slab in dark.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe1.mjs` (all four arms print the rail/track computed colours and rects).
defects.proposedCure: Transposition: the certified pick inks a 1.5 px OUTLINE plus the range indicator; the field stays the producer's neutral well at its own material tier. Identity then reads as edge, value as extent — and WCAG 1.4.11 is satisfied by the boundary it was written for. W·EC-α item 1.

defects.defect: The k rail renders discrete extracted colours as a continuous interpolated blend — ~429 of 434 px show colours the quantizer never returned — while the palette card 130 px below renders the same data as crisp bands.
defects.evidence: evidence/D-probe2-states.txt `developed-1440-light`: `linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.419876 0.112822 291.556) 0%, oklch(0.888177 0.0805526 92.1838) 25%, oklch(0.58703 0.159887 36.6838) 50%, oklch(0.520653 0.101123 155.227) 75%, oklch(0.681056 0.0824094 316.378) 100%)` — stops at POINTS, continuous interpolation between. Rendered proof: evidence/D-developed-k16-1440-light.png (smeary rail directly above a 10-band strip). Additionally ExtractControls.vue:21 `rounded-full` computes radius 12 px, pinching the first and last stop — the two ends of the data — into semicircles. Source: useExtractSession.ts `kSliderGradient`.
defects.mechanism: A categorical quantity encoded on a continuous colour scale. Two encodings of one dataset are shown 130 px apart and one of them is false.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe2.mjs` block `developed-1440-light`, or upload any image at http://localhost:9000/#/extract.
defects.proposedCure: Hard stops (`c1 0%, c1 20%, c2 20%, c2 40% …`) so the rail is band-for-band identical to the card strip. Same producer function, different stop grammar. W·EC-α item 4.

defects.defect: The "persistent certified identity edge" hairline ring is invisible in exactly the state its own comment says it rescues — the ring colour is byte-identical to the fill it sits on.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:6-11 claims the ring gives "a certified identity edge independent of its gradient content in every state". Measured undeveloped state, all four arms (evidence/D-probe1-rects.txt, `ringSameAsFill: True` in every block incl. dark): `backgroundColor: oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)` and `boxShadow: oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023) 0px 0px 0px 1.5px inset`. ΔE = 0. Source: ExtractControls.vue:22.
defects.mechanism: The ring and the fill are both bound to the same `trackInk` computed value, so the ring can only appear once a gradient occludes the fill — i.e. it exists precisely when the comment says it is redundant, and is absent precisely when the comment says it rescues the component.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe1.mjs` — every block prints `ringSameAsFill: True`. Visually: http://localhost:9000/#/extract with no image loaded.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of the D-5 transposition: once the field is a neutral well, the certified outline has a real ground to read against in every state, and the claim in the comment becomes true rather than aspirational. W·EC-α item 1.

defects.defect: Two `<DockSeparator />` are rendered — forbidden outright by the binding composition inventory — and they paint zero pixels while still being announced to AT with self-contradicting orientation attributes.
defects.evidence: Canon: docs/tranches/V/OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binding table — `| Extract | [] | none | none | image/specimen material and interval separate stage from controls |` followed by "Any additional line, automatic P122 divider, consumer-hidden producer line, terminal row rule, caster stroke or corner rule is a defect." Sites: ExtractControls.vue:57 and :81. Measured (evidence/D-probe2-states.txt, `seps` array, every arm — light, dark, forced-colors, developed, 320): `.dock-separator` in the Dock band = `w 1, h 27.5` (×5); in ExtractControls = `w 1, h 0` (×2). Markup: `role="separator" data-orientation="horizontal" aria-orientation="vertical"`. Also PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 (REMOVE) and §5.4.
defects.mechanism: A Dock-band primitive that derives its block size from the Dock's fixed band, borrowed into a resting-plate `flex items-center` row with no `align-self: stretch`, collapses to zero. The component both violates the `none` inventory by presence and fails to render the line it illegally asks for.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe2.mjs` — the `seps` array in every block shows the 27.5 px Dock separators alongside the two 0 px ExtractControls ones on the same page.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both. Spacing plus material already carry the grouping, which is exactly what the binding table says. W·EC-α item 5 (β4 for the producer contract becomes moot).

defects.defect: All three actions (Upload, Camera, Reset) are nameless buttons whose only labels are hover-only `title` tooltips — /#/extract is the highest nameless-button route in the entire 15-route audit, and 2 of its 4 matrices are touch.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json — `/#/extract` reports `"namelessButtons": 3` in ALL FOUR matrices; every other route is ≤ 1 (REPORT.md lines 96-113). Live probe confirms the identity: `nameless [('Upload image', 40, 40), ('Open camera', 40, 40), ('Reset', 40, 40)]` (evidence/D-probe1-rects.txt, every arm). Sites: ExtractControls.vue:41, :50, :85 — `title` and no `aria-label`. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 (ADD-AFFORDANCE/REMOVE — "every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state"), PR-16 and §5.6 ("do not compensate … with tooltip proliferation").
defects.mechanism: `title` is an accname fallback only and is entirely unreachable on touch, where half the audit matrix lives. Three icon-only actions in one row with no text and no touch-reachable label.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe1.mjs` — the `namelessButtons` array in every block; or read REPORT.json's `/#/extract` a11y node.
defects.proposedCure: Visible text labels for all three, or `aria-label` plus a non-hover-only affordance; delete the three `title`-only names. W·EC-α item 6.

defects.defect: The component accepts a `disabled` prop and honours it on exactly 1 of its 5 interactive controls; there is no pending/in-flight treatment at all, and the un-disabled Camera button makes a MediaStream leak reachable.
defects.evidence: Parent passes `disabled = session.isProcessing || cameraActive` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:70). ExtractControls.vue:84 is the ONLY `:disabled` in the file (Reset). The k slider (:24-34), kC slider (:67-77), Upload (:40-46) and Camera (:49-55) all ignore it. useExtractSession.ts `onKChange`/`onChromaChange` have no in-flight guard — they call `debouncedReQuantize()` unconditionally. `startCamera()` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-255) overwrites `cameraStream` without stopping the previous tracks. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 (ADD-AFFORDANCE); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ("pending … states are never color-only").
defects.mechanism: A prop threaded into the component but wired to one leaf. The pending state was never designed for the cluster, so nothing in the control row changes while a quantize is in flight or the camera is live.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED for the missing disable by inspection (:84 is the sole `:disabled`) and by the parent's binding at :70. HYPOTHESIS for the stream leak — reproduction would be http://localhost:9000/#/extract → Camera → grant → Camera again (first MediaStream's tracks never stopped, device indicator stays on); not executed, headless has no camera.
defects.proposedCure: Propagate `disabled` to both sliders, Upload and Camera; add an in-flight guard in `useExtractSession`; give the row an explicit pending register rather than relying on the parent's skeleton. W·EC-α item 11.

defects.defect: Neither axis satisfies the mandated domain-neutral axis composition: the k axis has NO label and NO unit (a bare number), the kC axis has jargon behind a tooltip and no unit, and neither exposes `aria-valuetext`.

Sites: ExtractControls.vue:15-17 renders `{{ k }}` with no label word anywhere; :66 renders `kC` with the expansion only in `title="Chroma weight"`. Measured `valuetext: null` on BOTH thumbs at every arm (evidence/D-probe1-rects.txt), against §5.2's requirement that Home/End "announce label, value, unit".
defects.mechanism: The axis composition was implemented as "a slider plus a number" rather than as the producer-mandated label/unit/value triad, so the sighted user gets an unexplained integer and a two-letter token.

defects.defect: Out-of-matrix type role `text-micro`, and the cluster's self-declared "ONE mono voice" is measurably two voices whose ratio is not even stable across viewports.

Permitted: text-display, --type-title, --type-subheading, text-heading, text-prose, text-small, text-mono-small, mono-caption. `text-micro` is absent from it and is used twice — ExtractControls.vue:66 and :78. Measured font sizes: k label 16.4 px @1440 / 14.0 px @390 (`text-mono-small`, fluid) versus kC label+readout 11 px at BOTH (`text-micro`, fixed) → ratio 1.49× @1440, 1.27× @390. The file's own comment at :12-13 claims the k label "speaks its cluster's ONE mono voice (weight 400, matching kC)" — weight matches (400/400), size does not and drifts.
defects.mechanism: Two different type mechanisms (one fluid, one fixed) used for two labels of one control cluster, plus a role that the closed matrix does not contain.
defects.reproduction: `node evidence/D-probe1.mjs` — `kLabel.cs.fontSize` vs `kc.label.cs.fontSize` in the 1440 and 390 blocks.
defects.proposedCure: Per §4: kC label is a control label → `text-small` / Plus Jakarta Sans; kC readout is a value → `text-mono-small`, matching the k readout. One size for the two labels of one cluster. W·EC-α item 8.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue (and its composables, children, styles, tests)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: C-3: the mix convergence animation NEVER lands on the result well. `MixResultDisplay.vue:69` stamps the destination anchor `data-mix-target` on a glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot`, which declares `inheritAttrs:false` and forwards ONLY `class`/`style` — so the attribute never reaches the DOM. `mixStage.ts:121-124` therefore always takes its masking fallback `{x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7}`. Measured with in-page `querySelector` instrumentation: lookup `FOUND:false`, fallback (255, 491.4); canvas brightest pixel at t≈800ms = (255, 492) — the fallback to <1px; the real ghost well center = (60, 650). That is 251 px off, and the screenshot shows the pigment pool landing ON TOP of the primary `Mix` button (canvas z-index 20), while the announced well waits empty below. MixPane.vue:63-66 and :107-110 assert the exact opposite in prose. The `targetEl ? … : …` fallback is a standing-edict-2 masking fallback: it converted a hard failure into a permanently wrong animation and hid it from every gate.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded anyway, since the seat must not over-claim: the rAF discipline is genuinely CLEAN. Under `reducedMotion:"reduce"` the mix settles in 20 ms with 11 total page-wide rAF calls and 0 in the following idle second; `arm()` (useMixingAnimation.ts:120-125) takes a PRM fast-path that COMPLETES rather than pauses, so the phase machine can never strand. Under no-preference the loop runs one frame budget and calls `loop.stop()`. No leaked loop, no leaked listener. Likewise absent: `defineModel` staleness (no defineModel in the tree), ValueUnit nesting, reka slider pointer-capture, WebGL. Re-entrancy is guarded (useMixingState.ts:83); the stagger arithmetic is bounded (max delay 220 ms < MIX_ARRIVE_MS 700) so `MIX_ARRIVE_MS - d.delay` is never <= 0; `z-controls` resolves to a real z-index 20; `verbatimModuleSyntax` is satisfied. The architecture — one-clock law, separated stage model, small phase machine — is not the defect; every BLOCKER is a seam failure.)

The throw reaches `App.vue:50`'s ErrorBoundary, whose `onErrorCaptured` returns false — halting propagation, so NOTHING is logged: no console.error, no pageerror, no window.onerror.

Invalid CSS color Try again", "boundaryVisible": true, "mainHTMLlen": 2795}}. Live DOM (WBMIXPANE-C-probe0b.mjs): querySelector('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]') → {"found": false}; the element is `<span aria-hidden="true" class="add-slot-ghost … watercolor-swatch" data-variant="ghost" style="…pointer-events: none…">`. defects.defect: The `mode="out-in"` transitions defer the ghost well past the measurement window on EVERY re-mix. `MixPane.vue:111` and the nested `MixResultDisplay.vue:60` are both `<Transition mode="out-in">`; on a re-mix at phase `done` the plate's content branch must finish leaving before the well branch can mount, so the `flush:"post"` watcher (useMixingAnimation.ts:171-183) measures a DOM that has no well. Its own comment — "the ghost well mounts in the same reactive flush that opens the mixing window" — is true only for the first mix.

The dock action bar's "Copy result" (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222 → MixPane.copyResult) takes the unconfirmed path and no-ops silently when mixResult is null, while remaining enabled in the action bar.
defects.mechanism: two idioms for one capability, split across a parent/child boundary, with the dock-dispatched path getting the weaker one
defects.reproduction: NONE (code read; the duplicate expression and the two import sites are directly citable).
defects.proposedCure: One clipboard idiom (useClipboard), lifted into useMixingState beside mixResult so the plate button and the dock action share one status; and one `resultToText(result)` helper so the serialisation exists once.

defects.defect: Dead import, and BOTH hygiene gates are vacuous on it. `MixPane.vue:2` imports `computed`, which is never used.
defects.evidence: `grep -n computed demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue` → line 2 only (the sole occurrence in the file). `npx eslint demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue ; echo EXIT=$?` → EXIT=0, no output — eslint.config.js disables @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars and vue/no-unused-vars by design. `grep -n noUnused tsconfig.base.json` → no match; the file sets only strict:true and verbatimModuleSyntax:true.
defects.mechanism: vacuous hygiene gate — the two mechanisms that would catch a dead import are both switched off by policy
defects.reproduction: npx eslint demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue  (exits 0 with the dead import present).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the import. Separately: enable noUnusedLocals for the demo program, or re-enable no-unused-vars with an argsIgnorePattern — the current config was written as a smoke gate with tightening explicitly deferred, and this is the deferral coming due.

defects.defect: The result is never invalidated when its inputs change. useMixingState.ts contains no watcher over colorSpace, hueMethod, leftoverStrategy, selectedColors or selectedPalettes; only clearSelection (:113-117) calls reset().
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts — the file's only `watch` is none; removeColor (:59-61) and removePalette (:70-72) mutate the operands without touching mixResult or animationPhase, and the four config refs (:44-46) are never observed. After a settle the plate keeps displaying, unlabelled, a mix of operands that may no longer be selected, beside controls that now describe a different computation.
defects.mechanism: derived display state with no invalidation edge from its inputs — a stale-read class expressed at the state-machine level rather than at defineModel
defects.reproduction: NONE (code read; reproducible by hand: mix 3 colours, remove 2, change the space — the plate is unchanged. Not driven in-browser because the colours-mode add path is dead per C-2).
defects.proposedCure: Either invalidate (`watch([colorSpace,hueMethod,selectedColors,selectedPalettes], reset)`) or stamp provenance on the result so the plate can say what it is a mix OF. Silence is the one option that is wrong.

defects.defect: The canvas backing store is retained for the pane's lifetime. `clearCanvas()` (useMixingAnimation.ts:160-167) clears pixels and resets style.height but never resets canvas.width/canvas.height.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:141-143 sets canvas.width = w*dpr, canvas.height = h*dpr with dpr = Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2); measured pane 510×770 CSS px → at dpr 2 that is 1020×1540×4 B ≈ 6.3 MB held after the mix ends. clearCanvas (:160-167) touches only style.height.
defects.mechanism: unbounded-ish retention — an allocation sized to the scroll extent, freed only on unmount
defects.reproduction: NONE (arithmetic from the measured pane dimensions in WBMIXPANE-C-probe2.mjs: cssW 510, cssH 770; dpr capped at 2).
defects.proposedCure: Set canvas.width = 0 in clearCanvas — one line, releases the backing store on the idle edge the composable already has.

defects.defect: VACUOUS GATE. Unit coverage of MixPane.vue, useMixingState.ts, mixStage.ts and useMixingAnimation.ts is ZERO. The only mix-named vitest file, test/mix-v4.test.ts, exercises mixColorSequence in demo/palettes/mix.ts — library maths, not this pane. The two e2e specs that touch the pane are currently RED and would not have caught C-3 or C-4 even when green.
defects.evidence: `npx vitest run test/mix-v4.test.ts` → "✓ test/mix-v4.test.ts (3 tests) 3ms / Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 3 passed (3)". Mutations that keep all 3 green: delete MixPane.vue entirely; delete the <MixAnimationCanvas> element (MixPane.vue:67-73); make settleMix() a no-op (useMixingState.ts:104-106) so the plate is ghosted forever; make startMix() never set animationPhase (:100); drop @save/@reset (:116-117); swap the result type between "color" and "palette". e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:52-55 asserts only that [data-mix-target] is VISIBLE — never that pigment lands on it; neither spec performs a second mix, so C-4 is uncovered by construction. Both specs are RED at HEAD (see C-2).
defects.mechanism: gates that test the library beneath the component and the existence of the component's markers, but never the component's behaviour or its animation's outcome
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run test/mix-v4.test.ts  (3 passed) — then apply any mutation in the list above and re-run: still 3 passed.
defects.proposedCure: Add a canvas-pixel landing oracle to the e2e leg: after MIX_CONVERGE_MS, the brightest-alpha pixel of the mix canvas must lie within r of the well's measured layout centre. That single assertion kills C-3, C-4 and C-5 permanently and costs ~40 lines (the probe in evidence/challenge-C/WBMIXPANE-C-probe2.mjs is the implementation). Add a vitest suite over useMixingState's phase machine (idle→mixing→done, the re-entry guard, reset, and the error variant C-1 introduces).

result.axis: design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context), model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` — the tier declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — glass-ui 7.0.0 ships `InstrumentChassis`, the exact housing contract the tranche canon names as Mix's outer housing, carrying the exact `proportion: "golden"|"preview-dominant"`, `boundaries`, `reserve`, `state: "ready"|"active"|"complete"|"loading"` vocabulary the canon specifies plus `stage`/`inspector`/`action` slots — and `grep -rn "InstrumentChassis" demo/` returns nothing. MixPane instead hand-rolls the generic pane shell (`MixPane.vue:61-62`, byte-identical to `GeneratePane.vue:30-31` and `GradientPane.vue:19-20`): a `Card tier="resting"` with `box-shadow: color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.8) 8px 8px 0px 0px` in a scene measured at an exact 512/512 equal split (49.14% each), where `OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:43` requires "P122 golden: rack 61.8033989%; result/method/provenance 38.1966011% … Landmark-neutral chassis; no shadow Card/local grid". Every other composition-level defect in the register — 40.8% dead default plate, no failure arm, no provenance inspector, no status region, no invitation tray — is a consequence of that one refusal, because the declined chassis is the exact shape of each missing thing.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but five things are, and are recorded as D-27 so no later seat re-litigates them: (1) reduced motion is correct for an unusual and well-documented reason — `useMixingAnimation.ts:113` sets `respectReducedMotion:false` on the RAF host deliberately, because that loop carries the phase machine's only forward edge and a paused loop would strand the mix, with `arm()` at :120-125 owning a PRM fast-path; measured settle 20ms under reducedMotion:"reduce" vs 942ms normally. (2) The `vj-morph` transition keys the correct family per `animations.css:70-74`, is neutralised by the global PRM guard at `animations.css:184-194`, and animates no layout property (no `--vj-morph-collapse/-expanded` set, so max-height resolves to `none`). (3) The convergence canvas geometry is right: `useMixingAnimation.ts:135-145` sizes to `parent.scrollHeight` and DPR-caps at 2 so a below-fold target is reachable; canvas is aria-hidden + pointer-events:none; measured 510x683 tracking card 512x684.73. (4) The one-clock law holds — `useMixingState.ts` owns no timers, the only forward edge is the canvas `onSettled` (:104-106) with a re-entry guard at :83; measured phase "mixing" at t+300ms then "done". (5) `writeClipboard` is a live glass-ui 7.0.0 export (`dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:37`), not dead API — D-8 is a dual-path defect, not a broken import. The mid-convergence frame (`frames/D-mixing-ghost.png`) is genuinely good design delivered.

defects.defect: The composition root declined the housing contract the design system ships for it. MixPane hard-codes the generic pane shell (Card + one flex column) where the binding canon requires Mix's own InstrumentChassis composition with a golden 61.8/38.2 internal split, landmark-neutral chassis and no shadow Card. The producer ships InstrumentChassis in glass-ui 7.0.0 with exactly the proportion/boundaries/reserve/state vocabulary the canon names; the demo has zero consumers.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:61-62 `<div class="relative w-full mx-auto h-full min-w-0"><Card tier="resting" class="relative pane-scroll-fade w-full overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden min-w-0 h-full">` — byte-identical to GeneratePane.vue:30-31 and GradientPane.vue:19-20. `$ ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | grep -i chassis` → instrument-chassis.d.ts, instrument-chassis.js. `$ grep -rn "InstrumentChassis" demo/` → (no output). Producer types: `InstrumentChassisState = "ready"|"active"|"complete"|"loading"`, `InstrumentChassisProportion = "golden"|"preview-dominant"`, `InstrumentChassisBoundary = "stage-inspector"|"inspector-action"`, `InstrumentChassisReserve = "none"|"stage"|"inspector"|"both"`, slots stage/inspector/action. Measured scene: pane-wrapper--left w 512, pane-wrapper--right w 512 inside pane-container--dual w 1042 = 49.14% each; mixShareOfMain 36.364%. Computed box-shadow `color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.8) 8px 8px 0px 0px`. Canon: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:43 and :77; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:29,47; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:66-67.
defects.mechanism: Composition root reuses the generic pane shell instead of the instrument housing, so no canon proportion / region / boundary / state vocabulary is expressible at this site.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "InstrumentChassis" demo/` → empty; `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | grep chassis` → two files. Load /#/mix at 1440x900 and measure the two pane wrappers: 512 and 512.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: compose `InstrumentChassis proportion="golden" :boundaries="[]" reserve="none" :state="chassisState"` with #stage = the operand rack, #inspector = result + method + provenance, #action = the commit set; map idle→ready, mixing→active, done→complete and land the new failure/pending arms on `loading`. This single move dissolves D-2, D-4, D-5, D-6, D-9, D-11, D-15, D-16 and D-25 structurally rather than patching each.

defects.defect: The commit verb can throw and the design has no failure arm — a thrown mix leaves the UI byte-identical to idle. AnimationPhase is idle|mixing|done, MixResult has no error member, and startMix calls throwing library code with no catch and no error surface anywhere in the pane.
defects.evidence: useMixingState.ts:38 `export type AnimationPhase = "idle" | "mixing" | "done";`; :32-36 MixResult has only {type, css?, colors?}; :85-98 startMix calls parseColorIn + mixColorSequence with no try. demo/palettes/mix.ts:28-36 `mixedOrThrow` throws by construction, :45-54 throws on four more input classes. Measured (evidence/challenge-D/D-edge.mjs §C): `{"thrown":{"threw":true,"msg":"Invalid CSS color"},"after":{"plate":false,"anyErrorSurface":false,"cardText":"Mix | Mix colors and palettes together. | Colors | Palettes | Selected | COLOR SPACE | OKLab | HUE METHOD | Shorter | Mix"}}`. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 — "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."
defects.mechanism: The state enum has three members and the domain has four; the unrepresentable fourth renders as nothing. The throw fires before animationPhase is assigned (:100), so the machine never leaves idle and the canvas never arms.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-pane/evidence/challenge-D/D-edge.mjs — drives addColor("#ff0000"), addColor("definitely-not-a-color"), startMix(); throws `Invalid CSS color`; the rendered card is indistinguishable from a user who has not clicked. Real-world trigger (HYPOTHESIS, not observed): an operand string sourced from the palette API rather than the picker.
defects.proposedCure: Widen the machine to `idle | mixing | done | failed` and give MixResult a discriminated failure arm carrying the library's error code; render it in the chassis #inspector at state="loading"→failed alongside the D-6 status region. Do not wrap the call in a swallowing try/catch.

defects.defect: The result is never invalidated. Changing the colour space, the hue method, removing an operand or switching source mode all leave the previous result on screen, enabled, copyable and saveable — a value the visible configuration does not produce.
defects.evidence: useMixingState.ts imports only `{ ref, computed }` — there is no `watch` in the file; nothing invalidates mixResult. MixPane.vue:111-119 renders on `v-if="mixResult"` alone. Measured (evidence/challenge-D/D-stale.mjs): after mix → `RESULT | oklab(63.526245979824% 0.065915559829 -0.028691150076)`; set space→oklch, hue→longer (triggers now read "OKLCh"/"Longer") → plate text UNCHANGED; re-mix with the same operands → `oklch(63.526245979824% 0.184955540821 127.453572934423deg)`, proving the config genuinely changes the answer; removeColor(0) → chips 1, mixDisabled true, plate still shows the 2-operand result; mode→palettes → chips 0, plate still shows the colors-mode result.
defects.mechanism: The result is a ref snapshot with no dependency on the inputs that produced it; the design has no stale state, so staleness renders as currency. MixResultDisplay.vue:42-47 will copy it and MixPane.vue:38-47 will persist it.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-pane/evidence/challenge-D/D-stale.mjs (uses the proxyRefs write-through form `setupState.colorSpace = "oklch"`, not `.value =`, which is silently discarded).
defects.proposedCure: Make the result a function of a captured input tuple: either derive it over {operands, space, hueMethod, leftoverStrategy} with the animation window as a separate presentation concern, or stamp the result with the tuple it was computed from, compare every render, and drop the chassis to state="ready" with the plate marked stale the instant they diverge. The provenance datum of D-11 is the comparison key — the two rows are one fix.

defects.defect: 40.8% of the default plate is dead acreage, in the state every visitor lands on. The canon caps empty secondary content at 15% of the stage and forbids filler when operands are absent.
defects.evidence: Measured at 1440x900 (evidence/challenge-D/D-geometry.mjs): mixCard h 684.73 bottom 832.73; content column bottom 553.16 → dead band 279.57 px = 40.8%. Below the last ink (Mix button bottom 537.16) = 295.57 px = 43.2%. Shrinks only under load: 2 operands 272.4 px (39.8%); 2 operands + result 97.7 px (14.3%); 12 operands + result 32.5 px (4.7%). Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 "Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears"; :203 "No shadow palette filler appears when an operand is absent"; :47 "absent operands occupy no filler"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04 "Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE".
defects.mechanism: Fixed-height housing (`h-full` on both wrapper and Card, MixPane.vue:61-62) + top-aligned content (:78 `flex flex-col gap-4`) + a terminal region that does not exist until after a mix.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 1440x900; `card.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - contentColumn.getBoundingClientRect().bottom` = 279.57.
defects.proposedCure: Under D-1 the chassis content-hugs when #inspector is absent; the rack's empty state becomes a real invitation tray (D-5) rather than a fixed-height well floating inside a fixed-height card.

defects.defect: The empty state never states its requirement and cannot be left by keyboard. The pane's entire text content is ten fragments, none of which says a mix needs ≥2 colours or how to add one, and no add-operand control is keyboard-reachable.
defects.evidence: Measured full card text in the default state: `Mix | Mix colors and palettes together. | Colors | Palettes | Selected | COLOR SPACE | OKLab | HUE METHOD | Shorter | Mix`. Measured focusables inside the Mix card (evidence/challenge-D/D-composition.mjs): Colors, Palettes, Color space, Hue method, Mix(disabled) — five, with no add control; the disabled commit is out of the tab order. The ≥2 rule lives at useMixingState.ts:50-53 and is never surfaced. Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 "Add affordance when the surviving action/state is otherwise undiscoverable"; PR-07 "every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state".
defects.mechanism: The empty state was styled but never written: a well with a label and a ghost, no copy, no instruction, no keyboard path out. (The add control's own dead-API defect is owned by the wb-mix-sourceselector seat; the pane-level consequence — a keyboard dead end with no explanatory copy — is this row.)
defects.reproduction: Load /#/mix, press Tab repeatedly: four controls, then focus leaves the pane. Nothing in the pane states the requirement.
defects.proposedCure: An invitation tray in the chassis #stage naming the requirement and carrying the add action as a real named <button>, plus aria-describedby on the commit pointing at that requirement so the disabled state explains itself.

defects.defect: The mix command's result is announced to nobody. There is no live region, status or alert anywhere in the pane, and the only feedback channel is an aria-hidden decorative canvas.
defects.evidence: Measured `liveRegions: []` across the whole Mix card in both empty and populated states (evidence/challenge-D/D-composition.mjs). `$ grep -rn "aria-live|role=\"status\"|role=\"alert\"" demo/workbenches/mix/` → NONE FOUND. MixAnimationCanvas.vue:33 is `aria-hidden="true"`. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:114 — a successful command must yield "one durable operation result"; §5 — "Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace. A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth."
defects.mechanism: The convergence animation is the design's only completion signal, and it is explicitly hidden from assistive technology, so the settle event has no non-visual expression.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-composition.mjs — the probe queries `[aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert]` inside the Mix card in every state and returns [].
defects.proposedCure: One polite status region owned by the chassis #inspector, announcing the settled result value and operand count. It is the same surface D-2's failure text and D-3's stale marker need — three rows collapse into one region.

defects.defect: Save is silent, always mints an identically-named palette, and discards the Palette its own port returns. Copy in the same action row has a designed confirmation; the persistent command has none.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:38-47 calls `pm.createPalette("Mixed Color", colors)` / `pm.createPalette("Mixed Palette", …)` with hard-coded names and discards the return. Signature: `createPalette: (name: string, colors: PaletteColor[]) => Palette` (demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:14). Measured (evidence/challenge-D/D-dark.mjs): three consecutive clicks on `Save to palettes` → `anyConfirmation: false`, pane text unchanged, three indistinguishable palettes named `Mixed Color`. Contrast MixResultDisplay.vue:31-32 where Copy uses `useClipboard({resetMs:1500})` and swaps to a Check icon. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104.
defects.mechanism: The composition root treats a persistence command as fire-and-forget: no name derivation, no returned identity, no confirmation register — while the cheaper sibling command in the same row has all three.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-dark.mjs — clicks Save three times and reports anyConfirmation:false.
defects.proposedCure: Name the artefact from its provenance tuple (the same datum D-11 and D-3 need), surface the returned Palette identity through the D-6 status region, and give Save the confirmation register Copy already has.

defects.defect: Two Copy implementations for one user gesture, with divergent feedback, and the producer's discriminated failure result is thrown away by the path that has no feedback at all.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:12 imports `writeClipboard`; :49-55 `await writeClipboard(text);` — the CopyResult is discarded — and usePaneRouter.ts:222 routes the dock's `Copy result` to it. MixResultDisplay.vue:31,42-47 uses `useClipboard({resetMs:1500})` with a status-driven Check icon. Producer docstring, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:31-37: "Stateless one-shot clipboard write — the honest primitive shared by useClipboard and by consumers that own their own feedback. Returns the discriminated result ({ ok } / { ok, reason }) rather than a lossy boolean." Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-13 precedent: "Picker specimen and action region both host Copy → REMOVE … total 2→1." Owner edict 2 (no dual paths).
defects.mechanism: The same verb is declared twice at two altitudes, and the declaration that owns no feedback consumes the primitive that assumes the caller owns feedback.
defects.reproduction: Read MixPane.vue:49-55 against MixResultDisplay.vue:42-47; the dock path returns no signal on a rejected clipboard write while the in-plate path confirms.
defects.proposedCure: One Copy owner: MixPane exposes the plate's reactive `copy`; the dock action calls it. Delete the writeClipboard import and the second implementation.

defects.defect: The dock's Mix and Copy-result actions are permanently enabled and are silent no-ops when the pane cannot service them, while the in-pane twin of the same verb is correctly gated.
defects.evidence: usePaneRouter.ts:220-222 registers clear/mix/copy for the mix view and never sets `disabled`. `DockAction.disabled?: boolean` exists at usePaneRouter.ts:45 and is bound through GenericActionBar.vue:27 → ActionButton `:disabled`. In-pane the same verb IS gated: MixConfigBar.vue:164 `:disabled="!canMix"`. Pressing the dock Mix with <2 operands returns at useMixingState.ts:80; pressing Copy result with no result returns at MixPane.vue:50.
defects.mechanism: MixPane exposes clearSelection/startMix/copyResult but not canMix or hasResult, so the route table has no state to gate on and declines to gate — producing two controls for one verb with contradictory disabled semantics.
defects.reproduction: Read usePaneRouter.ts:220-222 (no `disabled` key) against usePaneRouter.ts:45 and GenericActionBar.vue:27 (the prop exists and is bound). Load /#/mix with an empty rack and invoke the dock Mix action: nothing happens, no signal.
defects.proposedCure: Under D-1 the commit set lives once in the chassis #action region and the dock mirrors it rather than re-declaring it. Minimum: MixPane exposes canMix/hasResult and the route table gates on them.

defects.defect: The canon's ordered N-operand rack has no reorder, though the rendered order is an input to the answer and the canon specifies the exact keyboard contract for it.
defects.evidence: `$ grep -rn "reorder" demo/workbenches/mix/` → NONE FOUND. useMixingState.ts:119-137 returns addColor/removeColor/addPalette/removePalette only; MixSourceSelector.vue:25-31 emits the same five; MixPane.vue:85-89 wires exactly those. The concept exists next door: `reorderPalettes` at usePalettePorts.ts:62. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:200 "An ordered N-operand rack … add/remove/reorder"; :132 (§5.2) gives the full contract: "horizontal explicit reorder: palette colors, operands, stops — after Space grabs, Right moves one visual position right … Home=first ordinal, End=last; every move announces item and `position of total`; Space drops, Escape cancels." Order is load-bearing: demo/palettes/mix.ts:56-64 is a sequential pairwise fold.
defects.mechanism: The composition root presents an ordered rack, makes the order materially affect the result, and provides no affordance to change it.
defects.reproduction: grep as above; then observe the 12-operand rack (frames/D-12operands.png) — twelve chips in fixed insertion order with no grab, drag or arrow affordance.
defects.proposedCure: Add `reorderColor(from, to)` to the state machine, implement §5.2's grab/move/drop keyboard contract on the rack seats, and announce the resulting ordinal through the D-6 status region.

defects.defect: The result inspector receives no provenance. MixPane passes only the result object, so the plate cannot say what was mixed, in what space, along which arc, or from where the operands came — although the state machine already captures operand source.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:112-118 passes `:result` and `:ghost` only — not colorSpace, hueMethod, leftoverStrategy, operands or their source. useMixingState.ts:25-28 captures `SelectedColor { css, source }` ("palette name or 'picker'") and MixPane routes it only to the rack. Rendered plate content, measured: `RESULT | oklab(63.526245979824% 0.065915559829 -0.028691150076)` plus one dot and three icons. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:47 — Mix support region is the "result/provenance inspector"; OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:43 regions "result; method/provenance/commit", W26 close condition "Close modes, 2/3/12/unequal inputs/order/provenance"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08.
defects.mechanism: Ownership inverted at the composition root: the pane holds every provenance datum and forwards none of it to the region the canon designates as the provenance inspector.
defects.reproduction: Read MixPane.vue:112-118; then inspect the rendered .mix-plate innerText in any populated state — it contains the word RESULT and one CSS string, nothing else.
defects.proposedCure: Route the captured input tuple into the chassis #inspector as the provenance line. The same tuple is D-3's staleness comparison key and D-7's save-name source — one datum closes three rows.

defects.defect: The library supports weighted mixing and the design exposes none, so every mix is an unbiasable equal-weight mean that reliably desaturates with no lever and no warning.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/mix.ts:43 `mixColorSequence(colors, space, hueMethod, weights = colors.map(() => 1))`; :25 `PaletteMixOptions.weights?: number[]`; both threaded, validated at :48-54 and honoured. `$ grep -rn "weight" demo/workbenches/mix/` → NO WEIGHTS IN MIX UI. useMixingState.ts:89,92-96 never passes weights. Measured consequence: twelve evenly-spaced hues → `oklab(70% 0 0)` — pure grey (frames/D-12operands-result.png); red + sky + amber → dusty mauve (frames/D-dark-result.png). Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:105 already mandates the domain-neutral axis composition over BI Slider for "Picker, Generate count, Extract, Gradient, Atmosphere and Blob" — Mix is the missing adopter; :200 requires the rack remain "legible at 2, 3 and 12 colors".
defects.mechanism: A first-class library capability has no representation at the composition root, so the instrument's headline operation is a mean the user cannot bias.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-states.mjs — seeds twelve oklch hues at 30° spacing and mixes; the plate reads `oklab(70% 0 0)`.
defects.proposedCure: A per-operand weight on the rack seat, built from the shared Slider composition the canon already mandates, feeding the `weights` argument that already exists.

defects.defect: In the light scheme the pane's only add affordance has a 1.52:1 boundary contrast — WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 — while the identical element measures 4.44:1 in dark. A 2.9x legibility swing between schemes for the same token.
defects.evidence: Composited pixel measurement (evidence/challenge-D/D-contrast.mjs — the screenshot is decoded in-page to a canvas and the modal colour of each element box taken). Light: dash ink rgb(255,143,200) against well plate rgb(236,215,215) → 1.52:1. Dark: rgb(255,143,200) against rgb(89,65,65) → 4.44:1. Visible in audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png where the dashed circle all but vanishes. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:81 — "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."
defects.mechanism: A single tinted dash token is used against two very different plate luminances without a per-scheme boundary rung, so one scheme passes and the other fails.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-contrast.mjs — prints ghost modal/darkest/lightest and the contrast pair for both schemes.
defects.proposedCure: Give the affordance boundary its own certified per-scheme rung at ≥3:1 on the composited well, not a single tint. Element attribution is MixSourceSelector's .add-slot-ghost; filed at pane level because it is the pane's sole exit from the empty state.

defects.defect: The dark specimen well is not neutral — it composites to a warm brown with 34% relative channel spread, so the stage carries seed tint the canon forbids outside the ambient field.
defects.evidence: Composited modal pixel of the Selected well (91.4% of its pixels): dark `rgb(66,55,47)` — channel spread 19 on a mean of 56; light `rgb(233,225,217)`. Card token computed `oklab(0.395241 0.00968 0.016528 / 0.7536)` — chroma 0.0191 at alpha 0.75 over a chromatic ambient field. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19 — specimen well is an "opaque/quiet neutral stage; the specimen supplies color"; :23 — "Dark chrome uses the restrained neutral pole. Seed tint is forbidden outside the ambient field, active accent, WatercolorDot/specimen, and pastel Palettes lanes."
defects.mechanism: The well is an alpha veil over the seeded ambient field rather than an opaque neutral plate, so the seed reads straight through and the stage cannot let the specimen supply the colour.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-contrast.mjs with colorScheme dark; see also frames/D-dark-result.png where the whole right plate reads rose-brown.
defects.proposedCure: Raise the well to an opaque neutral at the dark pole rather than an alpha veil; the material-tier decision belongs to the chassis (D-1) via reserve/tone, not to a per-instance background.

defects.defect: At 200% zoom the pane's primary action is below the fold on first paint, and the card itself no longer scrolls — the document does.

Independently corroborated by the prior seat's shots/desktop-zoom200.png where the Mix button is clipped by the viewport edge — two methods agree. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:31.
defects.mechanism: The commit is the terminal element of a fixed-height column that grows past the viewport under zoom; nothing in the design keeps it reachable or promotes it.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-edge.mjs §B; or open /#/mix and set browser zoom to 200%.
defects.proposedCure: Under D-1 the #action region is a distinct chassis region that can stay reachable independently of #stage/#inspector overflow.

defects.defect: One glyph, two meanings: the rack's add-slot ghost and the result plate's convergence-landing well are both pink dashed organic circles of similar size, on screen simultaneously during the mix.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:65-73 renders the awaiting well as `WatercolorDot variant="ghost" seed="mix-result"`; MixSourceSelector renders the add slot as `.add-slot-ghost`. Measured 56 px and 48 px. Both visible together in frames/D-mixing-ghost.png at (908, 372) and (798, 632), 260 px apart, meaning "put a colour here" and "a colour will land here". Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 (§5 law 5) — "A small icon/mark is either data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus/selection register or removed."
defects.mechanism: Two different semantic registers (action affordance vs operation status) were given one form, differentiated only by size.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-states.mjs; inspect frames/D-mixing-ghost.png.
defects.proposedCure: The destination ghost is status and belongs to the chassis #inspector's state (state="active"), not to a repeated add-affordance silhouette. Differentiate by register, not by size.

defects.defect: The disabled commit is expressed by a single global opacity multiplier at roughly 3:1 composited contrast, with no non-colour channel and no explanation of the requirement it fails.
defects.evidence: Computed `opacity: 0.5` on the button. Composited best-case ink/plate contrast measured with the darkest (light) and lightest (dark) pixel in the button box: 3.12:1 light (rgb(134,107,112) on rgb(237,198,205)); 2.93:1 dark (rgb(176,157,156) on rgb(108,76,79)) — the mean ink is worse. No icon change, no label change, no aria-describedby. WCAG exempts disabled controls from 1.4.3, so this is a canon failure not an SC failure: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 "disabled states are never color-only".
defects.mechanism: Disabled is rendered as a presentation multiplier rather than a designed state with its own explanatory channel.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-contrast.mjs — prints the mix button modal/darkest/lightest and contrast pair for both schemes.
defects.proposedCure: Pair the visual de-emphasis with an aria-describedby pointing at the D-5 requirement copy, so the state names its own precondition rather than only dimming.

defects.defect: The result readout carries twelve decimal places, is broken mid-number across lines by break-all, and reflows the plate between one and two lines as the value changes.
defects.evidence: Rendered: `oklab(63.526245979824% 0.065915559829 -0.028691150076)` — 51 characters — wrapped by `class="text-mono-small text-foreground select-all break-all"` (MixResultDisplay.vue:85), splitting inside a number: `0.0659155598` / `29` in frames/D-result-2.png and `0.0626436033` / `24` in frames/D-dark-result.png. The plate is one line for `oklab(70% 0 0)` and two for the general case. OKLCh case: `127.453572934423deg`. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:77 — "Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis."
defects.mechanism: An unrounded library serialisation is rendered directly as display copy with a character-level break rule, so a numeric token can split and the chassis reflows on value change.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-states.mjs; read the plateText field and frames/D-result-2.png.
defects.proposedCure: Round to a display precision at the presentation boundary, use `break-word`/`overflow-wrap` rather than `break-all` so tokens stay intact, and reserve the widest legal representation so the plate height is invariant.

defects.defect: Two focus vocabularies inside one four-control stack: the mode tabs use the UA outline ring while the selects suppress the outline and draw a glass-ui box-shadow ring.
defects.evidence: Measured focus walk (evidence/challenge-D/D-a11y.mjs), light: Colors/Palettes → `outline: auto 3px rgb(28,25,23)`, boxShadow none; Color space/Hue method → `outline: none`, boxShadow `color(srgb 0.665034 0 0.261497 / 0.3) 0px 0px 0px 2px …`. Same split in dark (rgb(233,230,226) / color(srgb 1 0.924654 0.933001 / 0.3)). Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83.
defects.mechanism: Adjacent rows of one instrument consume two different focus registers because they come from two different producer families and the composition root never reconciled them.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-a11y.mjs — focuses each control in turn and prints computed outline and box-shadow.
defects.proposedCure: One focus register across the instrument, decided at the producer root, not per control family.

defects.defect: The mode tabs are the only centred, sub-measure row in a vertical argument that is otherwise full-bleed — a rhythm break visible in every capture.
defects.evidence: Measured row table (evidence/challenge-D/D-stale.mjs, D-edge.mjs): title ink 754→1216 (462 wide), Selected well 754→1216, Mix button 754→1216, selects 754→981 and 989→1216; mode-tabs pill 903.9→1066.1 = 162.2 px of ink in a 462 px measure, centred at 985. Visible in every /#/mix frame.
defects.mechanism: The segmented control's box is full width but its ink is centre-justified, so one row of five reads as a different alignment system.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-stale.mjs — prints the tab ink measurement {group, colors, palettes}.
defects.proposedCure: Resolve the mode selector to the same measure as the rows it governs, or move it into the chassis #stage header where a different alignment is earned.

defects.defect: Three control heights inside one stack — 39 / 36 / 40 px — produced by per-instance height overrides on producer roots.
defects.evidence: SegmentedTabs measures 39 px; MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147 hard-code `class="h-9"` on SelectTrigger (36 px); :165 hard-codes `class="h-10"` on the commit Button (40 px). Owner edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides); canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:36 "Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens. No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile."
defects.mechanism: Control rungs are set per call site rather than inherited from one producer scale, so adjacent rows land within 4 px of each other — read as jitter, not a ladder.
defects.reproduction: Read MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147,165; measure the three control boxes at 1440x900.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the per-instance h-9/h-10 and consume one producer control rung at the root. Element attribution is MixConfigBar; filed here as the composed rhythm the pane is responsible for.

defects.defect: The convergence canvas sits above the live controls and smears them for the duration of the mix window.
defects.evidence: MixAnimationCanvas.vue:32 `class="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full pointer-events-none z-controls"` → computed `z-index: 20`. Visible in frames/D-mixing-ghost.png: the red drop passes over and obscures the `COLOR SPACE` label and the `OKLab` select trigger for the ~900 ms window. Interactivity is preserved (pointer-events:none); legibility is not.
defects.mechanism: A decorative overlay was placed at the controls layer rather than beneath it, so its flight path crosses labelled interactive copy.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-states.mjs — screenshots at t+300 ms into the mix; see frames/D-mixing-ghost.png.
defects.proposedCure: Route the convergence beneath the control layer, or confine its path to the chassis #stage→#inspector corridor so it never crosses a labelled control.

defects.defect: In RTL the pane description's terminal period migrates to the visual left, rendering `.Mix colors and palettes together`.
defects.evidence: shots/desktop-rtl.png renders the caption as `.Mix colors and palettes together`. The copy is hard-coded LTR English at MixPane.vue:75 (`description="Mix colors and palettes together."`); in an RTL container the trailing neutral takes the paragraph direction. Everything else in RTL is correct: pane order swaps, tab order reverses, label/value pairing survives, the commit icon mirrors. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 (§6.1) isolates strings/hex/slugs/IDs but is silent on un-localised UI prose; the app ships no i18n.
defects.mechanism: Un-localised English prose is emitted into a container whose direction follows the document, with no bidi isolation.
defects.reproduction: Open shots/desktop-rtl.png, or load /#/mix with dir=rtl on documentElement.
defects.proposedCure: Either dir="ltr" / unicode-bidi: isolate on un-localised copy at the PaneHeader root — one edit, all nine panes inherit — or declare RTL out of scope in the canon. The current state is neither.

defects.defect: A dead value import ships in the component and the lint gate reports the file clean; the outer wrapper also duplicates a `relative` the Card already needs.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:2 `import { inject, computed } from "vue";` — `$ grep -n computed demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue` returns line 2 only. `$ npx eslint demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue -f json` → `[{"filePath":"…/MixPane.vue","messages":[],"errorCount":0,"warningCount":0,…}]`, exit 0. MixPane.vue:61-62 puts `relative` on both the wrapper and the Card; only the Card needs it (it is the canvas's containing block).
defects.mechanism: The project's lint configuration does not detect an unused value import inside an SFC `<script setup>` block, so dead imports accumulate under a green gate.
defects.reproduction: npx eslint demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue -f json
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead import and the redundant `relative`; separately, enable an unused-import rule that reaches `<script setup>` so the gate can see this class of defect.

defects.defect: The pane opts into a scroll-driven header grammar that can never fire at desktop — its scroll extent equals its client height in every state including maximum load.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:62 carries `pane-scroll-fade` + `overflow-y-auto`; PaneHeader.vue:54-57 builds the named `--pane-scroll` timeline on that class and :177-194 drives the veil swell and title shrink from it. Measured: `scrollHeight === clientHeight === 683` at empty, 2 operands, 2 operands + result, and 12 operands + result. Under zoom the card still does not scroll (772 === 772) — the document does (D-15).
defects.mechanism: A shared shell grammar built for a taller content profile is inherited by a pane whose content never exceeds its fixed height, so the most elaborately reasoned block in PaneHeader is inert here.
defects.reproduction: node evidence/challenge-D/D-geometry.mjs and D-states.mjs — both report scroll {scrollHeight: 683, clientHeight: 683} in every state.
defects.proposedCure: Under D-1 the chassis owns its own scroll-confinement decision per region; the pane should not inherit a scroll timeline it cannot drive.

defects.defect: `/#/mix` is absent from every state matrix in the mega-tranche visual audit, and two of the prior seat's substitute captures are mislabelled — forced-colors for this component remains uncaptured by any seat.
defects.evidence: `$ ls audit/visual/shots/{forced-colors,keyboard-focus,reduced-motion,rtl,zoom-200}-desktop/` → adminusers.png, blob.png, browse.png, gradient.png, picker.png in all five directories; Mix in none. The prior wb-mix-pane seat's shots/desktop-forced-colors.png still shows the full chromatic ambient field, so WebKit's forcedColors:"active" did not take. Its shots/desktop-twelve-operands.png shows the EMPTY pane, because seeding was blocked by wb-mix-sourceselector D-1; this seat's frames/D-12operands*.png are the first true twelve-operand renders.
