result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface, modularization
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — `parseCssColor`'s published type `ParseResult<CssColor>` promises totality but the function THROWS (`src/css/grammar.ts:181`, a false `!` non-null assertion on an empty `splitTopLevel` result). The demo's 302-line `gradientParse.ts` is architected explicitly on that contract ("the LIBRARY's own parsers — the validity oracles"). Live consequence, measured headless at localhost:9000: typing `linear-gradient(90deg, red, oklch())` into GradientCodeEditor destroys the ENTIRE application — both panes including the unrelated My Palettes (h3 census 'Gradient|Interpolation|Easing|CSS|My Palettes' → ''; bodyTextLen 649 → 142) — with ZERO console/pageerror/window.onerror output, because the app-root ErrorBoundary (App.vue:50) swallows it (ErrorBoundary.vue:68 `return false`). "Try again" restores the DEFAULT gradient, discarding the user's authored text and falsifying the component's own docblock invariant "WIP is never destroyed" (GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40).
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the finding set is not read as "everything is wrong" — the subject's OWN import discipline is sound, proven positively: (1) `GradientCodeEditor.vue` imports only `vue`, one demo utility, and `highlight.js` — nothing from `@mkbabb/value.js`, nothing from shell or boot; it reaches the parser only by emitting upward (:27-29 → GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108). No feature→shell edge, no component→boot edge. (2) `grep -rn "@src/|from \"../../../src|from \"../../src" demo/` → 0 hits; `grep -rn "\.\./demo|@demo" src/` → 0 hits — no deep reach, no cycle. (3) All 50 demo imports of the library go through published subpaths (25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize), each present in `package.json#exports`; the single textual bare specifier is inside a comment (demo/shared/utils.ts:12), not an import — so the demo is NOT a false proof of the public API on this axis. (4) The vite self-alias set is GENERATED from the exports map (vite.config.ts:23-32), so the demo cannot resolve an unpublished subpath. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied: the subject's four imports (:2,3,5,6) bind runtime values only; neighbours useGradientModel.ts:11,12,13,17 and GradientVisualizer.vue:22,25,26,28 all use `import type` correctly. (6) Vue 3.5 idiom correct — `useTemplateRef` :31, reactive props destructure with default :16. (7) The NON-throwing rejection path works end to end, measured: `notacolor` → verdict "unparseable color \"notacolor\"", aria-invalid=true, destructive border, user text preserved. (8) audit/visual/REPORT.md:125,140,155,170 — /#/gradient shows overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, main 1 on all four Safari matrices; the L-1 crash is interaction-only and therefore invisible to the static capture sweep, which is itself a recorded gap in the visual audit's reach.

defects.defect: The library's published `parseCssColor(source): ParseResult<CssColor>` is not total — it THROWS TypeError on eight empty-body color functions. The demo's gradient parser is architected on the false totality guarantee, so a mid-typing keystroke wipes the entire application with zero diagnostics and destroys the user's authored text.
defects.evidence: src/css/grammar.ts:257 declares the total signature. src/css/grammar.ts:63-85 `splitTopLevel` drops empty parts (line 79 `if (part) parts.push(part)`, line 85 `if (tail) parts.push(tail)`) ⇒ splitTopLevel("","/") === []. src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` — the `!` is FALSE. tsx repro output pasted verbatim: "oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" all -> THROW: TypeError : Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "oklch(0.7 0.1 145)" -> OK. Demo path: "linear-gradient(90deg, red, rgb())" -> THROW. Premise quoted at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:16-18 ("the LIBRARY's own parsers … the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color") and gradientParse.ts:44-47 ("Model-or-reject … Never a partial"); the oracle throws straight through isColorToken at gradientParse.ts:92-94. Live headless Chromium, localhost:9000/#/gradient — baseline {editorPresent:true, tilePresent:true, h3s:"Gradient|Interpolation|Easing|CSS|My Palettes", bodyTextLen:649}; after typing oklch() {editorPresent:false, tilePresent:false, h3s:"", bodyTextLen:142, uncaught:[]} and LOG:[]. Crash state bodyText: "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev` | This panel hit an unexpected error. | Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') | Try again", palettesGone:true. AFTER 'Try again': editorText reverts to the DEFAULT "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)". Boundary: demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 wraps the WHOLE app; ErrorBoundary.vue:68 `return false` halts propagation so nothing reaches console. Contradicted invariant: GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40 "WIP is never destroyed". Witness live-01-mtf001-oklch-empty.png.
defects.mechanism: unsound public contract — a declared-total Result-returning function that throws; the type system's `!` assertion silenced the very guard that was needed, and a downstream consumer built its architecture on the declared type
defects.reproduction: 1) dev server at localhost:9000. 2) Navigate /#/gradient. 3) Click the "Gradient CSS" editor, select-all, delete. 4) Type `linear-gradient(90deg, red, oklch())`. 5) Wait >500ms (the debounce). The entire app collapses to a bare "Try again" pill; both panes gone; console empty. 6) Click "Try again" — the pane returns with the DEFAULT gradient, the typed text destroyed. Also reproducible headlessly: `npx tsx` importing parseCssColor from src/css/index with input "oklch()".
defects.proposedCure: Make `parseCssColor` total — that is the library's job and its type already claims it: delete the `!` at src/css/grammar.ts:181 and return `failure(source, "css_syntax", ["color components"])` when `splitTopLevel(body, "/")` is empty; then sweep every remaining `!`-on-index in src/css/grammar.ts, since MT-F001 is one instance of a family. Architecturally: transpose the gradient parser into the library (see L-2) so parser totality is a library test rather than a user-facing app wipe. Secondarily make the ErrorBoundary per-pane (App.vue:50) so one workbench fault cannot evict an unrelated pane's state, and stop swallowing the error silently (ErrorBoundary.vue:68) so the crash leaves a telemetry trace.

defects.defect: `parseGradientCSS` — 302 lines of pure, DOM-free, framework-free CSS-Images-L3 grammar — lives in `demo/` instead of `@mkbabb/value.js/css` beside its own companions `parseCssColor`/`parseCssScalar`, and duplicates the library's private top-level splitter twice.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts — 302 lines, zero Vue imports, pure. Its serializer half is likewise in demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts (11,981 bytes) rather than beside serializeCssColor (src/css/grammar.ts:289). Duplicate ownership proven: the library already owns a depth-aware, quote-aware splitter with both char and "space" modes at src/css/grammar.ts:63 `function splitTopLevel(source: string, separator: string | "space"): string[]`, used at grammar.ts:177/181; the demo hand-rolls it twice, quote-unaware, at gradientParse.ts:52-67 (splitTopLevelCommas ≈ splitTopLevel(s,",")) and gradientParse.ts:70-89 (tokenizeTopLevel ≈ splitTopLevel(s,"space")). CSS unit arithmetic (deg/grad/rad/turn) is likewise re-owned at gradientParse.ts:97-108 and percentage at :111-118. Genuine gap noted: gradientParse.ts:210 needs empty segments retained to detect doubled/trailing commas, which the library version drops at line 79 — a missing MODE on the library primitive, not grounds for a second implementation.
defects.mechanism: wrong home / unique-semantic-ownership broken — library-domain pure code hosted in the consumer, producing two private implementations of one concept
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural, not behavioural). Verified by reading and by `grep -n "function splitTopLevel" src/css/grammar.ts` (line 63) against gradientParse.ts:52 and :70.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose: `@mkbabb/value.js/css` gains `parseCssGradient` / `serializeCssGradient`; `splitTopLevel` gains a `keepEmpty` mode and is exported on the subpath. `gradientParse.ts` and the serializer core of `useGradientCSS.ts` delete outright; `useGradientModel.ts` shrinks to ~60 lines of reactive glue. This also gives the gradient grammar the library's test suite, which is the structural fix for L-1's blast radius.

defects.defect: The component wears a retired CSS class, `glass-wash`, that has no definition in the default cascade but IS defined inside `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)` — so a dead class silently changes the editor's appearance only in the accessibility matrix.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:93 `class="hljs ... rounded-lg glass-wash border ..."`. Full-repo census of `.glass-wash`: only demo/styles/foundation.css:775 and :786 (both inside the block opened at foundation.css:764 `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)`), plus GradientStopEditor.vue:282 which records "glass-wash `contain: paint` clip — the R8-17 class — died with…", plus this one live usage. Zero definitions in demo/styles/ outside that media block and zero in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css. foundation.css:786-789 forces `background-color: var(--surface-reduced-opaque, var(--card)) !important` on `.glass-wash`. Measured live via CDP Emulation.setEmulatedMedia — DEFAULT: {"editorBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","editorBackdrop":"none","editorRadius":"8px"}; REDUCED-TRANSPARENCY: {"editorBg":"rgb(253, 245, 236)",...}. Witness live-03-reduced-transparency.png.
defects.mechanism: legacy corpse — a class retired elsewhere in the same directory but still worn by one consumer, whose only surviving definition is in an accessibility media query, making it invisible in the default matrix
defects.reproduction: 1) localhost:9000/#/gradient. 2) Read computed backgroundColor of `[role="textbox"][aria-label="Gradient CSS"]` → `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`. 3) CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia {features:[{name:"prefers-reduced-transparency",value:"reduce"}]}`. 4) Re-read → `rgb(253, 245, 236)`. The sibling `.readout-rail` is unchanged across both, confirming the divergence is the dead class, not the theme.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `glass-wash` from GradientCodeEditor.vue:93 and from foundation.css:775,786. The editor's surface must come from the glass-ui `CodeField` primitive of L-4, which owns its own reduced-transparency behaviour at the design-system root — never as an orphan utility on one instance (edict 5).

defects.defect: MT-F037 family. Two code-literal fields 137px apart in the same pane are hand-rolled two different ways, and the census of installed glass-ui 7.0.0 confirms no primitive fits either one — this is a marked glass-forward ask, not a local restyle.
defects.evidence: Measured live, same paint: easing readout (GradientEasingEditor.vue:176, hand-rolled `div.readout-rail`) radius 6px, bg oklab(0.913295 0.00550478 0.0130424) opaque, border 0px, padding 4px/8px, trailing actions INSIDE the row as two bare `<button class="rail-btn">`. defects.defect: The parse debounce timer is created in setup and never cancelled on unmount, so a pane switch within 500ms of a keystroke leaves a pending emit into a torn-down tree.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-57 `const debouncedParse = debounce((text: string) => { emit("parse", text); }, 500);`. The returned function carries `.cancel()` (demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41) which is never called. All 117 lines of the subject read — there is no `onUnmounted`. The pane is lazily mounted/unmounted on pane switch: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74 `defineAsyncComponent(() => import("../workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue"))`, :87 `if (name === "gradient") return GradientPane;`.
defects.mechanism: lifecycle ownership gap — a timer whose owner has no teardown, in a component the shell mounts and unmounts freely
defects.reproduction: NONE — I did not exercise a mid-keystroke pane switch. LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS. Falsifiable by: type one character into the editor, then switch panes within 500ms, and observe whether the pending emit lands on the unmounted instance.
defects.proposedCure: `onUnmounted(debouncedParse.cancel)` is the patch. The correct cure is deletion: the debounce belongs inside the glass-ui `CodeField` primitive of L-4, whose own lifecycle owns its timers, so the demo leaf has no timer to forget.

defects.defect: `highlight()` swallows any hljs failure and returns the RAW user string, which is then written to `innerHTML` unescaped — a masking fallback sitting on an HTML-injection sink.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:43-49 `function highlight(code: string): string { try { return hljs.highlight(code, { language: "css" }).value; } catch { return code; } }` — the catch arm returns the unescaped input. GradientCodeEditor.vue:51-53 `function render(code: string) { if (editorRef.value) editorRef.value.innerHTML = highlight(code); }`. The SUCCESS path is safe (hljs escapes its output); only the catch arm is raw.
defects.mechanism: masking fallback (edict 2) on an unescaped innerHTML sink — the failure is hidden rather than surfaced, and the hidden path is the unsafe one
defects.reproduction: NONE — hljs.highlight with a registered language did not throw in any probe, so I could not reach the catch arm. The INJECTION CONSEQUENCE IS A HYPOTHESIS. The silent swallow itself is a fact at line 46.
defects.proposedCure: Let it throw, or write the fallback via `textContent` rather than `innerHTML`. The sink disappears entirely with L-4: a glass-ui primitive renders highlighted tokens as a vnode tree, never through innerHTML.

defects.defect: A leaf feature component mutates a process-global singleton registry at module-evaluation time, inside a package that declares itself side-effect-free.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:5-8 — `import hljs from "highlight.js/lib/core"; import css from "highlight.js/lib/languages/css"; hljs.registerLanguage("css", css);` executes on module evaluation, at file scope, in a leaf component. `python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('package.json'))['sideEffects'])"` → `false`. The two declarations contradict each other: the package tells bundlers no module in the tree has import-time effects, and this module does.
defects.mechanism: boundary violation (feature leaf → shared global registry) with no owning module, plus a contradicted package-level side-effect declaration
defects.reproduction: NONE for the drop consequence — I did not produce a build in which the registration is elided. LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS on the drop. The CONTRADICTION between GradientCodeEditor.vue:8 and package.json `"sideEffects": false` is a fact, both pasted.
defects.proposedCure: The registration belongs wherever the highlighter is owned — glass-ui's `CodeField` (L-4), which can register the grammar lazily on first use inside its own setup, giving the registry a single owner and removing the module-scope side effect from a side-effect-free package.

defects.reproduction: Dev server at http://localhost:9000. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R1, R1b, R1c). By hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click the 'Gradient CSS' editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`, wait 0.5s. The entire workspace is replaced by 'This panel hit an unexpected error.' R1c reproduces the true mid-typing sequence: type `linear-gradient(90deg, red, rgb(` -> graceful verdict 'unparseable color "rgb("'; add the closing `)` -> dead.
defects.proposedCure: Two moves, root first. (1) Land the already-ruled total parser — registry/adjudicated/parser-band.md (cand-O): `parseCssColor` must be total, `string -> Result`, killing the family rather than this instance. (2) Make the component's parse channel total by construction: grow the verdict type's third case so an oracle that misbehaves still renders the destructive border and the Fira line — a user typo must be structurally incapable of reaching an error boundary. Explicitly NOT a bare try/catch around the emit swallowing to null: that is the masking fallback edict 2 forbids and the exact disease shell-dock-colorinput D-23 already documents (a shipping TypeError and a user typo rendering as the same sentence).

defects.defect: The 500 ms debounce is never cancelled on unmount, so a pending parse fires after the component is destroyed — detonating the C1 crash on whatever route the user has since navigated to.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue has NO onBeforeUnmount/onUnmounted; the only lifecycle hook in the file is `onMounted` at line 81. `debounce` at demo/shared/utils.ts:24-44 exposes `.cancel()`, which is never called. LIVE (evidence/live-probe.mjs R6): {"tag":"R6: navigated away inside the 500ms debounce window","url":"http://localhost:9000/#/mix","errorBoundaryVisible":1,"errorBoundaryText":"This panel hit an unexpected error.Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') Try again"}. Screenshot: evidence/R6-unmount-pending-debounce.png — the user is on #/mix and the MIX workbench is what dies.
defects.mechanism: Unreleased timer resource. The debounced callable is created in setup and outlives the component; Vue's `emit` still resolves the retained parent handler after unmount, so the parse runs against a dead model — and, with C1 live, throws into whatever boundary is currently mounted.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R6). By hand: on #/gradient type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` into the CSS editor and switch to the Mix view within 500 ms of the last keystroke — the Mix pane is replaced by the error plate.
defects.proposedCure: The debounced call is a resource acquired in setup and must be released there. Minimal: `onBeforeUnmount(() => debouncedParse.cancel())`. Better and idiomatic for this repo: use `useDebounceFn`/`watchDebounced` from `@vueuse/core` (already a dependency), whose effect-scope-bound cleanup makes the leak unrepresentable rather than remembered.

defects.defect: Blurring inside the 500 ms debounce window destroys the user's in-progress text and leaves the verdict naming a token that is no longer on screen — a direct breach of the file's own stated law.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:68-73 `onBlur()` reads `hasError` (line 32, derived from the `parseVerdict` prop) which the parent will not write until 500 ms later (GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108). The file's docblock at lines 34-40 states: 'A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed.' LIVE, with an isolating control (evidence/live-probe.mjs R2 / R2-control): defect {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)","editorClass":"border-destructive","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""} vs control (no blur) {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, notacolor, blue)","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""}. The only difference between the two runs is the blur.
defects.mechanism: Stale synchronous read of a prop written by an async parent round-trip — the repo's named `defineModel` hazard family, applied to a props+emit pair. `onBlur` decides whether to overwrite the user's text using the PREVIOUS parse's verdict.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R2 and R2-control). By hand: on #/gradient click the CSS editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, notacolor, blue)` and immediately click the 'CSS' heading. The editor snaps back to the old canonical gradient, wears the destructive border, and prints a verdict about a token that is nowhere visible.
defects.proposedCure: Blur is an authoring boundary and must RESOLVE the pending parse rather than race it: flush the debounce on blur (parse now, synchronously), then settle the text on the verdict that answers THAT text. Structurally, keep a local `shallowRef` mirror of the verdict written in the same tick that decides it — the canonical Vue-3.5 cure this repo already mandates — so `onBlur` can never read a value the parent has not yet written.

defects.defect: `textContent` collapses contenteditable line breaks, so multi-line authoring silently fuses tokens and rejects valid CSS with a message quoting a token the user never wrote.
defects.evidence:
GradientCodeEditor.vue:60 `const text = editorRef.value?.textContent ?? "";`. LIVE (evidence/live-probe.mjs R3), typing `linear-gradient(90deg, red` + Enter + `50%, blue)`: {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, red50%, blue)","verdict":"unparseable color \"red50%\"","dom":{"innerHTMLTail":"linear-gradient(90deg, red
50%, blue)
","textContent":"linear-gradient(90deg, red50%, blue)","innerText":"linear-gradient(90deg, red\n50%, blue)"}}. The element is styled `whitespace-pre-wrap min-h-[5rem] max-h-[12rem] overflow-y-auto` (line 93) — it invites the multi-line authoring it then corrupts.
defects.mechanism: Wrong text accessor for a contenteditable: the browser inserts a block element on Enter, and `textContent` concatenates block boundaries with no newline. `innerText` — already computed by the browser and captured in the same probe — carries the correct `\n`.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R3). By hand: click the CSS editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, red`, press Enter, type `50%, blue)`. The screen shows two lines; the verdict reads 'unparseable color "red50%"'.
defects.proposedCure: Stop hand-rolling a text editor over `contenteditable="true"`. Set `contenteditable="plaintext-only"`, where line breaks are real `\n` and `textContent` is honest — one attribute that also cures C8's paste injection. If the rich-content editor must stay, read `innerText` (the rendered-text semantics that match what the user sees), never `textContent`.

defects.defect: The failure surface is announced to nobody: `aria-invalid="true"` with no `aria-errormessage`/`aria-describedby`, the verdict has no `id`, the live region is v-if-mounted together with its content, its politeness contradicts the house register, and the multi-line textbox does not declare `aria-multiline`.
defects.evidence: LIVE census (evidence/live-probe.mjs R4): {"tag":"DIV","role":"textbox","ariaMultiline":null,"ariaInvalid":"true","ariaDescribedby":null,"ariaErrormessage":null,"contenteditable":"true","verdictInDom":true,"verdictId":"","verdictRole":"status","verdictAriaLive":null}. Source: GradientCodeEditor.vue:90-92 (role/label/aria-invalid) and 107-114 (`v-if="parseVerdict"` + `role="status"`, no id). `grep -rn "aria-describedby|aria-errormessage" demo` returns ZERO hits app-wide. House counter-idiom for a live region exists at demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:17 (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, permanently mounted); house register for a destructive failure is `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"` at demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:19-20.
defects.mechanism: Four separable a11y defects sharing one root: the field chrome and its error relation are hand-built rather than delegated to a field primitive that owns the id-wiring and live-region politeness. A screen-reader user on the field is told 'invalid' and never told why; a region created in the same patch as its text is unreliably announced; role=textbox defaults aria-multiline=false so AT offers single-line semantics for a box that scrolls to 12rem.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R4 runs against the live error state). The four attribute values above are read directly off the shipped DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Consume glass-ui's `LabeledField` (@mkbabb/glass-ui/labeled-field, installed 7.0.0). Its slot props are `{controlId, labelledBy, describedBy, errorId, invalid, disabled, required}`, it owns an `error` slot with an `errorLive: "off"|"polite"|"assertive"` prop, and `controlLabelable: false` exists precisely for non-labelable composite roots like a contenteditable div. That makes all four defects unrepresentable — and closes the app-wide zero-`aria-describedby` gap — instead of hand-fixing one file while 87 others keep it.

Ask glass-ui (standing BH/BI relay) for a `field-control` SHELL variant — `data-kind="code"`, or a `Field`/`Textarea` asChild/slot form — that owns surface, radius, rims, focus ring and `data-state=invalid` + its ring while accepting an arbitrary editable child. One primitive cures this file, the OM-13 readout rail, and every future code-shaped field. Until it lands, touch nothing here.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: zero tests exercise this component, and a mutation that deletes its central invariant — the editor truce — keeps all 19 unit tests and all 9 e2e tests green.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "GradientCodeEditor|gradient-parse-verdict" test/ e2e/ demo/` returns only the two .vue files, demo/styles/hljs.css and e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts. test/gradient-parse.test.ts has 19 tests, ALL against the sibling module `parseGradientCSS`; none instantiates the component. The e2e failure test (e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:222-247) uses `notacolor` — never an empty-argument colour function — and every e2e test ends with `expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([])` over e2e/smoke/fixtures/env-noise.ts:62-70, which listens on console AND pageerror; both are EMPTY during the C1 crash (R1-after: "pageErrors":[],"consoleErrors":[]) because the ErrorBoundary absorbs it and returns false.
defects.mechanism: The gate measures the sibling module and the console channel, neither of which observes the component's behaviour or its worst failure. The component's stated law lives only in a 7-line comment.
defects.reproduction: THE EXACT SURVIVING MUTATION: delete `focused` (line 41), `onFocus`/`onBlur` (lines 64-73), the `@focus`/`@blur` bindings (template lines 99-100) and the guard `if (focused.value) return;` (line 77), leaving `watch(() => modelValue, (newVal) => render(newVal))`. All 19 unit tests pass (they never import the component). All 9 e2e tests pass: `typeIntoEditor` types at delay:3 so the whole string lands in ~120 ms, well inside the 500 ms debounce, and NO model change occurs while the user types — the guard is never exercised; the round-trip test's assertions ('rebeccapurple', then 'red 0%, rebeccapurple 80%' after blur) are satisfied by the canonical simpleCSS the unconditional watch renders; the garbage test passes because a rejected parse leaves the model unchanged so the watch never fires. A second surviving mutation: make onBlur's `render(modelValue)` unconditional — no test ever blurs after a FAILED parse, so C3 becomes total and the suite stays green.
defects.proposedCure: The truce is a behaviour and needs a behavioural test at the component level: mount, focus, mutate modelValue, assert the DOM text did NOT change; blur, assert it did. And extend the e2e failure test past `notacolor` to the throwing corpus (oklch(), rgb(), hsl(  ), hwb(), rgba()) asserting a VERDICT — because a pageErrors-empty assertion cannot distinguish 'handled' from 'swallowed by a boundary that ate the app'.

defects.defect: Rich-HTML paste injects foreign markup with inline styles straight into the editor's DOM, destroying the syntax highlighting and overriding the design system's typography.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:88 `contenteditable="true"` with no `@paste` handler anywhere in the file. LIVE with a real system clipboard (evidence/paste-probe.mjs — clipboard-read/write granted, navigator.clipboard.write of a text/html + text/plain pair, then Cmd+V): {"innerHTML":"linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)","textContent":"linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)","foreignTags":["B[style]","I"],"verdict":null}.
defects.mechanism: An unsanitized contenteditable sink. The pasted markup persists until the next render(), which — if the parse is in an error state — never comes, because line 72 gates re-rendering on `!hasError`. NOT XSS: Chromium's paste sanitizer strips scripts and event handlers, so does not execute; this is an integrity and design-system defect, stated precisely rather than inflated.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/paste-probe.mjs`. By hand: copy syntax-highlighted CSS from any web page, click the Gradient CSS editor, Cmd+A, Cmd+V — the foreign fonts, sizes and colours land inside the glass panel.
defects.proposedCure: `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` (Chrome/Safari/Firefox 136+, and the demo's baseline is Safari + Chromium) — one attribute that also cures C4's line-break collapse. Failing that, `@paste.prevent` + an explicit plain-text insertion.

defects.defect: `highlight()`'s `catch { return code }` is a masking fallback that, if ever taken, feeds unescaped text into an `innerHTML` sink.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:43-49 (`try { return hljs.highlight(...).value } catch { return code }`) feeding line 52 (`editorRef.value.innerHTML = highlight(code)`). The happy path is safe, measured (evidence/hljs-bench.mjs): `hljs output for an HTML payload: linear-gradient(90deg, <img …` — highlight.js escapes `<` to `<`. The catch branch does not. `modelValue` is not only user-typed: seedFromPalette (GradientVisualizer.vue:110-116) pulls API-fetched saved-palette colour strings into stops[].cssColor, which serialize into simpleCSS, which render() writes.
defects.mechanism: A catch whose recovery is 'silently switch to the unescaped path' converts an unknown failure into an injection sink — the masking fallback edict 2 forbids.
defects.reproduction: NONE — reachability is a HYPOTHESIS, explicitly labelled. `css` is registered at module scope (line 8) so 'Unknown language' cannot fire, and hljs v11 handles illegal-lexeme errors internally in safe mode; I could not construct an input that takes the branch. The SHAPE is confirmed by reading lines 43-52.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the catch. If hljs.highlight can throw, that is a bug worth seeing; if it cannot, the catch is dead code impersonating safety. Either way the fallback sink must be `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.

defects.defect: Every model tick tears down and rebuilds the editor's entire subtree via `innerHTML`, destroying the browser's native undo stack and any selection — including once per pointer frame of an unrelated stop drag, on an editor that may be off-screen.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:51-53 (render sets innerHTML) driven by the watcher at lines 76-79 on `modelValue` = `simpleCSS`, which recomputes on every pointermove of a stop drag. MEASURED (evidence/live-probe.mjs R5): {"tag":"R5 editor DOM mutation records during a 40-step stop drag","dragMs":1024,"mutationRecords":40} — one full teardown-and-rebuild per frame. Cost MEASURED over 2000 iterations (evidence/hljs-bench.mjs): 2-stop (74 chars) 0.014 ms/highlight -> 0.8 ms per 60fps second; 4-stop (206 chars) 0.020 ms -> 1.2 ms per 60fps second.
defects.mechanism: An imperative innerHTML projection instead of a reactive render: Vue cannot patch what it does not own, so every change is a demolition.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R5). DOWNGRADED ON THE MEASUREMENT — ~1 ms per second of dragging is not a performance finding and I will not dress it as one. What remains real is the semantic cost: undo stack and selection destroyed on every frame.
defects.proposedCure: The editor is a rendered projection of the model and should re-render when the model changes MEANINGFULLY, not per frame. Render through Vue (a v-html-free token list, or a shallowRef of highlighted tokens) so the update is a patch rather than a demolition, restoring native undo and selection.

defects.defect: The CSS readout the editor displays carries 12-decimal channel values and a `deg` unit on OKLCH hue — the 'copy this CSS' surface emits `oklch(71.549999815004% 0.160350000555 186.400002219955deg)`.
defects.mechanism: Serializer formatting — CITED, NOT RE-FOUND. Belongs to the OM-14 value-formatting census (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/om-14-formatting/); the source is useGradientCSS's serializer, not GradientCodeEditor.vue.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/state-loss.mjs`, or by hand: on #/gradient click the stop rail twice to insert stops and read the CSS field.
defects.proposedCure: None from this seat — folds into the OM-14 formatting disposition. Recorded only because this component is where the user SEES it, and a copyable-CSS surface emitting 186.400002219955deg is the whole point of that mark.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Seat declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the component's constitutive law (Law 3, "zero letterbox / the drawn plot IS the element box") has NEVER executed against the pinned producer: it targets `svg[role="img"]` twice (EasingAuthoringStage.vue:48-50 and :104) while glass-ui 7.0.0 emits `role="group"` (grep of dist/easing.js returns exactly `role: "group"|"slider"|"status"`, zero `img`). Live WebKit measurement: `svgRoleImgFound: false`, producer inline style survives verbatim, canvas box 410x200 holding a 166.67x200 drawn plot — 121.67 px of dead letterbox per side, 40.65% ink fill. 53 of 116 lines (46%) of the file are dead machinery (vbRatio, syncVbRatio, onMounted, watch, 2 rAFs, :style binding, the whole Law-3 CSS block). The e2e oracle written to certify the law dies on the identical selector: `npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts` is 3/3 RED with "element(s) not found". The law and its only witness died in the same producer adopt and neither was noticed for a full tranche.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded anyway, so the report is not one-sided (report §8): Law 1 (one column) is genuinely alive — `pickerGridCols: "436px"` at 1440px where the producer would emit `1fr 18rem`; the unlayered scoped `:deep()` beats Tailwind's `@layer utilities` media rule and I checked for a layer-order defeat. Law 2 (wells, not cards) is genuinely alive — `cardShadow: "none"`, `cardBackdrop: "none"`, `cardBg` = the `--well-bg` mix in both schemes. The file's PRM claim at :112-113 is true — `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` neutralises `transition-duration` on `*`, measured `prm: true` with `aspect-ratio` absent from the transition list. Vue 3.5 idiom is correct (`useTemplateRef` :44, reactive props destructure :32, the `watch(() => value.css)` getter really is reactive, no `defineModel` stale-read hazard). `verbatimModuleSyntax` honoured (`import type` at :30). No horizontal overflow, no page error and no console error attributable to the component in its settled state (the one `/#/gradient` console error is the dev-config `VITE_API_URL` warning; the one pageerror is a benign ResizeObserver notice). Edict 1 (no god modules) passes: 116 lines, one job.

defects.defect: Two keypresses on this component's own canvas destroy the /#/gradient route. The seat wires an authoring domain of y in [-0.6, 1.6] (the producer's own sr-only instructions) into a consumer pipeline whose domain is [0,1], with no clamp, no validation, no invalid state and no error affordance. The shipped failure state is a bare unlabelled `Try again` pill on an empty page.
defects.evidence: EASD-overshoot.mjs verbatim: `t0: {"rows":1,"stage":true,"rowCss":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"}` / `shift+up x1: {"rows":1,"stage":true,"rowCss":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1.1)","vb":[0,-0.2,1,1.3],"drawnW":153.8,"inkFill":0.3752}` / `shift+up x2: {"rows":0,"stage":false,"tryAgain":true}`. Independently via the seat's own preset Select (EASD-crash.mjs): `ease-in -> rows:1 OK`, `ease -> rows:1 OK`, `ease-out-back -> {"rows":0,"stage":false,"tryAgain":true}`. Mechanism: src/color/operations.ts:90 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`; demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:200-208 feeds `easedT = easing(j/32)` straight into mixColors and THROWS on !ok. Screenshot: shots/route-crash-after-overshoot.png.
defects.mechanism: domain mismatch across a composition boundary with no designed invalid state; overshoot easing output escapes the [0,1] mix contract
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click `Author a custom curve`, focus bezier control point 2, press Shift+ArrowUp twice. Route falls into the error boundary. Also: open the stage's PRESET select and choose `ease-out-back`. Both reproduced headless in docs/.../EASD-overshoot.mjs and EASD-crash.mjs. NOTE: at y2=1.1 the max (1.0067 at parametric t~0.956) falls between the 33 grid samples and the crash is MISSED — the failure is sampling-luck-dependent, i.e. intermittent.
defects.proposedCure: Move the overshoot policy to the colour boundary, once, as a named parameter: `mixColors(from, to, t, { space, hue, overshoot: "clamp" | "extrapolate" | "error" })` with `"clamp"` default (CSS itself clamps easing output when interpolating). Retires the throw at all 3 call sites and unblocks the entire `back` family that easingCatalogue.ts:174 already advertises. Until then this seat must not ship an authoring surface whose advertised range is a route-kill.

result.axis: D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited; receipt is the first section of the written report.
result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the specimen well is not painted, so every syntax-highlight crayon fails WCAG AA in all four matrices. `GradientCodeEditor.vue:93` puts `.hljs` on a `glass-wash` surface whose computed style is `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `background-image: none`, `backdrop-filter: none` — the code artifact sits directly on the live seed-driven atmosphere. `demo/styles/hljs.css:22-33` states in its own header that the crayon palette is contrast-guarded *against the opaque `--well-bg` rung* ("Post-fix on the well: … all ≥4.5"), and `.hljs { background: transparent }` deliberately supplies no ground. Measured from the rendered composite (ink-free EMPTY frame, 82,560–126,144 px sampled), every crayon fails 4.5:1 in every matrix — light worst 3.89 (`--code-number`), dark worst 2.47 (`--code-keyword`, mobile). The ground ΔL against the guarded well has opposite sign per scheme (−0.170…−0.076 light, +0.044…+0.073 dark), so no crayon re-tune can rescue it, and because the ground is the user's live seed colour the delivered ratio is not a fixed number that can ever be certified. The damning part: the identical mechanism was diagnosed and cured 250px above in the same pane — `GradientEasingEditor.vue:170-176` carries an inline comment naming "~2.7:1 (fails AA)" and applies `bg-well` — and `docs/tranches/T/audit/SYNTHESIS.md:121` claims this exact file/line was already post-fixed. It was not. A class-level defect was patched at one instance.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded as genuine negative results (checked, and clean): (1) 200% zoom is sound in all four matrices — `document.documentElement.style.zoom=2` gives `docOverflowX:false`, `scrollW 1440/clientW 1440` desktop and `390/390` mobile, `scrollH == clientH` on the editor, no clipping introduced. (2) `prefers-reduced-motion` IS honoured — the global guard at `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important`) neutralises the component's transition; the two animated properties (`border-color`, `box-shadow`) are compositor-safe and force no layout; no animation was deleted. (3) Unmount during a pending 500ms parse is safe — typing then routing away produced zero page errors. (4) Keyboard reachability works — Tab from `Copy CSS` lands on the textbox (`isContentEditable:true`), Tab out proceeds. (5) Type role is correct — `text-mono-small`/Fira Code matches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:76; the verdict's size (16.4px) is identical to the sibling rail's `<code>`, correcting my own earlier mis-reading. (6) `horizontalOverflow: 0` on `/#/gradient` in all four captured matrices; the component contributes none of the route's 6 small tap targets or 1 nameless button. (7) Vue 3.5 idiom is clean (`useTemplateRef`, reactive props destructure); no god module, no back-compat shim, no new `shared/` dir; `verbatimModuleSyntax` has nothing to violate (no type-only imports exist).

defects.defect: Typing an empty-argument colour function (`oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl(  )`) — exactly what a human produces mid-keystroke — DESTROYS the entire Gradient workbench, falsifying the component's own written contract at GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40 ("A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed").
defects.evidence: evidence/probe2-log.txt, WebKit 1440x900 @dsf2 vs live dev server. After the 500ms debounce, identically for all three inputs: {"editorPresent":false,"verdict":null,"mainTextLen":102 (was 581),"mainHtmlLen":2832 (was 91196),"buttons":17 (was 53),"renderTilePresent":false,"bodyText":"… This panel hit an unexpected error. undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g[0].replace') Try again"}. Control `notacolor` (a designed rejection) keeps editorPresent:true, aria-invalid="true", border rgb(219,36,36), verdict 'unparseable color "notacolor"'. Visual: evidence/mtf001-panel-destroyed.png — both panes gone, a lone Try-again pill on the atmosphere. evidence/probe10: clicking Try again discards the user's text and resets to the default seed.
defects.mechanism: Closed-sum omission at a delegated-oracle boundary. The component models exactly two outcomes — applied (parseVerdict=null) or rejected-with-reason (string) — and models NO third arm for "the validity oracle threw". gradientParse.ts:92 delegates validity to parseCssColor; src/css/grammar.ts:181's false non-null assertion (MT-F001) supplies that third arm. The escape route is a bare `emit("parse", text)` inside a 500ms setTimeout (GradientCodeEditor.vue:63-65), so the throw surfaces asynchronously, detached from any interaction; the parent's onParseCSS (GradientVisualizer.vue:107-111) has no try, and it propagates to the route ErrorBoundary which unmounts the whole workbench.
defects.reproduction: 1. http://localhost:9000/#/gradient  2. scroll to the CSS field  3. select-all, type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`  4. wait 500ms. Also reproduces with rgb() and 'hsl(  )'.
defects.proposedCure: Make the parse boundary TOTAL, not caught. Adopt the adjudicated parser band (registry/adjudicated/parser-band.md, cand-O) so parseCssColor returns a failure value instead of throwing — the component's contract then holds by construction. A local try/catch here would be exactly the masking fallback owner edict 2 forbids: it converts a shipping library crash into a silent local lie. The component-side half is that its error model becomes one closed sum enforced by the TYPE crossing the emit, not by convention.

defects.defect: The specimen well is not painted: `glass-wash` on the code plate computes to zero fill, zero backdrop-filter, and only a bevel + drop shadow — so the hljs crayon palette, which its own theme header certifies only against the opaque `--well-bg` ground, renders on the live chromatic atmosphere and every token fails 4.5:1 in all four matrices.
defects.evidence: Computed live at GradientCodeEditor.vue:93 (evidence/cd-probe5.mjs): backgroundColor `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, backgroundImage `none`, backdropFilter `none`, boxShadow includes an outer `… 0px 2px 8px …`. Spec quote demo/styles/hljs.css:22-33: "the rung-2 well (`--well-bg` = card 92% + fg 8%) … Post-fix on the well: comment 5.33/5.04, string 4.99, number 4.91, keyword 4.91, entity/title 5.41 (light) — all ≥4.5"; `--code-comment: hsl(30 22% 34%); /* warm muted gray (well-guarded) */`; `.dark { /* … lifted for the dark chocolate WELL field. */ }`; hljs.css:56-58 `.hljs { background: transparent; }`. Measured delivered contrast (Pillow, ground from ink-free EMPTY frame, 82,560 px desktop / 126,144 px mobile; text is 16.4px = normal, floor 4.5): light comment 4.20 / keyword 3.90 / entity 4.27 / string 3.93 / number 3.89; dark 2.65 / 2.57 / 2.82 / 3.06 / 3.23; mobile-dark 2.55 / 2.47 / 2.71 / 2.95 / 3.11. Ground ranges: light rgb(240,189,202)…rgb(240,209,206) L .592–.686; dark rgb(119,78,85)…rgb(119,92,88) L .100–.123. Prior claim contradicted: docs/tranches/T/audit/SYNTHESIS.md:121 says "post-fix: the two sites (GradientStopEditor.vue:171, GradientCodeEditor.vue:93) paint their rung". Sibling cure present at GradientEasingEditor.vue:170-176 (`bg-well`, comment records the same "~2.7:1"). Rendered plate ΔL vs the surrounding pane: −0.050 light, −0.012 dark (the dark well is optically absent).
defects.mechanism: A material-tier contract enforced by convention instead of structure. The hljs theme deliberately ships `background: transparent` and delegates the ground to the consumer; the consumer applies a class (`glass-wash`) that paints a bevel and a drop shadow but no fill and no blur. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:14-19 defines the Specimen-well tier for "code artifact" as an OPAQUE/quiet neutral stage and states "Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well" — this surface has backdrop-filter:none, so it earns nothing. defects.proposedCure: Make the well a TIER, not a class two components remember to apply: one well material owns every code/value artifact on the route (the `bg-well` rung the sibling already proves), applied at the tier level so `.hljs` always lands on the ground it was guarded for. Do NOT re-tune the crayons — the ground error has opposite sign per scheme. Also drop the outer `0 2px 8px` caster (PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05: caster shadows that repeat a boundary → REMOVE) so the code plate reads as a recessed field, not a raised slab.

defects.defect: The one-line parse verdict is born 100% off-screen — clipped by the pane's own scroll box at the instant it appears — leaving a red border as the sole failure signal, which the constitution forbids; and it is never associated with the textbox.
defects.evidence:
evidence/probe7, identical light and dark at 1440x900: {"verdictBottom":904,"cardBottom":877,"viewportH":900,"belowCardBy":27,"visiblePx":0,"verdictH":22.9}. evidence/probe6 across desktop-light/desktop-dark/mobile-light: verdictClippedByHost:true, inViewport:false, scrollHost `glass-resting card rounded-card …`. has no id; role="status" sits on a v-if-mounted node (GradientCodeEditor.vue:107-113). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never colour-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."
defects.mechanism: Compositional: the editor is the LAST child of the pane, the verdict is its next sibling, and the verdict is created 500ms after the keystroke with no reveal — so every failure is announced into the clip. The a11y half is the same root cause: the error region is a hand-placed sibling paragraph rather than part of the field's anatomy, so nothing wires id→aria-describedby, and the live region is created at announce time (the classic non-announcement).

Folds into D-7's glass-forward ask.

defects.defect: The syntax highlighting — the component's headline capability and the sole reason highlight.js is imported — is dead exactly while the editor is being used. It decorates only the resting state.

Source: onInput (GradientCodeEditor.vue:57-60) reads textContent and debounces the parse but never calls render(); the model→editor watch (:76-79) early-returns while `focused`.
defects.mechanism: The "editor truce" (documented at :32-40 — never re-seat the caret mid-thought) is a real and correct constraint, but it was resolved by DELETING the feature in the used state rather than by solving it. Neither standard resolution was taken: caret restoration via Selection/Range offsets, or the overlay idiom.

defects.proposedCure: The overlay idiom: an aria-hidden highlighted mirror under a transparent-ink editable layer. Highlighting becomes live because the caret's host is never rewritten, the truce is preserved by construction rather than by an early-return, and the mirror can own code-correct wrapping — which also dissolves D-9.

defects.defect: There is no pending/settling state, so the error state lies: after the offending token is removed and the text is fully valid, the destructive border, aria-invalid="true" and a verdict naming a token no longer present all persist for at least 480ms.
defects.evidence: evidence/probe9, measured sweep. From a settled rejection, retyping `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)`: +0ms / +120ms / +300ms / +480ms all report border rgb(219,36,36), aria-invalid "true", verdict 'unparseable color "notacolor"' — while editorText is already `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)`. Only at +650ms does it clear. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 lists `pending` among the states that must be explicit.
defects.mechanism: The two-arm model (`null | string`) has no value for "not yet decided", so during the 500ms debounce the STALE arm is forced to impersonate current truth. It runs in both directions: a valid→invalid edit reads "fine" for 500ms.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → type `linear-gradient(90deg, notacolor, blue)`, wait for the rejection → select-all, type `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)` → poll border/aria-invalid/verdict at 120ms intervals.
defects.proposedCure: Three arms, not two: `settling | applied | rejected(reason)`. Entering `settling` on input immediately drops the destructive treatment — nothing is claimed while nothing is known — and the arm is a VALUE, not a timer side effect.

defects.defect: `word-break: break-all` fractures identifiers and numeric literals mid-token in a surface whose entire job is code legibility, and the overflow state slices its first line mid-glyph with no fade, scroll shadow, or visible affordance that content exists above.

defects.mechanism: `break-all` breaks between ANY two characters — the most aggressive available policy — chosen presumably to prevent horizontal overflow on long single tokens. A split numeric literal is a legibility failure, not a wrapping preference.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → paste a 12-stop `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.7 0.15 0) 0%, … )` into the CSS field at 1440x900 and at iPhone 14 width; read the rendered line breaks.

Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84 "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency."

defects.reproduction: Mechanism CONFIRMED (computed values pasted). Paint is a HYPOTHESIS: WebKit's emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'}) still paints the shadow (evidence/crop-m-desk-light-F-forcedcolors-focus.png shows a frame), so this harness cannot witness the real Windows High Contrast drop.
defects.proposedCure: Arrives with the producer field surface (D-7), which owns an outline-bearing focus grammar. A forced-colors focus indicator must be an `outline`, not a shadow.

defects.defect: A per-instance inline `:style` transition on the component root duplicating house motion tokens, plus a redundant `fira-code` font override on the verdict.

The font class is a no-op layered on a token that already resolves the family.

defects.defect: The highlight fallback writes untrusted text straight into innerHTML.

The success path is escaped by hljs; the catch arm returns the input verbatim as markup.
defects.mechanism: A catch whose recovery is "write the untrusted string as markup" is a designed-in sink, even where the likelihood of reaching it is low (hljs.highlight with a registered language does not realistically throw, and render() is called only with the model's own serialization).

defects.proposedCure: The catch arm should render as textContent, not innerHTML. Dissolves entirely under D-4's overlay idiom, where the editable host is never assigned markup.

Enable noUnusedLocals in tsconfig.base.json — the ">100 churn-only diffs" objection recorded at eslint.config.js:11-13 is precisely the debt this finding measures. Ten sites use the `!`-asserted inject idiom, so a single `injectStrict(key)` helper that throws with the key name is justified under KISS (>1 consumer).

defects.defect: The injection key is imported from the 250-line port FACTORY module, inverting the layer direction: a leaf feature statically depends on the composition-root module that provides to it.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:6 `import { LIBRARY_PORT_KEY } from "../../palettes/usePalettePorts"`. demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts has 18 import statements (grep -c '^import') and wires 15 composables — useAdminAuth, useUserAuth, useSession, useBrowsePalettes, useAdminUsers, useColorNameQueue, useSlugMigration, usePaletteActions, useFilteredList, useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit, usePaletteStore — plus ../shell/useViewManager. All of it, for one Symbol. `ls demo/palettes/` — 24 entries, no keys.ts. Five consumers pay: GradientVisualizer.vue:27, MixPane.vue:10, MixSourceSelector.vue:6, GeneratePane.vue:6, PalettesPane.vue:134. Sub-note L-4a: nullability is inconsistent for the same key — GeneratePane.vue:11 and MixPane.vue:16 use `inject(...)!`, GradientVisualizer.vue:30 and MixSourceSelector.vue:33 use bare `inject(...)`. Sub-note L-4b: GenerateControls.vue:16 imports PaletteColorStrip from ../../palettes/browser/card — reaching into a sibling FEATURE's card-internals subtree.
defects.mechanism: Family A — the dependency arrow points from consumer to provider's factory instead of both depending on a contract leaf. The repo already ships the correct idiom one directory over: demo/color-session/keys.ts is a leaf exporting nothing but InjectionKeys and types, and GeneratePane.vue:7 consumes CSS_COLOR_KEY from it correctly.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural, not behavioural). grep -rn LIBRARY_PORT_KEY demo enumerates the five consumers; grep -c '^import' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts returns 18.
defects.proposedCure: Add demo/palettes/keys.ts holding the five InjectionKey symbols plus five port INTERFACES — not `ReturnType<typeof providePalettePorts>`, which is what currently drags the factory into every consumer's type graph. usePalettePorts.ts imports the keys and provides; consumers import keys only. Move PaletteColorStrip to demo/color-session/color-chips/ beside PreviewStrip, where its four consumers (generate, extract, mix, palettes) already agree it belongs.

defects.defect: The pane shell is copy-pasted across 5-9 sibling components as a literal utility-class string, and the class the parent Card carries is DEFINED inside its own PaneHeader child's unscoped <style>.
defects.evidence: GeneratePane.vue:30-31 `<div class="relative w-full mx-auto h-full min-w-0">` + `<Card tier="resting" class="pane-scroll-fade w-full overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden min-w-0 h-full">`. The wrapper string appears in 5 files (generate, gradient, mix, extract, scenes/ConfigSliderPane); the Card string in 8; .pane-scroll-fade in 9 panes total. The class is defined at demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 in an UNSCOPED style block; the file's own comment at :43-52 describes the inversion as a constraint. demo/styles/foundation.css:578 records the move as deliberate.
defects.mechanism: Family C + B — no shared shell, so nine components restate the composition; and a child module owns a class applied to its parent and to eight sibling components it never sees. Edict 5 (root-level styling) violated by nine per-instance restatements.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). grep -rn 'pane-scroll-fade w-full' demo | wc -l → 8; grep -rn 'class="relative w-full mx-auto h-full min-w-0"' demo → 5 files. Latent hazard confirmed by inspection: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:106 applies .pane-scroll-fade to a plain <div> and works only because it happens to also import PaneHeader at :22 — coincidence of co-import, not construction.
defects.proposedCure: L-2's cure subsumes it: `class="card-scroll-host"` is glass-ui's, owned by glass-ui, and there is no demo class to misplace. If a demo shell is still wanted afterwards it is ONE demo/shared/ui/PaneShell.vue owning wrapper + Card + header slot, reducing nine call sites to `<PaneShell title="Generate" description="…">`.

defects.defect: The three verbs (Regenerate / Save / Copy) have two independent homes with no shared definition, producing two live controls with the identical accessible name on one route.
defects.evidence: In-plate buttons in GenerateControls.vue (direct handlers) vs dock DockAction[] at demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:181-186 (titles, descriptions, icons and aria-labels independently authored). Live probe: duplicateAccessibleNames: ["Save palette", "Color count"]. Playwright's strict-mode resolver stated it as a hard failure on my first probe run: 'strict mode violation: locator(\'button[aria-label="Save palette"]\') resolved to 2 elements: 1) class="action-button-wrapper…" (dock) 2) data-slot="button" data-icon-only="true" (plate)'. Visual audit REPORT.md:38,53,68,83 independently counts 5 small tap targets on /#/generate in all four matrices.
defects.mechanism: Family D — one concept, two mechanisms, no single definition. A screen-reader user hears "Save palette, button" twice with no disambiguation; an automation author cannot address either without a structural selector.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe-structure.mjs — collects every [aria-label] on /#/generate and returns the duplicates. Independently: any `page.locator('button[aria-label="Save palette"]').click()` on /#/generate throws Playwright strict-mode violation (pasted output in report).
defects.proposedCure: One definition. The feature session (L-1's cure) exports its verb list `{key,title,description,icon,handler}[]`; both the dock and the plate render THAT. The dock then needs no component ref at all, which kills L-7 outright.

defects.defect: The shell↔pane contract is `Ref<any>` and the call is optional-chained twice — a masking fallback on each side of the boundary, over a pure re-export bridge that adds nothing.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:103-107 `export interface PaneActionRefs { generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any>; }`. Shell call: usePaneRouter.ts:183 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()`. Pane call: GeneratePane.vue:23 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()`. GeneratePane.vue:22-26 forwards three names verbatim from GenerateControls.vue:120 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`.
defects.mechanism: Family A — edict 2 masking fallback. If an exposed name is renamed or the child fails to mount, the dock button becomes a silent no-op: no throw, no console, nothing for a gate to catch. The inner `?.` is doubly gratuitous — controlsRef is typed InstanceType<typeof GenerateControls> at GeneratePane.vue:12, so `regenerate` is a statically known non-optional member; the `?.()` defends a case the type system already excluded, which is how the pattern spread.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural; the failure mode is silence by construction). Verified by reading the three call sites — the `any` erases the contract so no compile-time check exists to demonstrate.
defects.proposedCure: L-6's cure deletes the bridge entirely. If an imperative handle must survive, type it `Ref<InstanceType<typeof GeneratePane> | null>` and drop every `?.` after the ref's own null-guard.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-file re-export alias layer over glass-ui with no encapsulation, and it is a LIVE dual path — GenerateControls.vue reaches glass-ui through both the barrel and the bare specifier in one file.
defects.evidence: 18 of 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts files are exactly 1 line; demo/ui/card/index.ts:1 `export { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Dual path inside one feature: GenerateControls.vue:6-13 imports Select/Slider/Button/Badge from ../../ui/*, while :14 imports writeClipboard from "@mkbabb/glass-ui" and :15 WatercolorDot from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot". GeneratePane.vue:3 takes the barrel route for Card. 12 files import the demo/ui barrels. Adjacent same-mechanism: demo/shared/utils.ts:4-6 defines cn() while glass-ui exports cn at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/index.d.ts:41.
defects.mechanism: Family D — a pre-glass-ui shadcn-vue era alias layer that was never deleted when the source moved upstream. Edicts 2 (no aliases/dual paths) and 3 (no wrapper contrivance). Also defeats subpath tree-shaking: ../../ui/card pulls the package ROOT barrel where @mkbabb/glass-ui/card is one of 74 declared export keys.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). for d in demo/ui/*/; do wc -l $d/index.ts; grep -c '@mkbabb/glass-ui' $d/index.ts; done → 19 dirs, 18 at exactly 1 line, every one a pure glass-ui re-export.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely (12 importing files). Import @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath> at the call site. Delete demo/shared/utils.ts's cn and import glass-ui's. The design system is the design system.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's value.js `paths` block is drifted from package.json#exports — three dead keys pointing at nonexistent files, two real exported keys missing — and the entire block is provably inert because TypeScript already resolves correctly by package self-reference.
defects.evidence: paths declares 8 value.js keys; exports declares 7 and NONE of them is `.`. Dead: `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts (ls → 'No such file or directory'); `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports nor in src/subpaths/, which holds exactly color|css|easing|math|quantize|transform|value). Missing from paths but real exports and actually imported: `/css` (demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:42) and `/value`. The file's comment claims it "Mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map" and calls it "the CLOSED 8-key set" — vite.config.ts:52-61 genuinely generates 7 anchored regexes from exports, with no `.`. traceResolution proves /css resolves DESPITE having no paths entry: 'Module name @mkbabb/value.js/css was successfully resolved to /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts with Package ID @mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'.
defects.mechanism: Family E — a hand-maintained mirror of generated truth, drifted away from the thing it claims to mirror. Its only live effect is to shadow a correct self-reference resolution with three broken targets.
defects.reproduction: npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution 2>&1 | grep -A6 "Resolving module '@mkbabb/value.js/css'" — output pasted in report. Plus: ls dist/index.d.ts → No such file or directory; ls src/subpaths/ → no parsing.ts, no units.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all seven value.js `paths` entries from tsconfig.demo.json. Package self-reference through the real exports map is the correct, drift-proof mechanism and is already working. That makes the tsconfig honest by construction — adding an export key needs no second edit.

defects.defect: demo/palettes/export.ts (132 L) and demo/palettes/export/ (12 modules) are both alive; the shipping path resolves to the 132-line legacy while the 12-module tree is reachable ONLY from a test. The byte-exact suite certifies code no user path executes.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:2-9 imports `from "./export"`, which under moduleResolution:bundler resolves to export.ts (the export/ dir has no index.ts). Consumers of usePaletteExport: BrowsePane.vue:198, PalettesPane.vue:152. Sole entry into the 12-module tree in the entire repo: demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23 `} from "../../palettes/export/serializers";`. The tree holds serializers.ts, canonical.ts, rfc8785.ts, digest.ts, bytes.ts, json.ts, css.ts, tailwind.ts, svg.ts, png.ts, reload.ts, types.ts.
defects.mechanism: Family D — a named historical suspect, still live and worse than described: the tested implementation is not the shipped one, so a green byte-exact suite (canonical JSON, RFC-8785, digests) reads as coverage while proving a property of dead code.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'export/serializers|export/json|export/png|export/svg|export/css|export/tailwind|export/canonical|export/digest|export/rfc8785|export/bytes|export/reload' demo test e2e | grep -v '^demo/palettes/export/' → exactly one hit, demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23. Out of GeneratePane's direct graph; recorded because it lives in the palettes/ domain GeneratePane depends on via L-4 and the brief named it.
defects.proposedCure: Delete export.ts, add demo/palettes/export/index.ts re-exporting serializers.ts, repoint usePaletteExport.ts, re-run the byte-exact suite against the live path so it certifies what ships.

defects.defect: Non-idiomatic Vue 3.5 template ref — hand-annotated `ref<InstanceType<typeof …> | null>(null)` instead of `useTemplateRef`.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:12 `const controlsRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof GenerateControls> | null>(null);`. Identical non-idiomatic line at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:9.
