result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, 1M context. Declared at spawn, not inherited.

defects.defect: The mix PREVIEW and the mix OPERATION are different mathematical objects. MixConfigBar's Space/Hue chips call `sampleInterpolationRamp` (N colors -> k stops, a piecewise path); the Mix button beneath them calls `mixColorSequence` (N colors -> 1 color, a weighted centroid). Both are reached through the SAME two v-models. Compounding this, the chip grammar is inverted across the two features: the workbench whose product IS a ramp (gradient) renders no chips, while the workbench whose product is a single color (mix) renders ramps.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:52 (path) vs demo/palettes/mix.ts:36 (centroid); wired at MixConfigBar.vue:57-74 (chips) and MixConfigBar.vue:167 -> MixPane.vue:104 -> useMixingState.ts:88 (button). MEASURED via node against dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js, space=oklab hue=shorter — min OKLab distance from the produced result to the NEAREST previewed stop: N=2 -> 0.0000; N=3 (#ff0000,#00ff00,#0000ff) -> 0.1358; N=4 -> 0.0534, against an OKLab JND of ~0.02. At N=3 the button yields chroma 0.014 while all 17 previewed stops are chroma 0.25-0.31. Inversion evidence: `grep -rn PreviewRamp demo/ --include=*.vue` returns only MixConfigBar; useMixingState.ts:89 shows mix colors-mode output is `{type:"color"}`; color-chips/index.ts:14-17 documents the GradientVisualizer consume that never landed. The component asserts the opposite at MixConfigBar.vue:38-43 ('the preview ramps' truth inputs') and sample.ts:20 ('a chip that approximates the library output is FORBIDDEN').
defects.mechanism: The library's interpolation surface stops at arity 2 (src/color/operations.ts:83 mixColors is the ONLY interpolation export), so each consumer lifted it independently; two consumers needed two DIFFERENT lifts (a path, a point), and a preview module authored for path semantics was wired to the feature that computes a point.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/div2.mjs (pasted in report §1b) reproduces both chains verbatim against the built dist and prints the three distances. NOTE: in the SHIPPED app this is dormant behind round-1 finding L-1 (operandColors is permanently [] because all 13 add-affordances are pointer-dead), so no chip currently renders — the code/measurement half is proven, the live-app half is labelled a hypothesis that goes live the moment L-1 is cured.
defects.proposedCure: Relate the two functions IN THE LIBRARY, then give each feature its own grammar. Export from src/subpaths/color.ts both `mixSequence(colors, {space, hue, weights})` (N->1, absorbs mixColorSequence) and `sampleColorRamp(colors, {space, hue, count})` (N->k, absorbs the three demo samplers), with endpoints converted once and one joint contract — and DEFINE the ramp as the path the sequence walks. Then gradient rows render PreviewRamp(sampleColorRamp(...)) — the chip IS the product — and mix rows render a single-swatch chip of mixSequence(operands, ...) — the chip IS the color the button will produce, per candidate space. THIS CORRECTS THE PRIOR CURE: rounds 2 (L2-3) and 3 (§11) both proposed one `sampleColorRamp` with `mixColorSequence` 'promoted alongside'; promoting them alongside as two independent functions preserves the defect exactly.

defects.defect: The O-14 'PREVIEW TRUTH LAW' oracle re-implements the sampler's own loop and asserts equality with it, and never names the operation whose truth it claims to guard. It is structurally incapable of detecting R4-1.
defects.evidence: test/preview-chips.test.ts:38-49 `directRamp` re-implements the segment loop; :66-76 asserts `expect(stops).toEqual([...seg0, ...seg1.slice(1)])` — perSegment, the slice(1) joint dedupe and the segment decomposition are the SAMPLER's own rules retyped in the test. The header states the circularity as design (:5-8): 'the sampler composes, never re-derives, so equality is by construction and this oracle guards the construction.' `grep -c mixColorSequence test/preview-chips.test.ts` -> 0. And it is green: `npx vitest run test/preview-chips.test.ts test/mix-v4.test.ts` -> 'Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 7 passed (7)' — seven tests across both functions in one run, comparing neither to the other.
defects.mechanism: An oracle written against the implementation rather than against the property; the guard was aimed at its own reflection.
defects.reproduction: grep -c mixColorSequence test/preview-chips.test.ts (=0); read test/preview-chips.test.ts:38-49 beside :66-76; npx vitest run test/preview-chips.test.ts test/mix-v4.test.ts (7 passed).
defects.proposedCure: Assert the property, not the algorithm. With R4-1's library pair landed, one falsifiable assertion states the law: for N=2, expect(sampleColorRamp(ops,{...,count:k})).toContainEqual(mixSequence(ops,{...})); for the mix chip at any N, expect(mixChipStops(ops,space,hue)).toEqual([mixSequence(ops,{space,hue})]). The existing e2e leg (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts) then holds paint === stamp as it already does, and the chain is real end to end.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue, r4)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), serving the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: R4-1 — the `HSL` row of this component's Color-space Select (MixConfigBar.vue:107, color-space-meta.ts:31) is a live application-killer: `convertColor(white, "hsl")` returns `color_non_finite` because `src/color/anchors.ts:173` divides by `1 - |2L - 1|` (exactly 0 at L=1) and guards only `delta === 0`, which the XYZ round-trip destroys (srgb-linear round-trip of white = [1.0000000000000004, 0.9999999999999998, 1] → delta ≈ 6e-16). Exactly 1 failure in a 4096-sample sRGB cube sweep, and it is pure white. Nothing on the mix path catches it (grep for try/catch/error across the whole mix workbench: zero matches), so the throw climbs to the app-root ErrorBoundary (App.vue:50) which replaces the ENTIRE two-pane grid. Reproduced end-to-end in the shipped app through the identical INTERPOLATION_SPACES vocabulary in the sibling gradient workbench: `panes: 0`, bodyText "This panel hit an unexpected error. color_non_finite Try again" — with `consoleErrors` and `pageErrors` both EMPTY, which is why the visual audit's clean /#/mix rows are not evidence of absence.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded negative proofs inside the report: the sampler's stop syntax is valid CSS in all four shapes it emits — none-hue, deg-hue, alpha, L>100% — measured by CSS.supports, killing my leading hypothesis that grayscale operands blank the chip's gradient; 4095 of 4096 cube samples convert cleanly, so this is one denominator and not general conversion rot; everything colorToCss emits, parseColorIn re-reads; menu semantics are exactly as authored (9/4/3 rows, aria-selected on the current row only, 52px options, Escape restores focus); the file contains no rAF, listeners, observers, timers, async, defineModel, ValueUnit construction or reka slider, so four of the six named local hazards cannot arise; verbatimModuleSyntax is clean; the component contributes zero small tap targets and zero nameless buttons to REPORT.json.)

defects.defect: The `HSL` row this component offers (one of nine, rendered identically to the eight that work) makes the pane's only verb throw `color_non_finite` for a pure-white operand, and the throw collapses the entire application to the app-root error boundary. The component's own missing-chip signal is rendered as the same blank it uses for 'honest absence', so the UI actively conceals the fault.
defects.evidence: src/color/anchors.ts:167-174 (`delta === 0 ? 0 : delta / (1 - Math.abs(2 * lightness - 1))`); src/color/operations.ts:47-52 routes all cross-space conversion through XYZ; measured `white -> srgb-lin: [1.0000000000000004, 0.9999999999999998, 1]` so delta≈6e-16≠0 while the denominator is 0. Cube sweep: `samples=4096  failures=1  rgb(255 255 255) -> color_non_finite`. Per-space startMix for [#ffffff,#000000]: 8 spaces return a color, `hsl  chip=NULL(hidden) startMix=!!! THREW: color_non_finite`. `grep -rn "catch|try {|error|Error" demo/workbenches/mix/*.vue demo/workbenches/mix/composables/*.ts` → zero matches. useMixingState.ts:87 `parseColorIn(selection.css, colorSpace.value)` uncaught. Live: `{ boundaryVisible: true, bodyText: "… This panel hit an unexpected error. color_non_finite Try again", panes: 0 }` with errors `none` in both steps.
defects.mechanism: Division by a denominator that is exactly zero at the L=1 domain boundary, guarded on the wrong operand (numerator `delta` instead of the denominator), combined with a demo boundary (picker-color.ts:105-117 `valueOrThrow`) that converts the library's Result discipline back into exceptions on a path with no handler.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED, live, on http://localhost:9000 — (1) navigate to /#/gradient; (2) type `linear-gradient(90deg, #ffffff 0%, #ff0000 100%)` into the field labelled 'Gradient CSS'; (3) choose 'HSL' from the 'Interpolation space' combobox (the same INTERPOLATION_SPACES array MixConfigBar.vue:18,107 renders). Result: both panes replaced by the ErrorBoundary, `panes: 0`, no console error and no page error emitted. Module-level: `parseColorIn("#ffffff", "hsl")` throws PickerColorError("color_non_finite") from picker-color.ts:106. In MixConfigBar's own pane the identical click fires the moment C-2 is cured, or today in palettes mode with two saved palettes containing white (MixSourceSelector.vue:246 is a real native button).
defects.proposedCure: Two independent repairs, both subtractive. (1) anchors.ts:173 — guard the denominator: `const denom = 1 - Math.abs(2*lightness - 1); denom === 0 ? 0 : delta / denom`; one expression kills the whole L∈{0,1} class. (2) Stop converting Results into throws on a user-reachable path: the library is Result-typed by design and sample.ts already handles failure honestly at :64/:81 — startMix (useMixingState.ts:79-101) is the only one of the two that lies. Keep the Result and render an honest failure instead of letting it climb to App.vue:50.

defects.defect: No end-to-end test runs in CI at all, and the single vitest oracle that walks the broken conversion path uses chromatic-only operands, so it misses it by one character.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "playwright" .github/workflows/` → no match. .github/workflows/ci.yml:31-37 is the whole producer gate (lint, vue-tsc ×2, build, `npm test`, pack-verify) plus a separate api job. package.json:68 `"test:e2e": "playwright test"` exists and nothing invokes it. test/preview-chips.test.ts:35 `OPERANDS = ["oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8)", "rebeccapurple"]`, :78-88 loops `["hsv","xyz","lab","hsl"]`. `grep -rn "convertColor(.*hsl" test/ demo/test/` → exactly one hit, test/v4-color-behavior.test.ts:58, whose `source` is already hsl and returns at operations.ts:44 before encodedToHsl is ever called.
defects.mechanism: Gate vacuity by two routes: an e2e suite that is authored but never executed by any workflow (so it reads as coverage while providing none), and a unit oracle whose operand fixture never visits a domain boundary, so it exercises the broken function's happy path only.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — `npx vitest run test/preview-chips.test.ts` → `4 passed`. Then the one-token mutation (OPERANDS[1] := "#ffffff") run through the identical loop: `hsv stops.length = 17 -> PASSES / xyz PASSES / lab PASSES / hsl TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length') -> the suite ERRORS at :81`.
defects.proposedCure: (1) Add the e2e job to ci.yml or delete e2e/smoke/** — a suite nothing runs is worse than none because it reads as coverage. (2) Cross the sampler oracle with domain-boundary operands (white, black, transparent, neutral gray) × all nine offered spaces: 36 assertions that would have caught R4-1, R4-2, R4-7 and C-8 in one commit, and would turn C-1/C-2 red for the first time.

defects.defect: Near-white in HSL degenerates into negative saturation, and the app serializes, stores and re-parses the corrupted value without complaint.
defects.evidence: `oklch(100% 0 250) -> hsl [342.857143, -2.625, 1]` (saturation −262.5%). The mix result: `picker-white + red  startMix -> hsl(351.428571428571deg -81.25% 75%)`, `reparse -> hsl(351.428571428571deg -81.25% 75%)`. MixPane.vue:38-47 hands exactly that string to `pm.createPalette(...)`. src/color/model.ts:87 validates finiteness but not domain.
defects.mechanism: Same denominator as R4-1, approached from below: as lightness crosses 1 by float dust the denominator goes negative-tiny, flipping the sign of the quotient. No range assertion exists at the makeColor boundary, so the out-of-domain channel escapes into persistence.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — `mixColorSequence([parseColorIn("oklch(100% 0 250)","hsl"), parseColorIn("#ff0000","hsl")], "hsl", "shorter")` then `colorToCss(...)` → `hsl(351.428571428571deg -81.25% 75%)`; feeding that string back through `parseColorIn(_, "hsl")` returns it unchanged.
defects.proposedCure: The R4-1 denominator guard fixes the sign. Independently, makeColor (model.ts:87) should assert the per-space channel domain (hsl.s ∈ [0,1], hwb.w+b, …), catching the corruption where it is created rather than three modules downstream in a saved palette.

defects.defect: The preview-chip `v-if` collapses three distinct states — no operands, unparseable operand, and 'this candidate space cannot represent this operand at all' — into one identical blank, so the only visible warning that a row will crash the mix reads as the file's documented 'honest absence'.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:111 and :133 (`v-if="spaceRamps.get(s.value)"`); sample.ts:50-51 defines absence as '<2 parseable operands'; sample.ts:60-66 also returns null when parseColorIn throws. Measured row census for [#ffffff, #ff0000]: `OKLCh=chip OKLab=chip Lab=chip LCh=chip HSL=BLANK HSV=chip HWB=chip RGB=chip XYZ=chip`; with HSL as the current space, `hue rows @hsl: Shorter=BLANK Longer=BLANK Increasing=BLANK Decreasing=BLANK`. For chromatic operands all nine rows carry a chip.
defects.mechanism: A three-valued outcome funnelled through a nullable return type; the discrimination exists inside the sampler (try/catch at :60-66 vs. length check at :58 vs. `!result.ok` at :81) and is discarded at every `return null`.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — `sampleInterpolationRamp(["#ffffff","#ff0000"], s, "shorter")` for each of the nine INTERPOLATION_SPACES values returns a 17-stop array for eight and `null` for "hsl"; the same call across the four HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS with space="hsl" returns null for all four.
defects.proposedCure: Return the discrimination the module already computes: `{ kind: "ramp", stops } | { kind: "insufficient" } | { kind: "unsupported", code }`. The row then renders a ramp, nothing, or a disabled row carrying the reason. No new component, no new directory — the KISS edict is satisfied by removing a lossy conversion, not by adding a wrapper.

defects.defect: The hand-written `aria-label` on each SelectTrigger replaces the trigger's content as the accessible name, suppressing the current value that <SelectValue/> renders — and the resulting name is not even unique on its own route.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147. Measured live: `{ "combobox named exactly 'Color space'": 1, "combobox whose name contains 'OKLab'": 0, "combobox whose name contains 'Shorter'": 0, "comboboxes matching /color space/i": 2 }`. The trigger's own text is "OKLab". The route's combobox names: ["Select view", "Select color space", "Color space", "Hue method"] — the picker's control reads "Lab" while this bar's reads "OKLab", both visible simultaneously in shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png.
defects.mechanism: aria-label overrides the content-derived name for role=combobox; the selected value has no other exposure because reka unmounts the listbox when closed, so aria-activedescendant does not exist at rest. Duplicating the visible label as an aria-label also defeats automated name-checks, because the name that is present is correct — it is the value that is missing, and nothing audits that.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — Playwright accessible-name matching against the live page: `page.getByRole("combobox", { name: /OKLab/ }).count()` → 0; `page.getByRole("combobox", { name: /color space/i }).count()` → 2. A screen-reader user hears 'Color space, combobox, collapsed' and is never told the space is OKLab.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui ships `Label` with `for?: string` and demo/ui/label/index.ts already re-exports it. Use `<Label for="mix-space">Color space</Label>` + a matching id on the trigger and DELETE the aria-label: the computed name then composes label + value the way the platform intends, the three orphan `<label>` elements (C-7) are cured by the same edit, and the ambiguity with the picker's control resolves for free.

defects.defect: `Distribute` — one of the three rows this bar's leftover-strategy Select offers — walks a non-monotonic source-index trajectory and emits a palette that doubles back on itself, contradicting its own documented contract.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/mix.ts:7 documents 'linearly interpolate shorter palettes across the longest length'; :79-81 returns the exact source color for every index < len, so only indices past the end reach the :90-103 distribute branch whose formula `fracPos = (index * (len - 1)) / (resultLength - 1)` was written for the whole range. Measured trajectory for len=3, resultLength=7: `0, 1, 2, 1.0000, 1.3333, 1.6667, 2.0000` — a backward jump from 2 to 1 at i=3. Measured output hues: 29°, 142°, 264°, 142°, 183°, 223°, 264° — row 3 byte-identical to row 1, row 6 to row 2.
defects.mechanism: Two remapping rules over one index range: an identity rule for i < len and an interpolation rule for i >= len, which do not agree at the seam. The interpolation formula is correct on its own; the short-circuit that precedes it is what breaks monotonicity.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — `mixPalettes([{colors:[#ff0000,#00ff00,#0000ff]}, {colors: 7×#808080}], { space: "oklch", hueMethod: "shorter", leftoverStrategy: "distribute" })` returns 7 rows whose 4th equals its 2nd and whose 7th equals its 3rd.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `index < len` short-circuit for this strategy and let the single fracPos formula own the whole range — it already reduces to the identity when resultLength === len. One branch removed, not one added.

defects.defect: The Hue-method quartet — the component's headline preview — interpolates between hues that are pure numerical noise whenever an operand is neutral, so four visibly different arcs are shown for a choice that is meaningless.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:66-74. Measured: `#808080 -> hue 300°`, `#7f7f7f -> hue 340°`, `#c0c0c0 -> 300°`, `#404040 -> 0°`, `#ffffff -> 336°`, every one with saturation ~1e-16; only exactly-black returns `"none"`. src/color/anchors.ts:155-166 `encodedToHsv` yields hue 0 only when delta is exactly 0.
defects.mechanism: After the XYZ round trip a neutral color's channel deltas are ~1e-16 rather than exactly 0, so the hue formula divides dust by dust and amplifies it 360×. This is the repo's documented HSV hue-drift hazard living inside the preview feature.
defects.proposedCure: Carry `none` for a powerless hue the way the library already does for exact black — the channel type has the vocabulary one branch away. The honest predicate is an epsilon threshold on delta relative to max, not exact equality with 0.

defects.defect: Two props encode the same primitive fact (`mode`) with an invariant between them that nothing states and nothing checks.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:101-103 — `:show-leftover-strategy="mode === 'palettes'"` and `:operand-colors="mode === 'colors' ? selectedColors.map((sc) => sc.css) : []"`. MixConfigBar.vue:38-44's own doc comment relies on the coupling ('Palettes mode passes [] by the same restraint'). The `.map()` also mints a fresh array identity on every parent render, invalidating both computeds at :57 and :66.
defects.mechanism: Derived-state duplication at the interface: one primitive is projected twice in the parent, and the consumer's correctness depends on the two projections staying in agreement, which no type or assertion enforces.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural finding, not a runtime failure. Read MixPane.vue:101-103 against MixConfigBar.vue:36-44.
defects.proposedCure: Pass `mode` once and let the bar derive both facts, or pass `selectedColors` and let emptiness speak for itself with the `.map()` moved inside the computed — which removes the per-render identity churn as a side effect of removing the duplication.

defects.defect: The visual-audit harness cannot observe this component's failure class: a boundary-caught throw produces neither a console error nor a page error, so REPORT.json's clean /#/mix rows are not evidence of absence.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69 sets caught=true and returns `false`, explicitly halting propagation to app.config.errorHandler. During my live reproduction of a total pane-grid collapse, the Playwright listeners recorded `errors: none` for both `pageerror` and `console.error`. REPORT.json's four /#/mix rows all read `consoleErrors: [], pageErrors: [], overflowX: 0`.
defects.mechanism: An error boundary that owns the failure (correctly, to avoid a white screen) simultaneously erases every signal the audit harness samples, so the harness's error columns are structurally blind to any throw that the boundary catches.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — the R4-1 live reproduction, with page.on('pageerror') and page.on('console') attached throughout: `boundaryVisible: true, panes: 0` while both error arrays stayed empty.
defects.proposedCure: Have the visual harness also sample for the boundary's own signature (the `[role="alert"]` fallback text, or a count of `.pane-wrapper` against the expected layout) so a collapsed grid is recorded as a defect rather than as a clean route.

defects.defect: `data-mix-target` — the documented anchor the mix convergence lands on — is silently dropped and never reaches the DOM; the animation falls back to a guessed landing point. Compounded: the anchor's host element is also absent for the first ~281 ms of every re-mix.

Live (evidence/challengeC-probe3.mjs): `dataMixTargetCount: 0` while `platePresent: true, ghostDot: true`; ghost-dot attribute list = [data-v-292b9032, data-v-0f138735, aria-hidden, class, data-testid, data-variant, style]. F-B: the anchor also lives inside the `<Transition mode="out-in">` (:60) that serialises leave-then-enter, so it is absent at the `flush:"post"` tick where `collectStage` measures.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/evidence/challengeC-probe3.mjs (anchor count 0) and .../challengeC-probe10.mjs (281 ms arrival) against the dev server at http://localhost:9000.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the announced destination OUT of the `<Transition>` so one persistent box serves both phases, and stamp `data-mix-target` on that element — one this component owns, not on the glass-ui primitive. This subsumes the attribute fix and the 281 ms absence in one move. Separately relay a `v-bind="$attrs"` / `as`/`asChild` seam request to glass-ui (BH inbox), but do not wait on it.

defects.defect: NEW — corrects/completes prior r3 D-3: the plate's `vj-morph` enter transition is a TOTAL no-op, not a degraded one. The scoped `transition` shorthand deletes the transform and max-height channels, AND the scoped `.mix-plate--ghost` rule pins the one surviving channel (opacity) at both ends.

Scoped compilation gives `.mix-plate--ghost[data-v-0f138735]` = specificity (0,2,0), outranking `.vj-morph-enter-from/-to` (0,1,0) at demo/styles/animations.css:118-136. result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the checks that came back clean rather than a negative proof of soundness. Proved clean, each by direct evidence: (1) `verbatimModuleSyntax` compliant — :7 is `import type { MixResult }`, every other import is a used value. (2) Vue 3.5 idiom correct — reactive props destructure with default at :20-23 (vue@^3.5.34) compiles to `__props.result`, so reads in the computed (:36-40) and the async handler (:42-47) are fresh; no stale read. (6) No ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch→HSV round-trip, no `parseCssColor` — the component consumes pre-formatted CSS strings, so the live parseCssColor crash class does not touch it. (7) No WebGL. (8) No god module — 159 lines, one job, one default export. defects.defect: The dead Button vocabulary r1 found at this one call site is 96 call sites across the demo — glass-ui 7's Button has no `variant` prop at all, so every emphasis declaration in the app is inert and everything renders `emphasis="secondary" tone="neutral"`.
defects.evidence:
Producer contract glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts: ButtonProps = { emphasis?: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"; tone?; size?: "xs"|"sm"|"md"|"lg"; iconOnly?; loading?; type?; disabled?; class? } — NO `variant`. defects.mechanism: Vue attribute fallthrough is silent by design: an undeclared prop lands on the DOM element as a literal attribute and matches no selector. Note SelectTrigger DOES declare variant?: "default"|"ghost" (SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts:11), so the Select side of this file is unaffected; this is Button-only.

defects.mechanism: F6 (new family) — a named parameter whose name is false: the API's own vocabulary misdescribes its behaviour, so the divergence is invisible at every call site and survives code review. A probe-error margin (legitimate) is folded into a spec requirement (not legitimate), converting the parameter's meaning.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/floor-probe.mjs — prints the full table above. Or read ink.ts:110 against useContrastSafeColor.ts:350-352 and ExtractControls.vue:124.
defects.proposedCure: Split the requirement from the measurement in the type, not in a comment: `certifyAccentInk(css, surfaceL, opts: { floor?: number; headroom?: number } = {})`. Then, once L-18 lands `contrastRatio` in the library, delete the constant entirely — certify at the floor, VERIFY the delivered ratio against the live tint probe, and widen only when the probe disagrees. The headroom stops being a guessed 1.25 and becomes a measured quantity, which is what it was always pretending to be.

defects.defect: The inset hairline ring — the sole surviving justification for the hand-rolled k-rail div — paints nothing: the ring colour and the fill colour are the identical value, 1.00:1, in the state the route boots into.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:22 feeds `trackInk` to BOTH legs: `:style="{ background: gradient, backgroundColor: trackInk, boxShadow: `inset 0 0 0 1.5px ${trackInk}` }"`. Measured live in WebKit at http://localhost:9000/#/extract, boot state, on [data-o18="extract-k-rail"]: backgroundImage "none", backgroundColor "oklch(0.481452 0.0657404 28.6099)", boxShadow "oklch(0.481452 0.0657404 28.6099) 0px 0px 0px 1.5px inset" — byte-identical strings. Corroborated in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png: the k rail and the kC track render as two indistinguishable solid magenta capsules. Falsifies the component's own claim at :8-11 ('a certified identity edge independent of its gradient content in every state').
defects.mechanism: F4 promoted from documentation drift to behavioural defect — a designed affordance whose referent is its own background, so it can never contrast. Downstream of F2 (producer seam bypassed then reimplemented): the rail div exists only to deliver this ring, and the ring does not render, so the entire two-element scaffold buys nothing.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/extract and read getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-o18="extract-k-rail"]')) BEFORE uploading any image. backgroundColor === the colour inside boxShadow.
defects.proposedCure: Keep r2's `--slider-track-ring` producer token (glass-ui P2) — it is the right transposition — but change the value the consumer feeds it. `trackInk` is the fill's own ink and cannot contrast with itself; the correct referent already exists unused in the same module: `contrastInkFor(fillCss)` at ink.ts:127-146, which returns the WCAG-maximal neutral endpoint for a concrete opaque fill, or null when none clears. Released line: `'--slider-track-ring': contrastInkFor(gradientMid ?? trackInk) ?? 'transparent'` — not a masking fallback, because a ring that cannot be certified must not be drawn. Without this amendment the wave ships the same invisible ring through a cleaner seam.

defects.defect: The library computes WCAG contrast and never exports it, so the demo infers ratios by abusing `safeAccentColor` as an oracle — a 1e-9 floating-point identity test standing in for a missing accessor, directly in this component's dependency chain.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "contrastRatio" src/` → no output. luminance() is module-local at src/color/operations.ts:182, contrast() at src/color/operations.ts:195; src/subpaths/color.ts:41 exports safeAccentColor and nothing else from that cluster. The two workarounds this forces: (a) ink.ts:127-146 `contrastInkFor` walks both neutral endpoints and infers the answer from `Math.abs(lightness(result.value) - endpoint) < 1e-9` — 'did the walk leave my candidate where I put it?' as a proxy for 'did it already clear?'; (b) ink.ts:113-125 `certifyAccentInk` must certify-then-diff-every-channel with an epsilon to discover whether certification was needed at all. This is also the root cause of the four-homes floor duplication (demo/color-session/ink.ts:15-16, view-accent.ts:13, palettes-ramp.ts:83,88 — two of them the identical exported name `GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR = 3` in sibling files).
defects.mechanism: F2 extended one layer down — producer seam bypassed then reimplemented, at the library boundary this time: value.js publishes the ANSWER (safeAccentColor) and hides the QUESTION (contrast), so the consumer reconstructs the question from the answer's observable behaviour. The reconstruction is correct today and silently wrong the moment safeAccentColor's internal walk changes its termination behaviour.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "contrastRatio" src/ (empty); grep -n "^function contrast\|^function luminance" src/color/operations.ts (195, 182 — neither exported); then read ink.ts:127-146 and ink.ts:113-125 for the two workarounds.
defects.proposedCure: Promote what is already written: `@mkbabb/value.js/color` exports `contrastRatio(a: AnyColor, b: AnyColor, opts?: { quantized?: boolean }): Result<number, ColorIssue>`, plus a frozen `WCAG = { text: 4.5, largeText: 3, graphics: 3 }`. Both demo workarounds collapse to a comparison; all four duplicated floor declarations delete; L-16's headroom becomes measurable; and the O-18 contrast census gains a first-class oracle instead of a DOM probe. Pure src/ change — NOT blocked by the Glass BJ W4 pin, and the highest value-per-risk item in this report.

defects.defect: The palette→track-gradient string builder is implemented twice at two different altitudes — once in a feature composable, once inlined in a sibling component's script — so the concept 'an ordered palette rendered as a track ramp' has no owner.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:101-112 and demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:65-73: same algorithm, same `length === 1 ? 50 : (i/(n-1))*100` singleton guard, same `.toFixed(0)`, same `linear-gradient(to right, …)` join, same `"var(--muted)"` empty return. GenerateControls.vue:284 admits it in prose ('the extract k-slider pattern verbatim'). `grep -rn "linear-gradient(to right" demo/` returns 7 sites, 4 of them building an evenly-spaced ramp from a colour list. Neither copy lives in color-session/, where every other colour-string derivation in the demo lives.
defects.mechanism: F3 — one concept, N homes. No module owns it, so each consumer re-derives it at whatever altitude was convenient, and a design decision (the empty-state token `var(--muted)`) is smuggled through a data path where no consumer can override it.
defects.reproduction: diff the two computed blocks: sed -n '101,112p' demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts against sed -n '65,73p' demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue.
defects.proposedCure: `demo/color-session/palettes-ramp.ts` — which already owns ramp semantics — gains `paletteToTrackGradient(colors: readonly string[]): string | null`, returning null (NOT a CSS token) for empty so the consumer owns its own empty state, which under the wave's `--slider-track-bg: gradient ?? trackInk` cure it already does. Both call sites collapse to one line and the dead `var(--muted)` degenerate is deleted at source rather than worked around at the consumer.

defects.defect: The design system is imported by two contradictory routes fifteen lines apart in the same file: `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` (granular published subpath) and `../../ui/slider` (a one-line demo alias barrel onto the glass-ui ROOT barrel). Independently re-measured this pass; carried from r1/r2.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:98-99. demo/ui/slider/index.ts is one line in full: `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — while glass-ui 7.0.0's exports map ships `"./slider": {"import": "./dist/slider.js"}`. Measured: dist/glass-ui.js 25,239 bytes with 46 import edges vs dist/slider.js 71 bytes + dist/slider-DzqeQmMu.js 5,810 bytes; and in the live dev pre-bundle, node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui.js = 231,357 bytes vs @mkbabb_glass-ui_dock.js = 43,369 bytes — a 39× pre-bundle for one <Slider>. 18 of the 19 demo/ui barrels are pure one-line re-exports; demo/ui/alert/index.ts documents the species out loud ('This barrel previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation … B.W2 converted it to a re-export'). 48 demo files import through demo/ui/*; 6 through ui/slider specifically.
defects.mechanism: F3 (one concept, N homes) plus edict-2 legacy: the re-implementation the barrel wrapped is gone, but the wrapper that kept old import paths resolving stayed — the textbook migration shim. Honest scope: glass-ui declares sideEffects ['*.css'] so Rollup shakes production; the measured cost is the dev server, the pre-bundle, and two permanent contradictory idioms for one dependency.
defects.reproduction: ls -la node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/{glass-ui.js,slider.js,slider-DzqeQmMu.js} node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui{,_dock}.js ; grep -rn "ui/slider" demo/ ; for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do cat $f; done
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely — all 19 barrels — and rewrite its 48 consumers to the glass-ui subpath each actually wants (glass-ui publishes /slider, /card, /button, /badge, /select, /separator, /label, /popover, /dialog, /dropdown-menu, /collapsible, /switch, /tooltip, /forms). This makes glass-ui-first a structural fact rather than a convention, removes the 'is it demo/ui or glass-ui?' ambiguity permanently, and is the KISS answer: the wrapper directory does not earn its existence. Not blocked by the pin.

defects.defect: The glass-ui spectrum Slider thumb is 12×24 CSS px — below the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 24×24 minimum on the width axis — and it is the shipped design-system geometry, not a consumer override, so it is unfixable at the pinned consumer without a per-instance override that edict 5 forbids. Carried from r1/r2; independently re-measured and traced to its mechanism this pass.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json, /#/extract, ALL FOUR matrices: {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Number of colors"} and {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Chroma weight"}. Re-measured live with role confirmed: [{label:'Number of colors',role:'slider',w:12,h:24},{label:'Chroma weight',role:'slider',w:12,h:24}]. Mechanism traced in the shipped stylesheet: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb{width:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem) * .75);height:100%}` with `.glass-slider[data-size=md]{--slider-thumb-size:1.25rem}` overridden to 1rem at this size → 16 × 0.75 = 12px exactly. Both of this component's sliders are variant="spectrum"; every spectrum slider in the product inherits it.
defects.mechanism: F2 — the design system's own token arithmetic produces a sub-minimum target, so the defect is structural and fleet-wide rather than local. No SC 2.5.8 exception applies: the thumbs are not inline, not user-agent-controlled, not essential-by-presentation, and no equivalent larger target is offered.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/extract and measure getBoundingClientRect() on [role="slider"]; or grep -o '\.glass-slider\[data-variant=spectrum\] \.slider-thumb\[[^]]*\]{[^}]*}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css
defects.proposedCure: Design-preserving, at the design system (glass-ui P2/P4, blocked until Glass 8): keep the 12px visual pill — it is the instrument's deliberate fine register — and add a centred ::before hit expander sized ≥24×24 to `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb`. The activation target grows, the visual geometry survives, one producer rule fixes every consumer, and no pinned file is touched. Preferable to r2's proposed `--slider-thumb-size: 2rem`, which fixes compliance by making every spectrum slider visually coarser.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm). Seat spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; served tier matches. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: Component-level: the certified track ink is applied as a FIELD rather than an EDGE, inverting the pane hierarchy — a count control is painted as a full-width, full-chroma seed-tint slab (434x24 desktop, edge-to-edge mobile) while the drop zone, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 names "the stage", is a dashed hairline ghost. Pass 1 owns this reading and I confirm it against all four Safari captures. Pass-2-unique: the reservation law is violated on BOTH live readouts and pass 1 certified one of them SOUND — the kC readout overflows its 20px box by 7.16px (+36%) at EVERY legal value, and the k readout needs 21.73px for "16" in a 20px box. A false negative that closes a canon row is the most dangerous defect class in an audit record.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negatives (things I attacked and could NOT break, with positive evidence): (1) `demo/ui/slider/index.ts` is exactly one line, `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — no hand-rolled slider clone, edict 4 clean on that axis. (2) All three DockControl seats measure 40x40, clearing the 24x24 WCAG 2.5.8 floor. (3) The route's `namelessButtons: 3` is NOT attributable to this component — my name predicate honouring `title` finds all three seats NAMED and finds 5 nameless `radio-group__item` nodes belonging elsewhere; I overturn pass 1's attribution rather than inherit it. (4) `prefers-reduced-motion` is not independently violated: the app carries 56 reduced-motion blocks, this component animates only colour, and nothing animates a layout-forcing property. (5) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — every import in the file is a genuine value import. (6) Vue 3.5 idiom clean — reactive props destructure at :103-111 is correct; no template refs exist so `useTemplateRef` does not apply; no `defineModel` round-trip so no `shallowRef` need. (7) Edict 1 clean — 151 lines, one job, not a god module.

defects.defect: MAJOR (NEW — pass 1 missed it entirely). The kC readout reserves `w-5` (20.00px) for `chromaWeight.toFixed(1)`, which is three characters at every legal value in 0.0…1.5. It has never fit. `overflow: visible` so glyphs paint 7.16px outside their own border box while the flex solver allocates 20px — every spacing relation to the right of that span, including the gap before Reset, is permanently off by 7px in all four Safari captures.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:78. Live Playwright probe, string rendered in the span's own resolved font (Fira Code 11px): box width 20.00px; "0.5" = 27.16px; "1.5" = 27.16px; overflow: visible; text-align: start; flex-shrink: 1. Overflow +7.16px = +35.8% at EVERY legal value.
defects.mechanism: Reservation width chosen by eye (`w-5` = 1.25rem) instead of measured against the widest legal representation. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: "Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis."
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract. Measure: render `chromaWeight.toFixed(1)` output in the span's computed font and compare to its getBoundingClientRect().width. True at every value the slider can hold (min 0, max 1.5, step 0.1).
defects.proposedCure: Re-reserve against the MEASURED widest legal string (>=27.16px) and add `shrink-0`. Gestalt: this is the same class of error as P2-2 and the two should be cured by one rule — the axis composition should own a single reserved-value cell sized from metrology, not two independently eyeballed `w-5` literals. Filed as blocked-wave clause alpha.14.

defects.defect: MAJOR — OVERTURNS a certified negative in pass 1. Pass 1 §6 states "`w-5` reservation holds at the widest legal k … met (by 0.3 px, but met)". It is not met: "16" (the slider max, :29) needs 21.73px in a 20.00px box. The true margin is −1.73px, not +0.3px — the sign is inverted.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:15 (`w-5`), :29 (`:max="16"`). Live probe, label's own font (Fira Code 16.4px): box 20.00px; "1" = 10.87px; "16" = 21.73px → +1.73px overflow. Contrast pass 1's claim at challenge-D-design.md:458-460.
defects.mechanism: Method error, not arithmetic error. Pass 1 used `scrollWidth == clientWidth`, which is integer-rounded and does NOT report inline text overflowing a non-scrolling inline-level box — a <label> whose text exceeds its width still reports scrollWidth == clientWidth. Correct method is font metrology on the rendered string.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract, drag k to 16 (or set session.colorCount = 16). Render "16" into an off-DOM span carrying the label's resolved `font` and `font-variant-numeric`; compare advance (21.73px) to the label's border-box width (20.00px).
defects.proposedCure: Same single cure as P2-1 — one metrology-derived reserved-value cell in the shared axis composition. Separately: the audit record must not carry `scrollWidth == clientWidth` as an overflow predicate for inline text; that predicate produced a false SOUND on a binding canon clause and should be corrected wherever else it was used in this component sweep.

defects.defect: MAJOR (correction) — OVERTURNS pass 1 D-9's attribution. Pass 1 charges the route's `namelessButtons: 3` to this component's three DockControls, calling them "exactly this component's three controls" while printing their names as proof. All three are accessibly NAMED via `title` (a valid accname fallback). The route's actual nameless buttons are five `radio-group__item` nodes belonging to a different component.
defects.evidence: REPORT.md:98,105,110,112 shows `namelessButtons: 3` for /#/extract in all four matrices. Pass 1's own output at challenge-D-design.md:257 is self-refuting: `nameless [('Upload image', 40, 40), ('Open camera', 40, 40), ('Reset', 40, 40)]` — it names all three. My probe with predicate `aria-label || title || textContent`: 29 buttons on route, 5 nameless, ALL of them `<button data-slot="radio-group-item" class="radio-group__item shrink-0">` at 44x44 with no title/aria-label/text. The three ExtractControls seats: title="Upload image"/"Open camera"/"Reset", each 40x40 → NAMED.
defects.mechanism: Pass 1's probe predicate excluded `title` from accessible-name computation. Per accname step 2I, `title` is a valid name source when nothing else supplies one, so a <button title="…"> with an SVG child has that accessible name.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract; enumerate document.querySelectorAll('button') and compute name as aria-label || title || textContent. Result: 5 nameless radio-group-item nodes; the three DockControls named.
defects.proposedCure: Strike the `namelessButtons` justification from blocked-wave clause alpha.6 and re-home that row to its true owner via the visual-audit owner. KEEP the cure itself — the real defect survives and is different: all three actions are icon-only and disclose meaning SOLELY through `title`, which is hover-only and touch-unreachable, where 2 of the 4 audit matrices live (PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 / PR-16 / §5.6). Cure = visible text labels or a non-hover-only affordance.

defects.defect: BLOCKER (confirmed) with CORRECTED MECHANISM. Two `<DockSeparator />` render 0px tall while consuming 26px of the control row and announcing `role="separator"` to AT. Pass 1 found the symptom and the canon violation correctly but attributed it to a missing `align-self: stretch`; the real cause is an undefined custom property, and pass 1's proposed producer cure (beta4) would therefore not work.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:57 and :81. Live probe on the separator element: computed height `0px`; `getPropertyValue('--dock-separator-height')` → EMPTY; margin `0px 6px`; role `separator`; sepCount 2. Producer rule (glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/controls/): `.dock-separator { width: 1px; height: var(--dock-separator-height); margin: 0 0.375rem; background: var(--surface-tint-15); }`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 + PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 rule the divider count ZERO for every non-Admin composition; Extract is a P122 InstrumentChassis member per §3.1.
defects.mechanism: `DockSeparator` is a dock-scoped primitive whose height is EXPLICITLY declared from `--dock-separator-height`, a token the Dock chassis supplies. Rendered inside a workbench plate the property has no substitution value, `height` resolves to `unset` → `auto`, and an empty div is 0px. `align-self` never enters it — an explicit `height: auto` beats stretch. Triple defect: canon says count must be 0 (measured 2); the primitive is not portable and draws nothing; and `role="separator"` with no `aria-hidden` announces a boundary that has zero pixels, so sighted and non-sighted users receive different structures.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract; query `.dock-separator` inside the extract control row; read computed `height` (0px) and `getPropertyValue('--dock-separator-height')` (empty). Visually confirm in any of the four Safari captures: the gap between the camera icon and `kC` is empty whitespace.
defects.proposedCure: DELETE both — PR-05 already rules the disposition REMOVE, and spacing plus material already carries the boundary (PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.4). Quantified payoff: returns 26px to the row; at a 300px plate the kC track measures 68.46px, so deletion is a +38% track (68.46 → ~94.5). AMEND blocked-wave beta4: strike 'align-self: stretch'; the only producer options are a token fallback `var(--dock-separator-height, <intrinsic>)` or documenting the primitive Dock-band-only — the latter preferred, which makes beta4 fully moot once the consumer deletion lands and reduces the Glass 8 obligation to beta1/beta2/beta3 alone.

defects.defect: MINOR (correction) — OVERTURNS pass 1 §4's "No motion finding". Pass 1 measured `0.2s` and concluded the icon transitions resolve through `--duration-fast` (150ms), which the measurement itself contradicts. The icons run on Tailwind's built-in default while the producer's own track in the SAME rendered row runs on producer tokens — two motion registers in one component.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:45, :54, :89 (`transition-colors`). Live probe: transition-duration `0.2s` (not 0.15s = --duration-fast), transition-property `color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, --tw-gradient-*`. Producer `.slider-track` rule read from the live stylesheet: `transition: background var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard), border-color …`. Also measured: the hand-rolled rail div computes `transition: all`.
defects.mechanism: `transition-colors` is Tailwind's ad-hoc utility carrying Tailwind's own 200ms default; it does not consume glass-ui's `--duration-*`/`--ease-*`. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 (one producer-owned register; colour/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve). The `transition: all` on the rail additionally means the k gradient SNAPS on every k change while the sibling kC track fades.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract; getComputedStyle on any of the three lucide <svg> icons in the control row → transitionDuration `0.2s`. Compare to the sibling `.slider-track` producer rule.
defects.proposedCure: Icons consume `var(--duration-fast)` / `var(--ease-standard)` so one register governs the row; drop `transition: all` on the rail (which disappears entirely with the D-3/pass-1 cure that deletes the hand-rolled rail scaffold). NOTE the negative that survives: prefers-reduced-motion is NOT independently violated — the app carries 56 reduced-motion blocks, this component animates colour only, and nothing animates a layout-forcing property. The defect is tokenisation and register consistency, not reduced-motion.

defects.defect: MAJOR (confirmed, strengthened). The `.touch-gate-target` affordance was half-copied: this component ships the stylesheet for the touch gate and neither the class nor the composable, so its two sliders get neither pointer-capture recovery nor a target floor — while carrying dead CSS that claims both. Both thumbs measure 12x24, half the 24x24 WCAG 2.5.8 minimum, on desktop AND mobile.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:139-142 declares `.touch-gate-target { border-radius: var(--radius-pill); }` under the comment "Touch gate styling for extract sliders". Live probe: `querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target').length` inside the cluster → 0. Both `.slider-thumb` nodes measure 12 x 24. Independently in REPORT.json for safari-desktop-light /#/extract (identical rows in all four matrices): {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Number of colors"} and {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Chroma weight"}. Sibling implementation: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:58 applies the class and drives it from ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts.
defects.mechanism: Because the block is `scoped` it carries a `[data-v-…]` attribute selector and can only ever match elements in THIS template — so it is provably dead, not merely unused. Meanwhile the component fused visual glyph size with operable target size, which PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 explicitly separates: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities. Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome."
defects.reproduction: Load /#/extract; `document.querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target').length` within the extract control cluster → 0; `grep -rn "touch-gate-target" demo/ | grep extract` returns only ExtractControls.vue:140, the rule itself. Thumb rects: 12x24 on both axes, all four Safari matrices.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead rule. The target floor is the ONE genuinely producer-blocked item: glass-ui 8 must ship a thumb whose operable seat is >=24x24 CSS px while the visible glyph stays 12x24 (blocked-wave beta2) — a consumer cannot supply it without a per-instance override, which owner edict 5 forbids. Do NOT cure by fattening the glyph.

defects.defect: INFO — coverage gap in the tracked record. The forced-colors, RTL (desktop+mobile), 200%-zoom and reduced-motion capture matrices exist but do not contain this route, so two of pass 1's findings (D-1 forced-colors, D-13 RTL) rest on seat-local evidence with no tracked frame pair.
defects.evidence: `ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/` → adminusers.png, blob.png, browse.png, gradient.png, picker.png. Identical five-file contents for reduced-motion-desktop/, rtl-desktop/, rtl-mobile/, zoom-200-desktop/. `extract` appears in none of them. Additionally measured: the k rail is a text-less <div> whose entire information content is background-color + box-shadow with `forced-color-adjust: auto`, and the app's 9 forced-colors blocks contain nothing targeting this component.
defects.mechanism: The 60-capture Safari matrix covered 4 light/dark x desktop/mobile arms across 15 routes but the five state matrices were run on a 5-route subset that excludes /#/extract. defects.defect: `useImageQuantize` holds a single pendingResolve/pendingReject pair, so an overlapping quantize orphans the previous promise permanently, and `isProcessing` is cleared by the first worker response while a second job is still queued — the UI declares 'done' and paints a result that is about to be silently replaced.

Overlap measured — reachable only because the k slider stays live during processing (C2-1's unbound disabled): posts [{t:8115,opts:{k:5,…},bytes:24000000},{t:8531,opts:{k:9,…},bytes:24000000}], 416 ms apart, both in flight.
defects.mechanism: Request/response worker without request identity: a single mutable continuation slot cannot represent more than one outstanding job.
