Library default: `grep -o "targetPixels[^,;)]*" node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/quantize.js` → `targetPixels ?? 1e4`. useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 imageFileToPixels does a full-resolution getImageData; :93 `pixels.buffer.slice(0)` copies it again; :102-103 buildOptions constructs only {k, chromaWeight} and never targetPixels. Retention twin: previewDataUrl (useExtractSession.ts:166) holds the whole file as base64 — measured dataUrlChars 54294 for a 40704-byte PNG (~1.33×), and that string is also the .
defects.mechanism: Full-resolution decode at the boundary with downsampling deferred to the consumer inside the worker; the library's own guard option is never passed.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe3.mjs stage B — generate a 3000×2000 PNG, setInputFiles, read window.__wpm[0].bytes.
defects.proposedCure: Downsample where the pixels are first produced: size the OffscreenCanvas from a √targetPixels-derived geometry instead of bitmap.width × bitmap.height. One line of geometry removes both main-thread copies and the transfer; set previewDataUrl only after a successful decode.

defects.defect: `variant="spectrum"` is misused on the kC slider. glass-ui's spectrum variant zeroes `.slider-range`'s background by contract because it assumes the track IS the data; kC's track is a flat certified ink, so the value-fill paints nothing and the pixels left of the thumb are identical to those right of it.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:69 variant="spectrum" with :75 `--slider-track-bg: trackInk` (a flat colour, no gradient). glass-ui.css: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{ -webkit-backdrop-filter:none;box-shadow:none;background:0 0 }`. Measured live: {"name":"Chroma weight","rangeBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","rangeImg":"none","trackBg":"oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)","rangeW":76.8,"trackW":230.5} — a 76.8 px fill region on a 230.5 px track that paints nothing. Visually corroborated: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/extract.png shows a uniform crimson bar with a lone white thumb. The O-18 census samples this element and passes because it measures the track COLOUR (e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1106,1126), never the fill-vs-remainder distinction.
defects.mechanism: A design-system variant selected against its documented contract; the variant's defining behaviour (no fill) is only correct when the track carries a gradient, which is true for the k slider and false for kC.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe1.mjs stage 1 — read computed backgroundColor/backgroundImage and box widths of .slider-range and .slider-track inside each glass-slider root on /#/extract.
defects.proposedCure: kC has no spectrum — use the `standard` variant so .slider-range paints its liquid fill and the value is readable without the thumb. Reuse the design system correctly instead of styling around it.

defects.defect: Neither slider exposes `aria-valuetext`, violating the repo's own ratified BR-4 law ('every channel slider exposes a HUMAN-READABLE, unit-aware aria-valuetext'); the oracle that enforces it enumerates only the default route's main region, so the Extract pane is never visited — a vacuous gate, not a passing component.
defects.evidence: Measured: [{label:'Number of colors',role:'slider',valuenow:'5',valuetext:null,min:'1',max:'16'},{label:'Chroma weight',role:'slider',valuenow:'0.5',valuetext:null,min:'0',max:'1.5'}]. Law text: e2e/smoke/oracles/o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts:24-29. Gate scope: o27:140-160 does `await page.goto("/")` with NO openView, then enumerates getByRole('main',{name:'Color tool panes'}).getByRole('slider') — the Extract pane is a lazy KeepAlive pane the default route never opens. Second-order: at kC=1.0 the thumb announces aria-valuenow="1" while the visible readout (ExtractControls.vue:78 toFixed(1)) reads "1.0"; neither carries a unit.
defects.mechanism: A universally-worded law enforced by a route-local oracle; the component sits outside the oracle's traversal.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe2.mjs stages A and B — read aria-valuetext/aria-valuenow off both role=slider thumbs on /#/extract and after 11 ArrowRight presses.
defects.proposedCure: Use the demo's existing formatter and delivery leg (demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/sliderAnnouncement.ts + useSliderAnnouncements.ts) rather than inventing a second announcement idiom, and widen o27's BR-4 assertion from 'the default route's main' to every route that mounts a slider, so the law's own words are what the gate tests.

defects.defect: `trackInk` is a render-path computed guarded only by truthiness that calls into a stack which throws on four measured input classes — including `oklch()`, which reproduces the repo's recorded R1 parseCssColor shipping-crash signature. Inputs that fail to parse WITHOUT throwing are echoed back unchanged, so invalid CSS reaches background-color/box-shadow and the 'certified' rail silently loses both its fill and its identity ring.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:123-125 guards with `cssColor ?` only. Measured against the real module: {"in":"oklch()","THREW":"TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g[0].replace')"}, {"in":"oklch(none none none)","THREW":"Error: Ink certification failed: color_missing_channel"}, {"in":"transparent","THREW":"…color_invalid_input"}, {"in":"rgb(0 0 0 / 0)","THREW":"…color_invalid_input"}; and the echo class: "NaN"→"NaN", "#"→"#", "var(--nope)"→"var(--nope)". ink.ts:38-43 parseOklch handles !parsed.ok but not a throw; ink.ts:135 returns the input on parse failure.
defects.mechanism: Wrong guard shape — a truthiness check in front of a partial function that both throws and silently echoes; a throw inside a computed feeding an inline :style is a subtree render error, not a pixel error.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe5.mjs stage A2 — in-page import of demo/color-session/ink.ts, then certifyAccentInk over 15 boundary inputs. REACHABILITY CAVEAT, stated honestly: cssColor arrives as cssColorOpaque ?? '' (ExtractWorkbench.vue:69), which is serializePickerColor(withAlpha(color,1)) — opaque by construction — so I did NOT demonstrate a live throwing input from this component's own prop. The guard shape and the throwing input classes are measured; live reachability is a HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: Make certifyAccentInk return the demo's own Result shape instead of throwing-or-echoing; the consumer then has one honest branch and the certified de-emphasis token (`var(--ink-muted)`, which :124 already names) becomes the TYPED degenerate instead of an accident.

defects.defect: The k rail is a hand-rolled reimplementation of glass-ui's `.slider-track`: the real track is blanked with `--slider-track-bg: transparent` and an absolutely-positioned sibling div is painted instead, with a hardcoded `h-6` duplicating glass-ui's token-derived track height. The same file proves the mechanism is unnecessary 43 lines below.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:19-23 (`absolute inset-0 rounded-full overflow-hidden h-6` + three inline style properties) and :32 (`--slider-track-bg: transparent`) vs :75, where the kC slider passes a colour straight into the same custom property. glass-ui.css: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track{ height:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem) * 1.5); background:var(--slider-track-bg,var(--secondary)) }`. Measured rail box {x:173,y:535,w:434,h:24} — the hardcoded 24 px and the derived 24 px agree today and desynchronize the moment --slider-thumb-size moves.
defects.mechanism: Two mechanisms for one job in one file; a hardcoded literal shadowing a token-derived value.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe4.mjs — read the rail's inline style attribute and bounding box; compare with the glass-ui rule text above.
defects.proposedCure: Pass the gradient straight into `--slider-track-bg`. That deletes the div, the absolute inset-0, the overflow-hidden, the hardcoded 24 px, and the hit-test coincidence that pass 1 had to measure to prove was safe. Edicts #3/#4/#5.

defects.defect: The rendered slider puts `aria-label` and `aria-disabled` on a roleless <span> (implicit role generic, where both are ARIA-prohibited), and duplicates the accessible name across the root and the thumb.
defects.evidence: Measured: [{tag:'SPAN',role:null,ariaLabel:'Number of colors',ariaDisabled:'false',cls:'glass-slider relative w-full',thumbLabels:['Number of colors']},{tag:'SPAN',role:null,ariaLabel:'Chroma weight',ariaDisabled:'false',cls:'glass-slider flex-1',thumbLabels:['Chroma weight']}]. The duplication is self-evidencing — a [aria-label="Chroma weight"] locator is ambiguous: 'strict mode violation: locator(…) resolved to 2 elements: 1) <span data-slot="slider" aria-disabled="false" aria-label="Chroma weight" class="glass-slider flex-1"> 2) <span tabindex="0" role="slider" aria-valuenow="0.5" aria-label="Chroma weight" class="slider-thumb …">'. ARIA 1.2 prohibits aria-label on role=generic (axe rule aria-prohibited-attr).
defects.mechanism: glass-ui forwards the consumer's aria-label to both the root and the thumb; the consumer's only lever is that one prop.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe2.mjs stage B — enumerate [data-slot="slider"] and read role/aria-label/aria-disabled plus the nested role=slider labels.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui relay, NOT a consumer patch (edict #4): glass-ui 8 must name only the role="slider" thumb and leave no aria-label/aria-disabled on the roleless root. Filed as blocked-wave step XC2-7 with that as an explicit release condition.

defects.defect: `useSafeAccentFn`, called unconditionally by this component, injects INK_AMBIENT_KEY with a non-null assertion and no default, so mounting outside the boot provider throws inside a render computed — while the component's own parent defends the sibling injection key with an explicit default.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:118 `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("resting")` → useContrastSafeColor.ts:347 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!;`. Contrast: ExtractWorkbench.vue:218 `inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY, undefined)`; demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:128 and demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:95 both use `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null)`. This composable is the outlier.
defects.mechanism: Two injection keys with contradictory contracts inside one subtree; the assertion converts a wiring omission into a render-time TypeError.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis by code read. No route in the app mounts ExtractControls outside the App.vue provider tree today.
defects.proposedCure: `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null)` with an explicit degenerate branch, matching the two existing consumers, so the missing-provider case is a typed state rather than a crash.

defects.defect: At the k slider's own declared minimum (:min="1"), and for any image the quantizer collapses to one cluster, the rail's 'DATA layer' degenerates to a one-stop gradient that paints a flat wash — indistinguishable in kind from the undeveloped state the header comment says it occludes.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:28 `:min="1"`; useExtractSession.ts:104-111 emits `${css} 50%` as the sole stop when length === 1. Measured in WebKit after ArrowLeft ×4 on a four-colour image: inlineStyleAttr 'background: linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.653565 0.039943 87.79792) 50%) oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)'. Reproduces from a SOLID-colour image at k=5 (library `dedupeThreshold ?? .02` collapses it). HONEST NEGATIVE: the one-stop gradient is VALID — CSS Images 4 permits a single stop and WebKit agrees ({"oneStopAccepted":"linear-gradient(to right, red 50%)","cssSupports":true}) — so this is NOT a malformed-CSS defect and must not be filed as one.
defects.mechanism: A degenerate cardinality (n=1) flowing through a formatter written for n≥2, producing a syntactically valid but semantically empty encoding; compounded by :22 painting the identity ring and the fill with the same token, so every visual channel the rail owns is simultaneously degenerate.
defects.reproduction: evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe4.mjs stages 2 and 3 — upload a 200×200 four-quadrant PNG, drive k to 1, read the rail's inline style; then upload a 200×200 solid PNG at k=5.
defects.proposedCure: Make the single-cluster state an explicit branch rather than a degenerate gradient, and separate ring from fill (the ring's job is separation from the plate, so it should carry the certified ink while the fill carries the de-emphasis rung — not the same token twice).

defects.defect: Vacuous gate — no unit test references this component, and six single-token mutations survive all three e2e specs that touch its tree.
defects.evidence: Surviving mutations: (a) delete variant="spectrum" from the k slider — o18 samples [data-o18="extract-k-rail"], the sibling div, not the slider; (b) :min="1" → :min="0" — no gate asserts either bound; (c) toFixed(1) → toFixed(0) — nothing reads the readout; (d) delete aria-label="Chroma weight" — only the k slider is located by name (o9-shadow-palette); (e) delete @click="$emit('camera')" — no gate activates the camera; (f) replace trackInk with the literal "red" — o18 asserts a contrast RATIO (o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1106,1126,1133) and a saturated red clears the 3:1 graphics floor on this plate. o27 never visits the route at all (C2-7).
defects.mechanism: Gates assert rendered colour and DOM hooks, never the component's contract (prop propagation, emission arity, accessible names), so the entire behavioural surface is unguarded.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "ExtractControls" test/ e2e/` returns no spec; the three touching specs are e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:147-158, o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1106-1134, and o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts (route never opened).
defects.proposedCure: One @vue/test-utils spec asserting the CONTRACT rather than the paint: that `disabled` reaches all four controls (kills C2-1's enabling defect), that both sliders expose aria-valuetext (C2-7), and that one update:k emission produces exactly one quantize request (C2-3/C2-4). test/ is not under the BJ W4 pin — this can land immediately.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface) under demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: BLOCKER — the demo speaks a `WatercolorDot` prop contract that glass-ui 7.0.0 does not implement. `tag`, `aria-label`, `:disabled`, `@click` and `data-*` are all silently discarded by the component, whose root is a decorative `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. Both of the Mix workbench's colors-mode add-a-color affordances are therefore DEAD, so colors mode cannot be used at all on the running application.
defects.evidence: API: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts declares exactly {color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed} — no `tag`. Call sites: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:163-176 and :211-221 pass tag="button" + aria-label + :disabled + @click. Live DOM (localhost:9000/#/mix, 390x844), document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost').__vnode: {"vnodeProps":["aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"],"hasOnClickProp":false,"tag":"SPAN","aria":null,"pointerEventsSelf":"none"}; document-wide {"ariaLabelAnywhere":0,"elementsWithTagAttr":0}. `--watercolor-color: oklch(56.84% 0.0657 28.61deg)` is present, proving the `color` prop DID arrive, so the addCurrentColor guard at MixSourceSelector.vue:69-73 is not the cause. Blast radius: 12 files / ~25 `tag=` sites (grep -rc 'tag="' over WatercolorDot consumers).
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency at a package boundary: the demo needed an interactive swatch and invented one by prop-guessing against a decorative design-system primitive instead of asking glass-ui for the affordance. Unswept W44 'Glass 7.0.0 adopted whole' fallout — the adoption swept imports, not prop contracts. Vue routes unknown props to fallthrough attrs and vue-tsc does not reject extra attributes on a component tag, so the contract evaporates invisibly.
defects.reproduction: 1) Real Playwright click on `.add-slot-ghost` -> TimeoutError after 5s, log: `<div class="swatch-row …"> intercepts pointer events`, retried 14x (glass-ui sets pointer-events:none inline). 2) Two programmatic el.click() calls, which bypass hit-testing entirely, + 450ms settle -> document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-source]').length === 0; no color added; the listener was never attached. 3) document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]').length === 0 document-wide. Corroborating: e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:53 selects getByRole('button',{name:'Add current color to the mix'}) — zero DOM matches, so that oracle can only be failing or unrun. npx eslint over the four Mix SFCs: 0 problems. No unit test names any Mix component.
defects.proposedCure: Two moves, no new wrapper component (edict 3). (1) Demo-side now: make the host the control and the dot the face — the idiom this very file already uses correctly at MixSourceSelector.vue:245-263 and :132-158 — `<button type="button" class="add-slot-ghost" aria-label=… :disabled="!canAddColor" @click="addCurrentColor"><WatercolorDot … class="pointer-events-none"/></button>`. (2) Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox (standing fond): either declare `tag`/`as` as a real polymorphic root with attr+listener pass-through, or publish a WatercolorSwatchButton. (3) Structural gate: a DOM-level assertion in demo/test/ that every @click/aria-label lands on an element present in the rendered accessibility tree — this class of defect is invisible to vue-tsc by design and needs a runtime gate.

defects.defect: MAJOR — `[data-mix-target]` can never exist, so mixStage's invented-geometry fallback is not a latent risk (as pass B filed it) but the ONLY branch ever taken. The mix convergence has never landed on the result plate's well; it lands on fabricated coordinates.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:64-72 stamps `data-mix-target` as a fallthrough attribute on a <WatercolorDot>, which discards fallthrough attrs (see C-1's vnode-props measurement: only aria-hidden, class, data-testid, data-variant, style survive). Live measurement with a Mix pane mounted: document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-target]').length === 0. Consumer: demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:121-123 — `const targetEl = root.querySelector('[data-mix-target]'); const target = targetEl ? layoutCenter(targetEl, root) : { x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28 };`. Contrast: data-mix-source survives because it sits on a plain <div> (MixSourceSelector.vue:127-133) and on a real <button> (:245-263) — never on a WatercolorDot.
defects.mechanism: A masking fallback (standing edict 2) concealing a dead structural contract. One anchor system with two homes — a plain wrapper for sources, a glass-ui component for the target — only one of which survives attribute fallthrough. MixPane.vue:63-66 and MixResultDisplay.vue's header both state in prose that the pigment pours into the well's silhouette; structurally it never has.
defects.reproduction: The DOM measurement `[data-mix-target].length === 0` with the Mix pane mounted, plus the vnode-props measurement in C-1, is the reproduction of the mechanism. The visual consequence (drops landing on a guessed point) is HYPOTHESIS until C-1 is cured and colors mode can be populated.
defects.proposedCure: Upgrades pass B's B-1 cure rather than replacing it. Move `data-mix-target` off the WatercolorDot onto the well's own wrapper element, matching how data-mix-source is already stamped, AND delete the `else` branch — a missing anchor must make collectStage return null and skip the narration, never fabricate geometry. Pass B's stronger transposition (pigment and element arrive as arguments; only geometry is measured from the DOM) subsumes both and should be the landing shape.

defects.defect: MAJOR — the shell's imperative pane-action channel is never bound in the mobile layout, so all three Mix dock actions (Clear / Mix / Copy result) are structurally unreachable on mobile, and the `?.()` masking swallows it silently.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/App.vue:319 `const mixPaneRef = ref<any>(null);`; :331 `mixPaneRef.value = currentConfig.value.right === "mix" ? el : null;` inside onDesktopRightMount — the ONLY assignment site; :315 comment says 'Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots'; :83-91 the mobile <PaneSlot> passes :component, :component-key, :component-props, :transition-name, :max, appear, :on-appeared and NO :on-mount (desktop slots at :105 and :131 do pass it); :39 <Dock :generic-action-bar="actionBar"> sits in the root <nav>, outside the isDesktop branch. demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:52 `onMount?: (instance: any) => void` — optional, so omission is silent. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:107-111 types all three handles Ref<any>; :219-222 dispatch `paneRefs.mix.value?.clearSelection?.()` / `?.startMix?.()` / `?.copyResult?.()`. Live at 390x844 on /#/mix: {"layout":"mobile","paneSlots":1,"hasMixHeader":true,"buttons":[…,"Clear","Mix","Copy result",…]} — pane mounted through the mobile slot, dock rendering all three actions.
defects.mechanism: Inverted ownership: the shell reaches INTO the pane instance through untyped Ref<any> handles and hardcodes three panes' private method names, and the binding is layout-conditional. The double optional-chain is a masking fallback (edict 2) that turns a missing binding into a silent no-op instead of an error.
defects.reproduction: The four measured facts above make the consequence deterministic. End-to-end button-press reproduction is HYPOTHESIS: I could not populate the pane to observe the no-op because C-1 kills both colors-mode add paths, and a scripted Palettes-mode selection did not take within the probe budget (selected: 0). The blocker blocks its own downstream verification.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the edge (pass A's F-9 cure, raised from type hygiene to shipped-behaviour correctness). The DockAction/DockActionBar types already exist at usePaneRouter.ts:36-56: add an ACTION_BAR injection key, have each workbench provide/write its own action list on mount and clear it on unmount, and have Dock read it. PaneActionRefs, three Ref<any>, nine ?.() masks, PaneSlot.onMount and the desktop/mobile fork all delete together, and the binding becomes layout-independent by construction because the publisher is the mounted component itself. It also makes `disabled` honest — today all three Mix dock actions are enabled at zero selection because the shell cannot see canMix.

defects.defect: MAJOR (independently re-measured; twice-confirmed with passes A/B) — the demo does NOT dogfood the published `exports` map for 5 of 7 subpaths. tsconfig.demo.json#paths shadows exports with hardcoded file paths, carries 3 keys naming a surface that no longer exists, and omits 2 real exports.
defects.evidence: tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 declares 8 keys; package.json#exports declares 7 different ones. Dead keys whose targets do not exist: `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (MISSING), `/parsing` -> ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts (MISSING), `/units` -> ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts (MISSING). Real exports with no paths entry: `/value`, `/css`. Measured with `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution` from demo/color-session/picker-color.ts, two sibling imports, two regimes: `/color` -> "'paths' option is specified … matched pattern '@mkbabb/value.js/color' … Trying substitution './dist/subpaths/color.d.ts'" (paths shadow); `/css` -> "Found 'package.json' … Entering conditional exports. Matched 'exports' condition 'types'. Using 'exports' subpath './css'" (the real consumer path). Header comment at tsconfig.demo.json:2-19 still describes 'the 8 public keys' incl. parsing/units.
defects.mechanism: A published-surface trust boundary asserted by comment and simulated by two hand-kept mirrors (tsconfig paths + the Vite generated alias) rather than exercised. Drift is undetectable because nothing fails when a paths key names a nonexistent file. The /css trace is the standing proof the paths block is unnecessary — TS self-name resolution through exports already works.
defects.reproduction: npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution 2>&1 | grep -B30 "Module name '@mkbabb/value.js/css' was successfully" — pasted in the report. Plus: for f in dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts; do [ -e $f ] || echo MISSING $f; done -> all three MISSING.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the whole @mkbabb/value.js* block from tsconfig.demo.json#paths (keep the vue/@vue/* dedupe entries). Self-name resolution through package.json#exports already reaches the correct .d.ts — proven by the /css trace — and a missing or renamed export then becomes a hard typecheck error instead of silence. Keep the Vite generated alias (a package cannot install itself at runtime), and add a one-line invariant test that the demo's set of @mkbabb/value.js/* specifiers is a subset of Object.keys(package.json.exports). SEQUENCING (per pass B's C-2): rebuild and align dist/ BEFORE deleting paths, or resolution falls through to the frozen tarball.

defects.defect: MAJOR (independently re-measured) — the published `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` duplicates the core color model as a nominally-distinct `*_2` shadow family. The seven subpath barrels are seven independently type-bundled islands with private copies of the shared model, not one lattice with one type identity.
defects.evidence: grep -nE '^declare type (Color|SpaceId|Alpha|Channel|ChannelsBySpace)(_2)?[<= ]' dist/subpaths/css.d.ts -> ten declarations where five suffice: Alpha:1/Alpha_2:3, Channel:37/Channel_2:39, ChannelsBySpace:41/:61, Color:102/Color_2:108, SpaceId:321/SpaceId_2:323 — each pair byte-identical in body. The published 4.0.0 snapshot at node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts declares each ONCE (lines 1,35,37,78,291). Byte diff: css.d.ts 12490 (local) vs 10910 (installed), +1580B; color.d.ts and color.js are byte-identical between the two. MixPane's cone reaches it via demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:28-34. Mechanism source: vite.config.ts:250-275 runs one vite-plugin-dts pass with rollupTypes:true over seven entries; the model is reachable from src/css by two module identities (src/css/types.ts:1 and src/css/grammar.ts:18,19, both -> ../color/model).
defects.mechanism: Ownership of `Color` is declared once in src/color/model.ts but MATERIALISED twice in the published artifact. Degenerate today (structural typing makes Color and Color_2 assignable), but it doubles the declaration surface and breaks the moment any of these types gains a unique symbol, a private brand, or a class — and picker-color.ts mixes /color and /css imports in one file.
defects.reproduction: The greps and byte diffs above, deterministic against the committed dist/ (built Jul 27 11:52). No rebuild needed.
defects.proposedCure: The core model is a package-level shared concept, so it must be a shared EMITTED declaration, not per-entry inlined. Give the seven subpaths a common src/subpaths/_model.ts re-export root and drop rollupTypes:true in favour of per-entry .d.ts that REFERENCE it — one declaration of Color, seven barrels importing it. That is the same acyclic-topology rule the source tree already obeys; the build is the only place it is violated.

defects.defect: MINOR — three parallel homes exist for the single concept 'a test of demo code'; pass A's F-14 sees one of them. The mix algebra's only test lives in the library test tree, and no Mix component has any unit coverage.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 (BLOCKER) — the Mix workbench's colors mode has NO working way to add a color, on the live dev server, at every viewport, because the demo asserts a `tag` / `aria-label` / `@click` / `:disabled` contract onto glass-ui 7.0.0's `WatercolorDot`, whose published prop surface is only {color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed} and whose root is a decorative `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">` that discards every consumer attribute and listener. Proved three independent ways: a real Playwright click times out with "swatch-row intercepts pointer events" (14 retries); two programmatic el.click() calls that bypass hit-testing add zero mix sources; and the vnode carries no onClick at all (`hasOnClickProp: false`, props = [aria-hidden, class, data-testid, data-variant, style]). This DISPLACES pass A's F-1 as the strongest defect across all three passes: F-1 is a measured wrong answer; C-1 is a measured absence of the ability to ask the question. It also corrects pass B's N-B5, which read the dead control in the Safari screenshot as a correctly-rendering drop target.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records the negatives I did prove — each is positive evidence that a suspected defect is absent, and each constrains the cure. (N-C2) Every value.js import in MixPane's entire transitive closure is a PUBLISHED subpath a real consumer could write: /color x25, /css x10, /math x6, /easing x5, /quantize x4 across the whole demo; zero `@src/*`, zero relative reaches into src/, zero bare-root imports (`grep -rhoE '@mkbabb/value\.js[^"'"'"']*' demo/`). The T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds at the SPECIFIER level — the defect (C-6a) is one layer down, in resolution. Third independent confirmation. (N-C3) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean: all eleven type-only imports across the eight files of the closure use `import type` (useMixingState.ts:19, mixStage.ts:17, MixConfigBar.vue:11, MixAnimationCanvas.vue:3, …). Zero violations. (N-C4) The one-clock discipline the code claims is the discipline it has: useMixingState.ts contains no setTimeout and no requestAnimationFrame; the only clock is useMixingAnimation's glass-ui useRAFLoop, and settleMix is its single downstream edge. (N-C1) glass-ui 7.0.0's published dist imports @mkbabb/value.js/color x7, /css x4, /easing x2 and the bare root ZERO times, and package.json#exports declares no "." — so the dead `"@mkbabb/value.js": ["./dist/index.d.ts"]` paths entry is inert, not a boot hazard. That is exactly why it survived. (C-6c counter-evidence) The PRODUCTION bundle is clean: dist/gh-pages/assets (built Jul 28 18:35) has 0 hits for seven glass-ui root-barrel members the demo never uses, so the demo/ui barrel finding is a structure defect only and must NOT be cited as a shipped-bundle cost — this settles pass B's N-B1 from the artifact rather than by reasoning about eager importers. (N-C5) The route renders without error — REPORT.md:123,138,153,168 give /#/mix overflowX 0, main 1, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, no blankOrNearBlank, no darkClassMissing across all four Safari matrices. This is a true negative about RENDERING and a false comfort about FUNCTION: it is the reason two prior expert passes, a hard CI typecheck, and `eslint --max-warnings=0` all reported green over a dead control. The single technique that found C-1 was comparing the rendered vnode props against the package's published .d.ts — what the demo says versus what the package accepts — and that comparison should run for every cross-package component contract in the constellation.

An empty mix result ([]) is saveable as a zero-colour palette, which then throws `colors[NaN].css` when re-mixed with the `repeat` or `distribute` strategy.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientCodeEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m], as declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the published ParseResult contract is a type-lie. src/css/types.ts:25-27 declares parseCssColor total (value-or-typed-failure, no throw channel); src/css/grammar.ts:181's `slash[0]!` is false whenever a color function body is empty, because splitTopLevel("", "/") === []. The demo consumes the contract exactly as declared (gradientParse.ts:91-94, `return parseCssColor(token).ok`) and is destroyed by it: typing `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), …)` — the exact mid-typing state of any user authoring an oklch stop — unmounts the ENTIRE two-pane <main> via the app-root ErrorBoundary (App.vue:50), emits ZERO console/pageerror/onerror output (ErrorBoundary.vue:68 `return false`), and "Try again" restores the seed gradient, destroying the user's authored text — directly falsifying the component's own stated invariant at GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40 ("WIP is never destroyed"). A component cannot defend an invariant against a partial function masquerading as a total one; the cure belongs in src/, and a demo-side try/catch must be refused as a masking fallback (edict 2).
result.negativeProof: Sound on several sub-axes, proven positively. (1) Published-surface discipline HOLDS: every @mkbabb/value.js import in the whole gradient subtree resolves through a package.json#exports subpath — gradientParse.ts:21 (/css); useGradientModel.ts:11, useGradientInterpolation.ts:8,9, useGradientCSS.ts:12,13 (/color); useGradientCSS.ts:20,24 (/easing); useGradientCSS.ts:25,29 (/css). `grep -rn 'from "@src|\.\./src/|dist/subpaths' demo/workbenches/gradient/` → 0 hits; `grep -rn "@src" demo/` → 0 hits; `grep -rn "\.\./demo\|@demo" src/` → 0 hits. A real external consumer could write every one of them. (2) The vite self-alias set is GENERATED from the exports map with anchored ^…$ regexes (vite.config.ts:41-50), so the demo structurally cannot resolve an unpublished subpath and a prefix rewrite cannot swallow a subpath specifier — the exact mechanism that would otherwise make the demo a false proof of the public API is correctly built. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied: the subject's four imports bind runtime values only; neighbours (useGradientModel.ts:11,12,13,17; useGradientInterpolation.ts:8; useGradientCSS.ts:12; GradientVisualizer.vue:22,25,26,28) all use `import type`. (4) Vue 3.5 idiom correct: useTemplateRef (:31), reactive props destructure with default (:16), typed defineEmits (:27). (8) useGradientInterpolation is not a dead export (useGradientModel.ts:14,86; GradientVisualizer.vue:23,79; easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:15,53). defects.defect: CSS <gradient> grammar — 301 lines of pure, Vue-free CSS-Images-L3 parser plus its serializer half — lives in demo/ although it is squarely the published library's domain, and the docblock justifying the demo's private re-tokenizer is FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT: parseCssValue preserves comma grouping exactly.

Measured: parseCssValue('linear-gradient(red 30%, blue)') => args=[list<space>[color:rgb, number:30%], color:rgb] (2 args); parseCssValue('linear-gradient(red, 30%, blue)') => args=[color:rgb, number:30%, color:rgb] (3 args) — STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT. defects.mechanism: Unique-semantic-ownership violated in the direction of absence: a concept in the library's declared domain has its only home one layer out, and the demo re-implements a private library primitive on a false premise about the public one. Two independent implementations of 'split CSS at paren depth 0'.
defects.reproduction: `node --input-type=module -e "import { parseCssValue } from './dist/subpaths/css.js'; for (const s of ['linear-gradient(red 30%, blue)','linear-gradient(red, 30%, blue)','linear-gradient(red,,blue)']) { const r=parseCssValue(s); console.log(s, r.ok && r.value.args.length); }"` → 2, 3, 2.
defects.proposedCure: Add parseCssGradient / serializeCssGradient to src/css and publish on the ./css subpath beside parseCssColor/serializeCssColor, IMPLEMENTED OVER parseCssValue's existing call/list tree — not over a new string splitter. Export splitTopLevel with a keepEmpty mode to close the one real gap (doubled/trailing-comma arity). gradientParse.ts then collapses to a thin projection CssGradient → {stops, intervals}, retaining only the demo-specific narrowing, the authored-literal preservation (line 18) and the easing seeding (:295-298). defects.defect: The glass plate the component asks for never paints: `.glass-wash` (a LIVE glass-ui ladder rung, @layer components) is defeated on the same element by `.hljs { background: transparent }`, which is UNLAYERED and therefore beats all layered normal declarations. Net effect is inverted — the editor is transparent in every normal matrix and opaque only under prefers-reduced-transparency, where an unlayered !important wins.
defects.evidence: Definition: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/ladder.css:1 `@layer components { … .glass-wash { background: var(--glass-plate-tinted); … } }`, reachable via demo/styles/foundation.css:56 `@import "@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles"` → index.css → glass.css → glass/ladder.css. Live token probe on the subject element: --glass-level "1", --glass-opacity-wash "0.30", --glass-bg-rung and --glass-plate-tinted both resolve to valid color-mix(), boxShadow = the glass rim (applied), supportsColorMixOklab true — the rule matches and applies. Yet editorBackground = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)". Defeater: demo/styles/hljs.css:56-60 `.hljs { color: var(--code-ink); background: transparent; font-family: … }`, with NO @layer in the file, @import'ed at foundation.css:81. Inversion: foundation.css:764 opens @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) at brace depth 0 (verified by parse) and :784-789 forces `background-color: var(--surface-reduced-opaque, var(--card)) !important` on .glass-wash — measured there as rgb(253, 245, 236) (live-03-reduced-transparency.png). Element class list: GradientCodeEditor.vue:93 `class="hljs … glass-wash …"`.
defects.mechanism: CSS Cascade 5 layer arbitration: unlayered NORMAL declarations beat all layered normal declarations; unlayered IMPORTANT beats unlayered normal. Two independent style owners (glass-ui's plate ladder, the demo's hljs ink theme) both claim `background` on one node, and the winner is decided by an accident of layer membership rather than by design — hljs.css's own docblock says 'The theme paints no background — the surface belongs to the plate (… the editor's glass wash)', but `background: transparent` is the opposite of not painting.
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient and evaluate getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[role="textbox"][aria-label="Gradient CSS"]')).backgroundColor → "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)", while the same element's --glass-plate-tinted resolves to a valid color-mix() and its box-shadow carries the glass rim.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `background: transparent` from hljs.css:58 — an ink theme declares ink and nothing else; or, if a reset is genuinely wanted, move hljs.css into @layer components so the two owners arbitrate by order rather than by layer accident. Structurally the deeper fix is L-4: one element should never compose two independently-owned surface claims — the plate belongs to the glass primitive and the ink to the theme, on different nodes. NOTE: this CORRECTS a prior pass which called .glass-wash a dead class with no definition in the default cascade; that grep missed dist/styles/glass/ladder.css.

defects.mechanism: glass-ui runs two distinct plate systems — the container ladder (.glass-wash/.glass-quiet/…) and the control plate (.field-control, --input-on-glass, --control-surface-border). The component selects the container system for a control, then re-implements the control system per-instance, violating edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance).

defects.proposedCure: NO installed glass-ui primitive fits a syntax-highlighted multi-line code field or an icon-trailing single-line code readout (Input/Textarea are native elements with zero slots). Per standing law this is a MARKED GLASS-FORWARD ASK, never a local restyle — relay to the glass-ui BH/BI inbox: a `CodeField` in ./forms, or more cheaply `.field-control[data-kind="code"]` — same plate, --radius-field, mono register, white-space: pre-wrap, the same data-state invalid/readonly/disabled contract, a contenteditable host, and an optional trailing-adornment slot for the copy/tune icons BOTH this editor and the OM-13 readout need. Consumers then inherit invalid-state, focus ring, readonly and disabled at the root, and OM-13 plus this finding are cured by one primitive. The demo must not restyle locally in the interim.

defects.defect: A runtime highlight.js chunk exists solely for this component, is switched OFF during the one activity it exists for (authoring), runs a third tokenizer over a string already tokenized twice in the same 500ms window, and sits beside a DEAD build-time highlighting facility. The previously-ledgered cost figure was wrong by 2.2x.
defects.evidence: Highlighting is off while focused: render() (:51-53) is called only from onMounted (:81), the model watcher (:76-79, gated `if (focused.value) return`) and onBlur (:68-73); onInput (:59-62) debounces the parse emit only. Measured token counts: MOUNT 9 → MID-TYPING(focus) 0 → AFTER DEBOUNCE 0 → AFTER BLUR 3. Corrected cost, bundled+minified as shipped: `npx esbuild hl.mjs --bundle --minify --format=esm` → 34,368 B; `gzip -9 -c | wc -c` → 12,670 B gz (a prior pass reported 27.9 KB gz by gzipping the two source files separately — 22,405 + 5,448 — which is not how a bundle ships). Dedicated chunk group at vite.config.ts:269-272. Mitigation: the pane is lazy (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74). Third tokenizer: hljs CSS grammar (paint) + gradientParse splitTopLevelCommas/tokenizeTopLevel (structure) + the library's splitTopLevel inside parseCssColor/parseCssScalar per token (validation). Spans already exist in the library vocabulary: ParseIssue carries start/end at src/css/types.ts:19-20. Dead build-time twin: plugins/vite-source-export.ts:14-16 ('No runtime formatting or highlighting libraries are needed'), with zero consumers per L-7.
defects.mechanism: A concept (tokenize this CSS string) has three live implementations, and the one that costs bytes is the one disabled when it would matter. The dependency is also mis-homed: highlight.js is a devDependency of the library package because the demo has no manifest of its own.
defects.reproduction: cd to a scratch dir; write hl.mjs importing highlight.js/lib/core + highlight.js/lib/languages/css and calling hljs.registerLanguage('css', css); run `npx esbuild hl.mjs --bundle --minify --format=esm --outfile=hl.bundle.js`; `wc -c hl.bundle.js` → 34368; `gzip -9 -c hl.bundle.js | wc -c` → 12670.
defects.proposedCure: Extend the L-2 parseCssGradient result with a `tokens: readonly {start,end,kind}[]` channel — the parser already walks the string, so emitting spans is bookkeeping, not new work — and paint from it. One tokenizer, one home, −12.7 KB gz from the route, and the highlighter and the validator can no longer disagree about the same text. Once glass-ui owns CodeField (L-4), the direct highlight.js import, the vendor-highlight chunk group and the truce logic delete together; a surviving truce belongs in the primitive as a documented `rehighlight: "blur" | "input"` policy.

defects.defect: demo/shared/utils.ts — the subject's only non-vendor import — is a two-unrelated-concepts junk drawer (a class-name merger and a timer) containing one dead symbol, and its 14-line docblock justifies itself by citing a library root barrel that does not exist.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:3 `import { debounce } from "../../../shared/utils";`. Docblock demo/shared/utils.ts:11-17 claims 'the library's root-barrel export stands for external consumers'. Measured: `grep -rn "debounce" src/` → no output; `node -e "const p=require('./package.json')"` → main: undefined, module: undefined, types: undefined, has "." export: false (only the seven subpaths ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize). Dead second occupant: demo/shared/utils.ts:4 `export function cn(...)`; `grep -rn "\bcn(" demo/ --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` → 1 hit, the definition itself; `grep -rn "import { cn }" demo/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: God-module seed (edict 1): a module named `utils` holding two unrelated concepts pre-authorises a home for the next unrelated helper. Compounded by legacy documentation of a dual path that was fully retired — a bare `import … from "@mkbabb/value.js"` is unresolvable for a real external consumer.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "debounce" src/` → empty; `node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); console.log('.' in p.exports, p.main, p.module)"` → false undefined undefined; `grep -rn "\bcn(" demo/` → only demo/shared/utils.ts:4.
defects.proposedCure: Delete cn and its clsx + tailwind-merge devDependencies if nothing else uses them; rename the module demo/shared/debounce.ts (one concept, one home); delete the stale docblock paragraph outright rather than amending it.

defects.defect: The 500ms debounce timer is never cancelled on unmount, so a pane switch within 500ms of a keystroke leaves a pending timer emitting into a torn-down tree.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-57 `const debouncedParse = debounce((text: string) => { emit("parse", text); }, 500);`. demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 shows the returned function carries .cancel(). All 117 lines of the SFC read: no onUnmounted, no .cancel() call. The pane is lazily mounted/unmounted on pane switch — demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74,87.
defects.mechanism: Lifecycle ownership gap: the component creates a timer whose lifetime exceeds its own, and the utility that hands it a cancel handle is never asked for one.
defects.reproduction: NONE — I did not exercise a mid-keystroke pane switch. Labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: onUnmounted(debouncedParse.cancel) — or, correctly, delete the concern: the debounce belongs inside the L-4 CodeField primitive, whose lifecycle owns its own timers.

defects.defect: A silent masking fallback returns the raw user string into an unescaped innerHTML sink.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:43-49 `function highlight(code){ try { return hljs.highlight(code,{language:"css"}).value; } catch { return code; } }` and :51-53 `function render(code){ if (editorRef.value) editorRef.value.innerHTML = highlight(code); }`. The success path is safe because hljs escapes its output; the catch arm returns the raw string, which line 52 writes to innerHTML unescaped.
defects.mechanism: Masking fallback (edict 2) sitting on an HTML-injection sink; the swallow also hides any real highlighter failure.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the injection consequence — hljs.highlight with a registered language did not throw in any probe, so I could not reach the catch arm. The silent swallow itself is a fact at :46. Labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: Let it throw, or write the fallback via textContent. Better: the sink disappears with L-4 — a primitive renders highlighted tokens as a vnode tree, never via innerHTML.

defects.defect: A leaf feature component mutates a process-global singleton registry at module-evaluation time, inside a package that declares itself side-effect-free — and the same singleton is mutated by a second owner at build time.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:5-8 `import hljs from "highlight.js/lib/core"; import css from "highlight.js/lib/languages/css"; hljs.registerLanguage("css", css);` at module scope. The same singleton is mutated for typescript at plugins/vite-source-export.ts:57-61 via a lazy dynamic import. `node -e "require('./package.json').sideEffects"` → false.
defects.mechanism: No module owns the hljs grammar registry; ordering is implicit and there are two writers with different lifetimes. The `"sideEffects": false` declaration tells bundlers no module in the tree has import-time effects, which line 8 contradicts.
defects.reproduction: `node -e "console.log(require('./package.json').sideEffects)"` → false, against GradientCodeEditor.vue:8. I did not produce a build in which the registration is tree-shaken away, so the DROP consequence is a hypothesis; the contradiction is a fact.
defects.proposedCure: Move the registration to wherever the highlighter is owned — glass-ui's CodeField (L-4) — which can register lazily on first use.

defects.defect: A multi-line contenteditable carrying role="textbox" omits aria-multiline, so assistive technology announces a single-line text field for a control that accepts and displays line breaks.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:88-93 — contenteditable="true", role="textbox", class includes whitespace-pre-wrap and min-h-[5rem]; no aria-multiline attribute anywhere in the file. Live DOM confirms the attribute is absent.
defects.mechanism: aria-multiline defaults to false; the visual and interaction affordance is multi-line, so the accessible name/role/value triple misdescribes the control.
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; document.querySelector('[role="textbox"][aria-label="Gradient CSS"]').getAttribute('aria-multiline') → null.
defects.proposedCure: aria-multiline="true" — but preferably solved once in the L-4 glass primitive, which should own the role wiring for every consumer rather than each call site restating it.

defects.defect: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/ holds two non-composables, one of which carries the `use` prefix while exporting zero composables — the directory and the prefix both misreport what the modules are.
defects.evidence: gradientParse.ts exports only ParsedGradientModel, GradientParseResult and parseGradientCSS (pure, no Vue import). useGradientCSS.ts exports COALESCE_RESOLUTION, linearInterval, easingFnOf, serializeGradient, CoalescedSample, sampleCoalescedStops, serializeIntervalRamp, serializeRailRamp — zero composables — yet carries the `use` prefix; it is consumed as the pure module it is at GradientVisualizer.vue:24 and gradientParse.ts:22. useGradientInterpolation.ts mixes a pure function (interpolateStopColors) with a real composable.
defects.mechanism: The `use` prefix is Vue's one hard signal that a module returns reactive state bound to a component instance; using it for a serializer library destroys that signal, and housing pure modules under composables/ compounds it.
defects.reproduction: `for f in demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/*.ts; do echo "--- $f"; grep -n "^export function\|^export const\|^export interface\|^export type" "$f"; done` → useGradientCSS.ts lists only pure functions and a constant.
defects.proposedCure: Rename useGradientCSS.ts → serialize.ts and gradientParse.ts → project.ts, and lift both out of composables/, reserving that directory for useGradientModel and useGradientInterpolation. Fold the surviving serializer core into the library per L-2.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingAuthoringStage.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, matches the model serving this turn; not inherited.

defects.defect: No library home for "an eased colour mix": @mkbabb/value.js/easing legitimately emits values outside [0,1] (the three `back` overshoot presets) while @mkbabb/value.js/color rejects exactly those values, and the library ships no composer. The demo owns the seam and does not adapt — it throws, annihilating the gradient pane with zero console output.
defects.evidence: src/color/operations.ts:65 and :90 — `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`. My browser-free re-derivation against the built dist: `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/easing.js')"` → bezierPresets count = 30; ease-out-back=[0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275] f(0.5)=1.0676 (>1); ease-in-back f(0.5)=-0.0636 (<0); ease-in-out-back max=1.0927 (>1). Throw sites: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (`fn(0.5)` straight into interpolateStopColors) → useGradientInterpolation.ts:37; and useGradientCSS.ts:202-207. ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69 returns false from onErrorCaptured, so nothing reaches the console — audit/visual/REPORT.md shows pageErr 0 / consoleErr 0 for /#/gradient. Aggravating: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/constants.d.ts declares DEFAULT_BEZIER_PRESET: "ease-out-back" — a picker mounted without modelValue crashes the pane on mount.
defects.mechanism: missing-library-module: two public subpaths of the same library have contradictory contracts at their composition point; the join has no home so it is performed ad hoc in the consumer
defects.reproduction: Analytic (this pass, browser-free): `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/easing.js').then(E=>{const f=E.CubicBezier(...E.bezierPresets['ease-out-back']).value; console.log(f(0.5))})"` → 1.0676 > 1, which useSpecimenRows.ts:56 feeds directly to mixColors. Browser (pass-1 assets, retained): `node scratchpad/wbL-probe8.mjs` clicks all 27 specimen tiles → TOTAL 27 CRASHED 3 = {ease-in-back, ease-out-back, ease-in-out-back}; `wbL-probe5.mjs` reaches the same crash through the SUBJECT component in 2 keystrokes (Shift+ArrowUp x2 on the second bezier handle).
defects.proposedCure: New first-class library module src/color/ramp.ts, public at @mkbabb/value.js/color: `easedMix(a,b,t,easing,opts & {overshoot?: "clamp"|"extrapolate"|"error"})` and `easedRamp(...)`, overshoot defaulting to "clamp" (CSS itself clamps easing output when interpolating non-numeric values). One rule, one home; both demo call sites collapse to a single call; the `back` family becomes usable instead of fatal. Do NOT clamp in the demo — that buries a library-contract mismatch in a consumer.

defects.defect: The seat reads and styles glass-ui's private DOM. Its "Law 3" (zero-letterbox, O-17) targets `svg[role='img']`; the shipped glass-ui 7.0.0 canvas is `role="group"`. Both the JS viewBox sync and all five CSS declarations are dead, so the producer's inline `aspect-ratio: 1` + `block-size: clamp(200px,38cqi,320px)` survive and the canvas letterboxes unconditionally.
defects.evidence: Static: `grep -o 'role: *"[a-z]*"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js | sort | uniq -c` → `1 role: "group" / 1 role: "slider" / 2 role: "status"` — zero `role: "img"`. Canvas at dist/easing.js:326-341. Live (Playwright/WebKit, http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, disclosure opened): {"roleImgMatches":0, "vbAttr":"0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002", "stageVbRatioVar":"1.2" (frozen), "computed":{"aspectRatio":"1 / 1","blockSize":"200px"}, "boxRect":{"w":272,"h":200}, "drawnPlot":{"w":166.7,"h":200}, "letterboxPxPerSide":{"x":52.7}, "deadPixelPct":38.7}. Pass 1 measured the identical defect at a 410px box: 243.3px / 59.3% empty — the drawn plot is 166.7x200 in both, so the letterbox is unconditional. Component sites: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:48-50 (querySelector) and :104 (stylesheet). Provenance: docs/tranches/U/audit/w-visual-close-artefacts.md:36 certified the law green under glass-ui 6.x; f2c8f565 adopted glass-ui 7.0.0 after a61094e3 and the file was never touched.
defects.mechanism: cross-boundary coupling to a producer's private render shape (an ARIA role) with no compile-time, test or lint binding — invisible to every gate
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click the sliders icon (aria-label="Author a custom curve"), then in the console: `const p=document.querySelector('[data-testid="easing-picker"]'); p.querySelectorAll("svg[role='img']").length` → 0; `getComputedStyle(p.querySelector('svg[viewBox]')).aspectRatio` → "1 / 1"; `.blockSize` → "200px".
defects.proposedCure: Do not patch the selector — that re-arms the trap. The law belongs to the producer, the only module that knows its own viewBox (useEasingPicker already publishes `viewBox: ComputedRef<{minY,height}>`, useEasingPicker.d.ts:63-66, and EasingPicker then overrides it with a hardcoded aspect-ratio:1 while exposing no door: no defineExpose, only a `footer` slot with {value}, no emitted CSS var). Add glass-ui props `layout="split|stacked"` (law 1), `surface="card|well|bare"` (law 2), `fit="square|viewbox"` (law 3, computed inside the producer). The subject file then deletes entirely and the coupling becomes type-checked.

defects.defect: The demo's import-boundary lint governs 0 of the 250 demo source files it names. G-DEMO-1/3a/3b are globbed on the `demo/@/…` tree, deleted by the same commit that created the subject's current home; the one surviving glob covers 16 files and bans a directory that no longer exists.
defects.evidence: `ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory. Glob census: demo/@/components → 0 files, demo/@/lib → 0 files, demo/@/composables → 0 files, demo/color-picker → 16 files; `find demo -type f \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.vue' \) | wc -l` → 250. `find demo -type d -name "palette-browser"` → no output, yet eslint.config.js:247-252 bans `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`. Config sites: eslint.config.js:234-238 and :275-277. Deleting commit: a61094e3 "feat(v-w43b3)!: home the feature UI trees; demo/@ dies (D-c)" — also the last commit touching EasingAuthoringStage.vue. The only live rule is inv-K-1 (eslint.config.js:204-218, files: ["src/**/*.ts"]), which correctly keeps the library glass-ui-free.
defects.mechanism: enforcement-vacuum: boundary rules pinned to a deleted directory tree; every other finding here is a boundary crossing nothing is positioned to object to
defects.reproduction: `npx eslint demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/` applies no boundary rule — no config object carrying no-restricted-imports matches that path. Verify with the two find/glob commands above.
defects.proposedCure: Re-home the guards onto the real lattice: an object over files:["demo/workbenches/*/**"] permitting demo/shared/**, demo/color-session/**, demo/ui/** and published @mkbabb/* subpaths, banning demo/shell/**, demo/color-picker/** (app-root boot) and cross-workbench internals. Add a rule banning `:deep(` selectors containing `[data-testid=` in demo/**/*.vue — that is the one class of cross-package coupling no type system can see, and it is exactly what killed L-2.

defects.defect: Inverted dependency direction in the domain model: the gradient's persisted per-interval truth is a bare type alias of a glass-ui component's v-model payload.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:49 — `export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;` (imported from @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing at :12). The docblock at :40-44 calls it "the persisted TRUTH" while EasingPickerValue carries `fn: EasingFn`, a live closure (useEasingPicker.d.ts:112-124), forcing the `fn ?? reparse` two-path fallback at useGradientCSS.ts:119-133. Dead fields by construction — easingCatalogue.ts:148-152: `points: [0,0,1,1]` / "Neutral transient cache — steps mode never reads points". value.js already publishes the correct discriminated type: src/css/types.ts:32-37 CssTimingFunction (keyword | cubic-bezier | steps | linear-function), exported at @mkbabb/value.js/css (src/subpaths/css.ts) — strictly more expressive, since EasingPickerValue cannot express linear() at all.
defects.mechanism: dependency-inversion: the design system's widget payload defines the domain model instead of the library's published type
defects.reproduction: NONE — shape defect (labelled). Its live signature: any interval round-tripped through storage loses `fn` and must be re-derived through easingFnOf's resolvedEasingCache, a fallback that exists solely because the model carries a value that cannot survive serialization.
defects.proposedCure: GradientInterval = CssTimingFunction; <EasingPicker> v-models CssTimingFunction too — glass-ui already depends on value.js (peer ^4.0.0) and already imports jumpTerms from @mkbabb/value.js/easing at useEasingPicker.d.ts:2. The callable is derived at point of use, never stored. Direction restored: value.js ← glass-ui ← demo.

defects.defect: Four independent implementations of "the CSS literal for an easing curve" at two precisions — and the library's own published minter has zero runtime consumers. The literal is the identity key of the whole feature, so any divergence silently deselects every tile.
defects.evidence: Four homes: (1) src/foundation/math.ts:113 cubicBezierToString, toFixed(2), exported at src/subpaths/math.ts:16 — `grep -rn cubicBezierToString src/ demo/ test/` hits only the definition, the export and test/math.test.ts + test/v4-c1.test.ts, i.e. ZERO runtime consumers; (2) glass-ui useEasingPicker.readout, easing.js:32-35, +n.toFixed(3); (3) demo easingCatalogue.ts:48 bezierLiteral / :54 stepsLiteral, hand-mirror of (2) with the mirror declared in prose at :40-45; (4) useGradientCSS.ts:55 hardcoded "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)", declared byte-identical in prose at :46-51. Measured divergence: cubicBezierToString(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) = "cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.10, 0.25, 1.00)" vs bezierLiteral = "cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)"; (0,0,1,1) → "cubic-bezier(0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00)" vs "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)". Shipped form confirmed in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png (readout reads `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)`). value.js has no steps serializer at all. Root asymmetry: parseTimingFunction is public in src/subpaths/css.ts; the inverse is absent, though /css does publish serializeCssColor and serializeTimelineOptions.
defects.mechanism: dual-path / missing-inverse: no module owns serialization of a CssTimingFunction, so each consumer hand-rolls it and byte identity is maintained by comment
defects.reproduction: `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/math.js').then(m=>console.log(m.cubicBezierToString(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)))"` → "cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.10, 0.25, 1.00)"; the demo's minter yields "cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)". Change either rounding rule in any of the four homes and every specimen tile deselects (easingCatalogue.ts:220 matches `t.css === interval.css`); no test fails, because no test binds the four.
defects.proposedCure: Add serializeTimingFunction(t: CssTimingFunction): string to src/css/, exported at @mkbabb/value.js/css — spec-minimal shortest round-tripping <number> form, all four arms. Retire cubicBezierToString into it; delete bezierLiteral/stepsLiteral and the hardcoded seed; have glass-ui's readout call the library. Round-trip property test: parse ∘ serialize ≡ id.

defects.defect: value.js's own /css and /easing subpaths do not compose: the library publishes the parser (string → CssTimingFunction) and the evaluators (CubicBezier/steppedEase/easing/linearEasing) but not the join, so 47 lines of pure library work — including the complete CSS linear() stop-input inference algorithm — live in a gradient workbench composable.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 (easingValue), :79-103 (linearStops — the full optional/double-position expansion), :106-117 (timingFunctionValue — the 4-arm CssTimingFunction switch). Nothing in those 47 lines is gradient-specific. Confirmed glass-ui does NOT carry a second copy: `grep -c "linear-function" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js` → 0; it only round-trips for reparseOk (easing.js:36-40). So this is a missing surface, not yet a duplication — but the next consumer writes it again.
defects.mechanism: missing-library-surface: two halves of one story published, the bridge unpublished, so every consumer must own it
defects.reproduction: NONE — surface-shape finding (labelled). Established by reading src/subpaths/css.ts, src/subpaths/easing.ts and useGradientCSS.ts:71-117.
defects.proposedCure: evaluateTimingFunction(t: CssTimingFunction): Result<EasingFunction, EasingIssue> in src/easing.ts, exported at @mkbabb/value.js/easing. Pairs with serializeTimingFunction (L-4) and easedRamp (L-1) to close parse → evaluate → sample → mix inside the library, where all four steps' domain knowledge already lives.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue silently drops 6 of the library's 30 bezier presets, filtered by a hand-maintained whitelist built on a regex that reverse-engineers library naming.
defects.evidence: `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/easing.js').then(E=>console.log(Object.keys(E.bezierPresets).length))"` → 30. The strip renders 27 tiles (24 bezier + 3 steps; roster measured in pass-1 wbL-probe8.mjs). Missing: ease-in/out/in-out-quart and ease-in/out/in-out-quint. Filter: easingCatalogue.ts:168 `/^ease-(in-out|in|out)-(.+)$/`, :174 FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"], :191 `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f)=>byFamily.has(f))`.
defects.mechanism: ownership-duplication: taxonomy about the library's own catalogue re-derived in a consumer by string-scraping, then truncated by an array the library cannot see
defects.reproduction: Compare `Object.keys(bezierPresets)` (30) against SPECIMEN_TILES (27, of which 3 are steps) — 24 bezier tiles for 30 presets. Adding a preset to src/easing.ts yields a tile only if its family name already appears in the demo's FAMILY_ORDER constant.
defects.proposedCure: Taxonomy is library data. Ship family/variant alongside the points in bezierPresets (or a parallel bezierPresetFamilies export to preserve the tuple shape). Consumer groups by family and orders by first appearance. No regex, no whitelist, no silent loss.

defects.defect: Three live implementations of "sample an easing function into an SVG path" across three repos, with three sampling-density and y-flip conventions, for one pure function of EasingFunction → string.
defects.evidence: demo: easingCatalogue.ts:66-75 glyphPath(fn, samples=48). glass-ui: bezierPathD/stepPathD at 240 samples, dist/easing.js:61-66, declared in useEasingPicker.d.ts. keyframes.js: generateCurveSVGPath, named by the demo's own header at easingCatalogue.ts:16-19 ("the kf `generateCurveSVGPath` idiom — ZERO re-derived curve math"), i.e. the duplication is documented and deliberate.
defects.mechanism: ownership-duplication: a framework-free numeric primitive homed in three UI consumers instead of the library that owns EasingFunction
defects.reproduction: NONE — census finding (labelled). Established by the three cited declarations.
defects.proposedCure: Move it to @mkbabb/value.js/easing, which is framework-free and already owns EasingFunction: `sampleEasing(fn, samples): Float64Array` and `easingPathD(fn, opts?: {samples?, flipY?, precision?}): string`. glass-ui and keyframes.js both already depend on value.js. Three deletions, one home.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json#paths has drifted from package.json#exports in both directions — and is simultaneously redundant. CORRECTION to pass 1: it does NOT cause a types-vs-runtime dual path; TypeScript package self-reference resolves the missing keys to the local dist/.
defects.evidence: exports keys (7): ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize — no `.` root. tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 declares @mkbabb/value.js → ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index.d.ts` → No such file), /parsing and /units (neither in exports; neither file exists in dist/subpaths/), and OMITS /value and /css (the latter imported 10x in demo/). The block's comment at :41 claims "a CLOSED 8-key set". CORRECTION probe: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution | grep '@mkbabb/value.js/css'` → "'paths' option is specified, looking for a pattern to match…" then "successfully resolved to '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts'" — the LOCAL build, via package self-reference, the same artifact vite.config.ts:41-49 aliases to. The node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 copy whose css.d.ts differs (vite-plugin-dts Alpha_2/Channel_2/Color_2 duplicate-declaration artifact; easing/math/color identical) is inert — nothing resolves to it.
defects.mechanism: generated-vs-handwritten asymmetry: the Vite half of the self-alias set is generated from package.json#exports, the tsconfig half is a hand list and has drifted
defects.reproduction: `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"` → 7 keys, no root; `ls dist/subpaths/` → no parsing.*, no units.*; `ls dist/index.d.ts` → No such file. Then the traceResolution command above shows the correction.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the seven hand-written @mkbabb/value.js* entries — self-reference already does the job. If they must stay, generate them from package.json#exports exactly as vite.config.ts:41-49 already does. Two generators reading one map; never a hand list.

defects.defect: A producer constant duplicated as a magic number across the package boundary, because the producer does not publish it.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:45 — `const vbRatio = ref(1.2); // linear's padded box (1 + 2·VIEW_PAD)`. glass-ui declares VIEW_PAD = 0.1 (also MAX_OVERSHOOT = 0.6, VIEWBOX_FIT_SAMPLES = 16) in dist/components/easing/constants.d.ts, but dist/components/easing/index.d.ts re-exports only the two SFCs, useEasingPicker and five types — and the package exports map has no ./easing/constants key. Live confirmation the value is right by luck: viewBox="0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002" → true ratio 1.2000000476837158.
defects.mechanism: producer public-surface gap forcing a consumer-side magic number
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/index.d.ts` — three export lines, no constants. `node -e "console.log('./easing/constants' in require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports)"` → false.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui re-exports its easing geometry constants through @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing. Better: under the L-2 `fit="viewbox"` cure the constant stops being consumer business at all and the line deletes.

defects.defect: The seat forks a component-type glass-ui already ships: EasingConfigurator is the existing "picker seated in a labelled layer" type, and EasingAuthoringStage is a second, demo-side one implemented as :deep() overrides.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/index.d.ts exports both `EasingPicker` and `EasingConfigurator`. result.strongestDefect: L-2 — the component's declared purpose is dead code. Its "zero-letterbox law (O-17)" targets `svg[role='img']`; glass-ui 7.0.0 ships that canvas as `role="group"` (`grep -o 'role: *"[a-z]*"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js` → group/slider/status only, zero img). Both the JS viewBox sync (early-returns at :51 forever, leaving `--vb-ratio` frozen at its 1.2 seed) and all five CSS declarations never apply, so the producer's inline `aspect-ratio: 1` and `block-size: clamp(200px,38cqi,320px)` survive. Measured live on the dev server with the disclosure open: box 272×200 px, drawn plot 166.7×200 px — 52.7 px of letterbox per side, 38.7 % dead pixels; pass 1 measured the same defect at a 410 px box (59.3 % empty), and the drawn plot is 166.7×200 in both, so the letterbox is unconditional, not viewport-dependent. The T-48 "liquid morph" aspect-ratio transition is deleted by the same drift (owner edict 6). Root mechanism: the demo is coupled to a producer's private ARIA role with no compile-time, test or lint binding — and it was forced into that coupling, because glass-ui publishes `viewBox` from `useEasingPicker` (useEasingPicker.d.ts:63-66) yet exposes no door to it from `<EasingPicker>` (no defineExpose, only a `footer` slot carrying `{value}`, no emitted CSS var) while overriding it with a hardcoded square aspect. L-1 is the more damaging *runtime* fault (3 of 27 catalogue tiles annihilate the pane silently), but L-2 is the strongest finding on this axis: it is the library-structure defect itself, it was certified green under glass-ui 6.x and died unnoticed at the 7.0.0 adopt, and no gate in the repo can see it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no global negative proof is claimed. The sub-negatives I did establish, positively, so their absence is evidence rather than silence: (1) Every import in the subject and its `easing/` siblings goes through a published export-map key — `@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing` is a real key in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json#exports and `@mkbabb/value.js/easing` is one of this repo's 7 exports keys; `grep -rn 'from "../../../../src|from "@src|value.js/dist|/src/units|/src/easing' demo/workbenches/` returns no output, so there is no deep-path escape and the demo is NOT proving a false public API through its imports — the violating edges are a querySelector and three :deep() selectors, not an import statement. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean: `import type { EasingPickerValue }` correctly split at :30, and likewise in easingCatalogue.ts:27-35, useSpecimenRows.ts:12,17-21, EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:12. (3) Idiomatic Vue 3.5: useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>("rootEl") at :44 matching ref="rootEl" at :72, reactive props destructure at :32. (4) Not a god module — 116 lines, one concern, four imports; the named historical suspects are all absent (no local reimplementation of a removed useLayerTransition, no second useDark, and the clipboard path uses glass-ui's own useClipboard at GradientEasingEditor.vue:29,94 rather than a hand-rolled copy+timer). (5) The library→consumer topology is acyclic and enforced where it matters: eslint.config.js:204-218 bans @mkbabb/glass-ui* from src/**/*.ts (inv-K-1) and that glob is live; direction glass-ui → value.js confirmed by glass-ui's peer dep "@mkbabb/value.js": "^4.0.0" and useEasingPicker.d.ts:2. (6) Two hypotheses I raised and KILLED rather than reported: a types-vs-runtime dual path on @mkbabb/value.js/css (refuted by `npx tsc --traceResolution`, which shows TS package self-reference resolving to the local dist/subpaths/css.d.ts — this also CORRECTS pass 1's L-8), and a glass-ui reparseOk round-trip bug (refuted — setHandle at easing.js:24-27 stores +a.toFixed(3), so the invariant holds).

An overshoot curve throws and destroys the whole pane.

Independent tile repro: click [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] → before {mainLen:717, rows:1, tiles:27} after {mainLen:102, rows:0, tiles:0}, errs:[] (swallowed by Vue's boundary — no window.error, no console error). Throw chain: src/color/operations.ts:88 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({code:"color_progress_out_of_range"})` (and :65 in interpolateHue); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199 `const easedT = easing(t)` unguarded → :201 mixColors → :204-206 `throw new Error(...)`; third sink demo/.../easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59. Preset census: `presets 30 | SAFE 27 | ESCAPES [0,1] -> CRASHES 3` — ease-in-back 0.09686@t=0.3438, ease-out-back 0.08679@t=0.6250, ease-in-out-back 0.09268@t=0.7813, all three live tiles. Boundary is grid-dependent: cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1.1) gridEscape(j/32)=0.00000 but trueMaxEscape=0.00643 → safe by accident; 1.15 → gridEscape 0.00684@t=0.9688 → CRASH. stepsPerInterval = max(2, round(32/(stops-1))) at useGradientCSS.ts:180-183, so adding a third stop halves the grid and re-rolls the catch set.
defects.mechanism: Unguarded emission across a domain-narrowing boundary; the library correctly returned a Result err and the demo sink converted it back into an uncaught throw.
defects.reproduction: npm run dev:web-only; http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; row 0 is open by default; click the rail button "Author a custom curve"; focus #easing-authoring-0 [role='slider'] index 1 (aria-label="Bezier control point 2"); press Shift+ArrowUp twice. defects.proposedCure: Do NOT clamp in onAuthored (that lies about what the user authored and must be repeated at every future consumer). Make the sampling law total over the easing codomain at the one place the demo converts easing output into mix progress — CSS's own linear-gradient semantics already answer it (an overshooting timing function paints the endpoint colour past the range): `const p = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, easing(t)))` at useGradientCSS.ts:199, applied identically at useSpecimenRows.ts:53. That makes the whole back family work as CSS defines it for every present and future consumer while the picker keeps its advertised authoring range. Add a back-family regression loop to test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts, which already imports SPECIMEN_TILES.

defects.defect: The component's single stated purpose — Law 3, "zero letterbox (O-17): the drawn plot IS the element box" — is dead code. Both arms (the syncVbRatio querySelector and the scoped CSS rule) key on `svg[role="img"]`, an ARIA role glass-ui removed at 6.0.0. --vb-ratio is frozen at its birth constant and the producer's inline aspect-ratio/block-size/margin survive untouched.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:48-50 (querySelector "svg[role='img']") and :104 (`.easing-authoring :deep(svg[role="img"])`). Producer: `grep -o 'role[:"][^,}]\{0,30\}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js | sort | uniq -c` → `1 role: "group" / 1 role: "slider" / 2 role: "status"` — zero role:"img". BISECTION (new): npm pack @mkbabb/glass-ui@5.0.0 → `1 role: "img"`; @6.0.0 → `role: "group"`. value.js jumped 5→7 in one commit: `git log --oneline -S'"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7' -- package.json` → f2c8f565, whose body migrates a dozen symbol-level drifts and never mentions the canvas role. LIVE MEASUREMENT at #/gradient row 0 disclosed: {svgRoleImgFound:false, svgRole:"group", vbRatio:"1.2", svgInlineStyle:"aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; block-size: clamp(200px, 38cqi, 320px); margin-inline: auto;", computed:{aspectRatio:"1 / 1", blockSize:"200px", inlineSize:"272px"}, rect:{w:272,h:200}, viewBox:{x:0,y:-0.1,w:1,h:1.2}, elAspect:1.36, vbAspect:0.8333, letterboxPx:{L:52.67,R:52.67,T:0,B:0}}. Second probe at a wider pane: element 410x200 → 121.67 px per side = 59.35% of inline extent dead. O-17 tolerance is ±1 px. After 20 ArrowRight presses the viewBox moved to `0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002` while --vb-ratio still read "1.2".
defects.mechanism: A consumer seat reaching into a third-party component's private DOM through an ARIA role used as a query/style hook — a coupling every instrument in the pipeline (vue-tsc, eslint, vitest) is structurally blind to. The producer's change was itself correct (a canvas of role=slider handles is a group, not an img); the consumer had no way to hear it.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; expand easing row 1→2; press the sliders icon in the readout rail; console: `const s=document.querySelector('#easing-authoring-0 svg'); s.getAttribute('role')` → "group"; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.easing-authoring')).getPropertyValue('--vb-ratio')` → "1.2"; `const r=s.getBoundingClientRect(),vb=s.viewBox.baseVal; (r.width - r.height*vb.width/vb.height)/2` → 52.67.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT re-point at svg[role="group"] — the bisection proves that re-arms the identical trap for glass-ui 8. Interim: re-scope Law 3 through the producer's published hook `[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg` (the one selector in this file that survived both majors — Law 1 keys on it and still works), paired with C-4's loud dev assertion. Terminal (owner edict 4, variants belong in glass-ui): relay to the glass-ui BH inbox an EasingPicker `fit="content"` prop that makes the canvas inline-size-driven with aspect-ratio bound to its own live viewBox, computed inside the component that owns the viewBox. That deletes rootEl, vbRatio, syncVbRatio, onMounted, the watch, both rAF hops and the whole Law-3 style block — C-2/C-3/C-4/C-6/C-7/C-9 all evaporate and the file falls from 117 lines to ~25.
