defects.defect: The producer probe fails silently by construction: the ref's birth constant (1.2), the CSS var() fallback (1.2) and the true ratio of the default seeded curve (linear's padded box, 1 + 2*VIEW_PAD = 1.2) are the same number, so a never-synced stage is byte-identical in the DOM to a perfectly-working one. syncVbRatio makes "the producer's DOM changed under me" and "the SVG has not laid out yet" the same bare `return`.

defects.mechanism: A masking fallback (owner edict 2) whose job is to make a broken state look like a working one, combined with a silent early-return on a foreign-DOM probe. This is why a producer major could delete the component's function and leave no trace for eleven days.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED — this is the mechanism behind C-2 and is evidenced by C-2's measurements: --vb-ratio reads "1.2" whether or not the sync has ever run, with zero console output.
defects.proposedCure: Dissolved entirely by C-2's terminal cure (a producer-owned fit prop has no fallback to mask). If the interim hook is taken instead: drop the var() default, initialise vbRatio to null, and make the miss loud in dev — `if (import.meta.env.DEV && rootEl.value && !el) console.error('[EasingAuthoringStage] producer contract drift: "' + CANVAS_SEL + '" matched nothing')`. A seat that scrapes a foreign DOM must scream when the DOM moves.

The unmount path (pending callbacks firing against a torn-down component, no-op only because of the ?. chain) is a LABELLED HYPOTHESIS: no misbehaviour observed.

Absent that, the idiomatic Vue 3.5 answer is not a hand-rolled rAF: one `useMutationObserver` from @vueuse/core (already a dependency, already used two files over in EasingSpecimenStrip.vue via useMediaQuery) with {attributes:true, attributeFilter:["viewBox"]} replaces onAuthored's rAF, the value.css watcher AND onMounted with a single scope-owned observer that is exact rather than one-frame-guessed and disposes itself.

defects.defect: The viewBox guard rejects <= 0 but not NaN or Infinity: `NaN <= 0` is false, so a non-finite dimension passes and lands in vbRatio, producing `calc(1 / NaN)` — an invalid aspect-ratio silently dropped at parse, in a component where silence is already the disease.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:51 `if (!vb || vb.width <= 0 || vb.height <= 0) return;` then :52 `vbRatio.value = vb.height / vb.width;`. The producer derives minY/height via Math.min/Math.max over 16 sampled fn(t) values (VIEWBOX_FIT_SAMPLES in glass-ui/dist/components/easing/constants.d.ts), so a callable returning NaN at any sample propagates into the viewBox string.
defects.mechanism: An incomplete domain-boundary guard: ordinal comparison used where a finiteness predicate is required.
defects.reproduction: NONE — LABELLED HYPOTHESIS. I did not construct an input that drives the producer viewBox to NaN: easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 throws on a bad Result and applyCSS is atomic, so every path I traced is clean. The guard's shape is nonetheless objectively incomplete against the boundary values (0, NaN, Infinity, huge) the brief names.
defects.proposedCure: `if (!vb || !Number.isFinite(vb.width) || !Number.isFinite(vb.height) || vb.width <= 0 || vb.height <= 0) return;` — or delete the arithmetic together with the DOM scrape via C-2's terminal cure.

defects.defect: The stage exports an `| undefined` arm on its own event and makes its parent guard, rather than absorbing the one piece of producer contract noise it is uniquely positioned to absorb — and schedules a rAF for an emission it knows will be discarded.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:39-41 `const emit = defineEmits<{ authored: [value: EasingPickerValue | undefined] }>();` and :57-60 `function onAuthored(v: EasingPickerValue | undefined) { requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio); emit("authored", v); }` vs GradientEasingEditor.vue:78-81 `function onPickerAuthored(index, v) { if (!v) return; … }`.
defects.mechanism: Contract noise passed through a seat whose stated job is to seat the producer; KISS / no-contrivance friction (owner edict 3). Every present and future consumer must re-guard.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — the types are the evidence, and no misbehaviour occurs (the sole consumer guards correctly).
defects.proposedCure: `if (!v) return;` as the first line of onAuthored, and narrow the emit signature to `authored: [value: EasingPickerValue]`. One line, one fewer arm in the contract.

defects.defect: The whole file is a per-instance override of a producer's internals — three :deep() blocks and four !important declarations reaching into glass-ui's private DOM, plus a querySelector into it — which owner edicts 4 (variants belong in glass-ui) and 5 (style at the root component level, never per-instance) forbid. It is a self-declared temporary that outlived its own retirement condition.

The file's own text, L10-11: "each recorded on the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet; the overrides retire at the adopt"; L102-103: "the seat overrides carry !important (retired at the P7 adopt)". The adopt happened — f2c8f565, glass-ui 7.0.0, 2026-07-17 — and the overrides did not retire. Two of the three coins are still live (Law 1 measured `grid-template-columns: 298px`; Law 2 measured `box-shadow: none` / `backdrop-filter: none`); one has flipped (C-2).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, `demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientCodeEditor.vue` (116 lines), route `/#/gradient`, branch tranche-u @ c654824e, live WebKit probes against http://localhost:9000
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm), explicitly declared at spawn; seat neither inherited nor undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: R1 — thirteen Backspaces on the app's OWN default editor text (`0.75 0.15 145` → `oklch()`) destroys the entire gradient pane and every piece of authored work in it: MT-F001 reaches the user through this component's unguarded `emit("parse")` from a bare setTimeout; the ErrorBoundary swallows it with ZERO console output (invisible to every console gate), and "Try again" restores the DEFAULT gradient, not the user's.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four candidate defects were tested and cleared, and are recorded as honest negatives: (1) KEYBOARD REACHABILITY — despite `el.tabIndex === -1`, WebKit's tab order does land on the editor (`r2-probe2.mjs` tag J2: seq[0] = "DIV[Gradient CSS](CE)"), so the surface is operable; no finding. (2) ACCESSIBLE NAME + VISUAL-AUDIT DEFECT SHARE — all 6 smallTapTargets on every gradient row of audit/visual/REPORT.json are shell (slug bar ×4) + GradientStopEditor handles (20×20 ×2); the editor is 462×80 and carries aria-label="Gradient CSS"; the single unattributed namelessButton cannot be this component because its whole template renders no button (lines 84-115). Zero contribution to the measured a11y defect counts. (3) `verbatimModuleSyntax` — every import in the file is a value import; no type-only import is mis-declared. (4) XSS via `highlight()`'s `catch { return code }` → `innerHTML`: the shape is unsafe but no reachable input makes `hljs.highlight` throw (language registered at module scope, line 8), so it is filed as a hypothesis (R11), not a live vulnerability. Also cited-not-re-found: the per-highlight CPU cost (r1 measured 0.014–0.020 ms) is genuinely negligible — R12 is filed for the semantic cost (undo stack/selection), not the time.

defects.defect: Thirteen Backspaces on the app's own default editor text destroys the whole gradient pane and every piece of authored gradient work; the component's own reject-verdict surface never fires. MT-F001 reaches production through this component's unguarded `emit("parse")`. The crash emits ZERO console errors, so every console-watching gate is blind to it. Recovery via the boundary's "Try again" remounts a FRESH model — the user's gradient is gone.
defects.evidence: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/r2-probe3.mjs webkit` → {"tag":"P-thirteen-backspaces-from-default","textAtRest":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch() 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)","editorGone":true,"paneNow":"… This panel hit an unexpected error. | undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g[0].replace') | Try again","consoleErrorsUnfiltered":[],"pageErrors":[]}. Oracle through the demo's own import path (`npx vitest run --config .../evidence/r2-vitest.config.ts`): parseCssColor THROWS TypeError on oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() hwb() 'hsl(  )' 'rgb( )' — hwb() and 'rgb( )' are TWO INPUTS BEYOND the eight MT-F001 names. State loss: r2-probe2.mjs M1/M2 — authored "linear-gradient(45deg, red 0%, lime 40%, blue 100%)" → after Try-again the editor holds the default "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, …)". Witnesses evidence/r2-P-thirteen-backspaces.png, r2-shot-C-crashed.png.
defects.mechanism: Partial-function-treated-as-total across a component boundary: GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62 fires `emit("parse")` from a bare setTimeout → GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 applyCSS → gradientParse.ts:92-94 `isColorToken` assumes parseCssColor is total → src/css/grammar.ts:181 `slash[0]!.replace` where the non-null assertion is false. Vue's emit routes the throw through callWithAsyncErrorHandling into demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:57-70, whose onErrorCaptured returns false — unmounting the pane subtree AND suppressing all console output.
defects.reproduction: Live: open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click just right of `145` in the editor, press Backspace 13 times, pause 500 ms. Scripted: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/r2-probe3.mjs webkit` (tag P).
defects.proposedCure: Three layers, only the third local: (1) make parseCssColor TOTAL — src/css/grammar.ts:181 is the single false `!`; this is the acceptance criterion for the already-ruled cand-O total parser, not a local guard. (2) gradientParse.ts declares a model-or-reject contract in its own header but honours it only for false returns — its oracle calls (isColorToken/angleToDegrees/percentValue) must convert throws into `reject(...)` so a text-validation failure can NEVER become an unmounted pane. (3) in this file, the debounced parse is unprotected async work: it belongs in one owned, cancellable, guarded parse task rather than a naked setTimeout→emit.

defects.defect: The pending 500 ms parse is never cancelled on unmount, so the crash detonates on a DIFFERENT pane the user has already navigated to.
defects.evidence: r2-probe.mjs tag G: type `linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(), blue)`, navigate to #/mix immediately → {"hash":"#/mix","bodyHead":"… This panel hit an unexpected error. | undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g[0]…"} (witness evidence/r2-G-cross-route.png). GradientCodeEditor.vue:2 imports no unmount hook. demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 gives debounce a `.cancel()`; `grep -rn debounce demo` shows this component is its ONLY consumer and never calls it, while the sibling workbench does the exact cleanup at demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:194-196 (`onBeforeUnmount(() => { if (debounceTimer) clearTimeout(debounceTimer); })`).
defects.mechanism: Uncancelled timer outliving the component scope; the emit still reaches the retained parent handler after unmount.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe.mjs webkit` (tag G).
defects.proposedCure: `onBeforeUnmount(debouncedParse.cancel)` — one line, using an affordance the util already ships and the neighbouring workbench already uses. No new util, no wrapper (KISS).

defects.defect: Blurring inside the debounce window DESTROYS the user's in-progress text and then shows a verdict naming a token that is no longer on screen — a direct breach of the law this file documents at lines 34-40 ("A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed").
defects.evidence: r2-probe2.mjs tag L: {"typed":"linear-gradient(90deg, red, notacolor)","nowOnScreen":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\"","userTextSurvives":false} (witness evidence/r2-L-wip-destroyed.png). Benign variant r2-probe.mjs tag F: typed → rightAfterBlur reverts to the old canonical → settled re-applies 1.2 s later, "wipDestroyed":true.
defects.mechanism: Stale read on an async round-trip: onBlur (lines 68-73) branches on `hasError`, which is derived from the `parseVerdict` prop — the verdict of the PREVIOUS parse. At blur the pending parse has not run, so the guard consults a value that is about to change. Same family as the repo's recorded defineModel stale-read hazard.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe2.mjs webkit` (tag L).
defects.proposedCure: Flush rather than race: on blur, cancel the timer and run the parse synchronously, THEN decide whether to settle to the canonical serialization. Blur and the last verdict become the same instant, and the WIP-preserving law holds by construction instead of by timing luck.

defects.defect: The parse verdict never clears when the model changes from anywhere else. After a rejected parse, nudging the Direction slider replaces the editor text with valid canonical CSS while aria-invalid="true", the destructive border and the stale error message all persist indefinitely.
defects.evidence: r2-probe.mjs tags D2→D4: {"tag":"D3-model-moved-verdict-should-be-gone","editorText":"linear-gradient(182deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""} and {"tag":"D4-border-state","classList":["border","border-destructive"],"ariaInvalid":"true","borderColor":"rgb(219, 36, 36)"} (witness evidence/r2-D-stale-verdict.png). parseVerdict is assigned in only two places: GradientVisualizer.vue:107 (onParseCSS) and :124 (resetGradient).
defects.mechanism: Derived state stored as raw state, owned by the parent, invalidated by exactly one of the many events that can invalidate it. The editor cannot self-correct because it does not own the value.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe.mjs webkit` (tags D1-D4).
defects.proposedCure: Make the verdict carry the text it judged: the parent stores `{ text, reason }` and the editor renders the verdict only while its current text still equals `text`. Any model write from any other control then invalidates it for free.

defects.defect: `textContent` fuses line breaks, so multi-line authoring silently corrupts the parsed text: `red` ⏎ `0%` is fed to the parser as `red0%` and the user is told a token they never typed is unparseable.
defects.evidence:
r2-probe2.mjs tag K: {"seenByUser":"linear-gradient(90deg, red\n0%, blue 100%)","textContentFedToParser":"linear-gradient(90deg, red0%, blue 100%)","verdict":"unparseable color \"red0%\""} (witness evidence/r2-K-newline-fusion.png). The DOM Enter builds (r2-probe.mjs tag E1) is `linear-gradient(90deg,
red 0%,
blue 100%)
`; innerText preserves the breaks, textContent does not.
defects.mechanism: GradientCodeEditor.vue:60 reads `editorRef.value?.textContent`, which concatenates block-level children without their line boundaries.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe2.mjs webkit` (tag K). Comma-terminated lines survive by luck (tag E2 parsed clean), which makes the failure intermittent.
defects.proposedCure: A code surface must round-trip newlines: read `innerText`, or — the direction R6 points — stop hand-rolling a contenteditable and bind a real multi-line control whose value is a string containing \n by definition.

defects.defect: Hand-rolled field chrome where the design system already ships the part (MT-F037 family): the editor re-derives a field surface by hand and diverges on every measurable property, plus a per-instance inline transition style. The whole gradient route contains ZERO glass field-control elements.

Dist census of @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0: `.field-control[data-kind=textarea]{min-block-size:max(5lh,calc(5rem*var(--ui-scale)));border-radius:var(--radius-field)}` is this component's exact silhouette; `Input-9BlLluik.js` has 0 occurrences of $slots|renderSlot|useSlots (no trailing-icon affordance); `dist/components/labeled-field/types.d.ts` ships `errorLive: "off"|"polite"|"assertive"`, slot props `controlId·labelledBy·describedBy·errorId·invalid`, and `controlLabelable` documented for non-labelable composite roots. Screenshot witness shots/safari-desktop-dark/gradient.png: the OM-13 easing readout plate and this editor sit adjacent on one route with two different materials, neither from glass.
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass. Every token the primitive needs already resolves in this page; the component re-implements the field with Tailwind utilities and lands on different numbers for all of them. Breaches owner edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and edict 5 (root-level styling — inline :style transition, lines 95-97).
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe.mjs webkit` (tags A1, B) + `grep -o '\.field-control[^{]*{[^}]*}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css`.
defects.proposedCure: MARKED GLASS-FORWARD ASK, never a local restyle (no installed variant fits a syntax-highlighted code surface or an icon-trailing code row): glass-ui should ship a CODE FIELD in the field-control family (`data-kind="code"`) that (a) takes a multi-line plain-text value, (b) permits a token-highlight overlay without owning the grammar, (c) supports `invalid` + the LabeledField error wiring, and (d) admits trailing control affordances (the OM-13 copy/tune pair). Both value.js code surfaces on /#/gradient then converge on one material.

defects.defect: The "LOUD" failure surface is neither reliably seen nor heard: the verdict paints 14 px below the pane scrollport with no scroll-into-view, the role="status" live region is created together with its text (announcement race), there is no aria-errormessage/aria-describedby, the verdict has no id, and the multi-line textbox has no aria-multiline.
defects.evidence: r2-probe5-verdict-fold.mjs: {"verdictRect":{"top":947,"bottom":970},"paneScrollportRect":{"top":124,"bottom":956},"fullyVisible":false,"pixelsBelowFold":14,"scrollTop":0,"scrollMax":31} at 1440×1000 (witness evidence/r2-shot-B-rejected.png shows it cut in half behind the pane fade). r2-probe3.mjs tag Q: {"verdictAttrs":{"data-testid":…,"class":…,"role":"status"},"verdictHasId":false,"editorDescribedby":null,"editorErrormessage":null,"editorAriaInvalid":"true"}. r2-probe.mjs tag B: hasAriaMultiline false.
defects.mechanism: Four independent hand-rolled a11y decisions, each made once and none of them the platform-correct one: v-if-mounted live region (lines 107-114), aria-invalid with no programmatic path to the reason (line 92), no id on the message, no scroll management on the state transition.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe5-verdict-fold.mjs` and `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe3.mjs webkit` (tag Q).
defects.proposedCure: Adopt glass-ui LabeledField (already installed): it supplies a stable errorId, a describedBy to hang on the control, and an errorLive policy, deleting all four hand-rolled decisions at once. Independently, scrollIntoView({block:"nearest"}) when the verdict transitions to non-null.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate. Nine e2e tests and nineteen unit tests exist and do exercise this component, yet all stay green under the mutation that deletes the component's ENTIRE documented editor truce; and every gradient e2e test's console gate is structurally blind to the R1 crash.
defects.evidence: `npx vitest run test/gradient-parse.test.ts` → Tests 19 passed (no test feeds an empty-argument colour function). e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:32-38 drives the editor; the truce assertions are substring checks satisfied by BOTH the authored and the canonical text — line 212 `expect(editor).toContainText("rebeccapurple")` (canonical is `linear-gradient(45deg, red 0%, rebeccapurple 80%)`, still contains it), line 217 `toContainText("red 0%, rebeccapurple 80%")` (MORE satisfied by the mutant), line 238 `toContainText("notacolor")` (a rejected parse never changes the model, so no watch fires either way). Every test ends `expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([])` while the R1 crash produces zero console output (measured unfiltered: consoleErrorsUnfiltered: [], pageErrors: []).
defects.mechanism: The assertions test the CONTENT of the editor, never the TIMING or provenance of writes — the exact property the truce exists to guarantee. The named mutation: delete `const focused = ref(false)` (line 41), onFocus/onBlur (lines 64-73) and their bindings, and the `if (focused.value) return;` guard (line 77), leaving `watch(() => modelValue, render)` unconditional. The debounce never fires mid-`keyboard.type` (no 500 ms gap), so the mutant cannot even garble the typed text.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the mutation itself — this formation forbids source edits, so the mutant was NOT executed; the green-keeping argument is derived from the quoted assertion texts and is labelled a hypothesis on that ground. The console-blindness half IS measured (r2-probe3.mjs tag P).
defects.proposedCure: Not more assertions — one property the component's law deserves: for ANY text the user leaves in the editor, the pane survives AND either the model equals parse(text) or the verdict names why. That single property kills R1, R3, R4 and R5 as regressions. Add the seven uncovered paths as its inputs: empty-argument colour functions, blur inside the debounce window, Enter/multi-line, unmount with a parse pending, verdict clearing from another control, verdict visibility, stop-identity survival.

defects.defect: `modelValue` prop declared with no `update:modelValue` emit — `v-model` on this component compiles, renders, and silently never writes back. A contract lie in the public surface.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:16-29 — `const { modelValue, parseVerdict = null } = defineProps<{ modelValue: string; parseVerdict?: string | null }>()` with `defineEmits<{ "parse": [css: string] }>()`. The parent avoids the trap only by convention (GradientVisualizer.vue:258-262 uses `:model-value` + `@parse`).
defects.mechanism: Reserved-name misuse: `modelValue` is the name of Vue's v-model contract, so the component advertises a two-way binding it does not implement.
defects.reproduction: NONE executed (writing a `<GradientCodeEditor v-model=…>` call site would require editing demo/, forbidden this formation) — hypothesis on the consequence, measured on the declaration.
defects.proposedCure: Name the prop what it is (`css`), keeping `@parse`. Given the parse is debounced and rejectable, one-way-in + event-out is the honest shape; the current naming is a legacy-shaped affordance that does not exist (edicts 2/3).

defects.defect: Every settled parse re-mints the identity of EVERY stop, so the pane's stop selection is silently dropped whenever the user edits the CSS text — changing one number destroys all handle identities.
defects.evidence: r2-probe4.mjs: S1 ids [stop-1-ms5hulak, stop-2-ms5hulak, stop-3-ms5hulak] with removeChipVisible true → after editing `lime 50%`→`lime 60%`, S2 ids [stop-4-ms5humuj, stop-5-ms5humuj, stop-6-ms5humuj], identitiesPreserved false, removeChipVisible false. GradientStopEditor.vue:230-232 keys handles on `stop.id`, so all handle elements are destroyed and rebuilt; GradientVisualizer.vue:51 `selectedStopId` then points at a stop that no longer exists.
defects.mechanism: applyCSS (useGradientModel.ts:158-168) swaps in wholly new stop objects from gradientParse, which mints ids from its OWN counter (gradientParse.ts:31-34) in the same `stop-${n}-${Date.now().toString(36)}` namespace as useGradientModel.ts:66-69 — two id authorities for one identity space (a same-millisecond counter collision is possible in principle; not observed — hypothesis).
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe4.mjs webkit` (tags S1, S2).
defects.proposedCure: Reconcile on apply: match parsed stops to existing ones positionally and keep the surviving ids (or make identity a pure function of index and drop the pretence of stable ids). One uid authority for the model.

defects.defect: `highlight()`'s `catch { return code }` is a masking fallback that would feed UNESCAPED user text straight into `innerHTML`.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:43-53 — `try { return hljs.highlight(code, {language:"css"}).value } catch { return code }` flowing into `editorRef.value.innerHTML = highlight(code)`. hljs's `.value` is escaped; the catch branch is not.
defects.mechanism: A catch that converts an unknown failure into silently different, less safe behaviour — owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks).
defects.reproduction: NONE — the language is registered at module scope (line 8) and I found no reachable input that makes hljs.highlight throw. LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS: the shape is confirmed, the reachability is not.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the fallback. If highlighting can fail, that is a bug to surface, and the safe degraded path is `textContent = code`, never `innerHTML = code`.

defects.defect: The editor's whole subtree is torn down and rebuilt via innerHTML on every model tick, even while the user is nowhere near it — destroying the native undo stack and any selection.
defects.evidence: r2-probe4.mjs tag S3: a 40-step Direction sweep with the editor unfocused produced 42 MutationObserver records on the editor subtree (~1 full teardown/rebuild per model tick). CPU cost cited-not-re-found from r1 (0.014–0.020 ms per hljs.highlight) — the time is negligible; the semantics are not, which is why R3's flash-back cannot be undone with Ctrl-Z.
defects.mechanism: `render()` (line 51-53) replaces innerHTML wholesale instead of diffing text.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/.../evidence/r2-probe4.mjs webkit` (tag S3).
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of R6: a real value-bound control diffs its text instead of replacing a subtree.

defects.defect: Editable-surface hygiene on a code field: contenteditable="true" (not plaintext-only) with no @paste handler accepts foreign markup, and the surface declares no autocapitalize/autocorrect/inputmode although its entire content is code.
defects.evidence: r2-probe2.mjs tag J1: {"contentEditableValue":"true","autocapitalize":null,"autocorrectAttr":null,"inputMode":null,"enterKeyHint":null}; r2-probe.mjs tag B attribute census shows only contenteditable/spellcheck/role/aria-label/class/style.
defects.mechanism: Platform defaults left unset on a surface whose grammar is case- and character-exact.

defects.defect: The component declares the `glass-wash` material tier and gets no plate at all: the co-applied `.hljs` ink class nulls the background. The code artifact therefore has no specimen well, and the hljs contrast guard — which was certified against the rung-2 `--well-bg` ground — does not apply at this site; the actual ground varies with the user's seed colour.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live editor: edBg "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)", edBackdrop "none". CONTROL: a bare <div class="glass-wash"> injected as a sibling in the same container, same frame → {bg:"oklab(0.881504 0.0054135 0.0126841 / 0.328)", borderColor:"oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.04)", borderWidth:"1px"}. Cause isolated: demo/styles/hljs.css:56-60 declares `.hljs { background: transparent }` UNLAYERED, beating glass-ui's `@layer components` `.glass-wash { background: var(--glass-plate-tinted) }`. Paint chain behind the editor: transparent → transparent → transparent → `glass-resting card` oklab(0.928268 0.00554796 0.0132111 / 0.664) over the live aurora field. hljs.css:21-33 certifies comment 5.33/5.04, string 4.99, number 4.91, keyword 4.91 "on the well" (--well-bg = card 92% + fg 8%) — a ground this surface does not have. hljs.css:13-15 states the intended division of labour that the shipped cascade inverts. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 "Specimen well | image, curve, palette or code artifact | opaque/quiet neutral stage".
defects.mechanism: declaration ≠ render (unlayered ink rule defeats a layered material rule)
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → getComputedStyle on [aria-label="Gradient CSS"] → backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0) while an injected sibling .glass-wash reads oklab(0.881504 …/0.328).
defects.proposedCure: Ink and plate must not both claim `background`. Delete `background: transparent` from `.hljs` (a defensive relic of the retired GitHub-theme imports its own header names) and let the plate own the surface — or, better, adopt the field primitive (D2-6) so no plate is hand-assembled at a call site at all.

The codebase already knows empty is its own species — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 requires "A true empty invitation content-hugs its text/action" for the palette field.

defects.proposedCure: Three states, not two: `empty` (placeholder specimen showing the last applied CSS, no verdict, no destructive border, model untouched) | `applied` | `rejected`. Empty must be recoverable in one keystroke.

defects.defect: The failure state is not programmatically associated with the field it invalidates: aria-invalid="true" with no aria-errormessage and no aria-describedby, and the verdict is a v-if-mounted role="status" region that announces once on creation.

Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit." glass-ui 7.0.0 ships useUserInvalidAria (dist/forms.d.ts) for exactly this and it is unused. I could NOT reproduce round 1's visiblePx:0 clipping — my probes had the section scrolled into view — so that half is neither confirmed nor disputed here.

defects.proposedCure: The error slot lives INSIDE the control's boundary with errorId/describedBy and a live-region policy as a prop — which is what glass-ui's LabeledField/useUserInvalidAria already model. Consume them rather than hand-placing a sibling paragraph the layout can exile.

defects.defect: Syntax highlighting is dead exactly while the editor is in use, and after a rejected parse the wrong colours persist indefinitely — typed characters inherit the token colour of the span the caret sat in, so the ink actively lies.
defects.evidence: onInput (GradientCodeEditor.vue:59-62) never calls render(); the model watch (:76-79) early-returns while focused; blur re-render at :72 is gated `if (!hasError.value)`. Measured: inserting characters into the live .hljs-number span leaves {"spanClass":"hljs-number","spanText":"145abc","renderedColor":"oklch(0.49 0.12 78)"} — the NUMBER crayon rendered on letters.
defects.mechanism: a real design trade (caret safety vs live ink) resolved by deleting the feature in the used state
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click inside the literal `145` in the CSS editor → type letters → they render in the ochre number crayon; type something that rejects → blur → the wrong colours never clear.
defects.proposedCure: The overlay idiom: a transparent-ink editable layer over an aria-hidden highlighted mirror. The caret's host is never rewritten, so ink can update every keystroke; it also dissolves D2-3 because the mirror can own pre-style non-breaking layout, and removes the innerHTML rewrite (and with it the undo-stack hazard).

defects.defect: Ad-hoc, mistimed motion authored as an inline style: a 0.3s border-color/box-shadow transition where the design system's own field control uses the 0.2s fast rung for the identical state change. Reduced motion survives only via a global !important guard, not via the component.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:95-97 inline `transition: border-color var(--duration-normal) …, box-shadow var(--duration-normal) …`. Measured tokens: --duration-normal 0.3s, --duration-fast 0.2s. Producer, from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css: `.input-pill { … transition: background-color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard), border-color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard), box-shadow var(--duration…`. Reduced motion covered only by demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on *). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 "Color/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve." focus-ring.css:14-15 explicitly warns against inline-style motion on the material.
defects.mechanism: ad-hoc motion at the wrong rung, authored at the highest-specificity surface
defects.reproduction: Read GradientCodeEditor.vue:95-97; read getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) --duration-fast (0.2s) vs --duration-normal (0.3s); grep .input-pill in glass-ui.css.
defects.proposedCure: Move the transition into the field primitive at the fast rung. Nothing layout-forcing is animated, so only the rung and the placement change — and hoisting it off the inline style is also the cascade half of the D2-2 cure.

defects.defect: A CSS-string surface with no LTR isolation: no dir attribute, no unicode-bidi, so the buffer's paragraph direction flips with the document and CSS punctuation becomes subject to bidi reordering.
defects.evidence: Measured with dir="rtl" temporarily set on <html>: ltr {direction:"ltr", textAlign:"start", dirAttr:null} → rtl {direction:"rtl", textAlign:"start", boxLeft:790, boxRight:1252, firstCharLeft:821}. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose" and §5.2 terminal row "…inside an LTR-isolated value". demo/color-picker/index.html:11 hard-codes dir="ltr" as "RTL mechanical readiness" — the readiness this component would break.
defects.mechanism: direction jurisdiction not applied to a domain-literal surface
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl') → getComputedStyle on the editor: direction becomes "rtl"; the element carries no dir of its own.
defects.proposedCure: dir="ltr" + unicode-bidi: isolate on the code surface (a property of the field primitive, not a per-call-site patch), so the CSS literal keeps its declared physical/domain meaning in any document direction.

defects.defect: Three code/value surfaces in one 462px column wear three radii, three grounds and three border idioms; affordance placement disagrees too (in-row icon rail vs section-header Copy).

result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D2-03 — the ratified topology forbids this object by name. `OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:45` (declared binding by `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:56`) specifies Easing as its own route with a "centered 19–22rem curve/time stage" at 61.8%, "no tiny nested Card", "no local picker". defects.defect: The authoring instrument's own controls destroy the whole `/gradient` route. Six distinct entry points, including the stage's own Preset dropdown and two keystrokes on its own canvas.
defects.evidence: Arm A (keyboard): focus `.easing-authoring [role="slider"]` nth(1), Shift+ArrowUp ×1 → literal `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1.1)`, stage alive; ×2 → `{"alive": false}` (probes/p3-overshoot-keyboard-crash.json). Arm C (strip tile `ease-out-back`): same boundary. Forensics: `"remainingRouteNodes": {"easingHeads": 0, "gradientRail": 0, "main": 1}` (probes/p4-crash-forensics.json). The producer's own sr-only text rendered into this stage says "Up and Down change y from -0.6 to 1.6" while the gradient consumer survives only [0,1].
defects.mechanism: the seat adopted the producer's full CSS-easing authoring domain without reconciling it against the gradient interval domain the value is written into; an unclamped fn(t)>1 throws during render
defects.reproduction: `node .../probes/probe3.mjs ./out3` (keyboard arm) — crashes on the 2nd Shift+ArrowUp; dropdown arm: navigate /#/gradient, click `button[aria-label="Author a custom curve"]`, open the Preset select, choose `ease-out-back`

Silently offering an authoring range the consumer cannot render is the defect.

defects.defect: The binding topology decision forbids this object by name: "no tiny nested Card", "no local picker", Easing owns a separate route. The component is all three violations at once, at 45% below the required stage size, on the wrong route, behind two disclosures.

defects.defect: Law 2 ("wells, not cards") is a four-property override and therefore does not flatten the producer's glass material at all: the specular pseudo-layer, its hover/active response and a full-width tonal seam all survive on a non-interactive specimen stage — and the override simultaneously suppresses the producer's card-level focus elevation.

Seam isolated: forcing `background:#ff0000 !important` on the card and `visibility:hidden` on the SVG still shows a full-width tonal step at ~56% of card height — frames/D-06-well-seam-over-red-svg-hidden.png; absent under forced-colors where `glass/a11y-fallback.css` sets `.glass-card::before{display:none}`; card-relative not viewport-relative (card y=746.3 and y=564.25 in two runs, same relative offset). result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (subject: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue, area demo/workbenches)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context arm) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1/D-2 (name discard) is the strongest USER-facing defect and D-19 the strongest NEW one, but the dominating design defect is the abdicated composition: GeneratePane.vue:31 ships a `Card tier="resting" ... h-full` page column where OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binds Generate to Card count 0 and §3 binds it to a landmark-neutral `InstrumentChassis` at `golden` (61.8033989/38.1966011). Measured live at 1440x900: leftSharePct = 50.00 against a legal floor of 61.8, with the deficit handed to an EMPTY `My Palettes` companion occupying 35.56% of the viewport — the exact mechanism PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04 already dispositioned REMOVE and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3 law 2 forbids in terms ("It never receives half the viewport"). Every other defect — the 125.9px dead tail, the 36.5px chrome wrap at the widest desktop arm, the duplicated commit region, the mobile Dock pane selector — is downstream of that one substitution. The producer ships the housing: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/instrument-chassis/types.d.ts exposes `proportion: "golden"|"preview-dominant"`, `boundaries`, `reserve`, `state` — prop for prop, the four canon clauses.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Negatives proved and recorded in the report (§5 of pass 1, §B/§F of the addendum): prefers-reduced-motion IS handled by the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192; only `transform` is animated (compositor-safe, no layout-forcing property); horizontal overflow is genuinely 0 at 1440/390/200%-zoom/RTL (measured document.documentElement.scrollWidth - innerWidth = 0), matching REPORT.md's `horizontalOverflow — 0`; `main` count = 1; verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied (GeneratePane.vue:8 uses `import type`); no god module was grown and no new shared/ dir or wrapper component was invented; the dropdown preset/harmony preview strips are seed-exact and do NOT lie (GenerateControls.vue:94-100 call the same pure mulberry32-seeded generatePalette with the live count/seed).

defects.defect: The editable palette name the user types is silently discarded on save. GeneratePane.vue:14 declares `function onSave(colors: string[])` (one parameter) and :19 calls `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)` with a hardcoded literal, while GenerateControls.vue:48-50 declares `save: [colors: string[], name: string]` and :103 emits `paletteName.value`. TypeScript accepts the narrower handler, so the contract breach is silent at compile time. The plate's dashed-underline in-place editable title (GenerateControls.vue:144-149) is therefore an affordance that does nothing.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:14,19 vs demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:48-50,103. Live Playwright run, 1440x900, localStorage cleared: inputValueAfter="MY CUSTOM NAME"; rendered Library pane text = "My Palettes1 (1 saved) ... Start a new palette Generated Palette 5"; localStorage['color-palettes'] = {"version":1,"palettes":[{"id":"894b9a3c-44b2-4b01-9ebf-41fc3215f8e3","name":"Generated Palette","slug":"generated-palette-cd1ec69a",...}]}. Replicated independently across two sessions four hours apart.
defects.mechanism: F2 — contract dropped at the seam: the pane is a thin relay that mis-consumes the interfaces on both sides (drops an emitted arg, injects what it never reads, optional-chains what always exists).
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/generate with localStorage cleared. Type any name into the plate title input (aria-label="Palette name"). Click the Save button (aria-label="Save palette"). Read the Library pane and localStorage['color-palettes'] — both read "Generated Palette". Because usePaletteStore.ts:66-81 dedups on name+colors, every palette this pane writes is named identically.
defects.proposedCure: Do not fix the relay — delete it. Move the draft ({name, colors, seed, preset, harmony}) into useColorGeneration() so the commit region reads it directly; the pane then has no onSave handler and no defineExpose, and the whole class of 'a relay dropped a field' becomes structurally impossible. Per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5, rename/lifecycle actions belong to the selected inspector, so Generate's commit region should hand off rather than fork a second naming path.

defects.defect: The decided composition was never built: GeneratePane.vue:31 uses `<Card tier="resting" ... h-full>` as the route page-column where OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binds Generate to Card count 0 and §3 to a landmark-neutral InstrumentChassis at golden. GeneratePane.vue:30 and :35 are the entire compositional statement — no stage, no inspector, no action region; all content is one flat `flex flex-col gap-4`, so the specimen plate, the two dropdowns and the count slider carry identical structural weight.

defects.defect: Five specimen swatches present as click-to-copy actions but are aria-hidden, role-less, unfocusable spans. GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes `tag="button"` and `:aria-label` to WatercolorDot, but glass-ui 7.0.0 executed the P051 abrogation and removed the interactive-host branch — the prop no longer exists, the producer forces aria-hidden="true", and @click still binds with cursor-pointer + active:scale-95 press feedback. The result is an operable ornament with no accessible name and no keyboard path.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208. Live DOM: `<span data-v-292b9032 aria-hidden="true" class="generate-swatch ... cursor-pointer active:scale-95 transition-transform ..." data-testid="watercolor-swatch" data-variant="solid">`; dot tag=SPAN, role=null, tabIndex=-1, aria-label=null. Plate tab order measured = ["INPUT:Palette name","BUTTON:Regenerate","BUTTON:Save palette","BUTTON:Copy all colors"] — zero swatches. Producer surface: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.d.ts __VLS_Props = {color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed} — no `tag`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.2 "Selection, activation, drag and keyboard focus belong to a named enclosing geometric button/seat"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 5 "operable ornaments without names are forbidden", law 9 "A renderer specimen is not an unlabeled button".
defects.mechanism: F3 — reached past the design system: the consumer codes against a retired producer API, so the prop evaporates silently with no compile-time or runtime signal (the same failure mode as `variant="golden"` on the chassis).
defects.reproduction: Load /#/generate and press Tab repeatedly through the plate: focus goes Palette name -> Regenerate -> Save palette -> Copy all colors and then leaves. The five swatches are never reached; VoiceOver never announces them. Clicking one with a mouse does copy.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the P051 seat contract: wrap each face in the named geometric seat the canon requires — `<button type="button" :aria-label="`Copy ${css}`"><WatercolorDot ... /></button>` — the seat owning focus/ring and accessible name, the organic face staying aria-hidden. Removing tag="button" alone would leave a silent specimen; the seat must be added in the same move. Also make the specimen list itself readable so the pane's chromatic output exists in text (PaletteColorStrip is aria-hidden too, so today the route's entire accessible text contains no color value).

defects.defect: The route has no mount state. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:73 registers GeneratePane with defineAsyncComponent and no loadingComponent, no errorComponent, no timeout, no onError — a slow chunk renders an empty 512x560 glass rectangle and a failed chunk fetch renders nothing forever, with no message and no retry. GeneratePane.vue:10,11 are two non-null-asserted inject(...)! calls that throw on a missing provider with no recovery surface. The pane expresses zero of the five states VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 requires.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:73 `const GeneratePane = defineAsyncComponent(() => import("../workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue"));` — no options object. demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:10,11. Producer vocabulary that goes unused: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/instrument-chassis/types.d.ts `export type InstrumentChassisState = "ready" | "active" | "complete" | "loading";`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08 ADD-AFFORDANCE.
defects.mechanism: F4 — state never designed: only the populated happy path at 1440-light was authored; loading, error, saved, save-failure, overflow/truncation and touch states were not.
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis-free static + producer-API proof; not exercised under a throttled/failed chunk fetch). The absence of loadingComponent/errorComponent on usePaneRouter.ts:73 is directly readable, and Vue's documented behaviour for defineAsyncComponent without those options is to render nothing while pending and to log-and-render-nothing on rejection.
defects.proposedCure: Bind `:state` on the InstrumentChassis from D-3's transposition — "loading" while the generation core is cold, "ready" at rest, "complete" after a commit — and give the async import a real error arm with retry. Under the chassis this is one prop, not a new component; without the chassis it would require inventing a wrapper, which edict 3 forbids.

defects.defect: The dead card tail is a function of the neighbouring pane, not of the pane's own content. GeneratePane.vue:31 carries h-full, chaining the Generate card's height to whatever the Palettes companion happens to contain, so the composition's vertical rhythm changes when an unrelated pane gains a row.

Measured 1440x900 with an empty library companion: paneCard {y:210, h:560.1}; last control (count-slider label) bottom = 434.2; emptyTailPx = 125.9 = 22.5% of the pane is empty glass. The first CHALLENGE-D pass measured 65px of dead interior on a differently-populated companion — both correct, which is the point: the tail is unstable. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 3 "Renderer, icon or touch footprints may reserve collision space only on the axis where collision exists" (there is no collision here, only coupling); §5 law 1 "A page region, empty column, inner stage or mere padding group does not become a Card by default".
defects.mechanism: F1 — wrong primitive: h-full is meaningful only because the pane sits in a shell grid it did not ask for; the Card is being used as a page column.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/generate at 1440x900 with localStorage cleared and measure the bottom of the count-slider label against the bottom of .pane-scroll-fade: 125.9px of empty card. Save one palette (so the companion gains a row) and re-measure — the value changes, proving the height is the neighbour's decision.
defects.proposedCure: Delete h-full (and overflow-y-auto) with the Card in D-3's transposition; let the chassis size to its content and the document scroll, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3 law 6 ("one document-scrolling stage->inspector->action sequence"). Tuning the tail value cannot fix it because the value is not the pane's to set.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to the first CHALLENGE-D pass: its D-1 cure prescribes `InstrumentChassis variant="golden"`. That prop does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0 — the prop is `proportion`. A `variant="golden"` would fall through as a stray DOM attribute and the chassis would silently resolve its default proportion, reproducing exactly the D-4 failure mode (`tag="button"` on WatercolorDot).
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/instrument-chassis/types.d.ts: `export interface InstrumentChassisProps { state?: InstrumentChassisState; tone?: string; proportion?: InstrumentChassisProportion; boundaries?: readonly InstrumentChassisBoundary[]; reserve?: InstrumentChassisReserve; class?: HTMLAttributes["class"]; }`. glass-ui version confirmed 7.0.0 via `node -p "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').version"`. The erroneous cure text is at challenge-D-design.md §2 D-1 ("Transpose the route onto InstrumentChassis with variant=\"golden\"").
defects.mechanism: F3 — reached past the design system: the same mechanism as D-4, now caught before it ships. Also strengthens D-3: the producer's four exported enums map 1:1 onto the four canon clauses (golden; []; none; a state machine), so the pane hand-rolled housing the design system ships prop for prop.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — the producer type declaration is the proof. Written as `<InstrumentChassis variant="golden">` the prop would land as an HTML attribute and the chassis would use its default proportion.
defects.proposedCure: The correct transposition is `<InstrumentChassis proportion="golden" :boundaries="[]" reserve="none" :state="...">`, matching OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5's binding Generate row exactly. Recorded in the report's §C so the W25 executor does not inherit the wrong prop name.

defects.defect: BLOCKER — the sampling intent rides an UNDECLARED native `click` riding attribute fallthrough, so it has no keyboard twin. The eyedropper is the pane's sole image-sampling affordance: keyboard-only users cannot sample a color. defects.defect: MAJOR — one intake concept, two entry paths, one MIME guard. The drop path guards `file.type.startsWith("image/")`; the file-picker path has NO type check (accept="image/*" is an advisory filter a user defeats with "All Files"), and no downstream owner re-guards. A non-image reaches , the zone flips to its specimen state and announces "Image preview area, tap to sample colors", NO destructive line is shown, and two unhandled InvalidStateError rejections reach window.onerror. Falsifies the component's own header comment 'the specimen never lies' (:3).
defects.evidence: ImageDropZone.vue:87-92 (onFileSelected — no guard) vs :94-100 (onDrop — guarded) · :30 accept="image/*" · useExtractSession.ts:164-168 (readAsDataUrl then runQuantize, unguarded) · useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 (createImageBitmap unguarded). Move intake to one owner: useImageIntake.ts = useFileDialog({accept:'image/*', multiple:false, reset:true}) + useDropZone(target,{dataTypes:['image/*'], multiple:false}) — one dataTypes declaration covering both entrances — and have the session return a typed decode failure into the existing destructive register instead of discarding the promise.

defects.defect: MAJOR — the plate material is a parallel mint. The component is a dashed-edged recessed in-plate fixture (the textbook rung-2 WELL) but re-mints its material by hand from `--primary` at post-hoc 5/10/30% alpha, while the certified home already exists (.dashed-well in demo/styles/utils.css, --well-bg, --card-edge, --shadow-cartoon-sm) with two consumers. Two dashed wells now ship with two fills, two edge mints, two radii, and only one cartoon stamp. The tint is also 120 degrees off the pane's live accent axis.

Species-of-one proof: `grep -rn "bg-primary\b|border-primary\b" demo/` → alpha fills only in ImageDropZone.vue:12,14,15; Markdown.vue:346 shows the correct idiom (bg-well + solid border-primary).
defects.mechanism: A concept with a certified home (rung-2 WELL material) re-implemented locally because the affordance's geometry is bespoke; geometry and material were never separated.

result.strongestDefect: The intake-and-intent capability is HOMELESS — L-3 · L-4 · L-12 · L-13 · L-14 are one mechanism, not five findings. "A File becomes a specimen; a specimen can be sampled" is split across a leaf SFC that owns the hidden , a parent that reaches into it through a template ref + defineExpose, a sibling that emits `upload` into that reach, and an undeclared native `click` that carries the sampling intent back out. Because no single module owns it, the MIME guard exists on only one of two entrances (L-12: a .txt through the picker reaches , imgNaturalWidth 0, destructiveText [], plus two unhandled "InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.") and the sampling intent has no keyboard twin (L-13: MEASURED — programmatic focus succeeds, Enter opens nothing (eyedropperCanvas false), a pointer click opens the eyedropper (eyedropperCanvas true), and tabindex is -1 so a keyboard user never arrives — a WCAG 2.1.1 Level A failure on the pane's only sampling affordance). Both ship on /#/extract today. The cure is not five patches but one architectural transposition: TWO STATES → TWO COMPONENTS (ImageDropZone = empty state, a drop target + a real
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these were checked and found SOUND — recorded so no later seat re-files them: (1) NO deep-path reach into the library — `grep -rn "@src/" demo/ | grep -v assets/docs` returns EMPTY; ImageDropZone imports nothing from @mkbabb/value.js, and the whole extract feature imports it only through published bare subpaths (/color, /css, /quantize), all present in package.json#exports — a real consumer could write every specifier; no false proof of the public API. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied across the cone — every type-only import is `import type`, including the split at quantize-worker.ts:6-7. (3) NO second drop-zone implementation in the demo: `grep -rn 'type="file"' demo/` = 1 site, `grep -rn "dataTransfer" demo/` = 1 site, `grep -rn "@drop|dragover" demo/` = 1 site — all this file (the concept is duplicated against @vueuse/core, not against another demo module). (4) Icon source uniform — @lucide/vue in 11/11 workbench files, 0 lucide-vue-next. (5) demo/ui/card is a pure re-export barrel of glass-ui (`export { Card, … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`), the DESIGN.md-sanctioned idiom, not a fork. (6) No JS import from demo/workbenches/ into demo/shell/ or demo/color-picker/composables/boot/ — the only boot edge is the --ink-muted token seam, which is a token seam by design. (7) defineExpose is not per se un-idiomatic here (15 demo components use it); what is wrong is this particular sibling→parent→child imperative reach, not the mechanism. (8) The visual-audit rows are clean for this component: /#/extract across all four Safari matrices shows overflowX 0, pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, imgNoAlt 0; the 6 smallTapTargets are the slug bar + slider thumbs and the 3 namelessButtons are not this component (its aria-label resolves in every state, measured; the zone measures 462×180 at 1440px). (9) Named historical suspects are OUT OF CONE and not traced: demo/palettes/export.ts + usePaletteExport.ts + export/{json,bytes,rfc8785,canonical,svg,css,png,tailwind}.ts all still exist and the three-useDark note is still live at useMarkdownColors.ts:16 / useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76, but neither is reachable from ImageDropZone and I make no claim about their current state; ActionBarLayer's useLayerTransition reimplementation was not traced.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the model this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the preview stage crops instead of containing, and the instrument contradicts itself on screen. A 300x1400 portrait renders at 458x2137.3px inside a 462x320px box with overflow:hidden (14.8% visible desktop; 17.5% on iPhone 14 Pro at 323x1507.3 in 327x264). `object-contain` at ImageDropZone.vue:41 is inert because `h-full` resolves against an indefinite parent to `auto`, so the img box already equals the intrinsic ratio and object-fit has nothing to fit. Consequence measured with an 8-band specimen: the stage shows bands 4-5 (green over blue) while the palette card 40px below renders indigo/orange/yellow/black/green — three swatches nowhere in the visible frame — under a headline reading "36% of the image". ImageEyedropper additionally receives the FULL previewDataUrl (ExtractWorkbench.vue:173-175), so shown != sampled != quantised. All of this in a file whose first comment (line 3) promises "the specimen never lies".
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded clean negatives for completeness: prefers-reduced-motion IS honoured (global guard demo/styles/animations.css:184-193, transition-duration 0.01ms !important outranks the non-important inline style); verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied (both imports at :66-67 are value imports, no type-only import exists); useTemplateRef used idiomatically at :78 (edict 7); not a god module (114 lines, real encapsulation); overflowX 0 / pageErrors 0 / consoleErrors 0 on /#/extract across all four Safari matrices; rounded-xl vs rounded-panel is not a VISIBLE mismatch today (both compute to 12px); the hidden input[type=file] at :27-33 is correctly exempt from the S-era hand-rolled-input census. Also NOT reproduced: pass-1's "blank preview" sub-claim (my higher-ratio 300x1400 specimen painted correctly in WebKit desktop-light AND mobile-dark) — downgraded to engine/ratio-conditional, §6 of the report.

defects.defect: The preview stage crops instead of containing; `object-contain` is inert, so portrait images lose ~85% of themselves and the extracted palette displays colors absent from the visible frame.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:41 `class="w-full h-full object-contain rounded-xl"` inside :8 `flex flex-col items-center justify-center overflow-hidden`. Measured (pass2-probe-D/probe.json): WebKit 1440x900 — natural 300x1400 -> img rect {x:226, y:-708, w:458, h:2137.3} inside zone {w:462, h:320}, objectFit "contain", overflow "hidden" => 14.8% visible. iPhone 14 Pro — 323x1507.3 inside 327x264 => 17.5% visible. Screenshot pass2-probe-D/shots/desktop-light-tall.png: stage shows only bands 4-5 of an 8-band specimen while the palette card renders indigo/orange/yellow/black/green and the readout says '36% of the image'.
defects.mechanism: Indefinite-box geometry: the parent has min-height/max-height but no definite block size, so `height:100%` resolves to `auto`; the img box then equals its intrinsic ratio and object-fit:contain has nothing to fit; overflow:hidden clips and justify-center eats both ends.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imagedropzone/pass2-probe-D/probe.mjs (dev server on :9000) — reads B_tall_desktop / D_tall_mobile from probe.json
defects.proposedCure: Transposition: the stage declares its own geometry and the image fits into it, the inverse of today. Replace flex-centring with `grid place-items-center` on a stage carrying a declared aspect-ratio; img becomes `max-w-full max-h-full w-auto h-auto`. object-contain then becomes unnecessary rather than inert, and the dvh-coupled `max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]` dies with it.

defects.defect: The sample/eyedropper affordance is keyboard-unreachable, while role="button" keeps advertising it and its aria-label instructs an action AT users cannot perform.

defects.reproduction: node .../pass2-probe-D/probe2.mjs — the tabWalk block, run after a real setInputFiles upload

defects.defect: The drag-hover state cancels itself whenever the pointer crosses a child, so the drop target strobes while the file is still over it.
defects.evidence: ImageDropZone.vue:23-24 put @dragover/@dragleave on the container; children at :37 (img) and :46 (placeholder) have no pointer-events:none and there is no dragenter depth counter. Measured (probe2.json, each step awaited across Vue's update tick): rest -> `border-primary/30 bg-primary/5`; dragover on ZONE -> `border-primary bg-primary/10 scale-[1.01]`; dragleave bubbling from CHILD (pointer still inside) -> back to `border-primary/30 bg-primary/5`; dragover from CHILD -> lit again. Computed transition-duration 0.3s on transition-all.
defects.mechanism: Absent state design: dragleave bubbles from descendants, and the handler cannot distinguish 'left the zone' from 'entered a child of the zone'; over a populated zone the img covers 100% of the surface.
defects.reproduction: node .../pass2-probe-D/probe2.mjs — the `drag` array in probe2.json

defects.defect: In forced-colors the drag state is invisible — border delta is exactly zero, leaving a 0.5% scale as the only signal.

Coverage gap: audit/visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/ holds 5 routes and /#/extract is not among them.
defects.mechanism: State conveyed by color alone — violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ('never color-only'; 'distinct ... in forced colors').

defects.defect: A rejected drop is completely silent — no error state was ever designed, and the zone has no channel to the error register the pane already owns.
defects.evidence: ImageDropZone.vue:94-100 — `if (file?.type.startsWith("image/")) emit("file", file)` with no else. defects.mechanism: Absent state design plus a missing emit channel: the error surface exists 200px away and the component has no way to address it.
defects.reproduction: node .../pass2-probe-D/probe2.mjs — the beforeReject/afterReject block

defects.defect: No disabled state exists at all — the zone stays live during quantization and while the camera viewfinder is open directly beneath it.

defects.defect: The corner tag is hover-only, so the sole visible hint that the image is tappable never appears on any touch device.

defects.reproduction: node .../pass2-probe-D/probe.mjs — D_tall_mobile.cornerTag in probe.json

defects.defect: No designed focus state: the control wears the WebKit UA ring while the demo's one certified focus recipe sits unused, and it mixes :focus with :focus-visible in the same file.

defects.reproduction: node .../pass2-probe-D/probe.mjs — A_focused block; visible as a blue-white system halo in pass2-probe-D/shots/desktop-light-{tall,wide}.png

defects.defect: Two upload affordances for one action in one pane — the 462x180 dashed zone and a 22px toolbar icon 8px below it, wired together by an imperative defineExpose.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, published surface) for demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — claude-opus-5[1m] (1M-context variant). The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; the declaration is honoured, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — GeneratePane.vue:14-20 handles GenerateControls' two-payload `save: [colors, name]` emit with a ONE-parameter function and substitutes the literal "Generated Palette" for the payload it drops, so the user's typed palette name (GenerateControls.vue:144-149, aria-label="Palette name", visibly editable in the shipped build) never reaches usePaletteStore.createPalette. The component's single piece of real logic silently destroys user input, and no gate in the repo can see it: TS assigns a 1-arity handler to a 2-arity emit by design, eslint exits 0, and the O-20 oracle asserts only that the save button exists.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative is claimed for the component as a whole. One sub-question DOES resolve clean and is proven positively: **the library-import question**. Nothing in the GeneratePane graph reaches src/ internals; the single value.js hop (demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:33-34) goes through `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`, both real keys in package.json#exports, both writable verbatim by a real downstream consumer. Proven three ways: (a) `grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js' demo/` yields only published subpaths (/color 25, /css 10, /math 6, /easing 5, /quantize 4) and zero `@src/*`; (b) `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution` resolves both to /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/*.d.ts; (c) the live dev server rewrites them to /@fs/.../dist/subpaths/color.js and css.js. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is also clean — every type-only import in both files carries `import type` (GeneratePane.vue:8; GenerateControls.vue:19,33,34).

defects.defect: The user's palette name is discarded at the pane/controls boundary. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors: string[], name: string]` and fires it with both payloads; GeneratePane's sole listener takes one parameter and calls `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", …)`. The plate's editable title is a live affordance that lies. usePaletteStore.createPalette dedups on name.toLowerCase(), so the whole generated library collapses into one name bucket.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:48-50 (emit decl), :102-104 (emit fire with paletteName.value), :144-149 (input v-model="paletteName" aria-label="Palette name"); demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:14-20 (onSave(colors) → createPalette("Generated Palette", …)); demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:66-72 (name-keyed dedup); shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png renders the editable title; `npx eslint demo/workbenches/generate/*.vue --max-warnings=0` → exit 0
defects.mechanism: Split semantic ownership — 'the palette's name' has two homes (a ref in the child, a string literal in the parent) and the emit boundary between them loses one. TS parameter bivariance makes a 1-arity handler assignable to a 2-arity emit, so the type system cannot see it.
defects.reproduction: Static and total: `onSave` has one binding position, the emit has two payload slots, and the literal "Generated Palette" is the only value that reaches createPalette. Both entry points (plate Save button and dock Tools → Save, usePaneRouter.ts:197 → GeneratePane defineExpose.save:24) funnel through the same emit. Not driven live — saving mutates the local store and this seat is read-only.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `onSave` AND the pane's LIBRARY_PORT_KEY inject entirely. Name, colours and the save verb already live together in the plate; move the store call into useColorGeneration (renamed useGenerate), which owns name/palette/save(). The pane then has nothing to forward — which is the point: a component whose only logic is re-emitting its child's data is a place for data to get lost.

defects.defect: The dock's three generate actions (Regenerate / Save palette / Copy colors) are dead no-ops on every mobile viewport. `generatePaneRef` is only ever written by `onDesktopLeftMount`, which is bound solely to the desktop-left PaneSlot inside the `v-else` desktop branch; the mobile PaneSlot carries no `:on-mount`. The action bar itself is keyed on currentView with no breakpoint guard, so it renders on mobile and every handler resolves null, swallowed by optional chaining.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/App.vue:77 (v-if="!isDesktop"), :83-92 (mobile PaneSlot — NO :on-mount), :101-109 with :105 (:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount", inside <template v-else>), :317 (const generatePaneRef = ref<any>(null)), :326 (the sole write site), :347; demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:191-203 (view-keyed, no breakpoint guard), :196-198 (paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()); shots/safari-mobile-light/generate.png shows the Tools paintbrush trigger present in the mobile dock; `grep -rn generatePaneRef demo/` returns exactly the three App.vue lines
defects.mechanism: An instance-handle command bus whose wiring is duplicated per layout branch, so one branch can silently omit it — and the masking `?.` (L-7) converts the omission into silence instead of a crash.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED-BY-CONSTRUCTION. The write site is unreachable when isDesktop===false, which is the same predicate that mounts the mobile slot; the static chain has no second branch. A live 390px probe was attempted and abandoned: the MCP browser is a headed window that ignored browser_resize(390,844) — innerWidth stayed 1440.
defects.proposedCure: Replace PaneActionRefs with a command registry: demo/shell/commands.ts provides a Ref<Command[]>; a workbench calls registerCommands([{key,title,icon,run}]) in its own setup and the dock renders what is registered. Layout-independent by construction (registration rides mount, wherever the pane mounts), fully typed. Deletes defineExpose from all three panes, PaneActionRefs from usePaneRouter, three ref<any> and both on*Mount callbacks from App.vue. One repair also cures L-7 and L-9.

defects.defect: The demo's declared value.js trust boundary has drifted from the exports map it claims to mirror. tsconfig.demo.json#paths declares 8 keys ('.', /color, /parsing, /math, /easing, /units, /transform, /quantize) under a comment calling them 'the 8 public keys'; package.json#exports declares 7 and a different set (/color /value /css /easing /math /transform /quantize, no root). Three path targets do not exist on disk; two real public keys have no path entry.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports dump (7 keys, and `node -e "p=require('./package.json'); console.log(p.main,p.module,p.types)"` → undefined undefined undefined); file-existence probe → MISSING dist/index.d.ts, MISSING dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts, MISSING dist/subpaths/units.d.ts, EXISTS dist/subpaths/css.d.ts, EXISTS dist/subpaths/value.d.ts; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution` → '@mkbabb/value.js/color' resolved to dist/subpaths/color.d.ts (path-mapped, no Package ID) vs '@mkbabb/value.js/css' resolved to dist/subpaths/css.d.ts WITH Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0' (Node package self-reference)
defects.mechanism: Two hand-maintained descriptions of one public surface. The component's transitive core imports one key from each side, so a single file typechecks through two different resolution mechanisms.
defects.reproduction: Run the traceResolution command above and grep for value.js — the Package ID appears on /css and not on /color, which is the fingerprint of the two mechanisms. Both land on the same file today, so this is drift, not a live break.
defects.proposedCure: One mechanism, not two. vite.config.ts:38-50 already GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports; do the same for tsconfig paths (a prebuild-emitted tsconfig.demo.paths.json), or delete `paths` outright and let Node self-reference serve all seven — it demonstrably already serves /css and /value.

defects.defect: The pane's entire public surface is a defineExpose of three optional-chained passthroughs onto methods that are statically guaranteed to exist, consumed through Ref<any> with a second optional chain — four ?. hops and two `any`s between a dock button and a seed assignment, none of it type-checked.

defects.defect: A second physical copy of @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 (the published tarball) is installed in node_modules as a transitive dependency of glass-ui and keyframes.js, inside the tree that is supposed to dogfood the working copy. vite.config.ts asserts the opposite as its rationale for the self-alias set.

defects.mechanism: percentage-height-against-an-indefinite-parent. ImageDropZone.vue:41 `w-full h-full object-contain`; `h-full` = height:100% whose containing block (the root, line 8-9 `flex flex-col` + min-h-[140px], plus ExtractWorkbench.vue:20's min-h-[180px] max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]) has an INDEFINITE height, so it resolves to `auto`. result.strongestDefect: P2-2 — `object-contain` is inert and a portrait preview renders at 9.32% of itself. Pass 1 owns the strongest statement about the component's INPUT (it cannot receive a dropped image); this is the strongest about its OUTPUT. A component whose own header comment states "the specimen never lies" (ImageDropZone.vue:3) shows a measured 9.32% of a portrait photograph — centred, silently guillotined, 1557px cut above and 1558px below — beside a palette strip computed from 100% of it and a readout claiming "36% of the image": three elements on one plate describing three different pictures (evidence-tall-image-crop.png). The declaration meant to prevent exactly this is present and doing nothing, because `h-full` against an indefinite parent height resolves to `auto`, so the img box is 458x3435 inside a 462x320 zone — 458 x (900/120) = 3435, exact. Reproduced through the real picker path with a real on-disk file, so it does not depend on the synthetic drag events my first method wrongly relied on.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the cleared-hazard proof rather than a soundness proof. Known local hazards checked and NEGATIVE with positive evidence: (1) no `defineModel` — the only reactive state is one `ref<boolean>` (`dragging`, :79), so the stale-read/async-round-trip hazard cannot apply; (2) no colour maths — no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no `stableHue`; (3) no `ValueUnit` construction, so no nesting accumulation; (4) no slider and no pointer capture taken, so no reka-ui pointercancel/lostpointercapture leak; (5) zero `requestAnimationFrame` in the file — `grep -n "addEventListener|requestAnimationFrame|setInterval|setTimeout|new .*Observer" ImageDropZone.vue` has no matches, so no PRM-RAF contribution (ExtractWorkbench.vue:249's single `await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)` is a one-shot, not a loop); (6) no WebGL — REPORT.md's `WebGL: context lost` console error is on `/#/`, not `/#/extract`; (7) no leak surface — only template-bound listeners torn down with the node, no timers, no observers, no accumulating collections. Also cleared with measurement: `input.value = ""` (:91) runs AFTER the synchronous emit so the File reference is already handed off — not a stale-read defect; the hidden input's synthetic click does NOT recurse (measured 3 file choosers for 3 activations, dz-probe9.mjs) because the HTML click-in-progress flag bounds it, which corroborates pass-1 C3's claim that the recursion is bounded while the duplicate event is not; the empty-state keyboard path is CORRECT (Enter→1 chooser, Space→2, scrollY 0 proving `.prevent` works); `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean (only value imports, no type-only import to mark); and this component contributes ZERO to REPORT.json's `/#/extract` a11y counts — the 3 namelessButtons are ExtractControls' DockControls, which carry `title` only and are missed by visual/capture.mjs:102-105 (it tests aria-label || aria-labelledby || textContent, never title), while the zone always carries an aria-label and measures 462x180 empty / 462x320 developed, so it is neither a small tap target nor a nameless button. Methodology caveat recorded in the report: my first probes used synthesised DragEvents, which bypass Chromium's drag controller and therefore cannot see pass-1's C1; those conclusions were discarded and every headline finding was re-reproduced through the real picker path with real on-disk files.
