defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/App.vue:83-92 (mobile PaneSlot, no :on-mount) vs App.vue:104 (:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"), App.vue:317,322-327; demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 (`paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` etc.). Measured on an iPhone 14 context (probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs): dockButtons includes "Regenerate","Save palette","Copy colors"; seedBefore "seed: 93eefeaa" → after dock Regenerate "seed: 93eefeaa" (unchanged) → after in-plate Regenerate "seed: 2d613b79".
defects.mechanism: A ref-capture callback wired to one of two mount sites, with optional-chaining on the method acting as insurance that converts a wiring break into silence.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs — the `mobile` block shows the dock Regenerate leaving the seed unchanged while the in-plate Regenerate moves it on the same page load.
defects.proposedCure: Pass :on-mount to the mobile PaneSlot with a handler keyed off currentConfig's mobile slot name, and drop the second `?.` throughout usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 (gradient and mix have the identical shape and identical exposure) so the next unwired slot throws instead of going quiet.

defects.defect: Clipboard failures are swallowed and successes are unannounced. glass-ui 7's writeClipboard returns a discriminated {ok}/{ok,reason} result explicitly so consumers own their feedback; GenerateControls awaits and discards it in both copy verbs.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:106-113; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts ("Returns the discriminated result … for identical call ergonomics: const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)"). Measured (probes/r2-c-clipboard-at-keyboard.mjs) with navigator.clipboard.writeText forced to reject NotAllowedError: {"writeAttempts":1,"unhandledRejections":0}, console warning "[useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected: NotAllowedError: denied", and ariaLiveBefore === ariaLiveAfter byte for byte.
defects.mechanism: A result-returning library primitive consumed as if it were void; no feedback channel exists in the pane at all (see C-3, C-6).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-c-clipboard-at-keyboard.mjs — patches writeText to reject, clicks Copy all colors, and diffs the page's live-region text before/after.
defects.proposedCure: Use the composable the app already uses for the share link — App.vue:361 `useClipboard({ resetMs: 2000 })` — for both plate copy verbs, and drive the button's own confirmation state from its `status`. Do not hand-roll a timer; that is the pattern Glass 7 retired.

defects.defect: Save reaches past the port's own action into the raw store, so the save produces no feedback anywhere in the app. GeneratePane calls pm.createPalette (the raw usePaletteStore writer) instead of pm.onCurrentPaletteSaved, which is the same write plus the expandedId assignment that is the app's only save confirmation.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:19; demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:142 (raw createPalette) vs :151 (onCurrentPaletteSaved); demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:73-76 (`const palette = deps.createPalette(name, colors); if (palette.id != null) expandedId.value = palette.id;`). demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:49 uses the action correctly. Measured: plate liveRegions 0 (probes/r2-a-dom-save-a11y.mjs), so with C-3 and C-5 the save is entirely invisible.
defects.mechanism: Two consumers performing the same domain operation by different routes — one through the action layer, one through the store — so the action layer's side effects are silently skipped by the newer caller.
defects.reproduction: Read GeneratePane.vue:19 against usePaletteActions.ts:65-77; then run probes/r2-a-dom-save-a11y.mjs and observe savedPalettes grows while the plate reports nothing (liveRegions 0) and the Palettes pane does not expand the row.
defects.proposedCure: Folded into C-1: `@save="pm.onCurrentPaletteSaved"`. The pane's script then holds only the two injects and the defineExpose.

defects.defect: The component's only test is deterministically FAILING, and Playwright is not in CI. o20 test #2 asserts string equality between the raw generatePalette serialization stamped on data-stops and getComputedStyle().backgroundColor, which re-serializes; the spec's own comment claims 'rgb() strings' that the generator has never produced. There are zero unit tests, and the passing leg is vacuous against every defect above.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --reporter=line` → "1 failed, 1 passed", twice, with the same shape: Expected "oklch(91.103090821765% 0.046221964117 83.517225617543deg)" vs Received "oklch(0.911031 0.046222 83.5172)". Assertion at e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts:98-105; serializer at demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:235-243. `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` → lint, vue-tsc ×2, build, npm test (vitest), verify-packed-surface — no playwright step. `grep -rln "GeneratePane|GenerateControls|useColorGeneration|generatePalette" test/` → no matches.
defects.mechanism: An oracle asserting byte-equality across a serialization boundary, guarding a component in a suite no runner executes — so it rotted silently when the generator's output space changed.
defects.reproduction: npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --reporter=line (run twice; deterministic). Vacuity check: GeneratePane.vue:19 already hardcodes the name (C-1) and the swatch attrs are already inert (C-2), yet lint + both vue-tsc + npm test + o20 test #1 are all green.
defects.proposedCure: (a) Make o20 test #2 compare colours rather than strings — resolve both sides through one serializer (the app's own colorToCss) or compare parsed components with a tolerance. (b) Add a smoke-project step to .github/workflows/ci.yml; an oracle no runner executes is a comment. (c) Add the two vitest legs that would have caught C-1 and C-2: mount GeneratePane, emit save with a name, assert createPalette saw it; mount GenerateControls, assert the swatch is a button with an accessible name whose click calls writeClipboard.

defects.defect: Unchecked casts at the Select seam. onPresetChange/onHarmonyChange cast reka-ui's AcceptableValue (string|number|boolean|Record|null) straight to PresetName/HarmonyName; generatePalette then dereferences GENERATION_PRESETS[preset] unconditionally inside a render-critical computed.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:75-81; demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:220 (`const p = GENERATION_PRESETS[preset]` then `p.l[0]`); demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts:26-28 (the computed the render reads). Measured (probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs boundary sweep): {"label":"bad preset name","ok":false,"err":"TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'l')"}; {"label":"bad harmony name","ok":true,"out":{"len":0}}.
defects.mechanism: `as` erases a runtime check at an external-library boundary; the resulting invalid state is only discovered by a throw inside render, which unmounts the pane into the ErrorBoundary.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the live Select path — this is a HYPOTHESIS on reachability. The throw itself is reproduced: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs, boundary rows 'bad preset name' / 'bad harmony name'.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow, do not cast: `const isPreset = (v: unknown): v is PresetName => PRESET_NAMES.includes(v as PresetName); function onPresetChange(value: AcceptableValue) { if (isPreset(value)) preset.value = value; }` and the same for harmony. Optionally make generatePalette refuse an unknown preset explicitly rather than dereferencing undefined.

defects.defect: Generated colours are unrounded 15-significant-digit OKLCh strings, and they reach both the clipboard and localStorage. generatedCss serializes without rounding.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:235-243. Measured clipboard payload for a count-5 'Copy all colors' (probes/r2-c-clipboard-at-keyboard.mjs): "oklch(65.524221608648% 0.131932607486 230.90389332734deg), oklch(71.749844222795% 0.183381911378 8.411657377378deg), …" with {"payloadLen": 294}; ~700 chars at the slider's max of 12. Every PaletteColor.css persisted under localStorage['color-palettes'] carries the same.
defects.mechanism: No precision policy at the serialization boundary of the generator; twelve significant digits of a value whose input was Math.random are pure noise, and the same noise makes C-7's string oracle unfixable as written.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-c-clipboard-at-keyboard.mjs — prints copyResult.payload and payloadLen.
defects.proposedCure: Round inside generatedCss before serializing (3 decimals on L%, 4 on C, 2 on H is well inside 1 JND), or thread a precision option through serializeCssColor. One site in the shared core, not a per-consumer format.

defects.defect: The count slider thumb is 12 CSS px wide — the component's entire contribution to the visual audit's smallTapTargets — and separately, the 5–12 swatches escape that audit altogether because C-2 leaves them as roleless spans with tabIndex -1.
defects.evidence: Measured: {"sliderThumb":{"tag":"SPAN","w":12,"h":24,"aria":"Color count","valuenow":"5"}} (probes/r2-a-dom-save-a11y.mjs). REPORT.json /#/generate rows list exactly {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Color count"} on both desktop matrices and {"w":12,"h":44,…} on both mobile — 1 of the 5 flagged; the other 4 are the dock login capsule (22×22 ×3) and its 160×23 unnamed slug input. WCAG 2.5.8 AA requires 24×24. Audit probe selector at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:89-91 excludes roleless spans, so the swatches (36×36 on mobile, 40×40 desktop) are never measured.
defects.mechanism: A root-primitive geometry defect surfaced per-consumer, compounded by an audit selector that can only see elements a component chose to make interactive.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-a-dom-save-a11y.mjs — sliderThumb block; cross-check docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json rows for /#/generate.
defects.proposedCure: Expand the thumb's hit area in glass-ui's Slider via a pseudo-element so the 12 px visual rail is preserved (edicts 4/5) — not a per-instance class here; note GenerateControls.vue:305 already carries one per-instance override (--slider-track-bg: transparent) standing in for a missing glass-ui variant. Separately, add a roleless-interactive cross-check to the audit harness so C-2-class components cannot hide from the tap-target census.

defects.defect: The plate title's editability is hover-only, so it is undiscoverable on touch, and its focus ring is a per-instance re-implementation of glass-ui's root focus-ring that also renders wrong.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:144-149. Measured (probes/r2-d-title-affordance-slider.mjs): rest {"boxShadow":"none","border":"0px","bg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","textDecoration":"none","cursor":"text"}; hovered {"textDecoration":"underline"}; focused boxShadow "… rgb(28, 25, 23) 0px 0px 0px 2px …" — fully opaque, not the requested ring-ring/40. The sibling Copy button uses the root class: measured className "button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover shrink-0". Visually confirmed in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png — the title reads as a display heading with no field chrome.
defects.mechanism: An affordance expressed only through :hover on a surface whose primary matrix is touch, plus a per-instance Tailwind override duplicating (and mis-rendering) an existing root primitive.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-d-title-affordance-slider.mjs — nameInput.rest / .hovered / .focused.
defects.proposedCure: Use the root `focus-ring` class (edict 5) and give the field a rest-state affordance that survives no-hover — a dotted underline at rest, or reuse the card family's existing rename control rather than a bare styled input.

defects.defect: `cssColorOpaque` is a dead injection carrying a non-null assertion: declared in GeneratePane, never read in script or template.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:7,10. `grep -c cssColorOpaque demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue` → 1 (the declaration itself). It survives noUnusedLocals because <script setup> bindings are template-visible by construction.
defects.mechanism: Dead code retained through a refactor; the `!` additionally converts a missing provider into a silent undefined binding rather than a failure.
defects.reproduction: grep -c cssColorOpaque demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue → 1; grep -n cssColorOpaque on the same file shows only line 10.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 7 and 10. If a future need arises, inject without the `!` and handle absence explicitly.

defects.defect: Not the Vue 3.5 idiom, and the optional-call that masked C-4. The pane uses ref + InstanceType with a string template ref where the house idiom is useTemplateRef, and its defineExpose optional-chains methods the child demonstrably exposes.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:12,22-26,36 (`controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()`); the child exposes all three at demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:115. House idiom already in use at demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:78, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:223, demo/color-picker/App.vue:161. Same older shape at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:9 and ExtractWorkbench.vue:222.
defects.mechanism: Optional chaining used as wiring insurance: the second `?.` can only ever hide a broken wire, which is exactly what happened one level up in usePaneRouter.ts (C-4).
defects.reproduction: Read GeneratePane.vue:12,22-26 against GenerateControls.vue:115; the exposed methods always exist, so `?.()` is unreachable-by-design except when the ref itself is stale — the C-4 case.
defects.proposedCure: Switch to `useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof GenerateControls>>("controlsRef")` and drop the method-level `?.` (keep only the ref-level one), so a future unwired slot throws loudly. Move GradientPane.vue and ExtractWorkbench.vue with it.

defects.defect: The count slider has no reka-ui pointer-capture leak recovery, and neither does the glass-ui root Slider, while the picker carries a per-consumer cure for exactly this documented hazard.
defects.evidence: `grep -c "pointercancel\|lostpointercapture" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/slider.js` → 0; same for dist/glass-ui.js → 0. `grep -rn "lostpointercapture|pointercancel" demo/ | grep -v node_modules | wc -l` → 8, all in gradient / eyedropper / picker; none in workbenches/generate. The cure exists at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts ("leak recovery (pointercancel/lostpointercapture)"). Consumer at demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:297-307.
defects.mechanism: A known upstream (reka-ui) defect cured once, per-consumer, in the picker, and never lifted to the design-system root — so every other Slider consumer is unprotected.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a HYPOTHESIS. No touch pointer-capture leak was attempted against this slider. The asymmetry is measured by the greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Lift the recovery into glass-ui's Slider (edict 4) and dissolve useSliderTouchGates into it, rather than copying the gate into a second consumer.

defects.defect: Domain boundaries degrade silently: generatePalette returns [] for count 0 / negative / NaN, and mulberry32's `seed |= 0` aliases NaN, 0 and 2^53 to the same stream.
defects.evidence: Measured (probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs boundary sweep): count=0 → len 0; count=-3 → len 0; count=NaN → len 0; seed=NaN, seed=0 and seed=2^53 all yield the identical palette (first stop "oklch(55.008243642515% 0.11313958766 95.914515126497deg)"), while seed=-1 differs. Source: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:213-233 and demo/color-session/prng.ts:3 (`seed |= 0`). The empty cases are currently unreachable through the UI (`:min="1"` at demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:301); the count=1 analogous guard at generate-color.ts:110 holds correctly.
defects.mechanism: A pure core that returns a degenerate value rather than refusing invalid input, plus int32 coercion in the PRNG seed that silently aliases out-of-range seeds.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the UI path — HYPOTHESIS on reachability. The function-level behaviour is reproduced: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-pane/probes/r2-b-mobile-perf-boundary.mjs, `boundary` array.
defects.proposedCure: Make generatePalette refuse non-positive / non-finite counts explicitly rather than returning []; and either document the int32 seed domain on mulberry32 or coerce with `>>> 0` at the seed source so the plate's bench-note hex is unambiguously the seed in use.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — ExtractPane.vue:27 imports one `Symbol` (COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY) from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts, a 92-module god facade that constructs the entire palettes/admin/auth subsystem. Measured marginal cost to ExtractPane's closure: 22 modules / 84,995 bytes of runtime (value-edge) code, or 41 modules / 161,227 bytes counting type edges — including all 4 admin API clients, all 7 admin panel SFCs, and the whole auth stack. Runtime-confirmed: Playwright resource probe on http://localhost:9000/#/extract shows useAdminUsers.ts, useAdminAudit.ts, useAdminTags.ts, useAdminFlagged.ts, admin-users.ts, admin-palettes.ts, admin-colors.ts, admin-audit.ts, sessionToken.ts, useUserAuth.ts, useSession.ts all loaded. The cost is currently masked because App.vue:351 wires the facade eagerly — which sharpens rather than softens the finding: five lazy workbench panes hard-import the module that defines the admin graph, so the eager-boot defect can never be cured while they do.

defects.defect: ExtractPane imports the COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY injection Symbol from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts — the module that also constructs the 5-port palettes/admin/auth facade — welding a 37-line presentational shell to a 92-module subsystem. Key co-location with the provider means every consumer pays the producer's cost. Systemic: 5 workbench files do this (extract, generate, mix ×2, gradient). Secondary asymmetry: the same key is injected 3 ways — ExtractPane.vue:36 `inject(...)!`, PalettesPane.vue:165 `inject(...)!`, ColorPicker.vue:198 `inject(...)` with no assertion.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:27 `import { COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY } from "../../palettes/usePalettePorts";` · key declared at demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:275, factory at :43 importing 15 sub-composables at :4-20. Static closure walk (value-edges only, type imports excluded): ExtractPane 45 modules / 206,496 B; ExtractWorkbench 22 modules; MARGINAL from the key import = 22 modules / 84,995 B (demo/palettes/api/index.ts, useAdmin{Audit,Flagged,Tags,Users}.ts, useBrowsePalettes.ts, useColorNameQueue.ts, usePaletteActions.ts, useSlugMigration.ts, useTagEdit.ts, useVersionHistory.ts, useFilteredList.ts, constants.ts, demo/platform/auth/{sessionToken,sessions,useAdminAuth,useSession,useUserAuth}.ts, platform/storage/useSafeStorage.ts, platform/transport/{api-problem,client}.ts). Including type edges: 41 modules / 161,227 B, adding 7 admin panel SFCs + demo/shell/{useViewManager,viewSchema}.ts. Live Playwright page.evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/extract returned adminModules=[useDockAdminMode.ts,useAdminAuth.ts,useAdminAudit.ts,useAdminUsers.ts,useAdminTags.ts,useAdminFlagged.ts,admin-users.ts,admin-palettes.ts,admin-colors.ts,admin-audit.ts], authModules=[useAdminAuth.ts,useUserAuth.ts,useSession.ts,sessionToken.ts]. Peer sites: GradientVisualizer.vue:27, MixSourceSelector.vue:6, MixPane.vue:10, GeneratePane.vue:6.
defects.mechanism: Injection-key co-located with the provider factory: a leaf value (Symbol + type) lives inside the module that constructs the whole subsystem, inverting the consumer/producer cost relationship.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/delta2.mjs (prints the 22-module / 84,995-byte marginal set). Runtime: Playwright navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/extract then page.evaluate reading performance.getEntriesByType('resource') filtered on /Admin|admin-/ and /sessionToken|useUserAuth|useSession/.
defects.proposedCure: Extract a leaf demo/palettes/keys.ts holding the 5 InjectionKey symbols plus 5 HAND-DECLARED port interfaces — the exact idiom demo/color-session/keys.ts already runs (which is why ExtractWorkbench.vue:190's CSS_COLOR_KEY import costs nothing). usePalettePorts.ts imports its keys instead of exporting them. The derived `ReturnType<typeof providePalettePorts>` types at usePalettePorts.ts:264-269 must go — that idiom is precisely what forces the consumer to see the constructor. Five call sites repoint; the admin graph becomes splittable out of the eager boot for the first time.

defects.defect: `DisplayColorSpace` has four homes. ExtractPane.vue:30 declares its own copy of a type that demo/color-session/color-model.ts:29 already exports, and two more copies live in the same subtree. All four are structurally identical because demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:37 defines `PickerSpace = SpaceId` (itself a bare alias of a library type — a standing edict-2 violation). Aggravated by the router boundary erasing the contract entirely.
defects.evidence: grep -rn 'SpaceId | "hex"' demo src → demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:202, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:30, demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:21 (this one EXPORTED). Canonical: demo/color-session/color-model.ts:29 `export type DisplayColorSpace = PickerSpace | "hex"` with demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:37 `export type PickerSpace = SpaceId`. Producer of the value: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:139 `return { colorSpace: model.value.selectedColorSpace }` typed by the color-session definition. Contract erasure: usePaneRouter.ts:62-66 types PaneSlot.props as `Record<string, unknown>`; demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:121-126 binds `v-bind="liveProps"` onto `<component :is>`.
defects.mechanism: Unique-semantic-ownership violation via alias chaining: SpaceId → PickerSpace (alias) → DisplayColorSpace ×4. Two names for one type make a third and fourth feel free.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'SpaceId | "hex"' /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/src
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three extract-local declarations plus useImageSampler.ts:21's export; import `type DisplayColorSpace` from demo/color-session/color-model. Retire PickerSpace in favour of SpaceId from @mkbabb/value.js/color — the demo should speak the library's name for the library's concept. Separately give the pane registry a discriminated union of per-pane prop shapes so Record<string, unknown> stops erasing the contract at the only call site.

defects.defect: glass-ui's DockControl declares no accessible-name prop, so the demo invented two conventions that split cleanly along the shell/workbench boundary — and ExtractControls picked the one that produces unnamed buttons. The 3 nameless buttons the visual audit reports on /#/extract in all 4 Safari matrices are exactly the 3 DockControls of this component's control bar.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts __VLS_Props = { shape, compact, active, type, disabled, as, asChild, class } — no label/ariaLabel; `title` is an undeclared fallthrough attribute. Naming split measured across demo/**/*.vue: DockControl with aria-label = 8 (ALL under demo/shell/dock/: Dock.vue:143,144,154; ActionBarToggle.vue:86; ActionBarLayer.vue:129; SlugEditLayer.vue:91,104,112); DockControl with ONLY title = 11 (ALL under demo/workbenches/: GradientVisualizer.vue:254; MixResultDisplay.vue:121,128,136; ExtractWorkbench.vue:49; ExtractControls.vue:40,49,83; ImageEyedropper.vue:11,44,51); with NEITHER = 0. Visual audit: REPORT.md:98,105,110,112 report namelessButtons=3 for /#/extract in every matrix (every other non-blob route reports 0 or 1). Live Playwright DOM probe on /#/extract: the only 3 visible buttons with aria-label=null are title="Upload image", title="Open camera", title="Reset", all with closest('.pane-scroll-fade') truthy; the other 8 visible buttons all carry aria-label. Probe caveat recorded: capture.mjs:102-105 computes the name from aria-label||aria-labelledby||textContent and ignores title, which accname admits as a last resort.
defects.mechanism: The design system does not own the accessible-name concept for its own control, so each consuming area invented one and they diverged. Two spellings of one concept means the concept is undefined.
defects.reproduction: Playwright: navigate http://localhost:9000/#/extract, then page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>b.getClientRects().length).map(b=>({title:b.getAttribute('title'),ariaLabel:b.getAttribute('aria-label'),inExtract:!!b.closest('.pane-scroll-fade')})))
defects.proposedCure: Add a `label?: string` prop to glass-ui DockControl, rendered as aria-label on the host button and reused for the tooltip — one prop, one name, one home (edict 4: primitives belong in glass-ui). Then delete all 19 title=/aria-label= spellings in favour of label=. This is a glass-ui BH-relay item under the standing relay edict, not a demo patch.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-directory layer of one-line re-export shims over @mkbabb/glass-ui — the fossil of the retired shadcn-vue tree kept alive as an import alias. Both paths are live simultaneously, and ExtractPane takes the shim while its own sibling takes the direct path. The shim also flattens glass-ui's subpath map, pulling the full barrel where the direct path pulls one chunk.
defects.evidence: demo/ui/card/index.ts is one line in full: `export { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Then make the e2e assert the landing, not the text: stamp the computed target on the canvas as a data attribute and compare it to the well's live box.

defects.defect: The settle event — the only completion signal the component owns — is inaudible to assistive technology. The design premise 'no spinner: the animation IS the progress' has no non-visual counterpart: no aria-live, no role=status, no focus move.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'aria-live\|role="status"\|role="alert"' demo/workbenches/mix/` -> no output. During `mixing` the plate contains only the aria-hidden ghost (MixResultDisplay.vue:63-73); the canvas is correctly aria-hidden (MixAnimationCanvas.vue:32-33). Premise stated at MixPane.vue:107-110 and useMixingAnimation.ts:11-13.
defects.mechanism: progress semantics carried entirely by a decorative, AT-removed surface, with no equivalent announced channel
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: grep of the whole mix tree plus reading the ghost branch. The absence is total, so no dynamic probe adds information.
defects.proposedCure: Announce on the forward edge, where the component already has the seam: a visually-hidden `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region in MixResultDisplay that emits the result string when `ghost` flips false, and `aria-busy` on the plate while ghosted. That is the honest non-visual twin of the animation, and it costs no spinner.

defects.defect: The rAF loop survives KeepAlive deactivation: `onBeforeUnmount` and `useRAFLoop`'s `onScopeDispose` never run on a pane swap, and there is no `onDeactivated`, so the narration keeps painting into a parked off-screen canvas and the phase machine advances while the pane is invisible.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:187 (`onBeforeUnmount(() => loop.stop())`) is the only teardown; glass-ui's dispose is scope-based (dist/useRAFLoop-B3YlWK4M.js:85 `r() && i(B)`). Live instance chain from `.dashed-well`: MixPane -> AsyncComponentWrapper -> KeepAlive -> BaseTransition -> ... -> PaneSlot (PaneSlot.vue:120 `<KeepAlive :max="max">`). MEASURED createRadialGradient counter across a mid-mix route swap: [{t:152,'still on /#/mix',27},{t:274,'just after route swap',83},{t:675,'deactivated +400ms',371,delta 288},{t:1376,'deactivated +1100ms',509,delta 426,mixPhase:'done'},{t:2177,'deactivated +1900ms',509,deltaAfterEpilogue:0}] — 426 gradient allocations painted while parked; bounded, terminates at the epilogue.
defects.mechanism: lifecycle coverage gap — teardown wired only to unmount in a subtree that is cached, not unmounted
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix: monkey-patch CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.createRadialGradient with a counter, call MixPane.setupState.startMix(), wait 150 ms, set location.hash='#/palettes', then sample the counter at +400/+1100/+1900 ms.
defects.proposedCure: Add `onDeactivated(() => { loop.stop(); if (!settledFired) { settledFired = true; onSettled(); } })` and `onActivated` symmetry if a parked mid-mix should re-arm. Park the clock but still discharge the forward edge, so reactivation can never land on a strand.

defects.defect: Hand-rolled prefers-reduced-motion subscription duplicates glass-ui's own `useReducedMotion` primitive — a second per-instance matchMedia listener for a query the library already tracks with a shared singleton.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:70-72 `useBreakpoint("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")`. glass-ui exports the purpose-built primitive: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/motion/core/index.d.ts:6 `export * from "./useReducedMotion"`; impl dist/useReducedMotion-vCXA_vyM.js is a module-level singleton mql with scope-refcounted listener attach, and useRAFLoop itself consumes it. useBreakpoint mints a fresh mql + change listener per call (dist/dom.js:38-52).
defects.mechanism: consumer re-implements a publisher primitive that already exists — design-system reuse violation plus duplicate subscription
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: the two dist implementations and the call site.
defects.proposedCure: `import { useReducedMotion } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core"` and drop the useBreakpoint call. Same semantics, one shared listener, and it aligns this component with the loop it is already driving.

defects.defect: The rAF callback performs two forced layout reads per frame for values that are constant for the life of the arm.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:97-99 reads `canvas.clientWidth` / `canvas.clientHeight` every frame; both are set once in arm() at :137-143 and the component ignores resize entirely. Counter-evidence on cost: the 12-drop arm measured armFlushMs 5.7 with longTasksMs [], so the current budget is not at risk.
defects.mechanism: loop-invariant work left inside the loop; layout-read in a paint callback
defects.reproduction: NONE for a perf impact (labelled hypothesis — not traced). The invariance itself is a fact from the code path.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist `w`/`h` onto `Stage` in collectStage alongside tx/ty/tr; the frame callback then does pure paint with zero DOM reads. If resize during the 1.2 s window ever matters, re-arm on resize rather than re-reading per frame.

defects.defect: Dead public surface: the composable's `{ stop }` return has no consumer, and line 49 re-exports three timeline constants that nothing outside the composables directory imports.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:189 `return { stop: () => loop.stop() }` vs MixAnimationCanvas.vue:20 which discards the return value. `grep -rn "MIX_ARRIVE_MS\|MIX_CONVERGE_MS\|MIX_EPILOGUE_MS" demo/` returns hits only inside demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/.
defects.mechanism: speculative API surface / dual import path to the same constants
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: the two greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both. The composable returns void; consumers that ever need the constants import them from mixStage, the one home.

defects.defect: `clearCanvas()` clears in device pixels through a dpr-scaled transform (disagreeing with the frame callback's CSS-pixel clear), and it releases only `style.height` — the canvas keeps a full-pane backing store for the parked pane's lifetime.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:163-166 `ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)` while the ctx carries `setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0)` from :145; compare the correct CSS-px clear at :99. Live measured armed backing store: canvasAttr [510, 683] with style.height "683px" retained after the mix completed (phase done).
defects.mechanism: two coordinate spaces for the same operation; incomplete resource release on the idle edge
defects.reproduction: NONE for harm (the mismatch over-clears, which is safe). Backing-store retention measured live: after a completed mix, canvas.width/height remain 510/683 and only style.height is reset on idle.
defects.proposedCure: Clear in one space (CSS px, matching :99) and on idle set `canvas.width = canvas.height = 0` alongside `style.height = ""` so the parked pane holds no backing store.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — `[data-mix-target]` does not exist in the DOM under glass-ui 7, so `mixStage.ts:121-124`'s synthetic-target fallback fires on every single mix and the convergence pool lands a MEASURED 193 px from the result well (pool centroid (255,478) == the fallback {clientWidth/2, scrollHeight*0.7} to the pixel; the well is at (69,529)). This falsifies the component's one stated invariant — "the convergence LANDS AT the result plate" — unconditionally, for every user, right now, with no fault injection needed. D-1 is the more catastrophic outcome (a silent, unrecoverable strand) but needs malformed data to fire; D-2 is firing continuously and is invisible precisely because the fallback is a masking fallback that renders a broken anchor as a convincing animation.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND overall, but these specific suspicions were investigated and disproved, with positive evidence: (1) NOT a PRM-RAF-epidemic site — `useBreakpoint` genuinely accepts arbitrary media queries (glass-ui dist/composables/dom/useBreakpoint.d.ts: "@param query A CSS @media query string") and `arm()` handles PRM by COMPLETING IMMEDIATELY (useMixingAnimation.ts:120-125) rather than pausing, which is the correct discipline for a phase-machine forward edge; `respectReducedMotion: false` on the host is deliberate and correctly justified. (2) No hand-rolled rAF anywhere in the component tree — the clock is glass-ui `useRAFLoop` with immediate:false, pauseWhenHidden:true, onScopeDispose teardown (dist/useRAFLoop-B3YlWK4M.js:85) plus an explicit onBeforeUnmount stop. (3) Four of the six named local hazards do not apply: no `defineModel` (read-only props via destructure + `toRef(() => x)`), no oklch->HSV roundtrip, no `ValueUnit` wrapping, no reka-ui slider, no WebGL, and the 2D context is created lazily inside arm(), never on the boot critical path. (4) Arm cost is NOT a defect: at MAX_DROPS=12 (192 mixColors + 24 parseColorIn) the measured flush was armFlushMs 5.7 with longTasksMs []. (5) `verbatimModuleSyntax` fully compliant — every type-only import in all three files is `import type`. (6) Idiomatic Vue 3.5 — useTemplateRef, reactive props destructure, toRef getters. (7) Re-entry/double-arm paths are clean: arm() stops and resets settledFired before every branch, loop.start() zeroes elapsed/frame, done->mixing during the epilogue re-arms correctly, and max drop delay is 11 * min(60, 240/12) = 220 ms so no `MIX_ARRIVE_MS - delay` denominator can approach zero. (8) `layoutCenter`'s transform-immune offsetLeft/offsetTop frame choice is correct — proved by the pool centroid landing exactly on the computed coordinate to the pixel. (9) The canvas element's own a11y is right: aria-hidden="true" + pointer-events-none, contributing zero rows to the visual REPORT's 8 small-tap-target / 1 nameless-button counts for /#/mix. (10) `.z-controls` is a real resolved utility (--z-controls: 20, rule present in the served sheets), not a dead class.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — declared at spawn, observed and confirmed in-seat.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the convergence never finds its target and lands 194 CSS px away from the well it claims to land in. `data-mix-target` is published as a fallthrough HTML attribute on a glass-ui 7 `WatercolorDot`, which has `inheritAttrs:false` and a prop set of exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}; the attribute is dropped, `root.querySelector("[data-mix-target]")` returns null on every frame of every mix, and mixStage.ts:122-124 silently substitutes a fabricated target derived from the pane's scroll extent ({clientWidth/2, scrollHeight*0.7, 28}) — a masking fallback that let the break survive an entire producer major. Measured: fallback (255, 478.1) vs. real well (68, 528) = 194 px; composited frame at t=715ms shows the pool floating in the void above the plate.

defects.defect: The mix convergence never locates its destination: the `[data-mix-target]` contract is dead, and a fabricated scroll-extent fallback hides the break. The pool lands 194 px (38% of pane width) from the result plate's well, contradicting the component's own thesis ("The convergence LANDS AT the result plate").
defects.evidence: Live DOM during the mixing window: ghost dot attribute list = ["data-v-292b9032","data-v-0f138735","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"] — no `data-mix-target`, no `title`, no `tag`. Producer typings node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:22-49 declare props {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} only. Measured: fallback={x:255,y:478.1,r:28} (mixStage.ts:124), real well layoutCenter={x:68,y:528,r:28}, distance=194 px; root.clientWidth=510, root.scrollHeight=683. Alpha-sampling table across one mix shows `[data-mix-target]` false at t=0/43/120/301/502/702/904/1152/1403 ms. Frames: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-animationcanvas/mix-frozen-t715.png and canvas-only-t880.png.
defects.mechanism: Cross-component contract carried by a stringly-typed fallthrough DOM attribute on a producer component, consumed by querySelector on an anonymous grandparent subtree — no type, prop, emit, or test on the path; plus a masking fallback (owner edict 2) that fabricates coordinates instead of failing loudly.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix → add two operands → Mix. Observe the pool settle in the void between the Mix button and the result plate. Programmatic: during the mixing window, `document.querySelector('[data-mix-target]')` → null.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the attribute contract entirely by transposing the convergence into the canon's structural trough (OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:43), which owns its own box and needs no target lookup. If any DOM measurement survives, the destination must be a required, typed input (prop / useTemplateRef) whose absence fails loudly — never a fabricated coordinate.

defects.defect: A decorative Canvas2D renderer owns the phase machine's ONLY forward edge. When `getContext("2d")` returns null the mix strands forever: the result plate stays ghosted at opacity 0.55 showing only the word "Result", with no error, timeout, or recovery.
defects.evidence: useMixingState.ts:5-15 declares the ONE-CLOCK LAW; MixAnimationCanvas.vue:15 repeats it. useMixingAnimation.ts:145 writes `if (ctx) ctx.setTransform(...)` then proceeds to collectStage + loop.start() regardless; frame 1 hits lines 92-95 `if (!canvas || !ctx || !stage) { loop.stop(); return; }` — stop WITHOUT onSettled. Reproduced live: patching HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext to return null for the mix canvas then calling startMix gives after 1800 ms { ghostStuck: true, plateOpacity: "0.55", hasResultText: false, plateText: "Result" }.
defects.mechanism: Essential state transition owned by an inessential subsystem; four abort paths guarded by firing onSettled, the fifth (null 2D context) left unguarded.
defects.reproduction: In the page: `const o=HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext; HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext=function(...a){return this===mixCanvas?null:o.apply(this,a)}`; then startMix; wait 1.8 s; `.mix-plate--ghost` still present at opacity 0.55 with no result content.
defects.proposedCure: Invert ownership: useMixingState advances mixing→done itself (the math is synchronous, nothing to wait on); the narration becomes epiphenomenal, observing `phase` and never gating it. Delete `onSettled` as a state edge — this also removes the four escape hatches and the PRM special case.

defects.defect: The rAF narration keeps drawing after KeepAlive deactivation — 100 frames painted into a zero-width, invisible canvas — violating VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 "Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work."
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:145 quoted. useMixingAnimation.ts:187 has only `onBeforeUnmount(() => loop.stop())`; no onDeactivated. MixPane is KeepAlive-cached at demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120. glass-ui useRAFLoop binds only useDocumentVisibility for pauseWhenHidden (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useRAFLoop-B3YlWK4M.js). Instrumented CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.clearRect on the mix canvas: framesBeforeNav (0–250 ms, visible) = 30; after `location.hash='#/gradient'`, canvas.clientWidth = 0 and framesAfterDeactivation (250–1250 ms) = 100.
defects.mechanism: Lifecycle blind spot: teardown hooked to unmount only, while the host route uses KeepAlive deactivation; the producer's pause seam tracks document visibility, not component activity.
defects.reproduction: Start a mix on /#/mix, at t≈250 ms set location.hash='#/gradient', count clearRect calls on the mix canvas for the next second → 100.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to glass-ui BH: `useRAFLoop` should pause on onDeactivated and resume on onActivated by default, exactly as it pauses on document.hidden — a producer-level invariant, not a per-consumer patch (edict 4).

defects.defect: The component is designed against a superseded composition. Canon mandates a P122 golden InstrumentChassis with a structural N-operand rack/TROUGH at 61.8034%; the shipped design is a single-column Card with a full-pane `absolute inset-0` overlay canvas whose geometry derives from an anonymous `parentElement`'s clientWidth/scrollHeight.
defects.evidence: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:43 — "P122 `golden`: N-operand rack/trough 61.8033989%; result/method/provenance 38.1966011%". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:48 (outer housing = its own InstrumentChassis composition), :202 ("converges through one trough into one result"), :38 ("Card ... is never the default page primitive"). Shipped: MixPane.vue:61-62 single Card; MixAnimationCanvas.vue:32 `absolute inset-0 w-full h-full`; useMixingAnimation.ts:137-142 measures `parent.clientWidth` / `parent.scrollHeight`.
defects.mechanism: Design predates the ratified composition; correctness coupled to an untyped positional `parentElement`, so a housing change silently re-bases every measurement with no compile error — the same failure mode that killed D-1.
defects.reproduction: NONE — canon-vs-code comparison (quoted spec + file:line).
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the convergence into the trough: a real element with a real box between rack and result. This dissolves the attribute contract, the parentElement coupling, the scroll-extent arithmetic and the below-the-fold special case in one move.

defects.defect: The narration is optically negligible and blocks an instantly-available result for 900 ms. Terminal pool = 0.71% of the pane's area; the 700/900/300 ms timeline and cubic easings are hard-coded module constants outside the glass-ui spring register.
defects.evidence: mixStage.ts:22-26 (MIX_ARRIVE_MS=700, MIX_CONVERGE_MS=900, MIX_EPILOGUE_MS=300) and :16 (easeInOutCubic/easeOutCubic/smoothStep3 from @mkbabb/value.js/easing). Measured house tokens: --duration-fast .2s, --normal .3s, --slow .45s, --spring-snappy calc(.44s*1), --spring-smooth calc(.35s*1) → 1200 ms is 2.7× the slowest. Pool radius tr = max(target.r,14) = 28 → πr² ≈ 2463 px² on 510×683 = 348330 px² = 0.71%. Frame canvas-only-t880.png shows the entire payload. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:139 ("Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register"), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8, §5.5, §5.6.
defects.mechanism: Untokenized local motion register plus a decoration whose rendered mass is negligible against the stage it delays.
defects.reproduction: Measured: canvas backing store 510×683, pool disc radius 28 at t=880 ms (canvas-only-t880.png); token values read from getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).
defects.proposedCure: Either the convergence becomes proportionate inside the trough at protagonist scale, or it is subtracted (§5.6 subtraction precedes explanation). Whatever survives takes duration and curve from the glass-ui spring register, not from three integers in a stage file.

defects.defect: The narration silently under-represents the operands: two independent unconditional truncations mean a palette mix narrates a minority of its pigments while asserting "these are the things being mixed".
defects.evidence: mixStage.ts:29 `MAX_DROPS = 12` and :157 `origins.slice(0, MAX_DROPS)`; MixSourceSelector.vue:254 stamps `palette.colors.slice(0, 4)` into data-mix-colors. A 2×8-colour palette mix narrates 8 of 16; a 3×8 narrates 12 of 24. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:202 — "The rack remains legible at 2, 3 and 12 colors", palettes arm = "two or more potentially unequal palettes".
defects.mechanism: Narration derived from a locally capped projection of the operand model rather than the model the mix math consumes.
defects.reproduction: NONE executed — the palettes arm needs ≥2 saved palettes and the probe fixture had 1. Code-read finding, not a hypothesis: both slices are unconditional.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the narration from the same operand model the mix math consumes, with no local cap. If 24 pigments cannot be narrated legibly, make it a composition decision in the trough (one drop per operand, not per colour) — never a silent slice.

defects.defect: The primary path to this component is dead in the shipped build: there is no pointer and no keyboard way to add a colour to the mix, so the subject's colors arm is unreachable by any real user.
defects.evidence: Live DOM: `.add-slot-ghost` renders as { tag: "SPAN", ariaHidden: "true", ariaLabel: null, tabIndex: -1, pointerEvents: "none" }; two synthetic `.click()` calls with 120 ms settle leave `[data-mix-source]` count at 0→0 (listener not bound). Source: MixSourceSelector.vue:164-176 passes tag="button"/aria-label/@click to a glass-ui 7 WatercolorDot that has no `tag` prop and inheritAttrs:false; same at :211-221 for the "Add color … from …" palette swatches. I had to drive setupState.addColor() to exercise the subject at all.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui 7 P051 abrogated the interactive host; consumer fallthrough attributes and the tag branch went with it, silently — the same producer change that caused D-1.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix → attempt to click or Tab to the dashed add slot in the Selected well. Nothing is focusable or clickable; `[data-mix-source]` stays 0.
defects.proposedCure: Attribution: MixSourceSelector seat. Give the add slot a real named `<button type="button">` seat wrapping the noninteractive dot face (the P051 face-and-seat law), and relay the attribute-inheritance regression to the glass-ui BH inbox together with D-1's cause.

defects.defect: Geometry is sampled exactly once at arm(); resize, 200% zoom, font-size change and late reflow mid-narration are unhandled states leaving a stretched bitmap and coordinates measured against a dead layout.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:135-147 measures parent.clientWidth / parent.scrollHeight, sets canvas.style.height, canvas.width/height and the DPR transform, and never re-measures. No ResizeObserver and no window resize handler exist in the component, composable or stage module (grep of all three files).
defects.mechanism: One-shot measurement of a container the component does not own, with no observation of that container's box.
defects.reproduction: NONE executed — labelled a HYPOTHESIS; the code path is unambiguous.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of the trough transposition: a region-local canvas observes its own box via one ResizeObserver.

defects.defect: prefers-reduced-motion is sampled only at arm(); `respectReducedMotion:false` deliberately disables the host's live PRM watch, so PRM engaged during a narration is not honoured.
defects.evidence: useMixingAnimation.ts:113 `{ immediate:false, pauseWhenHidden:true, respectReducedMotion:false }`; the consumer branch reads prefersReducedMotion.value only inside arm() at line 120. The docstring at :33-36 justifies it: a paused loop would strand the phase machine — which is itself an artifact of D-2.
defects.mechanism: PRM treated as a one-shot arming predicate instead of a live constraint, because the loop cannot be allowed to pause while it owns a state edge.
defects.reproduction: NONE executed — HYPOTHESIS; code path is explicit.
defects.proposedCure: Once the phase machine owns its own forward edge (D-2 cure), restore respectReducedMotion:true and let the loop stop natively under PRM.

defects.defect: A transient decorative narration inherits the forced-colors exemption written for colour-DISPLAY surfaces, so in WHCM it paints arbitrary pigment across a surface the user asked to be rendered in the system palette.
defects.evidence: demo/styles/foundation.css:680 grants `forced-color-adjust: none` to the bare `canvas` selector; the governing rationale at lines 653-656 is explicitly about "the surfaces whose whole PURPOSE is to show a color — the actual content of a color tool", with chrome staying at UA `auto` (tier 2).
defects.mechanism: Leaf-level blanket selector in the tier-1 colour-surface roster catches a decoration that belongs on the chrome tier.
defects.reproduction: NONE executed — no /#/mix capture exists in the forced-colors matrix (see D-13). HYPOTHESIS grounded in the quoted rule and selector.
defects.proposedCure: Give the mix canvas a named class and place it on tier 2 (UA `auto`) in the roster, or suppress the narration entirely under forced-colors.

defects.defect: Contrivance: a 36-line wrapper component whose declared props are not its real inputs. Its actual dependencies are four data-attributes on subtrees it does not own plus the identity of its own parentElement — none visible at the component boundary.
defects.evidence: MixAnimationCanvas.vue:8-25 — four props (phase/result/space/hueMethod), one useTemplateRef, four toRef forwards, nothing else. Real inputs: mixStage.ts:121,129 query `[data-mix-target]`, `[data-mix-source]`, `.dataset.mixColor`, `.dataset.mixColors`; useMixingAnimation.ts:129,137 depend on canvas.parentElement.
defects.mechanism: A component boundary that hides coupling instead of encapsulating it (owner edict 3, KISS/no contrivance).
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural code read.
defects.proposedCure: After the trough transposition the canvas has no cross-subtree inputs; fold the 36-line shell into the trough region component, or keep it only if it then owns a real, typed contract.

defects.defect: Per-frame CanvasGradient allocation: up to ~38 gradient objects per frame at MAX_DROPS, roughly 5000 short-lived gradients per mix.
defects.evidence: mixStage.ts:199 `ctx.createRadialGradient(...)` inside drawDisc, called 3× per in-flight drop (2 trail + head, lines 227-240) plus 2 for the pool (lines 258-259). Measured 146 draw frames for one 1.4 s run via instrumented clearRect.
defects.mechanism: Gradient objects minted per draw call rather than cached per drop pigment ramp stop.
defects.reproduction: NONE — measured frame count (146) plus static call-site arithmetic; no profiling run at 12 operands.
defects.proposedCure: Cache one gradient per (colour, radius bucket) or draw the pigment as a pre-rendered offscreen sprite scaled per frame — after deciding (D-5) whether the narration survives at all.

defects.defect: Audit evidence gap: the state matrices never captured this route, so every claim about the component's reduced-motion, forced-colors, 200%-zoom and RTL behaviour in the mega-tranche record is unwitnessed.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/{reduced-motion-desktop,forced-colors-desktop,zoom-200-desktop,rtl-desktop,rtl-mobile}/ each contain only {adminusers,blob,browse,gradient,picker}.png — no mix.png. /#/mix appears only in the four Safari light/dark × desktop/mobile matrices (REPORT.md:123,138,153,168), all at rest with an idle canvas.

defects.defect: The published library declares the demo's design system and animation engine as runtime `dependencies`, closing a producer↔consumer package cycle. `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` dependencies = {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}; neither is referenced by src/ or dist/ (the only directory `files` ships). glass-ui@7.0.0 in turn declares `@mkbabb/value.js: ^4.0.0` as a peerDependency.
defects.evidence: package.json (repo root): dependencies = {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}; files = ["dist","!dist/gh-pages","!dist/gh-pages/**"]. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui\|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/` → NO OUTPUT. `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" dist/` → NO OUTPUT. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes "@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0". `du -sh` → glass-ui 5.2M, keyframes.js 608K, dist/ 1.7M. tsconfig.demo.json:27-28 states the broken invariant verbatim: "This is the ONLY value.js program that may see glass-ui; the library program (tsconfig.lib.json) never does (inv-K-1 — structurally glass-ui-free)."
defects.mechanism: A monorepo-shaped tree published as a single package: demo-only dependencies were added to the only package.json in the repo, which happens to be the library's public contract. The library/demo boundary exists in the type programs (tsconfig.lib.json vs tsconfig.demo.json) and in prose, but never in the manifest — the one artifact consumers receive. Same fusion r4 R4-3 found in the test suite (10 of 19 library vitest files import from demo/); two artifacts, one boundary never drawn.
defects.reproduction: `node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); console.log(p.dependencies)"` then `grep -rn '@mkbabb/glass-ui' src/` and `grep -rl '@mkbabb/glass-ui' dist/` (both empty). End-to-end: `npm pack && npm i ./mkbabb-value.js-4.0.0.tgz` in an empty project installs node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui; `grep -r glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist` → nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Move both entries to devDependencies. @mkbabb/value.js must declare ZERO runtime dependencies — dist/ already has none, so this is a manifest edit with no code consequence, and the cycle dissolves with it. Then make the invariant enforceable rather than aspirational: a CI assertion that `Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}).length === 0` — the manifest-level twin of the inv-K-1 rule tsconfig.lib.json already enforces at the type level. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox: the cycle is visible from their side and they should know value.js is about to stop being their dependent.

defects.defect: The library owns a complete runtime space registry and publishes none of it, so the dogfood consumer re-types it by hand — four times, all currently exact. `SPACE_SCHEMA` (channels, hueIndex, css flag per space) and `SPACE_IDS` live at src/color/model.ts:56,76, already `as const satisfies Record<SpaceId, SpaceSchema>`, and are re-exported by neither src/color/index.ts nor src/subpaths/color.ts.
defects.evidence: src/color/model.ts:56 `export const SPACE_SCHEMA = {...} as const satisfies Record<SpaceId, SpaceSchema>`; :76 `export const SPACE_IDS = Object.freeze(...)`. `grep -c "SPACE_IDS" dist/subpaths/color.d.ts dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` → 0 and 0. Measured duplication (scratchpad/dup.mjs parsing both files): "SPACE_SCHEMA spaces: 17 / PICKER_CHANNELS spaces: 17 / channel-key-list IDENTICAL for 17 of 17 / differences: []"; "SPACE_SCHEMA css:true = 13 [...] / CSS_PICKER_SPACES = 13 [...] / IDENTICAL SET: true"; "SPACE_SCHEMA hueIndex: hsl:0 hsv:0 hwb:0 lch:2 oklch:2" vs the `hue?: true` marker at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:49. Fourth copy — the one this component iterates at MixConfigBar.vue:129 — is demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:38 HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS, a hand-written value mirror of the PUBLISHED type at src/color/model.ts:46.
defects.mechanism: A type-only public surface over a value-carrying internal registry. Consumers can NAME the domain but cannot WALK it, so they rebuild it. This is the root cause beneath two prior findings that recorded only symptoms: r2 L2-4 (PickerSpace = SpaceId has 17 members, the dropdown renders 9, so the prop admits 8 unrenderable states — the demo cannot state the curation as a subset because SPACE_IDS is unpublished) and r2 L2-5 (HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS non-exhaustive over a library-owned union — the library publishes the type and withholds the tuple).
defects.reproduction: `grep -c SPACE_IDS dist/subpaths/color.d.ts` → 0. `node <scratchpad>/dup.mjs` → the 17/17 and 13/13 identity output pasted above. Drift demonstration: adding a space to SPACE_SCHEMA produces no diagnostic anywhere in demo/.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the registry, then derive. Add to src/color/index.ts + src/subpaths/color.ts: `export { SPACE_IDS, SPACE_SCHEMA } from "./model";` and `export const HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS = ["shorter","longer","increasing","decreasing"] as const satisfies readonly HueInterpolationMethod[];`. Then picker-color.ts derives PICKER_CHANNELS keys and CSS_PICKER_SPACES from SPACE_SCHEMA, keeping only the genuinely demo-owned min/max/unit ranges (a picker fact, correctly homed); and color-space-meta.ts becomes a label overlay keyed by the library's ids — Record<HueInterpolationMethod, Meta> for the arcs (exhaustive by construction, closes L2-5) and an explicitly-typed Record<Exclude<SpaceId, "kelvin"|"ictcp"|...>, Meta> for the spaces (states the curation instead of hiding it, closes L2-4). Both prior findings collapse into one export. Same subpath and same wave as r4 R4-1's mixSequence/sampleColorRamp pair: R4-1 adds the missing operations, R5-2 publishes the missing registry.

defects.defect: Per-instance costume over the design system's root registers: of the four override classes on the CTA and the three SelectTriggers, two are measured no-ops duplicating tokens the root already set, one re-implements an existing prop in raw Tailwind, and only one is a genuine (and unhomed) override.
defects.evidence: Live measurement at http://localhost:9000/#/mix via clone-and-strip page.evaluate. Tokens from :root — `--control-h-xs 1.75rem | --control-h-sm 2.25rem | --control-h-md 2.5rem | --control-h-lg 2.75rem`. Results: `mixH_asShipped: 40, mixH_noH10_noFontMedium: 40` (h-10 at MixConfigBar.vue:165 changes NOTHING — Button defaults to size="md" = --control-h-md = 40px); `mixWeight_asShipped: 500, mixWeight_noOverride: 500` (font-medium changes NOTHING — glass-ui components/button/styles.css sets `.button { font-weight: 500 }`); `trigH_asShipped: 36, trigH_noH9: 39` — h-9 at :100/:123/:147 forces exactly --control-h-sm = 2.25rem = 36px while glass-ui's SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts declares `size?: "sm" | "default"` with the doc comment "Trigger height register." and the live DOM shows data-size = null (the prop is never passed); `mixFont_asShipped: Fraunces, mixFont_noFontDisplay: "Plus Jakarta Sans"` (font-display is the one live override, and ButtonProps has no typographic-voice axis). GradientVisualizer.vue:182 carries the identical h-9.
defects.mechanism: Utility-first styling applied OVER a token-driven component system with no gate that can see redundancy. Tailwind classes always 'work', which is exactly why they mask a root register that already said the same thing. A class producing the RIGHT number by the WRONG mechanism is worse than a wrong number: nothing will ever flag it. This is the class-side twin of r2 L2-1 (the dead `variant` prop) — the same five lines of markup fight the design system on both the prop axis and the class axis, invisibly, for the same reason: nothing at the boundary compares what the consumer asked for against what the producer offers.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/mix, then in the console clone the CTA and a SelectTrigger, strip h-10/font-medium/h-9 from the clones, attach off-screen, and compare getBoundingClientRect().height and getComputedStyle().fontWeight against the originals. Token values from getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--control-h-sm'/'--control-h-md').
defects.proposedCure: Pass `size="sm"` on the three SelectTriggers (and GradientVisualizer.vue:182); delete h-9, h-10 and font-medium — three classes that say nothing the root did not. For font-display: if the house wants primary verbs in the display voice, that is a producer concern — a `voice` axis on glass-ui's Button, or a documented `--button-font-family` seam — relayed to glass-ui BH, not four Tailwind classes on one instance. The cure lands on the same five lines as r2 L2-1's `emphasis="primary"`, so one edit closes both. Add the boundary lint that would have caught it: no Tailwind class on a glass primitive that a token already sets.

defects.defect: The Mix verb has two homes with divergent affordances: MixConfigBar.vue:162-170 (a Button, Blend icon, `:disabled="!canMix"`) and demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:221 (a pane-action registry entry, same Blend icon, same "Mix" label, NO disabled concept). The dock copy is permanently enabled and silently no-ops.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:221 — `{ key: "mix", icon: Blend, title: "Mix", description: "Mix the selected colors.", handler: () => paneRefs.mix.value?.startMix?.() }`. MixConfigBar.vue:162-170 — `<Button variant=... :disabled="!canMix" ...><Blend/>Mix</Button>`. Live DOM on the pane button with 0 operands: hasDisabledAttr true, domDisabled true, matchesDisabled true, opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed. The dock action has no equivalent — its only guard is demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:82 `if (!canMix.value) return;`. Structural consequences: MixPane.vue:57 `defineExpose({ clearSelection, startMix, copyResult })` exists solely to give the shell a handle; MixConfigBar must accept a `canMix` prop and emit `mix` — two of its members have nothing to do with configuration. `usePaneRouter` appears ZERO times across audit rounds 1–4.
defects.mechanism: A component named for one responsibility (configuration) acquired a second (the page's primary action); the shell then needed a second route to it, and the enabled predicate travelled to only one of the two declarations. The shell reaches pane internals through `paneRefs.mix.value?.startMix?.()` — two optional chains that cannot fail loudly, so renaming startMix turns the dock action into a silent no-op with a green build. Same silent-fallthrough failure mode as r2 L2-1's dead prop, one layer out on the imperative surface.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix with no operands selected. The pane's Mix button renders disabled (measured above). Open the dock Tools menu: the "Mix" action is enabled and clicking it does nothing (guarded only inside useMixingState.ts:82).
defects.proposedCure: One home for the verb and one declaration of its predicate. Preferred: the config bar becomes configuration only and the Mix button moves to MixPane beside the result plate — then `canMix`, the `mix` emit and `defineExpose({ startMix })` all collapse into pane-local state (MixConfigBar 173 → ~55 lines). Alternative: the pane-action registry becomes the single declaration, gains a `disabled?: ComputedRef<boolean>` field, and the pane renders its primary action FROM the registry. Either way the registry entry must carry the predicate, and `paneRefs.mix.value?.startMix?.()` must become a typed pane contract rather than two optional chains — r3 L3-1's lint theme applied to the imperative surface. The shell should route, not hold verbs.

It is the only place in the entire application that explains what each of the nine interpolation spaces means. Worse, the ground is not a constant: the menu is `data-surface="glass"` (translucent) floating over a live aurora field, so no value of `--muted-foreground` makes an 11px string safe there — the register is the defect. The damning contrast: the repo's O-14 apparatus walks the *aria-hidden decorative chip*'s painted stops against real WCAG floors (`o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:230-231`, RAMP_MENU_FLOOR = 4.5), i.e. the ornament is certified per-site against the composited surface while the sentence beside it — the actual information — is walked by nothing.

(d) The sampler is total against hostile input: `""` → null, `"oklch()"` (the repo's live parseCssColor crash class) → null, `[]`/1-operand → null; stop counts correct at every arity (2→17, 3→17, 4→19, 17→17). defects.defect: The option descriptions this component authors fail WCAG 1.4.3 at 3.65:1, and they are the only explanation of the nine interpolation spaces. defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:112 and :134 — `{{ s.description }}`. Measured live with the menu open at 1280×720, compositing the ancestor background stack over the page ambient (the O-18 census model the repo's own oracles use): {"descText":"Perceptual, hue-preserving","fontSize":"11px","fontWeight":"400","color":"rgb(195, 185, 172)","ground":"rgb(99 86 71)","contrast":3.65,"wcagAA_normalText_4_5":false,"wcagAA_largeText_3":true}. 11px/400 gets no large-text carve-out (needs ≥18.66px bold or ≥24px). defects.defect: The component's only live gate is RED at HEAD, and beneath that failure sits a second independent RED nobody can reach: the O-14 byte-identity oracle's parser cannot match the serialization the sampler actually stamps — and for achromatic operands it passes having compared zero stops.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "T-17"` → "2 failed, 1 passed (1.5m)", both failures `locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded · waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' })` at :355 and :414. The second RED, measured in-browser: the stamp is `oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)`; the spec's parseOklchTriples regex (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:157) dies on the `%` after L and matches 0; the computed background-image canonicalizes to `oklch(0.627955 0.257683 29.2339)` and matches n — so `expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)` compares 17 against 0. For achromatic operands the sampler emits `oklch(59.987080562215% 0 none)`; both sides match 0 and the assertion passes having compared nothing.
defects.mechanism: two serializations of one value with no shared writer — the sampler emits specified CSS syntax (L%, Hdeg), the oracle parses computed CSS syntax (unitless) — layered under an operand path that no longer exists in the DOM
defects.reproduction: Run the command above (pasted output). For the regex arithmetic: in the live page, set a probe element's backgroundImage to the exact stops sample.ts emits, then apply the spec's regex to both the joined stamp and getComputedStyle(el).backgroundImage.
defects.proposedCure: Make serializeStop emit the COMPUTED form the browser canonicalizes to — unitless `oklch(<0..1> <C> <H>)`, alpha as a unit number, `0` rather than `none` for a missing hue — so specified ≡ computed by construction and the oracle needs no parser at all: compare the strings. Named green-keeping mutations to close first: (a) replace the whole gradient with `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.5 0 none), oklch(0.5 0 none))` — a flat grey chip lying about every space and arc survives the byte-identity leg for achromatic operands; (b) delete MixConfigBar.vue lines 57-74 and 104-137 entirely — the ramps, chips and whole #description slot — and the one currently-passing leg ("honest absence") stays green.

defects.defect: The mix pane's sole colours-mode operand affordance is inert — it renders as an aria-hidden `<span>` with an inline `pointer-events: none`, because glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot has no `tag`, `as`, or `disabled` prop and the consumer's aria-label is dropped. Operands can never reach length ≥ 2, so this component's headline T-17 chips have never rendered for a real user.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:164-174 passes `tag="button"`, `aria-label="Add current color to the mix"`, `:disabled`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts prop surface is color / variant / animate / cycleDuration / range / seed only. Live DOM: {"addSlot":{"tag":"SPAN","aria":null,"rect":{"w":44,"h":44}},"role":null,"tabindex":null,"tagAttr":null}; outerHTML head `<span … aria-hidden="true" class="add-slot-ghost …"`; inline style `…; pointer-events: none; --watercolor-color: …`. Playwright hit-test: "<div class=\"swatch-row …\"> intercepts pointer events".
defects.mechanism: a decorative-by-construction primitive (aria-hidden + pointer-events:none are its own inline output) being consumed as an interactive one, with no `strictTemplates` to reject the non-existent props

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue

result.strongestDefect: L-20 — `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` declares `@mkbabb/glass-ui@^7.0.0` and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js@^6.0.0` as runtime `dependencies`, while `src/` imports neither and the published `dist/` contains ZERO `@mkbabb/*` specifiers (both greps exit 1). glass-ui peer-depends on value.js `^4.0.0`, so the declared package graph is a cycle. eslint.config.js:211-214 enforces exactly this invariant ("inv-K-1: the topology is glass-ui → value.js(lib), one direction, no cycle") at the IMPORT level, where it holds — and nothing enforces it at the MANIFEST level, where it is violated. Every consumer of a package described as "CSS color, value, easing, transform, math and quantization capabilities" is forced to install 5.8 MB of Vue design system + animation runtime (5.2M + 608K measured), plus glass-ui's own reka-ui/embla/vueuse/tailwind/vue peer chain. This is the root cause of the prior revision's L-9 ("a package does not install itself" — it does, transitively): glass-ui was declared where the DEMO would resolve it, in the LIBRARY's dependencies, and the real consumer inherits the demo's needs. Shipped and immutable in 4.0.0.

defects.defect: The published library declares runtime dependencies on the design system that peer-depends on it, for code `src/` never imports — inverting the dependency direction and closing a declared package-graph cycle.
defects.evidence: package.json dependencies = {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui\|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/` → exit 1 (ZERO matches). `grep -rn "@mkbabb/" dist/` → exit 1 (ZERO matches in the published artifact; package.json#files ships dist/ alone). node -p on glass-ui's manifest → peerDependencies.@mkbabb/value.js = ^4.0.0. `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M + 608K. eslint.config.js:211-214 names the violated invariant verbatim: "inv-K-1: the value.js LIBRARY (src/) must never import glass-ui — the topology is glass-ui → value.js(lib), one direction, no cycle."
defects.mechanism: F7 — the invariant enforced at the wrong altitude. inv-K-1 is policed on import statements, where it holds, and unpoliced on the manifest, where it is violated. The manifest is the level a consumer's package manager reads. Root cause: glass-ui was declared where the DEMO resolves it (the library's own dependencies) rather than where it is used (devDependencies), so the real consumer inherits the demo's needs — the same mechanism the prior revision's L-9 observed downstream in vite.config.ts.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui\|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ ; echo $?  # 1 && grep -rn "@mkbabb/" dist/ ; echo $?  # 1 && node -p "JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').dependencies)" && node -p "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').peerDependencies['@mkbabb/value.js']" && du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js   # verified at HEAD 06377848
defects.proposedCure: Move both entries from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` — one edit to package.json, no consumer breaks because nothing resolves them at runtime (proven by the dist/ grep). Then give inv-K-1 its missing manifest half as a publish gate: assert Object.keys(dependencies) is a subset of the bare specifiers appearing in dist/ — today that set is empty, so the correct assertion is `dependencies === undefined`. Born RED today by construction. NOT pin-blocked, NOT src/. Epoch note: 4.0.0 is published and immutable, so the cure must gate the NEXT publish; the shipped 4.0.0 manifest stays wrong forever.

When one concept has two implementations, a fix applied by SEARCH reaches the copy that carried the finding and not the copy cloned from it; and when the gate's probe hook is hand-placed (data-o18) rather than producer-owned, the gate inherits the same blindness and can only measure the set already cured. defects.defect: The quantize domain has four homes and three of them disagree; the published .d.ts declares none of it, so a consumer authoring a control must guess the bounds.
defects.evidence: src/quantize.ts:39-49 enforces k integer 1..64 (default 8), chromaWeight finite >=0 (default 1). dist/subpaths/quantize.d.ts:42-48 publishes only `k?: number; maxIterations?: number; targetPixels?: number; chromaWeight?: number; dedupeThreshold?: number` — five bare numbers, zero domain. ExtractControls.vue:28-30 caps k at 16; :71-73 caps chromaWeight at 1.5 (a bound the library does not have at all). GenerateControls.vue:301-303 caps the same product question at 12. useExtractSession.ts:44-45 and :181-182 default 5 / 0.5. src/quantize.ts:137 `dominantColor` hardcodes { k: 5 }. `grep -rn "MAX_K|K_MAX|MAX_COLORS|CHROMA_WEIGHT" demo src` → one unrelated local at MixSourceSelector.vue:38; no shared name for the concept exists.
defects.mechanism: F3 — one concept, N homes — crossing the PACKAGE boundary rather than staying inside demo. The owner (src/quantize.ts) has the knowledge and declines to publish it, so the domain exists only as an unpublished runtime guard behind a .d.ts trust boundary that tsconfig.demo.json was explicitly written to establish. Every consumer must re-invent the domain, and the demo's guesses (16, 1.5, 5, 0.5) are now frozen into the affordance that defines what the feature can express.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && sed -n '39,49p;135,139p' src/quantize.ts && grep -n "QuantizeOptions" -A 10 dist/subpaths/quantize.d.ts && grep -rn "MAX_K\|K_MAX\|MAX_COLORS\|CHROMA_WEIGHT" demo src   # verified at HEAD 06377848
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a shared literal: export the domain as data from @mkbabb/value.js/quantize — `export const QUANTIZE_DOMAIN = { k: {min:1,max:64,step:1,default:8}, chromaWeight: {min:0,max:4,step:0.1,default:1}, ... } as const` — and have the single validation block at :44-49 READ its bounds from it instead of restating them. One home, checked by the compiler. ExtractControls' :min/:max/:step then become QUANTIZE_DOMAIN.k.min etc., making a slider that cannot express a value the library accepts (or can express one it rejects) impossible to author. dominantColor's hardcoded {k:5} takes the default or documents why 5. The src/ half is NOT pin-blocked and lands now; the consumer half (removing the four literals) waits for Glass 8. Born-RED gate: zero numeric literals in the subject's slider bounds — today four.

defects.defect: INK_AMBIENT_KEY has two incompatible injection contracts; the subject's path takes the non-null-asserted one, and the key's sole provider is app-root boot — an undeclared feature-leaf → shell/boot edge invisible in the component's prop contract.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:347 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!;` (no default) vs ConsoleRail.vue:128 and HeroBlob.vue:95 `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null)` (explicit default). Sole provider: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:92 `provide(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, derivedLightness)`, called once at demo/color-picker/App.vue:285. The subject reaches it via :118 `useSafeAccentFn("resting")`. Its defineProps at :103-111 declares only `cssColor?: string | undefined` — the stated contract is "give me a colour string"; the true contract is "and mount me beneath color-picker/App.vue". Consequence measured: `grep -rln "ExtractControls|useSafeAccentFn" demo/test test` → no output; zero tests mount this 151-line, 6-prop, 3-emit leaf.
defects.mechanism: An implicit cross-layer edge carried by an injection key rather than an import, so it is invisible to import-graph tracing (the shared kernel is import-clean: `grep -rn 'color-picker' demo/color-session/` yields only prose in comments, zero import statements). Two contracts for one key means neither is THE contract — `inject(K, null)` says absent is legitimate, `inject(K)!` says absent is impossible and silences the compiler's disagreement with a bang. This is precisely the edge G-DEMO-1 names, and L-21 proves nothing enforces it.
defects.reproduction: COUPLING — MEASURED: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && grep -rn "INK_AMBIENT_KEY" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' && grep -rn "useAtmosphereBoot" demo | grep -v boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts && grep -rln "ExtractControls\|useSafeAccentFn" demo/test test. CRASH — NONE; LABELLED HYPOTHESIS. The mechanism is certain from the code (ambient is undefined without a provider; safeCss at :353-359 dereferences ambient.value) but the throw requires provider-absent AND cssColor-truthy, and ExtractWorkbench.vue:69 passes `cssColorOpaque ?? ''` (falsy), which short-circuits trackInk at :123-125. No shipped route produces the combination. I did not execute it.
defects.proposedCure: Give the key ONE contract: useSafeAccentFn takes `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null)` and degrades to the certified de-emphasis token when absent — the exact degenerate path trackInk already implements for a missing cssColor, so the component's two 'no live pick' states unify instead of one being graceful and the other fatal. Then encode the edge as the lint rule L-21's cure adds. Not pin-blocked: the edit is in demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts and the subject's own lines do not change.
