result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm). Seat spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; observed, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the k axis paints its gradient on a hand-rolled `<div>` positioned at a rectangle PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the producer track it then blanks with `--slider-track-bg: transparent` (measured delta {x:0,y:0,w:0,h:0}), while the producer variable provably accepts and correctly renders a `linear-gradient()` — and the SAME FILE's kC slider 40 lines later already uses that correct path. Two mechanisms for one job in one component; the second proves the first unnecessary. This is the posture every other finding descends from.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable — verdict is DEFECTIVE. For completeness, the negatives I did establish (attacked and could not break, stated so the verdict is not mistaken for a sweep): `variant="spectrum"` is a legal SliderVariant; the three DockControl tap targets are 44x44 coarse / 40x40 fine, both clearing the 24px floor (the route's small-target rows belonging to this component are the two 12px THUMBS, not the buttons); horizontal overflow is 0 on all seven arms driven including 320 and RTL; zoom-200 (720@4x) holds with overflowX 0 and no reflow defect; zero console/page errors on /#/extract across all four shipped matrices (REPORT.json); `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied (no type-only import mis-declared); Vue 3.5 idiom correct (reactive props destructure at line 103, no stale defineModel round-trip); not a god module (151 lines, one job); `prefers-reduced-motion` not independently violated (nothing spatial animates, no layout-forcing property animated). I also explicitly DOWNGRADED pass-1's D-1 BLOCKER ("both tracks disappear under forced-colors") to an open verification: WebKit's forced-colors emulation is unfaithful and measured the OPPOSITE result (author colour survived into the computed value), so severity is unproven until a real Windows High Contrast host is run.

defects.defect: The k axis hand-rolls a decoy track: an absolutely-positioned `<div>` painted at coordinates identical to the producer `.slider-track`, which is then blanked via `--slider-track-bg: transparent`. The producer variable accepts a gradient natively, and the same file's kC slider already uses it correctly.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:19-34 (decoy div + transparent override) vs :75 (kC uses --slider-track-bg correctly). Measured live 1440/light: decoyDiv {x:252,y:494.65625,w:434,h:24}; realTrack {x:252,y:494.65625,w:434,h:24}; deltaPx {x:0,y:0,w:0,h:0}. KILL-SHOT: setting --slider-track-bg to a linear-gradient yields computed backgroundImage 'linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255,0,0) 0%, rgb(0,255,0) 50%, rgb(0,0,255) 100%)', acceptsGradient:true. Producer rule in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css: `.slider-track { background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--muted-medium)) }` — `background` shorthand accepts any <image>. Rendered proof: evidence/pass-4/d4-PROOF-gradient-renders-through-slider-track-bg.png
defects.mechanism: Consumer decorates AROUND the design-system primitive instead of composing OVER it — it declines the producer's exposed lever and rebuilds the same geometry beside it. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 names Extract as an adopter of the one axis composition and forbids exactly this: 'feature waves own their domain arrangement, not new slider mechanics.'
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-4/d4-killshot.mjs (dev server live at localhost:9000). Output at evidence/pass-4/d4-killshot.txt.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural, not a patch: delete the div and the transparent override; pass `:style="{ '--slider-track-bg': gradient || trackInk }"` on the k Slider, exactly as kC already does. Net -16 lines, -1 stacking context, -1 absolutely-positioned node, one mechanism instead of two. Also removes one of the three timing registers in the row (the div computes `transition: all` with no duration, so the gradient SNAPS while the sibling kC track fades on --duration-fast).

defects.defect: Dark mode annihilates the live pick's chroma. The 'certified ink' contract is satisfied numerically and voided perceptually: the crimson accent becomes a near-white bar that is the brightest object on the dark page, brighter than the H1, and reads as a loading skeleton while the actual skeletons beneath it are darker.
defects.evidence: Same trackInk, same pick, two schemes, measured computed background-color: 1440 light = oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023) [L .545, C .218]; 390 dark = oklch(0.958322 0.021053 9.834023) [L .958, C .021]. Hue preserved to 6 decimals; chroma falls 90.3%. Visible in the project's own shipped captures: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/extract.png and .../safari-mobile-dark/extract.png. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 — 'No path desaturates through gray.'
defects.mechanism: useSafeAccentFn('resting') -> certifyAccentInk(..., GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR) walks LIGHTNESS ONLY to meet a WCAG 1.4.11 ratio. It has a floor on ratio, no floor on chroma, no ceiling on lightness. Against a dark plate the only L-only path to contrast is toward white, and white in OKLCH costs all available chroma. The whole point of threading the live pick — that the control wears the user's colour — is defeated in exactly one of the two schemes.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — compare kRailStyle.backgroundColor between the DESKTOP-1440-light and MOBILE-390-dark blocks. Output at evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.txt.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side in demo/color-session/ink.ts (wave W·EC-β1): certify in OKLCH with a chroma floor AND an L ceiling; when the ratio cannot be met by L alone, move the RELATIONSHIP rather than the colour — ink the hairline ring at full chroma and drop the fill to a tinted low-alpha wash. Identity survives, the ring carries the ratio, and light/dark become transpositions of ONE design rather than two unrelated ones.

defects.defect: On every coarse-pointer arm both slider thumbs overhang their own rails by 10px top and bottom, rendering as black-outlined lozenges protruding from the track. It reads as a rendering fault.
defects.evidence: Measured 390/dark: k track {y:459.28,h:24} spans 459.28->483.28; k thumb {y:449.28,h:44} spans 449.28->493.28. kC track {y:505.28,h:24}; kC thumb {y:495.28,h:44}. Reproduced at 320 (thumb {y:367.8,h:44} vs rail {y:377.8,h:24}). Desktop is flush (h:24 vs h:24) — coarse-pointer only, which is why desktop review never caught it. Plainly visible in the shipped capture .../shots/safari-mobile-dark/extract.png.
defects.mechanism: The spectrum variant thumb is `height:100%` of a track computed as calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5)=24px at the default size='md'. A coarse-pointer rule then grows the thumb to the 44px touch minimum WITHOUT growing the track. The consumer never set `size` or `--slider-thumb-size`, inheriting a pairing the producer only guarantees on fine pointers.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — MOBILE-390-dark block, compare sliders[].thumbRect vs sliders[].trackRect. Also evidence/pass-4/d4-states.txt narrow-320 block.
defects.proposedCure: Consumer: `size="lg"` on both Sliders -> --slider-thumb-size 1.5rem -> track 36px, thumb 18px, so the 44px touch grow no longer overhangs; this simultaneously lifts the thumb above the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 target floor. Producer (W·EC-β2): the coarse-pointer thumb grow must raise the TRACK with the thumb, preserving the spectrum height:100% contract.

defects.defect: The kC axis is unoperable at the canon's own narrow arms. At 320 the thumb is wider than four of the fifteen positions it must distinguish and occupies 27% of the whole track; a fingertip covers eleven of fifteen steps.
defects.evidence: kC domain 0->1.5 step 0.1 = 15 intervals. Measured track widths: 1440 = 230.45px (15.4 px/step); 390 = 80.45px (5.36 px/step, thumb 2.2 steps wide); 320 = 44.0px (2.93 px/step, thumb 4.1 steps wide, thumb = 27% of track). Thumb is 12px on every arm. Screenshot: evidence/pass-4/d4-narrow-320-kc-collapse.png shows a 44px crimson stub with the thumb near-centred and overhanging, jammed against the reset icon.
defects.mechanism: Compositional, not dimensional: the controls row packs three 44px buttons + two separators worth 26px of zero ink (D-5) + a label + a readout + the axis onto ONE flex line and lets `flex-1` hand the axis whatever remains. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.6 requires mobile to be 'one document-scrolling stage->inspector->action sequence' — a compressed desktop row is not that.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-states-rtl-zoom-320-focus.mjs — narrow-320 block reports kcTrack {w:44}. Output evidence/pass-4/d4-states.txt.
defects.proposedCure: At the narrow arm kC takes its own row, exactly as k already does one line above — the pattern is already proven in this same component. Deleting the two forbidden separators (D-5) alone returns 26px, taking the 320 track from 44px to ~70px (+59%).

defects.defect: Two <DockSeparator /> elements: forbidden outright by the binding composition inventory, AND they render zero pixels — invisible to sighted users while still announced to assistive technology as role=separator, and costing 26px of the very row whose axis is starved.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:57 and :81. Canon OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binding inventory, Extract row: 'Retained non-P122 dividing line: none'; and below the table 'Any additional line ... is a defect.' PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 already carries terminal disposition REMOVE. Measured on all three arms: {cls:'dock-separator', role:'separator', ariaOrientation:'vertical', rect:{w:1,h:0}, display:'block', opacity:'1'} — height 0. Confirmed by eye in all four shipped captures: the gaps contain nothing. Cost: 2 x (1px + 12px margin) = 26px.
defects.mechanism: Contract says 0 retained lines; component renders 2. They are also non-functional because DockSeparator declares `height: var(--dock-separator-height)` explicitly and that property is supplied only by the Dock chassis (see D-6) — so off-dock the height resolves to auto = 0.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — rowSeparators array in every arm shows rect {w:1,h:0}.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both. The inventory's own grouping-job column names the replacement — 'interval' — and the row already carries `gap-2`. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.4: 'Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative.' (Corrects pass-1, which blamed a missing align-self:stretch; an explicit height declaration defeats stretch — pass-2 was right and I confirm it.)

defects.defect: Dock-context primitives (DockControl, DockSeparator) are worn on a Card plate. Off-dock every dock-scoped custom property falls to its fallback, and --dock-separator-height has no fallback at all — which is the precise mechanism of D-5.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:98 imports both from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock'; all five instances sit inside a Card, not a GlassDock. Producer docs (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockSeparator.vue.d.ts): 'reads the dock orientation/layout via useOptionalDockContext()'. DockControl.vue.d.ts: 'the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (>=44px on coarse via the density clamp)', paint inset 'via the dock-scoped --dock-control-safe-inset fold'.
defects.mechanism: Design-system boundary crossed INWARD — generic jobs (an icon action, a group divider) solved by borrowing a different component family's primitives rather than the plate's own control grammar. This is the mirror of D-1: there the component ignored a producer lever it should have used; here it borrowed a producer contract it was never inside. Same root failure to sit where the design system expects the consumer to sit.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural reading of the producer type declarations plus the D-5 measurement that instantiates it (rect h:0 because --dock-separator-height is unset off-dock).
defects.proposedCure: Icon actions on a workbench plate use the plate's control grammar, not the dock's. If no such primitive exists it belongs in glass-ui (owner edict 4), not re-solved locally and not borrowed from the dock. Producer-side W·EC-β4: --dock-separator-height gains a fallback, OR DockSeparator is documented dock-band-only and DockControl gains an off-dock seating contract.

defects.defect: The `disabled` prop reaches 1 of 5 interactive controls. While a quantization is running and while the camera viewfinder is open, both sliders and both of Upload/Camera remain fully interactive.
defects.evidence: grep -n disabled demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue -> exactly 3 lines: :84 (the ONLY use, on Reset), :103 (destructure), :109 (type). Consumer passes a meaningful value — ExtractWorkbench.vue:70 `:disabled="session.isProcessing.value || cameraActive"`. Measured live: 'disabledAttr': null on both .glass-slider nodes; 'disabled': false on the Upload and Camera buttons. Both producers expose the lever: SliderProps has `disabled?: boolean`; DockControl props carry `disabled` documented as 'the four-state contract'.
defects.mechanism: A prop is accepted into the contract and then not threaded — the component's disabled state is a claim its render does not honour. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value ... are explicit.' There is no pending state expressed on this component at all.
defects.reproduction: grep -n "disabled" demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue (3 hits, 1 use); and evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.txt rowButtons/sliders blocks.
defects.proposedCure: Thread `disabled` to both Sliders and to the Upload and Camera DockControls. The producers already accept it; this is four attribute bindings, not new mechanism.

defects.defect: Neither axis satisfies the axis composition the constitution mandates and names Extract in. The k axis has no label at all — the value numeral occupies the label seat — and neither axis carries a unit or aria-valuetext.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: 'The domain-neutral axis composition sits over BI Slider: label, unit, reserved live value ... Picker, Generate count, Extract, Gradient, Atmosphere and Blob adopt that one composition.' Measured: k label = absent (line 15-17 renders {{ k }} in the label seat); k unit = absent; k aria-valuetext = null (announces '5', not '5 colors'). kC label = 'kC', an unexpanded symbol disclosed only by title; kC unit = absent; kC aria-valuetext = null.
defects.mechanism: Reading down the rendered cluster, `5` and `kC` are vertically adjacent and typographically identical (both Fira Code 400) while being semantically opposite — one a value, one a name — and nothing in the design distinguishes them. The same §5 sentence forbids the remedy the component chose: 'feature waves own their domain arrangement, not new slider mechanics.'
defects.reproduction: Read ExtractControls.vue:14-36 and :65-79; aria-valuetext null confirmed in evidence/pass-4 probes and the concurrent pass-3 aria dump.
defects.proposedCure: Give the k axis a real label, both axes a unit, and both thumbs an aria-valuetext ('5 colors', 'chroma weight 0.5'). Adopt the one composition rather than an ad-hoc arrangement per axis.

defects.defect: The empty state — the state the route boots into — inverts the pane's visual hierarchy. The two slider rails are the loudest, largest, most saturated objects on the plate and they change nothing; the only actions that move the user forward (Upload, Camera) are quiet 40px ghost icons.
defects.evidence: Visible in all four shipped captures. .../shots/safari-desktop-light/extract.png: the crimson k rail is the single highest-contrast element inside the Extract card, above a dashed drop-zone and two low-contrast icons. Reset is correctly disabled; the equally-inert sliders are not (D-7). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.8 'One pane may have one full-strength visual protagonist. Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow.' §7·Extract: 'The image is the stage.'
defects.mechanism: The support IS the protagonist. Configuration for work not yet started is rendered at full accent strength, so the pane's loudest signal carries no information in its default state.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — read the four shipped PNGs at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/*/extract.png.
defects.proposedCure: Gestalt, not a tweak: pre-image both axes take the de-emphasis register (neutral track, quiet ink) and yield the plate to the drop-zone and the two actions. The gradient's arrival on first extract then IS the state change — the control lights up because it now carries data. One design serving both states, instead of one loud state serving neither.

defects.defect: Three icon-only actions whose only name is a hover tooltip. On the two mobile matrices — half the shipped audit surface — there is no mechanism by which a user can learn what Upload, Camera and Reset do.
defects.evidence: Measured on every arm: all three buttons have {title:'Upload image'|'Open camera'|'Reset', ariaLabel:null, ariaLabelledby:null, text:''}. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 'Hover-only/unlabeled controls ... every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state'; PR-16 'no tooltip proliferation'; §5.6 'do not compensate ... with tooltip proliferation. Subtraction precedes explanation.'
defects.mechanism: Naming delegated entirely to `title`, which is hover-only and therefore unreachable on touch. Scope stated honestly: `title` IS a valid accname fallback, so these are named to AT — I therefore do NOT charge the visual audit's namelessButtons:3 on /#/extract to this component, because the harness predicate (capture.mjs:104) tests only aria-label||aria-labelledby||textContent and excludes title, so its count is consistent with these three but does not prove them. Pass 2 reached the same conclusion independently and I confirm it.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — rowButtons array, every arm. Sizes are fine (44x44 coarse, 40x40 fine), so this is purely a naming failure.
defects.proposedCure: Add aria-label to all three (keep title for the pointer affordance). The deeper cure per PR-16 is to ask whether three icon-only actions on this plate are earned at all before explaining them.

defects.defect: The component's own comment certifies a 'ONE mono voice' for its cluster; the cluster renders two type sizes, 1.49x apart, and one of them uses a role absent from the binding type matrix.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:12-13 asserts 'The k label speaks its cluster's ONE mono voice (weight 400, matching kC — E1-R1)'. Measured 1440/light: k readout '5' = Fira Code 16.4px/400; kC label 'kC' = Fira Code 11px/400; kC readout '0.5' = Fira Code 11px/400. Weight matches; size is 1.49x. Additionally text-micro is NOT in the binding type matrix (OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md, Binding type matrix), which enumerates for values/code/provenance exactly text-mono-small or the established mono-caption.
defects.mechanism: The comment certifies the axis it was checked on (weight) and is silent on the one that differs (size). Documented intent diverges from render — the same failure family as D-12.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-killshot.mjs — KILL-SHOT 3 block reports fontSize/fontWeight for all three text atoms.
defects.proposedCure: Put both readouts on one in-matrix mono role (text-mono-small), and correct or delete the certifying comment. A comment that certifies a property the render lacks is worse than no comment.

defects.defect: The documented 'outward hairline ring' is implemented as an INSET box-shadow — inward, eroding 1.5px of the data layer on every edge — and it is invisible in the very state the comment says it carries.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:5-11 claims the ink 'survives OUTWARD as a persistent hairline ring ... giving the component a certified identity edge independent of its gradient content in every state.' Implementation at :22 is `boxShadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px ${trackInk}`. Measured pre-image: backgroundColor 'oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)' and boxShadow 'oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023) 0px 0px 0px 1.5px inset' — ring colour IDENTICAL to fill colour, so the ring is invisible.
defects.mechanism: Inverted claim: the certified identity edge exists only in the state the comment says it is redundant in (post-image, over the gradient) and is absent in the state the comment says it carries (pre-image). 'in every state' is false as written.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — kRailStyle block shows backgroundColor === boxShadow colour, and boxShadow carries the `inset` keyword.
defects.proposedCure: If an identity edge is wanted, make it an outset ring or a border that does not consume the data layer; and rewrite the comment to describe what is built. Folded into D-1's cure, since the whole decoy apparatus goes.

defects.defect: `.plate-ink` — a token-resolving rule — is copy-pasted into five components' scoped styles with no root definition anywhere.
defects.evidence: grep -rln '^\.plate-ink' demo/ -> demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue, demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue, demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue (5 files). grep -rn 'plate-ink' demo/styles/ -> no output. Two copies are in the same directory; one is in this file's immediate parent.
defects.mechanism: Owner edict 5 — style at the root component level, never per-instance. A rule that resolves a design token belongs in demo/styles/, defined once. Five identical definitions is five places for the token contract to drift.
defects.reproduction: grep -rln "^\.plate-ink" demo/ && grep -rn "plate-ink" demo/styles/
defects.proposedCure: Move `.plate-ink` to demo/styles/ once and delete all five scoped copies.

defects.defect: A dead scoped rule `.touch-gate-target` that matches zero elements, whose stated purpose (touch-target sizing) is exactly what is measurably broken here — and which strands a deliberately-unscoped global block another component maintains partly to serve this one.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:139-142 declares `.touch-gate-target { border-radius: var(--radius-pill) }` under the comment 'Touch gate styling for extract sliders'. Measured live: document.querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target').length === 0 on /#/extract. The class appears nowhere in this component's template; glass-ui never emits it (grep -c over glass-ui.css and the slider chunk -> 0, 0). It is also inside <style scoped>, so it could not reach the Slider's internals even if applied. Meanwhile ComponentSliders.vue:245 keeps an intentionally UNSCOPED global block whose comment names its reason: '...plus the ExtractControls/PointerDebug touch-gate-target uses — the block is intentionally UNSCOPED so the cascade reaches consumers outside this SFC's data-v-* attribute scope.'
defects.mechanism: A cross-component global escape hatch is carried in ComponentSliders partly on this component's behalf, and this component never opts in. The dead rule documents an intent (touch gating) the component does not deliver, while D-3/D-4 measure exactly that failure.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-probe-geometry.mjs — 'touchGateApplied': 0 in every arm. Plus: grep -rn touch-gate-target demo/ (only the CSS rule, never the template).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead rule, and relay to ComponentSliders that its unscoped block no longer serves this consumer so the escape hatch can be re-scoped or retired. Do not 'fix' it by applying the class — the real cure for touch targets is D-3's size=lg.

defects.defect: `text-right` is a physical property; in RTL the flex row reverses but the alignment does not, so the k numeral hugs the edge AWAY from its rail and the optical tie between value and bar is broken.
defects.evidence: Measured 1440 with dir=rtl applied live. LTR: label box 224->244, text-align right, rail left edge 252 -> ink sits 8px from the rail (hugging). RTL: label box 1196->1216, text-align STILL right, rail right edge 1188 -> ink sits ~28px from the rail across an empty box. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document.'
defects.mechanism: Physical directional keyword used where a logical one is required. Closes a genuine coverage gap: the state matrix at shots/{rtl,forced-colors,zoom-200,keyboard-focus,reduced-motion}-desktop/ covers only adminusers, blob, browse, gradient, picker — extract is in NONE of them, so this is the first RTL measurement of this component.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-states-rtl-zoom-320-focus.mjs — rtl-1440 block; screenshot evidence/pass-4/d4-rtl-1440.png.
defects.proposedCure: `text-right` -> `text-end` (logical). One token. Also align both readouts alike — k is text-right and kC is text-align:start (measured), two numeric readouts in one cluster with opposite alignment.

defects.defect: The k value reservation has 1.3% headroom and depends on a webfont resolving; the box is whitespace-nowrap so any wider fallback spills into the 8px gap against the rail rather than wrapping.

EXPLICIT DISAGREEMENT RECORDED: pass 2 (P2-1/P2-2) reports the k and kC reservations overflowing at every legal value; I measured scrollWidth === clientWidth and overflows:false for both at 1440/light with Fira Code resolved. The disagreement should be adjudicated before either number enters a wave.
defects.mechanism: A reservation with 1.3% slack and a webfont dependency is not reserved — it is a coincidence that holds while the primary font loads.
defects.reproduction: node .../evidence/pass-4/d4-k16-reservation.mjs (focuses the k thumb, presses ArrowRight 20x, measures ink advance against the box). Output evidence/pass-4/d4-k16-reservation.txt; screenshot d4-k16-reservation.png.

defects.defect: Every producer lever that would have prevented D-1, D-3, D-4 and D-7 exists on glass-ui 7.0.0 and none is used; the one number the component chose by hand is the one number the producer's size scale does not contain.
defects.evidence: Unused: --slider-track-bg on the k axis (D-1); size='sm|md|lg' -> --slider-thumb-size .5/1/1.5rem (D-3, D-4); --slider-track-height; `disabled` on Slider AND DockControl (D-7); `marks?: readonly number[]` (the k axis is 16 discrete integers with no positional legibility). The hand-rolled rail is h-6 = 24px; the spectrum variant at the default size='md' computes calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5) = 24px — the component hand-built and then maintained the exact number it already had. The producer size scale is 12/20/28px (glass-ui.css: [data-size=sm|md|lg] --slider-track-height .75rem/1.25rem/1.75rem), so 24px is OFF that scale.
defects.mechanism: Symptom of the D-1 posture: because the component never drives the producer's levers it never inherits the producer's responsibilities — the coarse-pointer thumb contract, the size scale, the disabled contract, and the dock-context geometry the separators silently need.
defects.reproduction: cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts (SliderProps: disabled, size, marks); and the extracted size-scale rules in the report §D-17.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the levers rather than the hand-rolls — this is the single change that collapses D-1, D-3, D-4, D-7 and D-17 into one refactor rather than five patches.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue (pass 3; pin SHA-256 71aa0a65…d46c28 VERIFIED byte-for-byte)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Matches the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: XC-1 — the component's longest comment (lines 3–13) specifies a certified identity edge that "survives OUTWARD … in every state"; line 22 writes `inset`, which paints that ring ON the palette gradient while `trackInk` was certified against the RESTING PLATE. Measured: 1.000:1 pre-image (ring colour byte-identical to the fill it sits on) and max 2.673:1 anywhere along its run in light (min 1.002:1), never reaching the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor the comment itself invokes. The O-18 gate the comment cites as its authority reads only `backgroundColor`, so it cannot distinguish the defect from its one-word repair.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative is claimed for the component as a whole. Recorded here are the hypotheses I tested and DISPROVED by positive measurement, so no later pass re-litigates them: (1) `w-5` clipping — FALSE, k="16" clientW 20 / scrollW 20, kC="1.5" clientW 20 / scrollW 20 (xc3-probe1.txt, xc3-probe2.txt); (2) float accumulation on the 0.1-step kC slider — FALSE, aria-valuenow walks 0, 0.1 … 1.4, 1.5 exactly over 16 keypresses; (3) parseCssColor passthrough in certifyAccentInk — NOT a bug, it is tested intent at test/ink.test.ts:199; (4) Reset lacks a disabled affordance — FALSE, disabled + aria-disabled="true" + opacity 0.5 + cursor:default (xc3-probe4.txt); (5) DockControl tap targets — FALSE, all three measure 40×40; (6) ungated rAF / leaked listeners / observers / timers / WebGL / ValueUnit nesting — ALL ABSENT, the file is purely presentational with no lifecycle hooks at all; route console errors 0 and page errors 0 in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:122,137,152,167); (7) gradient stop collision at k=16 — FALSE, 0,7,13,…,93,100 strictly monotonic; (8) reka-ui pointer-capture leak — glass-ui's Slider already installs and removes pointerup/pointercancel/blur teardown; (9) defineModel stale-read hazard — structurally absent, the component is emit-only and holds no local state, which is the safer pattern deliberately chosen.

defects.defect: The "certified identity edge" hairline ring is invisible in every state. ExtractControls.vue:3-13 specifies a ring that "survives OUTWARD … giving the component a certified identity edge independent of its gradient content in every state". Line 22 paints it `inset`. Per CSS Backgrounds 3 §5.3 an inner shadow paints ABOVE the element's background colour AND image, so the ring lands on the palette gradient — while trackInk (:123-125) is certified via useSafeAccentFn("resting") against the resting PLATE. Certification referent ≠ paint referent.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:22 — `boxShadow: `inset 0 0 0 1.5px ${trackInk}``. Live computed style (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.txt): backgroundColor "oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023)" and boxShadow "oklch(0.545141 0.218024 9.834023) 0px 0px 0px 1.5px inset" — the ring colour string is IDENTICAL to the fill string, so pre-image contrast is 1.000:1 by identity. Developed, 401-column sweep of the live background-image in both schemes (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe5.txt): LIGHT MAX_contrast_anywhere_along_the_ring 2.673 (at fraction 1.0, an exact stop value), MIN 1.002 (at fraction 0.438), PASSES_ANYWHERE false; DARK MAX 6.992, MIN 1.845 (at fraction 1.0) — fails at the right terminus. Exact per-stop values, light: 0% oklch(0.578513 0.213789 27.172258) → 1.168; 33% oklch(0.471973 0.216301 267.259979) → 1.294; 67% oklch(0.701065 0.208852 144.531006) → 2.273; 100% oklch(0.767351 0.016744 73.637039) → 2.673. Visual: evidence/pass-3/xc3-rail-developed.png (3× DPR clip).
defects.mechanism: Certification referent decoupled from paint referent by one keyword. `inset` moves plate-certified ink onto an arbitrary quantizer-produced gradient, making the guarantee a pure function of the very content it claims independence from (2.7× contrast spread in light, 3.8× in dark, on one image).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe5.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — uploads a synthetic four-band PNG in-page, reads back the rail's computed background-image and box-shadow, samples the ring contrast at 401 positions in light and dark.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the keyword `inset` from ExtractControls.vue:22. The ring then becomes exactly what the comment already specifies: an outward hairline seated on the resting plate, where trackInk's ≥4.25:1 certification (GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR 3 + CERTIFY_HEADROOM 1.25, ink.ts:16-17,137) IS the correct guarantee for that ground. Geometry verified to admit it: `overflow:hidden` on the rail clips children, never the element's own box-shadow; the 1.5px spread lands in the parent h-6 row (:18) and no ancestor up to the plate sets overflow. This is a transposition, not a patch — it adds no guarantee, it moves the ring back onto the surface the guarantee was already computed for.

defects.defect: The `disabled` prop is declared, destructured and bound to exactly ONE of five interactive controls. The parent passes a two-condition guard; the child honours it only on Reset. Upload, Camera, the k Slider and the kC Slider all ignore it, so the parent's contract is inert.
defects.evidence: `grep -n disabled demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue` returns exactly three lines: 84 (`:disabled="disabled || !hasImage"` — Reset), 103 (destructure), 109 (prop type). ExtractWorkbench.vue:70 passes `:disabled="session.isProcessing.value || cameraActive"`. Both glass-ui DockControl and Slider expose a `disabled` prop (dist/dock.js `disabled: { type: Boolean, default: !1 }`; slider-DzqeQmMu.js `disabled: { type: Boolean }`). Measured over 30 samples at 100ms spanning a full 1600×1600 decode→quantize→render window (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe3.txt): `{"upload": false, "camera": false, "k": false, "kc": false, "reset": false}` — not one control disabled at any sample; and driving the k slider by keyboard inside that window dispatched a fresh worker job: `[{"t": 7860, "k": 10, "cw": 0.5}]`.
defects.mechanism: A prop declared as a contract but honoured at a single site. TypeScript cannot catch an unused destructured binding and no gate reads the prop, so the omission is invisible to every mechanical check.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe3.mjs — uploads a 1600×1600 noise PNG, samples every control's disabled state 30× at 100ms, then focuses the k slider thumb and presses ArrowRight, counting Worker.prototype.postMessage dispatches.
defects.proposedCure: Bind `:disabled="disabled"` on the Upload and Camera DockControls and on both Sliders (four attributes); keep Reset's compound predicate, revised per XC-6. The structural cure that makes reintroduction impossible is to gate the group once at its root rather than hand-threading five bindings — but for a file under a byte-pin, the four explicit bindings are the KISS reading.

defects.defect: Camera MediaStreams are acquired and never released. Two independent mechanisms: (a) the pane is KeepAlive-cached so onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera) never fires on route change; (b) NEW — startCamera's catch block handles a throw that occurs AFTER acquisition (the srcObject assignment), setting cameraActive=false and unmounting the only UI that could stop the live stream, while never stopping it.
defects.evidence: ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-255 — `cameraStream = await getUserMedia(...)` then `if (videoRef.value) videoRef.value.srcObject = cameraStream`; the catch sets quantizeError and cameraActive=false but never stops tracks. Measured with a getUserMedia stub counting track.stop() (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.txt): after 1st press `{gumCalls: 1, stops: [], liveTracks: ["live"], cameraBtnDisabled: false}`; after 2nd press `{gumCalls: 2, stops: [], trackStates: [{id:"s1",track:"t1",state:"live"},{id:"s2",track:"t2",state:"live"}]}`; after navigating to /#/palettes `{stops: [], trackStates: [ …both "live" ]}`. TWO acquisitions, ZERO stop() calls, both tracks still live after leaving the route.
defects.mechanism: Acquisition and release have no single owner. The re-entry that produces the second stream is enabled by XC-2 (the Camera button ignores the `disabled=true` the parent asserts precisely when cameraActive is set), and the post-acquisition throw path treats an acquisition-failure handler as a general error handler.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.mjs — replaces navigator.mediaDevices before app boot with a counting fake, clicks 'Open camera' twice, then changes route, printing gumCalls / stops / per-track readyState at each step.
defects.proposedCure: Give the stream one owner: make startCamera idempotent (early-return while a stream is held — XC-2's binding also enforces this at the button), release inside the catch (`cameraStream?.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` before nulling), and own the lifetime with onScopeDispose rather than onBeforeUnmount so a KeepAlive-cached pane still releases. Workbench-side (unpinned, lands now); the pinned file's half is XC-2's binding.

defects.defect: This component contributes 100% of the /#/extract nameless-button count — 3 of 3, in all four Safari capture matrices, making /#/extract the worst route in the application and the only route above 1. Upload, Camera and Reset carry `title` only; every other button on the route carries an aria-label.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:97-115 — namelessButtons 18 total; `safari-desktop-light /#/extract: 3`, `safari-desktop-dark /#/extract: 3`, `safari-mobile-light /#/extract: 3`, `safari-mobile-dark /#/extract: 3`; every other route reports 1. Attribution by live enumeration under the capture script's own rule (visual/capture.mjs:102-105), evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.txt §BUTTONS: exactly three visible buttons have `ariaLabel: null` — `title: "Upload image"` (ExtractControls.vue:41), `title: "Open camera"` (:50), `title: "Reset"` (:85). The other nine (Save edit, Cancel edit, Switch to slug, Generate new slug, Cancel, Select view, Toggle action bar, Login/@mbabb, ImageDropZone) all carry aria-label or text. glass-ui's own DockControl consumer DockBackgroundToggle passes BOTH: `aria-label: i.value, title: i.value` (dist/dock.js).
defects.mechanism: Reliance on `title` as the sole accessible name. `title` is the accname algorithm's last-resort fallback, inconsistently announced across AT, and has NO touch affordance at all — on the two mobile matrices, which cover this route's own camera-capture use case, the result is three unlabelled glyphs.
defects.reproduction: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json')); [print(r['matrix'], r['probe']['a11y']['namelessButtons']) for r in d['results'] if 'extract' in r['route']]" → 3, 3, 3, 3. Attribution: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Add `aria-label` beside the existing `title` on all three DockControls, matching DockBackgroundToggle verbatim — glass-ui's own demonstrated idiom. Three attributes; the route's count goes 3 → 0 and the application total 18 → 6. Relay to glass-ui BJ that the aria-label+title pairing should be the DOCUMENTED DockControl contract rather than an internal habit.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate. The O-18 graphics leg that this file's comments cite as their authority ("the O-18 graphics leg is its born-RED gate", :63-64) reads exactly one property — backgroundColor — and never visits the developed state. The box-shadow ring that carries the file's entire load-bearing claim is under no test in either direction: the gate cannot distinguish the XC-1 defect from its correct repair.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:293 — `const rawBg = getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor;` is the sole measured property; never backgroundImage. `grep -in "boxShadow|box-shadow" e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts` returns NO OUTPUT. The extract graphics leg (:1080-1140) navigates to /#/extract?space=lab&color=… and samples [data-o18="extract-kc"] .slider-track and [data-o18="extract-k-rail"] — it never uploads an image, so it measures a backgroundColor that in the developed state is 100% occluded by an opaque four-stop gradient spanning 0%–100% (measured, xc3-probe1.txt §RAIL developed). No unit test references ExtractControls: `grep -rln ExtractControls test/ e2e/` returns nothing.
defects.mechanism: The gate holds the one property it looks at and nothing else. Killing mutations that keep every gate green: (g) delete boxShadow from line 22 entirely; (h) inset 0 0 0 1.5px → inset 0 0 0 0px; (i) flip `inset` to outward — i.e. THE CORRECT FIX also passes unchanged. That symmetry is the indictment.
defects.reproduction: grep -in 'boxShadow\|box-shadow' e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts  → (no output). Then read o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1085-1140 and confirm no setInputFiles / file upload occurs anywhere in the extract graphics leg.
defects.proposedCure: Extend the extract graphics leg to a DEVELOPED state: upload a fixture image, then assert (a) the rail's ring colour against the sampled live gradient at its own extrema ≥3:1, and (b) that a rail whose box-shadow is `none` FAILS. e2e/ is not under the glass pin, so this lands NOW — ahead of the consumer wave — turning XC-1 into a born-RED gate instead of a claim, and making the cure verifiable rather than asserted.

defects.defect: Reset is disabled in exactly the state where it is the only way out. The gate is `disabled || !hasImage`, but the state Reset restores (colorCount, chromaWeight) is fully mutable WITHOUT an image — the ShadowPalette ghost re-segments live under the k slider, which the repo's own oracle asserts. A user who moves k pre-image cannot put it back.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:84 `:disabled="disabled || !hasImage"`. useExtractSession.ts:180-184 — onReset() sets colorCount=5, chromaWeight=0.5, and only calls runQuantize() `if (lastFile.value)`, so the function is ALREADY safe with no image. e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:147-155 asserts the ghost re-segments 5 → 6 → 5 under the k slider with no image loaded; ExtractWorkbench.vue:159 binds `:count="session.colorCount.value"` to prove it. Measured (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.txt): after focusing the k slider on a fresh /#/extract and pressing End (k → 16, no image), `RESET pre-image, k=16 → {"disabled": true, "ariaDisabled": "true"}`.
defects.mechanism: The gate condition was written for the re-quantize SIDE EFFECT, not for the state the action owns. The composable already separates the two; the template conflates them. chromaWeight, which has no ghost feedback at all, is likewise stranded.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract, focus the 'Number of colors' slider thumb, press End. The ghost re-segments to 16 segments; the Reset button reports disabled=true and aria-disabled="true". Automated: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.mjs §RESET pre-image.
defects.proposedCure: `:disabled="disabled || (k === 5 && chromaWeight === 0.5)"` — disable Reset when there is nothing to reset, which is the TRUE predicate and is also correct post-image. The `hasImage` prop then has no consumer in this file and dies with it, removing a prop and its parent binding (edict 3, KISS).

defects.defect: Reset does not cancel the pending debounce: one user intent produces two identical worker jobs. onReset calls runQuantize() directly without clearing debounceTimer, so an in-flight debounced re-quantize fires again ~300ms later with the same payload.
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:159-162 (debouncedReQuantize sets a 300ms timer) and :180-184 (onReset calls runQuantize() directly, never clearTimeout). Measured by instrumenting Worker.prototype.postMessage (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe3.txt): ArrowLeft on the k slider, then Reset 60ms later → `[{"t": 9165.000000000002, "k": 5, "cw": 0.5}, {"t": 9307, "k": 5, "cw": 0.5}]` — two dispatches, 142ms apart, byte-identical payloads. On the 1600×1600 fixture that is a complete redundant k-means pass over 2.56M pixels. Compounding: useImageQuantize.ts:51-52 holds a SINGLE pendingResolve/pendingReject slot overwritten at :90-91 on every dispatch, so the second job orphans the first — its promise never settles in either direction for the lifetime of the page.
defects.mechanism: Two entry points (the debounced path and the immediate path) write to the same scheduling resource, and only one of them owns the timer. The immediate path must remember to clear a timer it did not set.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe3.mjs — patches Worker.prototype.postMessage to log every dispatch with its options, uploads an image, focuses the k slider, presses ArrowLeft, then clicks Reset within the 300ms debounce window.
defects.proposedCure: One scheduler owns the timer: `requestQuantize({ immediate })`, with onReset and onFile taking the immediate path THROUGH it, so the pending timer is cleared by construction rather than by remembering to. Pair with request tokens and `isProcessing = inFlight > 0` so an overlapping job cannot orphan a promise or clear the processing flag early. Composable-side, unpinned, lands now.

defects.defect: The accessible name lands on TWO nodes, one of them a roleless generic. glass-ui's Slider forwards $attrs['aria-label'] to the thumb but does not declare inheritAttrs:false, so the same attribute also falls through to SliderRoot — a 434×24 span with no role. ARIA 1.2 §5.2.8 prohibits aria-label on role=generic.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/slider-DzqeQmMu.js — the component definition carries only [["__scopeId", …]], no inheritAttrs:false, while explicitly reading `e.$attrs["aria-label"]` for the thumb. Measured (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.txt): `{label:"Number of colors", tag:"span", cls:"glass-slider.relative", role:null, valuenow:null, tabindex:null, w:434, h:24}` AND `{label:"Number of colors", tag:"span", cls:"slider-thumb…", role:"slider", valuenow:"5", valuemin:"1", valuemax:"16", tabindex:"0", w:12, h:24}` — both sliders, both schemes. Related: the 12×24 thumbs are this component's two smallTapTargets in REPORT.json ({"w":12,"h":24,"label":"Number of colors"} desktop, {"w":12,"h":44} mobile), from the glass-ui recipe `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb { width: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem) * .75) }`.
defects.mechanism: A library component that forwards an attribute explicitly AND inherits it implicitly, duplicating it. This is a glass-ui defect, not a consumer one — the consumer's aria-label is the documented input — but it changes what the consumer's attribute does.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.mjs §aria-label carriers — enumerates every element matching [aria-label="Number of colors"],[aria-label="Chroma weight"] with its role, value attributes and box.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui 8: declare `inheritAttrs: false` on Slider so the name reaches only the role=slider thumb, and expose an `aria-valuetext` pass-through prop (XC-13). Re-measure the 12px spectrum thumb against the 24×24 target floor at the same time. Requires a Glass 8 release — this is the ONLY item in the wave that genuinely does. Relay to the glass-ui BJ inbox per the standing formation invariant.

defects.defect: Two <label> elements that label nothing: neither has a `for` attribute and neither wraps a control. The k readout is marked up as a <label>, contributing a stray '16' to the accessibility tree that names nothing; the kC label's only expansion lives in a `title`.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:15-17 (`<label class="text-mono-small plate-ink …">{{ k }}</label>`) and :66 (`<label class="fira-code text-micro plate-ink whitespace-nowrap" title="Chroma weight">kC</label>`). Measured (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.txt §ORPHAN LABELS): `[{text:"16", htmlFor:null, controlInside:false, title:null}, {text:"kC", htmlFor:null, controlInside:false, title:"Chroma weight"}]`.
defects.mechanism: A labelling element used for a value readout and for a decorative abbreviation. The semantics are borrowed for the typography, not for the association — and the association never exists.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.mjs §ORPHAN LABELS.
defects.proposedCure: k readout → <span> (it is a readout, not a label). kC → <abbr title="Chroma weight">kC</abbr>, or an aria-hidden glyph paired with the slider's existing aria-label, which already carries the full phrase — so no information is lost and the touch-invisible `title` stops being the sole carrier.

defects.defect: Three identical per-instance style overrides — a direct violation of owner edict 5 (style at the root component level, never per-instance overrides).
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:42, :51, :86 — each carries `:style="{ '--btn-hover-color': cssColor }"`: the same custom property, the same value, pinned three times on three sibling DockControls.
defects.mechanism: A cascading, inheritable custom property applied at the leaves instead of at the group root. Each render also allocates three fresh object literals for Vue's patchStyle to diff, and cssColor is the live pick.
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'btn-hover-color' demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue → three lines: 42, 51, 86.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist one `--btn-hover-color` declaration to the controls row container (:39). Custom properties inherit, so it reaches all three DockControls and any control added later — three overrides become one declaration, and edict 5 is satisfied structurally rather than by convention.

defects.defect: A load-bearing, undocumented style-object key ordering is the only thing keeping the born-RED `var(--muted)` rail material off screen. `background` (shorthand) precedes `backgroundColor` (longhand) in the style object; Vue's patchStyle iterates in insertion order, so the longhand wins. Reversing two keys reinstates the exact material the T-44a remediation existed to kill.
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:22 — `{ background: gradient, backgroundColor: trackInk, boxShadow: … }`. useExtractSession.ts:103 — the pre-image degenerate returns the literal string `"var(--muted)"`. Measured pre-image (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.txt): `backgroundImage: "none"`, `backgroundColor: "oklch(0.545141 …)"` — the `background: var(--muted)` shorthand reset background-image to none and was then overwritten, so kSliderGradient's degenerate branch is DEAD CODE that can never render. The value it returns is the file's own recorded born-RED material (:119-122: 1.88:1 light / 1.85:1 dark, 'the owner's "un-readable" sliders, measured').
defects.mechanism: A shorthand and its longhand set in one object, where correctness depends on iteration order that no comment records and no test pins. Reordering keys in a style object is a plausible tidy-up.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe1.mjs §RAIL pre-image — shows backgroundImage "none" with backgroundColor set to the certified ink, proving the shorthand's value was computed and discarded.
defects.proposedCure: Make the degenerate a STATE, not a colour string: return null from kSliderGradient and branch the template, or return `"none"` and let backgroundColor be the sole colour authority. Then the `background` shorthand never carries a colour, the ordering stops being load-bearing, and the born-RED literal leaves the tree entirely (edict 2). Composable-side, unpinned.

defects.defect: A guard that does not guard. `(v: number[] | undefined) => v && $emit('update:k', v[0]!)` — an empty array is truthy, so the guard rejects only `undefined`; for `[]` it passes and the non-null assertion `v[0]!` is a lie, emitting `update:k: undefined` → colorCount.value = undefined → ShadowPalette :count="undefined".
defects.evidence: ExtractControls.vue:33 and :76 — `@update:model-value="(v: number[] | undefined) => v && $emit('update:k', v[0]!)"`.
defects.mechanism: Defensive code written for a case (an empty payload) that its own truthiness test cannot detect, paired with a non-null assertion that silences the type system in precisely that case.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a labelled HYPOTHESIS. reka-ui's SliderRoot was not observed to emit an empty array in any probe. The finding is that the defence is written as if it could and would fail if it did.
defects.proposedCure: `(v?: number[]) => { const n = v?.[0]; if (n !== undefined) emit('update:k', n); }` — test the value that is actually used, and delete the assertion. Or, since the parent handlers are plain setters, drop the inline arrow entirely and let the typed emit signature do the narrowing.

defects.defect: No aria-valuetext on either slider. A screen reader announces 'Chroma weight, 0.5' for a control ranging 0–1.5 with no unit and no meaning; 'Number of colors, 5' is serviceable, 'Chroma weight, 0.5' is not.
defects.evidence: Measured (evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.txt): `"valuetext": null` on both role=slider thumbs, all schemes, at every step of a 16-keypress walk from 0 to 1.5. aria-valuenow itself is clean (0, 0.1 … 1.4, 1.5 — no float drift). glass-ui's Slider exposes no aria-valuetext pass-through prop (slider-DzqeQmMu.js forwards only aria-label / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / aria-errormessage / aria-invalid to the thumb).
defects.mechanism: The consumer cannot supply aria-valuetext because the library does not forward it; the library does not forward it because no consumer asked. Corroborates pass-2 C2-7, which files it as MAJOR against a ratified repo law.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-controls/evidence/pass-3/xc3-probe2.mjs §kC keyboard walk — 16 samples of aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext against the rendered .toFixed(1) readout.
defects.proposedCure: Add an aria-valuetext pass-through to glass-ui's Slider thumb forwarding list (Glass 8, bundled with XC-8's inheritAttrs:false fix), then supply `:aria-valuetext="`${chromaWeight.toFixed(1)} chroma weight`"` and `:aria-valuetext="`${k} colors`"` from this file. Relay to glass-ui BJ.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface). Pass D of a four-pass E-1 twice-audit chain; passes A/B/C preserved verbatim as challenge-L-library-pass-{a,b,c}.md.
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier explicitly declared at spawn. The seat is declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: The value.js library publishes TWO mutually incompatible failure algebras across two of its seven subpaths. `@mkbabb/value.js/color` re-exports `Result<T,E>` whose failure arm carries `.error` (src/color/model.ts); `@mkbabb/value.js/css` re-exports `ParseResult<T>` whose failure arm carries `.diagnostics` and has no `.error` at all (src/css/types.ts:26-27). A consumer cannot write one generic unwrap; it must branch on which subpath the value came from. The demo pays with two different unwrap adapters eight lines apart in ONE file, plus a third hand-rolled inline. This is the root cause beneath pass A's F-4, which described the erasure of failure-explicitness but never asked why two adapters were needed. Failure-explicitness is the package's headline property (package.json description) and is the one property the published surface fails to give a single shape.
defects.evidence: src/css/types.ts:26-27 (`{ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,...]}`) vs src/color/model.ts:38-43 + foundation `Result` (`{ok:false, error:E}`); both published at src/subpaths/css.ts:21 and src/subpaths/color.ts:9. Consumer cost measured in one file: demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:104-107 (`valueOrThrow`, reads `result.error.code`) and :110-114 (`parsePickerColor`, reads `result.diagnostics`); a third at demo/palettes/mix.ts:36. Executed against the committed dist: `node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCssColor} from './dist/subpaths/css.js'; const r=parseCssColor('color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)'); console.log(r); try{r.error.code}catch(e){console.log('DEREF THROWS:',e.constructor.name+': '+e.message)}"` → `{ ok: false, diagnostics: [ { code: 'css_syntax', start: 0, end: 30, expected: [Array], actual: 'color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)' } ] }` / `keys: [ 'ok', 'diagnostics' ]` / `DEREF THROWS: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'code')`.
defects.mechanism: Missing unique semantic owner INSIDE the published surface — one concept ("failure-explicit result"), two shapes, two subpaths. Wrong public surface.
defects.reproduction: Run the `node --input-type=module` command above verbatim at repo root against the committed dist/. It prints the `{ok,diagnostics}` shape and then the TypeError from dereferencing `.error.code`, which is the exact expression `valueOrThrow` (picker-color.ts:106) applies to every /color result.
defects.proposedCure: One algebra. `ParseResult<T>` becomes `Result<T, readonly [ParseIssue, ...ParseIssue[]]>` — the foundation `Result` already generalises over E, only the failure arm's field name changes. Then `valueOrThrow` is the SINGLE adapter; `parsePickerColor`'s bespoke throw (picker-color.ts:113) deletes; demo/palettes/mix.ts:36's third unwrap deletes; and pass A's F-4 cure (surface failures instead of throwing) becomes a one-place change rather than a three-place one. Migration is mechanical — no call site reads `.diagnostics` structurally except the two shown.

defects.defect: CARRIED BLOCKER, owned by pass C, independently reproduced by pass D. The demo passes a `tag="button"` + `aria-label` + `@click` + `:disabled` prop contract to glass-ui's `WatercolorDot`, which declares none of them; every consumer attribute and listener is discarded. The Mix workbench's colors-mode add-a-color control renders as a decorative `<span aria-hidden="true">` that cannot be clicked and is absent from the accessibility tree, so colors mode has no working entry point.
defects.evidence: MixSourceSelector.vue:161-171 passes tag="button" aria-label="Add current color to the mix" :disabled @click. Live DOM at localhost:9000/#/mix, 390x844: `document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost')` → `<span data-v-292b9032 aria-hidden="true" data-variant="ghost" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" class="add-slot-ghost …">`; `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]')` → null. Two programmatic `el.click()` + 900ms settle → `document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-source]').length === 0`. Real Playwright click on `.add-slot-ghost` → TimeoutError 5000ms, log: `<div class="swatch-row flex items-center gap-2.5 flex-wrap"> intercepts pointer events`, retried 14x. Screenshot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/mix.png shows the dashed ghost rendering as designed — the defect is invisible to the visual matrix.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency at a package boundary: the demo needed an interactive affordance and prop-guessed one into existence against a decorative primitive instead of asking the design system for it (edict 4). Vue routes unknown props to fallthrough attrs, so vue-tsc cannot see it.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 390x844, ensure the Colors tab is selected, then evaluate `const g=document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost'); g.click(); g.click(); document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-source]').length` → 0. Pass C's fuller reproduction is in challenge-L-library-pass-c.md §C-1.
defects.proposedCure: Pass C's cure stands, unchanged: make the host the control and the dot the face — a real `<button type="button" aria-label=… :disabled @click>` wrapping `<WatercolorDot class="pointer-events-none">`, the idiom this same file already uses correctly at :245-263. Plus a glass-ui BH relay (declare `tag`/`as` as a real polymorphic root with attr+listener pass-through, or publish a WatercolorSwatchButton). No demo-side wrapper component (edict 3).

defects.defect: Pass C's C-3 closed from HYPOTHESIS to CONFIRMED, by direct instance read rather than button press. The shell owns the Mix feature's verbs (usePaneRouter.ts:215-225 names Clear/Mix/Copy-result) and reaches them through an untyped imperative channel (`PaneActionRefs`, three `Ref<any>`, usePaneRouter.ts:107-111) that only the DESKTOP pane slots bind. On mobile, `mixPaneRef` is null while all three dock actions render and are visible, so `paneRefs.mix.value?.startMix?.()` is a guaranteed no-op — silenced by the `?.` masking fallback (edict 2).
defects.evidence: Live read of App.vue's setupState via `document.querySelector('[data-v-app]').__vue_app__._instance`. Mobile 390x844, /#/mix, clean load + 4s settle, pane fully rendered (pane-header-title="Mix", both tabs, both selects, Mix button present): `{layout:"mobile", currentView:"mix", mixPaneRef:"null", generatePaneRef:"null", gradientPaneRef:"null", colorPickerRef:"null", actionBar:"BAR:Tools", dockLabels:["Clear","Mix","Copy result"]}`. Desktop 1440x900, same route, same read: `{layout:"desktop", mixPaneRef:["clearSelection","startMix","copyResult"], exposedOk:true, canvases:3}`. Static mechanism: App.vue:319 declares mixPaneRef; App.vue:331 is its ONLY assignment, inside onDesktopRightMount; App.vue:83-91 the mobile PaneSlot passes no `:on-mount` while App.vue:105,131 do; Dock.vue:153-157 renders GenericActionBar with no breakpoint gate; usePaneRouter.ts:220-222 the three `?.` masks.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency — the shell names a feature's verbs and reaches into its instance imperatively — combined with a masking fallback that converts a structural miswiring into silence.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 390x844, then evaluate: walk `document.querySelector('[data-v-app]').__vue_app__._instance` down `subTree.component` until `setupState` has `mixPaneRef`, and read it → null, while `[...document.querySelectorAll('button.action-button-wrapper')].map(b=>b.getAttribute('aria-label'))` → ["Clear","Mix","Copy result"]. Repeat at 1440x900 → mixPaneRef is a live instance. The asymmetry is the reproduction.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the imperative channel entirely (adopts pass A's F-9 / pass C's C-3 cure, now at confirmed severity). The mounted feature PUBLISHES its action descriptors — `provide(PANE_ACTIONS_KEY, …)` from MixPane, injected by Dock — so binding cannot be layout-conditional because the publisher is the component itself. `PaneActionRefs`, the three `Ref<any>`, the nine `?.` masks, `PaneSlot.onMount` and the desktop/mobile fork all delete together. It also makes `disabled` honest: today all three Mix dock actions are enabled at zero selection because the shell cannot see `canMix`.

defects.defect: Census correction to pass B's B-2, which reads "demo/palettes/mix.ts has 1 consumer, in another feature". The true count is three importers, and ZERO of them are in demo/palettes/. The module is named after a feature that does not use it and is wholly owned by demo/workbenches/mix/ — a library-grade N-ary color algebra homed in the wrong feature, which is also why the library's own test tree had to reach across into demo/.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "palettes/mix" demo/ src/ test/ e2e/ | grep -v node_modules` → demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:14 (type-only `LeftoverStrategy`), demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:21 (`mixColorSequence, mixPalettes, type LeftoverStrategy`), test/mix-v4.test.ts:4 (`import { mixColorSequence } from "../demo/palettes/mix"`). demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:92 is prose in a comment, not an import. Zero importers under demo/palettes/.
defects.mechanism: Wrong module home — unique semantic ownership violated by placement: the concept lives under a feature directory that has no stake in it.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above at HEAD c654824e; it returns exactly the four lines listed, three of which are imports.
defects.proposedCure: Split on the ownership seam (pass A's F-1, now unambiguous): `mixColorSequence` — pure weighted N-ary fold over `AnyColor` with zero palette semantics — ascends into src/color/operations.ts beside the binary `mixColors` and ships on the ./color subpath; `mixPalettes` + `LeftoverStrategy` descend into demo/workbenches/mix/mix.ts beside their only consumers. test/mix-v4.test.ts then splits too: its mixColorSequence half becomes a genuine library test under test/color/, discharging pass A's F-14 for this cone.

defects.defect: Census extension to pass A's F-12 ("4x duplicated pane chrome"). The pane shell is four INDEPENDENTLY duplicated layers, not one, recurring 5 / 3 / 11 / 9 times; and MixPane's own outermost wrapper is inert — it duplicates positioning and sizing that its child Card already provides.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'class="relative w-full mx-auto h-full min-w-0"' demo --include='*.vue'` → 5 (GradientPane:19, MixPane:61, GeneratePane:30, ExtractPane:2, ConfigSliderPane:98). `grep -rn 'flex flex-col gap-4 pb-4 px-4 sm:px-6 pt-2' demo --include='*.vue'` → 3 (GradientPane:24, MixPane:78, GeneratePane:35). `grep -rn "pane-scroll-fade" demo --include='*.vue'` → 11 host sites. `grep -rln "PaneHeader" demo --include='*.vue'` → 9 panes + the SFC. Inertness: MixPane.vue:61 wrapper carries `relative`, MixPane.vue:62 `<Card>` carries `relative` too, and the only absolutely-positioned descendant (MixAnimationCanvas.vue:32, `class="absolute inset-0 …"`) is the Card's child — so the Card is already its containing block; the wrapper additionally repeats w-full, h-full, min-w-0, all carried by the Card.
defects.mechanism: A missing module: the pane shell is a real component that was never minted, so nine call sites hand-assemble it. Compounded by pass A's F-10 — PaneHeader.vue's UNSCOPED `.pane-scroll-fade` rule (PaneHeader.vue:54) styles its SIBLINGS' root element, so a child defines the CSS contract of its parent's root.
defects.reproduction: Run the four greps above at HEAD c654824e; they return 5, 3, 11 and 9 hits respectively.
defects.proposedCure: The shell belongs to glass-ui as Card + CardHeader variants, not to a demo wrapper (edict 3 forbids minting one here; edict 4 says the design system owns it). PaneHeader.vue's own comment already names the producer successor — "until P3's ScrollCardHeader knobs land (BOOKED)" — and its unscoped .pane-scroll-fade rule is exactly the producer concern it claims to be. When that lands, all four duplicated layers collapse at once and MixPane.vue loses its outer <div> and its Card class bag with it.

defects.defect: MixConfigBar type-imports glass-ui's headless peer directly, bypassing the design system. glass-ui declares reka-ui a peer and owns every Select the demo renders (demo/ui/select/index.ts re-exports glass-ui's); the demo naming reka-ui is the last structural trace of the pre-glass primitive layer.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:15 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";`. Fleet-wide: `grep -rn 'from "reka-ui"' demo src` → 4 sites (GradientVisualizer.vue:28, MixConfigBar.vue:15, GenerateControls.vue:33, AuroraPane.vue:25), all the same AcceptableValue type import. Checked before claiming: reka-ui IS declared — `npm ls reka-ui` → `reka-ui@2.9.9` at top level (devDependencies) and `deduped` under @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 — so this is a layering defect, not an undeclared-dependency one.
defects.mechanism: Boundary crossed in the wrong direction: feature code reaching past its design system to the design system's own implementation detail (edict 4).
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'from "reka-ui"' demo src` at HEAD c654824e returns the four sites listed.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui's ./select re-exports the value type its own Select accepts; the demo imports it from glass-ui and never names reka-ui. reka-ui then leaves value.js's devDependencies entirely. Rides the standing glass-ui BH relay.

defects.defect: Dead published surface on the mix algebra, kept alive only by its own test, plus one word owning two unrelated concepts one directory apart. `PaletteMixOptions.weights` has zero production callers; the parameter, its three validation branches and their three error strings are reachable only from test/mix-v4.test.ts.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/mix.ts:25 declares `weights?: number[]`. `grep -rn "weights" demo/ test/ | grep -v node_modules` → definition + internal plumbing at demo/palettes/mix.ts:25,44,47,50,51,53,58,60,115,141; test-only callers at test/mix-v4.test.ts:9,45; and a DIFFERENT concept at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:34,38,44,55,56. The sole production caller, useMixingState.ts:92-96, builds the options object with space/hueMethod/leftoverStrategy only, so mixPalettes always forwards undefined. Name collision: PaletteColor.weight (demo/palettes/types.ts:11) is a quantizer population share; PaletteMixOptions.weights is a per-palette blend ratio; nothing relates them.
defects.mechanism: Surface without an owner — an API kept alive by its test rather than by a consumer (edict 2), and a vocabulary collision that makes the two unrelated concepts look like one.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "weights" demo/ test/ | grep -v node_modules` at HEAD c654824e returns exactly the lines above; no line under demo/ outside demo/palettes/mix.ts passes a weights argument.
defects.proposedCure: Under D-5's split, mixColorSequence ascends into src/color/ WITH its weighted fold intact — weights are genuinely part of an N-ary mix's contract and belong in the library. The demo-side pass-through nobody calls, PaletteMixOptions.weights, deletes. One concept keeps the word.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the library publishes two mutually incompatible failure algebras (`{ok,error}` on ./color vs `{ok,diagnostics}` on ./css), proven by executing the committed dist: `parseCssColor('color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)')` returns `{ok:false, diagnostics:[…]}` and `r.error.code` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'code')`. It is the only pass-D finding at the library's OWN published surface — this seat's actual subject — and it is the root cause beneath pass A's F-4: the demo did not erase failure-explicitness by carelessness, it wrote two different unwrap adapters eight lines apart (picker-color.ts:104-107 and :110-114) because the library ships two answers to "what does failure look like". NOTE: the strongest defect OVERALL across all four passes remains pass C's C-1 (BLOCKER, colors mode has no working entry point), which pass D independently reproduced and does not displace — a feature with no entry point outranks an API that forces two adapters.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but one sub-area of this seat's charter is genuinely SOUND and is recorded so no later pass re-files it. **The demo consumes @mkbabb/value.js correctly, through the published subpath export map only — there is no import a real downstream consumer could not write.** Positive evidence: (1) `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value\.js"' demo src` → 0 hits — no bare-root import, and package.json#exports declares no "." key, so none would resolve; (2) `grep -rn 'from "@src' demo --include='*.vue' --include='*.ts'` → 0 hits — no reach into the source tree (the @src alias survives only for assets/docs reference pages and vitest); (3) subpath census `grep -rho '@mkbabb/value\.js/[a-z]*' demo | sort | uniq -c` → /color 25, /css 10, /math 6, /easing 5, /quantize 4 — five real exports keys, zero phantom specifiers; (4) resolution verified rather than assumed, `tsc --traceResolution` on the real file demo/color-session/picker-color.ts → `'@mkbabb/value.js/color' … resolved to …/dist/subpaths/color.d.ts` and `'@mkbabb/value.js/css' … resolved to …/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts with Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'` — both land on the published dist trust boundary. Related negative, also positively proven: ./value and ./transform are unused by the demo but are NOT dead keys — node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js/dist/engine/index.js:7-8 imports both, so every one of the seven published subpaths has a real consumer; the correct narrower statement is that the demo's consumer-truth proof covers 5 of 7. Finally, a WITHDRAWN pass-D finding recorded as a negative: I measured `colorPickerRef === null` at both layouts and did not file it, because `.picker-shell` was absent and `<main class="pane-main">` was rendering the U-F58 error boundary (console: `404 … /demo/color-session/color-utils.ts`) — the picker had not mounted, so the null was a consequence, not a structural binding gap; the shipped capture shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows a healthy picker with a live Tools control. D-1 survives the same test — the Mix pane rendered completely in both layouts and the desktop read of the identical expression returned a live instance.

defects.defect: ROOT CAUSE (new, not in passes A/B): glass-ui commit `490cc46e` deleted `WatercolorDot`'s `tag` prop, its `:is`/`:type` host binding, and its default `<slot/>` in one cut; value.js adopted Glass 7 whole without migrating 25 surviving `tag="…"` bindings across 12 demo files. Every Mix-pane seam failure (dead add slot, dead palette swatches, dropped `data-mix-target`, dropped `<Plus>`, dropped `title`) is this one producer regression.
defects.evidence:
`cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui && git show 490cc46e -- src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue | grep '^-' | grep -i 'tag\|slot'` →
70:-        /** Host tag — `div` (decorative) or `button` (interactive). */
71:-        tag?: "div" | "button";
79:-        tag: "div",
131:-        :is="tag"
133:-        :type="tag === 'button' ? 'button' : undefined"
197:-        <slot />
`git log --oneline -5 -- src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue` → a77ae9fe "restore live-consumer props a stale census mis-cut" / f04f05d8 "close BJ.W-REDUCE-PROPDIET" / 490cc46e "land the Glass 7 … public-surface cut". Shipped surface: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` — props only `color|variant|animate|cycleDuration|range|seed`, `inheritAttrs:!1` consuming only attrs.class/attrs.style, root `<span aria-hidden="true" style="…pointer-events:none">`, no `<slot/>`.
defects.mechanism: Producer public-surface cut + unmigrated consumers, made soundless by Vue silently dropping unknown props and `inheritAttrs:false` swallowing listeners/attrs; `vue-tsc` does not type-check attr fall-through on such a component. f04f05d8's own message names the trap ("passed only because Vue drops unknown props — the stale-binding no-op trap") and a77ae9fe already reversed the same class of mis-cut.
defects.reproduction: `git show 490cc46e -- src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue` in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui; then `grep -rn 'tag="button"\|tag="div"' demo --include=*.vue | wc -l` → 25 in the value.js tree.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox citing the a77ae9fe precedent. Architecturally, do NOT restore `tag`: the dot is decorative pigment, interactivity belongs to the consumer — wrap it in a real `<button aria-label=…>` (the shape MixSourceSelector.vue:127-159 already uses for chips) with the dot left `pointer-events:none` so the button owns hit area and accessible name. Sweep all 25 sites; delete the now-meaningless `tag`/`title` bindings.

defects.defect: Colors mode cannot accept a single operand: both add affordances (the add-slot ghost, MixSourceSelector.vue:164-176, and the per-palette swatches, :211-221) render as aria-hidden, pointer-events:none `<span>`s with no click handler, no accessible name, and the slotted `<Plus>` glyph discarded. The Mix button is therefore `disabled` forever. Third-seat confirmation of passes A/B on independent instruments.
defects.evidence: Live at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: `[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]` count = 0; add slot = {tag:"SPAN", ariaHidden:"true", ariaLabel:null, title:null, pointerEvents:"none", hasSvgChild:false, rect 48×48}. Click probe: elementFromPoint at the slot centre returns {tag:"DIV", cls:"swatch-row flex items-center gap-2.5 flex-wrap"} (the PARENT), chipsBefore 0 → chipsAfter 0. Palette swatches: {paletteSwatchCount:4, firstSwatch:{tag:"SPAN", pe:"none", ariaLabel:null}, chipsAfter:0}. Full pane button census in colors mode: Colors, Palettes, "From palettes2", OKLab, Shorter, {"t":"Mix","disabled":true}. defects.mechanism: R-0 (producer cut) + Vue's silent drop of unknown props/attrs on an `inheritAttrs:false` component.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/mix in colors mode; click the dashed 'add' blob in the Selected well — nothing happens; `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]').length === 0`; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost')).pointerEvents === 'none'`.
defects.proposedCure: Per R-0: a real `<button type="button" :aria-label>` wrapping the decorative dot, with the `<Plus>` as a sibling child of the button; move `.add-slot-ghost`'s flex-centering to the button.

defects.defect: `[data-mix-target]` never exists at runtime, so the convergence never lands on the announced destination; `mixStage.ts:121-124`'s `targetEl ? … : {clientWidth/2, scrollHeight*0.7, r:28}` fallback is not an edge case but the sole determinant of where the animation goes. The fallback is itself a forbidden masking fallback — it is why a total structural break rendered as a plausible animation for a whole tranche.
defects.evidence: 14 samples at ~100 ms across a complete palettes-mode mix, measured live: `[data-mix-target]` = 0 at t=101,201,301,402,503,604,705,806,907,1009,1110,1211,1312,1412 ms (ghost plate present 101–806, gone from 907 — the 900 ms clock is correct, the choreography is not). Source: MixResultDisplay.vue:64-73 stamps `data-mix-target` on a `WatercolorDot`, which discards it (R-0).
defects.mechanism: R-0 attribute swallowing, hidden by a masking fallback that converts a missing destination into a computed guess instead of failing loudly.
defects.reproduction: Seed two local palettes, open /#/mix, switch to Palettes, select both, click Mix, and poll `document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-target]').length` every 100 ms for 1.5 s → 0 at every sample.
defects.proposedCure: Put the anchor on an element the producer cannot swallow (the wrapping button/div), AND delete the fallback branch so `collectStage` returns `null` when the destination is absent — `arm()` already settles honestly on `null` (useMixingAnimation.ts:149-154). No guess, ever.
