defects.defect: The mix path has no guard against a throwing parse. `parseColorIn` propagates a raw `TypeError` from the library parser (the R1 crash class), and every mix entry point calls it unguarded. Worst frame: `mixStage.ts:99-100` inside `pigmentRamp`, reached from `arm()` in a `flush:"post"` watcher AFTER `animationPhase` is already `"mixing"`.
defects.evidence: In-page against the running server: {"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)":"ok", "#aa3344":"ok", "oklab(0.5 0 0)":"ok", "oklch()":"TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')"}. Stack: at ae (dist/subpaths/css.js:265:17) → at T (css.js:354:13) → parsePickerColor (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:157:17) → parseColorIn (demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:5:28). Unguarded sites: useMixingState.ts:87; demo/palettes/mix.ts:78,86,94-97; mixStage.ts:99-100,106; color-utils.ts:18. No try/catch anywhere in MixPane.vue.
defects.mechanism: A partial function (`parseColorIn` throws; `picker-color.ts:112`) handed straight to a click handler over user/remote-authored CSS strings, with the failure landing inside a post-flush watcher that runs after the phase has already advanced.
defects.reproduction: Parse throw: PROVEN (pasted stack, in-page, at HEAD). The downstream STRANDING of the phase machine in `mixing` forever (startMix re-entry-guards at :83; the plate stays ghosted; its Reset button lives only in the non-ghost branch, MixResultDisplay.vue:76,136-142; sole escape = dock Tools ▸ Clear) is a HYPOTHESIS — mechanism read from source, not reproduced live because C-2 blocks the colors path and the palettes path throws earlier inside `startMix`.
defects.proposedCure: Make `startMix` total: validate/normalise operands once at the data seam with a result-typed parse, give `MixResult` an error species, retire the `*OrThrow` seam on this path; and wrap `collectStage` in `arm()` with a catch that joins the three existing settle-honestly arms so no throw can strand the machine. Hoist `Reset` out of the ghost/content Transition so no state can hide it.

defects.defect: NEW: the 'Stable keys for TransitionGroup' machinery in MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98 is anti-stable. Keys are derived from `${css}::${index}`, so removing one chip rekeys every survivor — TransitionGroup then plays leave on all chips and enter on all survivors instead of animating the one removal. Strictly worse than the naive `:key="i"` it replaces, and 20 lines of Map + counter + pruning watcher to achieve it.
defects.evidence:
Faithful transcription of :79-98 plus useMixingState.removeColor (:59-61), run with node (saved at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-pane/evidence/passC-keychurn.mjs):
initial        ["red","blue","lime"] keys = [ 0, 1, 2 ]
after remove#0 ["blue","lime"]       keys = [ 3, 4 ]
defects.mechanism: An index-derived key wearing the costume of an identity key, laundered through a Map + monotonic counter + prune watcher. KISS / no-contrivance edict violation.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-pane/evidence/passC-keychurn.mjs` — output above. The on-screen consequence is currently unreachable because C-2 makes chips unaddable; it becomes live the moment C-2 is fixed.
defects.proposedCure: Mint identity where the object is born: give `SelectedColor` an `id` in `useMixingState.addColor` (a monotonic counter suffices) and key on `sc.id`. Delete the map, the counter, the watcher and the computed (−20 lines).

result.strongestDefect: C-2/R-0 — the Mix workbench's colors mode cannot accept a single operand in the running application, and the cause is one dated producer commit (glass-ui `490cc46e`) that removed `WatercolorDot`'s interactive host (`tag`, `:is`/`:type`, `<slot/>`) from under 23 call sites with no compile-time or runtime signal. Measured live: `[aria-label="Add current color to the mix"]` count 0; host is `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events:none`; `elementFromPoint` at the slot centre returns the parent div; click → 0 chips; the `Mix` button is `disabled: true` forever; and the pane's own e2e fails at `expect(addSlot).toBeVisible()`.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the hazard-list clean sheet rather than a negative proof of soundness — recorded because it now carries three-seat agreement and bounds where the repair must NOT go. Checked and clean: no PRM-RAF site (useMixingAnimation.ts:88-114 rides glass-ui `useRAFLoop` with pauseWhenHidden, epilogue stop, missing-canvas stop, and onBeforeUnmount stop; `respectReducedMotion:false` is deliberate and correct because `arm()` completes rather than pauses, so PRM cannot strand the machine); no `defineModel` anywhere in demo/workbenches/mix/ (plain refs + explicit props/emits, so the stale-read hazard is absent); no `ValueUnit` construction on this path; no HSV round-trip (pigmentRamp interpolates in the same space + hue method as the mix itself); no reka slider (no pointer-capture leak surface); no WebGL (Canvas2D radial gradients only, no `ctx.filter`, no engine branch — the "Safari-true by construction" docstring is accurate). The one-clock law holds in measurement: my ghost→inked transition landed between 806 ms and 907 ms against MIX_CONVERGE_MS = 900. Palettes-mode source controls are correct and are the pattern C-2's repair should copy (native `<button type="button">` with aria-pressed and a real aria-label; measured "Select palette Audit Alpha" and `[data-mix-source]` 0 → 2). MixConfigBar's "sampling costs nothing at rest" claim holds (spaceRamps/hueRamps are lazy computeds read only inside SelectContent, which reka unmounts when closed). `mixPalettes` emits `position` on every result colour (demo/palettes/mix.ts:142). A slug-collision hypothesis against the K-PALID selection keying was formed and KILLED by reading `createSlug` (demo/palettes/utils.ts:14-16 appends a UUID suffix, so two "Mixed Palette" saves cannot collide). Not settled: pass A's C-7 (keyboard operability of the overflow-y-auto Card at a scrolling viewport) — I did not probe it either, so after three seats it remains un-corroborated; a fourth should measure it or the fleet should retire it as unverified. Environment caveat recorded in the report: late in the session EVERY pane (Mix and Generate alike) began booting into the shell error boundary with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')" with localStorage restored to its original keys — because it reproduces on Generate it is NOT a MixPane defect and is not reported as one; all measurements above were taken before that state.

result.axis: design (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context), model id claude-opus-5[1m] — declared, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: DC-2 / A-D-5 as one mechanism: the design placed activation, accessible naming, disabled state and a layout anchor on `WatercolorDot` — a producer primitive glass-ui 7.0.0 enforces as decorative (`inheritAttrs: false`, hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true">` root, inline `pointer-events: none`, no slot). At the entry end this makes /#/mix's DEFAULT mode unusable: both add-a-color paths are inert (measured span/pointer-events:none/aria-label null; a real mouse click leaves chipCount 0 and Mix permanently disabled). At the exit end `[data-mix-target]` never reaches the DOM (measured targetAnchorPresent: false), so the pane's signature convergence lands on mixStage.ts's invented fallback point inside an operand card. The finding behind the finding: no gate this project owns can see the difference between a working WatercolorDot consumer and an inert one — vue-tsc green, vitest green, console clean, and the Safari harness photographs a dead end and reports zero defects.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict, but recorded so no later seat re-litigates: (1) prefers-reduced-motion is exemplary — sampled at t+120ms with reducedMotion:"reduce", {ghost:false, plate:true}; useMixingAnimation.ts:70-72 gates on the media query and :120-125 fires onSettled() synchronously, with respectReducedMotion:false on the host deliberately correct per its own docstring :29-36. (2) Motion fully tokenised — both Transitions key vj-morph, both TransitionGroups key vj-enter (animations.css:82-137, --duration-*/--spring-*/--ease-*); no fourth family, no bespoke keyframes; the only scoped transition is opacity-only (MixResultDisplay.vue:152-157); vj-morph's max-height is opt-in via --vj-morph-collapse/-expanded, unset at every Mix site, so nothing layout-forcing interpolates. (3) RTL mirrors cleanly — left x199→729, right x729→199, well x754→224, widths unchanged, overflowX 0. (4) overflowX 0 in all four Safari matrices and in my LTR/RTL/zoom probes. (5) Zero pageErrors/consoleErrors/failedRequests on /#/mix in all four matrices and all five of my probes — every defect found is SILENT. (6) forced-colors: .dashed-well survives as black-dashed on white. (7) verbatimModuleSyntax clean across all six files. (8) Vue 3.5 idioms correct — reactive props destructure ×4, useTemplateRef, toRef(()=>prop). (9) Not a god module: 123 lines, four children, one composable. (10) The state machine is honest — no timers, one forward edge, re-entry guard.

defects.defect: Mobile and 200% zoom: the committed mix result renders outside every scrollable extent. MixPane.vue:62's Card is `h-full overflow-y-auto`, making the pane its own scroll container; the document never scrolls, so no gesture reveals the result.
defects.evidence: WebKit iPhone 14 (390x664), Palettes mode, 2 operands, Mix pressed, settled 2.2s: card.scrollHeight 791 / clientHeight 550; card.scrollTop 0; document.scrollHeight 664 === innerHeight 664; plate.bottom - card.bottom = +223.8px. Reflow arm 720x450@2dpr (states.mjs:21 convention): document.scrollHeight 450 === innerHeight 450, card.scrollHeight 426 / clientHeight 336 (90px trapped). Frame: scratchpad chD-mix-mobile-settled.png (fullPage:true) shows RESULT sheared at the card edge. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32 (§3 law 6) 'Mobile uses one document-scrolling stage->inspector->action sequence'; :48 binds Mix mobile order to 'operand rack, result, controls' while MixPane.vue:78-119 ships rack->controls->result.
defects.mechanism: The pane is its own scroll box — no region model, so 'where the result appears' is wherever a scrolling flex column happens to end. Same missing-housing family as pass A D-1 / pass B DB-1, but this arm is unrecoverable by the user.
defects.reproduction: iPhone 14 context (or any viewport <=664px tall) -> http://localhost:9000/#/mix -> Palettes tab -> select two palettes -> click Mix -> wait 2s. Evaluate: document.scrollHeight === innerHeight (true), card.scrollTop === 0, .mix-plate bottom is 223.8px past the card's visible bottom.
defects.proposedCure: The Card sheds `h-full overflow-y-auto` and content-hugs; the document scrolls. Re-sequence to rack -> result -> controls per canon, placing the outcome adjacent to the operands that produced it. Under pass A's InstrumentChassis cure the result becomes #inspector and this dissolves — but the cure's pi MUST carry the 390px and 720x450@2 arms or the chassis will inherit the same inner-scroller habit.

defects.defect: The convergence choreography has no destination: `data-mix-target` never reaches the DOM, so mixStage.ts always takes its invented fallback point and the pigment drops land inside an operand card instead of the announced result well.
defects.evidence: Measured mid-mix (Palettes mode, 2 operands, 1440x900, +320ms): {ghost: true, targetAnchorPresent: false} where targetAnchorPresent = !!document.querySelector('[data-mix-target]'). Source: MixResultDisplay.vue:63-73 passes data-mix-target to a <WatercolorDot>; mixStage.ts:120-123 falls back to {x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r:28}. Visual: scratchpad chD-mix-midmix.png — drops suspended inside the Ocean operand card at y~600-680 while the ghost well sits at y~1090. Producer contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js has `inheritAttrs: !1`, root tag hard-coded "span", hard-coded aria-hidden="true", inline pointerEvents:"none", and consumes only attrs.class + attrs.style; WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts declares only {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}. Falsified design claims: MixPane.vue:63-66, :107-110; MixResultDisplay.vue:14-18.
defects.mechanism: A DOM contract expressed through a component that discards DOM contracts. The asymmetry is the design defect: the SOURCE anchors work (MixSourceSelector.vue:130-132 puts data-mix-source/-color on a plain wrapper div; measured sources: 2) — only the TARGET was hung on a WatercolorDot.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix -> Palettes tab -> select two palettes -> click Mix -> within 900ms evaluate !!document.querySelector('[data-mix-target]') -> false.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: move data-mix-target onto the <div> that already wraps the ghost dot (MixResultDisplay.vue:63) — the exact construction the source side already uses. Gestalt: every WatercolorDot in this feature becomes a face INSIDE a named geometric seat that owns name/state/anchors/focus, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91's abrogation. Eight call sites.

defects.defect: The pane's declared dock action set is structurally unreachable on /#/mix, so there is no way to clear the operand rack at all, and MixPane's copyResult/writeClipboard is dead code rather than a live second path.

Dead surfaces: usePaneRouter.ts:216-224 (Clear/Mix/Copy result), MixPane.vue:57 defineExpose, MixPane.vue:12,49-55 writeClipboard+copyResult. The live Copy is MixResultDisplay.vue:5,31 useClipboard({resetMs:1500}).
defects.mechanism: A v-if/v-else-if pair whose first arm is unconditionally satisfied on this route. Generate and Gradient escape it only because their VIEW_MAP rows do not put the picker in the left slot. This CORRECTS pass A D-8's stated mechanism ('Dock routes to the silent one').
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 1440x900 -> click Tools -> enumerate rendered dock buttons; the mix set never appears.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientCodeEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 + L-16 as a chain. The published `@mkbabb/value.js/css` surface declares `parseCssColor` TOTAL via `ParseResult<T>` and ships a PARTIAL implementation — `src/css/grammar.ts:181` asserts `slash[0]!` on an empty `splitTopLevel("")`, so `oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )'` all throw TypeError. Seven demo call sites correctly trust the type and do not guard. Typing `oklch()` mid-edit in this code editor destroys BOTH panes and every unsaved gradient, the component's entire designed failure affordance (`parseVerdict` rail, destructive border, aria-invalid) never fires because a throw is not a verdict, and the boundary is sticky across hash navigation. L-16 then extends the blast radius off-route: because `debouncedParse` is never cancelled on unmount, the 500 ms timer fires after the user has navigated away and destroys the MIX workbench — an unrelated pane the user is actively looking at. Both reproduced live from a fresh page load.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but the following are genuine, evidence-backed negatives so the verdict is not read as "everything is wrong". (1) The subject's OWN import graph is boundary-clean: `vue`, one relative demo import, one npm package — no feature→shell edge, no component→boot edge, no demo→src internal; `grep -rn "@src" demo --include="*.ts" --include="*.vue"` → 0 hits. (2) Every demo import of the library uses a specifier a real external consumer could write — only the published subpaths `/color` (24), `/css` (10), `/math` (6), `/easing` (5), `/quantize` (4); zero deep paths, zero bare-root imports. (3) The parse path's ownership split is correct and well-argued: `gradientParse.ts:16-18` delegates color/scalar validity to the library ("the demo never hand-validates a color") and keeps only the comma-grouping segmentation the library's flat FunctionValue stream cannot express. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied — all four subject imports bind runtime values. (5) Idiomatic Vue 3.5 — `useTemplateRef` at :31, reactive props destructure with default at :16; no `defineModel` deliberately, since the focus-gated editor truce requires one-way prop + event. (6) Edict 6 honored — the `#hljs-gradient-theme` head-injection was MOVED to static `demo/styles/hljs.css`, not deleted, and correctly killed a second dark store. (7) The prior pass's claim that `cn` has zero call sites re-verified: `grep -rln "\bcn(" demo` → 1 file, its own definition. (8) The vite self-alias set genuinely IS generated from `package.json#exports` with anchored regexes (`vite.config.ts:38-49`) — the runtime resolution posture is correctly built; it is only the TypeScript half that drifted (L-13).

defects.defect: The published `@mkbabb/value.js/css` surface declares `parseCssColor` TOTAL (`ParseResult<T>` = ok|diagnostics, i.e. never throws) and ships a PARTIAL implementation that throws TypeError on every empty-argument color function. Seven demo call sites correctly trust the type and do not guard. Reaching this component, it destroys the entire two-pane application.
defects.evidence: Contract: src/css/types.ts:25. Defect site: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space");` — for an empty body `splitTopLevel("","/")` returns [] so `slash[0]` is undefined and the `!` lies. Against the BUILT artifact: `node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCssColor} from './dist/subpaths/css.js'..."` → "oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" all -> THROWS TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); stack `at ae (dist/subpaths/css.js:265:17) at T (dist/subpaths/css.js:354:13)`. Note "oklch(" (unbalanced) correctly returns ok=false — the parser is total on INCOMPLETE input and partial on COMPLETE-but-empty input, exactly what a human types. Trusting call sites: gradientParse.ts:93, useImageSampler.ts:58, useMarkdownColors.ts:31, picker-color.ts:110, view-accent.ts:28, ink.ts:39; none wraps in try.
defects.mechanism: A public API whose TYPE asserts totality while its IMPLEMENTATION uses non-null assertions to skip the degenerate arm. The `!` is the defect generator; grammar.ts carries dozens more, each an undischarged totality proof on a surface whose type says none exist.

defects.proposedCure: Make the arm real and abolish the class, in the library — never by wrapping the seven demo call sites in try/catch, which would make the demo carry the library's broken contract (the inverted dependency this seat exists to find). At grammar.ts:177-181 add `if (slash.length === 0) return failure(source, "css_syntax", ["color components"]);` and drop the `!`. Then enforce structurally: `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion` as an ERROR for `src/css/**`. A ParseResult-returning module is precisely where `!` may not appear.

defects.defect: UPGRADE of prior-pass L-9 from MINOR/HYPOTHESIS to MAJOR/CONFIRMED. `debouncedParse` is never cancelled on unmount, so the 500 ms timer fires after the user has navigated away — converting L-1 from a bounded in-pane crash into an arbitrary-route crash that destroys a DIFFERENT workbench.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62 creates `debounce((text)=>emit("parse",text),500)`; `debounce` returns `.cancel()` (demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41); the component never calls it and has no onBeforeUnmount. The codebase knows the discipline elsewhere — demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383-384 and demo/color-session/useColorPersistence.ts:116 both cancel. The pane is lazily mounted/unmounted per route (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74,87).
defects.mechanism: A lifetime-unaware timer utility used inside a component lifetime. A `.cancel()` that must be REMEMBERED is not an invariant; the hand-rolled debounce cannot know about the Vue effect scope.
defects.reproduction:

Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')

Try again"}`. The MIX workbench is destroyed by a keystroke typed into the GRADIENT workbench. Control probe, identical navigation with valid text "linear-gradient(45deg, red, blue)": `{windowErrors:[], mainHasBoundary:false}` — so the cross-route damage is specifically L-1 arriving after unmount, where no boundary owns the throwing subtree.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `demo/shared/utils.ts#debounce` entirely and migrate all nine call sites to `useDebounceFn` from `@vueuse/core` — already a live dependency, already imported by six demo files (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:12, ColorPicker.vue:123, Dock.vue:16, useColorPersistence.ts:2, useAtmosphere.ts:23, usePaletteStore.ts:1). It binds to the effect scope and cancels on unmount BY CONSTRUCTION, retiring the finding class rather than adding one more onBeforeUnmount the next component will forget. End state is not `demo/shared/debounce.ts` but NO demo-owned debounce, leaving `demo/shared/cn.ts` — one module, one concept, the existing shared/ dir narrowed rather than a new one invented.

defects.defect: The component hand-rolls the design system's control surface and state ladder. Both prior passes censused only glass-ui's 74 export SUBPATHS and concluded no code-field primitive exists — correct but incomplete: glass-ui ships a CSS control layer carrying the exact contract this component re-implements. This sharpens the MT-F037/OM-13 glass-forward ask from 'build a new ladder' to 'unpin the existing one'.

Against GradientCodeEditor.vue:93-97: `rounded-lg glass-wash border … focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40` + `:class="[hasError ? 'border-destructive' : 'border-border/40']"` + an inline `:style` transition — line-for-line the same contract on a different, partly-empty token set. The component ALREADY emits `:aria-invalid="hasError || undefined"` (line 92), so glass's selector would fire for free. Component census: ./forms exports Input (native <input>, props only, no slot/asChild), Textarea (native), Combobox; ./labeled-field yields controlId/labelledBy/describedBy but never the control; ./surface is a plate. OM-13 witness read: a rounded-rect wash with `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` in Fira + two trailing ghost icons, implemented at GradientEasingEditor.vue:176-198 as `div.rounded-md.bg-well.px-2.py-1` + hand-rolled `.rail-btn`.

Two blockers only: `.input-pill` is hard-pinned to `border-radius: var(--radius-pill)`, and nothing seats a non-native control in it.

One `Field`/`ControlSurface` in ./forms carrying the EXISTING .input-pill ladder, decoupled from <input> and from the pill radius: (a) `asChild`/default slot so a contenteditable or a <code> row wears the certified surface; (b) a `radius` token prop (pill|lg|card); (c) leading/trailing adornment slots for the copy + tune icons. One primitive discharges OM-13/MT-F037, this component's chrome, its focus ring (L-14), and the three parallel contenteditable sites (GradientCodeEditor.vue:88, ColorInput.vue:13 at 377 lines, ColorComponentDisplay.vue:23 at 214 lines). Adoption deletes GradientCodeEditor.vue:94 and :95-97 outright.

defects.defect: The focus ring resolves to the wrong ink: `--ring`/`--color-ring` are EMPTY at :root, so `focus-visible:ring-ring/40` silently degrades to `currentcolor` and paints a hard opaque near-black ring instead of a 40%-alpha token. It is a FOURTH focus idiom in a folder whose two siblings use the certified house recipe, and an exact recurrence of a defect the house recipe's own docblock records as cured.
defects.evidence: Measured live on the focused editor: `--tw-ring-color: (EMPTY)`, `--tw-ring-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(2px + 0px) currentcolor`, resolved `boxShadow: rgb(28, 25, 23) 0px 0px 0px 2px`, `outline: none`, `matchesFocusVisible: true`. At :root — `--ring: (EMPTY)`, `--color-ring: (EMPTY)`, while `--focus-ring-inner: rgba(0,0,0,0.85)`, `--focus-ring-outer: rgba(255,255,255,0.92)` and glass's `--focus-ring-color: oklch(47.1% 0.188 9.8deg)` all resolve. demo/styles/focus-ring.css:11-13 documents this exact failure as cured: 'the --ring/--color-ring token it reached resolved EMPTY — so even an un-clobbered ring painted nothing.' The cure is in use two files away: GradientStopEditor.vue:346-347 (`0 0 0 1px var(--focus-ring-inner), 0 0 0 3px var(--focus-ring-outer)`) and GradientEasingEditor.vue:230,287 (`box-shadow: var(--focus-ring-shadow)`). `grep -rn "focus-visible:ring-" demo --include="*.vue" | wc -l` → 27 sites all silently downgraded.
defects.mechanism: Tailwind v4 compiles `ring-ring/*` against `--color-ring`; when that custom property is undefined the ring falls back to currentcolor rather than failing loudly. A design token that resolves empty is a silent downgrade — the precise failure mode a token system exists to prevent — and four idioms for one concept mean no single place can fix it.
defects.reproduction: Fresh load of http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; focus the editor via `el.focus()`; read `getComputedStyle(el)` for boxShadow / --tw-ring-color / --tw-ring-shadow / outline, and `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` for --ring / --color-ring / --focus-ring-inner / --focus-ring-outer / --focus-ring-color. Outputs pasted above.
defects.proposedCure: Adopting the L-15 Field primitive deletes line 93's ring clause and inherits one certified affordance. Independently and immediately: lint-ban the `ring-ring` class literal across demo/ via `no-restricted-syntax`, so the remaining 26 downgraded sites surface rather than degrading in silence.

defects.defect: A second CSS grammar ships to lex the very string the library's own CSS parser then reads, and the two disagree exactly on the L-1 input class. Carried forward from the prior pass (its L-5) with a complementary development-cost measurement; the prior pass's shipped figure remains authoritative.
defects.evidence: GradientCodeEditor.vue:5-8 statically imports `highlight.js/lib/core` + `/lib/languages/css` and calls `hljs.registerLanguage("css", css)` at module scope. Development cost served by the live dev server: node_modules/.vite/deps/highlight__js_lib_core.js = 57,066 B + highlight__js_lib_languages_css.js = 15,967 B = 73,033 B. Prior pass's authoritative SHIPPED figure (bundled+minified+gz) = 12,670 B; I could not re-derive it — dist/gh-pages/assets/index-*.js is a 698-byte stub from a failed build. Honest scoping: the gradient pane is lazily routed (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74 defineAsyncComponent), so this is chunk weight, not eager boot weight. The library cannot supply the need today: src/subpaths/css.ts exports only whole-value parsers (parseCssColor, parseCssScalar, parseCssValue, parseStylesheet…) with NO positional token stream.
defects.mechanism: A missing library surface, not a mis-import — a highlighter cannot be built on the published API, so a third-party grammar was the only available move. The consequence is semantic, not just weight: highlight.js tokenizes `oklch()` as a valid function and paints it as correct code at the same instant value.js detonates on it.
defects.reproduction: `wc -c node_modules/.vite/deps/highlight__js_lib_core.js node_modules/.vite/deps/highlight__js_lib_languages_css.js`; `cat src/subpaths/css.ts` (no tokenizer export); disagreement shown by the L-1 repro (editor ink says the text is fine while the parser throws).
defects.proposedCure: Library-forward: add `tokenizeCss(source): readonly {kind, start, end}[]` to /css. It retires the third-party grammar, makes highlighter and validator agree BY CONSTRUCTION (one grammar, one truth), removes the innerHTML sink of L-10 (spans render as vnodes), and turns the demo into a real proof of the library's CSS surface instead of a proof of highlight.js's.

defects.mechanism: A consumer zeroed a CSS property that the design system uses as a STATE CHANNEL, not merely as decoration. The design gate is then satisfied by the defect it should be measuring — an inversion (moot today only because per N-1 the clause never executes).

defects.defect: @mkbabb/value.js/easing does not export the Result type it returns, so all three consumers hand-roll the unwrap-or-throw adapter and the two TypeScript ones cannot name their own parameter type.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "Result" src/subpaths/*.ts` → only `src/subpaths/css.ts:21: ParseResult` and `src/subpaths/color.ts:9: Result`. src/subpaths/easing.ts exports 5 types + 16 values and NO result type, yet CubicBezier/steppedEase/easing/linearEasing all return Result<EasingFunction, EasingIssue> (src/easing.ts:145). Three adapters exist: easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 `function easingValue(result: ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>, source: string): EasingFunction`; useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 byte-similar, differing only in the error prefix; glass-ui dist/easing.js:12-15 `function U(e,t){ if(!t.ok) throw Error(...); return t.value }`. Both demo sites then pass OTHER constructors through the CubicBezier-typed parameter — easingCatalogue.ts:137 passes steppedEase(n,position); useGradientCSS.ts:110-116 passes easing(), steppedEase(), linearEasing().
defects.mechanism: Published-surface hole. Three subpaths, three different result-type disclosure policies in one package (/color publishes Result, /css publishes ParseResult, /easing publishes neither). Forced to spell a type as another function's return type, the code typechecks only because the four Result instantiations are structurally identical today; widening EasingIssue for one constructor breaks every call site with an error naming CubicBezier. Two byte-similar copies in one demo tree is also plain duplicate ownership (edicts 1/3).

defects.proposedCure: Re-export Result (EasingIssue is already exported) from src/subpaths/easing.ts and ship the unwrap as library API — an EasingResult<T> alias plus expectEasing(result, context): EasingFunction. Three deletions, one home; strictly the smallest of all the cures and it removes a type-level footgun from the published surface.

defects.defect: /css and /easing disagree on the TYPE of a linear-easing stop inside one package, so value.js parses a CSS production it cannot evaluate — and the CSS Easing L2 inference algorithm is orphaned in a gradient workbench composable.
defects.evidence: src/css/types.ts:28-31 `export type CssLinearStop = Readonly<{ output: number; input: readonly [] | readonly [number] | readonly [number, number] }>` (what parseTimingFunction produces, via CssTimingFunction's `linear-function` arm at :36). src/easing.ts:14 `export type LinearEasingStop = Readonly<{ output: number; input: number }>` and :145 `export function linearEasing(stops: readonly LinearEasingStop[])` (what the evaluator consumes). The bridge lives at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:79-103 (`linearStops`, 25 lines implementing first→0 / last→1 / non-decreasing clamp / linear interpolation of omitted-position runs / double-position split) and :106-117 (`timingFunctionValue`, the 4-arm switch). Nothing in those 47 lines is gradient-specific; both input and output types are value.js's own. glass-ui carries no second copy — useEasingPicker only round-trips parseTimingFunction for its reparseOk flag (dist/easing.js:36-40) and never touches the linear-function arm.
defects.mechanism: Missing published join between two halves of the same package, expressed as a type mismatch rather than as prose. The next consumer will re-implement the inference rules because they cannot find them four directories inside a demo feature.

defects.proposedCure: Add `evaluateTimingFunction(t: CssTimingFunction): Result<EasingFunction, EasingIssue>` to src/easing.ts, exported at @mkbabb/value.js/easing, owning the stop-inference internally so CssLinearStop never escapes /css. 47 lines move down one package; three call sites collapse to one. Pairs with serializeTimingFunction (pass-2 L-4) and easedRamp (pass-2 L-1) to close the parse→evaluate→sample→mix chain inside the library.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue is built eagerly at module scope, converting value.js's failure-explicit Results back into a module-eval throw that no ErrorBoundary can catch.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:198 `export const SPECIMEN_FAMILIES: SpecimenFamily[] = buildFamilies();` is top-level; buildFamilies() calls bezierTile/stepsTile → easingValue(), which throws at :103 and :137. Cost is NOT the issue — measured equivalent work against the built library: 33 constructions + 33×49-sample glyph walks = 1.24 ms / 22,651 chars. value.js's own package.json#description is "Immutable, failure-explicit …"; every constructor returns a Result precisely so bad input is a value, not an exception.
defects.mechanism: Direction-of-dependency fragility: the demo inverts the library's failure discipline AND places the inversion at module scope, where the route chunk evaluates it before any component mounts — outside the reach of the ErrorBoundary that catches the render-time sibling of the same throw (the L-1 crash). A future preset whose quad fails validation turns a caught pane error into a white screen.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the failure — no shipped preset fails validation today. The reachability is a HYPOTHESIS; the code shape is confirmed (easingCatalogue.ts:198 top-level; :103 and :137 throw).
defects.proposedCure: Make the catalogue lazy (computed/memoised getter), or better — consistent with N-5 — let it hold Results and let the render site decide. Under the greenfield lattice the whole file moves to glass-ui as <EasingGallery> and the question moves with it.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (r3) on demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientCodeEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm). The seat's declaration was explicit at spawn and matches what I observe; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: R15 — one keypress (drag-select `0.75 0.15 145`, Backspace) on the shipped default text throws through the unguarded debounced `emit("parse")` into `parseCssColor("oklch()")`, and because the app has exactly ONE ErrorBoundary wrapping the whole two-pane `<main>` (App.vue:50-140), the entire workspace is replaced — on every route, persisting across navigation — with zero console output.
result.negativeProof: Honest negatives measured this round (stated so no later seat re-chases them): (1) my Infinity-poisoning hypothesis is REFUTED — `parseCssScalar("1e400deg")` returns ok=false against dist, so no non-finite value can reach the model through the angle path; (2) the mid-typing gesture `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(` does NOT crash (r3-probe2.mjs tag G, editorGone:false) because parseGradientCSS rejects the unbalanced tail first — the crash requires a BALANCED empty colour function, i.e. a deletion, not forward typing; (3) the ErrorBoundary's accessibility behaviour is correct — activeElement after the crash is DIV[role=alert] with aria-live="assertive" (the defect is paint, not the a11y tree); (4) highlight.js is NOT on the boot critical path — usePaneRouter.ts:74 loads GradientPane via defineAsyncComponent(() => import(...)); (5) this component contributes ZERO nameless buttons and ZERO small tap targets to the visual REPORT's four gradient rows — it renders no button at all, and its editor is 462x80 with aria-label="Gradient CSS".

defects.defect: One keypress on the shipped default text destroys the entire workspace — both panes, every route — and it stays destroyed across navigation. Drag-select `0.75 0.15 145` in the editor, press Backspace once, and the text at rest is `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch() 0%, ...)`; the debounced parse throws and the app's only ErrorBoundary replaces all of `<main>`.

Structure: demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 opens and :140 closes ONE <ErrorBoundary> around the whole two-pane grid. Library oracle against the exact file the demo imports (vite.config.ts:37-50 aliases @mkbabb/value.js/css -> dist/subpaths/css.js): `node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCssColor} from './dist/subpaths/css.js'..."` throws TypeError for oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() hwb() 'hsl(  )' 'rgb( )' and 'oklch( / )' — 11 inputs, 3 beyond the registry's MT-F001 row of 8.
defects.mechanism: Partial library function treated as total: GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62 fires emit("parse") from a bare setTimeout -> GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 applyCSS -> gradientParse.ts:92-94 isColorToken -> src/css/grammar.ts:181 dereferences slash[0]! on an empty split. gradientParse's documented 'model-or-reject' contract honours values but not throws. Blast radius is set by App.vue's single app-wide boundary, whose `caught` state no route change resets.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/r3-probe4.mjs webkit (tag H2); also r3-probe3.mjs tag H1 (thirteen backspaces) and r3-probe5-keepalive.mjs (K2/K3).
defects.proposedCure: Three layers, none of them a local try/catch: (1) make parseCssColor total at src/css/grammar.ts:181 — the mega-tranche parser band's ruled total parser is exactly this acceptance criterion; (2) make gradientParse honour its own model-or-reject header for THROWS at its oracle call sites (isColorToken/angleToDegrees/percentValue), so a text-validation failure returns reject(...) and can never become an exception; (3) move the ErrorBoundary to the pane slot and reset it on route change so one pane's bug is not an app outage.

defects.defect: The crash surface the user actually sees is blank: a lone 'Try again' pill on the aurora. The alert icon, the message and the machine-truth line are in the DOM, computed visible, and are not painted.
defects.evidence: r3-probe6-blank-boundary.mjs: SVG rect{706,447,28,28} opacity 1 visibility visible; P 'This panel hit an unexpected error.' rect{498,487,445,36} color rgb(28,25,23) opacity 1; P 'undefined is not an object...' rect{488,535,464,46}; BUTTON ' Try again' rect{658,597,124,36}. r3-boundary-element.png (element-clipped) and r3-boundary-clip.png (600x240 viewport clip spanning all four children) show ONLY the button. r3-probe6c.mjs: -webkit-text-fill-color rgb(28,25,23) on both the paragraph and the button; no ancestor to <html> carries mask/filter/mix-blend/opacity<1/background-clip:text. r3-probe6d.mjs: elementsFromPoint at the message centre returns the P first (the canvas is pointer-events-none).
defects.mechanism: App.vue:11 mounts <canvas class="atmosphere-canvas absolute inset-0 ..."> as a positioned (position:absolute, z-index:auto) sibling BEFORE <main class="pane-main"> (App.vue:47), which is static. Per CSS painting order, positioned descendants with z-index:auto paint after in-flow content of the same stacking context, so the canvas covers every static box in <main>. Pane cards and the glass Button escape because they create their own stacking contexts; the ErrorBoundary fallback has no surface at all.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe6-blank-boundary.mjs then r3-probe6b.mjs (element + clip captures).
defects.proposedCure: Give the boundary fallback a real surface — the same card/plate every other pane content sits on — which fixes the paint by giving it a stacking context and stops it reading as a system dialogue. Land in ErrorBoundary.vue's template plus a stacking-context guarantee on .pane-main; do not patch with z-index whack-a-mole.

defects.defect: A keystroke that changes nothing destroys authored easing. Pressing Enter at the end of the editor leaves textContent byte-identical, yet the parse re-applies and every interval is re-seeded to the linear preset.
defects.evidence: r3-probe2.mjs: {"tag":"B0-easing-authored","headName":"1 → 2ease-out","railLiteral":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)"} then {"tag":"B2-enter-at-end-textContent-identical","textContentUnchanged":true,"after":{"headName":"1 → 2linear","railLiteral":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"},"easingSurvived":false}. Source: GradientCodeEditor.vue:59-62 submits on every input event; gradientParse.ts:295-298 re-seeds all intervals with linearInterval(); useGradientCSS.ts:147-162 (serializeGradient) has no CSS spelling for easing at all.
defects.mechanism: Two defects meet: (a) no change detection — onInput submits text that cannot have changed the model, and every successful parse is destructive (new stop ids, reset intervals, dropped selection); (b) the submitted string cannot carry easing, so the surface advertised as the round-trip readout is lossy by construction and loses state silently.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe2.mjs webkit (tags B0/B2): pick ease-out on interval 1→2, click the editor, End, Enter, wait 1.3s.
defects.proposedCure: Submit only when the text differs from the text that produced the current model (one lastSubmitted string held beside the debounce — no new module, no wrapper), and make applyCSS reconcile rather than replace: intervals whose endpoints are unchanged keep their authored curve. A no-op edit must be a no-op.

defects.defect: The standing cure filed for the un-cancelled debounce (r2 · R2: onBeforeUnmount(debouncedParse.cancel)) can never fire on the path that produces the bug — the panes are KeepAlive-cached, so navigation deactivates instead of unmounting.
defects.evidence: r3-probe5-keepalive.mjs K1: {"authored":"linear-gradient(45deg, red 0%, lime 40%, blue 100%)","editorRemovedFromDomWhileAway":true,"afterReturn":"linear-gradient(45deg, red 0%, lime 40%, blue 100%)","statePreserved":true}. Structure: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 wraps the pane in <KeepAlive :max="max">, demo/color-picker/App.vue:88 passes :max="9". GradientCodeEditor.vue:2 imports no lifecycle teardown hook at all; demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 exposes an unused .cancel().
defects.mechanism: KeepAlive deactivation is not unmount; onBeforeUnmount fires only on LRU eviction or teardown. A disposition written against the wrong hook ships a green diff and an unchanged defect — the cross-route crash (K2) still lands.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe5-keepalive.mjs (K1 proves state preservation; K2 shows the crash landing on #/mix).
defects.proposedCure: onDeactivated(debouncedParse.cancel) AND onBeforeUnmount(debouncedParse.cancel) — both, using the .cancel() that already exists. Correct the filed R2 disposition before any wave consumes it.

defects.defect: The 'CSS' section shows one string and copies another, and the app's own copy cannot be re-ingested without damage: pasting it back explodes the model from 2 stops to 33.

at :253.
defects.mechanism: Two different serializations of one model are presented as one surface. The copied form also rewrites the authored literals (oklch(0.75 0.15 145) -> oklch(75% 0.15 145deg)), contradicting the literal-preservation law gradientParse.ts:18 advertises.

defects.proposedCure: One string per surface: either the editor edits exactly what Copy copies, or the Copy control names the form it copies and offers the other. A code readout that shows X and hands you Y is the one thing a code readout must not do.

defects.defect: CSS Color Level 4 `in <space> <hue> hue` — the exact syntax this pane's own Space and Hue selectors mean — is rejected, and for a valid angle followed by an interpolation clause the verdict blames the wrong token.
defects.evidence: r3-probe2.mjs tag D: 'linear-gradient(in oklch, red, blue)' -> verdict 'unparseable color "in"'; 'linear-gradient(90deg in oklch, red, blue)' -> verdict 'unparseable color "90deg"'; 'linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue, red, blue)' -> 'unparseable color "in"'. Source: gradientParse.ts:150-154 only accepts a bare angle when the first segment has exactly one token; GradientVisualizer.vue:181-210 ships the Space/Hue selectors whose CSS spelling this is.
defects.mechanism: The preamble grammar recognises only the shapes the model happens to store, so a superset of valid CSS falls through to the stop branch and is mis-reported as an unparseable colour. simpleCSS also never emits `in <space>`, so the string the editor shows renders a different gradient (sRGB interpolation) if pasted into a real stylesheet.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe2.mjs webkit (tag D, three inputs).
defects.proposedCure: Teach the preamble the L4 interpolation clause and have serializeGradient emit it, so the editor's text is the CSS that actually renders; and never let a fall-through path name a token it did not judge — a rejection must cite the token the rule actually failed on.

defects.defect: The editor is an unvalidated ingress into a bounded control: it writes a direction of 3.6e12 (or 1e308, or -720) into a slider declared min 0 / max 360, ending in an ARIA state the slider contract forbids.
defects.evidence: r3-probe4.mjs tag I: {'src':'linear-gradient(1e10turn, red, blue)','verdict':null,'readout':'3600000000000°','ariaValueNow':'3600000000000','ariaValueMax':'360'}; {'src':'linear-gradient(-720deg, ...)','ariaValueNow':'-720'}; {'src':'linear-gradient(1e308deg, ...)','readout':'1e+308°','ariaValueNow':'1e+308'}. Source: GradientVisualizer.vue:232 declares :min="0" :max="360"; gradientParse.ts:97-108 converts any accepted angle unit; useGradientModel.ts:165 assigns it; gradientParse.ts:281-283 clamps stop positions but nothing clamps direction.
defects.mechanism: 'Model-or-reject' guarantees structural completeness, not domain validity. aria-valuenow outside [aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax] fails WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value): AT is told a value outside the control's own range and arrow-key navigation cannot return to it.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe4.mjs webkit (tag I, three inputs).
defects.proposedCure: Normalise direction into the model's declared domain at the parse boundary (mod 360 for angles, as CSS itself does), so the one place that mints models cannot mint an invalid one. A complete model must also be a valid model.

defects.defect: A radial edit silently resets the direction the user set: 90° -> 0°, no verdict, and switching Type back to Linear does not restore it.
defects.evidence: r3-probe2.mjs tag F: {"directionBefore":"90°","directionAfter":"0°","verdict":null} after typing 'radial-gradient(red 0%, blue 100%)'. Source: useGradientCSS.ts:151-155 writes no angle for radial; gradientParse.ts:214 initialises direction = type === "linear" ? 180 : 0; useGradientModel.ts:164 assigns it unconditionally.
defects.mechanism: Same family as R17: a field the model still carries is destroyed by a round trip through a text form that cannot express it, and the atomic 'whole model swaps in' rule makes the silence total.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe2.mjs webkit (tag F).
defects.proposedCure: applyCSS must not overwrite fields the parsed text does not mention. Parse results should carry presence, not just values — the same reconciliation R17 needs.

defects.defect: The syntax highlighting is dead for the entire authoring session — exactly when a code editor's highlighting earns its keep. It returns only when the user looks away.
defects.evidence: r3-probe7-highlight.mjs: P1-at-rest hljsSpans 9; P2-while-authoring hljsSpans 0 (innerHTML is bare text); P3-after-parse-applied-still-focused hljsSpans 0; P4-after-blur hljsSpans 3. Cost: `wc -c node_modules/highlight.js/lib/core.js node_modules/highlight.js/lib/languages/css.js` -> 75941 + 18879 = 94820 raw bytes. Source: render() (lines 51-53) is the only markup producer and is gated to the unfocused state (lines 72, 76-79).
defects.mechanism: The editor truce (never rewrite while focused) and the highlight mechanism (rewrite innerHTML wholesale) are the same code path, so protecting the caret necessarily disables highlighting. innerHTML rewriting also destroys the native undo stack and any selection.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../evidence/r3-probe7-highlight.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of the MT-F037 glass ask: a value-bound code field with a highlight overlay layer highlights while you type without ever touching the editable node — or the dependency and the claim both go. Do not add per-keystroke innerHTML rewriting to the current shape; that trades the defect for a caret bug.

defects.mechanism: The suite asserts the states that are easy to reach (type, then assert while focused) and never the transitions where the component's documented law lives (blur timing, unmount/deactivate, no-op edits, domain boundaries). defects.reproduction: Mutation reasoned from the quoted assertion texts, NOT executed — this formation forbids source edits. Labelled a hypothesis on that ground; the argument is textual and checkable by anyone who may edit. The vitest count and the crash console silence are measured.

defects.defect: A byte-identical no-op edit in the CSS editor silently destroys every per-interval easing curve the user authored. The editor auto-commits on a 500ms debounce, and a successful parse re-seeds every interval to the `linear` preset — so the trigger for a total model replacement is the ABSENCE of typing for 500ms. No verdict, no confirmation, no undo, no visual cue. The route's own subtitle is 'Build gradients with per-interval easing and CSS output'; the CSS half silently deletes the easing half. Neither round 1 nor round 2 found this (grep for 're-seed|reseed|easing.*reset|destroys.*easing' over both prior reports returns zero hits).
defects.evidence: WBGCE-probe8.mjs, real WebKit 1440x900, three measured states in order: {"easingBefore":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)", "easingAfterPreset":"cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)", "easingAfterParse":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"}. Mechanism documented as intent at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue:102-105 ('A successful parse re-seeds every interval to the `linear` preset'); executed at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:158-168 (`intervals.value = model.intervals`). Debounce at GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62.
defects.mechanism: no commit gate — a debounce standing in for a commit, so there is no user act that means 'replace my model' and therefore none that means 'don't'. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: 'The global grammar is select → tune → commit… Selection changes the active specimen without committing it.'
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait for settle. Click the `ease` preset dial in the Easing section (readout goes cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1) → cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)). Scroll to the CSS editor, click into it, press End, type one space, press Backspace (buffer now byte-identical). Wait 1.5s. The easing readout has silently reverted to cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1).
defects.proposedCure: Retire the auto-commit entirely. Compose glass-ui 7.0.0 `LabeledField` + `Textarea` (resize="content", invalid, placeholder) with one explicit Apply in the existing Copy DockControl action set (GradientVisualizer.vue:254-256); parse ONLY on Apply and on blur-with-change, and have Apply name its destructive effect (replaces stops, resets per-interval easing) before taking it. This is the round-3 addition to the cure both prior rounds converged on: a Textarea that merely debounces update:modelValue into applyCSS would fix the crash and KEEP the data loss.

defects.defect: The app's own Windows-High-Contrast focus restoration exists and this element falls through every arm of it. foundation.css:698-719 restores a real `outline` under @media (forced-colors: active) for a named selector list; `[role="textbox"]` is not in that list, and the element carries no `tabindex` (a contenteditable is focusable natively), so it matches neither the role arms, nor the [tabindex] arm, nor input/select. The only editable text surface on the Gradient route is the one operable control the app's own WHCM rule cannot see — and it is invisible to that rule precisely because it was hand-rolled instead of composed from input/textarea. Round 2's D2-2 establishes the box-shadow-only symptom but does not identify this cause.
defects.evidence: demo/styles/foundation.css:698-719 — `:where(a[href], button, [role="button"], [role="combobox"], [role="tab"], [role="slider"], [role="menuitem"], [role="option"], input, select, summary, .rail-handle, .rail-remove-chip, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px; }` with the comment 'box-shadow rings vanish in WHCM, so restore a real `outline`'. Measured attribute set of the live element (WBGCE-probe4.mjs): {"contenteditable":"true","spellcheck":"false","role":"textbox","aria-label":"Gradient CSS","style":"transition: border-color …"} — no tabindex. Measured focus indicator: outline "3px none rgb(28,25,23)" (style NONE) + box-shadow "rgb(28,25,23) 0 0 0 2px". Same root one line up: `.readout-rail` IS in the tier-1 forced-color-adjust:none roster at foundation.css:687; the CSS editor is in no roster at all.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled primitive outside the design system's element vocabulary — every app-level and producer-level a11y layer keys off native control elements/roles it does not carry. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.reproduction: Read demo/styles/foundation.css:698-719 and the measured attribute set. The element matches no arm of the selector. (Playwright WebKit's forcedColors emulation did not strip box-shadow in my run, so the erasure itself is the CSS Color Adjust spec's stated behaviour, not a frame I hold — the selector-list miss is measured directly and does not depend on it.)
defects.proposedCure: Nothing local. A native <textarea> via the glass-ui `Textarea` primitive matches the existing input-family arms of that selector and inherits the producer's :focus-visible recipe (glass/control-surfaces.css `.input-pill:focus-visible`) with no new CSS. Adding [role="textbox"] to the app selector would be patching around the real defect.

defects.defect:
RESOLVES THE ONE OPEN DISPUTE BETWEEN ROUNDS 1 AND 2. Round 1's D-3 claimed the parse verdict has visiblePx:0; round 2 explicitly withdrew ('I could not reproduce the visiblePx: 0 clipping; my probes had the section scrolled into view'). Measured: round 1 is upheld, and it is not a viewport accident. The verdict

is the last element in a column whose second-to-last element is an 80px-minimum box, inside a pane that clips — so at the moment of a rejection the user gets a 1px red hairline and nothing else. Scrolling the section into view moves the EDITOR into the pane, not the verdict; the verdict lies below the pane's own bottom edge.
defects.evidence: WBGCE-probe6.mjs, real WebKit, typing 'linear-gradient(90deg, nope)' (a clean rejection, no throw). Desktop 1440x900: editor 795.1→875.1; verdict top 881.1 → bottom 904.0; nearest clipping ancestor DIV.glass-resting card, overflow 'hidden auto', bottom 877.0 → verdict starts 4.1px BELOW the clip edge, 100% clipped, and also below the 900px viewport. Mobile 390x844: editor 740.5→820.5; verdict 826.5→846.1; same pane clip bottom 835.98 → ~52% clipped, also crossing the 844px viewport. Visual: WBGCE-error.png shows the red hairline and NO sentence. DOM holds 'unparseable color "nope"' at rgb(219,36,36). Source comment GradientCodeEditor.vue:102-103 calls this 'explicit destructive failure … LOUD'.
defects.mechanism: failure explanation placed as a sibling AFTER the tallest element at the tail of a scroll container, rather than owned by the field. Compounded by GradientCodeEditor.vue:107-114 emitting no id and the field carrying no aria-describedby/aria-errormessage (measured: describedBy null, errorMessage null, verdictId null, verdictRole 'status').
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900, scroll the CSS editor into view, click it, select-all, type 'linear-gradient(90deg, nope)', wait 1.4s. Measure the verdict's getBoundingClientRect against its nearest overflow-clipping ancestor.
defects.proposedCure: The message belongs to the field, not after it. glass-ui `LabeledField`'s slot contract (errorId / describedBy / errorLive, dist/components/labeled-field/types.d.ts) renders and associates the message as part of the control inside the control's own reserved block — removing the tail-of-scroller placement by construction and closing the unassociated-ARIA half in the same move.

defects.defect: A press-lit BUTTON material is composited over editable code. `glass-wash` (GradientCodeEditor.vue:93) brings two overlay pseudo-elements the component neither asked for nor wants: a specular ::before at z-index 1 with mix-blend-mode plus-lighter, and a paper-grain ::after with mix-blend-mode overlay. The code text is unpositioned (z-index auto), so both composite ABOVE the glyphs. Worse, the producer drives the specular off press semantics — so hovering the code sweeps a conic highlight across it and the click that focuses the field to type flashes it to 0.16 over the very glyphs the user is aiming at. The material says 'press me', the role says 'type here'.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live element, identical across light/dark x 1440/390/320 (WBGCE-probe4.mjs): ::before {content:"", z-index:1, mix-blend-mode:plus-lighter, opacity:0.07}; ::after {content:"", mix-blend-mode:overlay, opacity:0.025}. Producer source node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/material.css declares both at position:absolute; inset:0; border-radius:inherit; z-index:1, and `.glass-wash:hover::before { --specular-intensity: var(--glass-specular-intensity-hover, 0.1) }` / `.glass-wash:active::before { --specular-intensity: var(--glass-specular-intensity-active, 0.16) }`. No hits for 'specular', 'plus-lighter' or 'grain' in either prior round's report.
defects.mechanism: wrong material tier for the job. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2 files a code artifact as a Specimen well ('opaque/quiet neutral stage'); glass-ui's own README:145 files Wash as 'Dock backgrounds, input fills, hover overlays'. Because the plate itself is nulled when nested (backdrop-filter none, background rgba(0,0,0,0)), only the interaction lighting survives — on the one surface where it is semantically wrong. §2: 'Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well.'
defects.reproduction: getComputedStyle(editor, '::before') and (editor, '::after') on the live /#/gradient route; read glass/material.css hover/active rules.
defects.proposedCure: Drop glass-wash. Adopt the glass-ui Textarea primitive, which owns its control surface via .control-surface / .input-pill and carries no press-lit specular. Interim, the certified opaque `bg-well` ground already used by the sibling `.readout-rail` (GradientEasingEditor.vue:176) — never a glass rung.

defects.defect: The MT-F001 blocker's real trigger is the single most ordinary edit on the route, not an adversarial string — and the recovery loses the user's work. Rounds 1 and 2 both reproduced by typing the literal `oklch()`. In product terms: the seeded value is `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`, and clearing the three numbers you came to a colour tool to change destroys the entire workbench. Every intermediate state of `0.75 0.15 145 → (empty) → 0.8 0.2 200` passes through `oklch()`. `Try again` then restores the SEED, not the edit.
defects.evidence: WBGCE-probe3.mjs: caret placed after the first `oklch(`, Delete pressed 13x, 1.5s wait → {"editorPresent": false, "bodyText": "→ Gradient Tools Login @mbabb This panel hit an unexpected error. undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g[0].replace') Try again", "bodyTextLen": 133, "h1Count": 0, "mainCount": 1}. Frame: WBGCE-realistic-edit-crash.png (both panes gone; a lone Try again pill on the aurora, with the diagnosis sentence present in innerText but painting nothing). Driving Try again: {"editorPresent": true, "editorText": "linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)"} — the seed. Library boundary confirmed independently: parseCssColor throws TypeError on oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' while 'oklch(0.7' correctly returns ok:false. Bare call site: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:92-94. Source comment GradientCodeEditor.vue:39-40 asserts 'A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim … WIP is never destroyed.'
defects.mechanism: same root as D3-1 — a debounce standing in for a commit hands the parser every intermediate character sequence a human types, i.e. the one input class it is known not to survive.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. In the CSS editor, place the caret immediately after the first `oklch(` and press Delete 13 times. Within 500ms the whole workbench unmounts to a bare 'Try again' pill. Click it: the seed returns, the edit does not.
defects.proposedCure: Total parser (parseCssColor returns {ok:false} for every string, per the V·π mandate) plus the Apply-gated commit of D3-1. A try/catch at the call site is the masking fallback owner edict 2 forbids and is explicitly not the cure.

defects.defect: A mobile contenteditable code field with no input-correction guards. GradientCodeEditor.vue:88-93 sets spellcheck="false" and nothing else — no autocapitalize, no autocorrect, no inputmode. On iOS Safari a contenteditable autocapitalises the first letter of the buffer and applies smart-quote / en-dash substitution, each of which corrupts CSS, and one of which (`linear-gradient` → `Linear-gradient`) lands the user directly in the D3-4 blocker.
defects.evidence: Measured attribute set: {"contenteditable":"true","spellcheck":"false","role":"textbox","aria-label":"Gradient CSS","style":"…"}. `grep -rn "autocapitalize\|autocorrect" demo/` returns zero occurrences repo-wide. The route ships a mobile matrix — docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md rows 155 and 170 (safari-mobile-light/dark /#/gradient).
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled editing surface inheriting UA text-assistance defaults meant for prose. A native <textarea> composed through the design system would carry the guards as producer props.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. The missing-attribute fact and the zero-hit grep are measured; the corruption is inferred from documented iOS Safari behaviour, which I cannot drive from this seat.
defects.proposedCure: Fold into the Textarea transposition and set the guards at the primitive level for all code-bearing fields, not per instance (owner edict 5).

result.strongestDefect: D3-1 — a byte-identical no-op edit in the CSS editor silently destroys every per-interval easing curve the user authored. Reproduced end-to-end on real WebKit: seeded cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1) → user clicks the `ease` dial → cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) → user types one space in the editor and Backspaces it (buffer byte-identical) → 500ms later cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1). No verdict, no confirmation, no undo. Neither prior D round found it. It is the strongest because it damages the user on the SUCCESS path, with no parser bug involved, and it proves the root defect is architectural — a 500ms debounce standing in for a commit — rather than the MT-F001 throw that both prior rounds treated as the headline.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records the hypotheses I killed rather than a clean bill — the boundary of the finding set. (1) REDUCED MOTION IS HANDLED: I expected the inline `:style` transition at GradientCodeEditor.vue:95-97 to be unreachable by @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), since inline declarations outrank stylesheet rules. It is reachable — demo/styles/animations.css:184-191 uses `*, *::before, *::after { transition-duration: 0.01ms !important }` and !important in a stylesheet beats an inline declaration. The inline style survives only as an edict-5 root-vs-instance defect (already round 2's D2-4/D2-6), NOT as a reduced-motion defect. (2) `scrollbar-thin` IS PRODUCER-DEFINED, not a dead class: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css → `.scrollbar-thin{scrollbar-width:thin}`. (3) THE DESTRUCTIVE BORDER SURVIVES FORCED COLORS: measured with context-level forcedColors:"active" — forcedResting.border rgb(0,0,0) → forcedError.border rgb(255,255,0), a distinct system colour. Only the FOCUS indicator dies (D3-2). This also corrects round 2's method claim that "the matrix contains no forced-colors truth for this route at all" — the emulation works when set at browser.newContext level rather than page level. (4) 200% ZOOM IS CLEAN: {w:462, h:80, scrollH:78, clientH:78, clipped:false} at 720x450@DSF4, and REPORT.md records overflowX = 0 for /#/gradient in all four Safari matrices. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8) IS CLEAN: every import at lines 2-6 is a value import; no type-only import exists to mark. (6) VUE 3.5 IDIOMS (edict 7) ARE CLEAN: useTemplateRef at line 31, reactive props destructure with default at line 16; the component takes a one-way modelValue prop and emits, so the defineModel stale-read hazard does not apply. (7) NO GOD MODULE (edict 1): 117 lines, one job, one consumer. (8) NO ANIMATIONS DELETED (edict 6): the file declares no @keyframes and documents the retired head-injection theme swap at lines 10-14. (9) PAGE/CONSOLE ERRORS AT REST ARE ZERO in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md rows 125/140/155/170) — which is exactly why the static visual matrix missed the blocker: every defect above is interaction-only.

defects.mechanism: Styling and measuring another package's private DOM by role/test-id/class. The producer shipped a new major (Glass 7, W44), its private DOM moved, and the consumer's law died silently because nothing binds the two contracts.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe2.mjs (Chromium) or probe-easing-stage.mjs (WebKit) against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient — click button[aria-label="Author a custom curve"], then read svgImgCount / svgBox / drawn. defects.proposedCure: Delete Law 3 and the whole vbRatio machinery. Zero-letterbox is a producer requirement — glass-ui owns the canvas, its viewBox and its preserveAspectRatio and is the only party that can make the drawn plot equal the element box without archaeology. Send it as the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet clause it was always meant to be (`fit="contain"`, or simply drop the inline block-size/aspect-ratio and let the box follow the viewBox). A consumer cannot own another package's geometry through a role selector.
