defects.mechanism: Two domains never reconciled at the seam. The seat's header comment actively celebrates the mismatch ("a regime flip (linear → back → steps)", "overshoot draws past the box, never clipped") — the design was authored around a curve family the host cannot evaluate.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click button[aria-label="Author a custom curve"] → focus `.easing-authoring [role='slider']` → press Shift+ArrowUp x11. Script: scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe6.mjs. Frame: evidence/crash-after-11-shift-arrowup.png
defects.proposedCure: One decision, made once, at the model boundary: either the gradient interval accepts overshoot and mixColor clamps/extrapolates under a named, tested policy, or GradientInterval's easing is [0,1]-valued by type and the authoring instrument is constrained to it (a `clampY` prop on the producer, or a `domain` on EasingPickerValue). No try/catch in the seat — catching would convert a contract break into a silent no-op, which is worse.

defects.defect: The reduced-motion cure the component documents does not exist: the effective transition duration in this subtree under prefers-reduced-motion is 100 ms, not ~0 — refuting r2's negative proof on the same clause.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:112-114 claims "The global PRM carve-out (animations.css) neutralizes it under reduced motion"; challenge-D-design-r2.md:498-500 accepted it on a code read. Measured with reducedMotion:"reduce" in BOTH Chromium and WebKit: a bare `<div style="transition: opacity 5s">` computes transitionDuration `0.1s`; the same div with setProperty(...,"important") computes `5s`; `.easing-authoring svg` computes `0.1s`; the guard rule `*, ::before, ::after { transition-duration: 0.01ms !important }` IS present in the CSSOM (found twice). Which declaration wins is UNRESOLVED (hypothesis: cascade-layer reversal for important declarations) — the 0.1s measurement is not a hypothesis.
defects.mechanism: A motion cure asserted in prose and never witnessed by a test. Compounded by the choice to animate `aspect-ratio` — a layout-driving property — inside a container-query container, so the intended fix for one lurch is ~18 frames of continuous relayout of everything below.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe12.mjs (enumerates PRM rules, both engines) and WBGEAS-probe13.mjs (normal vs !important inline probe) against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient
defects.proposedCure: Delete the aspect-ratio transition with the rest of Law 3. If the disclosure's height change deserves easing, ease it at the disclosure (interpolate-size / grid-template-rows) with a house duration token — never on the specimen's own aspect. Separately, the demo's global PRM guard needs a real witness; it is currently an assertion no test makes.

defects.defect: The protagonist measures 10.42 rem where the ratified register says 19–22 rem, inside a housing of 27.25 rem that exceeds the ceiling — the exact inversion PR-09 exists to close. The written intent fails the canon too.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:210 "The curve is a centered, container-clamped 19–22rem stage… Catalogue and specimen strips support the curve rather than reducing it to a tiny nested widget." PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:53 PR-09 "ENLARGE. One 19–22rem protagonist." Measured: drawn curve 166.7px = 10.42rem = 55% of the 19rem floor, inside a 436px = 27.25rem card = 124% of the 22rem ceiling. The seat's own intended override `inline-size: min(100%, 19rem)` caps at exactly the floor and never reaches 19–22; `margin-inline: 0 !important` deliberately deletes the producer's centring, contradicting "centered".
defects.mechanism: Proportion delegated to a CSS clamp written against a breakpoint intuition rather than derived from the canon's register; and the canon's own numbers were never checked against the written override.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe9.mjs — reads stageW, svgBox, drawnW at 1440/320/RTL. Frames: evidence/stage-desktop-light.png, evidence/stage-mobile-light.png
defects.proposedCure: The stage is not the seat's to clamp. Give the producer a container-scaled size contract (`--easing-canvas-size: clamp(19rem, …, 22rem)`) and let it centre its own canvas; the seat supplies the token, not the geometry.

defects.defect: Two selection owners in one disclosed row, and the second is permanently empty: the stage's entire bezier-mode chrome is a `Preset` combobox duplicating the sibling specimen strip, and it displays the placeholder in every state.
defects.evidence: The seat's own header states "the strip selects; THIS stage authors." Measured interactive inventory inside `.easing-authoring` (bezier regime): exactly three — `Bezier control point 1`, `Bezier control point 2`, and one 436x40 `role="combobox"` named `Easing preset`. Its rendered text is `"Pick a curve"` in every matrix (light, dark, mobile, PRM, forced-colors, 200% zoom) and after every specimen selection, while the row header reads `linear` and the readout reads `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)`. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 PR-06: "Three adjacent action species or duplicated selected fills → REMOVE. One action/selection owner."
defects.mechanism: The producer was seated wholesale and its chrome accepted unexamined; the seat imposed three laws on the chrome's material and none on its content, so a second selection surface shipped alongside the one the design chose.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe2.mjs — read `interactives` and `selectTriggerText` per matrix. Frame: evidence/stage-desktop-light.png (the full-bleed "Pick a curve" control under the canvas)
defects.proposedCure: Pass `:preset="false"` (or the P7 equivalent) so the strip is the only selection owner, per the seat's own stated law. If the producer has no such door, that is the packet clause — not a reason to ship two selection surfaces that disagree.

defects.defect: The mode trap — a modal editor whose fundamental regime is owned by a sibling component, with no mode control in the stage in either regime and no path back.
defects.evidence: Measured `data-mode` and the stage's accessible-name set: open (default) → `bezier`, controls {Bezier control point 1, Bezier control point 2, Easing preset}; select the `steps` tile in the sibling strip → `steps`, controls {Step count, Jump term}; select `step-start` → `steps`; select `ease-in-out-sine` → back to `bezier`. The seat never passes or toggles the producer's `mode` prop (EasingAuthoringStage.vue:76-82 passes only model-value, readout, playback, label). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:98-100: "Selection changes the active specimen… Tuning is continuous and interruptible."
defects.mechanism: A mode was treated as derived state rather than as an affordance. The stage's control inventory, accessible names and keyboard model change identity underneath the user with no affordance, no label and no announcement.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe11.mjs — fresh context per tile; prints data-mode and the control list after selecting steps / step-start / ease-in-out-sine / ease-in-back. Frame: evidence/stage-steps-regime.png
defects.proposedCure: Either the stage owns the regime — one labelled two-item control (house SegmentedTabs) at the top of the stage — or the regime is not a mode. It cannot be an invisible consequence of a sibling's press.

defects.defect: Law 2's well houses only the canvas card and leaves the producer's chrome column on the raw translucent pane, below the AA contrast floor — the exact condition the parent component already diagnosed, certified and fixed 30 lines above the mount point.
defects.evidence: With `:readout="false"` there is exactly one `.glass-card` in the subtree, so Law 2 (:93-99) covers the canvas only. Real-pixel, tight-glyph measurement in the same frame (Range-derived glyph box, Chromium canvas decode): stage "Preset" label 4.44:1 (light) / 3.02:1 (dark); parent readout literal on `bg-well`, identical ink rgb(112,89,66)/rgb(195,185,172), 5.07:1 / 6.03:1. WCAG 1.4.3 AA needs 4.5:1 at 14.38px weight 400. GradientEasingEditor.vue:167-175 records the same diagnosis verbatim: "on the raw translucent pane over the saturated atmosphere it composited ~2.7:1 (fails AA); a `bg-well` well floors it." Compounding: the label is `text-mono-caption` (Fira Code, uppercased) where VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 assigns control labels to `text-small` Plus Jakarta Sans.
defects.mechanism: A cure certified once at one site and not generalised to the component mounted inside it — the well was attached to the producer's card class rather than to the stage's own surface.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe8.mjs (light + dark) — clips the Range-tight glyph box of both labels and decodes them through a Chromium canvas. Frames: evidence/stage-desktop-light.png, evidence/stage-desktop-dark.png
defects.proposedCure: The well is the stage's material, not the canvas card's. Move it to `.easing-authoring` itself so the whole disclosed instrument — canvas and chrome — rides one certified paper, and drop the `.glass-card` override with it. One surface, one tier (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19).

defects.defect: The only operable targets on the canvas are 13.3 CSS px — 55% of the WCAG 2.5.8 floor — and the dead Law 3 is the direct cause.
defects.evidence: Both `role="slider"` bezier handles measure 13.3 x 13.3 px in all 9 matrices (r=0.04 viewBox units x the 166.7 fit scale). WCAG 2.5.8 minimum is 24x24. Counterfactual arithmetic: had Law 3 bound, the canvas would be 304x365 (min(100%,19rem) at aspect 1/1.2), fit scale 304, handles 24.3px — passing; axis annotations 15.2px instead of 8.33px. The route-level census in audit/visual/REPORT.md records 6 small targets on /#/gradient per matrix and cannot see these two, because no capture in the 60-frame corpus or the 6 state matrices ever discloses the stage.
defects.mechanism: Operable size derived from a drawing scale instead of being an independent quantity (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 7: visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe2.mjs — `interactives[].w/h`; confirmed identical under WebKit in probe-easing-stage.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Fix D3-01 at the producer (the geometry cure recovers 24.3px for free), and give the producer an explicit hit-target contract so handle hit area is decoupled from render radius — the producer already has HANDLE_HIT_RADIUS/HANDLE_HIT_RADIUS_TOUCH constants for pointer grab, they simply do not govern the rendered target.

defects.defect: The component is a per-instance override shim on another package's private DOM — styling through a test-id, a role and a utility class with !important — declared temporary in its own header and shipping permanently.
defects.evidence: The entire file body is three `:deep()` blocks and four `!important` declarations targeting `[data-testid="easing-picker"]` (:88), `.glass-card` (:93) and `svg[role="img"]` (:104). Header text: "each recorded on the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet; the overrides retire at the adopt" (:10-11) and "retired at the P7 adopt" (:103). Violates standing edict 4 (variants belong in glass-ui), edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides), edict 2 (no shims), edict 3 (KISS — a wrapper whose only content is another component plus overrides). Edicts 1, 6, 7 and 8 pass.
defects.mechanism: Design authority located in the consumer instead of the producer. A test id is a test contract; styling through it makes every producer refactor a silent visual regression in the consumer — which is precisely what happened at the Glass 7 adoption (W44).
defects.reproduction: Read demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingAuthoringStage.vue:86-116 against the standing edicts; cross-check the producer surface at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/EasingPicker.vue.d.ts (props: mode, preset, steps, term, readout, playback, label — no column, material or fit door).
defects.proposedCure: Delete EasingAuthoringStage.vue entirely and mount `<EasingPicker>` directly from GradientEasingEditor. Move the three laws into the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet as props — `columns="1"`, `material="well"`, `fit="contain"`, a container-scaled `size` clamp, `preset={false}`, and one visible labelled `mode` control — where they are cheap, testable and owned by the party that can hold them.

defects.defect: The oracle that certifies this component's constitutive law is red on disk and structurally unable to report: CI runs no Playwright step at all.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:51 locates the canvas by the same dead `#easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img']`. Live run: `VJS_E2E_PORT=9000 npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts --reporter=line` → `3 failed` (zero-letterbox desktop, zero-letterbox 390, composition/dot-rest/one-literal/mint-law), all on `Error: element(s) not found`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs lint, two vue-tsc passes, build, npm test and a packed-surface check — `grep -rn playwright .github/` returns nothing.
defects.mechanism: A bespoke oracle written to certify one law, then dropped out of the enforcement path. A law whose only witness is un-runnable is not a law; it is a comment — which is how the producer's DOM change went unnoticed through a whole major adoption.
defects.reproduction: VJS_E2E_PORT=9000 npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts --reporter=line (dev server already on :9000); then grep -rn playwright .github/
defects.proposedCure: Re-anchor o17 on `[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg` — a producer-owned id that actually exists — and wire the Playwright projects into .github/workflows/ci.yml. If the geometry law moves to the producer per D3-01, the oracle moves with it and becomes a producer gate.

defects.defect: Focus on the bezier handles is expressed in the identical ink as the curve that passes through them, on a 13.3 px dot; the house focus register the parent already uses is not adopted.
defects.evidence: Tab-reached, `:focus-visible` measured true; computed `stroke: oklch(0.438102 0.0748123 205)`, `stroke-width: 0.045` → 7.5px of stroke on a 13.3px dot — the same `--easing-curve-accent` ← `--motion-accent` ink that this seat's parent supplies per interval for the curve itself. The parent uses `box-shadow: var(--focus-ring-shadow)` on `.rail-btn:focus-visible` (GradientEasingEditor.vue:285-288) and `.interval-head:focus-visible` (:229-231). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84: "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency."
defects.mechanism: The seat supplies the accent ink but never asked what else that ink already paints; the producer's focus affordance is a recolour into a variable the consumer controls.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe10.mjs — Tabs until activeElement role=slider, reports `:focus-visible` true and the computed stroke, then screenshots. Compare evidence/stage-focus-handle1.png with evidence/stage-desktop-light.png
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the house `--focus-ring-shadow` register for the seated instrument, or give the producer a `--easing-focus-ring` door so focus never resolves to the same ink as the data it sits on.

defects.defect: The canvas's own reference frame — the unit box, the gridlines and the axis annotations — is below every legibility floor, so a cubic-bezier editor ships without visible axes.
defects.evidence: Colours resolved through a canvas 2D context (not string-parsed) and composited over the measured well: plot frame 1.56:1 light / 1.66:1 dark; gridlines 1.18:1 / 1.22:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 floor 3:1); axis `0`/`1` labels render at 8.33 CSS px (font-size 0.05 viewBox units x the 166.7 fit scale) at 2.41:1 light / 3.19:1 dark (WCAG 1.4.3 floor 4.5:1).
defects.mechanism: Half producer ink choice (`stroke-border/40`, `fill-muted-foreground/60`), half the dead Law 3 — the 8.33px is a direct consequence of the 166.7 fit scale.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe9.mjs — plotFrameVsWell / gridVsWell / axisTextVsWell / axisTextRenderedPx per scheme. Frames: evidence/stage-desktop-light.png, evidence/stage-desktop-dark.png
defects.proposedCure: Fix D3-01 (recovers 15.2px axis type) and raise the producer's frame/grid inks to clear 3:1 on the well tier — a producer packet clause, since the ink is producer-owned and the well is the tier the consumer certified.

defects.defect: Most of the component's state space was never designed: no loading, disabled, dragging, hovered, pressed or in-stage error state exists; a producer cancel is silently swallowed; forced-colors is undesigned; and the parent's own `v-if` contradicts the documented "alive from birth, v-show never v-if" law.
defects.evidence: Enumerated live: no skeleton or reserve on mount; no `disabled` prop on seat or producer; no cursor/crosshair/coordinate readout during a handle grab; the only failure surface is the route-level ErrorBoundary (D3-02). `GradientEasingEditor.vue:78-81` — `function onPickerAuthored(index, v) { if (!v) return; ... }` drops an undefined (cancel) emission silently. Forced colors (Chromium `forcedColors: active`): the well and border remap to system Canvas/ButtonText (measured cardBg rgb(255,255,255), border rgb(0,0,0)) while the curve, handles and gridlines are SVG stroke/fill and remap for nothing — the instrument keeps arbitrary chroma on a system-white ground and focus stays the curve's ink. `GradientEasingEditor.vue:208` is `v-if="intervals[row.index]"` against its own doc at :16-18 ("Picker instances stay ALIVE (v-show, never v-if)"). RTL and 200%-zoom pass geometrically.
defects.mechanism: State coverage inherited from the producer rather than designed for the seat; the header documents an aliveness law the template does not implement.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/WBGEAS-probe2.mjs (forced-colors row) and WBGEAS-probe9.mjs (RTL, 320px); read GradientEasingEditor.vue:78-81 and :200-213
defects.proposedCure: Design the state set at the seat: a real disabled/busy expression, a drag expression with live coordinates (which also satisfies VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's "pointer drag, arrow movement and numeric entry must resolve to the same model value"), a forced-colors treatment that gives the curve and handles system-mapped inks, an honest handling of the cancel emission, and — since the picker's state is fully model-driven — remove the contradiction by making the mount unconditional or deleting the aliveness claim.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation audit (round 4) of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (the 1M-context seat), matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: The component validates a gradient stop with `parseCssColor` but draws it with `parseColorIn` + `mixColors` — two different predicates. A spec-valid CSS Color 4 `none`-channel stop is ACCEPTED (`parseGradientCSS` returns `ok:true`, `parseVerdict` stays `null`), applied to the model, and then throws from five separate render sites, destroying the whole pane and every stop / position / easing curve / setting. Distinct from the filed C-1 / R2-N5 (there `parseCssColor` itself throws); this door survives making the parsers total (mini-tranche V·π) AND survives round 3's model-hoist cure, which converts a silent reseed into a crash loop.
defects.evidence: Oracle gap, pasted from `probes/challenge-C-r4-oracle-gap.ts`: `oklch(none 0.15 145)` → oracle=ACCEPTED render=*** mixColors NOT-OK: color_missing_channel; `rgb(none 0 0)` / `hsl(none 50% 50%)` / `lab(none 20 30)` → *** THROWS PickerColorError: color_missing_channel; `oklch(0.7 0.15 145 / none)` → color_missing_alpha; while `oklch(0.7 0.15 none)`, `transparent`, `color(srgb 1 0 0)`, `rebeccapurple`, `#ff000080` all render (gap is channel-position-specific). End-to-end: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(none 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` → parse=OK (verdict null), coalescedCSS=THROWS, railRampCSS=THROWS. Code: gradientParse.ts:92-94 (`parseCssColor(token).ok`) vs useGradientCSS.ts:192-193 + :206-208 (`throw new Error('Gradient color mix failed: '+mixed.error.code)`). Five throw sites: useGradientCSS.ts:206-208 (coalescedCSS→GradientVisualizer.vue:224 tile + :128 copyCSS), same via serializeRailRamp (GradientStopEditor.vue:204), useGradientCSS.ts:192-193, useGradientInterpolation.ts:34-37 via GradientVisualizer.vue:79-85 (child `ghostColor` computed, GradientStopEditor.vue:71-73), useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59.
defects.mechanism: Validation oracle ≠ render operation. The declared total contract `GradientParseResult` ('a COMPLETE model or an explicit reason. Never a partial') is unsound: it certifies `ok:true` for a model the render path cannot draw, and the render path signals failure by throwing instead of by Result — inside computeds, i.e. in render position, where the ErrorBoundary unmounts the whole subtree.
defects.reproduction: Live, twice, at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (HEAD d19da6d3). (1) click the rail at 50% → 3 stops: {"handles":["Gradient stop at 0%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]}. (2) In the CSS box select the `0.75` of the first `oklch(...)` and type `none` via a real caret edit (Range + document.execCommand('insertText'), a genuine `input` event) → editorText `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(none 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`. (3) 800 ms later (debounce fired): {"textbox":false,"editorText":null,"handles":[],"rail":false,"tile":false,"easingHeads":false,"verdict":null,"mainText":"This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_missing_channel Try again"}. Repeated from the untouched two-stop default → crashed:true. Screenshots evidence/challenge-C-r4-pane-destroyed-none-channel.png and -color-missing-channel.png; the reseeded-to-default pane in evidence/challenge-C-r4-error-card-1512.png. Offline: npx vite-node probes/challenge-C-r4-oracle-gap.ts.
defects.proposedCure: One predicate, once, at the boundary. `parseGradientCSS` must validate each stop with the operation that will be performed on it — `parseColorIn(token, space)` composed with a trial `mixColors` — and reject through the `{ok:false, reason}` surface the design already owns (e.g. 'oklch(none 0.15 145) has no lightness — a gradient stop needs every channel'). Structurally: make `parseColorIn` / `mixColors` / `serialize*` return `Result` instead of throwing, so the render path's TYPE states what `GradientParseResult` currently only promises. try/catch at any of the five sites is a masking fallback (edict 2) and leaves four doors open. Must be paired with round 3's model-hoist, not substituted for it.

defects.defect: The parser's in-band `-1` sentinel for 'no position authored' collides with an authored negative percentage, so a legal CSS negative position on an interior stop is silently RELOCATED (not clamped) by up to 50 percentage points, with `ok:true` and no verdict. Behaviour is discontinuous at zero. Distinct from the filed R2-N6, which charged the terminal-stop clamp.
defects.evidence: gradientParse.ts:252 `stops.push({ id: uid(), cssColor: colorToken, position: -1 })`; the auto-fill at :266-279 recognises the sentinel as `position < 0` and runs BEFORE the clamp at :281-283. Pasted probe output: `linear-gradient(90deg, red 0%, green -20%, blue 100%)` → red@0 green@50 blue@100; `green -0.0001%` → green@50; `red 0%, green -20%, lime -40%, blue 100%` → 0 / 33.333333333333336 / 66.66666666666666 / 100; control `green 20%` → green@20; `green -0%` → green@0 (because `-0 < 0` is false in JS). CSS Images 3 §3.4.1 requires an out-of-order stop to be corrected UP to the largest preceding position (a hard stop at 0%), and permits positions outside [0%,100%]. The module's own header states the opposite doctrine it violates: gradientParse.ts:175-176 'Silent-drop is forbidden (P2-17) → explicit reject'.
defects.mechanism: A sentinel drawn from the value's own domain. 'Unspecified' is encoded as a member of the position type, so the parser cannot distinguish absence from an authored negative — and the range test (`< 0`) widens the collision from one value to a half-line, leaving a −0 cliff where two inputs 0.0001 apart are read 50 points apart.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r4-oracle-gap.ts — section C, output pasted above and in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Take the sentinel out of the position domain: carry `number | null` in the parser's `positions` array (or make `GradientStop.position` optional until fill), so absence is not a number. The negative case then falls through to the documented clamp/reject path, and the `-0` cliff disappears with it. One type change, no new module.

defects.defect: `defineModel("selectedStopId")` publishes a public two-way model prop + `update:selectedStopId` emit that no parent binds, to hold state that never leaves the component; and the child's selection is written twice on every handle press — once through `v-model:selected-id`, once through a redundant `@select` handler.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "selectedStopId|selected-stop-id" demo/ e2e/ test/` returns exactly three hits, all inside the subject: GradientVisualizer.vue:51 (`defineModel<string|null>("selectedStopId", { default: null })`), :140 (`v-model:selected-id="selectedStopId"`), :144 (`@select="(id) => selectedStopId = id"`). The sole parent mounts it bare: GradientPane.vue:25 `<GradientVisualizer ref="visualizerRef" />`. Double write: GradientStopEditor.vue:128-130 sets `selectedId.value = id` (its own defineModel → emits update:selectedId) and then `emit("select", id)`; the deselect path at :151-153 uses only the first, proving the second is unnecessary.
defects.mechanism: A public API surface invented for a private value (edict 3 contrivance) plus two channels for one piece of state (edict 2 dual path) — and it voluntarily adopts this repo's own recorded `defineModel` async-round-trip stale-read hazard (edict 7) for a value that has no round trip to make.
defects.reproduction: Static: the grep above plus GradientPane.vue:25. No runtime failure today — the hazard is latent because an unbound defineModel behaves as local state.
defects.proposedCure: `const selectedStopId = shallowRef<string | null>(null)`; delete the `select` member of GradientStopEditor's `defineEmits` and the `@select` handler at :144. Net −2 declarations, one writer.

defects.defect: About 55 lines of CSS-timing→numeric machinery behind `easingFnOf` — its `parseTimingFunction` fallback, the module-level `resolvedEasingCache`, `timingFunctionValue`, `easingValue` and `linearStops` — are unreachable from the shipped app; the only caller that exercises them is a test. Round 1's C-17 charged the cache as 'unbounded'; the sharper truth is that it is never written.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:120-133 returns at :122 (`if (interval.fn) return interval.fn`) for every live interval, because `fn` is REQUIRED on the payload type (`EasingPickerValue.fn: EasingFn`, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts) and every producer supplies it: `linearInterval()` sets `fn: linear` (useGradientCSS.ts:53-62), `parseGradientCSS` seeds every interval with `linearInterval()` (gradientParse.ts:296-298), `updateInterval` copies `fn` verbatim (useGradientModel.ts:134-140). Probe section D: 'linearInterval().fn is function → easingFnOf returns at line 122 always'. Dead: :69 cache, :126-132 fallback, :106-117, :71-77, :79-104 (26 lines of linear() position arithmetic). Sole reaching caller: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:39-53, which passes `{ css: "…" }` objects with no `fn`.
defects.mechanism: Two representations of the same fact (a live callable AND a re-parseable literal) both persisted, with a resolver written for the case that the payload type forbids — so the resolver's body is decoration and a test exists to cover code the product never runs.

It exists — with zero non-test consumers, a format no live consumer can use (cubic-bezier(0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00) vs the required cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)), 9.5x more round-trip loss than the private glass-ui mint the demo hand-copies, and seven assertions in test/math.test.ts pinning the wrong law by name ("should format numbers to two decimal places"). This is the sharpest form of this axis's question: not a missing public surface, but a published one that is a FALSE PROOF — unfixable by consumer discipline and now costing a semver decision. NOTE: across all four passes the strongest defect on this axis remains r2's R2-1 (eased-ramp adapter unowned; ease-*-back emits progress outside [0,1], mixColors rejects it, the whole app is erased). Round 4 did NOT find R2-1 and records that as a miss.

defects.defect: @mkbabb/value.js/math publishes cubicBezierToString — a bezier->CSS serializer with ZERO non-test consumers, in a fourth incompatible format, lossy, with seven tests pinning the wrong law. This materially corrects r1 L-3, which concluded the library had no serializer and proposed adding one. The concept now has four homes in three formats, one of them on the public API.
defects.evidence: src/foundation/math.ts:113 + src/subpaths/math.ts:16 (published at package.json#exports "./math"). Executed against built dist/: `node --input-type=module -e "import {cubicBezierToString} from './dist/subpaths/math.js'"` -> library mint "cubic-bezier(0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00)"; demo/glass-ui mint "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"; byte-identical? false. Lossiness measured: authored [0.345678,0.789012,0.123456,0.901234] -> published mint "cubic-bezier(0.35, 0.79, 0.12, 0.90)" -> reparsed, max abs round-trip err 4.322e-3; glass-ui 3dp mint err 4.560e-4 (9.5x lossier). Zero callers: `grep -rn cubicBezierToString demo/ src/ test/ e2e/` returns only test/math.test.ts and the v4-c1 export-surface list. Wrong law pinned: test/math.test.ts:413-416 `it("should format numbers to two decimal places", () => expect(cubicBezierToString(0,0,1,1)).toBe("cubic-bezier(0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00)"))`, plus :432 (0.123456 -> "0.12"). The other three homes: glass-ui useEasingPicker.readout (toFixed(3), private, measured in dist/easing.js); demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:48-51,56-58 hand-mirroring it "byte-for-byte" per its own comment at :40-45; demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:56 hardcoding the literal.
defects.mechanism: A published function nobody consumes, whose output format was fixed by its unit test rather than by the CSS grammar it serializes into. Because no consumer ever exercised it, the drift was invisible; because a test pins it, correction is a semver decision. Underlying family: the published surface has a parse/serialize ASYMMETRY — /css ships parseTimingFunction with no serializeTimingFunction, while shipping the serializeCssColor/parseCssColor pair — so every consumer needing the inverse mints its own.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node --input-type=module -e "import {cubicBezierToString} from './dist/subpaths/math.js'; import {parseTimingFunction} from './dist/subpaths/css.js'; const a=[0.345678,0.789012,0.123456,0.901234]; const l=cubicBezierToString(...a); const b=parseTimingFunction(l); const g=[b.value.x1,b.value.y1,b.value.x2,b.value.y2]; console.log(l, Math.max(...a.map((x,i)=>Math.abs(x-g[i]))).toExponential(3));" then `sed -n '405,445p' test/math.test.ts`
defects.proposedCure: Publish serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string at @mkbabb/value.js/css — the true inverse of the parseTimingFunction already shipped and the exact sibling of the parseCssColor/serializeCssColor pair (r1 L-3's cure, still right). SIMULTANEOUSLY retire cubicBezierToString from /math: it is a CSS concern misfiled under math with zero consumers, so retiring costs one export line and one test block. Replace its seven pinned-string assertions with ONE round-trip property test parseTimingFunction(serializeTimingFunction(ast)) ~= ast, minimal-digit canonical numbers. Then glass-ui's readout, easingCatalogue.bezierLiteral/stepsLiteral and useGradientCSS's hardcoded literal all collapse onto one published call and byte-identity becomes structural rather than comment-enforced. Leaving both published is a dual path on the public API itself.

defects.defect: Inverted dependency direction inside the gradient feature: the domain types live in the ORCHESTRATOR and four modules import upward to fetch them, producing seven import cycles. No prior pass enumerated cycles.
defects.evidence: DFS over resolved local edges in demo/workbenches/gradient/** yields 7 cycles: gradientParse->useGradientCSS->useGradientModel->gradientParse; gradientParse->useGradientModel->gradientParse; useGradientCSS->useGradientModel->gradientParse->useGradientCSS; useGradientCSS->useGradientModel->useGradientCSS; useGradientModel->gradientParse->useGradientCSS->useGradientModel; useGradientModel->gradientParse->useGradientModel; useGradientModel->useGradientCSS->useGradientModel. The upward edges: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:31-34; demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:23-27; demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue:36-40; demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:36 — all `import type {GradientStop|GradientInterval|GradientType|GradientModelState} from "./useGradientModel"`. Types declared at useGradientModel.ts:33-62.
defects.mechanism: Domain vocabulary declared inside the composable that consumes it, so the only way to name a GradientStop is to import the orchestrator. All back-edges are `import type` and therefore erased at runtime, which hides the cycle from every runtime signal — that is why it survived three prior audits. Same mechanism family as r1 L-2 (injection key declared inside its provider): a vocabulary module that is not a leaf is a coupling.
defects.reproduction: python3 script (session scratchpad) doing DFS over `(?:import|export)\s+(?:type\s+)?...from "(\.[^"]+)"` edges across .ts/.vue in demo/workbenches/gradient; or read the four cited import statements directly.
defects.proposedCure: Extract demo/workbenches/gradient/model/types.ts — a LEAF holding GradientStop, GradientInterval, GradientType, GradientModelState, importing only value.js and glass-ui types. Every other module points AT it; nothing imports a composable for a type. All seven cycles become impossible by construction rather than by convention. This is the type-side twin of r1 L-2's key-side cure (demo/palettes/keys.ts) — one rule, two axes: a vocabulary module is a leaf, or it is a coupling.

Because each site owns its own grid and its own aria-label, no site can fix sizing or naming for the others.

LabeledField threads controlId/labelledBy/describedBy, which also retires the three hand-written aria-labels. Reflow grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3 (or auto-fit with a real minimum); drop the per-instance h-9. glass-ui BH relay: LabeledSelectProps.items is `readonly string[]` and cannot carry per-item descriptions — precisely why five demo files hand-roll <template #description>; it should be `readonly {value:string; label:string; description?:string}[]`.

defects.defect: The mechanism under the known DockControl defect (r1 L-10 / R2-9): DockControl declares NO `title` prop, so the label is a raw HTML attribute fallthrough, not an accessible name — and the demo has three different conventions for naming the same copy control.

defects.mechanism: A prop list that silently accepts an undeclared attribute as a passthrough. `title` is a last-resort accname source and the audit scanner (and VoiceOver practice) does not accept it, so three demo sites believed they had labelled a control and had not. Compounded by dock-scoped CSS custom properties that do not travel outside the dock, voiding the primitive's own geometry contract.
defects.reproduction: cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts | head -60 (no title in __VLS_Props); then navigate /#/gradient and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => !(b.getAttribute('aria-label')||b.textContent||'').trim())`.

defects.defect: Two independent stop-ID minters with an identical format, and the selection state is written twice on every stop click through two parallel mechanisms.
defects.evidence: (a) demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:66-69 `let nextId = 0; function uid() { return `stop-${++nextId}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`; }` and demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:30-33 `let nextParseId = 0; function uid() { return `stop-${++nextParseId}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`; }` — identical format, independent counters. applyCSS (useGradientModel.ts:158-168) installs parse-minted ids into the same stops ref that addStop (:116-120) appends model-minted ids to; the id is the v-for :key at GradientStopEditor.vue:237 and the referent of selectedStopId. (b) GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 does `selectedId.value = id;` (propagating via v-model:selected-id bound at GradientVisualizer.vue:140) AND `emit("select", id)`, which GradientVisualizer.vue:144 handles as `selectedStopId = id` — the identical assignment a second time. The child declares both a defineModel("selectedId") at :26 and a `select` emit at :23 for one concept.
defects.mechanism: One concept, two homes, in both halves: identity minted wherever a stop is constructed, selection propagated by whichever channel each author reached for. (b) compounds r2's R2-8 — the ref being double-written is a defineModel no parent binds.
defects.reproduction: Duplicate ownership CONFIRMED by the cited file:line pairs. Double-write CONFIRMED: click any gradient stop handle; StopEditor:129 writes the model (reaching the parent via v-model) and StopEditor:130 emits, making GradientVisualizer:144 assign the same value again. ID COLLISION: NONE — hypothesis only; it requires equal counter values AND the same millisecond across two independent counters, which I could not force.
defects.proposedCure: demo/workbenches/gradient/model/identity.ts exporting one nextStopId(), imported by both construction sites. For selection: delete either the `select` emit or the defineModel from GradientStopEditor — not both — and per R2-8 make the parent's selectedStopId a plain ref rather than an unbound defineModel.

defects.defect: Three masking fallbacks on the single 'Seed from palette' dock-button path, and the same DI port treated as optional here while three sibling consumers assert it non-null.

result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four negatives were established as positive evidence and matter to the formation. (1) THE VALUE.JS CONSUME IS HONEST — the axis's central question answered in the library's favour: `grep -rn '@src\|value.js/src' demo/workbenches/gradient/` returns no matches; every bare specifier in the feature (@mkbabb/value.js/color x6, /easing x4, /css x3) is a real key of package.json#exports backed by a src/subpaths/*.ts barrel; HueInterpolationMethod is genuinely exported by src/subpaths/color.ts; resolution is by GENERATED anchored-regex self-alias (vite.config.ts:38-52) derived from the exports map itself, so demo specifiers cannot drift from the published surface. A real npm consumer could write every value.js import in this component verbatim — the demo dogfood is not faked. (Caveat, r3's L3-4: the TEST half does not hold — test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts straddles src/ and dist/.) (2) PACKAGE HYGIENE IS SOUND — type:module, sideEffects:false, files:["dist","!dist/gh-pages","!dist/gh-pages/**"], seven subpaths, no "." root export and no main/module/types; `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` returns zero root-barrel imports. The absent root export is a deliberate subpath-only design, not a gap. (3) NO RUNTIME IMPORT CYCLE — all seven cycles in L4-4 close through `import type` only, so no TDZ or partial-module hazard exists today; the finding is direction, not breakage. (4) NO GOD MODULE — largest file in the closure is GradientStopEditor.vue at 392 L, the subject is 279 L, composables 301/334/193/56 L; every defect on this axis is a boundary or ownership defect, not a size defect. Also: verbatimModuleSyntax is honoured (every type-only import in the subject is `import type` — lines 22, 25, 26, 28); the brief's named historical suspects (useLayerTransition/ActionBarLayer, palettes/export.ts vs export/serializers, the three useDark stores) are absent from this closure and belong to other seats; and /#/gradient reports zero console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests and overflowX 0 across all four Safari matrices, with docScrollW == 390 at phone width in my own probe. FINALLY, an honest negative about this pass itself: round 4 MISSED six defects the priors found, including BOTH blockers — r2's R2-1 (ease-*-back erases the app; I exercised only the default linear interval) and r1's L-1 (the demo import-boundary eslint globs match zero files after the W43/RF-15 tree rename, so effective no-restricted-imports for the subject is `undefined` — the enabling defect beneath every boundary finding in all four passes). Also missed: L3-4, L3-1, R2-4, r1 L-12 / L3-5. Recorded in the report's section 5 rather than omitted.

defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained mirror of data the library already orders, used as a gate rather than as a hint — so any future family is deleted on arrival with no type error and no test failure.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → disclose the authoring stage → open `Easing preset` → choose `ease-out-quart`. The literal mints correctly, the strip shows nothing pressed, the closed-row head reads `custom`.
defects.proposedCure: `FAMILY_ORDER` becomes a hint, never a gate: `[...new Set([...FAMILY_HINT, ...byFamily.keys()])]` so an unlisted family appends instead of vanishing (src/easing.ts:34-63 already authors PRESETS in family order, so `byFamily.keys()` alone would suffice). Enforce with the exact-equality gate in C-12, not with prose.

defects.defect: The generic `steps` tile misreports identity and is inert: it renders pressed for ANY steps curve (family identity), advertises `n = 4`, and refuses to emit when pressed — so there is no path back to `steps(4, jump-end)` through the selection surface.
defects.evidence: Independent three-step repro at d19da6d3 — A: press generic `steps` → lit `steps(4, jump-end)`, pressed ['steps']. B: bump n on the producer's Step count slider → {"lit":"steps(5, jump-end)","pressed":["steps"],"aria-valuenow":"5"} (the tile labelled `n = 4` is lit while the readout three pixels below says n=5). C: press the still-lit tile → {"literalAfterPressingPressedStepsTile":"steps(5, jump-end)","pressed":["steps"],"ariaPressed":"true"} — nothing happens. Sites: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:33-35 (`if (on) emit(...)`), easingCatalogue.ts:219-223 (tileIdFor's steps fallback). Surjectivity measured: steps(5,jump-end), steps(12,jump-both) and steps(1,jump-none) all map to tile `steps`. Contradicts the strip's own stated law at :7-8 ('pressed tile IS the interval's curve').
defects.mechanism: A surjective identity function feeding a press handler that assumes injectivity — the emit is gated on the toggle's boolean instead of on curve identity.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click [data-specimen="steps"] → disclose authoring → focus the Step count slider → ArrowRight → click [data-specimen="steps"] again → the readout stays steps(5, jump-end).
defects.proposedCure: Idempotent selection: `function onTileToggle(tile) { emit("select", tile) }` — press always mints, harmless on an exact match, corrective on a family match. This is the radio semantics the control already wants (C-08), at the cost of one boolean; do the two together.

defects.defect: A 27-way single-select gallery is exposed as 27 independent toggle buttons behind a focusable, roleless, nameless scroll container — so AT announces 'toggle button, pressed' with no set membership or position, and the family grouping (the only structure on the surface) is withheld entirely.
defects.evidence: Measured tile: `<button type="button" aria-pressed="true" data-state="on" aria-label="linear" data-specimen="linear">`. `.fading-scroll` measured `tabindex="0"`, `role: null`, no aria-label → 28 tab stops per open row. Family eyebrows are aria-hidden="true" (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:96). The consumer CANNOT repair the semantics: glass Chip strips role/aria-pressed/data-state from $attrs before spreading — chip-DFZQr6rV.js: `!/^(role|aria-pressed|data-state|name|required)$/i.test(e)`.
defects.mechanism: Semantics authored on the wrong element — state on 27 toggles instead of one group, name on an unfocusable child instead of on the focusable region.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → inspect any [data-specimen] element; tab through the open easing row and count 28 stops.
defects.proposedCure: Pass `aria-label` to <FadingScroll> (its ariaLabel prop flips the root to role=region), drop the inner role=group, and make the tiles a radiogroup with a roving tabindex. The child half is producer-blocked — FOLD-BANK a `mode="radio"` on glass Chip (reka RadioGroup root + items, shape="cell" unchanged); a role=radiogroup wrapper over aria-pressed children would be a worse lie than the status quo.

defects.defect: WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failure on the `steps` tile: visible label `n = 4`, accessible name `steps` — a speech-input user cannot activate the tile they can read.
defects.evidence: Measured over all 27 tiles, exactly one fails: [{"id":"steps","name":"steps","vis":"n = 4","contains":false}]. Site: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:105 (`:aria-label="tile.id"`) vs :116 (visible `{{ tile.label }}`).
defects.mechanism: An accessible name assumed to contain the visible label, with no invariant enforcing it — true for 26 of 27 entries by coincidence of naming.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → compare `[data-specimen="steps"]`'s aria-label with its `.tile-label` text.
defects.proposedCure: Compose the accessible name from id AND label (`steps, n = 4`) rather than assuming containment; per-family role=group with a labelled (non-aria-hidden) eyebrow restores the grouping at the same time.

defects.defect: Edict-5 violation: the producer Chip is re-sized and re-laid-out from consumer scoped CSS, and the touch-target value is hardcoded as a literal instead of consuming the token.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 re-declares display/flex-direction/gap/padding and sets `min-width: 2.75rem`, overriding the producer cell recipe `flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro` (chipVariants.d.ts) purely on scoped-attribute specificity (.specimen-tile[data-v-…] 0,2,0 beats .px-2 0,1,0). The seat's own docstring at :162 states the violation ('the seat sizes it to specimen scale'). 2.75rem is the value of --touch-target, the same token glass's orphaned coarse-pointer rule reads.
defects.mechanism: Producer surface lacks the needed axis → the consumer hand-authors what the recipe owns, winning on specificity luck.
defects.reproduction: Read EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/chipVariants.d.ts SHAPE.cell.
defects.proposedCure: Bank a density/size axis for shape="cell" on glass Chip (a `size="xs"` specimen scale); consume `var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)` meanwhile. Re-judge after C-03 lands — if the override still survives, it belongs in glass, not here.

defects.defect: Every interval row mounts its own full 27-Chip strip (and its own live EasingPicker), so the DOM cost of the selection surface multiplies with stop count even though selection is per-open-row.
defects.evidence: Measured at d19da6d3 with the default 2-stop gradient: 27 tiles, `.specimen-strip *` = 133 elements of 583 page elements = 22.8% of the whole route's DOM for one strip (pass 3 measured 133/511 — the page grew, the strip's mass did not). Rows = stops − 1 (GradientEasingEditor.vue v-for over specimenRows), and the strip sits inside the row's v-show, not a v-if. This is also what forces the querySelector subtree scoping at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:39-41 ('sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id').
defects.mechanism: Per-row instantiation of a surface that is per-selection.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → `document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-strip *').length` = 133 with one interval; add stops and the count multiplies.
defects.proposedCure: ONE hoisted strip bound to the open row — 27 tiles total regardless of stop count. The data-specimen subtree scoping then becomes unnecessary, and the useMediaQuery subscription drops from N-1 instances to one.

defects.defect: Vacuous test gate: the catalogue's entire unit coverage is a `length > 20` floor against an actual 27, and the one e2e oracle that presses a specimen tile is RED on a dead premise — so both the BLOCKER and the 6 dropped presets are invisible to every gate.

Exact mutations that keep it green: (1) delete "expo" and "circ" from FAMILY_ORDER → 21 tiles, still > 20; (2) glyphPath(fn, samples = 1) → every portrait collapses to 'M 0.000 1.000 L 1.000 0.000'; (3) every payload() returns the linear payload → ids, count and glyphs untouched. No component test exists at all (no mount, no press, no assertion that selectedId maps to data-state="on"). e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts's discloseAuthoring waits on `#easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img']` — the selector C-05 proves matches nothing — so its clauses never execute, INCLUDING the press of [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] at :117 and :189, one of the three pane-destroying tiles.

defects.reproduction: Apply mutation (1) to easingCatalogue.ts:174 and run the suite — green, with three named curves gone from the UI.

Both fail today.

defects.defect: Hovering the PRESSED tile destroys half its selection ink: the label reverts from the interval accent to --foreground while the glyph stays accent, and the rule is unqualified so the ink sticks after tap on touch matrices.
defects.evidence: Measured triple at d19da6d3: no hover {"state":"on","labelColor":"oklch(0.438102 0.074812 205)"}; HOVERED {"state":"on","labelColor":"rgb(28, 25, 23)"}; unhovered — back to accent. defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → hover the lit `linear` tile → its label leaves the teal accent for --foreground while its sparkline stays teal.

defects.defect: Exported minters carry no arity or domain guard, and stepsTile launders a type through a no-op assertion that can only ever mask a future divergence into an import-time crash.

defects.proposedCure: Delete the `as JumpPosition` cast and let the types unify; type `bezierLiteral`'s parameter as the 4-tuple the callers already have (`readonly [number, number, number, number]`).

defects.defect: The keep-in-view watcher's getter allocates a fresh tuple on every evaluation, so the watch can never short-circuit on value equality.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-51 — `watch(() => [selectedId, visible] as const, …, { immediate: true })`. Vue compares with !Object.is, and two array instances are never Object.is-equal, so the callback runs on every getter re-evaluation.
defects.mechanism: Reference-identity comparison over a freshly-allocated aggregate.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis; harmless today because the getter's only deps are the two props, which already gate on change. Recorded as hygiene, not as a live defect.
defects.proposedCure: Watch the two sources as an array of getters (`watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], …)`), which compares element-wise.

defects.defect: Keep-in-view flake raised in pass 1 — DID NOT REPRODUCE for the third consecutive pass. Recorded as a negative proof, not a defect.

The dx nearest-edge arithmetic (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:65-70) is correct on both edges and no-ops inside the port; no ancestor is touched; scrollIntoView is genuinely absent, so the O-19 desktop flat-netting root cause cannot recur by construction.
defects.mechanism: n/a — closed as a negative proof.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improperly implemented)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited. No sub-agent spawned from this seat.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — `data-mix-target` (MixResultDisplay.vue:72) is written onto `<WatercolorDot>`, which is `inheritAttrs: false` in glass-ui 7.0.0, so the attribute never reaches the DOM. I patched `Element.prototype.querySelector` in-page and proved that `collectStage` (mixStage.ts:121) executes its lookup exactly once per mix and gets `null` — so the masking fallback at mixStage.ts:124 (`x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28`) runs on EVERY mix, on every engine. The component's entire stated reason to exist ("the anchor the canvas convergence lands on", docstring lines 9-19) is false in every shipped run, and both e2e specs assert only that the element is *visible*, never that the lookup succeeded — so the gate is structurally incapable of catching it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these classes were probed and came back clean, with positive evidence: (1) `flush:"post"` timing in useMixingAnimation.ts:182 is CORRECT and is not the cause of D-1 — the ghost plate is measured present from the first microtask (`plates:1, ghost:1` at dt:12ms) through the whole mixing window; the attribute simply does not exist. (2) No `defineModel` stale-read hazard — :25-28 is `defineEmits`, props are read-only reactive-destructure (:20-23 → `__props.result`), so `wellColor` and the async `onCopy` both read fresh; the `shallowRef`-cache cure has no site here. (3) No ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no reka-ui slider pointer-capture surface in this file. (4) Zero PRM-RAF exposure: no rAF, timers, listeners or observers in this file; the feature's single rAF (useMixingAnimation.ts:88-114) rides glass-ui `useRAFLoop` with `pauseWhenHidden:true`, an explicit `onBeforeUnmount(() => loop.stop())` at :187, and a PRM fast-path that COMPLETES rather than pauses (:120-125) — correct by construction. (5) The phase machine cannot strand: every early return in `arm()` calls `onSettled()`. (6) No WebGL — WatercolorDot is CSS/SVG by construction; the mix canvas is 2D. (7) No god module: 159 lines, one responsibility, one default export. (8) `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied — :7 is `import type { MixResult }`. (9) Console clean: `/#/mix` shows pageErrors 0 / consoleErrors 0 / overflowX 0 / main 1 across all four Safari matrices in REPORT.md, and 0 errors across this seat's entire live session — though per r5's R5-1 this proves less than it appears, since the pane error boundary swallows throws.

defects.defect: `data-mix-target` never reaches the DOM — the canvas convergence anchor is unreachable and a masking fallback runs on every mix
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:72 stamps `data-mix-target` on `<WatercolorDot>`. `grep -o "inheritAttrs:.\{0,40\}" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` → `inheritAttrs: !1,`. Live: the settled dot's COMPLETE attribute list is ["data-v-292b9032","data-v-0f138735","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"] — no data-mix-target. In-page `Element.prototype.querySelector` patch during a real mix: probe = [{"sel":"[data-mix-target]","found":false}]; 6-point sampling gives mixTargets:0 at dt=0,12,15,165,566,1167ms while plates:1/ghost:1 throughout.
defects.mechanism: A declared runtime contract routed through third-party attribute fall-through, which glass-ui 7.0.0 disabled (`inheritAttrs: false`, class/style forwarded explicitly). Silent decline: no diagnostic anywhere. mixStage.ts:121-124 then substitutes `{x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28}` — a masking fallback, itself an owner-edict-2 violation.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix; drive `startMix()` via `__vueParentComponent.setupState`; `document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-target]').length` is 0 at every point of the 1.2s choreography. With `Element.prototype.querySelector` patched, collectStage's single lookup is recorded returning null.
defects.proposedCure: Move the anchor off the third-party component onto a plain element this file already owns — line 63's `<div v-if="ghost" key="well">`. Then go further: have `collectStage` take the anchor ELEMENT as an argument (via `useTemplateRef`) instead of a string selector, which lets mixStage.ts:124's masking fallback be DELETED rather than repaired. Relay the passthrough seam to glass-ui BH per the standing relay edict.

defects.defect: NEW — the component's own scoped `transition` outranks and truncates the `vj-morph` animation family, deleting its transform and spring
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154 `.mix-plate { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard); }` compiles scoped to `.mix-plate[data-v-0f138735]` (specificity 0,2,0) vs demo/styles/animations.css:103-109 `.vj-morph-enter-active` (0,1,0). Measured on the frame the class is applied: {"transitionProperty":"opacity","transitionDuration":"0.2s","transitionTimingFunction":"cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)","transform":"matrix(0.97, 0, 0, 0.97, 0, 4)"} against the family's own `"opacity, transform, max-height | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1), linear(0 0%, … 1 100%), cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)"`.
defects.mechanism: Two `transition` SHORTHAND declarations on one element; the higher-specificity scoped rule replaces the whole declaration rather than merging, so `transform` and `max-height` are dropped and the `--spring-snappy` linear() curve is swapped for `--ease-standard`. `vj-morph-enter-from`'s scale(.97)/translateY(4px) is still applied to the element (matrix confirms) but, no longer being a transitioned property, it SNAPS instead of springing. Directly violates the law animations.css:60-65 states in prose: "The family owns the CURVE + TOKEN pairing; a consuming site may parameterise only GEOMETRY through the `--vj-*` custom properties." Also owner edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides) and edict 6 (animations never deleted, only moved or tokenized).
defects.reproduction: Live at /#/mix: set mixResult null → object; a MutationObserver captures getComputedStyle on the first frame `.mix-plate` carries `vj-morph-enter-active`. transitionProperty reads "opacity" alone. A detached `<div class="vj-morph-enter-active">` probe returns the family's full three-property value for contrast.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 152-154 outright. The plate is already inside a `vj-morph` <Transition> (MixPane.vue:111), so the family already owns its opacity; `.mix-plate--ghost { opacity: .55 }` needs no transition shorthand of its own. If the ghost step must be eased independently, use `transition-property`/`transition-duration` LONGHANDS (which merge instead of replacing) or a `--vj-morph-*` custom property, per the stated family law.

defects.defect: NEW (retires r3's N-3, carried unmeasured for three rounds) — Reset destroys the focused button and drops keyboard focus to `<body>`
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:139 `@click="emit('reset')"` → MixPane.vue:117 → useMixingState.reset() sets mixResult=null → MixPane.vue:113 `v-if="mixResult"` unmounts the plate. Measured: {"focusBeforeReset":"Reset","focusAfterReset":{"tag":"BODY","title":null,"isBody":true,"plateStillMounted":false}}.

defects.reproduction: Live at /#/mix with a settled result: `plate.querySelector('button[title="Reset"]').focus(); reset.click();` then after 500ms `document.activeElement === document.body` → true.

Implement in MixPane's reset handler (useTemplateRef + focus()), because the parent owns both the unmount and the successor; a self-restoring child would be the contrivance edict 3 forbids.

defects.defect: NEW (retires r3's N-4/N-5, carried unmeasured for three rounds) — `:key="i"` reuses DOM nodes on re-mix, so the `vj-enter` TransitionGroup never fires
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:99 `:key="i"` inside the `vj-enter` TransitionGroup (:92-106). Measured across a same-length, different-color palette swap: {"sameDomNodeReused":true,"hasEnterClass":false,"dots":2} — literally the same element object before and after, and no `.vj-enter-enter-active` anywhere in the plate during the swap.

The animation runs only when the palette GROWS; the common case (changing color space or hue method and re-mixing at the same length) is silent. Same shape as R6-1: an animation present in source, inert at runtime.

Locator: getByRole('main', { name: 'Color tool panes' }).getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' }). Expected: visible. defects.defect: A failed clipboard copy is completely silent — the producer's named failure, its error hook and its four-state status are all discarded

Measured with writeText stubbed to reject NotAllowedError: before={"title":"Copy color","icon":"lucide-copy"}, afterOk={"Copied!","lucide-check"}, afterFail={"Copy color","lucide-copy"} — afterFail is byte-identical to before.

(b) At the seam: startMix (useMixingState.ts:79-101) must not run partial-failure-capable parsing inside an event handler with no boundary. mixPalettes should return a Result, startMix should set mixResult to a failure variant, and the plate should render the failure it was handed — which also supplies the discriminated union D-6/D-9 asks for.

defects.defect: NEW at r6. The `useClipboard` contract is half-consumed. `copy()`'s discriminated CopyResult is discarded, `onCopyError` is not passed, `status === "failure"` has no reset timer so a failed copy is a permanent state rendered identically to idle, and `invalidate()` (the primitive's own stale-payload escape) is never called with no watcher on `result`. Compounded by the dual clipboard path: the dock's Copy-result action reaches a SECOND implementation with no confirmation state at all.
defects.evidence: Producer, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js: `n.ok ? (a.value="success", l=setTimeout(()=>{…a.value="idle"…}, i.resetMs ?? 1500), n) : (a.value="failure", i.onCopyError?.(n.reason), n)` — success resets, failure does NOT; `return { status: o, copy: p, invalidate: d }`. Consumer: MixResultDisplay.vue:31 `useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })` (no onCopyError), :32 `copied = status.value === "success"` (failure maps to the same render as idle), :46 `await copy(text)` (CopyResult discarded), and no `watch` on `result` anywhere in the file. Dual path: MixResultDisplay.vue:43-46 and MixPane.vue:51-53 carry byte-identical serialization (`result.type === "color" ? result.css ?? "" : result.colors?.map(c=>c.css).join(", ") ?? ""`) on two different primitives (useClipboard vs writeClipboard); demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222 routes the dock's "Copy result" action to `paneRefs.mix.value?.copyResult?.()` — the writeClipboard path, which returns nothing and shows nothing.
defects.mechanism: a concept (serialize a MixResult to clipboard text + confirm it) with no home and two call sites, each consuming a different fraction of its primitive's contract — so the same user command has two different observable behaviours depending on which chrome is used
defects.reproduction: Failure-silence half is reachable TODAY and not gated by F-1: serve the demo over the LAN http:// origin that vite.config.ts's `server.host: true` exists to enable (non-secure context → navigator.clipboard undefined → writeClipboard returns {ok:false, reason:"no-api"}), then fire the dock's "Copy result" action (usePaneRouter.ts:222). MixPane.vue:54 discards the result; nothing is rendered; glass-ui's console.warn is not collected by e2e setupEnvNoise (which watches console.error). Stale-confirmation half is HYPOTHESIS, mechanism proved from the source above but live repro BLOCKED-BY-F-1 (this component never mounts): click copy, then let a new mix settle within 1500ms — `copied` stays true and the checkmark asserts the current result is on the clipboard while the previous one is.
defects.proposedCure: One home: `mixResultText(r: MixResult): string` in a new `demo/workbenches/mix/mix-result.ts` beside the type it serializes. One clipboard seat: keep `useClipboard` in the plate (it owns the confirmation), delete `MixPane.copyResult` and its `writeClipboard` import, and point usePaneRouter.ts:222 at the plate's exposed `copy` so the dock and the in-plate button share one contract. Consume the whole primitive: pass `onCopyError`, branch on `CopyResult`, render the `"failure"` status, and call `invalidate()` from a watcher on `result`.

defects.defect: `MixResult` is an optional-field bag rather than a discriminated union, and it is homed in a composable rather than a type module. The consequence in this file alone is five masking fallbacks — the exact idiom edict 2 bans.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:32-36 `export interface MixResult { type: MixResultType; css?: string; colors?: PaletteColor[]; }` — both payload fields optional on both arms. Consequent guards in MixResultDisplay.vue: :37 `result.css ?? "var(--muted-foreground)"`, :39 `result.colors?.[0]?.css ?? "var(--muted-foreground)"`, :44 `result.css ?? ""`, :45 `result.colors?.map(...).join(", ") ?? ""`, :78 `v-if="result.type === 'color' && result.css"`, :91 `v-if="result.type === 'palette' && result.colors"`. The type is consumed by four modules across two directory levels: MixPane.vue:9, MixAnimationCanvas.vue:6, useMixingAnimation.ts:45, MixResultDisplay.vue:7 — all reaching into a behaviour module to obtain a shape.
defects.mechanism: an untagged optional bag forces every consumer to re-derive the invariant the type should have carried; each re-derivation is a masking fallback that hides the un-modelled state instead of making it unrepresentable
defects.reproduction: Read demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:30-36 and MixResultDisplay.vue:36-47,78,91. With `type: "color"` and `css: undefined` — a state the type permits — line 78 renders nothing but line 120's action row still renders, producing a result plate with buttons and no result.
defects.proposedCure: Move the type to a new `demo/workbenches/mix/mix-result.ts` as a true discriminated union: `type MixResult = { readonly kind: "color"; readonly color: PaletteColor } | { readonly kind: "palette"; readonly colors: readonly PaletteColor[] }`. All five guards in this file delete themselves by typing, and useMixingState.ts becomes a state machine that imports its shape rather than defining it.

defects.defect: `TransitionGroup` is imported at :4 but the Vue compiler auto-imports it as a built-in regardless of the setup binding — and `<Transition>` at :60 is used with no import at all. defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:4 `import { computed, TransitionGroup } from "vue";` vs :60 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (no import). defects.mechanism: redundant import of a compiler built-in, made undetectable by the SFC template-usage heuristic; the defect is the in-file convention split, not the byte

defects.defect: 19 pass-through `demo/ui/*` barrels shadow the design system. `demo/ui/card/index.ts` is a bare re-export of glass-ui's Card — a pure alias shim (edict 2) that also puts a demo/ui/ layer in front of glass-ui (edict 4). defects.evidence: `cat demo/ui/card/index.ts` → `export { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — the entire file, and it also goes through the ROOT barrel. demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue:3 `import { Card } from "../../ui/card";` against MixResultDisplay.vue:3 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";`. `ls demo/ui/` → 19 directories (alert, avatar, badge, button, card, checkbox, collapsible, dialog, dropdown-menu, input, label, popover, radio-group, select, separator, skeleton, slider, switch, tooltip).
defects.mechanism: a re-export shim kept as a migration alias long after the migration; it manufactures a second import identity for one component and hides which layer actually owns the primitive
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/card/index.ts (one line, pure re-export) then sed -n '3p' demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue and sed -n '3p' demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue — same package, two paths, adjacent files.

MixPane.vue:103 sources it from `selectedColors`, whose only two writers are `emit("addColor")` at MixSourceSelector.vue:70 and :220, both on `<WatercolorDot tag="button" @click=…>`. `grep -rn addColor demo/ | grep -v workbenches/mix` → 9 hits, none wired to the mix. defects.mechanism: design-system boundary silently swallows the consumer's contract: a decorative primitive with inheritAttrs:false is asked to be a command, and drops onClick/aria-label/tag/disabled without error; the consequence lands two components away as dead code.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/mix in colors mode with an empty selection. Click the add-slot ghost: nothing happens (elementFromPoint returns the parent .swatch-row). Restores click, accessible name, disabled semantics and focus ring in one root-level edit with no new vocabulary. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox: WatercolorDot's inheritAttrs:false must either forward listeners or refuse them loudly.

defects.defect: `variant="primary-audacious"` is not a glass-ui 7 prop — it leaks into the DOM as an invalid attribute and the pane's one verb ships in the quiet `secondary` wash register its own comment says it must not be; the hard typecheck gate is structurally blind to it.

Live attribute dump: ["data-slot=\"button\"","data-emphasis=\"secondary\"","data-tone=\"neutral\"","data-size=\"md\"","class=\"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display\"","variant=\"primary-audacious\""]. glass-7 ButtonProps = emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class, `emphasis` default "secondary" (dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-18; dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js). `grep -rl "primary-audacious" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → 0 files. Provenance: authored at a34d20f4 (pre-glass-7), not migrated by f2c8f565 ("adopt @mkbabb/glass-ui 7.0.0"). Two live sites: MixConfigBar.vue:163, GenerateControls.vue:158. defects.mechanism: legacy vocabulary surviving a major design-system bump because the repo's only mechanical prop check (vue-tsc) does not diagnose unknown component props — every gate reads a representation, none reads the rendered element.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/mix → inspect the Mix button: `variant="primary-audacious"` is present as a raw attribute and `data-emphasis="secondary"`. Then run `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` at HEAD: exits 0.
defects.proposedCure: `emphasis="primary"` (plus a `tone` for the audacious accent) at both sites — the glass-7 axis that means what the comment says. And because vue-tsc demonstrably cannot see a dead prop, make a design-system bump's migration step a prop-name grep against the new `.d.ts` surface, not a gate run.

defects.defect: The hue-method dropdown draws four byte-identical chips beside four different descriptions in the app's shipped default space, and the control itself is fully operable while being completely inert there.

Library census (probe-ramp-identity.mjs against dist/subpaths/color.js): oklab 1/4, lab 1/4, rgb 1/4, xyz 1/4 (ALL IDENTICAL); oklch/lch/hsl/hsv/hwb 2/4. Violates the module's own O-14 TRUTH LAW (sample.ts:16-19).

defects.defect: The three Select handlers are typed with reka-ui's `AcceptableValue` — a vocabulary glass-ui 7 explicitly rejects at runtime — reaching past the design system to a transitive dependency, then narrowing with unchecked `as` casts.

defects.mechanism: design-system boundary crossed for a type the design system already publishes — a glass-6-era import that the glass-7 adoption left in place.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the runtime consequence (SelectItem :value always supplies a valid member, so the casts never actually mis-narrow today). The vocabulary mismatch and the runtime throw are both quoted facts.
defects.proposedCure: `import type { SelectionValue } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` — the type the emitter actually emits — across all four demo sites; the three `as` casts then narrow from a two-member union instead of a five-member one.

defects.defect: Two orphan `<label class="section-label">` elements (three in palettes mode): no `for`, no wrapped control — invalid HTML and the visible text is not programmatically associated with the control it names.

defects.defect: Per-instance `class="h-9"` on all three SelectTriggers overrides the design system's control-height token, putting the triggers 4px out of register with the verb directly beneath them in the same bar.

OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §3 decides `source mode/rack; result; method/provenance/commit`; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 repeats it as `operand rack, result, controls`. MixPane.vue renders rack (:80) → MixConfigBar (:97) → MixResultDisplay (:112). Either the strip IS the rack — a single non-wrapping ramp with the values enumerated beside it, which also closes D-1's information void — or the dots are the rack and the strip is deleted as a duplicate telling. defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:102 (`class="w-10 h-10 shrink-0"`), measured 40×40 with 8px gaps, 6 per row at 390. Rendered filter on the live nodes: `<feTurbulence baseFrequency="0.05" numOctaves="5">` + `<feDisplacementMap scale="1.3">`. defects.mechanism: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §1 names WatercolorDot as one of exactly two signature forms; §2 lists Watercolor/data as `the only ornamental color-bearing species`. A 1.3px displacement against a 40px box is ~3% of the edge; the seeded radius has no room to read at that scale in a tight grid. A signature form legible at only one of its two rendered sizes is spent without being received.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the pixel mechanism — this is a rendered-appearance judgement from the two frames. The displacement-to-diameter ratio is labelled a HYPOTHESIS in the report: I measured the filter parameters and the box, not the resulting edge deviation in pixels.
defects.proposedCure: Either grow the palette face to the size at which the species reads (the single-colour branch's 56px, at fewer per row), or accept that a dense ordered set is a strip and let D-47's cure make it one — reserving the WatercolorDot for the specimen, which is what §1 calls it.

Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome.` These are three of the smallTapTargets the mega-tranche visual REPORT.md counts on /#/mix — counted without this component even mounted.

result.strongestDefect: D-45 — the result region is rendered AFTER the method/commit region, contradicting the sequence OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §3 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 both decide (`source mode/rack; result; method/provenance/commit`). Measured at 390×844: rack y=192 → method/commit y=526 → result y=652.2, with the plate 126.2px below the top of the region holding the Mix button that produced it. Five prior runs quoted that very sequence line while arguing the provenance finding and none tested it. It is the strongest defect this run because it is not a styling slip but the composition being inverted: the decided order exists so the answer lands between the operands that made it and the knobs that would change it, and re-tuning Color space now requires scrolling back up past the answer.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records what I proved SOUND so run 7 does not re-probe it. (1) Focus ring survives outside dock scope — I expected a defect and there is none: `.dock-icon-button:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--dock-ring); outline: none }` is an UNSCOPED selector and `--dock-ring` is root-defined in dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css; measured resolving on the plate's buttons to `0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(47.1189% 0.1884 9.834deg) 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px …`. (2) Forced-colors focus is producer-covered: a11y-overrides.css gives `.dock-icon-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px }`. (3) Motion is tokenised, not ad hoc — `--duration-fast`/`--ease-standard` at :153 and the canon `vj-morph`/`vj-enter` families (demo/styles/animations.css:66-137); no fourth family name. (4) Reduced motion has a real global guard at animations.css:184 plus glass-ui a11y-overrides.css. (5) The gradient strip is semantically correct: measured `aria-hidden=\"true\"` + `role=\"presentation\"` — D-47 concerns its geometry, not its semantics. (6) The colour branch uses the correct value role: measured Fira Code 14px = `text-mono-small` per the closed type matrix; D-1 is the ABSENCE of that role in the palette branch, not its misuse. (7) Text contrast passes both schemes: label 5.08:1 light / 5.97:1 dark, value 13.52:1 light. (8) All craft edicts are satisfied: 159 lines and one job (no god module); no alias, shim, dual path or back-compat branch; no new shared/ dir or wrapper; Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure with default at :20; `import type { MixResult }` at :7 satisfying verbatimModuleSyntax; the hand-rolled copy timer already retired for the producer's useClipboard at :31. The defect in this component is design, not craft. STANDING GAP: the 400% actual in-app-zoom arm that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.2 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 both mandate (`not responsive emulation`) has NO coverage from this seat or, as far as I can tell, any of runs 1-5 — it is the one canon-required arm this directory has never exercised, and run 7 should take it.

defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./package-lock.json').packages['node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js']))" && for f in color css value math easing transform quantize; do echo $f $(md5 -q dist/subpaths/$f.d.ts) $(md5 -q node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/$f.d.ts); done && cmp dist/subpaths/css.js node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js
defects.proposedCure: Take r5 R5-1's cure (both @mkbabb deps → devDependencies) and add the piece that actually removes the self-copy: `overrides: { "@mkbabb/value.js": "." }` (or a workspace pin) so npm satisfies glass-ui's peer with THIS checkout rather than downloading a stranger. Then make reproducibility a gate: two `npm pack` runs from a clean tree must yield an identical integrity hash — the artifact twin of R5-1's manifest assertion. Together: the manifest declares zero runtime dependencies, no copy of the package can install inside it, and the one artifact that ships is byte-defined by the tree that ships it.

defects.defect: The cross-repo resolution posture that three config files document at length (mechanism-C / N.W1.C: a `file:` symlink to ../glass-ui kept fresh by sibling `build:watch`) is not the posture installed. defects.mechanism: A resolution posture was reasoned about once, written into three comment blocks as the stated REASON for three unrelated settings (no typecheck error-filter needed; the `dedupe` list; the `server.fs.allow` widening), and then the install changed underneath the prose. Comments that justify settings are contracts, and nothing checks them.
